title: Fully Funded AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 in Iceland – Applications Open
summary: Applications are now open for the AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 , a fully funded six-month training opportunity in Iceland for professionals working in African biosphere reserves and engaged in ecosystem restoration, sustainable land management, and related fields. The fellowship is jointly offered by AfriMAB , the network of UNESCO biosphere reserves in Africa, and Iceland’s GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) . Selected fellows will undertake postgraduate-level training at the Agricultural University of Iceland , combining academic coursework, practical training, field visits, and an individual land restoration project. The 2027 programme begins on 26 February 2027 , and applications must be submitted by 10 September 2026 . AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027: Key Details Host Country: Iceland Host Institution: Agricultural University of Iceland Programme: GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) Duration: Six months Start Date: 26 February 2027 Funding: Fully funded Target Group: Professionals working with African biosphere reserves Age Requirement: Under 40 years Academic Award: 30 ECTS postgraduate credits and GRÓ LRT Diploma Application Deadline: 10 September 2026 Applications open for AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 Applications are now open for the 2027 AfriMAB GRÓ LRT Land Restoration Fellowships, offering fully funded places for professionals from African biosphere reserves engaged in ecosystem restoration. GRÓ LRT/UNESCO 17 July 2026 Last update:23 July 2026 Summary A six-month, hands-on programme Conditions and criteria More information AfriMAB, the network of UNESCO biosphere reserves across Africa, and Iceland s GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) have opened applications for the 2027 cohort of their joint fellowship for professionals from African biosphere reserves. Selected candidates will spend six months, from 26 February 2027, at the Agricultural University of Iceland, combining coursework with an individual restoration project tailored to their home institution s needs, before returning to their posts with a postgraduate diploma and university credits. The fellowship which covers tuition, travel, health insurance, and a full living stipend responds to the growing priority restoration has taken on within the MAB Programme s agenda, responding to calls issued by the 2023 AfriMAB General Assembly and the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration. Candidates under the age of 40 with relevant academic and field experience have until 10 September 2026 to submit their applications. GRÓ LRT/UNESCO Over the past four months in the GRÓ LRT program, I have gained valuable experience in restoration through theoretical and practical sessions, all the while building meaningful networks with fellows, alumni, and staff. Beyond technical knowledge, living in Iceland, the “land of fire and ice,” has broadened my perspective and deepened my appreciation of nature. This journey has inspired me professionally and personally. Neba Estherbel Bih, Cameroon, GRÓ LRT 2026 cohort A six-month, hands-on programme In 2019, the GRÓ Category 2 Centre was established to work across four thematic areas: Gender, fisheries, geothermal, and land restoration. The GRÓ Land Restoration Training Programme (GRÓ LRT) provides postgraduate training for working specialists from middle- and low-income countries in the restoration of degraded land and sustainable land management. The GRÓ LRT programme runs an annual six-month training in Iceland, hosted at the Agricultural University of Iceland. The first 12 weeks focus on coursework — introductory and specialized — alongside practical training and field trips. In the following 12 weeks, each Fellow develops an individual project tailored to their academic background and the needs of their home institution. Fellows who complete the training receive 30 ECTS at postgraduate level from the Agricultural University of Iceland, as well as a GRÓ LRT diploma. In this context, GRÓ LRT offers to train at least two fellows from African biosphere reserves engaged in restoration activities in its 2027 cohort. Applications are open The deadline is 10 September 2026 . Check conditions below. Conditions and criteria The fellowship is fully funded, covering tuition and academic expenses, travel and health insurance costs, and a stipend covering all living expenses during the six-month stay in Iceland. Institutions nominating a candidate are asked to grant them full study leave for the six-month training in Iceland, continue paying their salary and benefits throughout the programme, and reinstate them in their position upon their return. Applicants should hold a prominent role in ecosystem restoration activity within a biosphere reserve, and hold at least one university degree relevant to GRÓ LRT s field of work, such as ecology, natural sciences, environmental management or studies, and related disciplines. Candidates must: have at least one year of relevant experience working in a biosphere reserve; be able to communicate in English (speak, read and write), the working language of GRÓ LRT; be under the age of 40. In some cases, GRÓ LRT has accepted candidates who do not fulfil the education requirement but bring extensive working experience in a relevant area. Applicants must submit: a letter of motivation; a CV; a letter of endorsement from the biosphere reserve where they work; a letter of endorsement from the national MAB Focal Point or MAB Committee in their country, and; certificates of academic achievement. All documents must be uploaded in PDF form as attachments via the online application form. Applications are evaluated jointly by GRÓ LRT and the MAB Secretariat, and only complete applications meeting the stated requirements will be considered. The deadline for applications is 10 September 2026. For further information, contact grolrt@grolrt.is or mab@unesco.org . More information GRÓ Category 2 Centre UNESCO s Man and the Biosphere Programme Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/applications-open-afrimab-gro-lrt-land-restoration-fellowships-2027 The post Fully Funded AfriMAB GRÓ-LRT Land Restoration Fellowships 2027 in Iceland – Applications Open appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme 2026: Up to US$10,000 for Research in Japan
summary: Applications are now open for the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme 2026 , also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme . The programme offers young researchers from eligible countries the opportunity to undertake postgraduate research at universities and research institutions in Japan , with fellowship funding of up to US$10,000 . For the 2026 cycle, 10 fellowships will be awarded to highly qualified young researchers, with priority given to applicants from Africa, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), Ukraine and Türkiye . Research stays will focus on areas including heritage conservation, sustainable development, artificial intelligence, climate action, education and societal resilience . Application Deadline: 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time Fellowship Amount: Up to US$10,000 Number of Fellowships: 10 Host Country: Japan Duration: 3–9 months Research Period: From February 2027, to be completed by December 2027 Age Limit: 40 years or younger at the time of application Minimum Qualification: Master’s degree or equivalent Application Route: Through the applicant’s National Commission for UNESCO Notice: The application for the Cycle 2026 is now open. Deadline for Candidate Submission: 30 September 2026 Useful documents for the Cycle 2026 Application Guide Annex 1 – List of invited Member States and Associate Members Annex 2 – Research areas and indicative sub-areas Annex 3 – Application Form Annex 4 – Research Proposal Template Annex 5 – UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge About the Programme Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO’s mandate. Since its establishment, the Programme has enabled 291 young researchers from 101 countries around the world to pursue postgraduate research, contributing to academic cooperation, capacity-building and the development of knowledge in fields of shared global importance. Under the 2026 cycle, UNESCO and the Government of Japan will award 10 fellowships to highly qualified young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Türkiye. The fellowships will support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence, with particular attention to interdisciplinary research connecting these themes with social, ethical, governance and contextual dimensions. Through research stays in Japanese universities and research institutions, fellows will have the opportunity to further develop their work and engage with Japan’s academic and research community. Cycle 2026 at a glance Key information Details Fellowships available 10 Fellowship grant Up to US$10,000 Duration No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months Host country Japan Fellowship period in Japan From February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027. Application deadline 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time Submission channel Through National Commissions for UNESCO Invited Member States and Associate Members AFRICA – 47 Member States: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Togo, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe ARAB STATES – 1 Member State: Bahrain ASIA AND THE PACIFIC – 17 Member States, 2 Associate Members*: Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Micronesia (Federated State of), Nauru, Niue, New Caledonia*, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Singapore, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tokelau*, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN – 16 Member States, 7 Associate Members*: Anguilla*, Antigua and Barbuda, Aruba*, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, British Virgin Islands*, Cayman Islands*, Cuba, Curaçao*, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat*, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Sint Maarten*, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago EUROPE – 2 Member States: Türkiye, Ukraine Research areas Research proposals submitted under the 2026 cycle should fall within one of the following research areas. Applicants should refer to Annex 2 for the full list of indicative sub-areas and select one primary research area and one corresponding sub-area that best reflect the focus of their proposed research. Heritage Conservation and Management (4 sub-areas) AI for Sustainable Management of Natural Resources and Climate Action （5 sub-areas) Ethical, Inclusive, and Human Centred AI for Sustainable Development (6 sub-areas) AI for Sustainable Cities, Infrastructure, and Societal Resilience (6 sub-areas) AI and Education (7 sub-areas) Eligibility requirements Applicants must: be nationals of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1 ; be no more than 40 years old at the time of application; hold at least a Master’s degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposed research and demonstrate strong academic and research potential; demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan; have obtained acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, who will oversee the proposed research. Fellowship grant and eligible costs Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000. The grant will be provided as a lump-sum contribution and is intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover: international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary; accommodation; medical insurance; personal subsistence in Japan, including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses; other research-related expenses, where applicable. The grant does not cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment, including computers, publication costs or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Medical insurance is mandatory for all selected fellows and will be arranged by UNESCO on their behalf. The cost of medical insurance will be deducted from the total fellowship amount before disbursement. How to apply Step 1 : Read carefully the Application Guide to understand the requirements for eligible candidatures and the procedures for the submission of application. Step 2: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country to enquire about the application procedures at the national level. Click here for the contact information of the National Commissions for UNESCO. Step 3: Prepare all required documents, including the application form ( Annex 3 ), academic documents, recommendation letter, host institution acceptance letter, language certificate and research proposal ( Annex 4 ). Step 4: Submit your application to the National Commission for UNESCO of your home country, at least 2 weeks before the required deadline . Step 5 : As soon as you are informed by the National Commission for UNESCO of your country that you are nominated as a candidate for this programme, you should communicate your the online application form and the supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org . Note: Only applications nominated by the National Commission will be accepted by UNESCO. Step 6: Letters of nomination, along with all the application documents should be submitted to UNESCO by the National Commissions no later than 30 September 2026, midnight Paris time . Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or submit the online applications beyond this deadline won t be considered. Selection process Applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields. The evaluation will take into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision will be made by the Japanese authorities, based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity. title: Global Child Health (GCH) Fellowship Program 2027 at SickKids, Canada
summary: The Centre for Global Child Health (CGCH) at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) in Toronto, Canada, is inviting applications for the Global Child Health (GCH) Fellowship Program. This prestigious fellowship is designed for professionals who are passionate about improving child health outcomes around the world through research, leadership, innovation, and capacity building. The fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity for individuals from diverse healthcare and research backgrounds to develop the skills needed to become leaders in global child health. Participants will work alongside internationally recognized researchers and practitioners while contributing to projects that address some of the world s most pressing child health challenges. About the Global Child Health Fellowship Program The Global Child Health Fellowship Program is a comprehensive two-year interdisciplinary training program that prepares fellows for impactful careers in global health. Rather than focusing solely on academic learning, the program combines practical experience with leadership development. Fellows become actively involved in the design, implementation, analysis, and evaluation of research and capacity-building initiatives that improve health systems and child well-being worldwide. Hosted by the Centre for Global Child Health at SickKids, one of the world s leading pediatric hospitals, the fellowship provides an exceptional learning environment where fellows collaborate with experts addressing complex global health issues. Fellowship Objectives The program aims to prepare the next generation of global health leaders by helping fellows: Build advanced leadership skills. Strengthen research capacity. Develop expertise in implementation science. Improve project management and evaluation skills. Contribute to innovative global health initiatives. Support health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries. Enhance collaboration across multidisciplinary teams. Research Areas Fellows may contribute to projects covering a wide range of global child health topics, including: Nutrition Child growth and development Pediatric oncology Infectious diseases Climate change and child health Microbiome research Vaccine development Complex systems and network science Implementation science Health systems strengthening Health workforce training Capacity building initiatives Other emerging global health priorities This broad range of research themes allows fellows to gain practical experience while addressing real-world health challenges affecting children globally. Fellowship Duration The fellowship runs for two years . During this period, fellows will participate in interdisciplinary research, leadership training, scholarly development, and collaborative projects under the mentorship of experienced global health professionals. Who Can Apply For This Fellowship Opportunity ? The fellowship welcomes applicants from a wide variety of educational and professional backgrounds. Eligible applicants may include professionals in fields such as: Medicine (MD) Doctoral graduates (PhD) Nursing Allied Health Professions Public Health Health Research Other relevant healthcare disciplines Individuals with a strong commitment to improving child health through research, education, implementation science, or capacity building are encouraged to apply. Why Apply? Participating in the Global Child Health Fellowship Program provides numerous professional and academic benefits, including: Training at one of Canada s leading pediatric research institutions. Mentorship from internationally recognized global health experts. Leadership development opportunities. Hands-on experience in global health research. Exposure to interdisciplinary collaborations. Opportunities to contribute to high-impact projects. Professional networking with researchers and health professionals from around the world. Preparation for long-term careers in global health research and policy. Application Process Interested applicants should review the official fellowship information and complete the online application before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents well in advance to avoid last-minute delays. Application Portal Apply for this opportunity HERE Important Dates Application Deadline : September 13, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EDT) Expected Fellowship Start : On or before July 2, 2027 Contact Applicants with questions regarding the fellowship may contact the Global Child Health Fellowship Program Committee through the official contact information provided by SickKids. Conclusion The Global Child Health Fellowship Program at SickKids offers an exceptional opportunity for healthcare professionals and researchers seeking to make a meaningful impact on child health worldwide. Through world-class mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and involvement in transformative research projects, fellows will gain the expertise needed to address global child health challenges. If you aspire to become a leader in global health research or capacity building, this fellowship represents an excellent pathway toward achieving that goal. Interested applicants should submit their applications before September 13, 2026 , to be considered for this highly competitive program. title: Africa CDC Youth Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 for Young African Professionals
summary: Young African professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, and healthcare innovation are invited to join the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 , a three-day virtual hands-on training taking place from 27–29 July 2026 . The training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa to strengthen their practical skills in research design, research methodology, and concept note development . Key Details Program: Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 Dates: 27–29 July 2026 Duration: 3 days Format: Virtual Participants: 100 young professionals from across Africa Eligibility: Exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Focus Areas: Research design, research methodology, and concept note development Collaboration: West African Institute of Public Health Network: Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN), an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program Join YiDHN: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn About the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 is designed to equip young African professionals with practical skills to strengthen their capacity to conduct research and contribute to innovation in public and digital health. Taking place virtually from 27 to 29 July 2026 , the three-day hands-on workshop will provide participants with practical knowledge in research design, research methodology, and the development of strong concept notes. Organized in collaboration with the West African Institute of Public Health , the training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa , creating an opportunity to build research capacity, foster collaboration, and advance digital health innovation across the continent. What Will Participants Learn? The training will focus on three core areas: Research Design: Strengthening participants ability to develop structured and relevant research approaches. Research Methodology: Building practical knowledge of methods and approaches for conducting effective research. Concept Note Development: Developing the skills needed to prepare clear and compelling research concept notes. Participants will also have the opportunity to connect with other young professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, technology, and healthcare innovation across Africa. Who Can Participate? The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop is exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) . The workshop will accommodate 100 young professionals from across Africa who are interested in strengthening their research capacity and contributing to digital health innovation. Those who are not yet members of YiDHN can join the network through the onboarding form. About the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) The Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) is an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program aimed at empowering young professionals across Africa to lead the transformation of healthcare through digital solutions. The network brings together young people passionate about digital health and provides opportunities to connect, build capacity, collaborate, and contribute to shaping the future of healthcare in Africa. Through the network, young professionals can also gain access to future training, mentorship, networking, and capacity-building opportunities . Why Join the YiDHN? Africa s rapidly evolving digital health landscape creates significant opportunities for young professionals to contribute to healthcare transformation through research, technology, innovation, and collaboration. By joining YiDHN, young professionals can become part of a growing continental network focused on fostering innovation, building capacity, and driving impactful change in digital health across Africa . Membership also provides an avenue to learn about opportunities such as the Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop and future initiatives for young digital health professionals. How to Join the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network Interested young professionals can complete the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Onboarding Form to join the network. Join the YiDHN here: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn Join a community of young African professionals working to advance digital health innovation, research, capacity building, and healthcare transformation across Africa . title: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Fellowship 2026 in Geneva, Switzerland | CHF 6,000 Monthly Stipend | Open Worldwide
summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is offering a Fellowship opportunity with the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) in Geneva, Switzerland. The fellowship has a contract duration of 12 months, with the possibility to renew, and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 6,000. Key Details Organization: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Eligibility: Open to applicants worldwide who meet the requirements. Fellowship: Fellowship 26229-FEL Section: WIPO Knowledge Center, IP Futures and Knowledge Management Section, Administration, Finance and Management Sector Duty Station: CH-Geneva Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland Contract Duration: 12 months Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026 Publication Date: 22-Jul-2026 Application Deadline: 06-Aug-2026, 10:59:00 PM Grade: N/A IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING APPLICATION DEADLINE: Please note that the deadline for applications is indicated in local time as per the time zone of the applicant s location. 1. Organizational context (a) Organizational Setting The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a United Nations specialized agency. Its WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) is the custodian of the knowledge repository, which is an authoritative source for global IP academic research. The WKC oversees WIPO’s physical and digital library collection, in addition to the dissemination of WIPO publications. The WKC team requires a qualified Fellow to support the library and knowledge services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting data that informs evidence-based decision-making. Working closely with colleagues, the fellow will contribute to the assessment of library services, digital resources, and user engagement, helping to identify opportunities to improve discoverability, accessibility, and service delivery. Fellowships aim to provide fellows with experience to strengthen their knowledge and professional competence, which they can apply in their professional field once they have completed their fellowship with WIPO. (b) Reporting Lines The Fellow shall work under the supervision of the Head of the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC). (c) Objectives During the fellowship, the Fellow will assist with the WKC activities and gain in-depth knowledge and competence in the respective field. 2. Duties and responsibilities The Fellow will provide support in the following areas: a) Collect, validate, and manage quantitative and qualitative data relating to library services, digital collections, and information resources. b) Gather, monitor, and analyze usage statistics from library platforms, repositories, websites, and other digital services. c) Produce regular statistical reports to support strategic planning and operational decision-making. d) Analyze trends in resource usage, identifying patterns and opportunities for improvement. e) Assist in developing and maintaining key performance indicators (KPIs) for library services and digital initiatives. f) Contribute to the evaluation of digital resources, collections, and services using evidence-based assessment techniques. g) Assist in collecting and analyzing citation, bibliometric, altmetric, and other research impact data, where applicable. f) Prepare reports, presentations, and briefing materials summarizing analytical findings for internal stakeholders. h) Collaborate with colleagues to improve workflows for data collection, reporting, and assessment. i) Perform other related duties as required. 3. Requirements (a) Education Essential: At least a first-level degree in library, information science, knowledge management or a related field. Recognized professional qualification. (b) Experience Essential: At least two years of professional experience working in a library, knowledge management, research support, or related environment. Experience collecting, managing, and analyzing library or information-related data. Experience working with usage statistics, service metrics, or other performance data to support assessment activities. Experience preparing analytical reports and presenting findings to support decision-making. Experience using spreadsheet software and data analysis tools. Desirable: Experience working with integrated library systems, institutional repositories, discovery platforms, or digital library services. Experience using business intelligence, dashboard, or data visualization tools. Experience working with bibliometric, altmetric, or research impact indicators. Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical tools would be an advantage. (c) Languages Essential: Excellent (written and spoken) knowledge of English. Desirable: Good knowledge of at least one of WIPO s other official languages would be an advantage. (d) Specific skills and competencies Essential: Sound understanding of library operations and digital information services. Knowledge of library assessment methodologies and performance measurement. Ability to collect, clean, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail. Ability to identify trends and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Good understanding of statistical concepts and data visualization principles. Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team. Excellent written and oral communication skills. 4. Organizational competencies Communicating effectively. Showing team spirit. Demonstrating integrity. Valuing diversity. Producing results. Showing service orientation. Seeing the big picture. Seeking change and innovation. Developing yourself and others. 5. Terms and conditions a) Term of fellowship: A fellowship may be granted for a period of up to 12 months with the possibility to renew. b) Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026. c) Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland. d) Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly. e) Travel expenses: WIPO shall contribute towards the cost of the fellow’s travel on engagement and separation from service. If necessary, WIPO may provide assistance in obtaining an entry visa to Switzerland. f) WIPO contributes towards the medical insurance and provides accident insurance coverage during the course of the fellowship. g) WIPO will request a “carte de legitimation” for the Fellow, which serves as a residence and work permit, from the Permanent Mission of Switzerland to the United Nations Office and to the other international organizations in Geneva. Family members of the Fellow are not eligible for a “carte de legitimation.” h) Tax and social security: Fellows shall be solely responsible for meeting any taxation and social security obligations that may arise directly or indirectly from their contract with WIPO. FOR MORE INFO AND TO APPLY NOW CLICK HERE Additional information WIPO values diversity among its personnel and is committed to equal employment opportunities. We welcome applications from qualified candidates from unrepresented Member States of WIPO, and from underrepresented geographical regions and groups, including people with disabilities. If candidates need any accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, they should contact their HR focal point when they receive an invitation. Fellows are not staff members of WIPO, and the position does not lead to any employment rights and entitlements beyond the terms of the fellowship. The Fellowship will take place in Geneva, Switzerland and it cannot be carried out remotely. By completing an application, candidates understand that any willful misrepresentation made on this web site, or on any other documents submitted to WIPO during the application, may result in disqualification from the recruitment process, or termination of employment with WIPO at a later date, if that employment resulted from such willful misrepresentations. In the event that your candidature is shortlisted, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of an identification and of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. WIPO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/ . Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and these will be reviewed individually. Additional testing/interviewing may be used as a form of screening. Initial appointment is subject to satisfactory professional references. title: Call for Applications: The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program (2026-2027)
summary: OVERVIEW In 2023, the CVF-V20 and the Boston University Global Development Policy Center launched the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program for finance officials (or equivalent) from CVF-V20 Member Countries. The Fellowship Program is an integral part of the CVF-V20’s ongoing efforts to promote and drive ambitious climate action and to mobilize international support for climate vulnerable nations. The aim of the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is to engender cooperation among CVF-V20 member states, provide them with the tools to combat challenges they may face in the pursuit of strategies to avert climate breakdown, and pioneer the development of economic and financial solutions, including the mobilization of domestic climate finance towards positive climate action. The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is designed to provide mid- to senior career officials with opportunities for peer-learning, building cutting-edge technical skills to integrate climate change into their work, and supporting their leadership in advancing innovative solutions. The CVF-V20 has consistently emphasized the need to reform the international financial architecture to unlock opportunities on the ground to promote climate prosperity. Through weekly webinars, interactions with experts, residencies, and immersive exercises, V20 Climate Prosperity Fellows will have a unique opportunity to work together in advancing a fit for purpose international financial architecture. COLLABORATION OBJECTIVES At the end of the program, Fellows are expected to be well positioned to support resource mobilization for Climate Prosperity Plans and to: Understand the international financial architecture and be able to identify opportunities to support climate prosperity; Engage in policy discussions concerning reform of the international financial architecture; Harness the knowledge and skills needed to engage and access processes associated with the international financial architecture, including on debt reform, shifting of financial flows, carbon financing exchanges, and mainstream surveillance of climate risks to drive new investment; Identify and deploy communications strategies used to raise awareness of the priorities of the climate-vulnerable countries in relation to the reform of the international financial architecture; and Contribute to the formulation and implementation of their countries’ Climate Prosperity Plans. TARGET OUTCOME To provide peer-learning and technical enhancement support to the finance ministries (or equivalent) of 16 to 20 CVF-V20 member countries by equipping Fellows with skills to pursue the mobilization of financial resources more effectively to support ambitious national climate prosperity plans for development positive climate action. KEY ACTIVITIES Participation in online classes/seminars/workshops; Participation in one-week in-person residencies in January 2027 and October 2027; Participation in relevant meetings, supported by the CVF-V20; Participation in interactive discussions with representatives of International Financial Institutions and partner groups with the support of the CVF-V20; and Preparation and delivery of presentations during V20 Senior Officials Meetings and relevant CVF-V20 workshops and events. CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION Candidates from Ministries of Finance (or equivalent) in CVF-V20 member countries who meet the requirements set out below are invited to apply to participate in the year-long Fellowship Program for the period 2026- 2027: Citizen of a CVF-V20 member country; Official with demonstrated five to ten years of mid- to senior-level experience in international affairs, public policy and/or development, including climate/environmental/sustainable development; Committed to participate in the Fellowship program’s activities organized throughout the year, both online and in-person and to complete and submit assignments as required; Willingness to travel abroad to attend in person meetings and training sessions with members of their cohort; Commitment to attend scheduled weekly virtual sessions for the duration of the fellowship period; Committed to working and sharing information with their national government and national stakeholders after the completion of the Fellowship; Committed to integrating into the growing network of V20 CPP fellows and staying engaged in the community to advance common priorities and mutual learning; and Proﬁcient in English. *Prospective Fellows interested in undertaking intensive training in debt sustainability analyses should indicate the same in their application and, in so doing, commit to an additional session to undertake this training each week. Proficiency in using Microsoft Excel and familiarity with macroeconomic concepts are recommended. APPLICATION PROCESS Interested officials must submit their application by accomplishing the form: Submit your application here The deadline for submission of applications is on 31 July 2026. title: UNDP Call for Proposals 2026: Funding Opportunity for CSOs and NGOs to End Violence Against Women and Girls in Africa

title: Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026: Fully Funded Remote Fellowship Offering $3,000 Stipend for Emerging Economic Policy Leaders
summary: The Roosevelt Institute is inviting experienced policy professionals, researchers, academics, and experts to apply for the Good Life Residents Program 2026 , a prestigious six-month remote residency designed to cultivate innovative policy leaders and generate transformative ideas that advance economic justice in the United States. As part of the Roosevelt Institute s broader Good Life Agenda , selected residents will work alongside leading economists, policy experts, researchers, and senior advisors to develop original policy proposals addressing some of the country s most pressing economic challenges. Participants will produce policy essays, collaborate with subject matter experts, contribute to national policy conversations, and receive $3,000 in compensation , along with travel and accommodation support for the program s concluding event if required. One of the featured residency tracks is the AI and Finance Residents Program , created in partnership with Data Society , which focuses on examining how artificial intelligence is transforming finance, investment, labor markets, industrial policy, and the broader economy. This residency provides an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who are passionate about shaping public policy, promoting equitable economic growth, and influencing the future of AI governance. About the Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month policy residency that brings together a small cohort of emerging and established policy thinkers to explore solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s vision for a stronger and more equitable economy. Rather than conducting traditional academic research, residents focus on producing practical, people-centered policy ideas that can influence public debate and policymaking. The program emphasizes collaboration, mentorship, public engagement, and intellectual exchange. Throughout the residency, participants work closely with: Roosevelt Institute Think Tank directors Senior organizational leadership Topic advisors Fellow residents Policy practitioners Academic experts Organizers and government leaders Each residency concludes with a public event designed to amplify participants ideas and encourage dialogue on important national and state-level policy issues. AI and Finance Residents Program One of the Roosevelt Institute s featured residency topics explores the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and finance. Massive investments in generative AI have significantly reshaped the economy, influencing: Stock markets Financial markets Corporate profits Bond issuance Employment trends Industrial development Trade policy Technology investment Economic growth Today, just seven technology companies account for more than one-third of the total market capitalization of the S P 500, raising concerns about market concentration, financial stability, and economic inequality. The Roosevelt Institute, together with Data Society , seeks residents capable of producing bold policy ideas that help redirect AI investment toward broader public benefit while protecting workers, strengthening democratic institutions, and encouraging sustainable innovation. Objectives of the AI and Finance Residency The residency seeks to answer important policy questions such as: How can governments better oversee private AI investments? How can policymakers reduce excessive concentration within the technology sector? How can AI investment benefit society rather than only large corporations? How can governments encourage investment across other important sectors of the economy? How should AI policy balance innovation, public safety, labor protections, and national competitiveness? What democratic institutions are needed to ensure accountability over public investments in AI? How can governments support technology research that strengthens supply chains and sustainability? Participants are encouraged to propose original, practical, and people-centered policy recommendations. What Residents Will Do Successful applicants will participate in numerous activities throughout the six-month residency. These include: Develop Original Policy Essays Residents will research and write an approximately 1,500-word policy essay presenting innovative solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda. Each essay responds to a specific policy prompt within the resident s assigned topic area. Join a Small Collaborative Cohort Each topic area consists of only three to four residents , creating an environment that encourages meaningful collaboration, peer learning, and intellectual exchange. Residents will work closely with one another throughout the program. Work with Expert Advisors Every cohort is supported by one or two Topic Advisors. These advisors include: Leading academics Government practitioners Policy leaders Organizers Industry experts They provide: Intellectual mentorship Strategic guidance Feedback on policy proposals Moderation during discussions and public events Participate in Public Events At the end of the residency, participants present and discuss their policy ideas during a public event organized by the Roosevelt Institute. The event helps amplify participants work while encouraging national dialogue around economic policy. Contribute to Public Engagement Residents may also participate in: Opinion editorials (Op-Eds) Press interviews Reporter briefings Public policy discussions Media engagement opportunities Serve as Good Life Agenda Ambassadors Participants are expected to promote and represent the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda throughout their professional and public networks. Program Structure Each residency topic includes: 3–4 Good Life Residents 1–2 senior Topic Advisors Roosevelt Institute policy staff Organizational leadership support The program emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and practical policy development. Program Duration The residency lasts: Six months Time Commitment Residents should expect to dedicate approximately: 5–8 hours per month This makes the residency suitable for professionals balancing existing work or academic responsibilities. Location The program is primarily: Remote However, participants may be invited to travel for selected meetings or the final public event. Compensation Selected residents will receive: $3,000 stipend Travel expenses covered (if required) Accommodation for the concluding event (if required) This financial support enables participants to fully engage in the residency while contributing meaningful policy work. Who Should Apply? The Roosevelt Institute encourages applications from individuals with substantial experience in policy development, technology, economics, or related fields. Ideal applicants include: Policy professionals Researchers Economists Academics Government practitioners Technology policy experts AI researchers Industrial policy specialists Think tank professionals Candidates should demonstrate both subject expertise and a commitment to developing policies that improve economic outcomes for society. Required Qualifications Successful applicants should have: Demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence, technology policy, industrial policy, or a related discipline. A minimum of five years of professional or academic policy experience . Strong analytical and writing abilities. An interest in advancing equitable economic policy. The ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary teams. A commitment to contributing original policy ideas. Benefits of Joining the Program Participants will enjoy numerous professional benefits, including: $3,000 financial compensation. National exposure through public events. Collaboration with leading policy experts. Individual mentorship from senior advisors. Opportunity to publish original policy work. Professional networking opportunities. Media and press engagement. Flexible remote participation. Travel and accommodation support for program events. Contribution to shaping future AI and economic policy discussions. Why This Residency Matters Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies worldwide. While AI offers tremendous opportunities for innovation and productivity, it also presents challenges related to wealth concentration, labor markets, financial stability, public accountability, and democratic governance. The Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Residents Program seeks individuals capable of proposing practical policy solutions that ensure AI serves broader public interests rather than reinforcing existing inequalities. Participants have the opportunity to contribute directly to one of today s most important public policy conversations while helping shape future economic policy. How to Apply Interested applicants should visit the Roosevelt Institute s official Good Life Residents Program webpage and complete the online application according to the published application instructions. Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements before submitting their materials. APPLY NOW Application Deadline Please read and complete this application by the end of the day on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to be considered for the Good Life Residents Program on AI, presented by the Roosevelt Institute and Data Society. Reach out to rooseveltsociety@rooseveltinstitute.org with any questions or concerns. Program Term: 6 months (September–February 2027) Time Commitment: Part-Time (~5–8 hours/month) Location: Remote; Travel may be requested for select convenings Conclusion The Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced policy professionals and researchers to shape conversations around artificial intelligence, finance, and economic justice. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, public engagement, and a funded six-month residency, participants can develop innovative policy ideas capable of influencing national discussions and future policymaking. For individuals passionate about AI governance, economic equity, and public policy, this residency provides a unique platform to contribute meaningful solutions while expanding professional networks and gaining national visibility. title: AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026: Apply for the Free Aspen Policy Academy Program to Develop Civic AI Policy Solutions in the United States
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming societies, economies, governments, and public services. To help address this challenge, the Aspen Policy Academy has launched applications for the AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026 , a free virtual accelerator program designed for individuals and small teams seeking to develop impactful AI policy initiatives that strengthen the relationship between governments, communities, and artificial intelligence. This unique accelerator combines policy education, expert mentorship, peer collaboration, and practical project development to help participants transform promising ideas into actionable policy solutions capable of creating real public impact. If you are passionate about civic technology, responsible AI governance, public policy, or community innovation, this program offers an exceptional opportunity to refine your ideas and present them directly to policymakers. Participants receive structured guidance to refine their ideas, strengthen their policy proposals, and develop practical advocacy strategies capable of influencing local or state-level decision-making. The accelerator is ideal for applicants who already have a promising idea but need support turning it into an effective, evidence-based policy initiative. Policy Pitching The accelerator concludes with participants presenting their refined policy solutions directly to a real decision-maker. Applicants might still need assistance with: Refining their concept Assessing feasibility Identifying stakeholders Developing policy engagement strategies Building advocacy plans Examples of Ideal Applicants Examples include: AI engineers Technology professionals Tech startup founders AI policy communicators Technology lawyers Civic innovators Community advocates Local organizers Public-interest technology professionals Residents seeking AI policy improvements within their municipalities Who May Not Benefit Most? The accelerator is designed as an introductory program. Applicants with substantial policy experience—such as those who have previously worked in professional policy roles or hold a Master s degree in Public Policy—are likely to be beyond the intended experience level. title: Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action: Free Global Online Course by UNITAR and C40 with UN Digital Certificate

To strengthen women s capacity to lead meaningful environmental change, the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), in partnership with C40 Cities and with the exclusive support of the Fondation L Oréal, has launched the Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action online course. This self-paced international e-learning programme is designed to inspire, educate, and empower women and girls to become effective climate leaders capable of developing and implementing inclusive climate initiatives within their communities and beyond. Whether you are just beginning your climate leadership journey or already working on environmental projects, this comprehensive online course provides the scientific knowledge, leadership skills, and practical tools needed to transform climate ideas into impactful actions. The programme combines climate science with practical leadership development, enabling learners to understand climate issues while learning how to design, lead, and advocate for equitable climate solutions. Developed through a collaboration between globally respected organizations, the course brings together expertise from: United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) C40 Cities Fondation L Oréal Columbia Climate School CARE France The programme recognizes that although women are among those most affected by climate change, they remain significantly underrepresented in climate decision-making processes. By strengthening leadership capacity, the course seeks to bridge this gap and encourage greater participation of women in climate governance and action. Why This Course Matters Climate change affects every country, yet its impacts are not distributed equally. Women and girls often experience disproportionate effects due to existing social and economic inequalities. At the same time, women play an essential role in developing resilient communities, promoting sustainable practices, and advancing climate justice. This course addresses these realities by helping participants: Understand climate science. Learn the principles of inclusive climate action. Build confidence as climate leaders. Develop practical climate projects. Influence decision-makers and communities. Promote equitable climate solutions. Create resilient and sustainable communities. title: Climate Action Reserve Remote Jobs 2026: Apply for Analyst, Associate and Senior Associate Program Operations Positions in the United States
summary: Are you interested in climate change, carbon markets, carbon credits, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, environmental sustainability, or climate action? The Climate Action Reserve is offering exciting full-time remote career opportunities for qualified candidates to join its Program Operations team as an Analyst, Associate, or Senior Associate . These positions provide an opportunity to contribute to one of the leading carbon crediting programs while supporting projects designed to quantify and verify greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals. Successful candidates will work in a professional, mission-driven environment focused on advancing credible, transparent, and market-based solutions to climate change. The available roles are remote and based in the United States. However, applicants must maintain legal authorization to work in the United States for the entire duration of their employment. The organization does not sponsor work visas or cover relocation expenses. About the Climate Action Reserve The Climate Action Reserve is a nonprofit organization established under Section 501(c)(3) of the United States tax code. Its vision is to create a world in which people and institutions cooperate to address climate change at speed and scale. The organization’s mission is to develop and implement trusted market-based programs that advance climate action for both people and the planet. A significant part of the Climate Action Reserve’s work involves carbon crediting. Through its programs, the organization develops high-quality standards for measuring and quantifying greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals. It also registers projects that meet the required standards, issues carbon credits associated with verified climate benefits, and maintains a transparent and publicly accessible registry system. This makes the organization an important participant in the broader carbon market and climate action ecosystem. Job Opportunity: Program Operations Analyst, Associate and Senior Associate The Climate Action Reserve is seeking candidates to join its Program Operations team. Depending on the applicant’s experience, qualifications, and level of expertise, candidates may be considered for one of three levels: Analyst Associate Senior Associate The exact duties, level of independence, and responsibilities will vary depending on the seniority of the successful candidate. The Program Operations team supports both the substantive and administrative functions of the organization’s carbon crediting programs. Employees in the team help ensure that carbon projects are properly reviewed, administered, monitored, and operated in accordance with established protocols and program requirements. Key Responsibilities Successful candidates may be responsible for a range of technical, administrative, analytical, and operational duties. 1. Review Carbon Project Documentation One of the key responsibilities of Program Operations staff is to review documentation submitted by carbon projects. This may include: Reviewing carbon project submissions. Examining verification documentation. Assessing project-related materials against applicable program requirements. Identifying inconsistencies, missing information, or areas requiring clarification. Supporting the evaluation of documentation related to emission reductions and removals. This responsibility requires a strong eye for detail and the ability to carefully analyze complex information. Candidates must be comfortable working with confidential materials and handling documents that may contain sensitive project, organizational, or account information. 2. Support Carbon Program Administration and Operations Program Operations staff will also support the day-to-day administration and operation of a growing number of emission reduction and removal projects. This may involve: Supporting the implementation of carbon crediting programs. Helping manage project processes. Coordinating administrative activities. Ensuring that projects move through the appropriate program procedures. Supporting communication and documentation requirements. Helping maintain accurate records and operational information. As the organization continues to manage a growing portfolio of climate projects, the Program Operations team plays an important role in ensuring that processes are efficient, accurate, and consistent. 3. Provide Technical and Administrative Guidance Employees may provide guidance to accountholders and other users of the Climate Action Reserve’s programs and systems. This could include helping users understand: Program procedures. Documentation requirements. Carbon crediting processes. Protocol-related requirements. Administrative procedures. Project submission and verification processes. Strong communication skills are therefore essential. Candidates should be able to explain complex technical or administrative information clearly and professionally to different audiences. 4. Support Protocol Training Program Operations staff may also help deliver and provide training on the organization’s protocols. This could involve: Supporting training sessions. Helping explain carbon crediting protocols. Assisting project developers and verifiers in understanding program requirements. Preparing or supporting training materials. Responding to questions during training activities. This aspect of the role may be particularly suitable for candidates who enjoy knowledge-sharing, professional presentations, technical communication, and working with stakeholders. 5. Participate in Audits and Verification Oversight The role may occasionally involve conducting audits of verification bodies to assess whether they are adhering to programmatic requirements. This responsibility can include: Reviewing verification processes. Assessing compliance with program requirements. Observing verification activities. Supporting audits of verification bodies. Traveling to project locations when required. The position therefore combines remote work with periodic travel. Employees may travel to project sites and events for approximately five to six weeks per year in the United States. Who Can Apply? The Climate Action Reserve is seeking candidates from different professional backgrounds who demonstrate an interest in carbon markets, carbon crediting, carbon accounting, climate action, or related areas. Applicants may demonstrate this interest through: Professional employment. Academic studies. Research. Co-curricular activities. Volunteer experience. Climate-related projects. Environmental or sustainability initiatives. Experience with carbon accounting or emissions-related work. The role is open at different career levels, making it potentially suitable for both entry-level candidates and experienced professionals. Analyst Position The Analyst position is designed for entry-level candidates and does not require prior professional work experience. This may be suitable for applicants who: Have recently completed an undergraduate degree. Are beginning a career in climate action or carbon markets. Have academic or co-curricular experience related to carbon markets or environmental issues. Demonstrate strong analytical and organizational abilities. Have an interest in learning about carbon crediting and greenhouse gas accounting. Associate Position Applicants for the Associate level are generally expected to have at least two years of professional work experience. However, the experience requirement may be reduced for candidates with direct experience in responsibilities relevant to the role. Relevant experience may include work involving: Carbon markets. Carbon crediting. Carbon accounting. Environmental programs. Climate policy. Project operations. Technical documentation review. Compliance. Auditing. Program administration. Stakeholder guidance. Senior Associate Position Applicants for the Senior Associate level are generally expected to have at least five years of professional work experience. The required experience may be reduced for candidates who have particularly relevant experience in the specific responsibilities of the position. Senior-level candidates should be capable of working with a higher level of autonomy and may be expected to take on more complex responsibilities within Program Operations. Essential Qualifications Applicants should meet the following requirements: Professional Experience The required experience depends on the level of the position: Analyst: No prior professional work experience is required. Associate: Generally requires at least two years of professional experience. Senior Associate: Generally requires at least five years of professional experience. Candidates with highly relevant experience in the specific responsibilities of the position may be considered even if they do not meet the standard experience thresholds. Interest in Carbon Markets and Climate Action Applicants must demonstrate an interest in one or more of the following areas: Carbon markets. Carbon crediting. Carbon accounting. Greenhouse gas emissions reduction. Greenhouse gas removals. Climate change mitigation. Environmental sustainability. Climate policy. Market-based climate solutions. This interest may come from professional experience, academic studies, research, extracurricular activities, or other relevant experiences. Strong Attention to Detail The role involves reviewing project documentation, verification materials, and other important information. Applicants should therefore have: Excellent attention to detail. Strong organizational abilities. The ability to identify errors and inconsistencies. The ability to work carefully with confidential materials. A commitment to accuracy. Strong Written Communication Skills Successful candidates must be able to communicate clearly in writing. This may involve: Writing professional emails. Preparing reports. Reviewing documentation. Providing guidance to stakeholders. Documenting project-related information. Communicating technical or administrative requirements. Undergraduate Degree Applicants must have an undergraduate degree. However, candidates with educational backgrounds related to environmental studies, climate science, sustainability, economics, public policy, political science, business, engineering, accounting, finance, data analysis, or other relevant areas may be able to demonstrate particularly relevant knowledge depending on their experience. Software and Artificial Intelligence Skills Applicants must be proficient in standard workplace software such as: Microsoft Word. Microsoft Excel. Microsoft Outlook. Other standard office and productivity tools. The organization also expects candidates to have proficiency with artificial intelligence tools. Applicants who can demonstrate practical experience using AI tools to improve research, analysis, productivity, document preparation, data organization, or workflow efficiency may be able to strengthen their applications. Professional English Proficiency Applicants must have professional proficiency in English. Strong English communication skills are important because the role involves written communication, technical guidance, stakeholder engagement, documentation review, and training-related activities. Preferred Qualification A graduate or professional degree is preferred. Although this qualification is not listed as essential, candidates with relevant postgraduate education may be considered favorably. Potentially relevant graduate-level backgrounds may include: Environmental management. Climate change. Sustainability. Environmental policy. Public policy. Economics. Business administration. Accounting. Finance. Data analysis. Energy. Engineering. Law. Other related disciplines. Remote Work and Travel Requirements This is a full-time remote position based in the United States. Although the position is remote, it is not entirely travel-free. Employees may be required to travel periodically to: Project sites. Professional events. Verification activities. Other relevant locations. The expected travel requirement is approximately five to six weeks per year in the United States . Candidates should therefore be comfortable working remotely while also being available for periodic professional travel. Work Authorization Requirement A major eligibility requirement for this opportunity is legal authorization to work in the United States. Applicants must be able to maintain legal authorization to work in the United States for the duration of their employment. The Climate Action Reserve does not: Sponsor work visas. Provide visa sponsorship. Cover relocation expenses. Therefore, international applicants who do not already have legal authorization to work in the United States may not be eligible for employment under this vacancy. Applicants should carefully evaluate their work authorization status before applying. Salary The salary depends on the level at which the successful candidate is hired. Senior Associate Salary range: $70,304 to $90,235 per year New hires are typically placed between: $70,304 and $80,270 Associate Salary range: $60,503 to $77,655 per year New hires are typically placed between: $60,503 and $69,079 Analyst Salary range: $52,068 to $66,829 per year New hires are typically placed between: $52,068 and $59,448 The final salary offered may depend on factors such as: Relevant professional experience. Qualifications. Level of responsibility. Knowledge of carbon markets and related fields. Skills and expertise. Benefits Package The position includes a comprehensive benefits package. Benefits include: Medical insurance. Dental insurance. Vision insurance. Retirement contributions. Paid annual leave. Other forms of paid leave. A monthly stipend to support phone and internet costs. The benefits package is designed to support employees working in a full-time professional capacity. How to Apply Interested candidates should prepare the following application materials: 1. Cover Letter Applicants must submit a one-page cover letter . The cover letter should ideally explain: Why you are interested in the Climate Action Reserve. Why you are interested in carbon markets and climate action. Your relevant professional, academic, or co-curricular experience. The specific skills you can bring to the Program Operations team. Why your experience is suitable for the Analyst, Associate, or Senior Associate level. Candidates should tailor their cover letter specifically to the organization and role rather than submitting a generic application. 2. Resume Applicants must submit a resume of no more than two pages . The resume should clearly highlight: Education. Relevant professional experience. Carbon market or climate-related experience. Project operations experience. Documentation review. Audit or compliance experience. Stakeholder communication. Technical or administrative skills. Microsoft Office proficiency. Artificial intelligence tools and relevant digital skills. Candidates should ensure that their resumes are clear, well-organized, and focused on the requirements of the position. Application Email Applications should be submitted by email to: operations@climateactionreserve.org Applicants should attach their one-page cover letter and maximum two-page resume. For more information on this job, visit climate action reserve website HERE For more remote jobs visit OFY Website HERE Important Application Tips Candidates interested in this opportunity should consider the following: Tailor Your Application Do not submit a generic resume and cover letter. Emphasize experiences that demonstrate your ability to: Review information carefully. Manage processes. Work with confidential documents. Communicate with stakeholders. Use standard office software. Work with AI tools. Understand climate-related issues. Learn and apply technical requirements. Highlight Transferable Skills Even if you have not worked directly in carbon markets, relevant transferable experience may be valuable. For example, experience in: Project administration. Research. Policy analysis. Compliance. Auditing. Data analysis. Program management. Environmental work. Technical documentation. Stakeholder engagement. may help demonstrate your ability to succeed in the position. Demonstrate Your Interest in Climate Action The organization specifically seeks candidates who can demonstrate an interest in carbon markets, carbon crediting, or carbon accounting. Applicants should clearly explain how their background, education, work, research, or activities connect to climate action. Be Clear About Your Work Authorization Because the position requires legal authorization to work in the United States and does not offer visa sponsorship, applicants should confirm that they meet this requirement before submitting their application. Application Deadline The vacancy announcement provided does not specify a closing date or application deadline . Applicants are therefore encouraged to apply as soon as possible and should verify whether the position remains open before submitting their application. Why This Opportunity Is Significant The global transition toward a lower-carbon economy is creating growing demand for professionals with knowledge of climate action, carbon markets, environmental programs, sustainability, and emissions accounting. This opportunity offers successful candidates the chance to work directly with carbon crediting programs and contribute to systems designed to quantify and verify climate-related outcomes. Conclusion The Climate Action Reserve’s Program Operations vacancies offer opportunities for professionals at different stages of their careers to contribute to climate action and carbon market operations. Candidates should have an undergraduate degree, strong attention to detail, excellent written communication skills, proficiency with standard workplace software and artificial intelligence tools, and a demonstrated interest in carbon markets, carbon crediting, carbon accounting, or related climate action fields. While Analyst roles are suitable for entry-level candidates, Associate and Senior Associate positions require progressively greater professional experience. The positions are full-time and remote, but applicants must have legal authorization to work in the United States and should be prepared for approximately five to six weeks of travel per year. Interested candidates should submit a one-page cover letter and a resume of no more than two pages to operations@climateactionreserve.org . Since no specific application deadline is stated, qualified candidates are encouraged to apply promptly while the vacancy remains available. title: Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026–2027: $125,000 Paid AI Research Fellowship for Graduate Students, PhDs, and Postdoctoral Researchers Worldwide
summary: Applications are now open for the Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026–2027 , a prestigious one-year, fully funded research fellowship designed for exceptional graduate students, recent PhD graduates, and postdoctoral researchers who are passionate about advancing frontier machine learning research with real-world scientific impact. The fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity to work alongside leading experts in artificial intelligence, biology, robotics, and scientific research while tackling some of the most challenging problems in machine learning and scientific automation. Successful fellows will receive $125,000 in annual compensation , comprehensive benefits, access to cutting-edge computational resources, and the opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking research that aims to transform how scientific work is understood, evaluated, and reproduced. Based primarily in the Boston/Cambridge area, the fellowship welcomes applications from talented researchers around the world and provides visa support for selected international fellows. About the Transfyr AI Fellowship The Transfyr AI Fellowship was established to address one of the biggest challenges facing modern science—the absence of a comprehensive observability layer that captures how scientific work actually happens. Scientific discovery often involves much more than published papers or laboratory protocols. It includes failed experiments, operator expertise, contextual decision-making, noisy instruments, repeated attempts, and numerous tacit processes that are rarely documented. Transfyr is building what it describes as the world s largest multimodal dataset of scientific execution, allowing artificial intelligence systems to understand science as it is performed in real-world laboratory environments rather than relying solely on polished publications and benchmark datasets. The fellowship provides participants with the opportunity to work directly on these frontier challenges. Fellowship Overview The programme is a full-time research fellowship lasting 12 months . Selected fellows will: Lead an independent research project. Work with real multimodal scientific datasets. Collaborate closely with scientists, engineers, operators, and AI researchers. Build prototypes and novel machine learning systems. Design new evaluation frameworks. Produce publishable research or demonstration-quality technical outputs. The fellowship is intended for individuals who are interested in pushing the boundaries of machine learning while solving practical scientific problems. Research Areas Fellows will contribute to one or more frontier AI research challenges. 1. Multimodal Reasoning Researchers will develop AI models capable of integrating multiple sources of scientific information. Physical-World AI This research area bridges robotics and artificial intelligence. Projects include: Robotics Embodied AI Demonstration learning Policy evaluation Transfer learning 7. Biosecurity and Bio-Risk Observability Fellows may develop AI systems capable of improving laboratory biosecurity through: Workflow monitoring Capability assessment Autonomous vulnerability detection Safety-critical containment systems 8.
