title: Canvas Home Small Grants 2026 for Artisan Groups in Developing Countries | Up to $1,500 in Funding for Craft Businesses and Cooperatives
summary: Artisan groups and craft-producing organizations in developing countries now have an exciting opportunity to access financial support through the Canvas Home Small Grants 2026 program. Administered by HANDMADE to MARKET (HtoM) , a division of Creative Learning , this initiative is designed to strengthen artisan enterprises by providing funding for materials, equipment, training, marketing, and other business development activities. The program offers grants of up to $1,500 to eligible artisan cooperatives, community-based organizations, and small craft businesses seeking to expand employment opportunities, improve production, preserve traditional crafts, and generate sustainable income. If your artisan organization is looking for financial assistance to scale production, improve product quality, access new markets, or strengthen business operations, this grant could provide the support needed to grow sustainably. Application Deadline: August 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). About HANDMADE to MARKET (HtoM) HANDMADE to MARKET (HtoM) is a division of Creative Learning , a Washington, D.C.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering artisan businesses around the world. The organization works with artisan communities by providing: Access to international markets Business development training Eco-effective production methods Design innovation Marketing support Strategic partnerships Community-building initiatives Through these efforts, HtoM seeks to promote sustainable economic growth while preserving cultural heritage and improving the livelihoods of artisan communities worldwide. Canvas Home Small Grants 2026 Overview The Canvas Home Small Grants program exists to strengthen established artisan groups by helping them obtain the resources necessary to improve production, increase sales, and create more employment opportunities. Each successful applicant may receive funding of up to $1,500 . Rather than supporting individual artisans or new businesses, the program focuses on strengthening existing craft-producing organizations that already have an established structure and are ready to grow. The grants help artisan groups become more competitive while preserving traditional craftsmanship and promoting environmentally responsible production practices. Grant Value Successful applicants may receive grants of up to $1,500 . Funding is intended to help artisan organizations: Expand employment opportunities Increase production capacity Improve product quality Reach new markets Increase income generation Strengthen long-term sustainability Types of Grants Available Applicants may apply for only one of the following grant categories. 1. Materials, Tools, Equipment, and Instruction Grant This funding category supports improvements in craft production through the purchase of essential resources and technical support. Eligible activities include: Purchasing raw materials Buying specialized craft tools Purchasing production equipment Establishing raw material banks Creating shared tool banks Setting up centralized artisan workshops Funding technical assistance Hiring trainers for capacity-building workshops Product design training Marketing training Business management training Technical skills development Purchasing digital cameras Internet connectivity costs Website development The goal is to improve production efficiency while enhancing artisans technical and business capabilities. 2. Marketing Support Grant This category is designed for artisan groups that already have established production systems and existing sales. The grant helps organizations expand into new markets and attract additional customers. Funding may be used for: Craft fair participation Exhibition stand costs Display shelving Marketing brochures Product catalogs Promotional materials Market expansion initiatives Launching new products Entering new domestic or international markets This category is ideal for organizations ready to grow beyond their current customer base. Eligibility Criteria To qualify, applicants must satisfy all eligibility requirements. Eligible Applicants The program primarily supports established craft-producing organizations such as: Artisan cooperatives Community-based organizations Small artisan businesses Craft-producing groups The primary focus is on organizations located in developing countries . Eligible Craft Products Supported products must: Be handmade Have artistic value Serve a functional purpose Reflect cultural significance Applicants must submit photographs demonstrating the products. Recommendation Letter Requirement Every application must include a: Signed recommendation letter Dated recommendation letter The recommendation should come from an organization familiar with the applicant s work. Suitable organizations include: Previous funding organizations Development partners National craft organizations International nonprofit organizations Organizations with direct knowledge of the artisan group The recommendation must be credible and independently written. Applications without a signed and dated recommendation letter will automatically be rejected. Important notes include: Letters from previous Canvas Home Small Grant recipients are not accepted. Recommendation letters must not be purchased. Recommenders must not charge fees. Language Requirements Applications must: Be written entirely in English Use only U.S. Dollar (USD) currency Photo Requirements Applicants must submit: At least five recent photographs Photos taken within the previous twelve months The photographs should clearly showcase the artisan products. Follow-Up Reporting Requirement Grant recipients agree to submit a follow-up report approximately six months after receiving the grant. This report helps HtoM evaluate: Grant impact Business growth Project implementation Outcomes achieved Banking Requirements Applicants must have access to a bank account capable of receiving: International wire transfers U.S. Dollar (USD) payments Recipients are responsible for: Currency conversion fees Bank transaction charges Any costs associated with receiving grant funds Selection Priorities Because funding is limited, HtoM gives preference to applications that: Provide detailed project explanations Include strong justifications for funding Benefit large numbers of artisans Promote cultural preservation Demonstrate environmental sustainability Clearly explain financial need Present a realistic implementation plan Identify specific markets for finished products Have reliable communication contacts Can provide regular project updates Have never previously received a Canvas Home Small Grant Although previous recipients may apply, first-time applicants receive preference. Activities Not Supported Canvas Home Small Grants will not fund: Individual artisans New craft start-up projects Building trade projects Industrial or household products lacking handmade artistic value Salaries Staff wages Travel expenses Vehicle purchases Environmentally harmful production practices Projects using uncertified timber from sensitive ecosystems Independent grant writers working without close relationships with artisan groups Designers or exporters who do not directly work with artisans Applicants should carefully review these exclusions before applying. Application Timeline The application process follows the schedule below. Activity Date Applications Open July 15, 2026 Application Deadline August 17, 2026 (11:59 PM EST) Internal Review August 2026 Award Notifications September 2026 Grant Payments First week of October 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. Application Process Applicants should complete every section of the online application carefully. The review process includes two stages. Stage One HtoM staff verify: Eligibility Required documents Completeness of the application Staff do not evaluate project quality during this stage. Stage Two Eligible applications are forwarded to an independent review committee responsible for selecting grant recipients. Applicants will receive notification by email whether they are selected or not. Successful applicants will receive funding after confirming their banking information. Required Documents Applicants should prepare: Completed online application Signed recommendation letter Five recent product photographs Supporting documentation requested within the application Preparing these materials before beginning the application can make the submission process easier. How to Apply Interested organizations should submit their applications through the official Canvas Home Small Grants Application Form . Applicants are encouraged to: Preview all application questions before starting. Review the Canvas Home Small Grants Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ). Prepare all required supporting documents. Create a free Jotform account to save progress and return later if necessary. Submit the completed application before the deadline. Applicants unable to complete the online application due to technical issues may request a PDF application by contacting: RachelL@creativelearning.org However, PDF submissions are accepted only with prior approval from HANDMADE to MARKET. For technical support during the application process, applicants should also contact the same email address. APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply The Canvas Home Small Grants Program provides much more than financial assistance. It enables artisan organizations to: Increase production capacity Preserve traditional craftsmanship Improve product quality Strengthen business operations Reach international markets Build sustainable livelihoods Create employment opportunities Promote environmentally responsible production Expand income-generating opportunities Strengthen community development For artisan organizations seeking practical funding to support growth while preserving cultural heritage, this grant represents an excellent opportunity. Visit HERE to learn more about the Canvas Home Small Grants 2026 for Artisan Groups in Developing Countries Important Deadline Application Deadline: August 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). Applications submitted after the deadline or missing required documentation will not be considered. Conclusion The Canvas Home Small Grants 2026 program offers a valuable opportunity for established artisan organizations in developing countries to strengthen their businesses through targeted financial support. With grants of up to $1,500 , eligible groups can invest in better materials, equipment, technical training, marketing initiatives, and business development activities that improve productivity and expand market opportunities. Beyond financial assistance, the program emphasizes cultural preservation, environmental sustainability, and long-term community development, making it an important initiative for artisan groups committed to creating lasting economic impact. Interested organizations should begin preparing their applications, recommendation letters, product photographs, and supporting documents early to ensure they submit a complete application before the August 17, 2026 deadline. title: European Commission OCT Youth Network 2026–2027: Fully Funded One-Year Leadership Opportunity for Young People from Overseas Countries and Territories
summary: The European Commission has officially opened applications for the 2026–2027 Overseas Countries and Territories (OCT) Youth Network , offering an exceptional one-year leadership and learning opportunity for young people from the 13 Overseas Countries and Territories associated with the European Union. Designed to strengthen the partnership between the European Union and the Overseas Countries and Territories, the OCT Youth Network equips young leaders with knowledge about European institutions, policymaking, sustainable development, and international cooperation while creating lasting connections among youth from different territories. Participants will embark on an engaging one-year journey that combines study visits, leadership dialogues, networking events, online learning sessions, and participation in international forums. The programme empowers young people to represent the voices of their communities while contributing fresh ideas to the future of the OCT-EU Partnership. If you are passionate about leadership, international affairs, youth participation, diplomacy, public policy, sustainable development, or European cooperation, this programme offers an invaluable opportunity to broaden your horizons and become part of an influential international youth community. What is the OCT Youth Network? The Overseas Countries and Territories Youth Network is a prestigious initiative established by the European Commission to strengthen engagement between young people living in Overseas Countries and Territories and the European Union. The Network consists of 25 carefully selected young people between the ages of 20 and 28 , representing all thirteen Overseas Countries and Territories associated with the EU. Since its launch in 2022 , the programme has become one of the flagship youth engagement initiatives supporting stronger collaboration between the European Union and its Overseas Countries and Territories. Rather than being a traditional training programme, the Network serves as a platform where young people actively contribute ideas, exchange experiences, influence dialogue, and represent youth perspectives within the OCT-EU Partnership. Members spend an entire year participating in collaborative learning activities while building professional relationships with policymakers, EU institutions, fellow youth leaders, and experts from across the territories. Purpose of the OCT Youth Network The initiative was created to increase youth participation in international cooperation and ensure that young voices play an important role in shaping the future of the OCT-EU Partnership. Its primary objectives include: Connecting young people from all 13 Overseas Countries and Territories. Building stronger relationships between OCT youth and European Union institutions. Increasing awareness and understanding of the European Union across the OCTs. Giving young people opportunities to contribute directly to important policy discussions. Promoting dialogue between youth and political decision-makers. Creating stronger links between OCT youth initiatives and other regional, national, and European youth programmes. Encouraging intercultural understanding among young people from diverse backgrounds. Supporting meaningful youth participation in sustainable development. What Participants Will Experience Successful applicants become members of a dynamic international network and participate in numerous educational and leadership activities throughout the year. The programme includes: 1. Study Visit to Brussels One of the highlights of the programme is a week-long study visit to Brussels , Belgium. During this visit, members will: Explore how European institutions function. Visit major EU institutions. Learn how European policies are developed. Meet European policymakers. Participate in interactive workshops. Engage in structured dialogue sessions. Exchange ideas with European leaders. Learn more about the OCT-EU Partnership. The Brussels experience gives participants firsthand exposure to European governance and international cooperation. 2. Online Learning Sessions Throughout the year, members participate in various virtual learning activities including: Interactive webinars. Capacity-building workshops. Educational seminars. Skills development sessions. Policy discussions. Expert presentations. These sessions deepen participants understanding of: European institutions International partnerships Sustainable development Youth participation Leadership Governance Public policy 3. Networking Opportunities Participants become part of a growing international youth community. Networking opportunities include: Connecting with youth leaders from all 13 OCTs. Building relationships with EU institutions. Meeting government representatives. Engaging with international organisations. Connecting with policymakers. Collaborating with experts and stakeholders. Building lifelong friendships and professional relationships. 4. Participation in International Events Network members participate in several prestigious international events. These may include: OCT-EU Forum Climate-related conferences European Youth events International policy dialogues High-level stakeholder meetings Participation allows young leaders to share perspectives from their territories while contributing to important international discussions. 5. Youth Representation Members play an active role in ensuring young people s voices are heard. They contribute by: Presenting youth recommendations. Participating in dialogue sessions. Co-leading discussions. Helping identify priorities for the Network. Sharing experiences from their territories. Promoting youth perspectives during high-level events. Benefits of Joining the OCT Youth Network Participants gain numerous academic, professional, and personal benefits throughout the programme. These include: One-year international leadership experience. Participation in a study visit to Brussels. Direct exposure to European institutions. Access to EU policymakers and decision-makers. Expanded international professional network. Opportunities to represent youth interests. Participation in international conferences and forums. Leadership development. Improved communication skills. Greater understanding of international cooperation. Cross-cultural learning experiences. Collaboration with young leaders from different territories. Enhanced knowledge of European governance. Personal growth and increased global awareness. Diversity and Inclusion The European Commission emphasizes diversity within the Network. The OCT Youth Network welcomes applicants from a broad range of backgrounds, including individuals with different: Educational qualifications. Professional experiences. Areas of expertise. Social backgrounds. Cultural identities. Personal interests. Economic circumstances. This diversity strengthens dialogue and promotes inclusive decision-making. History of the OCT Youth Network First Edition (2022–2023) The inaugural Network brought together 25 young people representing 10 Overseas Countries and Territories . One of its major achievements was the development of a Youth Declaration , which was presented during the OCT-EU Forum in Nouméa, New Caledonia in November 2022. The declaration highlighted young people s priorities regarding the OCT-EU Partnership. Second Edition (2023–2024) The second cohort included representatives from all 13 OCTs . Members participated in: Study visits to Brussels. Networking activities. Policy discussions. Cultural exchanges. A major achievement was the presentation of: A Youth Declaration. A photo exhibition. A video exhibition. These showcased the importance of cultural diversity and stronger exchanges between the OCTs and the European Union during the OCT-EU Forum held in Brussels in February 2024. Third Edition (2024–2025) The third cohort continued expanding the Network s impact. Highlights included: Structured dialogue with Younous Omarjee, Vice-President of the European Parliament responsible for OCT matters. Participation in the Climate Finance Forum in Brussels. Attendance at the European Youth Event in Strasbourg. Representation at the United Nations Ocean Conference in Nice. These experiences demonstrated the growing influence of OCT youth within international discussions. Why the European Union Created the OCT Youth Network The initiative reflects the European Union s increasing commitment to youth participation in global development. It aligns closely with the Youth Action Plan in EU External Action , adopted in October 2022. The Action Plan recognizes young people as key partners in building: Democratic societies. Inclusive communities. Peaceful societies. Sustainable development. Strong international partnerships. The OCT Youth Network is one practical way the European Union is turning this commitment into action. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the official European Commission application process. Interested candidates should carefully review the eligibility requirements and complete the application before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to prepare thoughtful responses that demonstrate: Leadership potential. Motivation. Interest in international cooperation. Commitment to representing young people from their territory. Enthusiasm for contributing to the OCT-EU Partnership. APPLY HERE Application Deadline 30 August 2026 (23:59 CEST) Late applications are not expected to be considered. Why You Should Apply The OCT Youth Network is much more than a youth programme—it is a gateway to international leadership, diplomacy, policymaking, and global collaboration. Participants gain unique access to European institutions, engage directly with policymakers, represent young people from their territories, and build lasting international friendships while contributing meaningfully to the future of the OCT-EU Partnership. For young people seeking to develop leadership skills, expand their international network, and play an active role in shaping youth engagement between the European Union and the Overseas Countries and Territories, this programme offers an exceptional platform for personal and professional growth. Visit HERE to learn more about the European Commission OCT Youth Network 2026–2027 Conclusion The European Commission s 2026–2027 Overseas Countries and Territories Youth Network presents an outstanding opportunity for ambitious young leaders from the 13 Overseas Countries and Territories associated with the European Union. Through a comprehensive one-year programme featuring study visits, online learning, policy engagement, international networking, and participation in prestigious global events, selected participants will gain invaluable knowledge, leadership experience, and lifelong professional connections. If you meet the eligibility requirements and are passionate about representing your community while contributing to the future of the OCT-EU Partnership, this is an opportunity not to miss. title: Leo’s Experimental Micrograntting Program 2026 | $10,000 Grants for Bold Ideas to Help Humanity Navigate AGI
summary: Have an ambitious idea that could genuinely help humanity navigate the future of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)? Leo s Experimental Microgranting Program offers a refreshing alternative to traditional funding by providing $10,000 microgrants with minimal bureaucracy and maximum flexibility. Unlike conventional grants that require lengthy proposals and institutional affiliations, this initiative encourages applicants to spend about an hour explaining a thoughtful idea. The emphasis is on originality, genuine reasoning, and ambitious thinking rather than polished grant-writing or impressive credentials. Leo s program is an experimental grantmaking initiative designed to discover unconventional projects that could contribute to ensuring AGI benefits humanity. About the Program The Experimental Microgranting Program is built around one simple principle: Actually try. Applicants are encouraged to submit thoughtful, ambitious proposals instead of incremental academic work or applications filled with buzzwords. Leo believes promising ideas can come from anyone and not only professors or established researchers wants to support projects that traditional grantmakers may overlook. The program is intentionally lightweight: Approximately one-hour application Maximum 1,000 words Minimal bureaucracy Flexible funding Fast, independent decision-making Grant Value Successful applicants receive: $10,000 USD Flexible funding Support for individuals, nonprofits, charities, or other entities Opportunity to reapply after project completion What Projects Are Being Funded? The program seeks projects that could positively influence humanity s future with AGI. Examples include: AI alignment research AI governance ideas Technical safety tools Educational initiatives Public awareness projects Novel research Policy work Community initiatives Experimental approaches with high upside Applicants are encouraged to justify how their proposal contributes to helping humanity navigate AGI. What Makes This Grant Different? Unlike many traditional grants, this program offers: Anonymous funder Flexible use of funding Learning is considered a successful outcome Supports unconventional ideas Values original thinking over credentials Minimal administrative burden The initiative itself is also an experiment and may evolve over time. Application Guidelines Applicants should carefully read the complete guidance before applying. Important expectations include: Spend around one hour preparing the application. Write clearly. Explain why the project matters. Avoid exaggerated claims. Avoid unnecessary buzzwords. Submit genuine work. Applications written or edited by AI will be rejected. Multiple ideas may be submitted separately. Leo specifically emphasizes that applications should reflect the applicant s own reasoning and writing. Eligibility The program welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds. Applicants do not need: Previous AI alignment experience Academic publications Prestigious university affiliations Extensive grant-writing experience Strong ideas and thoughtful reasoning matter far more than credentials. Funding Philosophy Rather than expecting every project to succeed, the program views experimentation as valuable. Even projects that produce negative results may still be considered successful if they generate meaningful learning. Once grant funds have been used, recipients may apply again by providing a progress update. Referral Bonus Applicants who refer others can receive a $100 referral bounty if the referred applicant is awarded a microgrant. Important Notes Applicants should note: Grants should not be used as credentials or endorsements. Leo may seek external reviewers. Grant decisions are highly selective. Funding availability is expected to support all successful applications. The program operates independently from Leo s employer. How to Apply Applicants should first read the complete guidance document before completing the application form. Application Form: https://tally.so/r/D4WlbR Questions: alignmentmicrogrants@gmail.com Conclusion Leo s Experimental Microgranting Program offers a refreshing alternative to traditional grant funding by placing trust in bold ideas, genuine reasoning, and intellectual curiosity rather than lengthy proposals or prestigious credentials. With a straightforward application process and flexible $10,000 funding, the program encourages individuals and organizations to pursue ambitious projects that could contribute to a safer and more beneficial future with Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Whether your proposal focuses on AI safety, governance, education, public engagement, technical research, or another innovative approach, this initiative welcomes unconventional thinking and recognizes that meaningful progress often begins with experimental ideas. Applicants are encouraged to write honestly, explain why their project matters, and demonstrate their own original thinking without relying on polished grant-writing or AI-generated content. If you have a well-considered idea that could help humanity navigate the opportunities and challenges of AGI, this microgrant program provides an excellent opportunity to secure funding and turn that vision into action. Be sure to read the full application guidance carefully before applying, follow all instructions, and submit your proposal through the official application form. Even if your project does not achieve every intended outcome, the program values learning and meaningful insights, making it an ideal opportunity for innovators who are willing to experiment, take thoughtful risks, and contribute to shaping a positive future for humanity. title: Methodology PhD Studentships in Maternity Disparities 2027 in the UK: Fully Funded NIHR PhD Opportunities for Researchers Passionate About Maternal Health Equity
summary: Persistent inequalities in maternity care continue to affect the health and wellbeing of women and babies across the United Kingdom. Addressing these disparities requires innovative research, skilled researchers, and multidisciplinary collaboration. To help build the next generation of experts in this critical field, the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC) has launched its Methodology PhD Studentships Competition for 2027. The Consortium is offering up to 13 fully funded PhD studentships across multiple universities within its UK-wide network. These studentships are designed to develop future research leaders who can generate evidence-based solutions that reduce inequalities before, during, and after pregnancy. This opportunity is particularly suitable for applicants with expertise in research methodologies such as statistics, health economics, implementation science, digital research, data science, trial design, co-production methods, and related disciplines who are passionate about improving maternal health outcomes. Whether you are an aspiring academic, healthcare professional, statistician, economist, data scientist, or researcher from another methodological background, this programme provides an exceptional opportunity to contribute to meaningful research while earning a fully funded doctoral degree. About the NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC) The Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC) is a major UK-wide collaboration established under the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) to address longstanding inequalities in maternity care. The Consortium brings together a diverse partnership of: Universities NHS Trusts Local councils Charities Industry partners Research organisations By combining expertise from these sectors, the Consortium aims to develop practical, evidence-based solutions that improve maternity outcomes for women and babies throughout pregnancy and beyond. The Consortium is committed to conducting inclusive research that reflects the experiences of diverse communities while ensuring that research findings lead to real improvements in healthcare services. Why This PhD Programme Matters Despite significant advances in healthcare, inequalities in maternity outcomes remain a major challenge in the UK. Certain communities continue to experience poorer maternal and neonatal outcomes due to social, economic, ethnic, and healthcare-related disparities. The Methodology PhD Studentships aim to strengthen research capacity by training specialists who can develop innovative research methods capable of addressing these complex issues. Successful students will become part of a national research community working towards improving maternal health through rigorous scientific investigation and interdisciplinary collaboration. Capacity Development Programme A central objective of the Maternity Disparities Consortium is to build sustainable research capacity across the United Kingdom. The Consortium s Capacity Development Programme seeks to: Develop the next generation of maternity disparities researchers. Build long-term expertise in methodological research. Strengthen the UK s maternity research workforce. Support future research leaders. Encourage collaboration across healthcare, academic, clinical, and community settings. Increase research participation from underrepresented disciplines. Promote inclusive research environments. Deliver lasting improvements in maternal healthcare. The programme also contributes to important UK government priorities, including: Women s Health Strategy for England. 10-Year Health Plan for England. Through this initiative, the Consortium hopes to create a stronger, more diverse workforce capable of delivering meaningful improvements in maternal healthcare for years to come. PhD Studentship Opportunities The Consortium will fund up to 13 PhD studentships , each based at one of the participating universities within the Consortium. Projects will focus on reducing maternity inequalities using advanced research methodologies. Additional research projects are expected to be announced throughout the recruitment period. Applicants are encouraged to review individual project descriptions before applying, as each project may have its own specific requirements. Research Areas Being Sought The Consortium is particularly interested in applicants with methodological expertise in areas such as: Health Economics Statistics Trial Design Data Science Digital Research Implementation Science Co-production Methods Applicants from other methodological backgrounds are also encouraged to apply if they believe their skills can contribute to maternity inequalities research. The Consortium values interdisciplinary approaches and welcomes innovative ideas that can improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. Programme Duration The PhD studentships will begin in: January 2027 Students may choose one of the following study options where available: Full-time study for up to 3 years. Part-time study (0.8 Whole-Time Equivalent) for up to 4 years. Some research projects may only be offered on a full-time basis. Applicants should carefully check the requirements for each individual project before submitting an application. Funding Package Successful applicants will receive a comprehensive funding package that includes: Full Tuition Fees The studentship covers: Full UK home tuition fees at the 2026/27 rate. Annual Tax-Free Stipend Students will receive a tax-free maintenance stipend at UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) rates: £21,805 per year for students based outside London. £23,805 per year for students based in London. These rates apply from 1 October 2026 . Research Support Funding Each award includes: £5,000 towards: Research expenses Training Travel Conference attendance Consumables This additional funding enables students to undertake high-quality research while developing their professional skills. International Student Information International applicants are welcome to apply. However, applicants should note that: The studentship only covers tuition fees at the UK Home rate. International students must independently secure funding to cover the difference between Home and Overseas tuition fees. Students must satisfy admission requirements set by their host university. Applicants are advised to consult the postgraduate admissions requirements of their chosen university before applying. Who Should Apply? The Consortium welcomes applications from individuals who are passionate about improving maternal health equity through high-quality research. Applicants should have methodological knowledge or experience relevant to one or more of the research areas being supported. The Consortium is especially interested in individuals who can contribute fresh perspectives and innovative research approaches. Applicants from diverse academic and professional backgrounds are encouraged to demonstrate how their previous experience will strengthen maternity inequalities research. Where this is not immediately apparent, applicants should clearly explain in their cover letter how their disciplinary expertise is relevant to their proposed PhD project. APPLY HERE Commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion The Consortium is committed to creating an inclusive, supportive and caring research environment. Applications are particularly encouraged from: People from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds. People living with disabilities. Individuals with neurodivergent conditions. People with long-term health requirements. Applicants of all genders. Applicants of all ages. Applicants of all beliefs. By promoting diversity within its research community, the Consortium aims to produce research that better reflects the populations it serves. Why You Should Consider Applying This studentship offers numerous benefits, including: Fully funded doctoral study. Tax-free annual living allowance. Additional research funding. Opportunities to collaborate with leading UK universities and NHS organisations. Participation in nationally significant health research. Access to multidisciplinary research expertise. Professional development and advanced research training. Opportunities to become a future leader in maternal health research. Contribution to reducing inequalities affecting women and babies. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, applicants should remember to: Review individual PhD project descriptions. Confirm eligibility with the host university. Check postgraduate admission requirements. Prepare a strong cover letter explaining their methodological expertise. Demonstrate how their experience aligns with maternity disparities research. Verify funding arrangements if applying as an international student. Deadline No application deadline has been announced yet. Applicants are encouraged to monitor the Consortium s official announcements regularly, as additional PhD projects will continue to be added and application timelines may vary by host university. Visit HERE to learn more about the Methodology PhD Studentships in Maternity Disparities 2027 in the UK Conclusion The NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium Methodology PhD Studentships 2027 represent an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers who want to make a meaningful contribution to maternal health equity. With up to 13 fully funded doctoral positions, generous financial support, and access to a nationwide network of leading universities, NHS Trusts, councils, charities, and industry partners, this programme provides an exceptional platform for developing advanced research skills while addressing one of the UK s most important public health challenges. The Consortium is not only investing in doctoral education but also building a diverse and inclusive research community capable of delivering long-term improvements in maternity care. If you have expertise in research methodology and a passion for improving outcomes for women and babies, this programme offers an excellent opportunity to develop your academic career while creating lasting social impact. title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026: Fully Funded Research Fellowships in Europe for International PhD Researchers
summary: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 are now open for applications, offering one of the world s most prestigious and competitive funding opportunities for postdoctoral researchers. Funded under the European Union s Horizon Europe Programme , these fellowships are designed to support outstanding researchers who wish to conduct high-quality research abroad, develop new skills, expand international collaborations, and advance their academic or non-academic careers. The programme encourages international mobility and interdisciplinary research while strengthening Europe s research and innovation ecosystem. Whether you are looking to move within Europe, relocate to Europe from another region of the world, or gain international experience outside Europe before returning, the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships provide generous financial support and access to world-class research environments. Application Deadline: 9 September 2026 (17:00 CEST) What are the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Postdoctoral Fellowships? The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) are among the flagship funding programmes of the European Commission that support researcher mobility, training, and career development. The Postdoctoral Fellowships (PFs) specifically target researchers who already hold a PhD and are looking to: Develop independent research careers Conduct research in another country Learn new scientific techniques Build interdisciplinary expertise Strengthen international research collaborations Gain exposure to both academic and non-academic sectors Improve long-term career prospects Rather than simply funding a research project, the programme focuses on developing the researcher through international experience, advanced training, networking opportunities, and career progression. Postdoctoral Fellowships in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme Why Apply for the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships? The fellowship provides far more than financial support. It enables researchers to become internationally competitive while working with leading universities, research institutes, companies, SMEs, and innovation organizations. Successful fellows benefit from: Fully funded research positions International mobility opportunities Career development support Advanced research training Cross-sector collaboration Networking with leading scientists Improved employability International research experience Opportunities to work in both academic and industry settings Types of MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships The programme offers two distinct fellowship schemes , allowing researchers to choose the pathway that best fits their career goals. 1. European Postdoctoral Fellowships European Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers who wish to carry out research in: European Union (EU) Member States, or Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Researchers may: Move from one European country to another Relocate from anywhere in the world to Europe Duration The fellowship lasts: 1–2 years Who can apply? Researchers of any nationality are eligible to apply, provided they satisfy the eligibility requirements. 2. Global Postdoctoral Fellowships Global Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers wishing to gain experience outside Europe before returning. The fellowship includes two phases: Outgoing Phase Researchers spend: 1–2 years At a host organisation located in a non-associated Third Country outside Europe. Return Phase Researchers then complete: A mandatory 1-year return phase At an organisation located in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Total Duration 2–3 years Who can apply? Only researchers who are: Nationals of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries, or Long-term residents of those countries. Have a look at the Postdoctoral Fellowships page and key resources for an introduction to the scheme’s characteristics and opportunities. Consult the MSCA Work Programme and annexes for all details about the call conditions. Additional Mobility Opportunities Both European and Global Fellowships may include: Short-Term Secondments Researchers may undertake secondments almost anywhere in the world to: Collaborate with external institutions Access specialist facilities Develop new research techniques Strengthen international partnerships For Global Fellowships, secondments cannot occur during the mandatory return phase. Non-Academic Placements To encourage collaboration beyond universities, fellows may receive additional support for placements lasting up to: 6 months These placements must take place at the end of the fellowship in a non-academic organisation based in: EU Member States Horizon Europe Associated Countries Examples include: Companies SMEs Government organisations NGOs Innovation centres Research-based industries Research Areas Supported One of the strengths of the MSCA programme is that it welcomes proposals from all academic disciplines . Eligible fields include, but are not limited to: Natural Sciences Engineering Technology Computer Science Artificial Intelligence Medical Sciences Life Sciences Agriculture Environmental Sciences Climate Change Mathematics Economics Education Humanities Arts Social Sciences Law Business Public Policy Research covered under the Euratom Research and Training Programme is also eligible, subject to additional nationality requirements. Who Can Apply? Applicants must submit their proposal jointly with an eligible host organisation. Host organisations may include: Universities Research institutes Businesses Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) Public organisations Private organisations Innovation centres Other eligible institutions located in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all programme requirements. 1. Hold a PhD Applicants must: Have been awarded a PhD before the application deadline. Applicants who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally received their degree are also eligible. 2. Research Experience Applicants must have: No more than 8 years of research experience following the award of their PhD. The following periods do not count toward the eight-year limit: Career breaks Time spent outside research Certain periods spent conducting research outside Europe (for eligible reintegrating researchers) 3. Mobility Rule Applicants must not have: Lived, Worked, Studied, or Carried out their main activity in the host country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the application deadline. This mobility requirement is one of the programme s defining eligibility criteria. 4. Resubmission Restriction Beginning with the 2026 call , applications that scored below 80% during the previous year s evaluation are subject to resubmission restrictions. Seal of Excellence Applicants whose proposals score: 85% or higher but cannot be funded due to budget limitations will receive a Seal of Excellence . This prestigious recognition demonstrates that the proposal met high-quality standards and may improve opportunities to obtain funding from other sources. What Does the Fellowship Funding Cover? The fellowship provides comprehensive financial support throughout the project. The beneficiary organisation receives EU funding to employ the researcher for the full fellowship period. Funding includes: Researcher Allowances Researchers receive: Living allowance Mobility allowance Where applicable, additional support is available through: Family allowance Long-term leave allowance Special needs allowance Institutional Support Additional funding is provided for: Research activities Scientific training Networking activities Project management Indirect institutional costs This ensures researchers have access to the resources needed to successfully complete their projects. How to Apply Applications are submitted jointly by: The researcher The host organisation The proposal is submitted by the host institution through the European Commission s Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal . APPLY NOW Steps to Apply Applicants should: Identify a suitable host organisation. Contact a potential supervisor. Develop a research proposal jointly. Confirm eligibility requirements. Prepare all required documents. Submit the proposal before the deadline. Start preparing your application to an open funding call published on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal Finding a Host Organisation Researchers can identify host institutions through: Existing academic networks Professional contacts Universities Research institutes Euraxess hosting offers Other international research job portals Many organisations publish expressions of interest seeking researchers for specific research topics. Check the list of hosting offers (expressions of interest) published on Euraxess Documents Available for Applicants The European Commission provides several resources to help applicants prepare competitive proposals. These include: MSCA Work Programme General Annexes Guide for Applicants Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Application Forms Evaluation Forms Guidelines for calculating the 8-year research experience Self-assessment tool Online application manuals For more information on the application and evaluation process and contact points for further guidance visit our page on how to apply visit the European Research Executive Agency website Responsibilities of the Host Organisation If awarded funding, the host institution will: Recruit the researcher Supervise the fellowship Provide research facilities Deliver training Support networking opportunities Arrange secondments where appropriate Submit the application on behalf of the researcher Why This Fellowship Stands Out The MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships are widely regarded as one of Europe s most prestigious research funding programmes because they combine: International mobility Career development Scientific excellence Cross-disciplinary collaboration Industry engagement Comprehensive funding High-quality research training Global networking opportunities Researchers gain access to world-leading institutions while developing skills that significantly enhance future academic and professional careers. Important Deadline Application Deadline: 9 September 2026 (17:00 CEST) Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing well in advance, as developing a strong proposal requires close collaboration with a host organisation and sufficient time to prepare all supporting documents. Conclusion The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 represent an exceptional opportunity for PhD holders seeking to elevate their research careers through international mobility, interdisciplinary collaboration, and advanced professional development. By supporting researchers across all disciplines and promoting partnerships between academia and industry, the programme helps cultivate the next generation of global research leaders. Whether you aspire to conduct groundbreaking research in Europe, gain international experience abroad before returning to Europe, or expand your professional network across sectors, the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships provide the funding, mentorship, and institutional support needed to achieve those ambitions. Eligible researchers are encouraged to identify a suitable host institution, prepare a competitive proposal, and submit their application before the 9 September 2026 deadline. Visit the OFY website for more fellowship opportunities. title: Workday Foundation Human Connection Microgrant Program 2026: Apply for Up to $10,000 to Build Stronger, More Connected Communities
summary: In today s increasingly digital world, people are more connected through technology than ever before. Yet, paradoxically, loneliness and social isolation continue to rise across all age groups. Recognizing this growing global challenge, the Workday Foundation has launched the Human Connection Microgrant Program 2026 , an innovative funding opportunity designed to support nonprofit organizations that create meaningful, joyful, and in-person community experiences. Through grants of up to $10,000 USD , the foundation aims to empower grassroots organizations, charities, and nonprofits to develop projects that bring neighbors together, strengthen relationships, reduce loneliness, and foster long-lasting community connections. If your organization is passionate about building stronger communities through shared experiences, this grant could provide the financial support needed to turn your ideas into reality. About the Workday Foundation Human Connection Microgrant Program The Workday Foundation Human Connection Microgrant Program is a new initiative dedicated to investing in in-real-life (IRL) human connection . Rather than funding traditional service delivery alone, the program supports creative community projects where human connection is intentionally designed into every aspect of the experience . The foundation believes that joyful social interactions create what it calls joyful feedback loops. These positive experiences encourage participants to return, invite others, and gradually build stronger, healthier, and more connected neighborhoods. The program recognizes that genuine relationships cannot always be built online. Instead, they flourish when people gather face-to-face, share experiences, and develop trust over time. Why the Program Matters Research continues to show alarming trends in loneliness around the world: One in six adults globally reports experiencing loneliness. One in three adolescents experiences loneliness. Communities are seeing fewer opportunities for spontaneous in-person interactions. Modern lifestyles increasingly reduce opportunities for neighbors to meet naturally. Several factors have contributed to this trend, including: Remote work Online learning Smartphones Social media Streaming entertainment Delivery services Self-checkout systems Reduced use of public gathering spaces Although technology has made communication easier, it has also reduced opportunities for meaningful face-to-face relationships. The Workday Foundation believes communities become healthier when people intentionally create spaces where neighbors can meet, interact, build friendships, and develop trust. Program Vision The Human Connection Microgrant Program seeks to fund projects that: Create opportunities for genuine in-person interactions. Build lasting friendships among neighbors. Encourage trust and belonging. Reduce loneliness. Inspire continued participation through enjoyable experiences. Strengthen neighborhoods one connection at a time. The foundation is particularly interested in projects where social connection is the primary purpose , rather than a secondary outcome. Types of Projects the Grant Will Support The Workday Foundation welcomes a wide variety of creative ideas that help people connect. Examples include: 1. Community Block Parties Organizations may organize neighborhood block parties that encourage residents to meet, socialize, and celebrate together. These gatherings should be: Welcoming Inclusive Easy to attend Designed for all ages 2. Community Potlucks and Cultural Celebrations Projects can include: Shared meals Cultural festivals Seasonal celebrations Story-sharing events Food exchange programs These activities allow people from different backgrounds to connect through food, traditions, and conversation. 3. Creative Community Projects The foundation encourages artistic experiences that naturally bring people together, including: Public murals Neighborhood art installations Storytelling walks Music sessions Community choirs Line dancing classes Open creative workshops 4. Games and Recreational Activities Shared play can become an effective tool for community building. Examples include: Board game nights Trivia competitions Neighborhood scavenger hunts Community sports Family game festivals 5. Volunteer and Service Projects Organizations may organize projects where neighbors work together toward a common goal, such as: Community cleanups Park improvement initiatives Neighborhood beautification Local volunteer events These activities strengthen relationships while improving communities. 6. Intergenerational Programs The grant encourages activities that connect people of different generations. Projects may involve: Youth Adults Seniors Examples include: Story-sharing sessions Community gardening Mentorship activities Shared learning events 7. Outdoor Community Activities Outdoor recreation provides another opportunity for meaningful interaction. Eligible ideas include: Hiking groups Camping events Walking clubs Run clubs Outdoor games Nature exploration programs. What Makes a Strong Project? Successful proposals should clearly demonstrate how their activities will: Build stronger social relationships. Create welcoming environments. Encourage participation from people outside the organization s existing network. Foster joy and belonging. Encourage participants to return for future activities. Expand community engagement over time. The activity itself should revolve around strengthening relationships rather than simply hosting an event. Who Is Eligible to Apply? Organizations must meet all of the following requirements: Be a registered nonprofit or charity. Be a 501(c)(3) organization in the United States or a registered charity internationally. Organizations using a fiscal sponsor may apply. Maintain an annual operating budget below USD 500,000 . Be eligible to legally receive grant funding. Be in good standing with relevant authorities. Grassroots organizations and small community organizations are especially encouraged to apply. Eligible Projects Projects must: Take place in one of the eligible cities. Focus primarily on building in-person human connection. Be open to the wider community. Encourage participation from neighbors. Be delivered during the grant period. Be either: A single event A series of events An ongoing community program. Projects That Are Not Eligible The program will not fund: Virtual-only events Online communities Building construction Facility renovations Capital improvement projects General organizational operating expenses Political campaigns Lobbying activities Religious proselytization Projects focused only on social services without emphasizing human connection Closed clubs or member-only groups For-profit businesses Projects outside the designated cities. Grant Amount Successful applicants may receive funding of up to: Up to USD 10,000 There is no minimum funding request , allowing organizations to seek support according to the scale of their proposed project. Final award amounts will depend on factors such as: Number of applications received Quality of the proposal Expected community impact Organizational experience Number of people expected to benefit. Application Requirements Applicants must complete a brief application including: Organization Background Applicants should provide: Mission statement Organizational history Why the organization was established Interested applicants should click HERE to apply Learn more about the opportunity HERE Project Hypothesis Applicants must explain: How the proposed project will strengthen human connections. Why they believe it will reduce loneliness and build community. Project Overview The proposal should include: Description of activities Whether the project is a one-time event or multiple events How new participants will be welcomed Community engagement strategy Proposed Budget Organizations should submit a detailed budget outlining: Expected expenses Funding allocation Overall project costs Measurement and Evaluation Plan Applicants must explain how they will measure success. Possible evaluation areas include: Human connection Sense of belonging Reduced loneliness Participant satisfaction Community engagement Applicants should also submit sample survey questions that will be used to evaluate project impact. Reporting Requirements Organizations receiving funding must submit a one-page final report within 60 days after completing their project. The report should include: Program summary Activities completed Participation numbers Outcomes achieved Photos or videos documenting events Organizations are also encouraged to use the hashtag #IRLhumanconnection in related social media posts. Program Timeline Milestone Date Applications Open May 28, 2026 Application Deadline July 31, 2026 (11:59 PM Pacific Time) Application Review August 1 – September 10, 2026 Grant Awards Announced September 21, 2026 Grant Period Begins Upon award notification Grant Period Ends June 30, 2027 Final Report Due Within 60 days after project completion Why Organizations Should Apply This microgrant provides much more than financial support. It offers nonprofit organizations an opportunity to: Address loneliness within their communities. Strengthen neighborhood relationships. Foster inclusion and belonging. Create sustainable community engagement models. Pilot innovative ideas for social connection. Build partnerships across diverse groups. Demonstrate measurable community impact. Contribute to a global movement promoting stronger human relationships. Whether your organization plans a neighborhood festival, community art project, volunteer initiative, outdoor recreation program, or cultural celebration, the Workday Foundation is looking for ideas that place human connection at the heart of every activity. Conclusion The Workday Foundation Human Connection Microgrant Program 2026 represents a significant opportunity for nonprofits and community organizations committed to creating stronger, healthier, and more connected neighborhoods. As loneliness continues to emerge as one of today s most pressing social challenges, this initiative encourages organizations to design joyful, inclusive, and meaningful experiences that bring people together in real life. With grants of up to $10,000 USD , the program supports innovative grassroots initiatives that prioritize genuine human interaction over digital engagement. If your organization has a creative idea capable of fostering trust, friendship, and belonging within your community, this funding opportunity could help transform that vision into lasting impact. title: EMBL ARISE2 Fellowships 2026 in Europe | Fully Funded Research Infrastructure Fellowship
summary: Applications are now open for the EMBL ARISE2 Fellowships , an exciting fully funded postdoctoral programme offered by the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL). Designed for outstanding early-career researchers, ARISE2 combines cutting-edge research with professional development, enabling fellows to build successful careers in research infrastructures across Europe. Unlike traditional postdoctoral fellowships, ARISE2 focuses on preparing scientists for leadership roles in research infrastructures. Fellows work on innovative technology or method development projects while receiving specialized training in project management, innovation, service delivery, entrepreneurship, and scientific leadership. If you are passionate about advancing scientific technologies while developing the skills needed to support world-class research facilities, the EMBL ARISE2 Fellowship offers an exceptional career opportunity. About the EMBL ARISE2 Fellowships The Career Accelerator for Research Infrastructure Scientists (ARISE2) is the successor to the highly successful ARISE programme at EMBL. The programme recruits talented postdoctoral researchers to work for three years at one of EMBL s research sites. During the fellowship, participants undertake technology or method development projects within EMBL research groups and core facilities while participating in a structured professional development programme. ARISE2 aims to train the next generation of research infrastructure scientists by combining scientific excellence with practical leadership skills, ensuring fellows are well-equipped to contribute to international research infrastructures and scientific innovation. Fellowship Benefits Successful fellows will receive: Fully funded three-year postdoctoral appointment Competitive salary and employee benefits Hands-on experience at one of EMBL s research sites Access to world-class research infrastructure and facilities Professional training in: Leadership Project management Technology development Innovation Entrepreneurship Service delivery International networking opportunities Career development support Collaboration with leading scientists and technology experts across Europe Research Areas Fellows will contribute to technology and method development projects in research infrastructures across various life science disciplines. Projects may involve: Advanced imaging technologies Bioinformatics Structural biology Genomics Molecular biology Data science Artificial intelligence applications in biology Microscopy Proteomics Scientific instrumentation Computational biology Eligibility Criteria Applicants should: Hold a PhD (or have completed all requirements before starting the fellowship). Demonstrate strong research achievements. Be interested in technology or method development. Have excellent communication and teamwork skills. Be motivated to pursue careers in research infrastructures. Meet the mobility and eligibility requirements outlined by EMBL. Researchers from around the world are encouraged to apply, provided they satisfy the programme s eligibility requirements. Programme Structure ARISE2 Fellows are employed for three years at one of EMBL s research sites. Each fellow will: Join an EMBL research group or core facility. Conduct a technology or method development project. Receive advanced career development training. Participate in innovation and entrepreneurship activities. Learn project and service management. Develop leadership skills for research infrastructures. The programme combines scientific research with professional skills that prepare fellows for leadership positions beyond traditional academic careers. Why Apply? The EMBL ARISE2 Fellowship offers much more than research funding. Participants gain: International research experience Practical technology development expertise Leadership training Innovation and entrepreneurship skills Exposure to Europe s leading life science research infrastructure Long-term career development support The fellowship is particularly valuable for researchers interested in scientific services, advanced technologies, and research infrastructure management. How to Apply Interested applicants should carefully review the programme requirements before preparing their applications. Applications must be submitted through the official EMBL application system before the published deadline. Applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents well in advance and ensure they meet the eligibility criteria before submission. Official Programme Page: https://www.embl.org/about/info/arise/ Application Portal: https://www.embl.org/about/info/arise/apply/ Why Choose EMBL? EMBL is one of the world s leading research organizations in molecular biology and life sciences. With multiple research sites across Europe, EMBL provides scientists with access to cutting-edge facilities, interdisciplinary collaboration, and an international research environment. Through ARISE2, fellows become part of a vibrant scientific community dedicated to advancing research technologies while developing the next generation of research infrastructure leaders. Conclusion The EMBL ARISE2 Fellowships provide an outstanding opportunity for postdoctoral researchers seeking to combine scientific excellence with leadership development in research infrastructures. By offering a fully funded position, world-class mentoring, and professional training, the programme prepares fellows for impactful careers at the forefront of scientific innovation. Researchers interested in technology development, interdisciplinary collaboration, and research infrastructure are encouraged to apply and take advantage of this unique opportunity at EMBL.
