title: Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program  Call for Applications (Cohort XXI) 2026
summary: Climate change continues to be one of the greatest challenges facing humanity today. Across Africa, communities are increasingly experiencing the devastating impacts of rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, floods, food insecurity, biodiversity loss, and other climate-related disasters. These challenges have significant implications for livelihoods, economic growth, sustainable development, and the well-being of millions of people, especially women, youth, and vulnerable communities. As the global community works together to address climate change through international agreements and negotiations, there is an increasing demand for skilled African professionals who understand climate governance, diplomacy, and international climate negotiations. Strong African representation in global climate discussions is essential to ensure that the continent s priorities, development needs, and climate realities are effectively represented. To strengthen Africa s climate leadership capacity, the African Group of Negotiators Experts Support (AGNES), through the Jael Vike Climate Change Training Institute (JVCCTI), has officially opened applications for the Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program (CLP) Cohort XXII . The programme is designed to equip current and emerging African climate leaders with the knowledge, leadership competencies, and practical negotiation skills required to engage effectively in regional and international climate policy processes while supporting climate action across the continent. Applications are now open for qualified candidates. About the Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program The Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program (CLP) is one of AGNES flagship capacity-building initiatives aimed at strengthening Africa s participation in global climate governance. The programme is delivered through the Jael Vike Climate Change Training Institute (JVCCTI), which focuses on developing highly skilled African professionals capable of influencing climate policy, participating in international negotiations, and supporting implementation of climate agreements at national and regional levels. As international climate negotiations become increasingly complex, African countries require a growing pool of professionals who understand the legal, scientific, political, and diplomatic dimensions of climate governance. The programme responds to this need by preparing participants to contribute meaningfully to Africa s climate agenda while strengthening their ability to influence climate policy both within their countries and on the international stage. Why This Programme Matters Climate change affects every sector of society, including agriculture, health, infrastructure, water resources, energy, education, and economic development. Africa contributes relatively little to global greenhouse gas emissions but remains among the regions most vulnerable to climate change impacts. Consequently, effective participation in international climate negotiations is critical for ensuring that African priorities receive appropriate attention in global decision-making processes. The programme recognizes that successful climate governance requires knowledgeable leaders who can: Understand climate science Develop evidence-based climate policies Participate effectively in international negotiations Advocate for African interests Support implementation of climate agreements Promote inclusive climate action involving women, youth, and marginalized communities The Role of International Climate Agreements The programme focuses on strengthening participants understanding of the major international climate frameworks that guide global climate action. These include: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Kyoto Protocol Paris Agreement These international agreements continue to shape global policies on: Climate adaptation Climate mitigation Climate finance Loss and damage Technology transfer Capacity building Transparency frameworks National implementation strategies Participants will gain practical knowledge of how these agreements influence climate policy at international, regional, national, and local levels. Programme Objectives The overall objective of the Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program is to strengthen Africa s climate leadership by building a new generation of knowledgeable and effective climate professionals. Specifically, the programme seeks to: Strengthen leadership capacity among African climate professionals Improve participants understanding of climate governance Develop advanced climate negotiation skills Enhance climate diplomacy competencies Increase effective African participation in international climate negotiations Build the capacity of leaders to implement climate actions across Africa Support emerging climate leaders, particularly women and youth Expected Learning Outcomes By the end of the programme, participants will have acquired both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in climate governance and international negotiations. Participants will be able to: 1. Understand Climate Science Participants will learn to: Explain the physical science behind climate change Understand the causes and impacts of climate change Assess climate risks affecting Africa Understand the role of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Interpret scientific evidence that informs climate policy 2. Develop Climate Leadership Skills Participants will strengthen their ability to: Lead climate initiatives Communicate climate issues effectively Engage multiple stakeholders Promote inclusive climate action Support collaborative decision-making 3. Understand the UNFCCC Process Participants will gain detailed knowledge of: Conference of the Parties (COP) Conference of the Parties serving as the Meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA) Conference of the Parties serving as the Meeting of the Parties to the Kyoto Protocol (CMP) Subsidiary Bodies Constituted Bodies Negotiating Groups Institutional structures of international climate governance 4. Build Practical Negotiation Skills The programme will provide practical experience in: Preparing for negotiations Participating in climate negotiations Reading and interpreting negotiating texts Understanding negotiation brackets Applying negotiation strategies Supporting consensus-building during negotiations Who Should Apply? The programme welcomes applications from professionals working across climate-related sectors. Eligible applicants include: Policy and Decision Makers Professionals responsible for designing and implementing: Climate policies National climate programmes Local climate initiatives Environmental strategies Climate Scientists Individuals working in: Universities Academic institutions Think tanks Climate research centres Scientific organizations Government Officials and Diplomats Professionals involved in: Climate negotiations International diplomacy National climate governance Regional climate cooperation Representatives of Organizations Applicants from: International organizations Intergovernmental organizations Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) Civil society organizations Youth-led organizations Women-led organizations Private sector institutions working in climate change, environmental governance, and sustainable development are encouraged to apply Legal Professionals The programme also welcomes: Lawyers Climate justice advocates Environmental law practitioners Legal experts working in climate governance Emerging Climate Leaders Young professionals and early-career practitioners who wish to contribute to Africa s climate agenda are strongly encouraged to apply. Women and Youth Are Encouraged to Apply The programme places particular emphasis on strengthening leadership among: Women leaders Youth leaders Early-career professionals Emerging climate practitioners By increasing participation from these groups, the programme seeks to build a more inclusive and representative climate leadership community across Africa. APPLY HERE Application Requirements Interested applicants should demonstrate: Interest in climate change Experience in climate policy Climate governance knowledge Climate diplomacy Environmental governance Climate science Sustainable development Climate negotiations Related professional or academic fields Applications should clearly show the applicant s motivation and commitment to strengthening Africa s climate leadership. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications is: 31 July 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid last-minute challenges. Visit HERE to learn more about Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program Conclusion The Climate Governance, Diplomacy and Negotiations Leadership Program Cohort XXII presents an outstanding opportunity for African professionals, policymakers, researchers, negotiators, legal experts, civil society representatives, and emerging leaders to strengthen their expertise in one of the world s most pressing development challenges. As climate negotiations continue to shape international policies on adaptation, mitigation, finance, and sustainable development, Africa requires highly skilled leaders who can effectively represent the continent s interests while driving meaningful climate action at every level. Through comprehensive training in climate science, governance, diplomacy, leadership, and negotiation, the programme equips participants with the practical knowledge and strategic skills needed to contribute to stronger climate policies and successful implementation across Africa. Professionals who are passionate about advancing climate action and strengthening Africa s voice in global climate governance should take advantage of this opportunity and submit their applications before the deadline of 31 July 2026 . title: International Anti-Corruption Academy Partial Scholarship 2026: Apply for Tuition Support to Study the Master in Anti-Corruption Studies (MACS/IMACC)
summary: Published Date: 17 July 2026 The International Anti-Corruption Academy (IACA) is offering a limited number of Partial Scholarships for students applying to its 2026 Master in Anti-Corruption Studies (MACS) or International Master in Anti-Corruption Compliance (IMACC) programmes. These scholarships are designed to support talented individuals from eligible developing countries who demonstrate both academic merit and financial need, while also showing strong leadership potential and a commitment to creating positive change in their communities. The scholarship provides partial financial assistance by covering tuition fees up to EUR 17,900 , helping deserving students access high-quality education in anti-corruption, compliance, governance, and ethical leadership. Individuals who aspire to become leaders in promoting transparency, integrity, accountability, and good governance are encouraged to apply. About the IACA Partial Scholarship The International Anti-Corruption Academy (IACA) recognizes that financial constraints can prevent outstanding candidates from pursuing postgraduate education. To address this challenge, the Academy provides a limited number of partial scholarships each year for qualified applicants enrolling in its master s programmes. These scholarships are awarded based on a combination of: Academic merit Financial need Leadership potential Capacity to successfully complete the programme Commitment to promoting positive change in society Rather than simply rewarding academic excellence, the scholarship aims to identify future leaders who can make meaningful contributions in combating corruption, strengthening compliance systems, and improving governance in both the public and private sectors. Because scholarship funding is limited, applications undergo a competitive selection process. Scholarship Benefits Successful applicants will receive financial support toward their postgraduate studies. The scholarship includes: Tuition fee support of up to EUR 17,900 Opportunity to pursue the Master in Anti-Corruption Studies (MACS) or International Master in Anti-Corruption Compliance (IMACC) Access to internationally recognized education in anti-corruption and compliance Opportunity to study alongside professionals from around the world Exposure to global best practices in governance, ethics, transparency, and compliance The scholarship is intended to reduce the financial burden of tuition while enabling participants to strengthen their professional expertise and leadership capacity. What the Scholarship Does Not Cover Applicants should note that this is a partial scholarship , meaning it does not cover all study-related expenses. Recipients must demonstrate that they can finance: Remaining tuition fees not covered by the scholarship Travel expenses (where applicable) Accommodation Living expenses Visa-related costs Insurance Any additional expenses not covered by the scholarship Applicants choosing the hybrid study format must also provide evidence that they can meet any travel and participation costs required by the programme. Who Can Apply? The scholarship is specifically designed for applicants from eligible developing countries. Applicants must satisfy all eligibility requirements established by IACA. Eligible candidates must: 1. Nationality Requirement Applicants must be citizens of: Least Developed Countries (LDCs) as defined by the United Nations, or IACA State Parties that are classified by the World Bank as: Low-Income Economies Lower-Middle-Income Economies Upper-Middle-Income Economies Only applicants from these eligible countries will be considered. 2. Admission Requirement Applicants must have: Submitted an application for admission to the Master in Anti-Corruption Studies (MACS) or International Master in Anti-Corruption Compliance (IMACC), or Already been admitted into one of these programmes for the 2026 cohort . Admission to the programme is an essential requirement before scholarship consideration. 3. Academic and Leadership Potential Applicants must: Meet all admission requirements for the master s programme. Demonstrate strong academic capability. Show potential to complete the programme successfully within the two-year duration. Demonstrate leadership qualities. Show the ability to create positive social impact. Display commitment to anti-corruption, compliance, transparency, governance, or related fields. Scholarship Selection Criteria Scholarships are awarded based on several factors, including: Financial Need Priority is given to applicants who genuinely require financial assistance to pursue their studies. Academic Merit Candidates should demonstrate the academic ability necessary to successfully complete the programme. Leadership Potential Applicants should possess strong leadership qualities and the ability to influence positive institutional and societal change. Potential Impact The selection committee seeks individuals who are likely to contribute significantly to anti-corruption efforts, ethical governance, and compliance initiatives after completing their studies. Programme Completion Capacity Candidates should demonstrate that they can complete the programme within its standard two-year duration. How to Apply Interested applicants should carefully complete the official scholarship application form. Before submitting the scholarship application, applicants should ensure that they: Complete every section accurately. Follow all application instructions. Provide truthful and complete information. Upload all required supporting documents. Incomplete applications may not be considered. Important Application Requirement Applicants cannot submit the scholarship application without an official IACA reference number . This reference number is issued by the IACA Admissions Team after confirming that an applicant s admission application is complete. The reference number is sent via email and must be entered when completing the scholarship application form. Applicants are therefore advised to complete their admission application early to allow sufficient time for verification and issuance of the reference number. APPLY HERE Why Apply for the IACA Partial Scholarship? This scholarship offers an excellent opportunity for professionals and future leaders committed to integrity and good governance. Benefits include: Financial support toward postgraduate tuition Internationally recognized master s education Specialized training in anti-corruption and compliance Opportunities to strengthen leadership skills Exposure to global governance best practices Networking with international professionals Enhanced career prospects in governance, compliance, public administration, law, development, and international organizations Important Notes Applicants should remember that: Scholarship funding is limited. Scholarships are awarded competitively. Admission into the master s programme is required before scholarship consideration. Financial need alone does not guarantee selection. Applicants must demonstrate leadership potential and commitment to creating positive societal impact. Scholarship recipients remain responsible for expenses not covered by the award. Application Deadline No application deadline has been provided in the available information. Applicants are encouraged to submit both their admission and scholarship applications as early as possible to avoid missing any institutional deadlines. Visit HERE to learn more about International Anti-Corruption Academy Partial Scholarship Conclusion The IACA Partial Scholarship 2026 provides an outstanding opportunity for aspiring leaders from eligible developing countries to pursue advanced education in anti-corruption, compliance, and ethical governance. By offering tuition support of up to EUR 17,900, the scholarship helps reduce financial barriers while investing in individuals who have the potential to drive meaningful institutional and societal change. Applicants who demonstrate academic excellence, financial need, leadership potential, and a strong commitment to integrity and transparency are strongly encouraged to apply. Since admission to the MACS or IMACC programme is a prerequisite for scholarship consideration, prospective students should begin the admissions process early and ensure they obtain their IACA reference number before submitting their scholarship application. title: Africa Health Collaborative Research Fund 2026: Up to USD 22,000 in Funding for Early Career Researchers Advancing Primary Health Care in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: The Africa Health Collaborative (AHC) Research Fund 2026 is now accepting Expressions of Interest (EOIs) from eligible Early Career Researchers (ECRs) seeking funding to develop innovative, collaborative research projects focused on strengthening Primary Health Care (PHC) systems across Sub-Saharan Africa. This prestigious funding opportunity aims to foster high-impact bilateral and multilateral research collaborations among member institutions of the Africa Health Collaborative. Through this initiative, researchers will receive financial support to build research capacity, strengthen partnerships across African institutions, and generate evidence capable of influencing health policy, health financing, and human resource development. Researchers with innovative ideas addressing health workforce challenges and financing policies in primary health care are encouraged to apply before the application deadline. About the Africa Health Collaborative (AHC) The Africa Health Collaborative (AHC) is a multi-year partnership dedicated to strengthening primary health care systems throughout Africa by investing in: Health workforce development Medical education Innovation Entrepreneurship Research collaboration Capacity building The collaborative recognizes research as one of the most important pillars for improving healthcare delivery across the continent. Through this funding scheme, AHC seeks to promote translational research capable of producing practical solutions that positively impact African communities. Rather than supporting isolated research projects, the program focuses on establishing sustainable partnerships that can continue attracting larger research grants in the future. Overview of the 2026 Research Fund The Africa Health Collaborative member institutions are jointly contributing matching funds to support collaborative research among their institutions. The fund specifically supports: Bilateral research projects involving two AHC member institutions. Multilateral research projects involving three or more AHC institutions. The overall objective is to empower Early Career Researchers by providing seed funding that enables them to: Build international research collaborations. Develop competitive research portfolios. Generate preliminary findings. Position themselves for larger external research grants. Produce evidence that improves primary healthcare systems. 2026 Research Theme The theme for the 2026 funding call is: Health Human Resources Policy and Health Financing Policy in Primary Health Care in Sub-Saharan Africa Applicants are expected to develop innovative research projects addressing policy-related issues affecting: Health workforce development Health worker distribution Human resource planning Primary healthcare financing Sustainable healthcare systems Universal Health Coverage Community health systems Policy implementation Health systems strengthening Projects should demonstrate clear potential for improving health outcomes within Sub-Saharan Africa. Funding Value Successful proposals can receive substantial financial support. Bilateral Projects Eligible projects may receive: Up to USD 22,000 Each participating institution may award up to USD 11,000 to its own investigator. Multilateral Projects Funding will be scaled according to the number of participating institutions. Each participating institution may receive: Up to USD 11,000 for investigators affiliated with that institution. Number of Projects to be Funded The joint funding initiative plans to support: Up to 9 collaborative research proposals The funding period for each project will last: 18 months Project Duration Approved research projects will: Begin on January 1, 2027 Continue for a maximum period of 18 months Eligible Research Activities Funding may support numerous collaborative activities, including: Joint research workshops Researcher exchange visits Collaborative research groups Cross-institutional partnerships Data collection Field research Research meetings Capacity-building activities Knowledge exchange Stakeholder engagement Publication activities (where institutionally permitted) The program emphasizes collaboration among institutions and encourages interdisciplinary approaches. What the Funding Can Cover Depending on institutional guidelines, eligible expenses may include: International and domestic travel Flights Hotel accommodation Subsistence costs Workshops Research meetings Research consumables (up to USD 1,500 where applicable) Graduate student stipends Research exchanges Field visits Software licenses External consultation fees Publishing costs Conference presentations (institution-dependent) Data collection Research dissemination activities Costs That Are Generally Not Eligible The program generally excludes funding for: Equipment purchases Replacement teaching costs Replacement research costs Directly allocated applicant salaries Estate and indirect costs Research assistants (institution-dependent) Entertainment expenses Excessive branding Non-research marketing activities Eligible Institutions Only Early Career Researchers affiliated with the following Africa Health Collaborative institutions may apply: Addis Ababa University African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) African Leadership University Amref International University Ashesi University Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology Moi University University of Cape Town University of Toronto Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy several important requirements. Research Leadership Applications must be led by an Early Career Researcher (ECR). Collaboration Projects must be either: Bilateral (two participating institutions), or Multilateral (three or more participating institutions) Student Participation Every proposal must include participation by: Master s students Doctoral students Postdoctoral trainees Application Limits Applicants may lead only one application. Applicants Without Co-applicants Researchers who do not yet have collaborators may still submit an application. If approved by their home institution, their proposal may be placed in a public repository to help identify suitable collaborators from other AHC member institutions. External Collaborators Researchers from: Government NGOs International universities Community organizations Other research institutions may participate in projects but cannot serve as principal applicants . Institutional Definitions of Early Career Researchers Each institution has its own definition of an Early Career Researcher. Examples include: Faculty within a specified number of years after PhD completion. Assistant professors. Lecturers. Postdoctoral researchers. Newly appointed researchers. PhD graduates within defined timeframes. PhD students meeting publication requirements. Master s graduates with peer-reviewed publications (institution dependent). Applicants should carefully review the requirements applicable to their institution before submitting an application. Equality, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion The Africa Health Collaborative strongly promotes Equality, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI). Applicant teams are encouraged to foster research environments that: Respect diversity Promote inclusion Encourage different perspectives Support persons with disabilities Promote gender equity Recognize indigenous peoples Include diverse sectors and disciplines Evaluation Criteria Applications will be assessed by a joint review committee representing all participating institutions. Evaluation will consider: Project design Research rationale Academic quality Complementarity among collaborators Potential translational impact Demonstrable societal impact Potential for future funding Alignment with Africa Health Collaborative priorities Application Process The application process consists of two stages. Stage One: Expression of Interest (EOI) Applicants first submit an Expression of Interest demonstrating: Eligibility Research concept Institutional affiliation Successful EOIs will receive an invitation to submit a full proposal. Stage Two: Full Proposal Only approved applicants from Stage One will be invited to submit comprehensive research proposals. One joint proposal will be submitted on behalf of the project team. Important Dates Applications Open: Currently Open Expression of Interest Deadline: 15 August 2026 (12:00 PM GMT) EOI Results Announcement: 7 September 2026 (12:00 PM GMT) Invitation for Full Proposals: 7 November 2026 (12:00 PM GMT) Project Start Date: 1 January 2027 How to Apply Interested applicants should: Confirm eligibility through their institution. Prepare an Expression of Interest. Submit the EOI before the deadline. Await institutional review. If invited, prepare and submit the full proposal. Applicants requiring clarification may contact: africasecretariat@utoronto.ca APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply The Africa Health Collaborative Research Fund represents an outstanding opportunity for emerging researchers to establish long-term international collaborations while addressing some of the most pressing healthcare challenges facing Sub-Saharan Africa. Beyond financial support, successful applicants gain access to an expanding network of leading African and international universities committed to advancing primary healthcare research. The collaborative nature of the program also enhances researchers competitiveness for future international funding, strengthens institutional partnerships, and contributes to evidence-based policymaking that can improve health systems across the continent. For Early Career Researchers seeking to build impactful research careers while contributing to stronger primary healthcare systems, this fund offers an excellent platform for professional growth and meaningful scientific collaboration. Visit HERE to learn more about the Africa Health Collaborative Research Fund 2026 Conclusion The Africa Health Collaborative Research Fund 2026 presents an outstanding opportunity for Early Career Researchers to contribute meaningfully to the future of primary health care in Sub-Saharan Africa. By providing substantial funding, encouraging cross-institutional collaboration, and supporting innovative research on health human resources and health financing policies, the program aims to generate practical solutions that can strengthen health systems and improve healthcare delivery across the region. Beyond the financial support of up to USD 22,000 for bilateral projects, the initiative offers researchers a valuable platform to establish international partnerships, build research capacity, mentor graduate trainees, and develop competitive projects capable of attracting larger grants in the future. The emphasis on translational research ensures that funded projects will not only advance academic knowledge but also contribute to evidence-based policies and sustainable improvements in primary health care. Eligible Early Career Researchers affiliated with participating Africa Health Collaborative member institutions are encouraged to begin preparing their Expressions of Interest well in advance of the 15 August 2026 (12:00 PM GMT) deadline. Applicants should carefully review their institution-specific eligibility requirements, develop strong collaborative partnerships, and design impactful research proposals that align with the 2026 funding theme. For researchers committed to advancing health systems and creating lasting impact across Africa, this grant represents an exceptional opportunity to transform innovative ideas into meaningful change. For more global Grant opportunities visit OFY HERE The post Africa Health Collaborative Research Fund 2026: Up to USD 22,000 in Funding for Early Career Researchers Advancing Primary Health Care in Sub-Saharan Africa appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: European Youth Foundation Living and Building Democracy Grants 2026: Funding for Youth Initiatives Promoting Democracy and Human Rights
summary: The European Youth Foundation Living and Building Democracy Grants 2026 provide funding for youth initiatives promoting democracy and human rights across Europe. Launched by the European Youth Foundation (EYF) of the Council of Europe, this call for proposals supports ad hoc youth initiatives that empower young people to strengthen democratic culture, promote human rights, develop critical thinking, and actively participate in democratic processes. Through this grant programme, eligible youth organisations can implement innovative projects that address contemporary democratic challenges such as misinformation, disinformation, fake news, barriers to voting, and limited participation in governance, while equipping young people with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes needed to become active democratic citizens. To strengthen youth participation and democratic engagement across Europe, the European Youth Foundation (EYF) of the Council of Europe has launched the Call for Youth Initiatives Living and Building Democracy 2026 . This funding opportunity is designed to support innovative ad hoc youth initiatives that empower young people to better understand democracy, develop critical thinking skills, promote human rights, and actively participate in democratic life. The grant programme encourages youth organisations to design impactful projects that respond to real democratic challenges facing young people while promoting democratic values, civic participation, and human rights education. Applications are now open for eligible youth organisations registered with the European Youth Foundation. About the European Youth Foundation Living and Building Democracy Call The Living and Building Democracy call is a special funding initiative established by the European Youth Foundation to encourage youth organisations to create practical projects that strengthen democratic culture among young people. Rather than supporting general youth activities, this call specifically focuses on initiatives that respond to contemporary democratic challenges and equip young people with the knowledge, attitudes, and skills needed to actively participate in democratic societies. The initiative recognizes that democracy is strengthened when young people understand their rights, think critically, participate responsibly, and contribute to decision-making processes within their communities. By supporting youth-led initiatives, the European Youth Foundation seeks to promote active citizenship while reinforcing the values of democracy, human rights, inclusion, and participation across Europe. Objectives of the Grant Programme The Living and Building Democracy grant aims to support initiatives that contribute to several important objectives. 1. Increase Young People s Understanding of Democracy Projects should create opportunities for young people to: Learn about democratic values. Understand democratic institutions. Explore how democracy functions in modern society. Understand the importance of protecting democratic systems. 2. Promote Human Rights Education Applicants are encouraged to design activities that help participants understand: Fundamental human rights. The relationship between democracy and human rights. Why human rights are essential to democratic societies. How human rights can be protected and promoted. 3. Develop Critical Thinking The European Youth Foundation seeks initiatives that help young people: Analyze information critically. Question misinformation. Recognize manipulation. Make informed civic decisions. Build democratic attitudes and values. This objective is especially important within today s digital environment where false information spreads rapidly. 4. Strengthen Democratic Culture Successful projects should encourage young people to: Respect democratic values. Participate in civic life. Engage in dialogue. Promote inclusion. Build trust within communities. Encourage democratic participation both online and offline. 5. Equip Young People with Citizenship Skills The programme also aims to provide participants with practical citizenship skills that enable them to: Participate in democratic decision-making. Promote human rights. Engage in community initiatives. Contribute to governance processes. Become active and responsible citizens. Democratic Challenges the Grant Seeks to Address The European Youth Foundation particularly welcomes projects that respond to specific barriers preventing young people from participating fully in democratic life. Examples include: Misinformation Disinformation Fake news Information manipulation Political disengagement Low voter participation Barriers to voting Limited youth participation in governance Weak civic engagement Challenges affecting democratic participation in digital spaces Applicants are expected to clearly explain: Which democratic challenge their project addresses. Why the challenge is important. How young people are affected. How the proposed activities will overcome or reduce that challenge. The expected impact of the initiative. What Kind of Initiatives Can Be Supported? The programme supports ad hoc youth initiatives that contribute directly to strengthening democracy and promoting human rights. Eligible activities may include: Youth workshops Democracy education programmes Civic engagement projects Human rights campaigns Public awareness activities Community dialogue sessions Critical thinking workshops Digital citizenship initiatives Youth participation events Democratic leadership activities Advocacy and awareness campaigns Projects should demonstrate innovation, relevance, and measurable impact on young people s democratic participation. Benefits of the Grant Successful applicants will benefit from: Financial support for implementing youth initiatives. Opportunity to strengthen democratic participation among young people. Support for innovative civic engagement projects. Promotion of human rights education. Increased youth involvement in democratic processes. Contribution to democratic resilience across Europe. Recognition through support from the European Youth Foundation. Who Should Apply? This funding opportunity is intended for: Youth organisations registered with the European Youth Foundation. Youth organisations committed to democracy and human rights. Civil society organisations working with young people. Organisations promoting active citizenship. Youth-led organisations implementing democratic participation projects. Applicants must ensure that their proposed projects align with the objectives and priorities outlined in the call for proposals. Application Requirements Applicants should carefully review the official call documents before submitting their applications. Applications will be assessed based on: Eligibility criteria. Exclusion criteria. Award criteria. Relevance of the proposed initiative. Quality of the project design. Expected impact. Demonstrated response to identified democratic challenges. The initiative should clearly explain how it intends to address a specific democratic issue affecting young people and provide practical solutions through its planned activities. Visit Here for more details. Application Timeline Applications opened for submission from the end of July 2026. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications is: 1 September 2026 at 23:59 CEST Late applications will not be considered. title: UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp 2026: Fully Funded Online Training on Human Rights Impact Assessment for AI Developers, Start-ups and Public Institutions
summary: The UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp 2026 is a fully funded online training programme designed to help AI developers, start-ups, and public institutions strengthen their understanding and application of responsible artificial intelligence through the Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) Toolkit. Organized by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the bootcamp provides participants with practical experience in assessing AI systems against responsible AI standards, while receiving guidance from international experts. Participants will explore AI governance, human rights considerations, and real-world AI implementation through interactive sessions, confidential breakout workshops, and hands-on use of the HRIA Toolkit. Successful participants will also receive a Certificate of Participation upon completing the programme. As organizations increasingly integrate AI into decision-making and service delivery, ensuring that these technologies are developed and deployed responsibly has become more important than ever. Recognizing this need, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for the Responsible AI Bootcamp 2026 , an intensive online training designed to help organizations assess and improve the human rights impacts of their AI systems. This unique learning opportunity moves beyond theoretical discussions about responsible AI and provides participants with practical experience using the Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) Toolkit. Through expert-led sessions, confidential workshops, and personalized guidance, participants will evaluate their own AI systems against internationally recognized responsible AI principles. Participation in the bootcamp is completely free, and successful participants will receive a Certificate of Participation upon completion. About the UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp The UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp is a specialized online training program created to help organizations transition from understanding responsible AI concepts to implementing them in practice. Rather than focusing solely on AI ethics theory, the bootcamp allows participants to test and assess their own AI projects using the Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) Toolkit. Throughout the program, participants will work directly with international experts while exploring practical methods for identifying and mitigating potential risks associated with AI systems. The bootcamp combines interactive learning, expert mentorship, and confidential group sessions where participants can openly discuss their AI projects in a secure environment. What is the Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) Toolkit? One of the central components of the bootcamp is the Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) Toolkit. The HRIA Toolkit is designed to help organizations systematically evaluate whether their AI systems align with responsible AI standards while protecting human rights throughout the AI lifecycle. Using the toolkit, participants will learn how to: Identify potential human rights risks associated with AI systems. Evaluate fairness and non-discrimination within AI models. Assess transparency and accountability mechanisms. Understand privacy and data protection considerations. Improve governance practices for AI deployment. Develop practical strategies for mitigating identified risks. Strengthen compliance with international responsible AI standards. Participants will also gain access to the HRIA online platform, which supports the assessment process throughout the bootcamp. Further explanations would be found here What Participants Will Learn During the bootcamp, participants will gain practical knowledge and experience in responsible AI implementation. Key learning areas include: Responsible AI principles and governance Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology AI risk identification and mitigation Responsible deployment of AI systems Ethical AI decision-making Human rights considerations in AI design AI governance frameworks Responsible innovation strategies Practical application of the HRIA Toolkit Expert feedback on participants own AI use cases Bootcamp Structure The program combines theoretical instruction with hands-on practical exercises. Participants will take part in: 1. Foundational Responsible AI Session The bootcamp begins with a comprehensive introduction to responsible AI principles, governance frameworks, and human rights considerations. This session establishes the foundation necessary to conduct meaningful AI assessments. 2. Confidential Breakout Sessions Participants will join confidential breakout rooms where they can directly apply the HRIA Toolkit to their own AI systems or projects. These sessions provide: Personalized guidance Practical demonstrations Individual feedback Expert mentoring Peer learning opportunities Because discussions are confidential, participants can openly discuss their AI projects without concern about public disclosure. 3. Expert Support International experts specializing in responsible AI, AI governance, and human rights will provide ongoing guidance throughout the program. Participants will receive support in understanding both technical and policy-related aspects of responsible AI. Sectors Covered The HRIA Toolkit focuses on AI applications across several high-impact sectors, including: Education Employment Healthcare Public services Participants working within these sectors will have the opportunity to evaluate how their AI systems affect individuals, institutions, and society. Benefits of Participating Selected participants will enjoy numerous professional and practical benefits, including: Free participation in the entire bootcamp. Practical training in responsible AI implementation. Hands-on experience using the Human Rights Impact Assessment Toolkit. Direct mentorship from international experts. Access to the HRIA online platform. Practical evaluation of participants own AI systems. Improved understanding of AI governance and human rights. Networking opportunities with professionals working in AI and public policy. Enhanced organizational capacity for responsible AI deployment. Certificate of Participation upon successful completion. Who Should Apply? The UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp is intended for organizations and professionals actively working with AI technologies. Eligible applicants include: Technology companies AI-focused start-ups Public institutions Individual professionals working with AI Teams developing or deploying AI systems Applicants should possess basic knowledge of: Artificial Intelligence AI governance Legal and regulatory considerations relating to AI Applications from both individuals and teams are welcome. UNDP also strongly encourages female candidates to submit applications. Want similar opportunities like this? Visit here Languages The bootcamp will be conducted in: English Additionally, the Human Rights Impact Assessment platform is currently available in: English French Spanish Russian BCMS (Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin and Serbian) Bootcamp Details Programme Dates 21–22 September 2026 Delivery Mode Online via Zoom Participation Fee Free of charge Cohort Size Approximately 25–30 participants Certificate Participants who successfully complete the program will receive a Certificate of Participation. Application Deadline The deadline to submit applications is: 15 August 2026 Interested applicants are encouraged to apply early, as only a limited number of participants will be selected. For more details click HERE How to Apply Applicants should complete the official UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp application form before the application deadline. They may also explore additional resources to better understand the Human Rights Impact Assessment Toolkit and online platform before participating. Conclusion As governments, businesses, and institutions continue to integrate artificial intelligence into everyday operations, responsible AI governance is becoming a global priority. The UNDP Responsible AI Bootcamp 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for organizations and professionals to move beyond theoretical discussions and gain practical experience in assessing AI systems through a human rights lens. With expert guidance, access to internationally recognized assessment tools, hands-on evaluation of real AI projects, and a free Certificate of Participation, this bootcamp provides participants with practical skills that can strengthen responsible AI development and deployment within their organizations. Eligible applicants from the participating countries are encouraged to submit their applications before the 15 August 2026 deadline and take advantage of this unique professional development opportunity.
