title: Literary Arts Fund 2026 Innovation Project Grants: Up to $100,000 Available for U.S. Nonprofit Literary Arts Organizations
summary: The Literary Arts Fund has officially opened applications for its 2026 Innovation Project Grants, a major funding opportunity designed to strengthen the nonprofit literary arts sector across the United States. As part of its long-term commitment to investing in literary organizations, the fund has pledged to provide at least $50 million in support to the nonprofit literary arts ecosystem over the next five years, with funding continuing through 2031. The 2026 Innovation Project Grants are specifically designed to support bold, forward-thinking projects that address structural and infrastructure challenges affecting nonprofit literary arts organizations. Successful applicants can receive grants ranging from $25,000 to $100,000 , with no matching funds required. Organizations that work directly with adult creative writers now have the opportunity to secure funding that will help strengthen their operations, improve services, and create long-term impact across the literary arts community. About the Literary Arts Fund The Literary Arts Fund was established to strengthen and sustain the nonprofit literary arts sector across the United States. Rather than distributing funding across every area of the arts, the Fund focuses specifically on organizations that help adult creative writers produce and share literary works. Its strategy prioritizes investments where they can create the greatest long-term impact. Over the next five years, the organization intends to distribute at least $50 million through various grant opportunities before concluding its funding cycle in 2031. Each year, the Fund offers two major grant opportunities: Innovation Project Grants General Operating Grants While the General Operating Grant application for 2026 has already closed, applications remain open for the Innovation Project Grants. What Are the 2026 Innovation Project Grants? The Innovation Project Grants provide funding for new, one-time projects that address major operational, structural, or infrastructure challenges faced by nonprofit literary arts organizations. Rather than funding routine activities, these grants are intended to support innovative solutions that produce lasting improvements for organizations and the broader literary arts ecosystem. Projects should generate benefits that continue well beyond the grant period and ultimately strengthen organizations ability to serve creative writers. The Fund expects the competition to be highly competitive due to the limited funding available. Grant Value Successful applicants may request funding between: Minimum grant: $25,000 Maximum grant: $100,000 In total, the Literary Arts Fund will distribute $1 million through the 2026 Innovation Project Grant program. One important advantage is that applicants are not required to provide matching funds , nor must they have additional project funding already secured. Purpose of the Funding Innovation Project Grants are intended to help nonprofit literary organizations solve important challenges that affect their long-term sustainability. Projects may focus on: Organizational infrastructure improvements New systems and processes Innovative collaborative initiatives Structural improvements Capacity-building efforts Long-term solutions benefiting literary arts organizations Projects may also involve collaboration between multiple eligible nonprofit organizations. Who Is Eligible? To qualify, applicants must be independent nonprofit literary arts organizations, publishers, or publications located in the United States. Their primary mission must directly support adult creative writers by helping them create and share literary works. Eligible organizations typically support writers through activities such as: Public literary events Festivals Readings Open mic events Spoken word performances Literary conversations Lectures Publishing opportunities Books Chapbooks Literary journals Magazines Digital publications Literary websites Zines Professional development Writing residencies Retreats Workshops Mentorship programs Audience development Book reviews Interviews Podcasts Online archives Feature articles Recognition of literary achievement Awards Fellowships Literary prizes Additional Eligibility Requirements Applicants must also satisfy all of the following requirements: 1. Organizational History Organizations must have existed for at least three years before applying. For fiscally sponsored organizations, eligibility is determined using the date of the fiscal sponsorship agreement. 2. Leadership Stability Applicants must have an Executive Director who has served continuously for at least one full year. 3. Financial Stability Applicants must have: Annual operating budget of at least $50,000 Budget excludes in-kind or non-cash contributions For fiscally sponsored organizations, the applicant organization—not the fiscal sponsor—must meet this requirement. Organizations That Are Not Eligible The Literary Arts Fund does not currently support: Screenwriting organizations Playwriting organizations Oral storytelling nonprofits Writing therapy organizations University or college departments University-sponsored projects Organizations primarily supporting young writers Arts education organizations focused on K–12 students Literacy organizations that teach reading or writing skills Academic libraries School libraries Public libraries Research libraries Trade associations serving nonprofits Collaborative Applications Organizations may submit collaborative proposals. Important rules include: Only one organization may serve as the lead applicant. The lead organization submits the application. Collaborators may receive sub-awards if included in the approved project budget. Every collaborating organization receiving funds must independently satisfy all eligibility requirements. The lead applicant is responsible for verifying collaborator eligibility. Restrictions for Previous Grant Recipients Organizations that received a 2026 General Operating Grant cannot independently apply for an Innovation Project Grant during the same year. However, they may: Participate as collaborators Receive project sub-awards Join collaborative applications led by another eligible organization Project Timeline Approved projects must: Begin after January 1, 2027 Finish on or before December 31, 2027 Grant funds must only be used during the approved project period. Payment Structure Successful applicants will receive their grant funding as a single payment . For collaborative projects: The lead applicant receives the full grant. The lead applicant distributes any approved sub-awards to collaborating organizations. Application Process Applications are submitted online through Submittable. Applicants should prepare all required materials before beginning the submission process. Organizations wishing to revise an application after submission must: Withdraw the original application. Submit an entirely new application before the deadline. For more information, visit Literary Arts Fund 2026 Innovation Project website HERE Use of Artificial Intelligence The Literary Arts Fund clearly states that applicants may not use generative AI to produce any portion of the application narrative . Organizations should prepare all narrative responses independently. Application Deadline Applications for the 2026 Innovation Project Grants opened on June 8, 2026 . Application Deadline: August 17, 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit well before the deadline to avoid technical issues or last-minute errors. APPLY HERE Key Dates By May 30, 2026 – General Operating Grant applicants notified June 8, 2026 – Innovation Project Grant applications opened August 17, 2026 – Innovation Project Grant application deadline By December 31, 2026 – Successful applicants notified January 2027 – Expected opening of the next General Operating Grant cycle Available Applicant Resources To help applicants prepare strong proposals, the Literary Arts Fund offers several free resources, including: Innovation Project Grant information session recording Application preparation guide Budget best practices webinar Budget templates and sample budgets Field Scan research presentation Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Submittable technical support resources These materials are intended to improve application quality and help organizations better understand the grant process. For more grant opportunities visit OFY Website HERE Why This Grant Matters Many nonprofit literary organizations face operational and infrastructure challenges that limit their ability to support writers effectively. The Innovation Project Grant program seeks to fund projects that create lasting improvements rather than temporary solutions. By investing in stronger organizational systems, collaborative partnerships, and innovative approaches, the Literary Arts Fund hopes to strengthen the entire literary arts ecosystem while expanding opportunities for adult creative writers across the United States. Conclusion The Literary Arts Fund 2026 Innovation Project Grants present an outstanding funding opportunity for eligible U.S.-based nonprofit literary arts organizations seeking to implement transformative projects. With grants ranging from $25,000 to $100,000 , no matching fund requirement, and support for collaborative initiatives, the program provides organizations with the resources needed to address significant structural challenges and build lasting impact. Interested organizations should carefully review all eligibility requirements, prepare their applications independently, and submit them before the August 17, 2026 deadline to maximize their chances of securing funding. The post Literary Arts Fund 2026 Innovation Project Grants: Up to $100,000 Available for U.S. Nonprofit Literary Arts Organizations appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: The Adidas Foundation Expression of Interest 2026: Up to €6 Million Available for Strategic Partners in the New Recovery Through Sport Program
summary: Organizations working at the intersection of humanitarian response, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection, and sport for development now have a unique opportunity to partner with the adidas Foundation through its newly launched Recovery Through Sport Program . Rather than seeking traditional project proposals, the Foundation is inviting experienced organizations to become long-term strategic partners in designing and implementing an innovative global initiative that supports children and young people recovering from crises and displacement. With a total funding commitment of €6 million , the adidas Foundation plans to select one to three strategic partners that will collaboratively develop programming, learning frameworks, funding structures, and implementation approaches over an initial period of more than three years . If your organization has demonstrated expertise in humanitarian programming, mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding, and sport or physical activity, this could be one of the most significant partnership opportunities currently available in the global development and humanitarian sector. About the adidas Foundation Recovery Through Sport Program The Adidas Foundation is expanding its impact through the introduction of Recovery Through Sport , a new program area designed to help children and young people rebuild their well-being after experiencing crises, conflict, disasters, or forced displacement. The Foundation recognizes that sport is far more than recreation. When implemented under the right conditions, sports and structured physical activity can help young people restore: Emotional well-being Self-confidence Social connections A sense of routine Feelings of safety Community belonging Personal agency Positive participation However, the Foundation also emphasizes that sport is not intended to replace humanitarian assistance. Instead, it complements recovery efforts where appropriate safeguards, expertise, and community conditions exist. Why the adidas Foundation Is Looking for Strategic Partners Unlike conventional grant calls that require applicants to submit complete project proposals, this Expression of Interest focuses on identifying organizations with existing expertise and long-term capacity. The adidas Foundation is intentionally starting with partners before defining projects because it believes sustainable solutions should be co-created with organizations that understand local realities. Selected organizations will work closely with the Foundation to: Design future programming Develop funding models Shape implementation strategies Build evidence on effective approaches Identify suitable implementation contexts Test and improve interventions over time This collaborative approach ensures that programs respond directly to real-world humanitarian needs rather than predetermined project concepts. Background Research Behind the Program Before launching Recovery Through Sport, the adidas Foundation undertook extensive groundwork. Working alongside an independent consortium of experts in: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Sport for Development Physical Activity Humanitarian Programming The foundation reviewed existing research and consulted organizations working across humanitarian and development sectors. The consultation revealed several important findings. Sport Can Support Recovery Research shows that carefully designed sport and physical activity programs can help children and young people recovering from crisis by strengthening: Emotional resilience Social relationships Daily routines Community participation Psychological well-being Significant Evidence Gaps Remain Despite growing interest in sport-based recovery interventions, evidence remains limited, particularly in: Low-resource humanitarian settings Crisis-affected communities Displacement contexts Refugee environments The adidas Foundation therefore wants its strategic partnerships to contribute not only to programming but also to expanding global evidence on what works. What Makes This Opportunity Different? This opportunity differs from traditional funding calls in several important ways. 1. It Is Not a Traditional Grant Competition Applicants are not expected to submit detailed project proposals. Instead, organizations are invited to demonstrate: Existing expertise Organizational capacity Operational systems Experience working in complex environments Willingness to innovate 2. Long-Term Collaboration Rather than funding isolated short-term projects, the Foundation seeks partnerships lasting at least three years , with potential for future expansion. 3. Co-Creation Selected organizations will jointly develop: Program design Learning priorities Funding arrangements Evidence-building approaches Operational strategies 4. Strong Focus on Learning The Foundation wants every partnership to generate valuable evidence that improves humanitarian recovery through sport. The Kind of Partners the adidas Foundation Is Looking For The Foundation seeks organizations that already possess strong operational experience and are ready to strengthen and expand their work. Ideal partners should demonstrate experience in areas such as: Humanitarian response Crisis recovery Forced displacement Child protection Mental health and psychosocial support Sport for development Physical activity programming Community-based interventions Organizations should also have: Robust safeguarding systems Strong organizational governance Experience working in complex operational environments Capacity to deliver large-scale programming A culture of learning and adaptation Willingness to collaborate over the long term Expression of Interest Focus Areas The Foundation wants to understand what organizations already bring rather than asking them to create entirely new concepts. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate: Existing recovery practice Mental health and psychosocial support expertise Safeguarding policies and systems Operational reach Sport or physical activity experience Organizational learning culture Readiness for long-term collaboration Key Funding Information The Recovery Through Sport initiative includes substantial financial support. Total Funding €6,000,000 This represents the total funding commitment across all selected strategic partners and future program activities. Number of Strategic Partners Between: One Two Three organizations will ultimately be selected. Partnership Duration The initial partnership will last more than three years with opportunities for continued collaboration beyond that period. Benefits of Becoming an adidas Foundation Strategic Partner Organizations selected through this Expression of Interest will benefit from: Multi-year funding instead of short project cycles Collaborative program design Long-term strategic partnership Joint development of implementation approaches Access to evidence-informed frameworks Opportunities to contribute to global learning on recovery through sport Close collaboration with the adidas Foundation Participation in shaping an emerging global program area Strong emphasis on safeguarding and quality programming Potential for long-term growth beyond the initial partnership period Key Dates Activity Date Expression of Interest opens 15 July 2026 Submission deadline 30 August 2026 (11:59 PM CEST) How to Apply Interested organizations should carefully review the complete Expression of Interest Guidelines before preparing their submission. The guidelines include: Complete eligibility requirements Partner profile Submission questions Selection criteria Application process Timeline Additional process details Applications must be submitted before the closing deadline. APPLY HERE What Applicants Should Know Before Applying Applicants should note that: This is a partner selection process. It is not a request for project proposals. Programming will be designed collaboratively. Contexts for implementation will be jointly identified. The Foundation prioritizes evidence, safeguarding, and quality implementation. Long-term collaboration is central to this initiative. Why This Opportunity Matters Children and young people living through conflict, disasters, displacement, and humanitarian emergencies often experience profound disruptions to their emotional well-being, education, social relationships, and daily routines. Recovery Through Sport seeks to explore how structured sport and physical activity can help restore normalcy while complementing broader humanitarian and psychosocial interventions. By investing in experienced organizations and emphasizing collaborative learning, the adidas Foundation aims to strengthen global evidence on sport-based recovery interventions and develop sustainable approaches that can benefit vulnerable communities worldwide. Visit HERE for more information about the Adidas Foundation Expression of Interest 2026 Conclusion The adidas Foundation s Recovery Through Sport Expression of Interest 2026 represents an important opportunity for organizations working in humanitarian response, child protection, mental health, psychosocial support, and sport for development. Rather than funding isolated projects, the Foundation is investing in long-term strategic partnerships built on trust, evidence, collaboration, and shared learning. Organizations with proven operational experience, strong safeguarding systems, and a commitment to improving the lives of children and young people affected by crisis are encouraged to review the guidelines and submit their Expression of Interest before the deadline. Successful partners will play a central role in shaping an innovative global program that seeks to harness the power of sport to support recovery, resilience, and hope for young people facing some of the world s most challenging circumstances. Application Deadline: 30 August 2026 at 11:59 PM CEST For more Grant opportunities, visit OFY HERE The post The Adidas Foundation Expression of Interest 2026: Up to €6 Million Available for Strategic Partners in the New Recovery Through Sport Program appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026: Apply for the Virtual En-ROADS Climate Leadership Training
summary: Applications are open for the Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 , a one-month virtual training programme designed to prepare professionals, educators, policymakers, business leaders and civil society practitioners to facilitate interactive, science-based climate events using the En-ROADS Climate Solutions Simulator. The live cohort will run from 4 August to 4 September 2026 , combining the self-paced Mastering En-ROADS online course with twice-weekly Zoom sessions led by members of the Climate Interactive team and other climate-engagement experts. Participants will learn how to use En-ROADS to explain complex climate and energy systems, explore high-impact climate solutions and lead workshops, simulations and role-playing activities for decision-makers in government, business, finance, education and civil society. Applications for the August 2026 cohort close on 2 August 2026 . The programme requires an estimated commitment of four to six hours per week . No previous experience with En-ROADS is required, and tuition is donation-based. Participants who cannot afford the suggested contribution may still access the training free of charge. About the Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 The Climate Ambassador Accelerator is an intensive virtual professional development programme focused on climate education, systems thinking and practical facilitation. It combines two forms of learning: Self-paced study through the Mastering En-ROADS course Live online sessions featuring expert presentations, questions and answers, facilitation guidance and group discussions The training is intended to help participants move beyond simply understanding climate policy. It prepares them to engage audiences in structured conversations about climate solutions, energy systems, land use, carbon removal, electrification, economic growth and other forces shaping the future of the climate. Participants will learn how to facilitate events for audiences such as: Government officials and policymakers Corporate executives and business leaders Investors and finance professionals University students and academic institutions Civil society organisations Community leaders Climate networks Professional associations Educational institutions By the end of the programme, participants should be able to confidently organise and facilitate their own En-ROADS workshops, Climate Action Simulation games and educational activities. What Is En-ROADS? En-ROADS is an interactive climate policy simulation developed by Climate Interactive and the MIT Sloan School of Management . The simulator allows users to explore how different policy choices may affect global temperature outcomes, energy systems, land use and emissions. Participants can test measures related to areas such as: Renewable energy Coal, oil and natural gas Energy efficiency Electrification Carbon pricing Deforestation Afforestation Methane and other greenhouse gases Population growth Economic growth Technological carbon removal Industry Waste Agricultural emissions Transport and buildings Instead of presenting climate policy as a fixed list of recommendations, En-ROADS allows participants to experiment with different combinations of solutions and observe how those choices interact. According to the programme information, En-ROADS has been used by more than 1.5 million people , including over 25,000 leaders from business, government and higher education programmes. Purpose of the Climate Ambassador Accelerator Climate change discussions often involve complicated scientific, political and economic questions. Even well-informed audiences may struggle to understand which solutions have the greatest potential impact and how different climate interventions influence one another. The Climate Ambassador Accelerator is designed to help participants make these discussions more accessible, interactive and actionable. The programme prepares facilitators to guide audiences through questions such as: Which climate solutions have the greatest potential to reduce future warming? How do energy supply and energy demand interact? What role can electrification play in reducing emissions? How significant are land-use changes and deforestation? What are the limits and opportunities of carbon removal technologies? How do economic growth and population affect emissions? Why are some apparently promising climate solutions less effective than expected? What combination of policies is required to achieve major temperature reductions? Participants will learn not only how to operate the simulator, but also how to explain its results, manage group discussions and adapt events to different audiences. Who Should Join the Climate Ambassador Accelerator? The programme is especially suitable for people who work with decision-makers in: Public policy Government Business Finance Higher education Schools Civil society Sustainable development Climate advocacy Environmental education Corporate sustainability Community engagement It may also be valuable for professionals who regularly organise workshops, training sessions, public consultations, strategic discussions or educational events. The training may be a good fit for applicants who: Want to make climate conversations practical and action-oriented Work with audiences that influence policy, investment, education or organisational strategy Want to lead interactive, science-based climate workshops Are interested in climate systems and climate policy Want to add climate facilitation to their professional skills Can commit four to six hours per week for approximately one month Have at least intermediate English proficiency Are prepared to participate in a virtual international learning environment No previous experience with En-ROADS is required. Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 Training Dates The main programme will run from: 4 August to 4 September 2026 Course modules will become available on 3 August 2026 , with access instructions sent to accepted participants by email. The programme includes five weeks of scheduled learning activities, although the main live training period is described as a one-month programme. Training Format The Climate Ambassador Accelerator is delivered entirely online. The format includes: Short on-demand videos Assigned readings Ungraded quizzes Self-paced online modules Expert-led Zoom presentations Questions and answers with the Climate Interactive team Small-group or breakout discussions Facilitation exercises Recorded sessions for participants who cannot attend live Participants can work through the online course material according to the weekly schedule. Live sessions will be held on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10:00 a.m. EDT , corresponding to GMT-4 during the programme period. Each live session will last approximately 60 minutes and normally include: Around 30 minutes of core expert content Around 10 minutes of questions and answers Around 20 minutes of group discussion The live sessions are designed to complement the self-paced Mastering En-ROADS course rather than repeat it. All sessions will be recorded and made available to participants. Time Commitment Participants should be prepared to dedicate approximately: Four to six hours per week for one month This includes: Completing the weekly course modules Watching training videos Reviewing readings Taking ungraded quizzes Attending or watching the live sessions Participating in discussions and facilitation exercises Practising with the En-ROADS Simulator Attending live is recommended, particularly when sessions include group discussions or breakout activities. However, participants who cannot attend every session can use the recordings. Language Requirement The training is delivered in English. Intermediate English proficiency is recommended because participants will need to: Follow expert presentations Read course materials Participate in discussions Ask and answer questions Practise facilitation Communicate with participants from different countries Lead future En-ROADS events The programme information does not state that an English-language examination certificate is required. Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 Cost The programme uses a donation-based tuition model . Participants are strongly encouraged to contribute at least US$20 , although larger donations are welcomed. However, applicants who cannot afford the suggested donation may still access the training free of charge. The En-ROADS Simulator and course materials are made available through support from Climate Interactive’s funders. The programme should therefore not be described as a paid employment opportunity or a conventional fee-based professional course. It is a donation-supported training opportunity with free access available to those who need it. Additional Regional Sessions Participants in selected regions may receive access to additional sessions addressing local climate conditions and regional policy contexts. The availability, timing and content of these sessions may vary by region. These sessions may help participants connect global climate modelling with: Regional energy systems National climate commitments Local development priorities Climate-vulnerable communities Regional policy debates Local economic and social conditions Skills Participants Will Develop By the end of the programme, participants should be able to: Explore Climate Solutions Participants will understand how to use the En-ROADS Simulator to investigate a wide range of climate policies and technological solutions. Navigate the En-ROADS Simulator Participants will become familiar with: Core controls Policy sliders Temperature outcomes Energy graphs Emissions data Advanced charts and tools Scenario comparison Model assumptions Explain System Dynamics Participants will develop the ability to explain how energy, land use, emissions, population, economic growth and climate systems influence one another. Facilitate Interactive Workshops Participants will learn how to structure and lead En-ROADS Climate Workshops for decision-makers and professional audiences. Lead Climate Action Simulation Games The training will prepare participants to facilitate role-playing exercises in which audience members represent different sectors or stakeholder groups. Adapt Events to Different Audiences Participants will learn how to tailor climate events for: Government leaders Policymakers Corporate boards Business executives Investors Finance professionals University students Educators Civil society organisations Strengthen Climate Communication Participants will practise translating complex climate science into understandable, relevant and actionable discussions. Types of En-ROADS Events There are three primary ways to use the En-ROADS Simulator with an audience. 1. En-ROADS Climate Workshop A workshop allows participants to propose climate solutions and immediately observe how those choices affect the projected global temperature increase and other model outcomes. The facilitator guides the discussion, tests proposals and helps the audience understand why some interventions have greater impact than others. 2. Climate Action Simulation Game This is a role-playing activity in which participants represent different groups involved in climate decision-making. Depending on the format, participants may represent governments, businesses, energy companies, civil society organisations, investors or other stakeholders. The exercise helps participants understand negotiation, competing priorities and the need for coordinated climate action. 3. Student Assignment Educators may use En-ROADS as part of a classroom assignment, course project or university curriculum. Students can develop climate scenarios, test assumptions and analyse the interaction between different policies. En-ROADS Climate Ambassador Certification Completing the Climate Ambassador Accelerator does not automatically make a participant a certified En-ROADS Climate Ambassador. To apply for certification, participants must: Complete the required training Facilitate at least two En-ROADS events Submit an application for Ambassador certification Applications for certification are accepted on a rolling basis, and there is no stated certification deadline. Participants will continue to have access to the training course after the live programme ends, allowing them to complete remaining materials and prepare their first events. Benefits of Becoming a Certified En-ROADS Climate Ambassador Certified Climate Ambassadors become part of a global community of climate facilitators. Ambassadors may have opportunities to: Participate in quarterly online gatherings Attend special events Collaborate with climate leaders from different regions Receive support from the Climate Interactive team Access selected professional opportunities Expand their facilitation portfolio Be listed in the Climate Ambassador directory Make it easier for organisations to contact them Use En-ROADS to inform policy and organisational strategy Build professional credibility in climate education and engagement Most Ambassadors are expected to identify and organise their own opportunities to facilitate events within their professional and community networks. Climate Interactive may occasionally share facilitation opportunities, but certification does not guarantee employment, paid assignments or direct placement in events. What Happens After the Live Training? After the scheduled Zoom sessions conclude, participants will retain access to the online course. There is no stated deadline for completing the remaining self-paced content. Participants may use the post-training period to: Review recorded sessions Practise using the simulator Complete unfinished modules Design an En-ROADS workshop Identify suitable audiences Facilitate their first two events Apply for Climate Ambassador certification This flexible access is particularly useful for participants who cannot complete every activity during August. Can Applicants With an Existing Mastering En-ROADS Account Apply? Yes. People who already have a Mastering En-ROADS account can apply to the Climate Ambassador Accelerator. Accepted participants can sign in with their existing account after receiving programme instructions and register for the live sessions. Having an existing account does not prevent participation. What If a Participant Cannot Attend Every Live Session? Live attendance is encouraged but not mandatory for every session. All sessions will be recorded and made available to participants. Participants should attend live where possible because group discussions and breakout activities may be difficult to reproduce through recordings. Nevertheless, the recorded format provides flexibility for applicants in different time zones or with professional commitments. What If Someone Cannot Participate in August 2026? Applicants who cannot join the August cohort may still take the self-paced Mastering En-ROADS course throughout the year. The course is available year-round through Climate Interactive’s online learning platform. However, participants taking only the self-paced course may not receive the same live expert sessions, cohort discussions and networking experience offered through the Climate Ambassador Accelerator. Climate Ambassador Accelerator Information Session An information session was scheduled for 7 July 2026 at 8:00 a.m. EDT . The session was intended to help prospective applicants understand: The training format The time commitment The En-ROADS Simulator Certification requirements Live-session expectations Whether the programme matched their professional goals Because the scheduled date has passed, prospective applicants should check whether a recording is available. How to Apply for the Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 Interested applicants must complete the official programme application to reserve a place in the August cohort. Before applying, candidates should be prepared to provide information about: Their professional background Their involvement in climate, policy, business, finance, education or civil society The audiences they work with Their interest in En-ROADS How they expect to use the training Their ability to commit four to six hours per week Their English-language ability Their plans for facilitating future climate events Applicants should submit the application before the deadline and monitor their email for acceptance instructions. Programme modules will become available on 3 August 2026 , making the period between the application deadline and the programme launch very short. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications for the Climate Ambassador Accelerator close on: 2 August 2026 The training begins on 4 August 2026 , while course modules and participant instructions are expected to become available on 3 August 2026 . Applicants should apply as early as possible rather than waiting until the final day. Important Dates Information session: 7 July 2026 at 8:00 a.m. EDT Application deadline: 2 August 2026 Modules available: 3 August 2026 First live session: 4 August 2026 Main training period: 4 August–4 September 2026 Final scheduled week: 31 August–5 September 2026 Climate Ambassador certification: Rolling applications with no deadline Important Points to Consider Before Applying Prospective participants should understand that: The programme is conducted in English. Intermediate English proficiency is recommended. The programme requires four to six hours per week. Live sessions are scheduled according to Eastern Daylight Time. The course is virtual. Live attendance is recommended but recordings are available. No prior En-ROADS experience is required. Tuition is donation-based. A contribution of at least US$20 is encouraged. Participants who cannot afford the contribution may access the training free of charge. Completing the course does not automatically result in Ambassador certification. Certification requires facilitating at least two En-ROADS events. Certification does not guarantee employment or paid facilitation opportunities. Conclusion The Climate Ambassador Accelerator 2026 offers an accessible and practical route for professionals who want to lead stronger, more informed climate conversations. By combining the Mastering En-ROADS online course with live expert-led sessions, the programme helps participants understand climate-system dynamics while developing the practical skills required to facilitate workshops, role-playing games and educational activities. The programme is particularly relevant for professionals working with decision-makers in government, business, finance, education and civil society. It may also be valuable for climate advocates, sustainability professionals, educators and community leaders who want a structured, science-based way to engage their networks. No previous experience with En-ROADS is required, and participants who cannot afford the suggested donation may still take part for free. However, applicants must be ready to commit four to six hours per week and participate in an English-language virtual learning environment. Applications close on 2 August 2026 , and the programme begins on 4 August 2026 . For more information about this opportunity, click here . Discover more global job opportunities, click here . title: 2026–2027 United Nations UNSCAR Application Cycle: Apply for Funding to Advance Conventional Arms Regulation and Disarmament Initiatives
summary: The United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs (UNODA) has officially launched the 2026–2027 United Nations Trust Facility Supporting Cooperation on Arms Regulation (UNSCAR) Application Cycle , inviting eligible organizations worldwide to submit project proposals that strengthen conventional arms regulation, improve weapons management, and contribute to international peace and security. UNSCAR is a multi-donor trust fund established to provide focused and effective financial support for initiatives that enhance the implementation of international conventional arms control instruments. Through competitive annual funding calls, the programme supports innovative projects that build national and regional capacities, strengthen policy frameworks, and reduce the risks associated with illicit conventional weapons. Organizations working in disarmament, arms control, security sector reform, weapons management, or related research are encouraged to submit proposals before the application deadline. About the United Nations UNSCAR Programme The United Nations Trust Facility Supporting Cooperation on Arms Regulation (UNSCAR) is managed by the United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs (UNODA) . The trust fund was created to strengthen global cooperation on conventional arms regulation by providing financial assistance to organizations implementing projects that improve arms control, enhance weapons and ammunition management, and support international peace and security. Each year, UNSCAR issues a Call for Proposals through a competitive selection process. The programme funds projects that align with its strategic objectives and address priority themes identified in the annual call. In addition to the regular funding cycle, UNSCAR also provides Special-Circumstances Projects to respond rapidly to emergency situations involving weapons management. Objectives of the Programme UNSCAR seeks to: Strengthen conventional arms regulation. Improve national and regional weapons management systems. Support the implementation of international arms control agreements. Build institutional and technical capacities. Promote international cooperation on disarmament. Reduce illicit trafficking and misuse of conventional weapons. Contribute to sustainable peace, security, and development. Who Can Apply? Applications are welcomed from organizations with legal status, including: United Nations system partners Regional organizations International organizations Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) Research institutes Member States that wish to access UNSCAR funding should partner with an eligible organization that can submit a proposal on their behalf. Project Requirements To be considered for funding, project proposals must: Be consistent with the objectives of UNSCAR. Align with the annual selection criteria, including funding limits and implementation timelines. Address one or more priority areas identified in the annual Call for Proposals. UNSCAR particularly encourages the submission of small-scale, high-impact projects . Special-Circumstances Projects In addition to the annual funding cycle, UNSCAR accepts applications throughout the year for Special-Circumstances Projects . These projects: Receive funding of up to USD 200,000 . Support rapid responses to emergency situations involving weapons management. Can be submitted at any time during the year. Application Process Applicants must use the official UNSCAR application templates available on the programme website. Each application must include: Completed Application Form. Logical Framework (Logframe), including a detailed implementation plan. Detailed Project Budget. All documents must: Be completed in English. Be submitted together. Be sent before the application deadline. Once submitted, proposals and budgets cannot be amended. Selection Process Following the submission deadline, all applications undergo a competitive review process. Projects are evaluated based on: Relevance to UNSCAR objectives. Technical quality of the proposal. Expected impact. Feasibility of implementation. Budget justification. Contribution to international cooperation on conventional arms regulation. Successful projects are expected to begin implementation from 1 January 2027 . Requirements for Selected Applicants Organizations selected for funding will work closely with UNODA to finalize project documentation before signing the Grant Agreement. Additional documents may include: Detailed implementation schedule. Risk assessment and mitigation strategy. Evidence of support from recipient governments (where applicable). Coordination plans with other UNSCAR implementing partners. UNSCAR encourages close collaboration among implementing organizations to maximize impact and avoid duplication of activities. Monitoring and Reporting Successful applicants are required to maintain high standards of programme management and accountability. Implementing partners must submit: Interim narrative reports. Interim financial reports. Final narrative reports. Final financial reports. UNSCAR also encourages applicants to include robust monitoring, evaluation, and auditing mechanisms within their project proposals. Important Dates Application Cycle Opens: July 2026 Online Briefing Session: 28 July 2026 (9:00 AM EDT) Application Deadline: 31 August 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT Project Implementation Begins: 1 January 2027 Applicants are encouraged to submit their proposals well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. How to Apply Interested organizations should download the official application forms and guidelines from the UNSCAR website before preparing their proposals. Application Link: https://www.un.org/disarmament/unscar/ Applications and supporting documents should be submitted electronically to: Email: unscar-unoda@un.org For detailed guidance, eligibility requirements, and downloadable application forms, visit the official UNSCAR webpage. Conclusion The 2026–2027 UNSCAR Application Cycle offers a valuable opportunity for eligible organizations to secure funding for projects that strengthen conventional arms regulation, improve weapons management, and promote international peace and security. Through its competitive funding process, UNSCAR supports innovative initiatives that build capacity, encourage international cooperation, and contribute to safer communities worldwide. Organizations with impactful project ideas are encouraged to prepare strong proposals and submit their applications before 31 August 2026 . Discover more grants opportunities like this on the OFY Opportunities webpage. title: Slovakia Scholarships for Talented International Students 2026/27: Study in Europe and Receive Up to €15,000
summary: Applications are available for the Slovakia Scholarships for Talented Students from All Over the World for the 2026/2027 academic year , an international funding opportunity created to attract talented students to selected public and state higher education institutions in the Slovak Republic. The scholarship supports eligible international students who wish to pursue full-time bachelor’s, combined bachelor’s and master’s, or master’s degree studies in Slovakia. Successful applicants may receive €500 per month for ten months of each academic year , with support lasting up to three years for bachelor’s or combined programmes and up to two years for master’s programmes. This means that eligible bachelor’s and combined-degree students may receive up to €15,000 , while master’s students may receive up to €10,000 over two academic years. The programme is open to applicants from around the world, including certain Slovaks living abroad, provided they meet the academic, residency, admission and standardised-test requirements. The official application banner states that applications are open and must be submitted by 31 July 2026 at 23:59 CEST . Applicants should nevertheless check the active application portal carefully, because a later section of the published information appears to contain older wording stating that registration had not yet opened. About the Slovakia Scholarships for Talented International Students The scholarship programme is part of Slovakia’s effort to attract talented international students and strengthen higher education in fields connected to the country’s development priorities. It is intended for students who plan to begin or continue eligible higher education studies in Slovakia during the 2026/2027 academic year . The programme supports study at selected public or state Slovak higher education institutions. Applicants must choose an eligible full-time programme connected to the Smart Specialisation Strategy of the Slovak Republic, SK RIS3 2021+ . This means that not every university, faculty or degree programme in Slovakia will automatically qualify. Applicants must confirm that both their chosen institution and study programme appear on the official list of supported programmes before submitting their scholarship application. The scholarship is designed to support talented students while encouraging them to pursue studies in areas considered important for Slovakia’s academic, economic, scientific and technological development. Scholarship Value and Financial Support The scholarship provides a monthly payment of: €500 per month Paid for ten months of each academic year Normally covering the period from September to June The academic year in Slovakia begins on 1 September and ends on 31 August of the following year, but scholarship payments are provided for ten eligible months rather than the full twelve-month period. Funding for Bachelor’s Students Students enrolled in an eligible full-time bachelor’s programme may receive: €5,000 per academic year Up to three academic years of support A maximum total value of €15,000 Funding for Combined Bachelor’s and Master’s Students Students enrolled in a supported combined bachelor’s and master’s programme may receive: €5,000 per academic year Support for the first three academic years A maximum total value of €15,000 The scholarship does not necessarily fund the entire duration of a longer combined programme. The published information specifies support for the first three continuing years. Funding for Master’s Students Students enrolled in an eligible full-time master’s programme may receive: €5,000 per academic year Up to two academic years of support A maximum total value of €10,000 Although the programme is promoted as offering scholarships of up to €15,000, the maximum available to a two-year master’s student is normally €10,000 under the stated monthly payment structure. Number of Scholarships Available The programme plans to award up to 225 scholarships across bachelor’s, combined bachelor’s and master’s study levels. Bachelor’s and Combined Degree Scholarships Up to 170 scholarships may be awarded to students entering bachelor’s or combined bachelor’s and master’s programmes. These places are divided as follows: 110 scholarships for students attending public higher education institutions outside the Bratislava region 60 scholarships for students attending public higher education institutions in the Bratislava region Master’s Scholarships Up to 55 scholarships may be awarded to master’s students. These places are divided as follows: 35 scholarships for students attending public higher education institutions outside the Bratislava region 20 scholarships for students attending public higher education institutions in the Bratislava region The Ministry may adjust the number of awards where necessary. During the evaluation process, applicants may also be organised into geographical groups covering Europe; the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Oceania; South America; Central America and Africa; and Asia. Eligible Levels of Study The scholarship applies only to the following study levels: Full-time bachelor’s degree programmes Full-time combined bachelor’s and master’s programmes Full-time master’s degree programmes The scholarship does not support doctoral or PhD studies. All supported programmes must be: Full-time Conducted in person Delivered at an eligible public or state Slovak higher education institution Included within the selected areas of Slovakia’s Smart Specialisation Strategy Part-time, external or distance-learning programmes do not qualify. Eligibility for Bachelor’s Applicants Applicants seeking funding for a bachelor’s or combined bachelor’s and master’s programme must generally meet the following conditions: They must be applying from abroad. They must have completed their secondary education outside Slovakia. They must plan to begin an eligible bachelor’s or combined programme in Slovakia during the 2026/2027 academic year. They must not have previously studied at a higher education institution in Slovakia, except through an eligible academic mobility arrangement. They must not have previously attended secondary school in Slovakia, subject to the stated exception for qualifying Slovaks living abroad. They must apply to or receive admission from a supported public Slovak higher education institution. At the time of submitting the scholarship application, it may be sufficient for the applicant to have already applied to the university. However, the student must eventually be admitted, officially enrolled and begin the eligible programme before scholarship payments can be made. Eligibility for Master’s Applicants Master’s scholarships are available to several categories of applicants. International Graduates Applying from Abroad Applicants may qualify if they: Completed their bachelor’s degree outside Slovakia Are entering a master’s programme in Slovakia for the first time Apply to an eligible full-time master’s programme at a supported institution Students Progressing From a Slovak Bachelor’s Degree Applicants who completed a bachelor’s degree at a Slovak higher education institution may also qualify if they: Progress directly and continuously to the master’s level Have not previously received support under the relevant Recovery and Resilience Plan scholarship scheme Previous Scholarship Recipients Students who previously received support under the earlier Recovery and Resilience Plan scholarship scheme at bachelor’s level may qualify if they: Successfully complete their bachelor’s degree Progress continuously to an eligible master’s programme For master’s applicants, previous study at a Slovak higher education institution does not automatically disqualify the applicant. Citizenship and Residence Requirements Applicants must normally hold citizenship of a country other than Slovakia. Citizenship must be demonstrated through an acceptable identity document, generally: A valid passport A national identity card for eligible citizens of the European Union, European Economic Area or Switzerland Dual citizens who hold both Slovak citizenship and another citizenship may apply under the stated rules. Slovaks living abroad may also qualify, but they must submit the appropriate certificate issued under Slovak legislation concerning Slovaks living abroad. Applicants must also demonstrate that they have not held permanent residence in Slovakia at any time from 1 January 2021 until the date of submitting the scholarship application . This condition is normally confirmed through a hand-signed solemn declaration. Temporary residence in Slovakia may not automatically make an applicant ineligible. The published announcement specifically notes that some holders of temporary residence permits may still qualify, depending on the programme’s conditions and exceptions. Admission to a Slovak University The scholarship application and university admission process are separate. Receiving the scholarship does not automatically mean that the applicant has been admitted to a university. Similarly, applying to a university does not automatically produce a scholarship application. Applicants must therefore complete two distinct processes: Apply directly to an eligible Slovak higher education institution for admission. Submit a separate online application for the scholarship. Applicants should communicate with their preferred university as early as possible to confirm: Whether the programme is supported Admission requirements Required academic documents Language requirements Tuition fees Recognition of previous qualifications Enrolment dates Programme-specific deadlines The official scholarship information strongly advises applicants to contact their selected institution early to avoid delays or misunderstandings. Standardised Test Requirement The selection process is based on the applicant’s results in an approved standardised test. Applicants must submit results from either: The SAT, administered by the College Board; or The SCIO Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites tests The standardised-test result is described as the only criterion used to determine the ranking of eligible applicants. Documents such as the CV and motivation letter are still mandatory, but applicants who do not meet the required test threshold will not proceed in the selection process. Minimum SAT Score Applicants submitting SAT results must achieve: A minimum total SAT score of 1,100 points Equivalent to approximately the 63rd percentile under the programme’s stated system SAT results from tests taken between 1 January 2021 and the application deadline may be accepted. The announcement identified 6 June 2026 as the latest relevant SAT date for the current cycle. Applicants applying close to the July deadline would therefore generally need to have already taken the examination and obtained an eligible result. Minimum SCIO Score Applicants using SCIO results must take both: Mathematics, known as MAT General Academic Prerequisites, known as VŠP The applicant must achieve an average percentile of at least 63 across the two tests. The application system calculates the average using the percentile achieved in each examination. Applicants must submit an official SCIO certificate. One SCIO test alone is not sufficient because both Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites are required. Selection Process After the application deadline, the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic or the relevant higher education institutions will verify submitted applications. The assessment may include confirmation of: Citizenship Residence history Educational background University application or admission Eligibility of the selected programme Full-time study status Standardised-test score Completeness and authenticity of documents Compliance with all declarations and requirements Eligible applicants will be ranked according to their accepted SAT or SCIO results. Applicants below the minimum threshold will not be considered. Meeting the minimum score does not guarantee selection because the number of scholarships is limited and the applicant’s ranking among other eligible candidates will also matter. Preliminary and final lists of successful applicants will be prepared after verification and enrolment procedures. Scholarship payments begin only after the student has: Been officially admitted Enrolled at the selected institution Commenced the eligible study programme Completed the required administrative process Where administrative delays occur, eligible payments may be made retroactively for the months during which the student qualified. Documents Required for the Application Applicants should prepare the following documents. 1. Identity Document Applicants must provide a certified copy of a valid passport or another accepted identity document. 2. Declaration of Permanent Residence A hand-signed solemn declaration must confirm that the applicant has not held permanent residence in Slovakia between 1 January 2021 and the application deadline. 3. Certificate for Slovaks Living Abroad This is required only for applicants applying under the special eligibility provisions for Slovaks living abroad. 4. Legal Guardian’s Consent Applicants under 18 must submit a hand-signed consent form from their legal guardian concerning the processing of personal data. 5. SAT or SCIO Certificate Applicants must provide proof of: An SAT score of at least 1,100; or An average SCIO percentile of at least 63 across Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites 6. University Acceptance Letter Applicants should upload an acceptance letter from a Slovak higher education institution where available. The published rules indicate that an applicant may still apply for the scholarship after applying to the university but before receiving final admission. Nevertheless, official admission and enrolment will be required before the scholarship can be awarded and paid. 7. Curriculum Vitae A structured CV in English is mandatory. The official template should be used where required by the application portal. 8. Motivation Letter Applicants must submit a motivation letter in English using the official template. The motivation letter should explain: Why the applicant wants to study in Slovakia Why the selected programme is appropriate How the applicant demonstrates talent What the applicant hopes to achieve academically and professionally Both the CV and motivation letter are described as essential application documents. How to Apply Applications must be submitted electronically through the official scholarship portal. Applications cannot be submitted by email. A complete application should include: Personal and citizenship information Education details Information about the chosen Slovak institution and programme SAT or SCIO results Certified identity documentation Required solemn declarations CV Motivation letter Supporting documents applicable to the applicant’s circumstances Applicants should not wait until the final day. The application may require certified documents, signatures, test certificates and information from a university, all of which may take time to organise. The active application announcement states that registration is open until 31 July 2026 . APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline for the Slovakia Scholarships for Talented International Students is: 31 July 2026 at 23:59 Central European Summer Time Applicants should confirm the time-zone difference in their country and submit well before the portal closes. Because the source material contains both an active application notice and older wording that registration had not yet opened, applicants should rely on the current online portal status and verify that the submission function is active before preparing a last-minute application. Tuition Fees The scholarship does not create an automatic universal tuition-fee waiver. Students admitted to a full-time foreign-language programme at a public Slovak higher education institution may have their tuition fees waived under the relevant Slovak legislation. However, the final decision belongs to the individual higher education institution. Applicants should therefore ask their chosen university: Whether tuition fees apply Whether scholarship recipients qualify for a waiver Whether the waiver covers the full tuition amount Whether any administrative or programme fees remain payable A scholarship applicant should not assume that receiving €500 per month also guarantees free tuition. Health Insurance Scholarship recipients may qualify for public health insurance in Slovakia under the applicable legislation where they: Do not have permanent residence in Slovakia Are not already insured in another European Union member state, European Economic Area contracting state or Switzerland Hold a scholarship under a programme approved by the Slovak Government Applicants should verify their individual insurance position before travelling, particularly because insurance arrangements may differ according to citizenship, residence status and existing coverage. Visa and Temporary Residence Requirements Non-EU students may need a national visa and temporary residence permit for study. Applicants currently outside Slovakia are advised to apply for a national Type D visa through the Slovak embassy or an authorised external service provider responsible for their country of residence. The published guidance recommends applying for a 120-day national D visa connected to a temporary-residence application for study. After arriving in Slovakia, students must apply for temporary residence for study within the permitted period. Students already legally present in Slovakia may be able to apply through a Foreign Police office. The scholarship does not remove the applicant’s responsibility to satisfy immigration, visa and residence requirements. Applicants should begin these procedures early, because university enrolment and scholarship eligibility may be affected by delays. Conditions for Keeping the Scholarship Successful applicants must remain enrolled in an eligible full-time programme. The scholarship may be lost where the student: Terminates the supported study programme Transfers to a different higher education institution Changes from full-time to part-time or external study Repeats a study year in circumstances not permitted by the programme Loses student status Interrupts studies beyond the permitted period Submits false or altered documents Fails to comply with inspections connected to the scholarship A student may be allowed to change to another eligible programme within the same institution if the studies remain continuous and the student does not lose their status, restart the first year or repeat an academic year. The scholarship cannot normally be transferred from one university to another. Important Application Advice Applicants should take the following steps before applying: Confirm that the chosen university is a public or state Slovak institution. Check that the selected programme appears on the eligible Smart Specialisation list. Apply separately for university admission. Confirm whether the programme is full-time and conducted in person. Verify that an eligible SAT or SCIO result is available. Prepare certified identity documents. Complete all required declarations by hand where instructed. Prepare the English CV and motivation letter. Confirm tuition-fee arrangements with the university. Research visa, temporary residence and health-insurance requirements. Submit the scholarship application before 31 July 2026. Keep copies of every document and submission confirmation. Applicants should also remember that reaching the minimum test score does not guarantee an award. Selection remains competitive because applicants are ranked and the number of available scholarships is limited. Conclusion The Slovakia Scholarships for Talented International Students 2026/27 provide a substantial opportunity for international students seeking to pursue higher education in the heart of Europe. With funding of €500 per month, eligible bachelor’s and combined-degree students may receive up to €15,000, while eligible master’s students may receive up to €10,000. The programme is available across selected academic fields and public or state higher education institutions in Slovakia. However, the application process is demanding. Applicants must satisfy citizenship and residence conditions, choose an eligible study programme, apply separately to a Slovak university, submit a valid SAT or SCIO result, prepare all required documents and complete the online application before the deadline. Interested students should begin by confirming programme eligibility and reviewing their standardised-test results. A complete application must be submitted by 31 July 2026 at 23:59 CEST . For more information about this opportunity, click here . Discover more global job opportunities, click here . title: ICEGOV 2026 Scholarships: Apply for Free Conference Registration and a $300 Grant to Attend the International Conference on Theory and Practice of Electronic Governance
summary: The International Conference on Theory and Practice of Electronic Governance (ICEGOV) 2026 has officially opened applications for its scholarship programme, offering accepted paper authors the opportunity to attend one of the world s leading conferences on digital governance with financial support. Organized by the United Nations University Operating Unit on Policy-Driven Electronic Governance (UNU-EGOV), the ICEGOV Scholarship Programme is designed to increase participation from students and researchers, particularly those from emerging economies. The initiative helps reduce financial barriers, enabling scholars to present their research, engage with global experts, and strengthen their academic and professional networks. Since its introduction in 2014, the programme has awarded approximately 300 scholarships to researchers from 56 countries, with about 85% of recipients coming from low-, lower-middle-, and upper-middle-income economies. Applications are currently open and must be submitted by 24 July 2026 . What is the ICEGOV Scholarship Programme? The ICEGOV Scholarship Programme supports authors whose research papers have been accepted for presentation at ICEGOV 2026. The scholarship aims to encourage broader global participation by assisting researchers who may otherwise face financial challenges in attending the conference. Successful applicants receive support that allows them to participate in discussions on electronic governance, digital transformation, public policy innovation, sustainable development, and citizen engagement while presenting their own research before an international audience. About ICEGOV The International Conference on Theory and Practice of Electronic Governance (ICEGOV) is one of the world s most respected conferences focusing on Digital Governance. Established in 2007, ICEGOV serves as an international platform where: Researchers present cutting-edge studies. Governments share policy innovations. International organizations exchange best practices. Industry leaders discuss technological advancements. Civil society organizations contribute practical perspectives on governance. The conference has been hosted in 16 cities across 15 countries on six continents, reflecting its truly global reach. Today, ICEGOV is coordinated by the United Nations University Operating Unit on Policy-Driven Electronic Governance (UNU-EGOV), headquartered in Guimarães, Portugal. UNU-EGOV functions as a policy-oriented think tank within the United Nations system, focusing on: Digital Governance Sustainable Development Public Sector Innovation Social Inclusion Active Citizenship Evidence-Based Policymaking Scholarship Benefits Selected applicants will receive: Free registration for ICEGOV 2026. A lump-sum financial support of USD $300 . The scholarship is intended to reduce participation costs and make attendance more accessible for researchers from developing and emerging economies. Expenses Not Covered Applicants should note that the scholarship does not cover: International airfare Local transportation Accommodation Visa expenses Personal expenses during the conference Recipients are expected to finance these costs independently. Because travel arrangements and visa processing can take considerable time, applicants are encouraged to begin preparations as early as possible after their papers have been accepted. Who Will Receive Priority? As scholarship funding is limited, preference will be given to applicants who satisfy both of the following conditions: They are enrolled as students during the 2025/26 academic year. They are citizens or residents of countries classified by the World Bank as: Low-income economies Lower-middle-income economies Upper-middle-income economies Applicants meeting both conditions have the strongest likelihood of selection. Student Eligibility Requirements For scholarship purposes, a student is defined as someone officially enrolled in one of the following programmes during the 2025/26 academic year: Bachelor s Degree Master s Degree Doctoral (PhD) Degree Applicants enrolled in postdoctoral programmes are not considered students under this scholarship policy. Student applicants must also submit proof of enrolment in English (PDF format) by email to the conference organizers to verify their eligibility. Scholarship Payment Conditions The USD $300 grant is subject to attendance requirements. Recipients must: Attend the conference in person. Participate throughout all four conference days. Attend the Doctoral Colloquium if their accepted paper is scheduled for that session. The financial support will be transferred to the recipient s bank account after the conference. Applicants should note that payment processing may take up to two months following the event. Required Information for the Scholarship Application Applicants will be required to provide the following details: Full name (matching passport or national ID) Email address Gender (for statistical purposes only) Country of residence Nationality Institutional affiliation and country Accepted paper title and paper ID Student status Scholarship motivation statement explaining why financial assistance is needed Student applicants must additionally email proof of enrolment for the 2025/26 academic year. Important Application Rules Applicants should carefully follow the scholarship guidelines. Key rules include: Submit only one scholarship application. If multiple applications are submitted, only the most recent submission will be considered. Only one author from each accepted paper may apply. If multiple co-authors of the same paper submit scholarship applications, all related applications may be disqualified. Following these rules carefully is essential to avoid losing eligibility. Why You Should Apply Receiving an ICEGOV Scholarship offers numerous academic and professional advantages. These include: Presenting your research at an internationally recognized conference. Networking with researchers, policymakers, government officials, and international organizations. Learning about the latest developments in Digital Governance and Electronic Governance. Gaining international visibility for your research. Building collaborations for future academic and professional opportunities. Receiving financial support that reduces conference participation costs. For students and early-career researchers, the programme provides valuable exposure to the global research community while enhancing academic development. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Deadline: 24 July 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete their applications well before the deadline and ensure all required documents, including proof of enrolment (where applicable), are submitted correctly. For more scholarships, visit the OFY website HERE Conclusion The ICEGOV 2026 Scholarship Programme represents an outstanding opportunity for researchers and students whose papers have been accepted for presentation at one of the world s leading conferences on digital governance. By providing free conference registration and a USD $300 financial contribution, the programme helps make international academic participation more accessible, particularly for scholars from emerging economies. If you meet the eligibility requirements and have an accepted paper, submitting a strong scholarship application before 24 July 2026 could significantly enhance your opportunity to participate in this prestigious global event while expanding your professional network and contributing to discussions shaping the future of electronic governance. title: One Young World Academy Introduces Planetary Leadership Course 2026: Free Online Learning Opportunity for Young Leaders Tackling Global Existential Threats
summary: As the world faces increasingly interconnected challenges such as climate change, artificial intelligence risks, global health emergencies, conflicts, and environmental degradation, there is a growing need for a new generation of leaders capable of addressing these complex issues through collaboration and long-term thinking. To help prepare young leaders for this responsibility, the One Young World Academy has launched an innovative online learning programme titled Introduction to Planetary Leadership . Developed with the sponsorship of the InterAction Council , this globally recognized e-learning course introduces participants to the concept of planetary leadership, explores humanity s most pressing existential threats, and presents Strategy X-EXIST , a comprehensive framework designed to safeguard the future of humanity. The programme offers participants expert-led instruction, practical leadership insights, and an internationally recognized digital certificate upon successful completion. It is specifically designed for professionals, community leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs, NGO workers, and young changemakers who are passionate about creating sustainable solutions to global challenges. Whether you work in climate action, public health, peacebuilding, technology governance, education, public service, or community development, this free online course provides valuable knowledge and practical tools to help you become a more effective global leader. About the One Young World Academy The One Young World Academy is an internationally recognized digital learning platform that equips young leaders with knowledge, leadership skills, and practical solutions to solve some of the world s biggest challenges. Through expert-led courses, participants gain access to world-class educational content developed by internationally respected organizations and thought leaders. The Introduction to Planetary Leadership course expands this mission by helping learners understand how today s interconnected global crises require coordinated international leadership and innovative thinking. The programme emphasizes collaboration between governments, scientists, civil society organizations, businesses, communities, and young people to collectively build a safer and more sustainable future. What is Planetary Leadership? Planetary leadership is a leadership model that encourages people to think beyond national borders and individual sectors. Rather than solving problems independently, planetary leadership recognizes that global issues are interconnected and require cooperation among multiple stakeholders. The course demonstrates how young leaders can contribute to building resilient societies capable of responding to existential threats through collaboration, responsible governance, innovation, and long-term planning. Participants will learn why leadership in the modern world must focus not only on immediate challenges but also on protecting future generations.
