title: United Nations Fund for Population Activities (UNFPA): APRO Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Partnership Call 2026
summary: Background of the UNFPA Asia-Pacific Regional Programme (APRO) UNFPA is launching a new Asia and Pacific Regional Programme covering the period from 2026 to 2029. The programme is aligned with the UNFPA Strategic Plan for the same period and the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development. The regional programme is intended to accelerate progress toward UNFPA’s three transformative results: Ending the unmet need for family planning Ending preventable maternal deaths Ending gender-based violence and harmful practices The programme also seeks to strengthen responses to demographic change while ensuring that no one is left behind. This includes promoting accessible, inclusive and rights-based programming for persons with disabilities and other populations facing exclusion. Its implementation covers the humanitarian-development-peace continuum, recognizing that sexual and reproductive health, gender equality and protection needs must be addressed in development settings, emergencies and fragile or conflict-affected environments. Why UNFPA Is Prioritizing Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Technological innovation and digitalization have created important opportunities to improve access to services, information, education and communication. However, digital platforms have also become environments in which violence against women and girls can be committed, intensified or extended. UNFPA’s approach recognizes an online-offline continuum. This means that violence occurring through digital technologies cannot always be separated from violence occurring in homes, workplaces, schools, communities or public spaces. Technology-facilitated abuse may affect survivors’ safety, privacy, dignity, access to services and participation in public life. Effective programming therefore requires more than isolated online-safety activities. It demands coordinated work involving survivor-centred services, legal and policy systems, digital security, technology design, evidence, ethical data management and prevention. UNFPA APRO is seeking partners that can contribute specialized knowledge and operational capacity to strengthen both the prevention of TFGBV and the response available to survivors across Asia and the Pacific. Purpose of the UNFPA Expression of Interest The purpose of the call is to identify qualified organizations that can collaborate with UNFPA APRO in delivering the Asia-Pacific Regional Programme. Selected partners may support activities involving: Specialized technical assistance Capacity-strengthening and professional training Survivor-centred support services Prevention and response programming Digital safety and security Legal and policy advice Research and evidence generation Monitoring and evaluation Technology-sector engagement Evidence-based advocacy Innovation and service delivery Eligible entities selected through the process will sign an Implementing Partnership Agreement with UNFPA APRO. This agreement will regulate the technical collaboration and partnership arrangement. Subject to the availability of funds, UNFPA APRO will subsequently work with successful implementing partners to agree on a work plan and enter into a funded collaboration. Selection through the Expression of Interest process therefore creates a potential pathway to funded implementation, but the announcement does not guarantee funding or state a predetermined grant amount. Organizations Invited to Submit an Expression of Interest UNFPA APRO is inviting Expressions of Interest from several categories of legally registered entities. Academic and research institutions Universities, research centres, think tanks and other academic institutions may apply where they possess relevant expertise in areas such as: Gender-based violence Digital safety Technology and society Public policy Human rights Law and justice Social research Monitoring and evaluation Statistical measurement Data systems Survivor-centred programming Academic applicants should demonstrate not only theoretical expertise but also their capacity to translate research into practical programming, policy advice, training or evidence-based advocacy. Civil society organizations Eligible civil society applicants include local and international NGOs, women-led organizations, youth-led organizations, civil society networks and rights-based organizations. Such organizations may be particularly relevant where they have direct experience working with: Survivors of gender-based violence Women and girls in diverse circumstances Young people Frontline responders Human rights defenders Women’s rights movements Youth rights movements High-risk civic actors Communities affected by humanitarian emergencies People facing digital exclusion or online threats Professional associations and regional technical bodies Professional associations and specialized regional institutions may submit an EOI where they can contribute technical knowledge, standards, training systems, practitioner networks or policy support. These may include associations or technical bodies working in social services, public health, law, justice, policing, digital technology, data governance, cybersecurity, research, evaluation or other relevant areas. Organizations of persons with disabilities Organizations of persons with disabilities are expressly included among eligible entities. Their participation can help ensure that TFGBV prevention and response systems are inclusive, accessible and designed around the rights and lived experiences of persons with disabilities. Specialized private-sector entities Private-sector entities may apply where appropriate, particularly when they possess specialized expertise in: Technology-facilitated gender-based violence Digital security Online safety Digital evidence Information management Safe technology development Ethical technology design Safety-by-design principles Private-sector participation must be relevant to the workstream proposed and consistent with UNFPA’s rights-based, ethical and survivor-centred requirements. Four Main TFGBV Workstreams Organizations may express interest in one or more of four specialized pillars. Pillar 1: Response The response pillar focuses on strengthening services, systems and professional capacity to assist survivors of technology-facilitated gender-based violence safely, ethically and confidentially. Training and capacity building Selected partners may help adapt and roll out UNFPA’s global TFGBV training package for frontline responders. Target participants may include professionals working in: Social work Health services Justice systems Police and law enforcement Local government Gender-based violence services Humanitarian response Training may be implemented across priority countries, including humanitarian contexts. Partners may also support the revision of national gender-based violence referral mechanisms so that they adequately incorporate survivor-centred responses to technology-facilitated abuse. This work is important because referral systems designed only for conventional forms of violence may not fully address digital evidence, online threats, data privacy, account security or the continuing relationship between online and offline harm. TFGBV responder support network UNFPA APRO intends to facilitate a regional support network for TFGBV responders. The network would allow digital programmers, gender-based violence specialists and frontline responders to exchange: Practical experience Technical guidance Response protocols Lessons from implementation Emerging risks Promising practices Referral approaches Survivor-safety considerations Qualified partners may be expected to help establish, coordinate or provide technical support to this network. Regional survivor-support mechanism The call includes the potential establishment of a regional mechanism providing safe, ethical and confidential services to survivors of technology-facilitated gender-based violence. Organizations interested in this area should be able to demonstrate strong safeguards relating to: Survivor confidentiality Informed consent Data protection Referral management Risk assessment Ethical case handling Staff training Accessibility Protection from retaliation or further harm Digital forensics Partners may be selected to develop or support digital-forensic protocols for TFGBV cases. These protocols should ensure that the collection and storage of digital evidence are: Safe Ethical Survivor-centred Confidential Technically reliable Consistent with relevant legal and protection requirements Digital evidence can be highly sensitive. Poor collection or storage practices may expose survivors to further harm, compromise confidentiality or weaken legal and institutional responses. Safe digital and information-management systems The response pillar also covers systems used by GBV service providers to manage digital information. Partners may support the design or implementation of secure systems that protect data held by organizations managing TFGBV cases. This may involve reinforcing survivor-centred information-management systems and helping service providers reduce risks such as unauthorized access, insecure storage, inappropriate information sharing or loss of sensitive case information. Pillar 2: Prevention The prevention pillar focuses on reducing the risk of TFGBV before harm occurs and strengthening the ability of vulnerable groups and frontline actors to operate safely in digital environments. Resilience of high-risk actors Selected partners may strengthen the digital security, safety and operational resilience of groups facing elevated online risks. These groups may include: Frontline responders Women’s rights movements Youth rights movements Human rights and civic actors Professionals managing sensitive survivor information Relevant interventions could include training, risk assessment, security protocols, technical guidance and institutional digital-safety measures. Diverting young people from harmful online subcultures The call also seeks support for developing digital-literacy modules and targeted programmes intended to divert young people away from the manosphere and other harmful online subcultures. This workstream requires organizations capable of developing prevention approaches that are: Evidence-based Age-appropriate Gender-responsive Culturally relevant Suitable for digital delivery Focused on long-term behavioural and social change Applicants proposing work under this area should clearly explain their experience with young people, online cultures, gender norms, digital literacy or violence-prevention programming. Pillar 3: Enabling Environment The enabling-environment pillar addresses the laws, policies, technologies, standards and financial systems that influence how TFGBV is prevented and addressed. Rights-based laws and policies Partners may help strengthen the ability of governments and civil society organizations to develop and implement laws and policies addressing technology-facilitated gender-based violence. Activities may include: Specialized legal advice Policy analysis Drafting support Peer learning Mentorship Institutional capacity development Rights-based assessment of existing legislation The focus should be on legal and policy approaches that protect survivors and promote rights without creating unintended harm, exclusion or excessive restrictions. Digital governance and technology-industry standards UNFPA APRO is also seeking expertise related to gender-responsive digital governance and technology-industry practices. Partners may advocate for or support the implementation of: Safety-by-design principles Ethical technology development Gender-responsive digital governance Improved technology-sector standards Safer digital products Platform policies addressing TFGBV Prevention measures built into technology before harm occurs Safety by design means considering user protection and foreseeable risks during the design and development of digital services rather than responding only after abuse has occurred. Sustainable financing Organizations may contribute evidence and investment cases that influence national planning and budgeting. The objective is to encourage governments to allocate dedicated resources for TFGBV prevention and response rather than treating technology-facilitated violence as an unfunded or temporary policy issue. This work may involve: Costing interventions Developing financing cases Budget analysis Public-finance advocacy Evidence-based investment proposals Engagement with national planning institutions Applicants interested in this component should be capable of connecting technical TFGBV programming with national planning, public budgets and sustainable financing mechanisms. Pillar 4: Research, Data and Evaluation The fourth pillar focuses on building the evidence, measurement systems and ethical monitoring frameworks needed to improve TFGBV programmes and policies. Ethical monitoring and evaluation Partners may support the development of monitoring and evaluation frameworks for TFGBV programmes. These frameworks should contain appropriate: Indicators Means of verification Data-collection methods Progress measures Outcome measures Impact-assessment approaches Ethical safeguards Monitoring systems must be survivor-centred and should not create additional risks for survivors or expose confidential information. The resulting evidence should help UNFPA and its partners assess implementation, understand impact and improve future programming and policy. Evidence generation and knowledge sharing Selected entities may generate, synthesize and share evidence concerning TFGBV prevention and response at: Regional level Subregional level National level This may include: Trend analysis Literature reviews Comparative research Programme evaluations Policy research Documentation of promising practices Evidence briefs Knowledge products Regional learning initiatives Statistical standards and prevalence measurement The call includes support for developing statistical standards and testing methods for measuring the prevalence of technology-facilitated gender-based violence. Organizations interested in this work should demonstrate expertise in areas such as survey design, gender statistics, research ethics, measurement, methodology development or sensitive-data collection. Administrative-data systems Partners may also help improve existing administrative-data systems by integrating variables that allow reported TFGBV cases to be identified and tracked. This work must balance the need for accurate information with survivor safety, confidentiality, informed consent and responsible data governance. Selection Criteria UNFPA APRO will assess applicants against several technical and institutional requirements. Legal registration Applicants must be legally registered entities. Both not-for-profit organizations and, where appropriate, for-profit organizations may be considered. Applicants should be prepared to provide official registration documents and evidence of their legal status. Technical capacity The organization must demonstrate proven experience and expertise in at least one of the four TFGBV pillars. A strong submission should clearly explain: The workstream or workstreams selected Relevant previous projects Technical methodologies used Results achieved Populations or institutions supported Geographic coverage Relevant publications, tools or training materials The organization’s comparative advantage Institutional capacity Applicants must demonstrate the institutional ability to implement activities effectively. UNFPA expects evidence of: Established internal governance Clear operational policies Human-resource policies Adequate staffing Results-based management capacity Robust monitoring and evaluation systems Suitable implementation and reporting arrangements Applicants should avoid making unsupported statements about institutional strength. Claims should be backed by policies, organizational structures, previous performance or concrete examples. Financial capacity Organizations must have experience managing funds and a sound financial-management system. The required financial capacity includes: Robust internal controls Fraud-prevention policies Established accounting procedures Reliable financial reporting Evidence of responsible fund management The organization’s financial systems must be supported by recent unqualified audit reports, such as audit reports covering the last two years. An unqualified audit opinion generally means that the external auditor concluded that the financial statements were presented fairly in all material respects under the relevant reporting framework. Applicants whose latest audit reports contain qualifications should carefully assess whether they meet this criterion before applying. Ethical standards Potential partners must demonstrate their commitment to UNFPA policies and ethical standards. Particular emphasis is placed on UNFPA’s zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, commonly addressed through Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse requirements. Applicants should be able to demonstrate appropriate safeguarding policies, reporting mechanisms, staff conduct requirements and accountability procedures. Geographical relevance The applicant must have a demonstrated track record of successfully managing and implementing programmes in Asia and the Pacific. The announcement does not expressly require every applicant to be headquartered within the region. However, organizations must provide credible evidence of relevant implementation experience, partnerships, networks or operational capacity in Asia and the Pacific. Required Expression of Interest Documents Interested organizations must prepare an Expression of Interest containing the following elements. 1. Cover letter The cover letter should identify: The organization submitting the EOI The selected area or areas of interest The relevant TFGBV pillar or pillars How the organization aligns with the UNFPA Asia-Pacific Regional Programme Why the organization is interested in collaborating with UNFPA APRO The organization’s principal comparative advantage The cover letter should be direct, evidence-based and tailored to the specific call. 2. Evidence of technical expertise Applicants must provide evidence of their technical capacity and record of similar work. Relevant evidence may include: Previous project descriptions Completion reports Evaluation findings Research publications Training materials Policies or technical tools developed Contracts or partnership agreements Examples of survivor-centred services Digital-safety programmes Advocacy outcomes Relevant organizational profiles Experience working with United Nations agencies is considered an advantage, although the announcement does not state that previous UN experience is mandatory. 3. Evidence of partnerships and networks Applicants must explain their partnerships, networks and comparative advantage within Asia and the Pacific. This may include relationships with: Government institutions Civil society networks Women-led organizations Youth-led organizations Research institutions Technology-sector actors Survivor-service providers Organizations of persons with disabilities Regional bodies International development partners The submission should explain how these networks would help the applicant deliver regional, subregional or national-level work. 4. Proposed modalities of engagement Applicants must indicate how they propose to collaborate with UNFPA APRO. Possible modalities identified in the call include: Technical support Research Advocacy Innovation Service delivery Organizations may propose more than one modality where this is consistent with their capacity and the selected workstream. A strong proposal should explain the proposed approach, expected contribution, institutional role and how the organization would coordinate with UNFPA and other partners. How to Submit the UNFPA APRO Expression of Interest Applications must be submitted by email. Submission email: apro.office@unfpa.org Required subject line: EOI on TFGBV Application deadline: 14 August 2026 Applicants should ensure that the correct subject line is used so the submission can be properly identified and routed. Before sending the email, organizations should verify that: The cover letter is signed by an authorized representative. The selected TFGBV workstream is clearly identified. All supporting evidence is attached. The organization’s legal name and contact information are accurate. Attached files open correctly. File names are clear and professionally formatted. The email is sent to the correct address. A copy of the complete submission is retained. Delivery confirmation or an email record is preserved. The official announcement does not specify a required application portal or closing time. Applicants should therefore follow the stated email-submission process and send their EOI before the deadline date. Funding and Partnership Arrangements The call does not publish a fixed grant amount, budget ceiling or guaranteed level of financial support. Eligible entities selected through the process will enter into an Implementing Partnership Agreement with UNFPA APRO. Subject to funding availability, UNFPA APRO will then coordinate with successful implementing partners to agree on a work plan and establish a funded collaboration. Organizations should therefore understand the process as involving two stages: Identification of technically and institutionally qualified partners through the Expression of Interest. Development of an agreed work plan and funded collaboration, subject to available resources. Submission of an EOI does not itself guarantee selection, funding or a specific financial award. Practical Tips for Preparing a Strong Submission Select only relevant workstreams Applicants should not claim expertise across all four pillars unless they can provide substantial evidence. A focused application demonstrating deep experience in one or two areas may be more credible than a broad application containing unsupported claims. Connect experience directly to TFGBV General experience in gender equality, gender-based violence or information technology may not be sufficient on its own. Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their experience relates to the interaction between digital technology and gender-based violence. Demonstrate survivor-centred practice Organizations proposing response, data, forensic or information-management activities should explain how they protect: Safety Privacy Confidentiality Dignity Informed consent Accessibility Survivor decision-making Provide evidence, not promotional language Statements such as “we are a leading organization” or “we have extensive experience” should be supported by: Project dates Countries covered Funding managed Outputs delivered People or institutions reached Evaluations completed Policies influenced Systems established Review financial documentation early Because recent unqualified audit reports are specifically mentioned, applicants should confirm the availability and status of their latest external audits before preparing the complete EOI. Explain regional value Applicants should show how their proposed contribution would be relevant beyond a single isolated activity. This may include regional networks, transferable tools, multilingual capacity, cross-country experience, policy connections or the ability to adapt interventions for different Asia-Pacific contexts. Submit before 14 August 2026 The official notice does not specify a closing hour. Applicants should not wait until the final day, especially where internal approvals or large supporting documents are involved. APPLY HERE. Conclusion The UNFPA APRO Expression of Interest presents a significant institutional collaboration opportunity for organizations working at the intersection of gender-based violence, technology, digital safety, survivor services, public policy, research, data and human rights. Through the call, UNFPA seeks partners capable of contributing to four major areas: survivor-centred response, prevention, an enabling legal and technological environment, and research, data and evaluation. Eligible organizations must demonstrate legal registration, relevant technical expertise, institutional governance, sound financial systems, appropriate ethical standards and a record of programme implementation in Asia and the Pacific. Successful entities may enter into an Implementing Partnership Agreement with UNFPA APRO and subsequently develop a funded work plan, subject to the availability of resources. Organizations considering an application should identify the workstream that best matches their expertise, assemble strong technical and financial evidence, explain their regional comparative advantage and submit the complete Expression of Interest to apro.office@unfpa.org using the subject line “EOI on TFGBV” no later than 14 August 2026 For more global opportunities, click HERE. title: YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator 2026: Empowering Young Entrepreneurs to Expand Across African Markets
summary: The YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator 2026 is a growth-focused initiative designed to help ambitious young entrepreneurs expand established businesses into new African markets. Developed in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the African Union (AU), the programme supports export-ready youth-led enterprises seeking to strengthen their export capacity, overcome barriers to intra-African trade and scale beyond their domestic markets. The initiative is particularly aligned with the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and its Protocol on Women and Youth in Trade. It seeks to increase the participation of young entrepreneurs in regional commerce while helping businesses become more competitive, investment-ready and capable of creating sustainable employment opportunities. What Is the YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator? The YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator, also known as the E-Accelerator , is a results-driven programme for young entrepreneurs whose businesses are already established locally and are ready to expand beyond their national borders. Rather than offering a traditional grant, the programme focuses on strengthening businesses so they can become more prepared for regional trade and international expansion. Selected enterprises may receive tailored support designed around their specific business needs, export potential and growth challenges. The programme aims to help participating enterprises: Strengthen their export capacity. Prepare for entry into new African markets. Improve their competitiveness. Overcome non-tariff barriers to trade. Navigate complex customs and regulatory requirements. Improve their access to finance and investment opportunities. Build stronger regional business networks. Expand their operations across African markets. Create more productive and sustainable jobs for young people. Who Is the Programme Designed For? The 2026 pilot phase is focused on young entrepreneurs and youth-led enterprises operating in six African countries: Rwanda Uganda Senegal The Gambia Zambia Zimbabwe Applicants should be under 35 years old and operate an already established business at the local level. The programme is designed for enterprises that are ready to move beyond their domestic markets and explore opportunities for expansion across Africa. This means the E-Accelerator is particularly suited to entrepreneurs who already have a functioning business and are looking to take the next step toward regional or continental growth. Important: This Is Not a Grant-Only Opportunity The YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator clearly states that the programme is not designed for applicants who are only looking for grants. The E-Accelerator is intended for ambitious, growth-oriented businesses that are prepared to invest effort and resources into their own expansion. Applicants should be interested in building a competitive enterprise capable of participating in intra-African trade. The programme focuses on business development, export readiness, market expansion and access to opportunities rather than simply providing direct financial grants. How the Export Accelerator Supports African Youth-Led Businesses Many young enterprises face significant barriers when trying to expand into other countries. These challenges can include complex customs procedures, regulatory requirements, limited knowledge of foreign markets, difficulties accessing finance and weak systems for connecting businesses with potential regional partners. The E-Accelerator adopts a systemic approach to addressing these challenges. Instead of offering only general training, the programme is designed to understand the specific needs of participating enterprises and provide support that is tailored to their individual growth and export journeys. The programme will help qualified businesses work toward: Export readiness. Business strengthening. Market expansion. Improved access to investment and finance. Better understanding of regulatory and trade requirements. Greater ability to navigate non-tariff barriers. Increased participation in intra-African trade. The YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator Journey The programme consists of several stages designed to take participating enterprises from initial assessment through to export opportunities and continental business exposure. 1. Application and Diagnostics The process begins with the Youth-Led Enterprise Registration and Diagnostic Form. Applicants are expected to provide information about their businesses, growth aspirations and current operations. The information collected through the application will help inform the diagnostic process. The diagnostic stage is important because it provides the foundation for identifying the specific areas where an enterprise may require support. Applicants are encouraged to provide complete and accurate information, including both mandatory and optional details where applicable. The information may also support future engagement with other relevant opportunities. 2. Selection and Announcement of the Pilot Cohort Following the application and diagnostic stage, eligible enterprises will be assessed for participation in the pilot cohort. The selected businesses will be announced as part of the next stage of the programme. Selection is expected to focus on enterprises with strong growth potential and the capacity or ambition to expand into intra-African markets. 3. Export FitLab Selected enterprises will participate in the Export FitLab, which is designed to help businesses understand their export potential and identify the steps required to become more competitive in regional markets. This stage may help enterprises examine their current business models, products, services, market readiness and expansion opportunities. 4. Tailored Enterprise Advisory Participating businesses will receive individualized support based on their specific needs. The advisory component is designed to move beyond a one-size-fits-all approach. Instead, support will be tailored to help each enterprise address its own challenges and strengthen its ability to expand. Possible areas of focus may include: Business growth strategies. Export readiness. Market entry. Regulatory requirements. Trade processes. Access to finance. Business competitiveness. Regional expansion planning. 5. Continental Bootcamp The programme also includes a Continental Bootcamp during the YouthConnekt Africa Summit. This stage will provide opportunities for participating entrepreneurs to connect with other young business leaders, gain additional knowledge and engage with broader continental networks. It may also create opportunities for exposure to potential partners, investors and other stakeholders involved in Africa s entrepreneurial ecosystem. 6. Business Export Accreditation A further stage of the programme is Business Export Accreditation. This component is intended to support the recognition and strengthening of participating enterprises as businesses that are better prepared for export and regional trade. Export accreditation can help businesses demonstrate their preparedness and improve their credibility when engaging with potential markets and partners. 7. Facilitated Intra-African Export Through Policy Sandboxes One of the distinctive features of the E-Accelerator is the use of Policy Sandboxes. These sandboxes are intended to help qualified enterprises navigate and address barriers that can make cross-border trade difficult. The approach will begin with the six pilot countries: Rwanda Uganda Senegal The Gambia Zambia Zimbabwe By addressing practical trade challenges, the programme aims to facilitate smoother export processes and improve the ability of youth-led businesses to participate in intra-African markets. 8. Exposure to Continental Business and Financing Opportunities The final component of the journey connects participating enterprises with wider business and financing opportunities across the continent. This may help businesses build relationships, explore new markets, identify potential investment opportunities and connect with relevant stakeholders who can support their expansion. Why This Programme Matters for Young African Entrepreneurs Young entrepreneurs are central to Africa s economic transformation, but many youth-led businesses remain focused on local markets because of the challenges involved in expanding across borders. The YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator aims to help address some of these challenges by supporting businesses that have already established a local foundation and are ready to grow. The programme can help participating entrepreneurs move from simply operating a business in one market to exploring opportunities in the wider African economy. Its broader objectives include: Supporting youth participation in regional trade. Strengthening youth-led enterprises. Supporting the implementation of the AfCFTA. Addressing non-tariff barriers. Improving business competitiveness. Mobilizing investment. Supporting sustainable job creation. Expanding opportunities for intra-African commerce. What Applicants Should Know Before Applying The application form is described as lengthy because it is designed to collect detailed information about the applicant and the enterprise. Applicants should therefore be prepared to provide information that can help programme organizers understand: The nature of their business. The current stage of business development. Their growth ambitions. Their readiness to expand beyond their domestic market. Their potential export opportunities. The challenges affecting their expansion. Their interest in the programme s value proposition. Applicants should complete the form carefully and provide accurate information. The quality and completeness of the information submitted may help inform the diagnostic process and future tailored advisory support. No Participation Fees YouthConnekt Africa states that it does not charge fees for participation in its programmes. Applicants should also be aware that neither YouthConnekt Africa staff nor its partners should request payment or contact applicants through personal channels regarding programme applications. Applicants are advised to verify the authenticity of any communication they receive and rely only on official communication channels. How to Apply Interested young entrepreneurs should begin by reviewing the programme information and completing the official YouthConnekt Africa Export Accelerator registration and diagnostic form. Applicants should: Confirm that they meet the basic age and country requirements. Ensure that their enterprise is already established locally. Consider whether their business is genuinely ready for growth beyond national borders. Review the programme s value proposition carefully. Complete the application and diagnostic questions accurately. Provide as much relevant information as possible to support the diagnostic process. Submit the form through the official application process. The programme is intended for entrepreneurs who are serious about expanding their businesses and participating in the wider African market. Through diagnostics, tailored enterprise advisory, export readiness support, accreditation, policy sandboxes, continental networking and exposure to business and financing opportunities, the programme seeks to help promising youth-led enterprises overcome some of the barriers that limit their participation in intra-African trade. title: ICGEB Arturo Falaschi SMART Fellowships September 2026: Fully Funded International Research Mobility Fellowship for Early-Career Scientists
summary: The ICGEB Arturo Falaschi SMART Fellowship Programme 2026 is now accepting applications from eligible researchers in ICGEB Member States. Offered by the International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB), this prestigious fellowship promotes international scientific mobility by supporting researchers to undertake advanced research training in another ICGEB Member State. The fellowship is designed to strengthen scientific cooperation, develop technical expertise, and encourage long-term collaboration between research institutions. Successful applicants will spend between 3 and 9 months at a host laboratory, gaining hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies while contributing to collaborative research projects in the life sciences. Whether you are a PhD student, postdoctoral researcher, or an early-career scientist, this fellowship offers a valuable opportunity to expand your research skills, build international collaborations, and advance your scientific career. About the ICGEB Arturo Falaschi SMART Fellowship Programme The Scientific Mobility for Advanced Research Training (SMART) Fellowship Programme was established to promote research collaboration between laboratories located in different ICGEB Member States. The programme enables scientists to receive practical training in technologies and methodologies that may not be available in their home institutions. A major objective of the programme is to strengthen scientific partnerships. Therefore, applicants are expected to demonstrate a strong collaborative research project jointly prepared by both the home and receiving laboratories. Supervisors from both institutions are strongly encouraged to work together during the proposal development stage to ensure a high-quality application. Applications are welcome in all areas of the Life Sciences, making this fellowship suitable for researchers from diverse scientific disciplines. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will receive funding for research visits lasting: Minimum duration: 3 months Maximum duration: 9 months The fellowship supports temporary scientific mobility and is not intended for long-term degree programmes or extensions of existing fellowships. Fellowship Benefits The ICGEB SMART Fellowship provides comprehensive financial support to selected fellows, including: International economy-class return airfare Monthly living stipend Health insurance Research mobility support Access to internationally recognized laboratories Hands-on training using advanced technologies Opportunities to establish long-term international scientific collaborations Monthly Stipend Selected fellows receive: USD 1,500 per month for PhD fellows USD 2,000 per month for Postdoctoral fellows In addition, a USD 500 monthly bench fee may be provided directly to the receiving laboratory to support research consumables required for the approved research project. Eligible Research Areas Applications are accepted in any area of the Life Sciences, including but not limited to: Biotechnology Molecular Biology Genetics Biomedical Sciences Agricultural Biotechnology Environmental Sciences Cell Biology Microbiology Biochemistry Bioinformatics Eligibility Criteria Applicants must meet the following requirements: Be nationals of an ICGEB Member State . Be actively working in a recognized research institution. Be registered for a PhD or have obtained a PhD within the last five years. Young scientists holding an MSc or an equivalent qualification are also encouraged to apply. Demonstrate a clear research collaboration between their home and receiving laboratories Apply to undertake research in another ICGEB Member State (not their own). There is no age limit for applicants. However, preference is given to scientists at the early stages of their research careers. SMART Fellowships are not intended to: Support attendance at conferences or workshops. Extend previous fellowship visits. Provide bridge funding before or after another fellowship programme. New Two-Stage Application Process ICGEB has introduced a new application procedure consisting of two stages. Stage 1 : Fellowship Expression of Interest Application Period: 1 July – 14 August 2026 Applicants must: Select their preferred host laboratory. Identify a prospective supervisor. Submit an online Expression of Interest through the ICGEB Service Gateway. Only applicants who complete this stage successfully will proceed to the next phase. Stage 2 : Full Fellowship Application Application Period: 16 – 30 September 2026 Applicants selected by their prospective supervisors will receive an invitation to submit the complete fellowship application through the ICGEB Service Gateway. Required Documents Applicants will need to upload the following documents: Full Curriculum Vitae (CV) CV of the Head of the Receiving Laboratory (including publications) Valid passport or national identity card Applicants should also ensure that both the Home Laboratory and Receiving Laboratory complete their respective sections before the application deadline. Applications lacking confirmation from both laboratories will not be considered. Selection Criteria Applications are reviewed by the ICGEB Fellowships Selection Committee based on: Scientific excellence of the proposed project Applicant s academic and research achievements Expected career impact Benefits to both home and host institution Suitability of the host laboratory Availability of expertise and research facilities Strength of the collaboration between institutions Additional institutional support from the host laboratory, such as accommodation or supplementary living support, may positively influence the evaluation. Bench Fee Support A monthly **USD 500 bench fee** may be awarded to the host laboratory for laboratory consumables directly related to the approved research project. Eligible expenses include: Laboratory reagents Chemicals Cell culture materials PCR and qPCR consumables Laboratory plastics and glassware Pipettes and laboratory consumables The funding cannot be used for equipment purchases, travel expenses, administrative costs, office supplies, software, or institutional overheads. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to allow both laboratories sufficient How to Apply Interested applicant time to complete the required confirmations. Applicants should carefully read the official application guidelines before beginning the online application process through the ICGEB Service Gateway. For detailed guidelines, application forms, FAQs, and additional fellowship resources, visit the official ICGEB fellowship Conclusion The ICGEB Arturo Falaschi SMART Fellowship Programme 2026 offers an outstanding opportunity for early-career researchers to gain international research experience while strengthening scientific collaboration across ICGEB Member States. Through generous financial support, advanced laboratory training, and international networking opportunities, the fellowship enables researchers to enhance their expertise and contribute meaningfully to scientific innovation in the life sciences. Eligible scientists are encouraged to prepare their applications early and take advantage of this prestigious international research opportunity. title: The Kennan Institute Digital Fellowship 2026–2027: Receive $12,000 in Funding to Advance Research on Russia and Eurasia (Fully Virtual)

Supported generously by the Lounsbery Foundation and the U.S. Russia Foundation , the fellowship provides six months of financial support, professional mentorship, networking opportunities, and publication assistance for outstanding scholars and experts from around the world. Fellows become part of an international community of researchers while contributing meaningful work that reaches policymakers, scholars, and the broader public. The fellowship responds to the growing need for renewed intellectual engagement between scholars from the former Soviet region and the wider international community. Through its fully digital format, the program removes geographical barriers and enables researchers worldwide to collaborate, exchange ideas, and contribute to informed policy discussions. Each fellowship lasts six months and combines financial assistance with professional development, mentorship, editorial support, and networking opportunities. Participants will work closely with the Kennan Institute throughout the fellowship while developing research projects designed to inform both academic audiences and policymakers. Professional Mentorship Participants will benefit from guidance provided by the Kennan Institute s network of internationally recognized experts. Monthly Virtual Meetings Fellows will participate in: Monthly virtual cohort meetings Discussions with fellow researchers Collaborative knowledge sharing Research progress updates Peer feedback sessions These meetings help create a collaborative international research community. 4. Publication Support An important feature of the fellowship is assistance with communicating research to broader audiences. Each fellow will work with Kennan Institute staff to develop and edit a final publication intended for: Policymakers Researchers Journalists The general public Possible publication formats include: Research articles Multimedia projects Documentary or short films Digital exhibitions Other public-facing formats 6. Global Alumni Network Upon completion of the fellowship, participants become members of the Kennan Institute s distinguished alumni network, which includes: More than 4,500 professionals worldwide This network offers long-term opportunities for collaboration, research partnerships, and professional growth. Fellowship Timeline The 2026–2027 Digital Fellowship will run from: October 1, 2026 – March 31, 2027 Following the fellowship period, participants may also have opportunities to engage in additional Kennan Institute events. Research Areas Supported The fellowship welcomes proposals covering Russia and the broader Eurasian region across numerous disciplines. Examples include: Political science International relations History Economics Sociology Security studies Public policy Journalism Technology Artificial intelligence Medicine Environmental science Natural sciences Regional studies Cultural studies Media studies Interdisciplinary research proposals are also encouraged. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is intended for experienced professionals whose work centers on Russia or the broader Eurasian region. Ideal applicants include: University researchers Faculty members Independent scholars Journalists Policy analysts Think tank researchers Subject matter experts Scientific researchers Technology specialists Medical researchers Applicants should demonstrate meaningful experience within their chosen research area. Apply here Fellowship Requirements During the fellowship, selected participants are expected to: Attend monthly virtual meetings. Participate actively in cohort discussions. Collaborate with Kennan Institute staff. Develop their research project throughout the fellowship. Produce a publication or public-facing research output. Language Requirement The fellowship is conducted entirely in: English Applicants should therefore possess a good working knowledge of English. Required Application Documents Applicants must complete the online application and submit: Completed application form Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume Research Proposal (maximum three pages) The research proposal should include: Previous experience with the proposed research topic. title: UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition 2026: Win Up to USD 750 by Showcasing the Power of TVET Through Photography
summary: The UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition 2026 is now open for submissions, inviting both amateur and professional photographers from around the world to showcase how Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) is transforming lives, empowering young people, and creating sustainable futures. The international competition offers photographers the opportunity to have their work recognized by UNESCO while competing for cash prizes of up to USD 750. Photography has long served as a powerful storytelling tool capable of documenting change, inspiring action, and highlighting the realities of communities across the world. Through this year s competition, UNESCO-UNEVOC seeks compelling visual stories that demonstrate how vocational education equips individuals with practical skills, promotes innovation, strengthens inclusion, advances sustainability, and prepares young people for the future of work. Whether you capture a young engineer, a green energy technician, a robotics student, or a skilled artisan, your photograph could become part of UNESCO s global efforts to promote the importance of skills development. Applications are now open, with submissions accepted until 31 August 2026 . About the UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition The Skills in Action Photo Competition is organized by UNESCO-UNEVOC, UNESCO s International Centre for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). The initiative celebrates the transformative impact of vocational education by encouraging photographers to capture authentic moments that reflect how technical and vocational skills contribute to: Innovation Social inclusion Sustainable development Green economies Digital transformation Youth employment Equal opportunities The competition aims to increase global awareness of TVET while providing photographers with an international platform to showcase their creativity and storytelling abilities. Successful entries will highlight how practical skills are helping individuals and communities address current and future global challenges. Competition Categories Participants may submit photographs under one or more of the following four competition themes. 1. Equity and Inclusion Photographs in this category should demonstrate that skills development opportunities should be accessible to everyone regardless of: Gender Nationality Ethnicity Disability Socio-economic background Participants are encouraged to capture stories that reflect diversity, equal opportunities, and inclusive vocational education. 2. Green Skills and Sustainability This category highlights the growing importance of environmentally sustainable skills. Entries may feature: Renewable energy Green jobs Sustainable agriculture Eco-friendly technologies Circular economy initiatives Resource-efficient practices Climate-smart vocational training The objective is to illustrate how TVET contributes to environmental sustainability and climate resilience. 3. Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence The future of work increasingly depends on digital skills. UNESCO welcomes photographs showing young people participating in: Coding Artificial intelligence Robotics Automation Virtual reality Digital manufacturing Emerging technologies Images should reflect how digital transformation is shaping vocational education. 4. Innovation and Excellence This category recognizes creative approaches to vocational education and skills development. Suitable entries may showcase: Innovative teaching methods Modern vocational training facilities Technical excellence Productive workplaces Creative problem-solving Advanced industrial practices The photographs should demonstrate how innovation improves quality, productivity, and efficiency. How Many Entries Can You Submit? Participants may submit: One photograph per competition category. A maximum of four photographs in total. Each submission must correspond to one of the official competition themes. Competition Prizes Outstanding photographers will receive the following cash awards: First Prize: USD 750 Second Prize: USD 500 Third Prize: USD 350 In addition to the monetary awards, winners will also receive: An official UNESCO-UNEVOC certificate. Publication of their winning photographs on the UNESCO-UNEVOC Flickr account. Promotion across UNESCO-UNEVOC s official social media platforms. International exposure through UNESCO s communication channels. Winning the competition offers photographers an opportunity to gain worldwide recognition while contributing to UNESCO s advocacy for technical and vocational education. Ownership of Submitted Photographs Applicants should note that all submitted photographs become the property of UNESCO-UNEVOC. The organization may use submitted images in: Future publications Promotional materials Media campaigns Awareness campaigns Educational resources Communication activities Participants should therefore ensure they fully understand these terms before submitting their work. Eligibility Requirements To participate, applicants must meet the following requirements: Be at least 18 years old. Be the owner or copyright holder of every submitted photograph. Failure to satisfy these conditions may result in disqualification. Photo Submission Requirements Every photo submission must include: A photo title. A brief description of no more than 75 words. Information indicating where the photograph was taken. Information indicating when the photograph was taken. A completed submission form. Providing complete and accurate information helps judges understand the context behind each image. Technical File Specifications Submitted photographs must satisfy the following technical requirements: JPEG format is mandatory. RAW or TIFF files may be included as supplementary files and are considered an advantage. The longest side of the image must measure at least 3,000 pixels. Minor digital adjustments are permitted, provided they are disclosed in the submission form. Applicants are encouraged to submit high-quality images that preserve important details and visual clarity. Competition Do s Participants are encouraged to: Select one or more official competition categories. Submit high-resolution images. Ensure the longest side measures at least 3,000 pixels. Maintain a resolution of 300 DPI/PPI. Obtain consent from all identifiable individuals appearing in the photographs. Declare all digital edits in the submission form. Submit photographs in JPEG format. Include RAW or TIFF files where available. Following these recommendations will improve compliance with competition requirements. Competition Don ts Participants should avoid the following: Submitting photo collages. Combining multiple images into one frame. Adding logos. Adding watermarks. Adding signatures. Adding graphic overlays. Submitting photographs unrelated to the official themes. Using AI-generated images. Using artificial intelligence to generate, extend, or manipulate parts of a photograph. Failure to comply with these rules may result in disqualification. How to Submit Your Entry Applicants should carefully follow the submission process below. Step 1 Complete and sign the official submission form. Be sure to indicate the competition category for each photograph. Step 2 Prepare your email submission. The subject line should include: Your Last Name – SAPC26 Submission Example: Muller – SAPC26 Submission Step 3 Attach: Your completed submission form. Your photograph(s). Step 4 Send your submission by email to: unevoc.skills@unesco.org Step 5 If your files exceed email size limits: Upload them to a cloud storage platform. Include a publicly accessible sharing link. Ensure the link does not require login credentials, permission requests, or additional approvals. Selection Criteria All eligible entries will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Relevance to the competition theme. Originality. Creativity. Innovative communication of the intended message. The judging panel will assess both the artistic quality of the photograph and its ability to communicate the importance of technical and vocational education. Announcement of Winners The winners will be officially announced through UNESCO-UNEVOC s digital platforms. Successful participants should monitor UNESCO-UNEVOC s official communication channels for announcements and updates following the close of the competition. Why You Should Apply Participating in the UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition provides far more than an opportunity to win cash prizes. It offers photographers the chance to: Gain international recognition. Showcase their storytelling abilities. Promote the importance of vocational education. Inspire future generations. Contribute to UNESCO s global education initiatives. Expand their professional portfolio. Reach worldwide audiences through UNESCO s international platforms. Whether you are documenting innovation in manufacturing, women breaking barriers in engineering, sustainable agriculture, digital technology, or youth entrepreneurship, your images can help shape global conversations on the future of skills. Visit HERE for more information about the UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition 2026 Application Deadline Submission Deadline: 31 August 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare and submit their entries well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical challenges. APPLY HERE Conclusion The UNESCO-UNEVOC Skills in Action Photo Competition 2026 presents an outstanding opportunity for photographers to combine creativity with global impact. By capturing authentic stories of Technical and Vocational Education and Training, participants can demonstrate how skills development is driving innovation, promoting inclusion, supporting sustainability, and preparing young people for the rapidly evolving world of work. With attractive cash prizes, international recognition, and the opportunity to have your work featured by UNESCO, this competition is ideal for photographers passionate about education, youth empowerment, sustainable development, and visual storytelling. If you have compelling images that reflect the transformative power of TVET, now is the time to share them with a global audience before the 31 August 2026 deadline. title: GitLab Foundation Powering Economic Opportunity Fund 2026: Up to $500,000 in Flexible Grants for Workforce Development Organizations in the United States
summary: Empowering Organizations to Create Lasting Economic Opportunities for American Workers The GitLab Foundation has officially launched the second round of its Powering Economic Opportunity Fund (PEOF) , a major funding initiative designed to strengthen workforce development across the United States. Through this initiative, the Foundation is committing $4 million in flexible grant funding to support organizations that partner directly with employers, unions, and industry leaders to improve job quality, expand work-based learning opportunities, and create sustainable career pathways for workers. Rather than simply supporting training programs, the Powering Economic Opportunity Fund focuses on transforming employer practices that help workers remain employed, advance professionally, and achieve long-term income growth. Organizations selected under this funding opportunity may receive grants of up to $500,000 over a period of one to two years. About the Powering Economic Opportunity Fund The Powering Economic Opportunity Fund is part of a broader two-year, $16 million partnership between the GitLab Foundation and the Families and Workers Fund. The initiative was created to address one of today s biggest workforce challenges: although thousands of workers receive skills training every year, many struggle to remain employed or advance into long-term careers. The Foundation believes that solving this challenge requires improving employer practices—not just worker training. Round 2 of the program therefore places greater emphasis on employer-side innovations that improve employee retention, career progression, workplace quality, and long-term earning potential. Why This Fund Matters The United States is experiencing major economic transformation driven by several rapidly expanding sectors, including: Clean and renewable energy Advanced manufacturing Infrastructure development Skilled construction trades Industrial technology Demand for skilled professionals such as electricians, welders, energy technicians, construction managers, and industrial specialists continues to increase. At the same time: Many experienced workers are retiring. Employers face growing shortages of skilled labor. Artificial Intelligence is reshaping the labor market by reducing many entry-level knowledge jobs. Workers increasingly need access to durable career opportunities offering stable wages and long-term growth. The GitLab Foundation believes that investing in better employer practices can help bridge this gap and produce lasting economic benefits for workers. Funding Available Successful applicants may receive: Maximum grant amount: Up to $500,000 Funding pool: $4 million Grant duration: One year Two years Flexible funding that allows organizations to implement innovative workforce solutions. What the Fund Supports The Powering Economic Opportunity Fund is specifically interested in initiatives that improve long-term employment outcomes rather than only increasing training participation. Priority will be given to projects that strengthen relationships between employers and workforce organizations while improving worker success. Areas of interest include: 1. Employer Partnerships Every application must include an active partnership with at least one of the following: Employer Labor union Industry association Workforce industry partner Strong partnerships may include: Hiring commitments Employer-recognized credentials Curriculum co-development Employer co-investment Apprenticeships Work-based learning opportunities Applications that do not include an active employer or industry partnership will not move beyond the concept note stage. 2. Employer Practice Change The Foundation seeks projects that improve workplace quality through employer-led innovations. Examples include: Structured career progression pathways Better supervisory and management practices Employer-funded education programs Predictable work schedules Childcare support initiatives Employee retention strategies Career advancement programs Workplace policies that improve long-term earnings 3. Durable Impact Applicants should demonstrate how successful practices will continue after grant funding ends. Possible long-term sustainability models include: Employer investment Collective bargaining agreements Public funding Other long-term financing mechanisms The Foundation is particularly interested in projects capable of producing lasting improvements in worker earnings over time. Expected Impact The GitLab Foundation prioritizes initiatives that generate measurable economic outcomes. Its goal is to create projects capable of producing at least: $100 in increased worker earnings for every $1 invested by the Foundation. This focus ensures that funded initiatives deliver meaningful and measurable economic benefits. Who Can Apply? Eligible applicants include: U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. Organizations operating under a fiscal sponsor. Nonprofit partnerships involving eligible 501(c)(3) organizations. Organizations that are not registered as 501(c)(3) nonprofits may still apply if they partner with an eligible fiscal sponsor or nonprofit organization. Application Process The application process consists of multiple stages. Step 1: Submit a Concept Note Applicants begin by submitting a short concept note describing: Their proposed initiative Employer partnerships Workforce impact Long-term sustainability Expected outcomes Concept notes will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Step 2: Invitation to Full Application Selected organizations will receive invitations to submit a comprehensive application during September 2026 . Step 3: Final Review Applications will undergo detailed review through November 2026 . Step 4: Grant Awards Successful organizations will be announced in early December 2026 . Request for Proposal or APPLY HERE Application Deadline Deadline to submit the concept note: August 12, 2026. Organizations are encouraged to apply as early as possible to allow adequate time for review. For more information and questions, visit GITLAB Foundation HERE Or send an email to: grants@gitlabfoundation.org Key Features of the Fund Up to $500,000 in grant funding. Flexible one- or two-year grant period. Focus on sustainable workforce development. Strong emphasis on employer partnerships. Supports innovative workplace improvements. Encourages work-based learning models. Promotes long-term career advancement. Supports higher lifetime earnings for workers. Requires sustainability beyond grant funding. Backed by a $16 million partnership between GitLab Foundation and the Families and Workers Fund. About the Families and Workers Fund The Families and Workers Fund is a collaborative funding platform supported by more than 40 philanthropic partners working together to build a stronger and more equitable economy. The organization manages approximately $130 million in collaborative funding and is housed at the Amalgamated Foundation, an independent 501(c)(3) charitable organization. Its partnership with the GitLab Foundation reflects a shared commitment to expanding economic opportunity and improving workforce outcomes across the United States. Why Organizations Should Apply Organizations working at the intersection of workforce development and employer engagement have an opportunity to secure significant flexible funding while helping shape the future of work in America. The fund goes beyond traditional workforce grants by investing in employer practices that improve retention, advancement, and long-term earnings. Organizations with strong employer partnerships, innovative workforce models, and sustainable financing plans will be particularly well positioned to compete. For more Grants opportunities visit OFY Website HERE Conclusion The GitLab Foundation s Powering Economic Opportunity Fund 2026 represents an important opportunity for workforce development organizations committed to creating lasting economic change. By investing in employer partnerships, innovative workplace practices, and sustainable career pathways, the Foundation aims to ensure that workers not only gain employment but also build rewarding, long-term careers with increased earning potential. Eligible organizations are encouraged to prepare strong employer partnerships, develop sustainable workforce strategies, and submit their concept notes before the August 12, 2026 deadline to be considered for grants of up to $500,000 . title: Eastern Partnership Civil Society Fellowships Without Borders 2026: Receive €5,000 to Strengthen Cross-Border Civic Leadership
summary: The Eastern Partnership Civil Society Facility has officially launched applications for the Fellowships Without Borders 2026 , an exciting opportunity designed to empower civic leaders and activists committed to creating meaningful social change across borders. The programme supports individuals from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine who are working to strengthen civil society through international cooperation, learning, innovation, advocacy, and community engagement. Successful applicants will receive approximately €5,000 in financial support , mentoring, coaching, networking opportunities, and access to one of the region s strongest civil society alumni networks. Application Deadline: 11 September 2026 About the Eastern Partnership Civil Society Fellowship Programme Since its launch in 2017 , the Eastern Partnership Civil Society Fellowship Programme has supported more than 250 civic leaders across the Eastern Partnership region. The programme was established to strengthen: Civic leadership Democratic participation Community development Accountability Public engagement Regional cooperation Social innovation Through financial support, mentoring, training, and international networking, Fellows have implemented projects that continue to improve governance and strengthen civil society across their communities. What is Fellowships Without Borders ? The Fellowships Without Borders initiative recognizes that today s civic challenges often extend beyond national boundaries. Many activists: Work with communities spread across several countries. Live temporarily abroad. Operate in exile. Collaborate internationally. Build regional partnerships. Rather than limiting impact to one country, this Fellowship encourages applicants to use international experience and cross-border cooperation to benefit communities in the Eastern Partnership region. Projects may be implemented in: Eastern Partnership countries European Union Member States EU Candidate Countries However, every project should ultimately generate positive impact for communities from the Eastern Partnership countries. Community Engagement Fellowships These Fellowships support projects focusing on: Civic participation Community engagement Policy advocacy Public accountability Organizational development Research and evidence generation Civil society cooperation Community mobilization Awareness campaigns 2. Civic Digital Fellowships Designed for civic technology professionals working on: Digital public participation platforms Civic technology solutions Transparency tools Open data initiatives Digital accountability systems Technology for social good Innovation that strengthens democratic participation Who Can Apply? Applicants must: Be citizens of Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, or Ukraine. Be at least 18 years old. Have a proven record of civic engagement or civic innovation. Demonstrate English language proficiency (minimum B1). Not have previously participated in the Eastern Partnership Civil Society Fellowship Programme. Please note that Fellowships are awarded to individuals , not organizations. What Makes a Without Borders Fellowship Project? Applicants must demonstrate: 1. Commitment to Positive Social Change Projects should clearly contribute to improving communities through civic engagement, leadership, or advocacy. 2. Cross-Border Component Applicants should explain one or both of the following: Learning Across Borders Show how learning activities in another country will strengthen civic engagement or policy work within their community. Supporting Communities Abroad Demonstrate how they will support fellow citizens and civil society actors located in another country while contributing to advocacy, policy dialogue, or community development. Priority Areas Projects should align with one or more of the programme s thematic priorities: Resilient and sustainable economies Rule of law and accountability Security Climate and environmental resilience Inclusive digital transformation Participatory governance Social justice Application Requirements Applicants must submit: Online application form (in English) Fellowship project proposal Budget Activity plan Curriculum Vitae (CV) Recommendation letter Proof of citizenship Proof of English language proficiency Applicants who cannot safely use the online application system may contact the programme team for alternative arrangements. Date: 15 July 2026 The webinar explains: Eligibility requirements Fellowship expectations Tips for preparing a competitive application Common mistakes to avoid A recording will also be made available after the live session. Why You Should Apply The Fellowship offers far more than financial support. Participants will gain: International exposure Leadership development Professional mentoring Access to regional experts Strong cross-border partnerships Membership in a growing alumni network Opportunities to influence policy and strengthen democratic participation It is particularly valuable for civic leaders seeking to expand their impact beyond national borders while maintaining strong connections to their communities. Application Deadline Deadline: 11 September 2026 Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered. Apply Here Final Thoughts The Eastern Partnership Civil Society Fellowships Without Borders 2026 provide an outstanding opportunity for emerging civic leaders to transform local ideas into regional impact. Whether you are a community organizer, policy advocate, civic tech innovator, researcher, or grassroots activist, this Fellowship equips you with the financial resources, mentoring, and international partnerships needed to strengthen democratic participation and build lasting social change across the Eastern Partnership region. title: CIVICUS External Learning and Community Design Consultancy 2026: Apply for a Global Consultancy to Build the WeRise Global Community

This three-month consultancy presents an exciting opportunity for professionals specializing in community building, participatory design, organizational learning, and movement strengthening to help shape the future of the WeRise Global FoPA Solidarity Infrastructure .
