title: SPARK Change-Makers Project 2026 in Ghana: Capacity Building, Mentorship and Grant Funding for Youth-Led Organizations
summary: Youth-led organizations and social enterprises in Ghana now have an exciting opportunity to strengthen their impact through the SPARK Change-Makers Project 2026 , an initiative under the EU-Ghana Youth Empowerment Programme . Implemented by SOS Children s Villages Ghana in partnership with the European Union and other collaborating organizations, the programme is designed to empower youth-led and youth-focused civil society organizations (CSOs) and social enterprises with the knowledge, skills, mentorship, and technical support they need to expand their impact and contribute to sustainable development. Beyond training and organizational development, the programme also provides successful participants with the opportunity to compete for grant funding , enabling them to scale their projects and create lasting change within their communities. If your organization is passionate about empowering young people, promoting innovation, protecting the environment, or strengthening communities, this programme offers an excellent platform to build capacity and access future funding opportunities. About the SPARK Change-Makers Project The SPARK Change-Makers Project is a comprehensive organizational development programme that seeks to strengthen youth-led organizations before providing access to financial support. Rather than offering immediate grants, the programme adopts a phased approach , ensuring participating organizations first receive intensive capacity-building support to improve their effectiveness, governance, sustainability, and long-term impact. Selected organizations will participate in a structured programme that equips them with practical skills, strategic guidance, and expert support before becoming eligible to compete for grant funding. The initiative focuses on empowering young people between the ages of 18 and 35 by strengthening the organizations that serve and represent them. Programme Benefits Organizations selected for the SPARK Change-Makers Project will receive a wide range of support designed to strengthen their operations and increase their impact. Benefits include: Comprehensive organizational capacity development. Leadership and organizational skills training. One-on-one coaching from experienced professionals. Expert mentorship throughout the programme. Technical assistance and advisory support. Networking opportunities with partners and stakeholders. Access to future grant funding opportunities. Support for developing sustainable income-generating activities. Improved organizational sustainability and long-term growth. Increased ability to deliver impactful community projects. Opportunity to Access Grant Funding One of the major highlights of the SPARK Change-Makers Project is the opportunity to access grant funding. Organizations that successfully complete the programme s capacity-strengthening phase become eligible to compete for grants that can help expand and scale their initiatives. This ensures that participating organizations are better prepared to manage funding effectively while maximizing community impact. Who Can Apply? The programme is open to organizations that are youth-led or youth-focused and operate within the programme s six implementing regions of Ghana. Eligible applicants include: Youth-led civil society organizations (CSOs). Youth-focused civil society organizations. Youth-led social enterprises. Youth-focused social enterprises. Priority Focus Areas The SPARK Change-Makers Project supports organizations working in sectors that contribute to youth empowerment and sustainable development. Priority areas include: 1. Gender Empowerment Projects that promote gender equality, women s empowerment, inclusion, and equal opportunities for young people. 2. Agriculture and Environmental Protection Initiatives focused on sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, environmental conservation, food security, and green innovation. 3. Peace and Security Projects that promote peaceful communities, conflict prevention, civic participation, and social cohesion. 4. Culture and Creative Industries Organizations supporting arts, culture, creative entrepreneurship, and cultural preservation among young people. 5. Digital Technology and Innovation Projects leveraging digital tools, technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship to improve lives and create opportunities for youth. Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on several important factors. Strong applications should demonstrate: Youth leadership within the organization. Clear organizational goals and objectives. Active community engagement. Commitment to inclusion and diversity. Environmental sustainability. Potential for long-term impact. Organizational readiness for growth and scaling. Organizations that clearly demonstrate these qualities will be well positioned during the selection process. title: UN Women Opens Applications for the Women’s Empowerment Principles Corporate Action Lab Philippines 2026 on Gender-Responsive and Inclusive Skills Development
summary: The United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) , in partnership with the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) through the Regional Cooperation on Labour Market Policy and Technical and Vocational Education and Training for a Twin Transition in ASEAN (RECOTwin) project, has officially opened applications for the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Corporate Action Lab Philippines 2026 . Applications are open from 15 July to 15 August 2026 . This six-month innovation programme is designed for businesses that are ready to strengthen gender equality while building a future-ready workforce capable of thriving in the country s rapidly expanding green and digital economy. The initiative comes at a critical time as the Philippines undergoes its green and digital Twin Transition, creating new employment opportunities while also exposing significant skills shortages across multiple sectors. At the same time, many talented individuals—including women, young people, LGBTQIA+ persons, people with disabilities and other underrepresented groups—continue to experience barriers that prevent them from accessing quality skills development and employment opportunities. The WEPs Corporate Action Lab seeks to help businesses address these challenges by developing innovative, practical and measurable solutions that promote inclusive skills development and equitable career pathways. About the Women’s Empowerment Principles Corporate Action Lab The Women’s Empowerment Principles Corporate Action Lab (WEPsCAL) is a cohort-based programme that supports companies over a period of approximately six months. Rather than offering theoretical discussions, the programme functions as an innovation laboratory where participating companies design, pilot, evaluate and improve real workplace solutions tailored to their own organizational needs. Participants receive expert guidance throughout the programme while collaborating with other businesses that are equally committed to promoting gender equality and inclusive employment. The programme is implemented under the UN Women Gender Action Lab (GAL): Innovation and Impact for Gender Equality in the Asia-Pacific, in partnership with Australia s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Why Inclusive Skills Development Matters The Philippines is experiencing rapid transformation driven by green technologies and digital innovation. Although these developments are creating thousands of new career opportunities, employers continue to report significant challenges in finding workers with the required skills. At the same time, structural inequalities continue to prevent many talented individuals from accessing technical education, vocational training and quality employment. UN Women believes that businesses can address these challenges while simultaneously improving productivity, innovation and long-term competitiveness by embedding Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles into workplace learning and career development. Gender-responsive and inclusive training programmes can help businesses: Build stronger talent pipelines. Improve employee retention. Increase productivity. Encourage workplace innovation. Develop a workforce prepared for future labour market demands. Support sustainable economic growth. Focus of the 2026 Corporate Action Lab The selected companies will work together to answer the following challenge: How can businesses design and implement skills development initiatives that create equitable career pathways for women and diverse talent during the green and digital transitions? Throughout the programme, participants will receive technical support to develop practical solutions that can be tested within their organizations. Objectives of the Programme The Corporate Action Lab will support participating companies to: Analyse the business case for gender-responsive training by demonstrating its financial and operational value. Identify and eliminate unconscious bias within corporate training materials, learning environments and delivery approaches. Remove systemic barriers preventing women and diverse learners from entering technical and emerging occupations. Design, pilot and evaluate innovative workplace solutions tailored to their specific organizational contexts. Develop measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to monitor progress and sustain inclusive training standards. Share successful practices with stakeholders across the Philippines and ASEAN to encourage wider policy adoption and scaling. Benefits of Participating Selected companies will receive numerous benefits throughout the programme, including: Access to the Women’s Empowerment Principles Gender Gap Analysis Tool. Use of exclusive WEPs resources. Development of customized organizational workplans. Individual technical assistance and coaching sessions. Innovation and problem-solving support. Peer learning with other participating businesses. Networking opportunities with experts and solution providers. Access to innovators working on gender equality and inclusive employment. National recognition. Regional recognition. Global recognition upon successful completion of the programme. Number of Companies to be Selected UN Women plans to select 8–12 companies for the 2026 Philippines Corporate Action Lab. Information Sessions Interested organizations are encouraged to attend one of the free online information sessions before submitting their applications. The sessions will explain: Programme requirements Eligibility criteria Benefits of participation Application process Selection process Information session dates include: 22 July 2026 29 July 2026 10 August 2026 Each session will be held online via Microsoft Teams. Application Process Interested companies should complete the official online application form before the deadline. After applications are reviewed, UN Women will contact successful applicants via email. Successful participants are expected to be notified in early September 2026 , while the official programme launch is tentatively scheduled for the second week of September 2026 . Application Deadline 15 August 2026 How to Apply Eligible companies should complete the official online application form through the UN Women application portal before the deadline. For additional information, applicants are encouraged to review the Challenge Brief, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), and attend one of the scheduled information sessions before submitting their applications. title: SEACAF 2026 Research Fellowship: Receive Up to USD 15,000 to Advance Academic Freedom Research in Southeast Asia
summary: The Southeast Asia Coalition for Academic Freedom (SEACAF) has officially opened applications for its 2026 Research Fellowships on Empowering Academic Freedom in Southeast Asia , offering funding of up to USD 15,000 for research projects that address some of the most pressing challenges facing higher education and academic freedom across the region. This prestigious fellowship is designed to support early-career researchers, academics, and research advocates committed to producing evidence-based research that strengthens academic freedom, promotes democratic values, and informs policy reforms throughout Southeast Asia. Each year, the programme selects six fellows who will participate in a structured fellowship lasting between 10 and 12 months , combining financial support, expert mentorship, peer learning, and opportunities to contribute meaningful policy recommendations that can influence higher education systems across the region. About the SEACAF Research Fellowship Academic freedom remains one of the foundations of quality higher education. It enables scholars, educators, and students to freely teach, research, publish, and engage in critical inquiry without fear of censorship or retaliation. Across Southeast Asia, however, academic freedom faces increasing pressure from democratic backsliding, government restrictions, institutional control, and broader political challenges. Academics and students who engage in research or public discussions on social justice, governance, human rights, and public policy increasingly encounter obstacles such as: State surveillance Administrative sanctions Restrictions on teaching and research Criminalization of dissent Limitations on publishing academic work Political interference in universities Constraints arising from national security policies Increased risks in conflict-affected areas The SEACAF Research Fellowship seeks to generate high-quality research that helps governments, universities, civil society organizations, and policymakers better understand these challenges while developing practical solutions that strengthen academic freedom across Southeast Asia. Fellowship Themes Applicants are invited to submit research proposals under one of three priority themes. Theme 1: Neoliberal Higher Education and Its Impacts on Academic Freedom Across Southeast Asia, universities increasingly operate under market-driven models that emphasize: Revenue generation Competition Commercialization International rankings Performance indicators While these reforms aim to improve institutional competitiveness, they may also weaken: Academic independence Institutional autonomy Research integrity Public service missions of universities Freedom of teaching and inquiry Research under this theme should use practical case studies to examine how neoliberal higher education policies affect academic freedom in real-world settings. The findings are expected to contribute to policy recommendations that promote universities as spaces for independent thinking, critical knowledge production, and public engagement. Funding: Up to USD 12,000 Duration: 10 months Application Type: Individual or team Theme 2: Developing Regional Indicators for Academic Freedom Measuring academic freedom requires reliable and context-specific indicators. This fellowship theme supports research that works closely with stakeholders across Southeast Asia to develop: Regional academic freedom indicators Monitoring frameworks Documentation systems Context-sensitive assessment tools Regional policy recommendations The long-term objective is to establish a comprehensive academic freedom monitoring system throughout Southeast Asia. Funding: Up to USD 12,000 Duration: 10 months Application Type: Individual or team Theme 3: Participatory Action Research for Training Modules on Academic Freedom This theme focuses on developing practical educational resources that strengthen understanding of academic freedom among universities and student communities. Research teams will collaborate directly with academic institutions, educators, and students to: Develop training modules Produce educational materials Test learning resources through participatory workshops Improve awareness of academic freedom Unlike the other themes, this fellowship requires collaborative research. Funding: Up to USD 15,000 Duration: 12 months Application Type: Team application only (minimum of three members) Fellowship Benefits Successful fellows will receive much more than financial support. Benefits include: Funding of up to USD 15,000 depending on the fellowship theme. Participation in a 10–12 month structured fellowship . Expert mentorship from experienced researchers and practitioners. Peer learning with researchers from across Southeast Asia. Opportunities to produce impactful research. Development of policy recommendations for governments and higher education institutions. Contribution to strengthening academic freedom across the region. Increased professional visibility and networking opportunities. What Can the Fellowship Funding Cover? The fellowship provides flexible funding to support research activities. Eligible expenses include: Researcher s Allowance Monthly stipend or compensation for researchers throughout the fellowship period. Research Expenses Funding may be used for costs directly associated with conducting research. Fieldwork and Travel Support includes: Transportation Accommodation Field visits Other fieldwork-related costs Research Assistants Funding may cover payments for research assistants supporting project implementation. Data Collection Eligible costs include: Surveys Interviews Transcription services Data acquisition Other research-related data collection activities Why Academic Freedom Matters Academic freedom allows universities to fulfill their public mission by encouraging independent thinking, innovation, and evidence-based research. Without academic freedom: Research quality declines. Public debate becomes limited. Universities lose institutional independence. Innovation and creativity suffer. Democratic participation weakens. The SEACAF fellowship seeks to strengthen higher education systems where scholars can freely pursue knowledge while contributing to more democratic and inclusive societies. Selection Information For the 2026 fellowship cohort: Only six fellows will be selected. Proposals aligned with the three priority themes will receive the highest consideration. Proposals outside these themes may still be submitted but will receive lower priority during the review process. Research Duration Depending on the selected theme, fellows will conduct research over: 10 months (Themes 1 and 2) 12 months (Theme 3) Throughout the fellowship, participants will receive structured support while conducting original research and producing policy-oriented outputs. Important Deadline Application Deadline: 20 July 2026 Applicants are encouraged to prepare their proposals early and submit all required documents before the deadline. Click here for more and to apply Why You Should Apply If you are passionate about higher education, human rights, democratic governance, or public policy in Southeast Asia, the SEACAF Research Fellowship offers a unique opportunity to conduct meaningful research while influencing regional policy discussions. Beyond funding, fellows become part of a growing regional network committed to protecting academic freedom, strengthening higher education institutions, and ensuring that universities remain places where knowledge, critical inquiry, and truth can flourish. title: Brandtech Group AI for Good Scholarship 2026: Fully Funded One Young World Summit Opportunity for Young African AI Leaders

title: Reaching Marginalized Communities MIL Conference 2026 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia: A Platform for Youth and Underserved Communities to Shape the Future of Media and Information Literacy.

Marginalized communities frequently face obstacles including limited access to credible information, online discrimination, misinformation, hate speech, and digital exclusion. This conference provides a platform where these communities can voice their concerns, share solutions, and collectively strengthen their capacity to engage safely and effectively in today s information landscape. By centering the experiences of underserved populations, DW Akademie aims to encourage more inclusive media systems that leave no community behind. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official application form by providing all requested information. Applicants who would like to give a presentation should indicate their interest in the application form and prepare a presentation lasting between 10 and 15 minutes . All personal information submitted through the application will be handled confidentially by the organizers. APPLY HERE. The Reaching Marginalized Communities Media and Information Literacy Conference 2026 represents an important opportunity for individuals, youth leaders, civil society organizations, and representatives of marginalized communities across Cambodia to engage in meaningful conversations about media, digital inclusion, and equitable access to information. By bringing together participants from diverse backgrounds, the conference seeks to strengthen collaboration, amplify underrepresented voices, and promote more inclusive approaches to media and information literacy. With travel support available for participants outside Phnom Penh, bilingual interpretation, and opportunities to present community experiences, the event offers an accessible platform for learning, networking, and advocacy. title: Rural Cooperative Development Grants (RCDG) Program 2026: USDA Offers Up to $1 Million to Strengthen Rural Cooperatives Across the United States
summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) , through the National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) , has opened applications for the Rural Cooperative Development Grants (RCDG) Program 2026 . The program provides substantial grant funding ranging from $200,000 to $1 million to eligible nonprofit organizations that establish and operate Centers for Rural Cooperative Development, helping strengthen rural economies through cooperative business development. With an estimated $5 million in total program funding, the RCDG Program supports organizations that provide technical assistance to rural cooperatives and mutually owned businesses. By improving access to business expertise, organizational development, and cooperative education, the initiative seeks to create stronger rural enterprises, generate employment opportunities, and improve economic conditions across rural America. Applications are now open, with interested organizations required to submit their applications by July 24, 2026 . About the Rural Cooperative Development Grants Program The Rural Cooperative Development Grants (RCDG) Program is designed to support nonprofit institutions that establish and operate Centers for Rural Cooperative Development . These centers play an important role in helping rural communities create, expand, and strengthen cooperative businesses. Rather than providing direct financial assistance to individual cooperatives, the program funds nonprofit organizations that deliver expert technical assistance, business counseling, training, and educational support to rural cooperatives and mutually owned enterprises. The ultimate objective is to improve economic opportunities in rural areas by encouraging sustainable business development through the cooperative business model. Program Objectives The Rural Cooperative Development Grants Program aims to: Strengthen rural economies through cooperative business development. Support the creation of new cooperatives in rural communities. Assist existing cooperatives in expanding their operations. Improve the long-term sustainability of mutually owned businesses. Increase employment and economic opportunities in rural America. Provide expert technical assistance to rural entrepreneurs and organizations. Enhance the capacity of nonprofit organizations serving rural communities. Funding Available Successful applicants may receive grant funding ranging between: Minimum Award: $200,000 Maximum Award: $1,000,000 The USDA has allocated an estimated $5,000,000 in total funding for this funding cycle. Applicants should note that the program includes a matching fund requirement . Details regarding matching contributions are provided in the official Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Who Can Apply? Applications will only be accepted from eligible nonprofit institutions. Eligible applicants include: Nonprofit organizations. Accredited nonprofit institutions of higher education. Other nonprofit institutions that satisfy all eligibility requirements established under federal regulations. A nonprofit institution is defined as an organization or institution whose net earnings do not benefit any private shareholder or individual. Applicants must also satisfy all eligibility requirements established under 7 CFR 4284.520(a) . Organizations that meet any of the ineligibility conditions described in 7 CFR 4284.520(b) will not be considered for funding. APPLY HERE What Can the Grant Support? Grant funding supports nonprofit organizations that establish and operate Centers for Rural Cooperative Development. These centers provide technical assistance that may include: Assisting communities in establishing new cooperatives. Supporting the expansion of existing cooperatives. Improving the operations of rural cooperative businesses. Delivering business planning and management support. Providing cooperative education and training. Strengthening governance and organizational capacity. Promoting sustainable rural economic development. Through these services, nonprofit organizations help rural communities build stronger businesses and create lasting economic opportunities. Why the Program Matters Cooperatives have long played a significant role in supporting rural economies by allowing individuals, producers, and businesses to work together toward shared economic goals. However, many rural communities lack access to the specialized technical expertise needed to establish and successfully manage cooperative enterprises. The Rural Cooperative Development Grants Program addresses this challenge by investing in organizations capable of delivering professional guidance and technical assistance to rural communities. By strengthening local cooperative development centers, the program contributes to: Increased rural entrepreneurship. Improved business sustainability. Stronger local economies. Job creation. Expanded economic opportunities. Community resilience. Matching Requirement The Rural Cooperative Development Grants Program requires applicants to provide matching contributions toward project costs. Applicants should carefully review the official NOFO for detailed information regarding eligible matching contributions and compliance requirements. Failure to meet the matching requirement may affect funding eligibility. Application Process Eligible nonprofit organizations must submit their applications in accordance with the instructions outlined in the official Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Before applying, applicants are encouraged to: Carefully review the complete NOFO. Confirm eligibility requirements. Prepare all required documentation. Ensure compliance with federal grant regulations. Submit applications before the closing date. Organizations that are new to federal funding opportunities are encouraged to review USDA NIFA s grant guidance to better understand the federal award process. Application Review Applications will be evaluated based on the eligibility requirements and evaluation criteria described in the official NOFO. Applicants that fail to meet program eligibility requirements by the application deadline may be excluded from consideration. Only complete applications submitted by eligible nonprofit institutions will be reviewed for funding. Visit HERE to learn more about Rural Cooperative Development Grants (RCDG) Program 2026 Reasonable Accommodation and Language Support The USDA is committed to ensuring equal access to funding opportunities. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodations should contact the information contact listed in the funding announcement at least 10 days before the application deadline . In addition, free language access services including interpretation and translation of essential information are available upon request. Requests for language services should also be submitted no later than 10 days before the closing date . Important Dates Applications Open: July 7, 2026 Application Deadline: July 24, 2026 Funding Opportunity Number: USDA-NIFA-OP-012058 Assistance Listing Number: 10.771 Grant Summary Funding Organization: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) – National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) Program: Rural Cooperative Development Grants (RCDG) Funding Available: $5,000,000 Award Range: $200,000–$1,000,000 Matching Requirement: Yes Eligible Applicants: Nonprofit institutions Application Deadline: July 24, 2026 Conclusion The Rural Cooperative Development Grants Program 2026 presents an important funding opportunity for nonprofit organizations committed to strengthening rural economies through cooperative development. With awards ranging from $200,000 to $1 million , the program enables eligible organizations to establish and operate Centers for Rural Cooperative Development that provide critical technical assistance to rural cooperatives and mutually owned businesses. Organizations interested in applying should carefully review the program requirements, confirm their eligibility, prepare a competitive application, and submit all required materials before the July 24, 2026 deadline. Given the significant impact these grants can have on rural communities, eligible nonprofit institutions are encouraged to begin the application process as early as possible. title: NYU Grossman School of Medicine Research Coordinator Job 2026 in the USA | Full-Time Population Health Research Opportunity
summary: The NYU Grossman School of Medicine , one of the leading medical schools in the United States, is inviting applications for a full-time Research Coordinator position at the Center for Opioid Epidemiology and Policy (COEP) within the Department of Population Health. This exciting career opportunity offers talented professionals the chance to contribute to cutting-edge public health research that addresses substance use, mental health, stigma, health equity, and overdose prevention. Working under the supervision of Dr. Suzan Walters , Assistant Professor at the Center for Opioid Epidemiology and Policy and Director of the Resilience, Intersectional Stigma, and Empowerment (RISE) Lab , the successful candidate will support multiple National Institutes of Health (NIH)-funded research projects and other impactful studies focused on improving health outcomes for vulnerable populations. This position is ideal for individuals passionate about public health, epidemiology, medical research, health policy, sociology, psychology, or related disciplines who wish to build a meaningful research career while working at one of America s premier academic medical institutions. About NYU Grossman School of Medicine For over 175 years , the NYU Grossman School of Medicine has remained at the forefront of medical education, scientific discovery, and patient care. As part of NYU Langone Health , the institution has educated thousands of physicians, researchers, and healthcare leaders who have made lasting contributions to medicine and public health worldwide. NYU Grossman School of Medicine is recognized for: World-class medical education Innovative biomedical and public health research Commitment to patient-centered care Diverse and inclusive workplace Strong emphasis on equity and belonging Collaborative academic environment The institution values diversity and strives to ensure that faculty, staff, researchers, and students from all backgrounds can thrive while contributing their unique skills, knowledge, and perspectives. About the Research Coordinator Position The Research Coordinator will join the Center for Opioid Epidemiology and Policy (COEP) and work directly with Dr. Suzan Walters on several NIH-funded and other externally funded research projects. The position combines scientific research, project coordination, administrative management, and stakeholder engagement. The successful candidate will contribute to studies examining: Social determinants of health Structural determinants affecting healthcare access Substance use Opioid epidemiology Mental health Harm reduction Stigma Health policy Community-based research This role offers an outstanding opportunity to gain experience in multidisciplinary public health research while collaborating with leading researchers, analysts, doctoral students, postdoctoral fellows, and faculty members. About the RISE Lab The successful applicant will support the work of the Resilience, Intersectional Stigma, and Empowerment (RISE) Lab . The laboratory focuses on understanding how different forms of stigma affect: Access to healthcare Engagement with treatment Mental health Substance use recovery Overall health outcomes Its research aims to improve services and develop evidence-based interventions for individuals facing substance use disorders and other health challenges. About the Center for Opioid Epidemiology and Policy (COEP) COEP serves as a leading research center focused on understanding and responding to the rapidly evolving opioid overdose epidemic in the United States. Its mission includes: Conducting high-quality research Informing evidence-based policies Preventing opioid misuse Reducing overdose deaths Improving treatment access Supporting national and global public health efforts As part of COEP, the Research Coordinator will participate in: Monthly analyst meetings Journal clubs Research seminars Career development sessions Faculty collaborations Scientific discussions Professional networking opportunities Key Responsibilities The Research Coordinator will play an important role across several stages of the research process. Responsibilities include: Research Activities Participate in participant recruitment and outreach. Conduct informed consent procedures. Administer surveys and interviews. Support primary data collection. Conduct literature reviews. Assist with qualitative and quantitative data analysis. Prepare scientific manuscripts. Draft policy briefs. Prepare grant proposals. Project Management The successful candidate will: Track project timelines. Monitor deliverables. Coordinate meetings. Prepare meeting agendas. Record meeting notes. Follow up on action items. Maintain organized project documentation. Regulatory Compliance Responsibilities include: Managing Institutional Review Board (IRB) submissions. Preparing grant documentation. Maintaining research compliance. Reporting study progress. Data Management Applicants will also: Manage REDCap databases. Administer research surveys. Track participants. Conduct data quality checks. Generate reports. Maintain research databases. Administrative Support The coordinator will: Coordinate service agreements. Order research supplies. Process study payments. Maintain compliance with institutional financial policies. Scientific Communication The successful applicant will help: Prepare presentations. Create research summaries. Develop data visualizations. Produce reports for collaborators. Translate scientific findings for non-academic audiences. Event Coordination Responsibilities also include: Organizing scientific meetings. Coordinating workshops. Supporting collaborative research events. Minimum Qualifications Applicants should possess: Bachelor s degree in Life Sciences, Allied Health, or a related discipline. At least 2 years of relevant experience , or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Excellent written communication skills. Strong verbal communication abilities. Effective interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently under supervision. Strong problem-solving abilities. Excellent organizational skills. Time management skills. Ability to work under pressure. Applicants should also have proficiency with: Microsoft Word Microsoft Excel Microsoft Access Microsoft PowerPoint Microsoft Outlook Internet-based research tools Preferred Qualifications NYU particularly encourages applicants with: Bachelor s or Master s degree in Public Health, Sociology, Psychology, Policy, or related fields. Two or more years of public health or academic research experience. Experience recruiting research participants. Experience with community-based research. Knowledge of quantitative or qualitative data analysis software such as: Stata R SAS NVivo Experience related to: Substance use Harm reduction Overdose prevention Public health systems Health policy Excellent scientific writing skills. Ability to communicate research findings to non-academic audiences. Strong organizational abilities. Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. Salary NYU Langone Health has published the annual salary range for this role. Annual Salary: USD 66,300 – USD 72,345 Actual compensation will depend on factors such as: Experience Education Specialty Institutional needs The salary does not include bonuses, incentives, or additional compensation. Employee Benefits NYU Grossman School of Medicine offers a comprehensive employee benefits package designed to support staff throughout every stage of life. Benefits include: Comprehensive wellness programs Financial security benefits Retirement support Generous paid time off Employee resource groups Career development opportunities Family support resources Physical wellness programs Mental health support Nutritional wellness initiatives Sleep wellness resources Social well-being programs Preventive healthcare support Employees also benefit from a collaborative academic environment that encourages professional growth and lifelong learning. Diversity and Equal Opportunity NYU Grossman School of Medicine is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where all qualified applicants receive equal consideration for employment regardless of background or identity. The institution values diversity and encourages applicants from all communities to apply. How to Apply Interested candidates should complete an online application through the official NYU Langone Health careers portal. Applicants are encouraged to prepare a strong application highlighting their research experience, project management skills, analytical abilities, and commitment to improving public health through evidence-based research. Apply Here Deadline No application deadline has been specified. Applications remain open until the position is filled or removed from the recruitment portal. So applicants are encouraged to apply early. title: Future Voices Program 2026/27: Apply for Climate Change Journalism and Media Leadership Training in Southeast Asia
summary: Applications are now open for the Future Voices Program 2026/27 , a leadership and professional development initiative for early- to mid-career media professionals across Southeast Asia. This year’s program focuses on climate change journalism , providing participants with opportunities to strengthen their reporting skills, develop their leadership capacity, and connect with a regional network of emerging media professionals. The Future Voices Program is delivered by ABC International Development , also known as ABCID, with support from the ASEAN-Australia Centre . It is designed for media professionals who want to improve the quality, impact, and ethical foundations of climate reporting within their newsrooms and communities. A total of 33 media professionals will be selected for the 2026/27 cohort. Participants will take part in online learning, professional development activities over the course of a year, and continued engagement through the program’s alumni network. From the full cohort, 11 participants will later be selected to attend an intensive in-country program in Australia from 20 to 30 October 2026 . Applications must be submitted by 25 July 2026 . About the Future Voices Program The Future Voices Program is a regional media leadership initiative created to support emerging professionals working in journalism and the wider media sector across Southeast Asia. The program recognises that climate change is not only an environmental issue. It also affects economies, public health, migration, food security, energy systems, livelihoods, governance, and community resilience. Media professionals therefore play an important role in helping the public understand climate-related developments and the consequences they may have for different communities. Through the 2026/27 program, participants will be encouraged to strengthen their ability to report on climate change accurately, responsibly, and ethically. They will also develop leadership skills that can help them influence newsroom practices, guide colleagues, engage audiences, and contribute to stronger public-interest journalism. The program combines several forms of professional development, including: Online learning activities Leadership development Climate change journalism training Professional networking Ongoing alumni engagement Opportunities for selected participants to undertake advanced training in Australia Rather than focusing only on short-term training, Future Voices offers a longer professional development journey. Participants will remain involved in the program for approximately one year, allowing them to apply what they learn within their own professional environments. Future Voices Program 2026/27 Theme: Climate Change Journalism The central theme of the 2026/27 intake is climate change journalism . Climate reporting often requires journalists to explain complex scientific, economic, political, and social issues in language that is accessible to the public. It also requires careful verification, ethical judgment, and an understanding of how climate-related developments affect different groups of people. The Future Voices Program aims to strengthen climate reporting across both newsrooms and communities in Southeast Asia. Participants will have the opportunity to improve how they identify, investigate, and communicate climate stories. The program may be particularly relevant to media professionals whose work involves topics such as: Climate change and environmental policy Renewable energy and energy transitions Extreme weather and natural disasters Community resilience Sustainable development Agriculture and food security Climate-related displacement Public health and environmental risks Government and corporate climate commitments The social and economic effects of climate change Applicants do not necessarily need to work exclusively as climate journalists. The program is intended for emerging media professionals who are ready to strengthen their understanding of climate reporting and use that knowledge within their wider professional work. How Many Participants Will Be Selected? ABC International Development will select a cohort of 33 media professionals from across Southeast Asia. All 33 participants will join the broader Future Voices professional development program, which includes online learning, year-long development activities, and ongoing connections with the program’s alumni community. Of these 33 participants, 11 will be selected to attend an intensive in-country course in Australia. Being selected for the initial cohort does not automatically guarantee participation in the Australia-based component. The Australian intensive course is a further opportunity available to a smaller group chosen from among the 33 participants. Future Voices Program Structure The program has several interconnected components designed to support participants at different stages of their professional development. 1. Online Learning Participants will take part in online learning activities focused on climate journalism, leadership, and professional development. The online format will allow media professionals from different parts of Southeast Asia to participate while continuing their regular work. It will also create opportunities for participants to exchange experiences across different media systems, communities, and national contexts. 2. One Year of Professional Development The Future Voices Program is not limited to a single workshop or training session. Selected participants will receive approximately one year of professional development support. This extended structure gives participants time to reflect on the training, test new approaches, and apply their learning in their workplaces and communities. Participants may also have opportunities to build relationships with other media professionals facing similar reporting challenges across the region. 3. Regional Networking The program brings together emerging media leaders from Southeast Asia, creating a professional network that extends beyond individual newsrooms or countries. Participants will be able to connect with journalists and media professionals who bring different experiences, perspectives, and areas of expertise. This regional network may support future collaboration, knowledge-sharing, cross-border reporting, and continued professional exchange. 4. Alumni Engagement Ongoing alumni engagement is another important part of the Future Voices Program. Participants will not simply complete the program and lose contact with the network. Instead, they will become part of a wider alumni community that can provide continued opportunities for professional connection and regional engagement. This long-term alumni element reflects the program’s aim of developing a sustained community of emerging media leaders. Australia Intensive Course for 11 Selected Participants Eleven participants from the cohort will be selected to travel to Australia for an intensive in-country course from 20 to 30 October 2026 . The Australia component will provide additional academic, professional, and networking opportunities. During the intensive course, selected participants will: Earn a Leadership and Climate Change Micro-Credential Participants will complete a leadership and climate change micro-credential at a leading Australian university. A micro-credential is a focused academic or professional qualification covering a specialised area of knowledge. This component will allow participants to deepen their understanding of climate change while also developing practical leadership capabilities. Receive Training at the Australian Broadcasting Corporation Participants will receive professional training at the Australian Broadcasting Corporation , commonly known as the ABC. The training will expose participants to the practices and professional experience of Australia’s national public broadcaster. It may also help participants reflect on newsroom leadership, ethical journalism, public-interest reporting, and methods of communicating complex climate issues to broad audiences. Attend the All-Energy Australia Conference The selected participants will attend the All-Energy Australia conference . The conference brings together people working across the energy and climate sectors. Attendance will provide participants with an opportunity to learn about developments in renewable energy, energy policy, technology, and the broader transition toward lower-carbon systems. For journalists, exposure to climate and energy experts can support more informed reporting and help them identify potential sources, story ideas, and emerging regional issues. Connect With Australian Climate Institutions Participants will have opportunities to engage with major Australian climate institutions. These connections may help participants gain a broader understanding of climate research, policy, advocacy, and communication. They may also allow participants to compare Australian approaches with the climate challenges and policy debates taking place in Southeast Asia. Develop a Personalised Leadership Action Project Each selected participant will develop a personalised leadership action project with support from industry mentors. The action project will allow participants to translate the program’s training into a practical initiative connected to their own professional goals. Depending on the participant’s role and newsroom context, such a project could involve strengthening climate coverage, introducing new editorial practices, developing a reporting initiative, improving audience engagement, or supporting professional learning within a media organisation. The exact format of each project will be shaped by the participant’s professional responsibilities and development objectives. Who Should Apply? The Future Voices Program is intended for early- to mid-career media professionals in Southeast Asia . It is particularly suitable for applicants who are interested in developing their leadership abilities and improving the quality of climate journalism within their organisations or communities. Potential applicants may include professionals working in areas such as: Journalism News reporting Editing Broadcasting Digital media Radio Television Multimedia production Newsroom management Media development Public-interest communication The original announcement does not provide a complete list of accepted job titles. Applicants should therefore consider whether their current work clearly places them within the media profession and whether they can demonstrate how the program relates to their professional development. English-Language Requirement Applicants must be proficient in English. Because the program includes regional interaction, online learning, professional training, and possible participation in the Australia-based intensive course, participants will need sufficient English-language ability to communicate effectively and take part in all program activities. The announcement does not specify whether applicants must submit an English-language certificate or test result. Applicants should carefully review the official application form for any additional instructions concerning evidence of English proficiency. What Makes a Strong Applicant? Although the announcement does not provide detailed selection criteria, the program is likely to appeal most strongly to applicants who can demonstrate a clear connection between their professional experience and the aims of Future Voices. A strong application should clearly explain: The applicant’s current role in journalism or the media sector. Their experience as an early- or mid-career media professional. Their interest in climate change journalism. The leadership skills they hope to develop. How the program could improve their work or strengthen their newsroom. How they would use the knowledge gained to benefit their community or audience. Their willingness to participate in online learning and longer-term professional development. Their ability to communicate and participate in English. Applicants should avoid relying on general statements about being passionate or motivated. They should instead use concrete examples from their professional experience. For example, applicants could describe a climate-related story they have reported, an editorial challenge they have faced, a gap in climate coverage within their newsroom, or a leadership responsibility they would like to take on. Why Apply for the Future Voices Program? The Future Voices Program offers more than technical journalism training. It combines climate reporting, leadership development, regional networking, and long-term professional engagement. Successful applicants may benefit from: Greater knowledge of climate change and climate communication Improved reporting and editorial skills Stronger ethical journalism practices Leadership development Connections with media professionals across Southeast Asia Access to a continuing alumni network Opportunities to learn from Australian institutions Potential selection for the intensive course in Australia Academic recognition through a micro-credential for participants selected for the Australia component Mentorship while developing a leadership action project The program may be especially valuable for professionals seeking to take on greater responsibility within their newsrooms or to become stronger voices in climate journalism. Important Program Dates Applicants should note the following dates: Applications opened: 30 June 2026 Announcement updated: 1 July 2026 Application deadline: 25 July 2026 Australia intensive course: 20–30 October 2026 Program intake: 2026/27 Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Early preparation provides time to review written responses, confirm eligibility, and address any technical problems with the application platform. How to Apply Interested applicants must apply through the official Future Voices Program application link provided by ABC International Development. Before beginning the application, candidates should prepare information about their: Current professional role Media and journalism experience Leadership experience or potential Interest in climate change reporting Professional development goals Expected contribution to the regional network English-language ability Availability to participate in program activities Applicants should carefully review every section of the official application form because additional questions, document requirements, or selection conditions may appear there. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Future Voices Program 2026/27 is 25 July 2026 . Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered. Candidates are advised to confirm the deadline according to the time zone stated on the official application portal, where applicable. For more information about this opportunity, click here . Conclusion The Future Voices Program 2026/27 offers an important professional development opportunity for emerging media leaders across Southeast Asia who want to strengthen climate change journalism. With 33 participants joining a year-long program and 11 receiving the opportunity to attend an intensive course in Australia, Future Voices combines regional learning with advanced leadership training, institutional engagement, and professional networking. The program is particularly relevant at a time when communities need climate journalism that is accurate, ethical, accessible, and grounded in the realities of people affected by environmental change. Early- and mid-career media professionals who are proficient in English and committed to improving climate reporting should prepare and submit their applications before 25 July 2026 . Discover more global job opportunities, click here . title: A Million Realities Fellowship 2027: Nominate Yourself or an Inspiring Youth Leader for a Two-Year Leadership Programme in the UK
summary: The A Million Realities (AMR) Fellowship 2027 is now accepting nominations for its next cohort of outstanding leaders and emerging leaders who are committed to improving the lives of young people in the United Kingdom. This prestigious two-year leadership programme brings together individuals from across the youth sector to collaborate, strengthen their leadership capacity, and drive meaningful change for young people transitioning into adulthood. Unlike many fellowship programmes that rely solely on direct applications, the AMR Fellowship begins with a nomination process. Whether you are nominated by someone who recognizes your leadership or choose to nominate yourself, this programme offers an exceptional opportunity to join a network of influential changemakers dedicated to creating a better future for young people. Nominations are open from July to September 2026 , with the successful Fellows beginning the programme in March 2027 . About the A Million Realities Fellowship The A Million Realities Fellowship is designed to identify and support leaders who are making a significant contribution to improving outcomes for young people across the UK. The Fellowship brings together individuals working in a wide range of sectors connected to youth development and wellbeing. Participants come from: Frontline youth organisations Education Public policy Mental health services Housing Philanthropy Community organisations Social enterprises Charities Youth advocacy initiatives Rather than focusing on the size or profile of an organisation, the Fellowship emphasizes the quality of leadership, demonstrated impact, commitment to young people, and the potential to influence positive change. The programme creates an environment where Fellows can strengthen their leadership abilities, exchange ideas, collaborate across sectors, and contribute to long-term improvements in youth development. Why the A Million Realities Fellowship Matters Young people face increasingly complex challenges as they transition into adulthood. These challenges may include access to education, employment, housing, mental health support, social inclusion, and economic opportunity. The A Million Realities Fellowship seeks leaders who are already working to address these issues and provides them with a platform to amplify their impact. By investing in leaders rather than projects alone, the Fellowship aims to strengthen the wider youth ecosystem and encourage collaboration between professionals from diverse backgrounds. Participants become part of a growing community of leaders committed to shaping policies, services, and initiatives that improve the lives of young people throughout the UK. Who Are the A Million Realities Fellows? A Million Realities Fellows represent a broad spectrum of professionals and emerging leaders whose work contributes to youth development. The Fellowship welcomes individuals working in areas such as: Youth development Education Community leadership Public policy Youth mental health Housing and homelessness Social justice Philanthropy Non-profit leadership Community engagement Youth empowerment Social innovation What unites Fellows is their commitment to creating opportunities for young people and their demonstrated ability to lead with purpose and impact. The Nomination Process One distinctive feature of the A Million Realities Fellowship is its nomination-based selection process. Why Nominations Matter A nomination serves as an independent endorsement of a candidate s leadership and influence. According to the Fellowship, a nomination is more than simply expressing interest—it acts as an important reference that demonstrates that others recognize the candidate s contribution and leadership within the youth sector. The Fellowship values nominations because they provide insight into a candidate s standing that may not be fully captured in a self-written application. Who Can Submit a Nomination? There are two ways to enter the Fellowship selection process: Nominate another leader Nominate yourself Although third-party nominations carry greater weight because they represent external recognition, self-nominated candidates have also successfully become A Million Realities Fellows in previous cohorts. Anyone wishing to nominate another person is encouraged to inform the nominee beforehand and obtain their permission before sharing personal details. Selection Timeline The Fellowship follows a structured selection process over several months. July – September 2026 Nominations open. During this stage, nominations are submitted for prospective Fellows. August – October 2026 Suitable nominees are invited to submit full Fellowship applications. Not every nominee automatically progresses to the application stage. The Fellowship team reviews nominations before inviting selected candidates to continue. 27–28 October 2026 Interviews take place. Candidates invited to interview will have an opportunity to discuss their leadership journey, impact, and aspirations. November 2026 – March 2027 Successful Fellows complete onboarding. During this period, selected participants prepare for the start of the Fellowship. March 2027 The two-year Fellowship officially begins. Fellowship Benefits Although the announcement primarily focuses on the nomination process, becoming an A Million Realities Fellow offers significant professional and leadership development opportunities. Participants can expect to benefit from: Membership in a prestigious UK leadership network Opportunities to collaborate with leaders across multiple sectors Enhanced leadership development Cross-sector networking Professional learning and knowledge exchange Greater visibility within the youth sector Opportunities to contribute to improving youth outcomes across the UK Participation in a two-year structured Fellowship programme Long-term connections with other Fellows and sector leaders The Fellowship is intended to strengthen participants capacity to create meaningful and lasting impact in their communities and organisations. Live Online Q A Sessions Prospective nominees, applicants, and nominators are invited to attend online information sessions where members of the AMR team and current Fellows will explain the programme and answer questions. The scheduled sessions are: 24 July 2026 Time: 3:00 PM – 4:00 PM 26 August 2026 Time: 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM These sessions provide an excellent opportunity to learn more about the Fellowship experience, eligibility expectations, and application process before submitting a nomination. Participants are encouraged to register in advance to receive joining details. Who Should Consider Applying? The Fellowship is ideal for individuals who: Demonstrate leadership within the youth sector Have a proven commitment to improving the lives of young people Are creating measurable impact in their communities Wish to strengthen their leadership capacity Value collaboration and cross-sector partnerships Are interested in joining a long-term network of changemakers The programme welcomes both established and emerging leaders whose work contributes to positive youth outcomes. How to Nominate a Leader To participate in the Fellowship selection process: Complete the official nomination form. Choose whether you are nominating yourself or another individual. If nominating someone else, obtain their consent before submitting their information. Wait for the Fellowship team to review nominations. Suitable nominees may receive an invitation to submit a full application. Contact Information Applicants or nominators who have questions about the Fellowship can contact the A Million Realities team via: Email: info@amillionrealities.com Why You Should Apply The A Million Realities Fellowship is an outstanding opportunity for leaders committed to improving opportunities for young people across the UK. Rather than simply recognizing past achievements, the programme invests in future leadership by bringing together talented professionals from different sectors to collaborate, learn from one another, and build stronger solutions for young people. Whether you work in education, mental health, housing, policy, philanthropy, youth development, or community leadership, the Fellowship provides an opportunity to expand your influence while becoming part of a powerful network dedicated to positive social change. If you—or someone you know—is making a meaningful difference in the lives of young people, this Fellowship offers a valuable platform to grow, collaborate, and lead. Click HERE to learn more and also apply for nomination. Conclusion The A Million Realities Fellowship 2027 seeks passionate leaders who are shaping better futures for young people throughout the United Kingdom. Beginning with a nomination process that recognizes leadership and community impact, the Fellowship offers participants the opportunity to join a two-year programme focused on leadership development, collaboration, and lasting change. title: Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded Opportunity for African Feminist Writers, Journalists, Researchers, Storytellers, and Creatives
summary: The Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications from emerging and established feminist writers, journalists, researchers, storytellers, poets, creatives, and movement builders across Africa. This exciting fellowship provides participants with the opportunity to strengthen their writing skills, receive mentorship from experienced feminist scholars and practitioners, develop publication-ready work, and contribute to shaping conversations around African integration, feminism, and social justice. Under the theme Narrative Sovereignty, Knowledge Justice, and Feminist Futures, the fellowship seeks to empower African voices to tell authentic stories that challenge dominant narratives surrounding borders, migration, citizenship, identity, and belonging. It is designed for individuals who are passionate about using storytelling as a powerful tool for advocacy, social change, and the advancement of a more inclusive and borderless Africa. If you are committed to feminist storytelling, Pan-Africanism, knowledge production, and creating narratives that reflect African realities, this fellowship offers a unique platform to grow your skills while joining a vibrant community of changemakers across the continent. About the Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship 2026 Africa s vision of greater regional integration, free movement, and stronger people-to-people connections cannot be achieved through policy reforms alone. The stories people tell and the voices that are heard play a critical role in shaping public opinion, influencing policies, and redefining ideas of identity, citizenship, mobility, and belonging. The Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship recognizes that knowledge production and storytelling are powerful instruments for transforming societies. Through this fellowship, participants will critically examine whose stories are being told, whose knowledge is valued, and how feminist perspectives can contribute to building a more just, inclusive, and united Africa. The fellowship creates an environment where participants can explore complex social issues while producing compelling written work that reflects lived African experiences and feminist futures. Participants will engage in thoughtful discussions and writing projects that explore how narratives shape the African continent and influence conversations about mobility, migration, citizenship, gender equality, and regional integration. Key Questions the Fellowship Will Explore Throughout the fellowship, participants will critically engage with important questions such as: Whose knowledge is being produced and recognized? Whose narratives are amplified across Africa? Whose voices continue to remain unheard? How do stories influence public perceptions of borders, migration, identity, and belonging? What role can feminist storytelling play in promoting African integration? How can African storytellers imagine and articulate a truly Borderless Africa? How can feminist perspectives reshape conversations around justice, dignity, freedom, and inclusion? These discussions will help fellows produce thoughtful, impactful, and original written work that contributes meaningfully to ongoing debates across the continent. Benefits of the Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship Successful applicants will enjoy numerous professional and personal development opportunities throughout the fellowship. Participants will receive: 1. Two-Day In-Person Writing Retreat Fellows will participate in an immersive two-day writing retreat where they will collaborate with fellow writers, receive guidance from experienced facilitators, and refine their storytelling skills in an engaging learning environment. 2. Expert-Led Learning Sessions Participants will benefit from specialized training sessions covering important topics, including: Narrative sovereignty Feminist storytelling Knowledge justice Pan-Africanism Free movement across Africa Writing for advocacy Storytelling for social change These sessions are designed to deepen participants understanding of how writing can influence policy, society, and public discourse. 3. Professional Mentorship Each fellow will receive mentorship from experienced: Feminist scholars Professional writers Editors Pan-African practitioners This mentorship will support participants in strengthening their writing, expanding their perspectives, and producing high-quality work. 4. Editorial Support Participants will receive editorial guidance to help transform their drafts into polished, publication-ready articles, essays, creative works, or research pieces. 5. Publication Opportunities Outstanding works produced during the fellowship may be published through: Borderless Africa platforms Partner organizations Affiliated publication networks This offers fellows an opportunity to showcase their work to broader audiences across Africa and beyond. 6. Access to a Growing Pan-African Network Fellows will become part of a dynamic network of: Feminist writers Storytellers Researchers Advocates Pan-African practitioners Social justice leaders This network provides valuable opportunities for future collaboration, learning, and professional growth. Suggested Writing Areas Applicants are encouraged to propose writing ideas related to one or more of the following themes: Narrative sovereignty Feminist knowledge production Free movement and mobility Citizenship and belonging Cross-border identities Women and migration Border communities Pan-Africanism and regional integration Language, culture, and identity Digital storytelling and narrative change Feminist futures Speculative feminist writing Applicants may also propose other relevant ideas that align with the fellowship theme. Who Should Apply? The fellowship welcomes applications from individuals across Africa, including: Feminist writers Journalists Bloggers Researchers Poets Creative writers Community storytellers Human rights defenders Students Young activists Digital storytellers Content creators Movement builders Whether you are an emerging writer seeking mentorship or an experienced storyteller looking to deepen your engagement with feminist and Pan-African issues, this fellowship provides an excellent opportunity for learning and professional development. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should demonstrate: A strong interest in feminist issues and social justice. Commitment to African unity, mobility, citizenship, or Pan-Africanism. Passion for storytelling, writing, research, or advocacy. Willingness to fully participate in both the in-person writing retreat and online learning sessions. Ability to submit all required application documents. Importantly, no prior publication record is required , making this fellowship accessible to both emerging and experienced writers. Application Requirements Applicants are required to submit the following documents via email: campaigns@africans-rising.org A short biography (maximum 250 words). A statement of interest (maximum 500 words). One writing sample. Applicants are encouraged to ensure that all documents clearly demonstrate their interest in the fellowship theme and their commitment to feminist storytelling and social justice. Application Deadline: 20 July 2026 Interested applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare and submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute challenges. Why You Should Apply The Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship is more than a writing programme, it is a transformative learning experience that empowers African storytellers to shape the narratives that influence society. By participating, fellows will gain valuable mentorship, strengthen their writing abilities, connect with influential feminist thinkers, contribute to knowledge production rooted in African realities, and potentially publish work that reaches audiences across the continent. Whether your interest lies in journalism, creative writing, research, advocacy, or digital storytelling, this fellowship provides an exceptional opportunity to amplify your voice while contributing to conversations about justice, freedom, belonging, and the future of Africa. Learn more about Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship 2026: HERE Conclusion The Borderless Africa Feminist Writing Fellowship 2026 presents an outstanding opportunity for African writers, journalists, researchers, creatives, and advocates who are passionate about feminism, social justice, and Pan-Africanism. Through mentorship, expert-led training, editorial support, publication opportunities, and collaboration with fellow storytellers, participants will gain the skills and networks needed to create impactful narratives that challenge dominant perspectives and promote a more inclusive and borderless Africa. If you are ready to use your voice to influence conversations around identity, migration, citizenship, belonging, and feminist futures, this fellowship offers the ideal platform to develop your ideas and contribute to meaningful change.
