title: ADB Innovation Challenges 2026: Win Up to USD 450,000 to Transform Laundry Systems and Urban Dengue Control Across Asia and the Pacific
summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is inviting innovators, startups, companies, research institutions, NGOs, universities, and multidisciplinary teams from around the world to participate in two groundbreaking innovation challenges designed to tackle some of the most pressing development issues in Asia and the Pacific. The Laundry Transformation Challenge and the Urban Dengue Control Innovation Challenge are seeking scalable, affordable, and inclusive technological solutions capable of improving lives while creating measurable social, environmental, and economic impact. Selected innovators will have the opportunity to receive grant funding of up to USD 450,000 per pilot project , collaborate directly with ADB and government partners, validate their innovations in real-world environments, and gain international visibility. Whether your innovation addresses sustainable laundry technologies or next-generation dengue control, these challenges offer an exceptional opportunity to scale your solution while contributing to sustainable development across the region. About the ADB Innovation Challenges The Asian Development Bank (ADB) regularly launches innovation challenges aimed at identifying transformative technologies that address critical development problems throughout Asia and the Pacific. The 2026 challenges focus on two major issues: Transforming laundry systems to reduce women s unpaid work while protecting water resources. Developing bio-enabled and digital technologies to improve dengue control in Sri Lanka with potential expansion across Asia. Both initiatives emphasize innovation that is: Affordable Inclusive Environmentally sustainable Scalable Evidence-based Capable of generating measurable impact Successful applicants will pilot their technologies under real operating conditions with support from ADB and strategic local partners. Challenge 1: The Laundry Transformation Challenge Overview The Laundry Transformation Challenge seeks innovative technologies capable of transforming the way laundry is performed across Asia and the Pacific. Millions of households still rely on manual handwashing, particularly in lower-income communities where washing machines remain inaccessible or impractical. More than half of the population across Asia and the Pacific continues to wash clothes by hand, with women performing the overwhelming majority of laundry-related work. Laundry remains an invisible but enormous burden that consumes time, affects health, limits economic participation, and contributes significantly to environmental degradation. ADB is looking for solutions that can fundamentally rethink laundry systems while reducing water consumption, minimizing pollution, and improving livelihoods. Why This Challenge Matters Across Asia and the Pacific: Over 50% of people still wash clothes by hand. Women spend approximately 20% of their productive time performing laundry. Manual washing contributes to physical strain and repetitive injuries. Untreated greywater containing detergents and microfibers pollutes rivers and lakes. Growing urbanization is increasing pressure on already stressed water resources. Innovative laundry technologies could significantly improve gender equality, public health, environmental sustainability, and household productivity. The Challenge Question ADB asks innovators: How can innovative technology create more inclusive laundry systems that reduce women s unpaid workload while decreasing water consumption and pollution across Asia and the Pacific? Solutions may address one or multiple aspects of laundry transformation. Learn more and Apply Here Challenge 2: Urban Dengue Control Innovation Challenge Overview The Urban Dengue Control Innovation Challenge seeks innovative bio-enabled and digitally-powered technologies capable of transforming dengue prevention in Sri Lanka s rapidly growing urban areas. Despite years of investment in mosquito control, dengue remains a serious public health challenge. ADB is looking for technologies capable of generating strong evidence through pilot implementation, paving the way for city-wide and national expansion. Why This Challenge Matters Sri Lanka continues to experience dengue incidence rates of approximately: 300–400 reported cases per 100,000 people annually. This remains three to four times higher than the country s national target. Conventional mosquito control methods—including spraying, larviciding, and community clean-up campaigns—have struggled to provide sustainable results due to: Insecticide resistance Urban population growth Climate change Operational challenges Limited public health resources ADB believes a new generation of technology-enabled solutions can transform urban dengue management. The Challenge Question ADB asks innovators: How might bio-enabled and digitally-powered technologies deliver cost-effective, scalable urban dengue control solutions suitable for deployment throughout Sri Lanka and eventually across Asia and the Pacific? Learn more and Apply Here Who Should Apply? Both innovation challenges welcome multidisciplinary teams and organizations capable of developing scalable solutions. Potential applicants include: Startups Technology companies SMEs Universities Research institutions Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) Engineering firms Health technology innovators Environmental innovators Social enterprises Innovation hubs Multidisciplinary teams Independent innovators Public-private partnerships Teams may consist of 1–10 members . Benefits of Participating Selected innovators will receive numerous advantages beyond financial support. These include: 1. Grant Funding Successful proposals may receive: Up to USD 450,000 per pilot project. Applicants should note that: A 10% co-financing contribution is required. 2. Pilot Your Innovation Participants will have the opportunity to: Test solutions under real-world conditions. Validate performance in new markets. Generate field evidence supporting larger deployment. 3. Collaborate with ADB Successful applicants will work alongside: Asian Development Bank experts National governments Local implementing partners International development stakeholders 4. Build Strategic Networks Participants gain exposure to: Government agencies Investors Development organizations Policy makers Industry experts 5. Increase Visibility Innovators will receive international recognition for their work among key stakeholders throughout Asia and the Pacific. 6. Drive Real Impact Selected projects have the potential to improve: Public health Women s economic empowerment Water conservation Environmental sustainability Urban resilience Community livelihoods Application Timeline Laundry Transformation Challenge Concept Note Submission 29 June – 31 August 2026 Full Application and Pilot Pitch 11 September – 23 October 2026 Winners Announced November 2026 Urban Dengue Control Innovation Challenge Concept Note Submission Deadline: 14 August 2026 Full Application and Pilot Pitch 7 September – 9 October 2026 Selected Technology Providers Announced November–December 2026 Pilot Implementation January 2027 Information Sessions Laundry Transformation Challenge ADB will host an online information session on: 24 July 2026 Time: 4:00 PM Manila Time (GMT+8) Applicants can attend to: Understand the challenge requirements Learn about evaluation criteria Ask questions directly to the challenge team Urban Dengue Control Innovation Challenge Applicants who missed the live webinar can watch the recorded information session featuring: Asian Development Bank National Dengue Control Unit of Sri Lanka The recording provides: Challenge overview Technology guidance Frequently asked questions Application insights Why You Should Apply Innovation has the power to solve some of society s biggest challenges. Whether you are developing sustainable household technologies or advanced public health solutions, these ADB Innovation Challenges provide an opportunity to transform your innovation into a real-world solution with regional impact. Participants will benefit from funding, expert collaboration, pilot implementation opportunities, and international recognition while contributing to healthier communities, gender equality, environmental sustainability, and stronger urban resilience. If your team has an innovative solution capable of creating lasting impact, this is an excellent opportunity to demonstrate its value on one of the world s leading development innovation platforms. title: Gulbenkian Institute Scholarships for Advanced Study 2026–2027 in Portugal | Fully Funded Research Residency for Internationally Renowned Academics, Scholars, and Artists

title: Bloomsbury Academic Writing Fellowship 2026: £1,000 Funding, One-Year Mentorship, Editorial Support and Publishing Opportunities for Early-Career Academics in the UK
summary: The Bloomsbury Academic Writing Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications from early-career academics and researchers based in the United Kingdom who identify as Black, Asian or Ethnically Diverse (BAED) . Now in its fourth consecutive year, this prestigious fellowship is jointly delivered by Bloomsbury Academic and Writers Artists to support emerging scholars in transforming innovative academic research into publishable books. title: 2027 Purpose Earth Grant Program: Receive Up to $10,000 in Funding and Mentorship for Environmental, Community, and Cultural Projects
summary: The Purpose Earth Grant Program has officially opened applications for its 2027 funding cycle, offering purpose-driven leaders and organizations an opportunity to receive grant funding of up to USD $10,000 , together with professional mentorship and global recognition. The initiative is designed to support innovative projects that create meaningful and lasting change within communities by addressing environmental challenges, strengthening community development, and promoting cultural collaboration. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis, with only the first 200 fully completed applications being considered. If the application cap is not reached earlier, the submission window will close on 10 August 2026 . About the Purpose Earth Grant Program Purpose Earth is an international grant and mentorship initiative dedicated to empowering individuals and organizations that are developing practical solutions to some of today s most pressing global challenges. Rather than simply providing financial assistance, the program seeks to partner with visionary leaders by combining funding, mentorship, and promotional opportunities to help projects grow sustainably and maximize their long-term impact. Each year, the organization invites applications from individuals and organizations whose work positively transforms local and global communities. Areas of Focus Projects submitted must align with at least one of the following priority areas. 1. Environmental Protection Projects should focus on protecting or restoring the environment through activities such as: Climate change solutions Conservation initiatives Environmental restoration Sustainable resource management Biodiversity protection Reducing environmental degradation 2. Community Activation Purpose Earth supports initiatives that strengthen communities by: Building resilient community networks Encouraging civic participation Promoting social innovation Improving quality of life Creating long-term positive social change 3. Cultural Collaboration Applicants may also submit projects that: Encourage creative expression Preserve cultural heritage Build connections across communities Foster compassion, inclusion, and collaboration Promote cross-cultural understanding What Successful Grant Recipients Will Receive Recipients selected for the 2027 Purpose Earth Grant Program will benefit from several forms of support beyond financial assistance. Grant Funding Successful applicants may receive funding ranging from USD $2,000 to USD $10,000 , depending on the needs and scope of their project. Professional Mentorship Awardees will receive personalized mentorship from experienced professionals who volunteer their expertise to help projects succeed. Mentorship may include guidance on: Project implementation Leadership Strategic planning Community engagement Organizational growth Long-term sustainability Global Visibility Grant recipients will also receive promotional support through Purpose Earth s communication channels, including: Featured project pages on the Purpose Earth website Digital media promotion Increased international exposure Participation in community celebrations and recognition events Who Can Apply? Purpose Earth welcomes applications from: Individual changemakers Community leaders Non-profit organizations Social enterprises Mission-driven organizations Environmental organizations Community development initiatives Cultural organizations Applicants must demonstrate that their project has a clear plan for implementation and will generate measurable community impact. APPLY HERE Funding Requirements Applicants should note the following funding conditions: Maximum funding available is USD $10,000 . Applications requesting more than USD $10,000 will not be considered. A detailed budget is mandatory. Applicants must clearly explain how every dollar of requested funding will be used. Projects That Will Not Receive Funding Purpose Earth does not provide funding for: Salaries or wages Consultant fees Contractor payments Advisor compensation Operational support Travel expenses Capital campaigns Sponsorships Conferences Prize programs Projects whose total cost greatly exceeds the maximum grant amount where Purpose Earth s contribution would only represent a small fraction of the overall budget. Eligibility Requirements Before applying, applicants should ensure they meet all eligibility requirements. Projects must: Still be active or in development. Not already be completed. Align with Purpose Earth s mission. Demonstrate community impact. Include a realistic implementation timeline. Include a detailed budget. Be submitted entirely in English. Supporting documents, including professional reference letters, must also be written in English. Videos should preferably be presented in English or include English subtitles. Professional Reference Letter Requirements Each application must include at least one professional reference letter. The reference letter must: Be dated within the last year. Come from someone who has worked professionally with the applicant. Clearly explain the professional relationship. Mention the project or similar work completed together. Support the applicant s qualifications. Include the referee s website or professional social media profile, such as LinkedIn. Personal references without professional relevance will not be accepted. Video Submission Requirements A one-minute video is a mandatory component of the application. The video should: Introduce the applicant. Explain the project s vision. Describe the expected impact. Show how the Purpose Earth grant would help achieve project goals. Professional production quality is not required. Applicants may record their video using a smartphone. The video link must remain accessible through one of the following methods: YouTube (Public or Unlisted) Google Drive Vimeo Dropbox WeTransfer (while ensuring the link remains active) Videos marked as private or requiring viewing permission may result in an incomplete application. Application Review Process Purpose Earth conducts a comprehensive review process to ensure every selected project meets its standards. Applications undergo careful evaluation and verification, including compliance with applicable financial regulations and sanctions screening. The organization also verifies that grant funding will be used appropriately and that applicants represent legitimate organizations or initiatives. For more information, visit 2027 Purpose Earth Grant Program HERE Grant Timeline Applicants should take note of the following schedule: Applications Open: 8 July 2026 Application Deadline: 10 August 2026 , or once 200 fully completed applications have been received. August 2026: Applications close. September to December 2026: Grant Selection Council reviews and vets applications. January to February 2027: Successful applicants receive award notifications. February 2027: First grant installment is paid. April to May 2027: Public announcement of recipients and online celebration. May 2027: Second grant installment is paid. Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on several important factors, including: Alignment with Purpose Earth s mission. Sustainability of the project. Potential for lasting community impact. Innovation and creativity. Quality of project planning. Strength of implementation strategy. Applicant experience and leadership. Realistic project timeline. Contribution to environmental protection, community activation, or cultural collaboration. Important Notes for Applicants Applicants should carefully review every application requirement before submitting. Keep the following in mind: Only fully completed applications will be reviewed. AI-generated applications are not accepted. Only one application may be submitted per project. Supporting documents must be submitted in English. Ensure every required attachment is included before submission. Applications cannot be edited after submission. Because only the first 200 complete applications will be accepted, interested applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents—including their budget, reference letter, and one-minute video—before beginning the application process. For more Global opportunities, visit OFY HERE Deadline Applications close on 10 August 2026 , or earlier if the maximum limit of 200 fully completed applications is rueached. Conclusion The 2027 Purpose Earth Grant Program represents an outstanding opportunity for individuals and organizations working to create meaningful environmental, community, and cultural change. Beyond financial support of up to USD $10,000, recipients gain access to experienced mentors, international visibility, and a global network committed to creating lasting impact. Applicants are encouraged to carefully review every eligibility requirement, prepare all supporting documentation in advance, and submit a complete application as early as possible due to the limited number of applications that will be accepted. Projects with a clear vision, measurable community impact, sustainable implementation strategy, and strong alignment with Purpose Earth s mission will be well positioned during the competitive selection process. title: DW Akademie and OHCHR Invite Journalists to Bangkok, Thailand for 2026 Migration and Scam Trafficking Reporting Training Program
summary: Journalists across South and Southeast Asia have an exciting opportunity to strengthen their reporting skills through a specialized international training program designed to improve coverage of migration, human rights, and scam trafficking. DW Akademie, in partnership with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), is inviting applications for the Navigating Narratives on Migration and Scam Trafficking Training for Journalists , which will take place in Bangkok, Thailand, from October 6–8, 2026 . The three-day, practice-oriented training will bring together journalists from selected countries across South and Southeast Asia to explore responsible migration reporting while addressing the growing challenge of scam-related exploitation. Participants will gain practical knowledge, enhance their storytelling skills, and learn how to report ethically on vulnerable populations without compromising their dignity or safety. Applications are currently open, and interested journalists must submit their applications before July 27, 2026 . About the Training Program Migration continues to be one of the world s most complex issues, intersecting with human rights, economic opportunities, technology, organized crime, and public policy. Unfortunately, migration is also increasingly linked to online scams, trafficking networks, misinformation, and disinformation campaigns that exploit vulnerable populations. Recognizing these challenges, DW Akademie and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) have developed a comprehensive regional training aimed at equipping journalists with practical reporting skills that contribute to accurate, ethical, and human-centered journalism. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical discussions, this workshop emphasizes hands-on learning and practical application. Participants will work through real-world reporting scenarios, engage with experienced trainers, and develop strategies for reporting on migration issues responsibly. The training seeks to improve public understanding of migration while helping journalists avoid harmful stereotypes and misleading narratives that often surround migration reporting. Training Dates and Venue The training will be held as follows: Location: Bangkok, Thailand Training Dates: October 6–8, 2026 Over three intensive days, participants will collaborate with fellow journalists from across the region, exchange experiences, and build professional networks that support cross-border reporting on migration and human rights issues. What Participants Will Learn The workshop has been carefully designed to address today s most pressing journalism challenges surrounding migration and scam trafficking. Participants will explore topics including: 1. Responsible Migration Reporting The training will help journalists: Produce balanced and evidence-based migration stories. Improve reporting accuracy on migration issues. Avoid sensationalism when covering vulnerable communities. Report in ways that respect the dignity and human rights of migrants. Understand ethical considerations when interviewing survivors and affected communities. 2. Scam Trafficking and Human Exploitation Participants will gain a deeper understanding of: Scam-related exploitation. Human trafficking connected to online scam operations. Cross-border criminal networks. The experiences of individuals trapped in scam compounds. Reporting approaches that protect victims from further harm. 3. Human Rights-Based Journalism A key focus of the workshop is ensuring that migration reporting reflects international human rights principles. Journalists will learn how to: Center human dignity in reporting. Minimize harm to interviewees. Avoid discriminatory language. Report on migration through a rights-based lens. 4. Migration, Disinformation, and Digital Media The workshop also examines how digital technologies influence migration narratives. Topics include: Misinformation surrounding migration. Disinformation campaigns targeting migrant communities. Algorithmic amplification of misleading content. The role of online platforms in shaping public opinion. Connections between digital ecosystems and online scam operations. Participants will explore practical tools for identifying false narratives and improving the quality of migration reporting in digital environments. Learning Resources Used During the Workshop The training is built upon two major resources developed by international experts. DW Akademie s Beyond Borders Toolkit Participants will work with the Beyond Borders Toolkit , a practical journalism resource developed by journalists for journalists. The toolkit provides guidance on: Ethical migration reporting. Story framing. Interview techniques. Responsible language choices. Human-centered storytelling. OHCHR Narrative Change Methodology The workshop also incorporates the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) s Narrative Change Methodology . This framework helps journalists: Challenge harmful narratives. Promote inclusive storytelling. Highlight human rights perspectives. Encourage accurate public understanding of migration. Why This Training Matters Migration stories significantly influence public opinion and policy discussions. Poorly framed reporting can reinforce stereotypes, increase discrimination, and contribute to misinformation. This training seeks to address these challenges by helping journalists produce reporting that is: Accurate. Ethical. Evidence-based. Human rights-centered. Sensitive to vulnerable communities. Resistant to misinformation and disinformation. By improving reporting standards, journalists can contribute to more informed public conversations while supporting accountability and protecting affected populations. About the Organizers DW Akademie DW Akademie is Germany s leading organization for international media development. It works with journalists, media organizations, and educational institutions worldwide to strengthen independent journalism, freedom of expression, and access to reliable information. Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) OHCHR is the principal United Nations office responsible for promoting and protecting human rights globally. The organization supports initiatives that strengthen human rights-based approaches across multiple sectors, including journalism and public communication. Project Background The training forms part of DW Akademie s Displacement and Dialogue Asia Project . The initiative is funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and aims to improve migration dialogue throughout Asia by supporting ethical journalism, informed public discourse, and responsible reporting practices. Why Journalists Should Apply Participants will benefit from: Practical journalism training. Hands-on reporting exercises. Regional networking opportunities. Exposure to international journalism methodologies. Improved understanding of migration reporting. Skills for reporting on scam trafficking. Human rights-based storytelling techniques. Knowledge on combating misinformation and disinformation. Cross-border collaboration with journalists from neighboring countries. The workshop offers an opportunity for journalists to strengthen both their professional skills and their contribution to responsible public-interest journalism across the region. Visit HERE For More Information About the Opportunity DW Akademie and OHCHR Invite Journalists to Bangkok, Thailand for 2026 Migration and Scam Trafficking Reporting Training Program Application Deadline Interested journalists should submit their applications before July 27, 2026 . Early application is encouraged, as the training is expected to attract significant interest from journalists across South and Southeast Asia. APPLY HERE Conclusion The Navigating Narratives on Migration and Scam Trafficking Training for Journalists represents an important opportunity for media professionals seeking to improve their reporting on migration, human rights, and online scam exploitation. Through practical learning, regional collaboration, and internationally recognized methodologies, participants will gain valuable tools for producing ethical, accurate, and impactful journalism. As migration-related issues continue to evolve across Asia, journalists play a critical role in shaping public understanding. This training equips them with the knowledge, skills, and ethical approaches needed to report responsibly while protecting the dignity of those most affected. Journalists from the eligible countries are encouraged to apply before the July 27, 2026 deadline and become part of a regional movement promoting responsible journalism. title: Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded 8-Year Fellowship for Outstanding Early-Career Scientists in Ireland
summary: Outstanding early-career scientists seeking to establish themselves as independent research leaders now have an exceptional opportunity to secure long-term funding through the Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship (URF) 2026 . This prestigious fellowship is designed to support talented researchers in the Republic of Ireland who have demonstrated exceptional scientific potential and are ready to build internationally competitive research careers. Jointly supported by the Royal Society and Research Ireland , the programme provides up to eight years of funding , enabling successful fellows to pursue ambitious research programmes while developing the skills, experience, and leadership needed to become permanent academic or research leaders. Open to researchers across the natural sciences—including biology, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics, and physics—the fellowship offers one of the most significant long-term career development opportunities available to early-career scientists in Ireland. The application deadline is 9 September 2026 at 15:00 (local Irish time) . About the Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship The Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship (URF) is a flagship funding scheme aimed at nurturing the next generation of world-class scientific leaders in the Republic of Ireland. The fellowship enables exceptional researchers in the early stages of their careers to establish independent research programmes while working at universities or eligible research institutions. By providing sustained financial support over an extended period, the programme allows fellows to focus on high-quality research, develop internationally competitive research profiles, and position themselves for permanent academic appointments. Successful applicants will receive fellowships awarded by the Royal Society , with the costs fully funded by Research Ireland . The scheme reflects the shared commitment of both organizations to advancing scientific excellence, strengthening Ireland s research ecosystem, and supporting innovative discoveries that address global scientific challenges. Purpose of the Fellowship The primary objective of the University Research Fellowship is to help outstanding scientists transition from promising early-career researchers into internationally recognized independent research leaders. Specifically, the fellowship aims to: Support the development of independent scientific research careers. Enable researchers to establish their own research programmes. Foster scientific excellence across the natural sciences. Build Ireland s long-term research capacity. Prepare fellows for permanent academic and research leadership positions. Encourage internationally competitive research. Promote innovation and scientific discovery. Fellowship Duration One of the most attractive aspects of this opportunity is its long-term funding commitment. Successful fellows will receive support for: Up to 8 years of funding The funding structure includes: Initial funding period Mid-point assessment Final three years of funding awarded following successful assessment This long-term model provides researchers with the stability needed to undertake ambitious, high-impact scientific research. Funding Structure Successful candidates will receive: Fellowship awarded by the Royal Society Funding provided by Research Ireland Up to eight years of research funding Long-term support to establish an independent research programme The final three years of funding are contingent upon a successful mid-point review, ensuring continued progress and research excellence. Research Areas Supported The fellowship supports all fields of the natural sciences . Eligible disciplines include, but are not limited to: Biological Sciences Researchers working in: Biology Ecology Genetics Molecular biology Evolutionary biology Microbiology Plant sciences Zoology Biomedical Sciences Including: Medical sciences Biomedical research Human health Translational medicine Immunology Neuroscience Chemistry Research areas such as: Organic chemistry Analytical chemistry Physical chemistry Materials chemistry Environmental chemistry Engineering Including: Civil engineering Mechanical engineering Electrical engineering Chemical engineering Biomedical engineering Materials engineering Mathematics Areas including: Pure mathematics Applied mathematics Statistics Computational mathematics Mathematical modelling Physics Research fields including: Theoretical physics Experimental physics Astrophysics Condensed matter physics Quantum science Particle physics The fellowship also welcomes proposals from other natural science disciplines aligned with the programme s objectives. Why Apply? The Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship is one of Ireland s premier career-development opportunities for early-career scientists. Successful fellows will benefit from: Long-term research funding Opportunity to establish an independent research group Increased research autonomy Career progression toward permanent academic positions International recognition through the Royal Society Enhanced research leadership experience Opportunities to build collaborations Increased competitiveness for future research funding Ability to undertake ambitious scientific projects Strong institutional support Career Development Opportunities Beyond financial support, fellows will have the opportunity to: Build an internationally competitive research profile. Develop leadership and supervisory experience. Mentor postgraduate students and junior researchers. Expand international research collaborations. Publish high-impact scientific papers. Increase research visibility. Strengthen applications for permanent university appointments. Eligibility The fellowship targets researchers who are: Outstanding scientists. In the early stages of their research careers. Demonstrating exceptional scientific promise. Ready to establish independent research programmes. Showing strong leadership potential. Applicants should have the potential to become internationally recognized leaders within their disciplines. Who Should Apply? This fellowship is ideal for: Early-career researchers Postdoctoral researchers Research scientists Academic researchers University-based scientists Emerging research leaders Scientists seeking independence in research Applicants should possess strong scientific achievements and demonstrate the capacity to build successful long-term research programmes. Fields Eligible for Funding The fellowship supports research across: Biology Biomedical Sciences Chemistry Engineering Mathematics Physics Other Natural Sciences Funding Timeline Call Launch 14 July 2026 Fellowship Duration Up to 8 years Mid-Point Assessment Funding for the final three years will be subject to a successful mid-term review. Application Process Prospective applicants are encouraged to: Carefully read the official scheme guidance notes. Review the eligibility requirements. Consult departmental contacts. Speak with current or former University Research Fellowship holders for advice and insights. Prepare all required application materials well before the submission deadline. Ensure nominated referees and Heads of Department complete their required documentation before the deadline. Applicants should note that the deadline also applies to: Nominated References Head of Department Statements Late submissions may not be accepted. Visit HERE to learn more and apply. Information and Support Applicants who require additional clarification after reviewing the scheme notes may contact the Royal Society University Research Fellowship team. Research Ireland also encourages prospective applicants to connect with current and former fellowship holders through their departments to gain valuable insight into preparing competitive applications. Important Dates Activity Date Call Launch 14 July 2026 Application Deadline 9 September 2026 (15:00 Irish Local Time) Fellowship Duration Up to 8 years Why This Fellowship Stands Out Several features distinguish this programme from many other research fellowships: Eight years of funding provides exceptional career stability. Joint backing by the Royal Society and Research Ireland offers significant prestige. Supports the transition to research independence. Covers all major natural science disciplines. Designed specifically for future research leaders. Provides a pathway toward permanent academic careers. Encourages ambitious, high-impact scientific research. For researchers aiming to establish themselves as internationally competitive scientists, this fellowship represents an outstanding career milestone. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Applicants may strengthen their submissions by: Clearly articulating the originality and significance of their proposed research. Demonstrating independence from previous supervisors. Highlighting previous publications, research achievements, and scientific impact. Presenting a realistic long-term research vision. Securing strong institutional support. Working closely with referees to ensure timely submission of references. Reviewing the official guidance thoroughly before applying. Conclusion The Royal Society – Research Ireland University Research Fellowship 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding early-career scientists to establish themselves as independent research leaders through one of Ireland s most prestigious long-term fellowship programmes. With funding of up to eight years, recognition from the Royal Society, and financial support from Research Ireland, the fellowship provides an ideal environment for ambitious researchers to pursue innovative scientific discoveries while building internationally competitive careers. Whether your expertise lies in biology, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics, physics, or another natural science discipline, this fellowship provides the resources, stability, and prestige needed to make a lasting impact on the global scientific community. title: WomenPower2030 Seed Grant 2026: Up to €5,000 for Women-Led Organizations in Nigeria and Sierra Leone Advancing Gender-Just Climate Action and Sustainable Development
summary: The Women Environmental Programme (WEP) has officially opened applications for the WomenPower2030 Seed Grant 2026 , inviting eligible women-led and women’s rights organizations in Nigeria and Sierra Leone to apply for funding of up to €5,000 to implement innovative initiatives that advance gender equality, climate justice, and sustainable development. The grant forms part of the WomenPower2030: Feminist Accelerate Actions for Sustainable Development initiative, a global partnership supported through a Financial Framework Partnership Agreement (FFPA) between the European Union and a consortium of leading feminist organizations. Through this funding opportunity, selected organizations will implement projects that strengthen women s leadership, influence public policies, promote gender-responsive climate action, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). About the WomenPower2030 Project WomenPower2030 is an international initiative designed to strengthen the participation and leadership of women, girls, and marginalized groups in sustainable development and climate governance. The project seeks to ensure that feminist organizations and women s civil society organizations play an active role in designing, implementing, and monitoring policies and programmes that promote inclusive and gender-just development. The overall objective is to advance the rights and leadership of women, girls, and marginalized communities while accelerating progress toward sustainable development. Consortium Behind the Initiative WomenPower2030 is implemented through a partnership led by Women Engage for a Common Future (WECF) alongside four international feminist organizations: Women Environmental Programme (WEP) African Women s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET) Asia Pacific Forum on Women, Law and Development (APWLD) Fundación para Estudio e Investigación de la Mujer (FEIM) Together, these organizations work to amplify feminist leadership and influence sustainable development policies at national, regional, and global levels. Seed Grant Objectives The seed grants are intended to empower women-led organizations to develop and implement impactful initiatives that contribute to the goals of WomenPower2030. Successful projects should strengthen women s participation in decision-making, influence policy reforms, promote sustainable solutions, and improve gender-responsive governance. Projects are expected to create measurable impact rather than focusing solely on awareness campaigns. Priority Areas of Support Applicants may propose projects addressing one or more of the following thematic areas: 1. Policy Monitoring and Policy Dialogue Projects that: Monitor government policies. Engage policymakers. Advocate for gender-responsive policies. Promote accountability in sustainable development. 2. Education and Awareness Initiatives that raise awareness on: Gender equality. Climate action. Sustainable development. Women s rights. However, awareness activities alone are not sufficient to qualify for funding. 3. Movement Building Projects that: Strengthen women s movements. Build coalitions. Increase collaboration among feminist organizations. Promote collective advocacy. 4. Demonstration of Sustainable Solutions Initiatives showcasing: Practical sustainable development solutions. Community-based innovations. Environmentally sustainable services. Gender-responsive climate interventions. 5. Women s Leadership and Capacity Building Projects focusing on: Women s leadership training. Gender-specific capacity development. Monitoring and accountability. Skills strengthening. 6. Tracking SDG and Climate Policies Projects that monitor: Sustainable Development Goal implementation. Climate policies. Government budgets. Gender-responsive budgeting. 7. Social Media and Mainstream Media Campaigns Strategic communication initiatives that strengthen advocacy through: Digital campaigns. Media engagement. Public awareness linked to policy influence. Important Funding Priorities The Women Environmental Programme emphasizes that priority will be given to projects that: Influence public policies benefiting women. Demonstrate sustainable and equitable solutions. Promote gender-responsive budgeting. Integrate women s needs into development planning. Applications focusing primarily on workshops or awareness-raising activities without broader policy or systems impact will not be considered. Grant Value Each successful organization may receive funding of up to: €5,000 The funding is intended to support the implementation of innovative projects aligned with the objectives of WomenPower2030. Project Duration Funded projects should be implemented within: 3 to 6 months Applicants should prepare realistic work plans that can be completed within this timeframe. Language of Application All applications must be submitted in: English Required Application Documents Eligible organizations must submit: Completed application form (Word format) Detailed budget (Excel format) Certificate of registration Letter of reference Evidence of previous work (reports, media coverage, testimonials, or related documentation compiled into one document) The organizers may request additional supporting information where necessary. Application Guidelines Applicants should note the following: Applications must not exceed 10 pages , excluding attachments. Only Word documents (.doc or .docx) will be accepted. Applications that fail to address the specified focus areas will not be considered. Only shortlisted or successful applicants may be contacted due to the expected high number of submissions. How to Apply Interested organizations should: Download the official application form. Complete the application in English. Prepare all required supporting documents. Attach the detailed budget and required organizational documents. Submit the application via email with the required subject line: WomenPower2030 seed-grant application Applications should be submitted to the official grants email provided by the Women Environmental Programme. Application Deadline Deadline: 31 July 2026 (23:59 WAT) Late applications are unlikely to be considered, and applicants are encouraged to submit well before the deadline. Why Organizations Should Apply The WomenPower2030 Seed Grant offers women-led organizations an opportunity to: Secure funding of up to €5,000. Strengthen advocacy for gender-responsive policies. Influence climate and sustainable development decision-making. Promote women s leadership. Demonstrate innovative sustainability solutions. Expand partnerships within regional and global feminist networks. Contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. Conclusion The WomenPower2030 Seed Grant 2026 presents an excellent opportunity for women-led organizations in Nigeria and Sierra Leone to access funding for initiatives that strengthen women s leadership, influence public policy, and advance gender-responsive climate action and sustainable development. Organizations with innovative ideas capable of creating lasting policy and community impact are encouraged to prepare strong applications and submit them before the 31 July 2026 deadline. title: PhD Scholarship at the University of Limerick, Ireland 2026: Fully Funded Opportunity in Applied Language Studies and Climate Journalism Research
summary: The University of Limerick (UL), Ireland , is inviting applications for a prestigious fully funded PhD Scholarship within the Centre for Applied Language Studies in the School of Modern Languages and Applied Linguistics . This four-year doctoral opportunity is designed for outstanding students with a passion for language, journalism, sociolinguistics, climate communication, and interdisciplinary research. The scholarship forms part of an ambitious research project titled Posthumanist Sociolinguistics and Journalistic Practices: Reporting on Climate Change in Irish and German Media. The project is funded by Research Ireland and the Irish Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and aims to transform understanding of how climate change is represented in mainstream journalism. Successful applicants will receive an annual stipend of €25,000 , payment of EU student tuition fees , extensive research training, conference participation opportunities, publication experience, and supervision from leading experts in the field. Scholarship Overview Climate change has become one of the defining global challenges of our time. As weather events become increasingly severe and environmental crises continue to intensify, journalists play an essential role in informing the public about climate issues and encouraging meaningful responses. Despite the growing importance of climate journalism, traditional media outlets across Europe have frequently been criticised for presenting climate change through predominantly human-centred perspectives. Researchers believe these reporting approaches may limit public understanding of the broader environmental crisis. This PhD project seeks to address these challenges by examining how Irish and German media organisations report on climate change and how language, images, and other communicative strategies influence public understanding of environmental issues. The successful PhD candidate will contribute significantly to this groundbreaking research while simultaneously developing an independent doctoral thesis. Scholarship Benefits Successful applicants will receive a comprehensive funding package that includes: Annual stipend of €25,000 Funding for 4 years of full-time doctoral study Payment of EU student tuition fees Opportunity to participate in: International conferences Career development programmes Academic workshops Collaborative publications Professional research training Supervision by experienced researchers at the University of Limerick Opportunity to work on a major internationally funded research project Important Note: Applicants from outside the European Union may be required to pay the difference between EU tuition fees and international tuition fees. Research Project Focus The scholarship is part of a wider comparative research project investigating climate journalism in Ireland and Germany. The research explores several important questions, including: How do journalists report climate change? How do newspapers frame environmental issues? What language is used when discussing climate protection? How do media representations influence public understanding of climate change? What differences exist between Irish and German reporting practices? How do political, cultural, and economic contexts shape climate journalism? The project combines qualitative and quantitative research methods to generate new insights into environmental communication. Responsibilities of the PhD Candidate The selected doctoral researcher will play a central role throughout the project. Primary responsibilities include: Compiling a large corpus of newspaper articles related to climate change Collecting articles from one Irish broadsheet newspaper and one German broadsheet newspaper Organising and preparing datasets for analysis Conducting corpus linguistic analysis Identifying linguistic patterns in climate reporting Examining anthropocentric news framing Performing detailed multimodal analysis of news reports Comparing climate reporting practices between Ireland and Germany Investigating cultural, economic, and political influences on media coverage Developing an independent doctoral thesis based on the research findings Academic Environment Throughout the four-year scholarship, the successful candidate will be based at the: Centre for Applied Language Studies School of Modern Languages and Applied Linguistics University of Limerick Ireland The researcher will work under the supervision of: Dr Sarah Josefine Schaefer (Principal Investigator) Professor Helen Kelly-Holmes In addition to direct supervision, the doctoral student will benefit from: Academic mentoring Research collaboration Networking opportunities Skills development workshops Career development programmes Opportunities for international conference participation Academic publishing experience Essential Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all of the following requirements: Demonstrate B2 (CEFR) level proficiency (or equivalent) in both: Written English Spoken English Written German Spoken German Hold an honours undergraduate degree (or equivalent) with at least 2.1 classification in one of the following or a closely related discipline: Linguistics German English Journalism Related fields Preferred Qualifications Although not mandatory, applicants with the following qualifications will be highly competitive: Master s degree in: Applied Linguistics Sociolinguistics Journalism Sociology Social Sciences Related disciplines Experience using qualitative research methods Experience using quantitative research methods Knowledge of discourse analysis Experience with linguistic corpus analysis Strong interest in interdisciplinary research Required Application Documents Applicants must submit a complete application consisting of the following documents: Cover Letter (maximum 1,000 words) explaining: Why you are interested in the project Your suitability for doctoral research What you would contribute to the research project Curriculum Vitae (CV) including: Educational background Employment history Relevant training Research experience Academic Writing Sample such as: Bachelor s thesis chapter Master s thesis chapter Published academic article Other scholarly writing Contact information for two academic referees Official university transcripts Certified English translations of transcripts if the originals are not in English or German Application document should be sent to this email: helen.kelly.holmes@ul.ie Selection Process Applications will undergo a competitive review process. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to participate in online interviews during September 2026 . The selection committee will assess: Academic excellence Research potential Suitability for interdisciplinary research Communication skills Motivation for pursuing doctoral study Alignment with the objectives of the project Important Dates Application Deadline: 17:00 Irish local time, Monday, 14 September 2026 Online Interviews: September 2026 Scholarship Start Date: 1 December 2026 Scholarship Duration: 4 years (full-time only) Why Apply? This scholarship provides an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers to contribute to internationally significant research examining how media shape public understanding of climate change. Participants will gain advanced expertise in: Applied Linguistics Sociolinguistics Climate Communication Journalism Studies Corpus Linguistics Discourse Analysis Multimodal Research Comparative Media Studies In addition to receiving generous financial support, doctoral researchers will build strong international academic networks, publish scholarly research, and develop highly transferable research skills for careers in academia, policy, journalism, communication, and beyond. Visit HERE to learn more about PhD Scholarship at the University of Limerick, Ireland 2026 Conclusion The University of Limerick s PhD Scholarship in the Centre for Applied Language Studies offers an exceptional opportunity for graduates interested in language, journalism, climate communication, and interdisciplinary research. title: Rithm Fellowship 2026–2027: Paid Youth Leadership Fellowship for Young Changemakers Shaping Human Connection in the Age of AI
summary: Artificial Intelligence is transforming nearly every aspect of modern life—from education and work to communication and relationships. While AI presents exciting opportunities, it also raises important questions about loneliness, digital well-being, and the future of human connection. To ensure young people are not just passive users of technology but active architects of a more connected future, The Rithm Project has opened applications for its Rithm Fellowship 2026–2027 . This paid fellowship is designed for five exceptional young leaders aged 18 to 22 who are passionate about shaping conversations around AI, technology, mental health, education, and human relationships. Fellows will receive a USD $2,000 stipend , work alongside researchers and innovators, contribute to national conversations, and help influence how society approaches human connection in the age of artificial intelligence. About The Rithm Project The Rithm Project is a mission-driven organization dedicated to building a future where human connection thrives alongside artificial intelligence. Rather than viewing AI solely through the lens of productivity or technological advancement, the organization focuses on helping young people cultivate meaningful relationships, empathy, belonging, and community in an increasingly digital world. The organization conducts youth-centered research, develops educational tools and resources, convenes leaders across sectors, and creates opportunities for young people to influence conversations around AI and society. Its vision is to ensure that the next generation helps shape technologies that strengthen rather than weaken human relationships. About the Rithm Fellowship The Rithm Fellowship is a youth leadership programme where participants play an active role in shaping The Rithm Project s work. Rather than simply attending workshops, fellows become trusted collaborators whose perspectives help guide research, influence organizational strategy, and shape products designed for young people. The fellowship intentionally brings together a diverse cohort of five individuals from different backgrounds, experiences, and geographic locations. The goal is to create a community where varied lived experiences contribute to richer conversations about AI, connection, and the future. The fellowship runs from September 2026 through May 2027 , combining leadership development, collaborative project work, public engagement, and opportunities to represent youth voices in national conversations. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will receive a range of professional and leadership development opportunities, including: USD $2,000 stipend for participation. Opportunity to influence national conversations on AI and human connection. Direct collaboration with researchers, educators, technologists, and mental health experts. Hands-on experience contributing to research and innovative projects. Opportunities to represent youth perspectives at conferences, workshops, and speaking engagements. Leadership development in facilitation, communication, and collaboration. Networking with a multigenerational community of changemakers. Participation in exclusive Rithm Project events and summits. Experience working with one of the leading organizations exploring AI and youth well-being. What Fellows Will Do The fellowship is divided into two primary areas of responsibility. 1. Youth Leadership and Public Representation (Approximately 60%) Fellows will: Represent youth perspectives during internal strategy discussions. Participate in conferences, workshops, and public events. Engage with educators, researchers, policymakers, funders, and mental health professionals. Facilitate discussions that encourage diverse viewpoints. Travel independently within the United States for selected fellowship activities. 2. Research and Project Contributions (Approximately 40%) Participants will also: Contribute to youth-focused research. Pilot educational resources and digital tools. Help shape The Rithm Project s products and initiatives. Share lived experiences that inform future programmes. Collaborate on projects addressing AI, belonging, and social connection. Develop practical ideas that can influence future systems and policies. Who Is the Fellowship Looking For? The Rithm Project is seeking young people who are thoughtful, curious, and willing to engage in meaningful conversations about technology and society. Ideal candidates are individuals who: Have lived experiences or insights related to AI and human connection. Care deeply about strengthening communities and relationships. Are confident sharing ideas while remaining open to different perspectives. Possess empathy and emotional intelligence. Enjoy storytelling and communicating complex ideas in accessible ways. Demonstrate initiative and a willingness to contribute to collaborative projects. Have a growth mindset and are eager to learn from feedback. Can think critically while translating ideas into practical action. Time Commitment The fellowship is intentionally designed to fit alongside academic or professional commitments. Participants should expect to dedicate: Approximately 7–10 hours per month . Additional time for occasional travel and public events. Successful applicants must be available for the following mandatory in-person events in Denver, Colorado: October 16–18, 2026 – Fellowship Kickoff. May 10–13, 2027 – Human Connection and AI Summit. Why You Should Apply The Rithm Fellowship is more than a leadership programme—it is an opportunity to help shape one of the most important conversations of our time. As AI continues to transform education, work, and relationships, young people are uniquely positioned to influence how technology is developed and used. By joining this fellowship, participants will not only develop leadership and communication skills but also contribute to research, public dialogue, and practical solutions that prioritize empathy, connection, and human flourishing. Whether your passion lies in education, technology, mental health, public policy, or community organizing, this fellowship offers a platform to make your voice heard and collaborate with leaders committed to building a healthier digital future. title: Lund University PhD in Sustainability Science 2027 in Sweden (Fully Funded with Salary): Apply for a Doctoral Research Position on Just Energy Transitions
summary: Lund University, one of Europe s oldest and most prestigious universities, is inviting applications for a PhD in Sustainability Science at the Lund University Centre for Sustainability Studies (LUCSUS) . This exciting doctoral opportunity offers successful applicants the chance to conduct cutting-edge interdisciplinary research on the role of finance in shaping just energy transitions while earning a full salary throughout the four-year doctoral programme. The position is based in Lund, Sweden , and is part of a prestigious FORMAS-funded international research project that explores how financial systems influence the transition away from fossil fuels. The successful candidate will work alongside researchers in Sweden and Canada while contributing to one of the world s most pressing sustainability challenges. Application Deadline: 28 August 2026 About Lund University Founded in 1666 , Lund University consistently ranks among the world s leading universities. With approximately 46,000 students and 8,500 staff , the university is internationally recognized for excellence in research and education. The successful PhD candidate will join the Lund University Centre for Sustainability Studies (LUCSUS) , a globally respected institute dedicated to addressing sustainability challenges through interdisciplinary research and innovative educational programmes. LUCSUS conducts research across several major sustainability themes, including: Climate change and resilience Land-use governance and development Urban governance and transformation Energy justice and sustainable energy systems Biodiversity and natural resource management The centre collaborates extensively with international partners and promotes both critical thinking and practical solutions to global sustainability issues. About the PhD Programme The Sustainability Science PhD programme is a 240-credit doctoral programme , equivalent to four years of full-time study . Unlike many doctoral programmes around the world, this position is a salaried employment opportunity. Successful candidates will: Receive a monthly salary from Lund University Conduct independent doctoral research Complete coursework Write and publicly defend a doctoral dissertation The appointment may also include teaching responsibilities of up to 20% of working time. If teaching duties are assigned, the doctoral appointment will be extended accordingly. The successful applicant will: Be based full-time in Lund, Sweden Receive office space at LUCSUS Become part of an international research community Collaborate with leading sustainability researchers Research Project: The Financial Sector s Role in Just Energy Transitions The doctoral research forms part of the FORMAS-funded project titled: (Dis)orderly Transitions: The Financial Sector s Role in Shaping Just Energy Transitions. The project builds upon the COP28 agreement , which emphasized the need for moving away from fossil fuels in a: Just Orderly Equitable manner. The research investigates an important question: How does the financial sector influence the global transition away from fossil fuels? Researchers will critically examine how financial institutions attempt to create orderly transitions through financial instruments that seek to manage uncertainty, risks, investments, and future pathways. The project combines perspectives from: Political economy Economic sociology Sustainability science Critical social sciences Research Focus The selected PhD researcher will conduct qualitative fieldwork involving financial actors across Scandinavia. Research topics include: Transition bonds Green taxonomies Financial markets Risk management Future-making practices Energy transitions Power dynamics within financial systems Fieldwork may include: Interviews Participant observation Document analysis Stakeholder engagement The research aims to improve understanding of how financial systems influence both the opportunities and inequalities emerging during energy transitions. What You ll Receive Successful applicants will benefit from numerous opportunities, including: Fully Paid Doctoral Position Candidates receive a monthly salary from Lund University throughout the four-year programme. Applicants should have either: A second-cycle qualification (Master s degree) before 1 January 2027 , or At least 240 higher education credits , including 60 credits at second-cycle level , or Equivalent international qualifications. Assessment Criteria Applicants will be evaluated based on: Academic excellence Independent research potential Motivation Communication skills English language proficiency Collaboration skills Suitability for interdisciplinary sustainability research Scandinavian language skills are advantageous but not required . Thesis Copies of thesis work totaling at least 30 credits , including: Master s thesis, or Master s and Bachelor s theses 5. title: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council Partnership Development Grants 2026: Receive Up to CAD 250,000 to Build Innovative Research Partnerships
summary: The Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) Partnership Development Grants 2026 Competition is now open for applications. This prestigious Canadian research funding opportunity provides grants ranging from CAD 75,000 to CAD 250,000 to support the development of innovative partnerships in the social sciences and humanities. The funding is designed to help researchers, postsecondary institutions, not-for-profit organizations, and partner institutions establish or strengthen formal collaborations that generate impactful research, advance knowledge, promote innovation, and create meaningful societal change. Projects funded through this program can run for one to three years , providing sufficient time for teams to establish strong collaborations, conduct high-quality research, engage stakeholders, train students and emerging scholars, and mobilize research findings nationally and internationally. Application Deadline Application Deadline: November 16, 2026 (8:00 p.m. Eastern Time) Results Announcement: March 2027 About the Partnership Development Grants The Partnership Development Grants form part of SSHRC s broader Research Partnerships Program , which aims to encourage collaborative research initiatives capable of producing lasting academic, social, economic, and cultural impacts. The grants support projects that either: Develop new research partnerships; Expand existing partnerships with new research activities; Design innovative partnership models; Test collaborative approaches that can become best practices; Develop scalable partnership models for regional, national, or international adoption. The initiative also places strong emphasis on: Knowledge mobilization Student engagement Research training Mentorship Cross-sector collaboration Public impact Funding Value Successful applicants may receive funding between: CAD 75,000 Up to CAD 250,000 Funding is provided over a period of: 1 year 2 years 3 years Objectives of the Grant The Partnership Development Grants support projects that aim to: Develop innovative research partnerships. Strengthen existing research collaborations. Foster interdisciplinary research. Support international research collaborations. Promote knowledge mobilization. Improve research capacity. Train students and emerging scholars. Create best practices for partnership development. Generate research with measurable societal impact. Increase collaboration between academia and external organizations. Types of Partnerships Supported SSHRC welcomes numerous partnership models, including: 1. Existing Partnerships Funding may support existing partnerships seeking to launch entirely new research initiatives beyond their current activities. 2. New Partnerships Support is available for partnerships in their early stages that are beginning collaborative research activities. 3. Disciplinary and Interdisciplinary Partnerships Projects involving one or multiple disciplines in the social sciences and humanities are eligible. Interdisciplinary collaborations involving: Natural sciences Engineering Health sciences may also qualify if they satisfy SSHRC subject matter eligibility guidelines. 4. Cross-Sector Knowledge Co-Creation Projects that unite: Universities Governments Non-profit organizations Community organizations Industry partners to solve major intellectual, social, economic, or cultural challenges. 5. Research Networks Funding supports networks established to: Conduct collaborative research Share expertise Train researchers Exchange knowledge Promote innovation 6. Knowledge Mobilization Partnerships Projects may focus on making research findings more accessible through: Public engagement Policy development Community outreach Institutional capacity building Practical implementation Indigenous Research SSHRC strongly welcomes proposals involving: Indigenous research Indigenous knowledge systems Research creation Indigenous partnerships Applications involving Indigenous research will be evaluated using SSHRC s specialized Indigenous research review guidelines. Joint Initiative Applicants may also participate in the: Mitacs Accelerate Grants joint initiative This collaboration provides additional opportunities for research partnerships and talent development. Future Challenge Areas Applicants are encouraged to consider SSHRC s Future Challenge Areas while designing proposals. Although alignment with these challenge areas does not affect funding decisions or provide additional funding, it can help applicants demonstrate the future relevance and broader significance of their research. Eligible Research Areas Projects may involve virtually any eligible social sciences or humanities discipline, including interdisciplinary work that satisfies SSHRC eligibility requirements. Examples include: Education Sociology Economics History Political Science Psychology Indigenous Studies Cultural Studies Public Policy Geography International Development Communication Studies Literature Philosophy Linguistics Anthropology Projects That Are Not Eligible Projects whose primary purpose is: Curriculum development Program evaluation Preparation of teaching materials Digitization of collections Database creation are not eligible under this funding opportunity. Who Can Apply? Applications are submitted by research teams consisting of: Applicant (Project Director) Co-directors Co-applicants Collaborators Eligible applicants generally include: Researchers affiliated with eligible Canadian institutions Eligible postdoctoral researchers Eligible PhD candidates Canadian not-for-profit organizations Eligible Canadian postsecondary institutions Partner Organizations Partner organizations may include: Universities Colleges Research institutes Government organizations Municipal governments Provincial governments Territorial governments Indigenous governments Indigenous governing bodies Non-profit organizations Philanthropic foundations Think tanks International universities Private sector organizations Partners may be located in Canada or internationally . Student Training and Mentorship One of the major strengths of the Partnership Development Grants is the emphasis on developing future researchers. Applications are expected to provide high-quality plans for: Student supervision Mentorship Research experience Professional development Employability Knowledge exchange Leadership development The quality of these plans forms an important component of the evaluation process. Institutional Contributions Although no minimum financial contribution is required, applicants are expected to demonstrate meaningful institutional support through: Cash contributions In-kind contributions Existing partnership commitments Strategic collaboration plans Application Process Applications must be completed using SSHRC s electronic application system. Most applications must be submitted through: An authorized research grants office at the applicant s institution; or An authorized representative of an eligible not-for-profit organization. Eligible postdoctoral researchers and eligible PhD candidates may submit applications directly to SSHRC. Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations well before the deadline. Evaluation Criteria Applications are reviewed through a competitive merit review process. The assessment is based on three major criteria. 1. Challenge (50%) Reviewers evaluate: Originality Significance Contribution to knowledge Research design Literature review Research methodology Student training Expected impact Progress indicators 2. Feasibility (20%) Assessment includes: Project timeline Partnership quality Leadership Governance Team expertise Budget justification Knowledge mobilization Institutional support 3. Capability (30%) Reviewers consider: Applicant experience Publications Creative outputs Knowledge mobilization Previous mentoring Previous partnerships Research achievements Applications must score 3.0 or higher in each evaluation category to be recommended for funding. Reporting Requirements Successful grant recipients will be required to report on: Fund utilization Project activities Outcomes Partnership achievements SSHRC will communicate detailed reporting requirements after awards are announced. Why This Grant Matters The SSHRC Partnership Development Grants provide an outstanding opportunity to establish transformative research partnerships capable of generating long-term academic and societal impact. By supporting collaboration among universities, governments, Indigenous organizations, communities, industry, and non-profit organizations, the grants encourage innovative research that addresses pressing social, cultural, economic, and intellectual challenges while training the next generation of researchers. Researchers seeking to launch impactful partnerships and expand collaborative research networks should strongly consider applying for this highly competitive funding opportunity.
