title: UNICEF StartUp Lab Reducing Single-Use Plastics through WASH & Social and Behaviour Change Innovation Challenge 2026: Win $5,000, Pilot Your Innovation in Ghana, and Help Protect Children’s Health
summary: Applications are now open for the UNICEF StartUp Lab Reducing Single-Use Plastics through Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Social Behaviour Change (SBC) Innovation Challenge 2026 . This innovation challenge is inviting startups, innovators, entrepreneurs, social enterprises, and changemakers to develop practical, scalable, and sustainable solutions that reduce the use of single-use plastics within Ghana s WASH sector while promoting healthier communities and protecting children from the harmful effects of plastic pollution. Selected innovators will receive funding, mentorship, technical support, and the opportunity to pilot their solutions within UNICEF WASH and community programmes. Application Deadline: July 23, 2026 About the UNICEF StartUp Lab WASH Innovation Challenge Plastic pollution has become one of the biggest environmental and public health challenges affecting Ghana today. Single-use plastics are widely used across the country, particularly within water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Products such as: Plastic water sachets Plastic packaging Disposable hygiene products Other single-use plastic materials continue to accumulate in communities due to inadequate collection and disposal systems. Improper disposal of these plastics blocks drainage systems, pollutes rivers and streams, contaminates soil, and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. The challenge goes beyond environmental concerns. Poor waste management creates stagnant water that becomes breeding grounds for mosquitoes, increasing the spread of malaria and other water-borne diseases. Burning plastic waste also contributes to poor air quality, increasing respiratory illnesses among vulnerable populations, particularly children. As plastics gradually degrade into microplastics, they contaminate water sources and food systems, posing long-term risks to public health and food security. Recognizing these growing challenges, UNICEF StartUp Lab is seeking innovative solutions that promote a circular economy while transforming how communities use, collect, reuse, replace, reduce, and recycle plastics. Why This Challenge Matters Current plastic waste management systems are not sufficient to address the growing environmental crisis. The UNICEF StartUp Lab seeks to encourage innovative approaches that move communities away from the traditional use-and-dispose model toward sustainable circular systems. The challenge combines innovation with Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) approaches to encourage lasting behavioural shifts that reduce dependence on disposable plastics. Ultimately, the initiative aims to improve sanitation systems, protect the environment, strengthen climate resilience, and improve health outcomes for children. Objectives of the Challenge The challenge seeks innovative solutions that can: Reduce dependence on single-use plastics. Promote responsible plastic collection and disposal. Encourage reuse, reduction, replacement, and recycling using the 3Rs. Improve sanitation and hygiene services. Strengthen community participation in sustainable waste management. Protect children from diseases associated with plastic pollution. Support climate-resilient WASH systems. Develop scalable and affordable innovations that can be implemented across Ghana. Challenge Themes Applicants may address one or more of the following innovation areas. 1. Alternative Solutions Develop affordable, accessible, and scalable alternatives to single-use plastics used within water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Solutions should promote: Reduction Replacement Reuse Recycling while remaining practical for local communities. 2. Behavioural Integration Design Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) strategies that encourage households, institutions, and communities to reduce their reliance on disposable plastics. Innovations may include: Behaviour change campaigns Digital engagement platforms Community education programmes Incentive systems School-based interventions 3. Circular Systems Develop closed-loop systems that improve the collection, reuse, reduction, replacement, recycling, or responsible disposal of plastics throughout the WASH value chain. Potential innovations may include: Plastic collection systems Community recycling programmes Deposit-return schemes Incentive-based recycling models Waste recovery technologies Circular business models 4. Climate Resilience Create innovative WASH infrastructure and services capable of reducing the environmental impacts of plastic pollution while protecting communities from climate-related risks. Solutions should improve both environmental sustainability and child health. What UNICEF Is Looking For UNICEF is seeking practical innovations capable of significantly reducing or eliminating single-use plastics from household and community environments. Successful applicants should demonstrate their ability to: Develop Sustainable Alternatives Innovations should introduce practical alternatives to disposable plastics that are affordable, locally available, and environmentally sustainable. Drive Behavioural Change Applicants should demonstrate how Social and Behaviour Change methodologies will encourage communities and service providers to adopt sustainable practices. Improve Community Health Solutions should reduce children s exposure to pollution caused by plastic waste while supporting healthier sanitation systems. Deliver Scalable Models Innovations should be: Affordable Scalable Adaptable Easy to integrate into existing government or community WASH programmes Benefits for Selected Innovators Successful applicants will receive: US$5,000 cash prize Opportunity to pilot their innovation within UNICEF WASH and community programmes Mentorship from experts Data support to strengthen and validate their innovation Opportunity to build scalable and cost-effective solutions Alignment with Ghana s National Plastic Management Policy Access to public-sector WASH implementation opportunities Strategic Importance This challenge supports several national and global development priorities, including: Ghana s National Plastic Management Policy Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 – Climate Action The programme also strengthens collaboration between startups, innovators, government institutions, and development partners to create sustainable environmental solutions that directly improve children s wellbeing. Expected Outcomes Selected innovations will be piloted within existing UNICEF WASH programmes and community initiatives. The pilot projects will generate evidence demonstrating how innovative approaches can: Reduce plastic waste. Improve waste collection systems. Encourage behavioural change. Strengthen sanitation infrastructure. Improve environmental sustainability. Protect children s health. Create scalable models for wider implementation across Ghana. The long-term vision is to build a portfolio of proven innovations capable of transforming plastic waste management while creating healthier communities and more resilient WASH systems. Why You Should Apply If your startup or innovation focuses on sustainability, waste management, climate action, circular economy, sanitation, recycling, behaviour change, environmental technology, or WASH, this challenge offers an excellent opportunity to test your innovation in a real-world environment. Beyond the financial award, successful innovators will gain valuable pilot experience, expert mentorship, technical support, and the opportunity to contribute to national environmental priorities while improving the lives of children across Ghana. title: Fully‑Funded PhD Program in Biomedical Sciences at the Max Delbrück Center (MDC), Berlin
summary: The Max Delbrück Center (MDC) in Berlin stands as one of Europe’s leading research institutions in biomedical sciences, offering an exceptional, fully‑funded PhD program designed for ambitious young scientists who want to explore the foundations of human health and disease. With cutting‑edge facilities, world‑class mentors, and a deeply collaborative research culture, the MDC PhD Program provides an outstanding environment for scientific growth and career development. Program Overview The MDC PhD Program is a structured, research‑intensive doctoral training pathway that supports students in conducting innovative biomedical research across multiple disciplines. The program focuses on three major scientific themes: Genes, Cells and Cell‑based Medicine Molecular Processes and Therapies Integrative Biomedicine These themes reflect MDC’s mission to advance tomorrow’s medicine through discovery, translational science, and interdisciplinary collaboration. What the Program Offers Doctoral researchers at MDC benefit from a comprehensive training ecosystem designed to support both scientific excellence and personal development. Key features include: International Research Environment — Work alongside scientists from more than 70 countries. title: AWLN 8th Intergenerational Retreat 2026 in Gabon: Fully Sponsored Leadership Opportunity for Young African Women Leaders and Diaspora Changemakers

Since its establishment, AWLN has built a powerful network of women leaders spanning government, diplomacy, civil society, academia, entrepreneurship, youth movements, and international organizations. The network promotes intergenerational dialogue, women s empowerment, mentorship, and collaborative leadership to address Africa s most pressing social, economic, and political challenges. The 2026 edition will take place in Libreville, Gabon , bringing together 40 selected young women leaders from across Africa and the African Diaspora. Participants will engage in interactive sessions, mentoring activities, leadership dialogues, collaborative workshops, and networking opportunities aimed at strengthening women s leadership across generations. The AWLN Intergenerational Retreat addresses these challenges by creating a platform where experienced African women leaders can mentor and support the next generation of changemakers. Support implementation of Agenda 2063 and the Sustainable Development Goals. Create lasting partnerships that contribute to Africa s transformation. What AWLN Expects from Participants The retreat is designed to create long-term impact rather than simply host an event. Selected participants are expected to: Participate actively in all sessions. title: Fully Funded Trinity Research Doctorate Award 2026–2030 in Nature-Based Solutions for Catchment Management in Ireland
summary: Are you passionate about environmental history, climate adaptation, landscape change, GIS, or community-based environmental research? Trinity College Dublin is inviting applications for a fully funded PhD studentship under the prestigious Trinity Research Doctorate Award (TRDA) 2026–2030 . This exciting doctoral opportunity focuses on Nature-Based Solutions for Catchment Management in Ireland and offers scholars the chance to contribute to cutting-edge interdisciplinary climate research while receiving full financial support. The PhD forms part of the ambitious Landscape Living Lab: Catchment Monitoring, Modelling, and Management project, funded through the AIB Trinity Climate Hub Trinity Research Doctorate Award Scheme . The successful candidate will work alongside leading academics and fellow PhD researchers to help shape innovative approaches to climate resilience, flood risk management, and sustainable landscape governance in Ireland. Application Deadline: Monday, 20 July 2026 About the Trinity Research Doctorate Award The Trinity Research Doctorate Award (TRDA) is one of Trinity College Dublin s flagship doctoral funding schemes that supports outstanding interdisciplinary research tackling global challenges. This project is developed under the theme of Nature-Based Solutions , bringing together expertise from environmental humanities, geography, civil engineering, environmental science, business, and climate research. The successful PhD candidate will become part of a collaborative research cohort examining the complex interactions between environmental systems and human societies within a river catchment in County Wicklow, Ireland . About the Landscape Living Lab Project The PhD is one component of the larger interdisciplinary research programme titled: Landscape Living Lab: Catchment Monitoring, Modelling, and Management The project investigates how river catchments can become more resilient to climate change through integrated research across four interconnected research pillars known as the 4Ms : Monitoring Current environmental dynamics Climate-related risks Nature-related risks Modelling Future resilience pathways Climate adaptation scenarios Predictive environmental modelling Memory Historical landscape change Environmental history Community knowledge Historical vulnerability Management Decision-making frameworks Nature-based solutions Sustainable catchment governance Each PhD candidate will specialize in one pillar while collaborating closely with the others. About This PhD Project The advertised studentship focuses on the Memory pillar under the title: Reconstructing Catchment Memory: Environmental History, Landscape Change and Community Knowledge for Nature-Based Catchment Management in an Irish Living Lab The project will be supervised by: Associate Professor Francis Ludlow School of Histories and Humanities Trinity College Dublin Research Objectives The research aims to reconstruct the environmental and social history of a river catchment in County Wicklow. The student will investigate how landscapes have changed over time and how these changes influence today s environmental challenges, particularly flooding and climate resilience. The research combines multiple disciplines including: Environmental history Historical GIS Digital humanities Art history Oral history Landscape studies Climate adaptation Nature-based solutions What Will the PhD Research Involve? The successful researcher will examine a wide variety of historical and environmental sources, including: Historical estate records Historical maps Aerial photography Paintings Photographs Forestry documentation Drainage records Local government archives Rural district council documents Historical newspaper reports Flood records Landscape change documentation These materials will be digitized and integrated into a Geographic Information System (GIS) to reconstruct historical environmental conditions. Community Engagement and Participatory Mapping An important feature of the project is collaboration with local communities. The PhD researcher will work directly with: Local residents Farmers Landholders Community organizations Catchment stakeholders Using ethical participatory methods, the researcher will collect community knowledge about: Historical woodland cover Wetland loss River changes Flood-prone areas Historic drainage systems Field boundaries Land improvement projects Infrastructure development Community mental maps will then be compared with documentary evidence to understand both environmental change and collective memory. Key Research Questions The project seeks answers to several important questions, including: How have land use and land cover changed across the catchment? When did significant environmental changes occur? Which historical management decisions contributed to today s flood risks? How can historical records be integrated into GIS-based environmental analysis? How can oral histories improve understanding of environmental change? How can historical evidence improve future nature-based catchment management? Candidate Profile Applicants should ideally possess: At least an Upper Second-Class Honours Bachelor s degree A Master s degree or equivalent experience is highly desirable Relevant academic backgrounds include: Environmental History Historical GIS Geography Digital Humanities Landscape Studies Archaeology Anthropology Art History Environmental Science Related disciplines Desired Skills and Experience Applicants should demonstrate experience or strong interest in: Historical archive research Documentary analysis Historical map interpretation Visual source analysis GIS software (QGIS, ArcGIS or equivalent) Digital mapping Spatial databases Environmental history Climate adaptation Nature-based solutions Flood risk studies Oral history Community engagement Participatory mapping Qualitative research methods Interdisciplinary research Academic writing Public communication The successful candidate should also be comfortable engaging respectfully with local communities and collaborating across disciplines. Funding Benefits This is a fully funded four-year PhD scholarship that includes: Annual tax-free stipend of €25,000 Full tuition fee coverage Four years of funding Opportunity to work within a major interdisciplinary climate research programme Collaboration with leading researchers at Trinity College Dublin Training in advanced interdisciplinary research methods Participation in the AIB Trinity Climate Hub Application Process Applicants should email their application to: Associate Professor Francis Ludlow Subject Line: Trinity College PhD Application: Catchment Memory Applications should include: Curriculum Vitae (CV) 1–2 page personal statement The personal statement should explain: Why you are interested in this PhD Why you are a strong candidate Relevant experience Research interests Applicants should also include contact information for two referees in their CV. Apply to fludlow@tcd.ie Selection Process Following submission: Applications will be shortlisted. Interviews are expected in late July 2026 . The successful applicant will then submit a formal PhD application through Trinity College Dublin s School of Histories and Humanities. The successful candidate will begin the PhD on 1 September 2026 . Important Dates Application Deadline: Monday, 20 July 2026 Expected Interviews: Late July 2026 Programme Start Date: 1 September 2026 Why You Should Apply This fully funded PhD offers an outstanding opportunity to contribute to internationally significant research addressing climate resilience and sustainable landscape management. By combining environmental history, digital mapping, community engagement, and nature-based solutions, the project will help shape future approaches to flood management and environmental governance in Ireland. Successful applicants will join an interdisciplinary research environment at one of Europe s leading universities while gaining advanced research skills applicable across academia, environmental consultancy, policy development, GIS, and climate adaptation. title: Allianz Climate Risk Award 2026: Global Opportunity for PhD Candidates and Postdoctoral Researchers Working on Climate Change and Extreme Weather
summary: Climate change continues to reshape economies, societies, and ecosystems around the world, making innovative research on climate resilience more important than ever. To recognize and promote groundbreaking scientific research in this field, Allianz Re has officially launched applications for the Allianz Climate Risk Award 2026 . Celebrating its 10th anniversary , the Allianz Climate Risk Award continues its mission of connecting emerging climate scientists with the global insurance industry, helping translate scientific discoveries into practical solutions that strengthen resilience against climate-related risks. Researchers whose work focuses on climate change, extreme weather events, technological innovation, and resilience are encouraged to apply for this prestigious international award. Application Deadline Deadline: Applications should be submitted before the official closing date specified by Allianz for the 2026 Award cycle. Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible. About the Allianz Climate Risk Award Established in 2017 , the Allianz Climate Risk Award is Allianz Re s flagship annual scientific award dedicated to supporting early-career researchers investigating climate-related risks. The award recognizes outstanding scientific work that helps answer important questions such as: How is climate change intensifying extreme weather events? How can societies better prepare for future climate risks? Which innovative technologies can improve resilience? How can scientific research help governments, insurers, businesses, and communities reduce disaster risks? The award serves as an important bridge between academic research and practical implementation by connecting promising researchers with experts from the insurance and risk management sectors. Celebrating 10 Years of Climate Research Excellence The 2026 edition marks a major milestone—the 10th anniversary of the Allianz Climate Risk Award. Over the past decade, the programme has supported numerous young researchers whose work has contributed significantly to improving understanding of climate risks and resilience worldwide. To expand its impact, the programme now operates across three award tracks : Global Award Thematic Spotlight: Allianz Trade Regional Spotlight: Asia (new for 2026) These tracks allow the programme to recognize excellence across different geographical and thematic areas while maintaining its commitment to advancing climate science. Research Areas Supported Applicants should be conducting research related to one or both of the following areas: 1. Understanding and Mitigating Climate Risks Research that investigates: Climate change impacts Extreme weather events Floods Droughts Hurricanes Heatwaves Wildfires Climate modelling Disaster risk reduction Adaptation strategies Risk assessment 2. Building Climate Resilience Through Technology Research involving: Artificial Intelligence Remote sensing Climate modelling technologies Early warning systems Digital resilience tools Predictive analytics Climate data science Infrastructure resilience Nature-based technological solutions Innovative adaptation technologies Projects that combine scientific excellence with practical application are especially encouraged. Who Can Apply? The Allianz Climate Risk Award welcomes applications from: PhD candidates Postdoctoral researchers Applicants should be conducting research focused on climate risks, climate adaptation, resilience, or technological innovations that address climate-related challenges. The programme is international, welcoming applications from researchers around the world. Why Apply? Successful applicants gain numerous professional advantages, including: International recognition Visibility within the global scientific community Exposure to leading experts in insurance and climate risk Networking opportunities Career advancement Opportunity to showcase innovative research Stronger connections between academia and industry Contribution to global climate resilience efforts Application Requirements Applicants must prepare several documents as part of their submission. These include: Completed application forms Signed documentation Curriculum Vitae (CV) Reference letter Supporting documents Non-technical research essay Non-Technical Research Essay The central part of the application is a concise non-technical essay . Requirements include: Maximum 800 words Clearly explain your research Describe your research objectives Highlight key findings Explain the real-world significance of your work Use language understandable to non-specialists Applicants are encouraged to review previous winning essays published in earlier Allianz Climate Risk Award Compendiums for inspiration. Previous Award Compendiums Applicants can explore previous award-winning research through Allianz s published compendiums, including: Pathways to Resilience: Mitigation and Adaptation in a Changing Climate (2024) Resilience in Action (2023) The Era of Resilience (2022) Confronting Climate Change (2021) A Glimpse of Tomorrow (2020) The End of Normal (2019) Weathering the Storms (2018) The Allianz Climate Risk Research Award (2017) These publications showcase high-quality research and offer valuable guidance for prospective applicants. How to Apply Interested researchers should submit the following by email: Completed application forms Signed documents Non-technical essay CV Reference letter Required supporting documents Applications should be sent to: climaterisk-award@allianz.com Applicants should carefully review the official application guidelines before submitting. Why This Award Matters Climate change remains one of the defining global challenges of the 21st century. Scientific research plays a critical role in helping governments, insurers, businesses, and communities better understand and respond to increasing climate risks. The Allianz Climate Risk Award recognizes researchers who are developing innovative knowledge and practical solutions capable of improving resilience against increasingly frequent and severe weather events. For early-career scientists, it offers an exceptional platform to gain international recognition, engage with leading experts, and contribute to shaping a more resilient future. title: African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training 2026: Free Digital Skills, STEAM, Financial Literacy and Entrepreneurship Training for Africans Worldwide
summary: The African Union International Centre for Girls’ and Women’s Education in Africa (AU CIEFFA) , in partnership with ImpactHER , has officially opened applications for the African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training 2026 under the theme “#AfricaEducatesHer – Digital Skills for All: Bridging the Gender Gap in STEAM, Financial Literacy, and Entrepreneurship.” This fully sponsored online training programme is designed to equip women and men from all 55 African Union Member States and members of the African Diaspora with practical knowledge and skills in gender equality, STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics), digital literacy, financial literacy, and entrepreneurship . The initiative aims to empower participants to become leaders and change-makers who contribute to inclusive education, economic empowerment, and sustainable development across Africa. The programme, which begins in August 2026 , builds on the success of previous editions that have already certified more than 12,500 young people across 55 African countries and 34 non-African countries , making it one of the continent’s leading online capacity-building initiatives. About the African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training The African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training is a regional initiative jointly implemented by the African Union CIEFFA and ImpactHER to strengthen the capacity of African youth through accessible online learning. The programme recognizes that despite growing opportunities in digital transformation and entrepreneurship, many young Africans—particularly women—continue to face barriers to accessing quality education, digital skills, financial knowledge, and entrepreneurial opportunities. By combining practical online learning with gender-responsive education, the programme seeks to prepare participants to thrive in today s rapidly evolving digital economy. The 2026 edition focuses on developing skills that are increasingly essential for employment, innovation, business creation, and community development across Africa. About African Union CIEFFA The African Union International Centre for Girls’ and Women’s Education in Africa (AU CIEFFA) is a specialized institution of the African Union operating under the Department of Education, Science, Technology and Innovation (ESTI) . The Centre was established to promote: Gender equality in education Girls and women s education Skills development Educational advocacy Inclusive education across Africa Its work supports the African Union s broader education and development agenda while promoting equal educational opportunities for women and girls. About ImpactHER ImpactHER is an internationally recognized non-profit organization committed to empowering African women entrepreneurs. Its mission focuses on: Bridging the gender financing gap Supporting women-owned businesses Providing entrepreneurial education Promoting financial inclusion Creating economic opportunities for African women By partnering with AU CIEFFA, ImpactHER brings practical entrepreneurship and financial literacy expertise to participants across the continent. Theme for the 2026 Training The 2026 programme will be delivered under the theme: #AfricaEducatesHer – Digital Skills for All: Bridging the Gender Gap in STEAM, Financial Literacy, and Entrepreneurship. The theme emphasizes the importance of ensuring equal access to digital knowledge and entrepreneurial opportunities while promoting gender equality in education throughout Africa. Objectives of the Programme The online training seeks to: Strengthen digital skills among African youth. Promote gender equality in and through education. Increase access to STEAM education. Improve financial literacy. Develop entrepreneurial skills. Empower young Africans to become community leaders. Promote inclusive economic growth. Encourage innovation and digital transformation across Africa. Training Areas Participants will receive training in several key areas, including: 1. Gender Equality in Education Participants will learn how gender-responsive education contributes to inclusive learning environments and sustainable development. Topics include: Gender equality in education Inclusive educational practices Women s empowerment Educational leadership 2. STEAM Education The programme promotes access to STEAM by helping participants understand how science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics contribute to solving real-world problems. 3. Digital Skills Participants will strengthen practical digital competencies needed in today s workforce and entrepreneurial ecosystem. Learning areas include: Digital literacy Technology applications Online productivity Digital innovation 4. Financial Literacy The training equips participants with knowledge in: Personal finance Budgeting Financial planning Savings Business finance 5. Entrepreneurship Participants will learn practical entrepreneurial skills, including: Business development Opportunity identification Business planning Innovation Enterprise management Benefits of the Programme Successful participants will receive numerous benefits, including: Free Online Training The programme is delivered online, allowing participants to learn from anywhere with internet access. Certificates Participants who attend the required percentage of each programme will receive certificates in: Digital Skills Entrepreneurial Skills Financial Literacy According to the application information, participants are expected to attend the required proportion of sessions for each programme to qualify for certification. Join Prestigious Networks Participants become members of: African Union CIEFFA Network ImpactHER Network These networks provide opportunities for collaboration, learning, and future engagement. Opportunities for Future Fully Funded Activities Completing the programme may increase participants chances of being invited to fully funded in-person activities organized by African Union CIEFFA. Access to Additional Training Participants may also gain access to future fully funded online training programmes sponsored by ImpactHER. Programme Format The programme will be delivered entirely online. Selected applicants will be divided into different batches. Each batch will undergo: One month of training Online learning sessions Practical skills development Training begins on 31 August 2026 . Who Can Apply? Applications are open to: African women African men African youth Members of the African Diaspora Applicants must demonstrate an interest in building skills in education, entrepreneurship, digital technologies, and leadership. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be an African woman or man. Hold African citizenship. Reside in Africa or anywhere in the world. Demonstrate motivation to learn digital skills, entrepreneurial skills, and financial literacy. Show leadership potential and commitment to promoting girls and women s education. Have access to a reliable internet connection. Have access to a laptop, computer, smartphone, or tablet. Understand at least one programme language: English French Portuguese Why You Should Apply This programme offers much more than online learning. Participants will have the opportunity to: Develop in-demand digital skills. Improve entrepreneurial capacity. Gain financial literacy. Join continental professional networks. Earn recognized certificates. Build leadership skills. Access future African Union opportunities. Contribute to gender equality and inclusive development in Africa. For young Africans seeking practical, career-enhancing skills while joining a continent-wide network of innovators and leaders, this training presents an outstanding opportunity. Application Process Interested applicants should complete the official online application form. Applicants should ensure they: Select their preferred language (English, French, or Portuguese). Complete all required application fields. Submit the application before the closing date. Applicants with questions may contact: youth.cieffa@gmail.com hello@impacther.org APPLY HERE Application Deadline 31 July 2026 Late applications may not be considered, so interested applicants are encouraged to apply early. Click HERE to learn more about the African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training 2026. Conclusion The African Union CIEFFA Online Capacity Building Training 2026 represents an exceptional opportunity for Africans across the continent and in the diaspora to strengthen their knowledge in digital skills, STEAM, entrepreneurship, financial literacy, and gender-responsive education. With free online learning, recognized certificates, access to continental networks, and opportunities to participate in future fully funded African Union activities, the programme is well suited for aspiring entrepreneurs, students, professionals, educators, and community leaders seeking to contribute to Africa s digital and economic transformation. Eligible applicants should prepare their applications and submit them before 31 July 2026 to take advantage of this valuable learning opportunity. title: Fully Funded SAIPA Scholarship Programme 2026: Study BCom Accounting in South Africa with Full Tuition, Accommodation, Books, and Monthly Allowance
summary: The South African Institute of Professional Accountants (SAIPA) has officially opened applications for its Fully Funded SAIPA Scholarship Programme 2026 , offering aspiring accountants the opportunity to pursue a BCom Accounting degree (or equivalent) at a recognized public university in South Africa. Designed to support academically talented students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds, the scholarship removes major financial barriers to higher education by covering tuition fees, accommodation, textbooks, and providing a monthly living allowance. If you dream of becoming a professional accountant and building a successful career in South Africa s accounting and finance sector, this scholarship presents an outstanding opportunity to receive comprehensive financial support while studying at university. About SAIPA The South African Institute of Professional Accountants (SAIPA) is one of South Africa s leading professional accountancy bodies, dedicated to developing highly skilled accounting professionals. With nearly four decades of experience and a membership exceeding 15,000 professional accountants , SAIPA has built a strong reputation for advancing the accounting profession through modern education, professional training, ethical leadership, and technology-driven learning. The SAIPA Scholarship Programme reflects the institute s commitment to expanding access to quality accounting education while strengthening the future of the profession in South Africa. About the SAIPA Scholarship Programme For the 2026 academic year , SAIPA will award five fully funded scholarships to deserving students pursuing a Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) in Accounting or an equivalent qualification. Among these awards is the Rashied Small Memorial Scholarship , established to honor the late Professor Rashied Small , a respected leader in South Africa s accounting profession who championed equitable access to accounting education. This memorial scholarship celebrates his enduring legacy by helping talented students achieve their educational and professional aspirations. What the Scholarship Covers The SAIPA Scholarship is a comprehensive funding package designed to support students throughout their academic journey. Successful applicants will receive: Full tuition fees Textbooks and academic learning materials Accommodation (where required) Monthly student allowance to assist with living expenses This extensive financial support enables recipients to focus on their studies without the burden of major educational costs. Why Apply for the SAIPA Scholarship? Beyond financial assistance, the SAIPA Scholarship provides students with an opportunity to begin their journey toward becoming qualified professional accountants. Benefits of the programme include: Complete financial support throughout university studies Access to quality accounting education Opportunity to join one of South Africa s most respected professional accounting communities A pathway toward professional accountancy qualifications Reduced financial stress, allowing students to concentrate on academic success Recognition through a prestigious national scholarship programme The scholarship also contributes to developing the next generation of accounting professionals who will strengthen South Africa s financial and business sectors. Fields of Study Covered The scholarship supports students pursuing: Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) in Accounting Equivalent Accounting qualifications offered by accredited public universities Applicants must intend to study full-time . Who Can Apply? Applicants must meet all the minimum eligibility requirements before submitting an application. You must: Be a South African citizen . Be currently in Matric or have completed Matric within the past two years . Intend to study full-time . Plan to enroll for a BCom Accounting degree (or equivalent) . Be accepted or intend to enroll at a recognized and accredited public university in South Africa . Have achieved at least 70% in both Mathematics and English . Demonstrate financial need with a household income not exceeding: R350,000 per year , or R600,000 per year for students with disabilities . Failure to meet any of the above requirements may result in the application not being considered. Selection Process Eligible applicants will undergo a competitive selection process consisting of: Initial eligibility screening. A qualifying examination. An interview conducted by a SAIPA selection panel. Successful applicants will be notified by: 23 January 2026 Applicants who do not receive communication by this date should consider their applications unsuccessful. Required Supporting Documents Applicants are not required to complete a formal application form. Instead, eligible candidates should submit an email application together with clear copies of the following compulsory documents: Certified copy of South African ID document. Certified copy of latest Matric results (if currently in Matric). Certified copy of Matric certificate or final statement of results (if Matric has already been completed). Proof of acceptance from an accredited South African public university. Certified copies of parents or guardians identity documents. Recommendation letters supporting the application. A 250-word motivational letter explaining why you should be awarded the scholarship and how it will benefit your educational journey. Incomplete applications or missing documentation may lead to disqualification. How to Apply Eligible applicants should submit their application via email. Email Address: scholarship@saipa.co.za Email Subject Line: SAIPA Scholarship 2026 There is no application form to complete. Applicants only need to email the required supporting documents. Why This Scholarship Matters The rising cost of university education continues to prevent many talented students from pursuing careers in accounting. Through this scholarship, SAIPA is investing in future accounting professionals by providing comprehensive financial support and expanding access to higher education for deserving students from financially disadvantaged households. The programme also strengthens the accounting profession by nurturing skilled graduates who will contribute to South Africa s economic development. For students passionate about accounting, finance, auditing, taxation, and business, this scholarship represents a valuable opportunity to begin a rewarding professional career without the burden of tuition and living expenses. Deadline Application Deadline: 15 January 2026 Late applications will not be accepted. Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their supporting documents early and submit their applications well before the closing date. Selected startups will gain access to structured incubation, expert mentorship, digital tools, investor networks, and opportunities to scale their businesses across Africa. title: Women’s Fellowship on Human Mobility in the Context of Climate Change (HMCCC) 2026: Fully Funded ECOWAS Fellowship for Young Women Leaders Driving Climate Mobility Solutions

Women and girls are among those most affected because of existing social, economic, and gender inequalities. Despite playing vital roles in building community resilience, women remain significantly underrepresented in climate migration governance, policy formulation, and decision-making processes. The Women’s Fellowship on Human Mobility in the Context of Climate Change (HMCCC) was established to address this gap by empowering young women leaders with practical skills, leadership training, mentorship, financial support, and regional collaboration opportunities. title: NASA STAR-7 Program 2026: Fully Virtual & Free NASA Space Biology Research Training for Scientists Worldwide | Applications Open Until July 31
summary: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has officially opened applications for the 7th annual Spaceflight Technology, Applications, and Research (STAR-7) Program , a prestigious virtual professional development initiative designed to prepare researchers for conducting biological experiments in space. The STAR Program is one of NASA s flagship educational initiatives in the field of space biosciences, helping experienced researchers transition into space-based biological research by providing comprehensive training on designing, planning, and implementing experiments aboard NASA and commercial spaceflight platforms. Running from September 2026 through February 2027 , the STAR-7 Program offers participants direct exposure to NASA experts, experienced spaceflight investigators, technology developers, and commercial space providers—all without requiring travel. Most importantly, participation is completely free , making this an exceptional opportunity for qualified researchers around the world who aspire to contribute to the future of biological research in space. What is the NASA STAR Program? Spaceflight Technology, Applications, and Research (STAR) is an annual virtual NASA training programme dedicated to advancing the field of space biosciences. The programme is specifically designed to prepare experienced researchers for conducting biological experiments under spaceflight conditions. Participants gain practical knowledge about the scientific principles, operational requirements, technological tools, and logistical considerations necessary for successful research missions conducted aboard spacecraft and orbital platforms. Unlike traditional academic courses, STAR focuses on real-world applications of space biology, allowing participants to understand both the opportunities and challenges associated with conducting scientific investigations beyond Earth. Since its launch in 2020, the programme has trained multiple cohorts of researchers and has established itself as one of NASA s premier educational initiatives for future space bioscience investigators. Programme Objectives NASA developed the STAR Programme to achieve several important goals, including: Train principal investigators, senior researchers, and postdoctoral scholars in space biosciences. Introduce researchers to available NASA and commercial spaceflight research platforms. Educate participants on designing successful biological experiments for space environments. Increase awareness of available technologies and flight hardware. Foster collaborations between new researchers and experienced NASA-funded investigators. Build interdisciplinary research teams capable of advancing space biology. What Participants Will Learn Throughout the six-month virtual programme, participants receive comprehensive instruction covering numerous aspects of space biological research. Topics include: Fundamental principles of space biosciences Biology experiments conducted in microgravity Spaceflight hardware and research technologies Designing biological experiments for space missions Technical requirements for conducting spaceflight research Logistical planning for experiments aboard spacecraft Scientific opportunities available through NASA Commercial spaceflight research platforms Experimental limitations in space environments Flight mission preparation Collaboration strategies within the international space biology community The curriculum balances theoretical knowledge with practical insights from scientists who have successfully completed spaceflight experiments. Learn Directly from NASA Experts One of the most valuable aspects of the STAR Programme is direct interaction with professionals actively working within NASA s space biosciences ecosystem. Participants have opportunities to engage with: NASA programme scientists Experienced principal investigators Space biology researchers Technology developers Commercial flight providers Researchers who have previously conducted spaceflight experiments These interactions provide valuable insights into planning, funding, collaboration, and executing research missions in space. Build an International Research Network Beyond technical education, STAR places a strong emphasis on community building. Participants become part of a growing international network of researchers interested in biological sciences conducted in space. Networking opportunities include: Collaborating with researchers from different scientific disciplines Connecting with experienced NASA investigators Meeting commercial spaceflight partners Establishing future interdisciplinary research teams Learning about future funding opportunities Sharing ideas and research interests with peers worldwide This collaborative environment has become one of the programme s defining strengths. Who Can Apply? NASA welcomes applications from qualified individuals worldwide. Eligible applicants include researchers affiliated with: Universities Research institutions Commercial organizations NASA Centers Government agencies International organizations The programme particularly encourages participation from researchers affiliated with countries that are signatories to the Artemis Accords. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the following requirements: Hold an advanced degree (MD, PhD, or equivalent qualification). Be a Principal Investigator, Senior Research Scientist, or Postdoctoral Scholar. Postdoctoral applicants must include a letter of reference from their supervisor. The programme is not currently open to undergraduate or graduate students. NASA notes that future complementary programmes may be developed specifically for students. Course Format The STAR Programme has been intentionally designed to maximize accessibility for researchers across the globe. Programme features include: Fully virtual delivery No travel required Free participation International accessibility Interactive online sessions Expert-led lectures Networking opportunities Collaborative discussions Because the course is conducted entirely online, participants can engage from anywhere in the world. Course Timeline Applications Open: Currently Open Application Deadline: 31 July 2026 Participant Selection: August 2026 Course Duration: September 2026 – February 2027 Why Researchers Should Apply The STAR Programme offers several significant advantages for scientists seeking to enter the rapidly growing field of space biology. Benefits include: Free NASA professional training Direct learning from NASA experts Practical understanding of spaceflight experiments Exposure to cutting-edge biological research Networking with international researchers Collaboration opportunities with experienced investigators Insights into NASA research opportunities Understanding commercial space research platforms Preparation for future biological space missions Enhanced research career development Feedback from Previous Participants Researchers who have completed previous STAR cohorts consistently highlight the programme s educational value and collaborative environment. Participants have praised STAR for: Providing an excellent introduction to space biosciences. Helping researchers understand NASA s research ecosystem. Building interdisciplinary collaborations. Offering valuable networking opportunities. Explaining the practical realities of conducting experiments in space. Preparing scientists to participate in future spaceflight research. Many alumni now work within NASA programmes, universities, national laboratories, and leading research institutions. STAR Programme Organizers The programme is led by distinguished NASA experts. Dr. Ursula Koniges (NASA Headquarters) Deputy Program Scientist for Translational Research at NASA s Biological and Physical Sciences Division. Dr. Christina CJ Johnson (NASA Ames Research Center) Chief of Space Biosciences Research and Deputy Center Lead for the Human Research Program. Together, they oversee the STAR Programme and guide its scientific and educational direction. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Is the programme free? Yes. Participation is completely free. Is travel required? No. The programme is entirely virtual. Does NASA provide funding? No participant funding is provided because there are no travel or participation costs. However, participants learn about future funding and collaboration opportunities throughout the programme. Can undergraduate or graduate students apply? No. The programme currently targets Principal Investigators, Senior Researchers, and Postdoctoral Scholars. How are participants selected? Applications submitted through NASA s NSPIRES system are reviewed by the STAR organisation team according to NASA policies. Successful applicants will receive notification through NSPIRES. Why This Opportunity Matters As biological research increasingly expands beyond Earth s atmosphere, researchers with expertise in designing experiments for spaceflight are becoming more valuable than ever. NASA s STAR Programme provides an accessible pathway for experienced scientists to enter this exciting field by combining world-class instruction, expert mentorship, practical guidance, and global networking. For researchers interested in understanding how biology behaves in space and contributing to future scientific discoveries aboard orbital platforms and beyond, STAR-7 represents one of the most comprehensive professional development opportunities currently available. Learn More Apply Researchers meeting the eligibility requirements are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before 31 July 2026 . Click HERE to learn more and apply for the NASA STAR-7 Program 2026. Explore more opportunities on OFY HERE . title: University of Canberra Fully Funded PhD Scholarships 2027 in Australia: AI & Democracy, Deliberative Democracy, and Organisational Creativity & AI Scholarships
summary: The University of Canberra is inviting outstanding domestic and international students to apply for three prestigious PhD scholarship opportunities commencing in February 2027 . Hosted by the internationally recognized Centre for Deliberative Democracy (CDD) and the Faculty of Business, Government and Law, these scholarships provide generous financial support, access to world-class researchers, and the opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking interdisciplinary research. The available scholarships focus on some of the world s most pressing challenges, including artificial intelligence, democratic participation, organisational creativity, digital politics, innovation, public policy, and technology-driven social transformation. Successful candidates will become part of a vibrant research community while undertaking original doctoral research under the supervision of leading academics at the University of Canberra. Why Choose a University of Canberra PhD Scholarship? The University of Canberra is recognized for its commitment to impactful research and innovation. These scholarships offer candidates the opportunity to conduct independent research while collaborating with internationally respected scholars and contributing to high-impact research projects. Successful scholars will benefit from: Annual stipend of AUD 40,000 , indexed each year. Scholarship duration of 3.5 years . Opportunity to undertake original doctoral research. Access to internationally recognized research centres. Collaboration with experienced supervisors and leading researchers. Participation in seminars, workshops, conferences, and collaborative publications. Exposure to interdisciplinary research environments. Additional relocation allowance for eligible international scholarship recipients (AI Democracy and Deliberative Democracy Scholarships). 1. AI Democracy PhD Scholarship The AI Democracy PhD Scholarship offers an exciting opportunity for highly motivated researchers interested in exploring the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and democratic participation. Hosted by the University of Canberra s Centre for Deliberative Democracy, the scholarship forms part of the Australian Research Council (ARC) DECRA-funded project Smart Democracy: Fostering Democratic Agency in the Age of AI. title: Study in Italy 2026–2027: ARDSU Basilicata Fully Funded Scholarships for International Master’s Students at the University of Basilicata
summary: Studying in Italy is a dream for many international students, and the ARDSU Basilicata Scholarships for Foreign Students 2026–2027 provide an outstanding opportunity to make that dream a reality. The Regional Agency for the Right to University Education of Basilicata (ARDSU Basilicata) has officially opened applications for 12 scholarships for international students wishing to pursue eligible Master s degree (MSc) programmes at the University of Basilicata (UNIBAS) during the 2026–2027 academic year. The scholarship programme is part of the University of Basilicata s internationalisation strategy and is designed to attract highly qualified students from around the world while strengthening international academic and scientific cooperation. The initiative is implemented through Memorandums of Understanding signed between ARDSU Basilicata and the participating departments of the University of Basilicata in June 2026. Unlike many scholarships that only cover tuition, the ARDSU Basilicata Scholarship provides accommodation, meals, and a one-time financial contribution to assist with travel, visa, insurance, and other essential living expenses, making it an attractive opportunity for talented international students seeking postgraduate education in Europe. About the ARDSU Basilicata Scholarship The ARDSU Basilicata Scholarship is offered by the Regional Agency for the Right to University Education of Basilicata for the 2026–2027 Academic Year . The programme supports foreign students enrolling in eligible Master of Science (MSc) programmes offered by three academic departments of the University of Basilicata. The scholarship seeks to: Attract outstanding international students. Promote academic excellence. Strengthen global research collaboration. Enhance the internationalisation of the University of Basilicata. Encourage cultural and scientific exchange between Italy and the rest of the world. Participating Departments Scholarships are available for eligible Master s programmes offered by the following departments: 1. Department of Agricultural, Forestry, Food and Environmental Sciences (DAFE-UNIBAS) Students may pursue programmes related to: Agricultural Sciences Forestry Food Science Environmental Sciences Sustainable Agriculture Natural Resources 2. Department of Basic and Applied Sciences (DiSBA-UNIBAS) Eligible fields include areas such as: Biology Biotechnology Chemistry Physics Applied Sciences Scientific Research 3. Department for Humanistic, Scientific and Social Innovation (DIUSS-UNIBAS) Students interested in interdisciplinary and social sciences may apply for programmes covering: Humanities Social Sciences Innovation Cultural Studies Social Development Public Policy Applicants should carefully consult the department-specific annexes to determine which Master s programmes are eligible under the scholarship scheme. Number of Scholarships Available ARDSU Basilicata will award: 12 scholarships reserved exclusively for foreign students enrolling in eligible Master s programmes for the 2026–2027 academic year. Scholarship Duration The scholarship is tenable for: 12 months From 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2027 Students may also apply for renewal for the following academic year, provided they meet the required academic progress, including obtaining at least 18 university credits (CFU) and maintaining full-time enrolment. What Does the Scholarship Cover? One of the strongest aspects of this programme is its comprehensive support package. Successful applicants will receive: 1. Free Accommodation Students will be accommodated free of charge in one of the ARDSU university residences located in: Potenza Matera The residences include kitchen facilities for weekend meals. 2. Free Meals Recipients will receive: Two meal vouchers per day Valid Monday to Friday Redeemable at the university canteens in Potenza or Matera campuses. 3. One-Time Financial Contribution Students will receive a one-time grant to assist with: International travel Visa costs Mandatory health insurance Regional tax Tuition fees (where applicable) Local transportation Other essential living expenses The amount depends on the distance between Italy and the applicant s country of origin: Distance from Italy One-Time Grant 500–1,499 km €1,500 1,500–2,999 km €2,000 3,000–5,999 km €2,500 6,000–8,999 km €3,500 More than 9,000 km €4,000 The grant is paid in two instalments: 50% by 31 October 2026 after enrolment verification. Remaining 50% by 31 December 2026 after verification of regular class attendance. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy several eligibility conditions. Nationality The scholarship is reserved for foreign (international) students . Academic Qualification Applicants must: Hold (or obtain by 1 August 2026 ) a Bachelor s degree relevant to the chosen MSc programme. Meet the curricular requirements specified by the selected department. Hold qualifications that permit admission into the chosen Master s programme. Age Limit Applicants must: Be 18 years or older Be no older than 26 years on the application deadline. Academic Merit Applicants must have: A GPA equivalent to at least 70% of the maximum grade available within their national grading system. Applications are evaluated using an Italian grade conversion methodology based on GPA and final Bachelor s degree results. Language Requirements Italian-Taught Programmes Applicants may provide evidence of: Italian language proficiency from A1 level (CEFR) onward. Students without Italian language skills may attend Italian language courses organised by UNIBAS. English-Taught Courses Where courses are taught in English, applicants may submit proof of: English language proficiency at B1 level (CEFR) or higher. Applicants from English-speaking countries may self-certify their English proficiency. Required Documents Applicants must submit the following (PDF format): Completed application form. Valid passport. Bachelor s degree certificate (or expected graduation declaration). Official academic transcript. Self-certification of curricular requirements. Proof of pre-enrolment through the UNIVERSITALY portal (or commitment to pre-enrol by 1 August 2026). Grading scale statement from the home university. Motivation letter. Optional documents include: Letter of recommendation. Proof of Lucanian origin (where applicable). Reserved Scholarships for Students of Lucanian Origin Up to 2 of the 12 scholarships are reserved, on a priority basis, for foreign students of Lucanian descent (up to the third degree of kinship), provided they meet all admission requirements. If these reserved places are not filled, they will be reallocated to other eligible applicants. Selection Process Applications are evaluated by departmental selection committees. The assessment considers: Compliance with eligibility requirements. GPA. Final Bachelor s degree grade. Academic merit. Where candidates have identical scores, preference is given to the younger applicant. The provisional ranking will be published on the ARDSU website, while the final ranking is expected by 1 August 2026 . Successful applicants will also receive notification by email. Tuition Fees International students benefit from special tuition arrangements based on their country of origin. Regardless of tuition fees, all scholarship holders must pay the €150 regional tax . Health Insurance All non-EU students must obtain valid health insurance covering the full scholarship period, including medical evacuation and repatriation where applicable. EU students are advised to hold a valid European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). How to Apply Applications must be submitted electronically to the designated ARDSU contact email, with copies sent to the relevant department and ARDSU secretariat, using the prescribed subject line indicated in the call. All required documents must be attached in PDF format. Applicants should also complete pre-enrolment through the UNIVERSITALY portal before the required deadline. APPLY HERE Important Dates Applications Open: Now Open Application Deadline: 21 July 2026 (12:00 PM Italian Time) Final Rankings Published: By 1 August 2026 Scholarship Starts: 1 October 2026 Scholarship Ends: 30 September 2027 Learn more HERE Why You Should Apply The ARDSU Basilicata Scholarship offers much more than financial assistance. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to: Study at a respected Italian public university. Live in Italy with accommodation and meals covered. Receive financial assistance for travel, visas, insurance, and living expenses. Join an international academic community. Gain access to European research and career opportunities. Experience Italian culture while pursuing a postgraduate degree. For ambitious international students seeking an affordable and high-quality Master s education in Europe, this scholarship represents an excellent opportunity. Visit the ARDSU Basilicata Scholarships for International Master s Students at the University of Basilicata page for further details. Conclusion The ARDSU Basilicata Scholarships for Foreign Students 2026–2027 provide comprehensive support for talented international students wishing to pursue Master s studies at the University of Basilicata . Through free accommodation, daily meals, travel assistance, and additional financial support, the programme significantly reduces the financial burden of studying abroad while promoting academic excellence and international collaboration. If you meet the eligibility requirements and aspire to study in Italy, this scholarship is an opportunity worth pursuing. Be sure to prepare all required documents carefully and submit your application before 21 July 2026 . Discover more global Fully Funded Scholarship opportunities on OFY HERE . title: Childlight Global Data Fellow Programme 2027: Fully Funded International Fellowship for Child Protection Professionals
summary: Professionals dedicated to protecting children through research, evidence, and data now have an outstanding opportunity to join one of the world s leading international child protection initiatives. Childlight, the Global Child Safety Institute based at the University of Edinburgh, has officially opened applications for its prestigious Global Data Fellow (GDF) Programme 2027 . This highly respected 12-month fellowship brings together experts from around the world who are passionate about strengthening child protection systems through innovative research, collaboration, and evidence-based policymaking. The programme provides participants with an exceptional opportunity to work alongside international experts while contributing to groundbreaking research focused on preventing child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSEA). If you are a professional working in child protection, public health, social work, law enforcement, academia, technology, policy development, or related disciplines, this fellowship offers an excellent platform to expand your expertise while joining a global network committed to making children safer worldwide. What is the Childlight Global Data Fellow Programme? The Global Data Fellow Programme is an international professional development fellowship designed to develop expertise in child protection data and research. The programme focuses on transforming reliable evidence into practical solutions that strengthen child protection systems across different countries and regions. Rather than being a traditional academic programme, the fellowship combines professional learning, collaborative research, international networking, and practical application of data-driven approaches to child protection. Throughout the fellowship, participants engage in virtual workshops, collaborative projects, research activities, and an in-person residency that enables deeper engagement with experts from around the globe. The programme runs for the entire 2027 calendar year, allowing fellows to continuously build knowledge while applying new skills within their own organizations and communities. What Fellows Will Gain Selected fellows will receive access to numerous professional development opportunities, including: Monthly virtual workshops led by global experts. Research collaboration with leading child protection specialists. Participation in international knowledge-sharing sessions. Access to Childlight s exclusive research resources and datasets. Membership in a global network of researchers and practitioners. Opportunities to contribute to Childlight publications. Presentation opportunities during the annual Childlight Research Symposium. Continued engagement through the Global Data Fellows alumni network after completing the fellowship. Financial Support Although the fellowship is not a salaried position and fellows remain employed by their existing organizations, Childlight provides financial support for selected participants attending the Edinburgh residency. Support may include: International return airfare. Accommodation during the residency. Meals throughout the residential programme. Applicants requiring additional assistance may discuss their circumstances with the programme team if selected. Areas of Expertise Encouraged Childlight welcomes professionals from multiple disciplines. Experience in any of the following areas is particularly valuable: Child protection. Violence prevention. Child sexual exploitation and abuse research. Public health. Epidemiology. Population health. Data science. Policy analysis. Education. Criminal justice. Law enforcement. Healthcare. Social services. Child helplines. Government agencies. Civil society organizations. Technology and digital safety. Academic research. The programme values professionals capable of translating research findings into policies and practical interventions that improve child safety globally. Programme Activities During the fellowship, participants will: Attend monthly virtual learning sessions. Participate in collaborative research projects. Engage with international experts. Exchange knowledge across sectors. Contribute to publications and reports. Present findings during symposiums. Participate in the Edinburgh residency. Build lasting international partnerships. Participants are generally expected to dedicate approximately 2–4 hours per month , in addition to the in-person residency. Why This Fellowship Matters Child protection challenges continue to evolve alongside advances in technology and changing social environments. Governments, NGOs, researchers, and international organizations increasingly rely on high-quality evidence to design effective interventions. The Childlight Global Data Fellow Programme equips professionals with the skills needed to: Generate better evidence. Improve child safeguarding systems. Strengthen international cooperation. Develop innovative research methodologies. Influence policy decisions. Support data-informed child protection strategies. Participants also become part of a global movement dedicated to preventing child sexual exploitation and abuse through research, collaboration, and innovation. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is ideal for: Researchers. University academics. Public health professionals. Child protection practitioners. Government officials. NGO professionals. Social workers. Technology professionals. Human rights advocates. Policy specialists. Law enforcement professionals. Data analysts working within child protection systems. Individuals committed to evidence-based approaches and international collaboration are strongly encouraged to apply. Application Process Applicants must complete the official online application form before the application deadline. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to participate in an informal discussion with the Global Data Fellow Programme Manager. Successful applicants will also complete organizational approvals, safeguarding requirements, and programme documentation before joining the fellowship. title: Google Africa Applied AI Lab 2026: Google Opens Applications for African AI Startups and Researchers to Access Early Google DeepMind Models, Technical Mentorship, and Potential Funding
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming industries across the globe, and Africa is increasingly emerging as a hub for AI-driven innovation. To support the continent s next generation of technology pioneers, Google has officially launched applications for the Google Africa Applied AI Lab 2026 —a groundbreaking initiative designed to accelerate African AI startups and researchers building solutions for uniquely African challenges. Hosted at the Accra AI Community Centre (AICC) in Ghana, the Google Africa Applied AI Lab provides founders and researchers with exclusive early access to Google DeepMind s cutting-edge AI models, personalized technical mentorship from Google experts, commercialization support, venture capital connections, and opportunities for potential funding. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between world-class AI research and commercially successful products, helping build Africa s first generation of AI-native unicorn companies. Applications are now open and will close on 31 August 2026 . What is the Google Africa Applied AI Lab? The Google Africa Applied AI Lab is an innovation and commercialization platform established by Google Labs through the Accra AI Community Centre (AICC) in Ghana, with support from the Google AI Futures Fund . Rather than functioning as a traditional accelerator or incubator, the programme focuses on collaborative product development between Google experts and selected African startups. Its primary objective is to help founders transform promising AI ideas into scalable, market-ready products capable of solving significant challenges across Africa. The programme connects entrepreneurs directly with: Google Research experts Google DeepMind engineers Product specialists Venture capital investors AI researchers Commercialization experts Participants receive tailored technical support based on the maturity and needs of their startup. The Mission of the Google Africa Applied AI Lab The programme seeks to: Accelerate AI innovation across Africa. Support commercialization of breakthrough AI technologies. Build globally competitive African AI startups. Connect founders with world-class AI expertise. Encourage responsible AI development. Strengthen Africa s AI ecosystem. Foster collaboration between research and entrepreneurship. Ultimately, the initiative aims to position Africa as a major contributor to the future of artificial intelligence. Where is the Programme Based? The Google Africa Applied AI Lab is headquartered at the: Accra AI Community Centre (AICC) Location: Accra, Ghana The AICC serves as one of Africa s leading AI innovation hubs, providing collaborative workspaces, community programming, and technical support to entrepreneurs and researchers across the continent. Although the programme culminates in an in-person event in Ghana, participants are not required to remain physically based at the Centre throughout the programme . Focus Areas of the Google Africa Applied AI Lab Google is looking for AI-powered products capable of addressing meaningful challenges across Africa. The programme focuses on five major technological futures expected to shape the continent over the coming years. 1. The Future of Work Innovations that improve productivity, employment, workforce development, automation, and digital labor. Examples include: Workforce AI tools HR technology Employment platforms AI productivity assistants 2. The Future of Knowledge Solutions that improve how people create, access, organize, and distribute knowledge. Examples include: Education technology Knowledge management AI tutoring systems Information accessibility 3. The Future of Software Development Products that enhance software engineering using AI. Possible innovations include: AI coding assistants Development automation Software testing Programming productivity tools 4. The Future of Creativity Projects supporting creative industries through AI. Examples include: Design tools Creative assistants AI-generated content Digital art solutions 5. The Future of Entertainment Applications using AI to transform media and entertainment. Examples include: Gaming Interactive storytelling Video creation Music technologies Benefits of the Google Africa Applied AI Lab Selected startups gain access to a comprehensive package of technical, commercial, and investment support. 1. Early Access to Google DeepMind AI Models Participants receive early access to Google s newest AI technologies before they become publicly available. Available models may include: Gemini Gemma Veo This gives startups a competitive advantage in developing innovative commercial AI products. 2. Technical Mentorship Founders work closely with: Google Research Google engineering teams Google AI specialists Mentorship includes: Product architecture AI implementation Technical guidance Model optimization 3. Commercialization Support The programme helps startups move from research and prototypes to scalable businesses. Support includes: Product validation Market strategy Business development Go-to-market planning 4. Venture Capital Mentorship Participants receive mentorship from leading venture capital firms, including: 4DX Ventures Norrsken22 Novastar Ventures Ventures Platform These firms provide guidance on: Scaling startups Fundraising Investor readiness Business strategy 5. Potential Funding Opportunities Selected startups may also become eligible for investment opportunities through: Google AI Futures Fund Partner venture capital firms Funding decisions are made separately and participation in the programme does not automatically guarantee investment. 6. Product Demo Day The programme concludes with an in-person Demo Day at the Accra AI Community Centre. Participants will present their AI products to: Google teams Investors Venture capital firms Strategic partners Industry experts This provides valuable visibility and networking opportunities. 7. No Equity Requirement One of the programme s most attractive features is that participating startups do not give up equity or ownership simply by joining the programme . However, founders may later receive investment offers from Google AI Futures Fund or participating venture capital firms. Programme Timeline The Google Africa Applied AI Lab follows a structured timeline. Applications Open 1 July 2026 Application Deadline 31 August 2026 Selection Notifications September 2026 Co-development Period Mid-September 2026 to Early December 2026 Demo Day Early December 2026 Programme Structure The programme consists of a collaborative co-development phase rather than classroom-based training. Eligible applicants include: Full-time startup founders AI entrepreneurs Researchers planning to become founders AI innovators Technology builders Applicants should have ambitious ideas capable of generating significant impact across Africa.
