title: Indo-Pacific NGO Blended Finance Accelerator 2026: Receive Up to AUD 840,000 (Approximately USD 550,000) Plus Expert Acceleration Support to Scale Climate and Gender Equality Solutions Across the Indo-Pacific
summary: Organizations working to solve climate change and gender inequality often face one common challenge—accessing sufficient financing to scale their impact. While grants remain important, attracting private investment has become increasingly critical for achieving sustainable development goals at scale. To address this challenge, the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) , in partnership with Convergence Blended Finance , has launched the Indo-Pacific NGO Blended Finance Accelerator , a five-year initiative worth AUD 10 million . The programme is designed to help NGOs develop innovative blended finance solutions that unlock private investment for climate action and gender equality initiatives throughout the Indo-Pacific region. The Accelerator combines catalytic grant funding with technical acceleration support, enabling NGOs to transform innovative ideas into investment-ready financial vehicles capable of delivering measurable environmental and social impact. Application Deadline: 20 July 2026 What is the Indo-Pacific NGO Blended Finance Accelerator? The Indo-Pacific NGO Blended Finance Accelerator is a comprehensive programme that helps NGOs bridge the gap between development funding and private capital. Although blended finance has expanded significantly across the Indo-Pacific, there remains a shortage of investable projects capable of attracting commercial investors. NGOs possess deep local knowledge, technical expertise, and trusted community relationships, making them well positioned to design impactful financial solutions. However, they currently sponsor only a small percentage of blended finance transactions globally due to several institutional and financial barriers. The Accelerator seeks to change this by providing financial support, expert guidance, investor connections, and technical resources that enable NGOs to create scalable blended finance vehicles capable of attracting long-term investment. Total Programme Funding The programme is backed by a five-year AUD 10 million investment and provides both financial support and capacity-building services. Available catalytic grants include: Up to AUD 300,000 (approximately USD 200,000 ) for early-stage blended finance initiatives. Up to AUD 840,000 (approximately USD 550,000 ) for advanced-stage and scaling initiatives. All grants are disbursed in Australian Dollars (AUD). What is Blended Finance? Blended finance refers to the strategic use of public, philanthropic, or concessional funding to attract private investment into projects that generate both financial returns and positive development outcomes. Rather than relying solely on donor funding, blended finance combines different sources of capital to create sustainable financing mechanisms capable of delivering large-scale impact. Examples include: Investment funds Project finance vehicles Private companies Bonds Financing facilities Results-based financing mechanisms Other innovative financial instruments Programme Objectives The Accelerator aims to: Increase private investment for climate action. Strengthen financing for gender equality initiatives. Build a pipeline of investment-ready blended finance projects. Support NGOs in becoming investment managers and impact managers. Expand partnerships between NGOs and private investors. Deliver measurable environmental and social outcomes. Strengthen financial sustainability for development initiatives. Priority Impact Areas Applications should focus on one or both of the programme s major themes. Climate Action Projects may support: Climate change mitigation Climate adaptation Clean energy Sustainable cities Responsible consumption Life below water Life on land These areas align with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production SDG 13 – Climate Action SDG 14 – Life Below Water SDG 15 – Life on Land Gender Equality Projects should demonstrate a strong commitment to gender equality through: Women s empowerment Financial inclusion Healthcare Education Gender-responsive investment models Gender integration throughout project design, implementation, and governance Applications should align with SDG 5 – Gender Equality . What Support Will Selected NGOs Receive? Successful applicants receive more than funding. The programme provides: 1. Catalytic Grant Funding Funding supports activities such as: Feasibility studies Legal structuring Financial modelling Vehicle design Investment pipeline development Fundraising Pilot implementation Governance development Impact measurement systems 2. Acceleration Support Participants also gain access to: Professional training Curated market intelligence Data and analytics Technical mentoring Peer-learning opportunities Investor introductions Ecosystem partnerships Ongoing feedback from blended finance experts Guidance on engaging commercial investors Types of Grants Available Stage 1: Scoping and Feasibility Maximum funding: Up to AUD 300,000 Suitable for NGOs that are exploring blended finance opportunities. Funding may support: Financial model development Vehicle design Legal structuring Market assessments Stakeholder consultations Investment pipeline development Governance framework design Initial impact assessment Applicants should already have: An initial theory of change Early scoping work Potential partners identified Stage 2: Proof of Concept and Pilot Maximum funding: Up to AUD 840,000 Funding supports: Investor outreach Legal refinement Governance improvements Impact framework development Pilot investments Investment pipeline expansion Applicants should demonstrate: Completed feasibility work Initial financial model Internal and external support Key implementation partners At least one soft or hard investor commitment Stage 3: Scale-Up and Expansion Maximum funding: Up to AUD 840,000 Funding may be used for: Vehicle expansion Operational scaling Additional fundraising Legal improvements Pipeline growth General Partner (GP) capital commitments Preparing vehicles for larger investment rounds Applicants should already have: An investment-ready or operational vehicle Anchor investors Committed implementation partners Defined NGO roles Eligible Financial Vehicles Projects may include: Investment funds Bonds Project finance structures Private companies Financing facilities Results-based financing mechanisms Other innovative blended finance instruments Countries Eligible for Project Implementation Projects must focus on one or more eligible Indo-Pacific countries, including: Bangladesh Bhutan Cambodia Indonesia Laos Mongolia Myanmar Nepal Pakistan Philippines Sri Lanka Timor-Leste Vietnam Eligible Pacific Island nations include: Cook Islands Federated States of Micronesia Fiji Kiribati Nauru Niue Papua New Guinea Republic of Palau Republic of the Marshall Islands Samoa Solomon Islands Tokelau Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu Applicants may be based anywhere in the world, provided their proposed blended finance vehicle serves eligible Indo-Pacific countries. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be an NGO applying independently or with consortium partners. Demonstrate a clear need for grant funding. Develop a blended finance solution capable of attracting private investment. Hold a significant implementation role. Obtain internal leadership approval. Target eligible Indo-Pacific countries. Focus on climate action, gender equality, or both. Present a credible pathway toward investment readiness and financial sustainability. Evaluation Criteria Applications will be assessed based on: Development Impact Projects should generate measurable environmental and social benefits, particularly for underserved populations including: Women Indigenous communities Persons with disabilities Communities in Least Developed Countries (LDCs) Frontier markets Scalability and Replicability Proposals should demonstrate potential to: Mobilize significant private investment Expand across multiple markets Serve as models for future blended finance initiatives Additionality Applicants should explain: Why blended finance is necessary How the project addresses financing gaps Why grant funding is essential Gender Integration Strong proposals integrate gender considerations throughout project design rather than treating gender as an additional feature. Investment Readiness Projects should demonstrate: Strong governance Financial sustainability Investor engagement Commercial viability Risk management Internal Organizational Commitment Applicants should show: Leadership support Dedicated implementation teams Alignment with organizational strategy Stakeholder Partnerships Preference is given to proposals with: Financial partners Implementation partners Regional stakeholder support Track Record Applicants should demonstrate: Relevant technical expertise Local implementation experience Strong partnerships Capacity to manage blended finance initiatives Why This Programme Matters Traditional grant funding alone cannot meet the growing financing needs for climate resilience and gender equality across the Indo-Pacific. By combining grants with technical expertise and private investment, the Indo-Pacific NGO Blended Finance Accelerator enables NGOs to create sustainable financing solutions that continue generating impact long after grant funding has ended. The programme also strengthens NGO capacity to engage commercial investors, manage innovative financial vehicles, and build scalable development solutions capable of transforming communities across the region. Key Dates Application Deadline: 20 July 2026 Interested NGOs are encouraged to prepare their concept notes well before the deadline to maximize their chances of success. title: GreenLight Fund Expression of Interest 2026: Receive Up to US$600,000 in Unrestricted Funding to Expand Your Nonprofit Across the United States
summary: Nonprofit organizations with proven, evidence-based programs often reach a stage where their impact has been demonstrated, but expanding into new communities requires significant financial investment, strategic planning, staffing support, and strong local partnerships. GreenLight Fund is addressing this challenge by inviting eligible U.S.-based nonprofit organizations to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for future funding and expansion opportunities. Through this initiative, selected organizations may receive up to US$600,000 in unrestricted funding over four years, together with comprehensive strategic support designed to help successful nonprofit models launch and thrive in new communities throughout the United States. Unlike many traditional grant opportunities that provide funding alone, GreenLight Fund combines long-term financial investment with practical implementation support through its nationally recognized Beyond the Check partnership model. Expression of Interest Deadline Expression of Interest Pilot Deadline: July 17, 2026 Organizations interested in joining GreenLight Fund s future partnership pipeline should submit their Expression of Interest before the deadline. It is important to note that submitting an Expression of Interest is not the same as submitting a full grant application. Rather, it allows GreenLight Fund to learn more about your organization and determine whether it aligns with current or future partnership opportunities. Organizations whose missions and programs align with GreenLight Fund s model may later be invited into additional review and selection stages. About GreenLight Fund GreenLight Fund is a national nonprofit organization that works alongside local communities across the United States to improve opportunities for inclusive prosperity. Rather than imposing predetermined solutions, GreenLight partners directly with communities to identify their most pressing unmet needs before selecting proven nonprofit organizations capable of addressing those challenges. The organization focuses on removing barriers that prevent individuals and families from achieving long-term economic mobility, particularly those rooted in racial and economic inequities. Today, GreenLight operates across multiple sites throughout the United States and continues expanding its national presence. Each year, every GreenLight site follows a structured community-driven process to identify one critical local challenge and invest in a nonprofit organization capable of delivering measurable and sustainable results. Funding Benefits Organizations selected into GreenLight Fund s portfolio receive far more than financial support. Successful nonprofits may receive: Up to US$600,000 in unrestricted funding over four years. Multi-year investment designed to support long-term growth. Strategic guidance throughout expansion into new communities. Access to GreenLight Fund s Beyond the Check support model. Coaching on organizational strategy. Leadership and staffing support. Assistance overcoming implementation challenges. Partnership development with local organizations. Connections to additional funding opportunities. Access to GreenLight s national network of community leaders. Support from experienced local advisory boards. Ongoing relationship-building with stakeholders. Assistance developing sustainable local operations. Long-term accountability and performance measurement. Because the funding is unrestricted, organizations have greater flexibility to invest resources where they are most needed to achieve successful expansion. What Makes GreenLight Fund Different? Many grant programs simply award funding and expect organizations to implement projects independently. GreenLight Fund takes a different approach. Through its Beyond the Check model, GreenLight works as a long-term strategic partner throughout the expansion journey. This includes: Strategic coaching Local relationship building Staffing guidance Partnership development Fundraising support Leadership mentoring Sustainability planning Performance measurement The objective is not only to help nonprofits launch in a new city but also to ensure they become sustainable, community-supported organizations capable of creating lasting impact. Priority Impact Areas Although each GreenLight community identifies its own local priorities annually, the organization commonly supports nonprofit solutions addressing: Housing stability Education Youth opportunity Workforce development Economic mobility Health and well-being Family support Community resilience Reducing racial disparities Reducing economic disparities Inclusive prosperity initiatives Organizations operating in one or more of these focus areas are encouraged to explore the opportunity. Who Should Apply? GreenLight Fund is seeking nonprofit organizations that are prepared to scale successful programs into additional communities. Strong candidates typically: Operate as U.S.-based nonprofit organizations. Have a proven, evidence-based model. Demonstrate measurable outcomes. Can clearly show the impact of their work. Are interested in expanding into new U.S. communities. Address challenges related to economic mobility and inclusive prosperity. Have leadership committed to long-term growth and partnership. Organizations still testing early-stage ideas or pilot programs may not yet be ready for this opportunity, as GreenLight is specifically looking for solutions with demonstrated success that can be replicated effectively in new locations. Understanding the GreenLight Method GreenLight Fund follows a structured five-step process to identify and scale nonprofit solutions. 1. Discover GreenLight works closely with local communities, advisory committees, residents, and stakeholders to identify unmet community needs using research, local data, and extensive listening sessions. 2. Scout Once priority challenges have been identified, GreenLight searches nationally for nonprofit organizations with proven models capable of addressing those needs. 3. Select Potential organizations undergo careful evaluation before one nonprofit is selected as the strongest local fit. 4. Invest Selected organizations receive unrestricted funding together with strategic support to establish and expand operations within the new community. 5. Measure GreenLight works with partner organizations to establish measurable goals and track both programmatic and financial performance throughout the partnership. This structured approach helps ensure that investments produce measurable outcomes and long-term community impact. The GreenLight Partnership Journey Organizations interested in partnering with GreenLight Fund can expect several stages throughout the selection process. Stage 1: Interest and Exploration Organizations submit an Expression of Interest indicating their desire to be considered for future partnership opportunities. Stage 2: Pipeline Qualification GreenLight reviews submitted information to determine whether the organization aligns with its partnership model. Qualified organizations may be invited to an introductory conversation. Stage 3: Diligence and Alignment Organizations may be asked to provide additional documentation and participate in deeper discussions regarding program effectiveness, expansion readiness, and organizational capacity. Stage 4: Community-Driven Selection Finalists may present their work before a Selection Advisory Committee and engage directly with local community stakeholders. Stage 5: Partnership and Investment Each year, GreenLight selects one organization per site to expand into a new community. Selected organizations enter a formal partnership agreement outlining funding, expectations, strategic support, and shared accountability. Why This Opportunity Matters Scaling nonprofit programs successfully requires much more than financial investment. Organizations often need: Strong local partnerships. Community trust. Leadership coaching. Sustainable staffing structures. Fundraising guidance. Strategic planning. Long-term implementation support. GreenLight Fund addresses all of these needs simultaneously through its integrated funding and partnership approach. For nonprofits with proven models ready to reach more communities, this opportunity offers one of the most comprehensive expansion support programs currently available in the United States. Important Notes Expression of Interest Deadline: July 17, 2026 Submitting an Expression of Interest does not constitute a formal application. GreenLight Fund staff will review submissions to determine organizational alignment. Organizations that demonstrate strong alignment may be contacted for additional conversations or future selection cycles. Selection is based on community priorities, organizational readiness, measurable impact, and alignment with GreenLight Fund s mission. How to Apply Eligible nonprofit organizations should complete the GreenLight Fund Expression of Interest Form before the July 17, 2026 deadline. title: Free SOUTHMOD Training Course 2026 on Tax and Benefit Microsimulation for Latin America | Hybrid Participation in Quito, Ecuador
summary: Professionals, researchers, policymakers, and academics interested in tax and social protection policy analysis are invited to register for the SOUTHMOD Training Course on Microsimulation for Tax and Benefit Analysis in Latin America , taking place 14–16 July 2026 in Quito, Ecuador . Organized by the United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER) in collaboration with Facultad Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales (FLACSO Ecuador) , Universidad del Pacífico , the International Inequalities Institute at the London School of Economics (LSE) , and Pontificia Universidad Javeriana’s Observatorio Fiscal , this three-day hybrid training programme provides participants with practical skills in using tax-benefit microsimulation models to evaluate fiscal policies. The training is completely free of charge , open to all eligible participants, and will be delivered entirely in Spanish . Registration Status Registration is currently open. Training Dates 14 July 2026 – 16 July 2026 Venue Quito, Ecuador The course will be offered in a hybrid format , allowing participants to attend either in person or through virtual participation. About the SOUTHMOD Training Course The SOUTHMOD training course is designed to equip participants with practical knowledge and hands-on experience in using microsimulation models to analyze the impact of tax and social benefit policies across Latin America. Participants will learn how to evaluate how different fiscal policies affect: Household income Poverty levels Income inequality Government revenues Social protection outcomes Distribution of taxes and benefits The programme focuses on practical applications that support evidence-based policymaking and economic research. What is SOUTHMOD? SOUTHMOD is an internationally recognized research initiative that develops, updates, and maintains tax-benefit microsimulation models for low- and middle-income countries. These models combine: Household income data Household expenditure data National tax legislation Social benefit policies Using these datasets, researchers and policymakers can simulate proposed policy changes before implementation and estimate their likely economic and social impacts. This makes SOUTHMOD an essential tool for governments, researchers, and development organizations seeking to design more effective fiscal and social protection policies. Countries Covered by the Training This training focuses on four Latin American microsimulation models: ECUAMOD (Ecuador) COLMOD (Colombia) BOLMOD (Bolivia) PERUMOD (Peru) Participants will gain practical experience using these country-specific models to assess tax and benefit reforms. What Participants Will Learn Throughout the three-day programme, participants will receive practical instruction on how to: Use tax-benefit microsimulation software. Analyze household-level income and expenditure data. Evaluate fiscal policy reforms. Estimate poverty impacts. Measure inequality outcomes. Assess government revenue implications. Compare alternative tax and social benefit scenarios. Interpret simulation results for policymaking. The course emphasizes applied learning through real-world examples and hands-on exercises. Who Should Attend? The programme is intended for both experienced and first-time SOUTHMOD users. Ideal participants include: Government officials involved in fiscal policy. Public finance specialists. Social policy analysts. Academic researchers. University lecturers. Think tank professionals. Public institution analysts. Graduate students interested in tax and social policy. Anyone interested in evidence-based policymaking and fiscal analysis is encouraged to participate. Why Tax-Benefit Microsimulation Matters Tax-benefit microsimulation has become one of the most valuable tools for governments and researchers because it enables policymakers to test the likely consequences of policy reforms before implementation. These models help answer important policy questions, including: How will a proposed tax reform affect low-income households? Which social benefit programme is most effective at reducing poverty? What impact will policy changes have on government revenues? How will inequality change under different fiscal scenarios? Such evidence supports smarter, fairer, and more efficient public policy decisions. Global Reach of SOUTHMOD UNU-WIDER currently hosts fourteen tax-benefit microsimulation models covering countries across multiple regions. Africa Egypt Ethiopia Ghana Mozambique Rwanda Tanzania Uganda Zambia Latin America Bolivia Colombia Ecuador Peru Southeast Asia Viet Nam Other Zanzibar These models complement previously developed systems for South Africa and Namibia, making SOUTHMOD one of the world s leading tax-benefit microsimulation initiatives for developing economies. Organizing Institutions The training course is jointly organized by: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER) Facultad Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales (FLACSO Ecuador) Universidad del Pacífico International Inequalities Institute, London School of Economics (LSE) Pontificia Universidad Javeriana – Observatorio Fiscal This collaboration brings together leading experts in economics, public finance, social policy, and fiscal analysis. Benefits of Participating Participants will benefit from: Free professional training. Practical hands-on learning. Hybrid participation options. Exposure to internationally recognized policy tools. Improved analytical skills. Better understanding of tax-benefit modelling. Networking opportunities with researchers and policymakers. Knowledge applicable to fiscal policy design and evaluation. Enhanced research and policy analysis capabilities. Why You Should Register Whether you work in government, academia, public policy, or development research, this course offers an excellent opportunity to strengthen your expertise in tax-benefit microsimulation and evidence-based fiscal policymaking. By learning to use SOUTHMOD, participants will gain practical skills that can support better policy design, improve social protection systems, and contribute to reducing poverty and inequality across developing countries. title: British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026–2027: Fully Funded Three-Year UK Research Fellowship for Early-Career Humanities and Social Sciences Researchers
summary: The British Academy has officially opened applications for its prestigious Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 —one of the United Kingdom s leading funding opportunities for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences. Designed to help postdoctoral scholars establish independent research careers, the fellowship provides three years of funding to enable recipients to complete a significant piece of publishable research while strengthening their academic profile within a UK university or recognised research institution. Funded by the UK Department for Science, Innovation Technology (DSIT) , the fellowship supports researchers in developing their research and teaching experience, expanding their professional networks, and improving their prospects of securing permanent academic positions. If you are an early-career researcher looking to advance your academic career through high-quality independent research, the British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 could be the ideal opportunity. About the British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships The British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships are awarded annually to an outstanding cohort of early-career researchers working in the humanities and social sciences. The scheme is specifically designed to: Support outstanding postdoctoral researchers as they establish independent academic careers. Enable fellows to complete a substantial piece of publishable research. Enhance research and teaching experience within a university environment. Strengthen fellows academic profiles and career prospects. Integrate fellows into communities of established scholars in their disciplines. The programme provides recipients with the time, resources, mentorship, and institutional support needed to become future academic leaders. Unlike short-term research grants, this fellowship offers sustained support over three years, allowing researchers to focus on producing high-quality research outputs while gaining valuable academic experience. Purpose of the Fellowship The British Academy created this fellowship to bridge the gap between completing a doctorate and securing a permanent academic position. The programme helps early-career researchers by: Developing independent research careers. Supporting publication of significant academic work. Encouraging excellence in humanities and social sciences research. Building teaching and research experience. Expanding academic networks. Improving long-term employability within higher education. The fellowship recognizes that the years immediately following a doctorate are often critical for developing an academic career. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will receive funding for: Three years The fellowship is: Non-renewable Full-time Hosted at an eligible UK institution The earliest fellowship start date is: 1 September 2027 Funding Information The British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship operates under the Full Economic Costing (FEC) model. Under this funding arrangement: The British Academy funds 80% of eligible Full Economic Costs. Funding includes salary costs. Funding also covers directly allocated and indirect research costs under the FEC framework. The fellowship is funded by the: UK Department for Science, Innovation Technology (DSIT). What Fellows Will Do Throughout the three-year fellowship, award holders will: Conduct an independent research project. Produce significant publishable research. Build an academic publication record. Gain valuable teaching experience. Participate in the scholarly community of their host institution. Collaborate with established academics. Strengthen professional research networks. Develop skills needed for long-term academic careers. The primary emphasis of the fellowship is on completing research that contributes meaningfully to the humanities or social sciences. Research Areas Supported The fellowship supports research within: Humanities Examples include: History Philosophy Literature Languages Archaeology Classics Religious Studies Cultural Studies Linguistics Social Sciences Examples include: Sociology Political Science Economics Human Geography Anthropology Education Psychology (where eligible) International Relations Public Policy Applicants should ensure that their proposed research falls within the British Academy s funding remit. Benefits of the British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships Successful fellows receive numerous professional and academic benefits. These include: Financial Support Funding under the Full Economic Costing model. 80% funding of eligible salary costs. Support for eligible research-related costs. Research Development Fellows gain opportunities to: Conduct independent research. Produce high-impact publications. Complete major research projects. Develop long-term research agendas. Academic Experience Recipients benefit from: Teaching opportunities. Research collaboration. Integration into academic departments. Access to university research resources. Career Advancement The fellowship significantly strengthens applicants prospects for: Permanent academic appointments. Future research grants. International collaborations. Leadership roles in academia. Professional Networking Participants become part of: Academic research communities. Established scholarly networks. Collaborative research environments. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must carefully review all eligibility requirements before applying. To qualify, applicants must satisfy the following conditions. 1. Research Discipline Applicants must be researchers in: Humanities Social Sciences 2. Host Institution Applicants must be based at an eligible: UK university UK recognised research organisation for the full duration of the fellowship. 3. Nationality Requirements Applicants are eligible if they are: British citizens Nationals of any European Economic Area (EEA) country, regardless of where they obtained their doctorate OR Applicants of any nationality are eligible if they: Hold a doctorate awarded by a UK university. Applicants who do not fall into either category may still be eligible if they can demonstrate: A strong prior association with the UK academic community. 4. Career Stage Applicants must be early-career researchers. Specifically, applicants are expected to have completed their: Viva Voce examination between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Applicants must also already hold postdoctoral status when the Research Awards Committee meets. 5. Permanent Academic Posts Applicants are not eligible if they have ever held: A permanent academic appointment At any higher education institution Either in the UK or overseas This restriction also applies if the appointment occurred before the doctorate was awarded. Certain exemptions may apply and require prior approval from the British Academy before submitting an application. Please check last round s scheme guidance notes further information regarding exemption from this criterion. Host Institution Requirements The fellowship must be held at an eligible institution such as: UK universities UK recognised research organisations The host institution will provide the academic environment in which fellows complete their research. Referee Requirements Applicants must nominate one referee . The referee will complete a questionnaire through the Flexi-Grant® system. Normally, the referee should be: The external doctoral examiner If unavailable: Another suitably independent external academic. The referee cannot be: Proposed mentor Doctoral supervisor Internal examiner Staff member from the proposed host institution Application Process Applications are submitted online using the British Academy s: Grant Management System (GMS) – Flexi-Grant® Applicants are encouraged to prepare carefully before submitting. Application Timeline Applicants should note the following important dates. Activity Date Applications Open 1 July 2026 Application Deadline 30 September 2026 (17:00 BST) Earliest Fellowship Start 1 September 2027 Fellowship Duration Three Years Late submissions will not be accepted. How to Apply Applicants should: Review the official Scheme Guidance. Read the Application Guidance Notes carefully. Confirm eligibility. Secure an eligible UK host institution. Identify an eligible referee. Prepare the research proposal. Submit the application through Flexi-Grant® before the deadline. Ensure institutional approval is completed before the submission deadline. Scheme Guidance Before applying, applicants are strongly encouraged to review: Scheme Guidance Notes Application Guidance Notes Eligibility requirements Funding rules Assessment criteria Carefully reviewing these documents can significantly improve the quality of an application. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) The British Academy provides a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) section to help applicants understand the fellowship and application process. Common topics covered include: Eligibility requirements Career stage requirements Host institution eligibility Referee requirements Funding arrangements Application process Research proposal guidance Fellowship conditions Applicants are encouraged to review the FAQs before contacting the British Academy. Applicant Support Applicants who require assistance can access several support resources. These include: Scheme Guidance Notes Application Guidance Notes Frequently Asked Questions Knowbot AI chatbot British Academy Research Funding Team Questions can also be directed via email to: posts@thebritishacademy.ac.uk Why Apply for the British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship? Securing a permanent academic position has become increasingly competitive. The British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship provides a unique opportunity to strengthen an academic career by offering dedicated time, funding, and institutional support to conduct independent research. Beyond financial support, fellows gain valuable experience in research, teaching, collaboration, and scholarly engagement—helping them build competitive academic portfolios and establish themselves within their disciplines. For researchers seeking to publish influential work, develop new collaborations, and secure future academic opportunities, this fellowship represents one of the UK s most prestigious early-career funding schemes. Visit HERE to learn more about the British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships. Conclusion The British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 provide exceptional early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences with the opportunity to establish themselves as independent scholars through a fully supported three-year research programme. Hosted at eligible UK universities and research organisations, the fellowship enables recipients to complete significant publishable research, gain valuable teaching and research experience, and integrate into leading academic communities. With applications opening on 1 July 2026 and closing on 30 September 2026 at 17:00 BST , eligible researchers should begin preparing their proposals, confirming host institution arrangements, securing an appropriate referee, and reviewing the official guidance documents well before the deadline. For ambitious postdoctoral researchers aiming to strengthen their academic careers and contribute impactful research to the humanities and social sciences, this fellowship offers an outstanding pathway toward long-term academic success. title: Free UN Online Course on Gender and Environment with Digital Certificate – Open for Global Learners

Unlike traditional classroom programs, this online course allows learners to study at their own pace from anywhere in the world. Participants can access learning materials whenever convenient, making it suitable for both students and working professionals. Women, men, girls, and boys often experience environmental issues differently because of varying social, economic, and cultural roles. Understanding these differences is becoming increasingly important for governments, NGOs, development agencies, researchers, and businesses seeking to design inclusive environmental policies and sustainable development strategies. This course helps participants understand: Why gender equality contributes to better environmental outcomes. How environmental degradation affects different populations differently. The importance of women s leadership and empowerment in climate action. How gender-responsive policies improve conservation and sustainable development. International frameworks that support gender equality in environmental governance. What You Will Learn The course provides practical and theoretical knowledge covering several major environmental themes. Participants will learn: The relationship between gender equality and environmental sustainability. Global environmental agreements that include gender considerations. How gender-responsive policies improve environmental outcomes. Practical approaches to integrating gender into environmental projects. Ways to promote women s empowerment within biodiversity conservation. Gender considerations in climate change adaptation and mitigation. Gender issues relating to international waters. Sustainable land degradation management. Chemicals and waste management from a gender perspective. Course Structure The learning programme consists of six comprehensive modules , each designed to build practical knowledge step by step. The modules include: Introduction Climate Change International Waters Biodiversity Land Degradation Chemicals and Waste Each module takes approximately one hour to complete, resulting in a total learning time of around six hours . Since the course is self-paced, learners can complete it according to their own schedules without fixed deadlines. Who Should Enroll? The course has been designed for a wide variety of learners, including: Students studying environmental sciences or sustainable development. Climate change practitioners. Biodiversity specialists. Government officials working on environmental policies. NGO staff involved in environmental conservation. Development practitioners. Researchers. Community leaders. Sustainability consultants. Anyone interested in learning how gender equality contributes to environmental sustainability. title: German Bundestag International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) 2026 for U.S. Citizens: Fully Funded Five-Month Fellowship in Berlin with Monthly Stipend, Free Accommodation and Travel Support
summary: Young leaders passionate about democracy, governance, public policy, and international affairs now have an outstanding opportunity to gain first-hand experience inside one of Europe s most influential democratic institutions. Applications are officially open for the International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) Programme 2026 , an initiative of the German Bundestag that enables outstanding young graduates to spend five months in Berlin while learning about Germany s parliamentary system and participating directly in legislative work. The International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) is one of Germany s flagship international exchange programmes designed to strengthen democratic values, encourage civic engagement, and foster long-term cooperation between Germany and partner countries. Established in 1986 , the programme has provided thousands of young professionals from approximately 50 countries with practical parliamentary experience while building an international network of future leaders committed to democracy and public service. For applicants in the United States, the programme is coordinated through the German Missions and offers selected participants the unique opportunity to work alongside a Member of the German Bundestag while also taking part in an extensive academic and professional development programme. About the International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) The International Parliamentary Scholarship is organized by the German Bundestag in cooperation with three of Germany s leading universities: Freie Universität Berlin Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin Technische Universität Berlin Together, these institutions deliver a comprehensive programme that combines academic learning, professional training, seminars, networking opportunities, and practical parliamentary experience. The fellowship is specifically designed for talented young graduates who have demonstrated a commitment to democratic principles and civic participation in their home countries. Through the programme, participants gain valuable insights into parliamentary decision-making, political institutions, governance structures, and international cooperation. What Makes the IPS Programme Unique? Unlike traditional academic scholarships, the IPS Programme offers participants the opportunity to experience politics from inside the German Parliament. Participants spend five months in Berlin , where they become immersed in Germany s democratic institutions and political culture. One of the highlights of the programme is a three-month internship placement with a Member of the German Bundestag , allowing fellows to observe parliamentary work closely while contributing to daily legislative activities. This practical experience is complemented by university courses, professional seminars, workshops, and political training sessions that deepen participants understanding of democratic governance. The programme aims not only to educate participants but also to encourage international dialogue and strengthen democratic cooperation between Germany and participating countries. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows receive a comprehensive financial package that allows them to fully concentrate on learning and professional development throughout the programme. Benefits include: Monthly scholarship of 700 Euros Free accommodation throughout the fellowship Travel expenses Health insurance coverage Practical experience working in the German Parliament Participation in seminars and professional training sessions University courses delivered by leading Berlin universities Networking opportunities with political leaders, scholars, and fellow participants from around the world Exposure to Germany s parliamentary decision-making processes International leadership and intercultural experience Programme Duration The International Parliamentary Scholarship runs annually from: March 1 to July 31 During these five months, participants complete academic, professional, and practical parliamentary activities designed to prepare them for future leadership roles in government, public administration, international organizations, academia, civil society, and policy development. Eligibility Requirements Applicants from the United States must meet all of the following requirements: Hold U.S. citizenship Possess a completed college degree Demonstrate very good German language proficiency (minimum B2 level) Have a good understanding of German politics, society, and history Be under the age of 30 at the beginning of the fellowship Demonstrate a genuine interest in democratic governance and parliamentary systems Show active engagement in promoting democratic values and civil society The programme is particularly suited to graduates interested in careers in diplomacy, public administration, political science, international relations, law, public policy, journalism, governance, and civic leadership. Selection Process Applications undergo a competitive pre-selection process. Shortlisted candidates are invited to participate in interviews conducted within the United States. Final scholarship recipients are selected by an independent panel appointed by the German Bundestag. The rigorous selection process ensures that successful applicants possess strong academic credentials, leadership potential, commitment to democratic values, and the ability to serve as ambassadors for international cooperation. Why You Should Apply Participating in the International Parliamentary Scholarship offers far more than international study. Application Deadline The deadline to submit applications for the International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) Programme 2026 is: 31 July 2025 Interested applicants should prepare their documents well before the deadline to ensure they have sufficient time to complete the application process. title: OPCW Scholarships 2026 for the Asser–OPCW Training Programme on Disarmament and Non-Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) in The Hague, Netherlands
summary: Professionals working in arms control, non-proliferation, international security, diplomacy, and chemical weapons policy now have an exceptional opportunity to strengthen their expertise through one of the world’s most prestigious disarmament training programmes. Applications are now open for the 2026 Asser–OPCW Training Programme on Disarmament and Non-Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD), jointly organized by the Asser Institute and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) in The Hague, Netherlands. As part of this initiative, the OPCW is offering tuition fee waiver scholarships funded by the European Union for selected participants working in civil society, NGOs, think tanks, and academia. The intensive five-day programme will take place from 26 October to 30 October 2026 and provides participants with advanced practical and policy-oriented training on the rapidly evolving global challenges surrounding weapons of mass destruction, arms control, export regulations, emerging technologies, and international law. Programme Overview The international arms control landscape is currently facing unprecedented pressure due to geopolitical fragmentation, technological disruption, and the weakening of global non-proliferation frameworks. Concerns over nuclear weapons have returned to global political discourse, chemical weapons continue to pose major threats in active conflicts, and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and biotechnology are reshaping traditional security environments faster than existing legal systems can adapt. Against this backdrop, the Asser–OPCW Training Programme was designed to equip professionals with the legal, diplomatic, technical, and strategic knowledge required to navigate today’s complex disarmament and non-proliferation challenges. Participants will engage directly with leading international experts, practitioners, policymakers, and researchers through interactive lectures, discussions, case studies, and field visits. Scholarship Benefits Selected scholarship recipients will receive: Full tuition fee waiver worth €1,895 Access to expert-led sessions and workshops Networking opportunities with international security professionals Exposure to high-level practitioners in arms control and disarmament Participation in exclusive institutional field visits Advanced practical understanding of modern WMD challenges Professional development in international law, export controls, and security governance The scholarships are funded by the European Union and specifically support professionals from civil society organizations and academic sectors. Female applicants and candidates from lower-income countries are strongly encouraged to apply. Programme Dates and Location Dates: 26 October – 30 October 2026 Duration: Five days Venue: Asser Institute and OPCW Location: The Hague, Netherlands Address: R.J. Schimmelpennincklaan 20-22 2517 JN The Hague Netherlands Key Topics Covered During the Programme Participants will receive comprehensive training on some of the world’s most urgent disarmament and security challenges. 1. Nuclear Weapons and Strategic Stability Sessions will examine: Expanding nuclear stockpiles Declining arms control agreements Challenges facing the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) Deadlocked NPT Review Conferences Future pathways for nuclear disarmament 2. Chemical Weapons and Accountability Participants will explore: Use of chemical weapons in modern conflicts International accountability mechanisms Verification and compliance systems Challenges of misinformation and disinformation Enforcement of chemical weapons conventions 3. Biological Weapons and Synthetic Biology Key discussions include: Risks posed by synthetic biology Advances in pathogen engineering Weaknesses in the Biological Weapons Convention Biosecurity governance challenges Future biological weapons threats 4. Export Controls and Emerging Technologies The programme also addresses rapidly developing technologies, including: Artificial intelligence-enabled systems Autonomous weapons Hypersonic missile technology Export control regulations Legal and ethical gaps in emerging military technologies Exclusive Field Visits One of the most valuable components of the programme is direct institutional exposure through guided visits to internationally significant facilities. Participants will visit: OPCW Centre for Chemistry and Technology (ChemTech) This advanced facility supports scientific research, verification training, and international cooperation related to chemical weapons prohibition. OPCW Headquarters Participants will gain firsthand insight into the operations of one of the world’s leading international organizations dedicated to eliminating chemical weapons globally. Confirmed International Experts and Speakers The programme brings together highly respected scholars and practitioners from globally recognized institutions. Confirmed speakers include: Dr León Castellanos-Jankiewicz – Asser Institute Simon Cleobury – Geneva Centre for Security Policy Dr Sico van der Meer – Clingendael Institute Dr Oliver Meier – European Leadership Network Ionut Suseanu – International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Dr Ana Sánchez-Cobaleda – University of Barcelona Dr Sibylle Bauer – Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) Dr James Revill – United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) Dr Miranda Smith – SIPRI Dr Edward Howell – University of Oxford Dr Abdolrasool Farzam Divsallar – UNIDIR Who Should Apply? This programme is ideal for professionals and students seeking specialized expertise in international security and disarmament policy. Suitable applicants include: Government officials Diplomats NGO professionals Think tank researchers Academic scholars International organization staff Compliance officers Legal advisers Graduate students transitioning into the security field Applicants with backgrounds in international relations, law, diplomacy, political science, security studies, public policy, arms control, and strategic affairs are especially encouraged to apply. Why This Programme Matters The global security environment is evolving rapidly. Traditional arms control systems are increasingly challenged by geopolitical tensions, technological innovation, and the growing complexity of modern warfare. This programme provides participants with: Practical policy knowledge Exposure to real-world disarmament challenges International networking opportunities Institutional access to global security actors Specialized expertise highly valued in diplomacy and international organizations For professionals seeking careers in international security, arms control, diplomacy, compliance, or multilateral policy-making, this programme represents a significant career-development opportunity. title: New York Climate Exchange Climate Tech Fellowship 2026: Win a $10,000 Non-Dilutive Stipend, Expert Mentorship, Investor Access, and Climate Week NYC Participation

Organized by the Foresight Institute , the fellowship connects emerging leaders with world-class scientists, industry experts, research mentors, investors, and funding opportunities. Participants also gain access to an international network of innovators working across groundbreaking scientific and technological fields. Unlike many fellowship programs, the Foresight Fellowship does not impose a minimum work requirement. Instead, it focuses on empowering talented individuals by providing mentorship, strategic career support, networking opportunities, technical discussions, and exposure to influential scientific communities. The fellowship recognizes that many exceptional researchers and builders possess tremendous technical ability but often lack access to influential networks, experienced mentors, and strategic career guidance. Through this program, Fellows receive personalized support that helps transform promising careers into globally impactful ones. After successfully completing the fellowship, participants become members of the Foresight Fellowship Alumni community, enabling them to continue benefiting from collaborations, networking, and future opportunities. title: Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship 2027: The Complete Guide to This Prestigious International Clean Energy and Climate Change Fellowship for Global South Professionals
summary: Yale University s Jackson School of Global Affairs has officially opened applications for the 2027 cohort of the Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship, an exclusive and highly competitive international fellowship designed to cultivate a global community of clean energy and climate change leaders from emerging and developing countries. Anchored by Yale s International Leadership Center and led by a former senior official of the International Energy Agency, this five-month fellowship combines world-class academic engagement, international networking, remote policy learning, and in-person convenings in both New Haven, Connecticut and Paris, France. This article provides a complete and detailed overview of the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship 2027 its mission, structure, programme details, leadership, eligibility criteria, selection process, and how to apply. The Mission of the Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship The mission of the Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship is to create a community of committed clean energy and climate change leaders from emerging and developing countries. This community is enriched through direct engagement with top Yale faculty and researchers, as well as leading global authorities in the clean energy transition, including experts from the International Energy Agency (IEA) and beyond. The fellowship recognizes that the individuals best positioned to drive meaningful climate action in the Global South are professionals who are already embedded within their countries energy, policy, business, and civil society sectors and who, with the right exposure, mentorship, and global network, can accelerate their impact as future leaders in the clean energy and climate space. Who Are the Yale Climate Fellows? Each year, sixteen young practitioners are selected from across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean to form a new cohort of Yale Climate Fellows. These fellows are drawn from multiple career tracks and share a common passion for becoming future leaders in the clean energy and climate change space, exchanging findings and experiences with other like-minded professionals from across the Global South. Yale Climate Fellows are intentionally selected to model diversity across several dimensions: Gender Country of origin Professional background The professional backgrounds represented within each cohort are intentionally broad and multidisciplinary, including: Public servants and government officials Entrepreneurs Energy company and utility professionals Financiers and bankers Journalists Educators and researchers Civil society representatives Legal advisers Legislators This diversity of professional perspective is central to the fellowship s design, as it allows fellows to engage with the clean energy transition from multiple angles policy, finance, technology, communication, and grassroots advocacy while learning from one another s distinct vantage points. Faculty, Partners, and Program Leadership Fellows in the programme engage directly with prominent Yale faculty as well as a broad network of top global practitioners working on the most pressing issues in the clean energy and climate change agenda. Program Leadership The fellowship is overseen by Paul Simons, a Jackson Senior Fellow and retired United States ambassador who has been actively engaged in global energy and climate change policymaking for more than two decades. Since 2020, Paul Simons has been teaching and mentoring Yale students on the clean energy transition, while also actively participating in the COP26 and COP27 international climate negotiation processes. From 2015 to 2020, he served as Deputy Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer of the International Energy Agency (IEA) the world s leading authority for energy and climate change analysis and policy development where he led outreach activities with emerging economies and coordinated engagement with the G-20. The fellowship is further supported by a group of seasoned professionals from the Jackson School s International Leadership Center (ILC). Director Emma Sky and her ILC team provide essential policy guidance and administrative support throughout the duration of the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship. Program Structure: A Five-Month Global Journey The Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship is structured around three core components spanning five months, beginning with an in-person orientation at Yale, continuing through a period of remote learning, and concluding with an in-person closing week in Paris. Phase 1: Yale Orientation Week (February 1-5, 2027) The fellowship begins with a one-week, in-person orientation programme at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, running from February 1 to February 5, 2027. During orientation week, fellows will: Engage in a series of interactive sessions with prominent Yale faculty and practitioners to help set the terms of the global climate change debate Explore the wide range of climate change initiatives and research housed across Yale University Delve into cutting-edge scholarship spanning a broad range of clean energy and climate issues Among the centers and institutions that may be featured during the orientation programme are: The Yale Program on Climate Change Communication The Yale Center for Natural Carbon Capture The Yale Open Lab The Yale Center for Business and the Environment The Yale Center for Environmental Law and Policy The Yale Office of Sustainability, which manages the University s net zero goal Phase 2: Remote Learning Journeys (March-June 2027) From March through June 2027, Climate Fellows will organize and participate in a series of interactive remote learning sessions with leading international experts, covering the full range of policy issues associated with climate change and the clean energy transition. These sessions function as spirited learning journeys that allow fellows to develop communities of practice around shared specialties, while benefiting from extensive mentoring opportunities. Sessions typically take place on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM Eastern Time. Possible topics covered during the remote learning journeys include: Strengthening global climate change governance, including the United Nations process Exploring decarbonization pathways, including the IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario Accelerating renewable electricity growth and addressing the challenges of system integration Strengthening innovation and uptake of promising clean energy technologies Promoting energy efficiency and behavioral change Investigating the challenges of a people-centered clean energy transition Developing and deepening financial vehicles to advance the clean energy transition Exploring market-based climate policy tools, including carbon pricing Exploring regulatory policy tools to support the uptake of clean energy solutions Improving climate change communication Closing energy access gaps with clean energy technologies Developing cost-effective negative emissions technologies, including direct air capture Exploring the role of nature-based climate solutions Broadening and deepening corporate and investor initiatives on climate change Tackling energy security issues, including the role of fossil fuels in the energy transition Exploring supply chain and related geopolitical challenges of the clean energy transition Analyzing the challenges of reducing methane emissions in emerging and developing countries In addition to these remote sessions, fellows will work collaboratively on a group project between March and June 2027. Phase 3: Paris Closing Week (June 14-18, 2027) The fellowship concludes with an in-person closing week in Paris, France, running from June 14 to June 18, 2027. During this final week, fellows will: Meet with top international climate change analysts and policymakers Share perspectives gleaned throughout the entirety of the programme Consolidate professional and personal contacts developed through peer learning and exchanges of views Fellows will also have valuable networking opportunities with: Staff members from the International Energy Agency (IEA) Representatives from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) French central government and municipal officials Representatives of civil society organizations, think tanks, academia, and the private sector As the culminating activity of the fellowship, fellows will present policy recommendations addressing specific clean energy and climate-related challenges to a global advisory board. These findings will then be published, and fellows will be invited to maintain ongoing contacts through the programme s alumni network following the conclusion of the fellowship. Find more program details HERE . Eligibility and Application Requirements Admission to the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship is highly competitive. Each cohort is intentionally geographically balanced and represents a wide range of professions, talents, experience, cultures, and perspectives. To be eligible to apply, candidates must meet the following requirements: Be between five and ten years into their professional career, with demonstrated accomplishments at a regional, national, or international level. There is no minimum or maximum age requirement, but the programme is seeking leaders who are still on the rise in their careers Be representatives of the Global South, specifically from Africa, Asia, the Middle East, or Latin America and the Caribbean Be fluent in English, as an excellent command of the English language is essential to successfully participating in the programme Be available to fully participate in all parts of the programme, including in-person attendance for two full weeks: the Yale Orientation Week (February 1-5, 2027) and the Paris Closing Week (June 14-18, 2027) Be available to participate in six remote learning journeys, held on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM Eastern Time Be available to work on a collaborative group project between March and June 2027 Learn More Selection Criteria Beyond the baseline eligibility requirements, the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship selection committee evaluates applicants against the following criteria: An established record of achievement in a profession linked to clean energy and climate change Representation across a diverse group of stakeholder categories, including government officials, entrepreneurs, energy company and utility professionals, bankers and financiers, journalists, educators and researchers, civil society representatives, legal advisors, and legislators A demonstrated commitment to making a positive impact at the local, national, or international level Demonstrated promise of a future leadership career at both the national and potentially global level An eagerness to expand and deepen professional networks, and to benefit meaningfully from exposure to top global leaders in the clean energy and climate change space Learn More Application Process Overview The application process for the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship is conducted entirely online. There are no paper forms to complete or mail in. Key details of the application process include: As of June 2026, an electronic application fee is required to complete submission of the application Applicants may work on their application at any time prior to the deadline and submit it whenever they are ready After creating an account and accessing the online application portal, applicants can upload required materials and request their letters of recommendation directly through the system Required Application Materials Applicants must submit the following as part of their complete application: A résumé or curriculum vitae, with a maximum length of three pages A brief video statement A personal statement, with a maximum length of 600 words One letter of recommendation Apply through the link here: Online Application Travel and Lodging Coverage For fellows ultimately selected to the programme, travel and lodging costs for both the Yale Orientation Week and the Paris Closing Week will be fully covered by the programme. This includes: Round-trip airfare Hotel accommodation Transfers Most meals during both in-person weeks Application Deadline Applications for the 2027 cohort of the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship close on Thursday, 30 July 2026, at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. This deadline is strict, and no extensions will be granted under any circumstances. Applicants are strongly advised to submit their application at least 24 hours before the deadline to avoid any last-minute technical issues or delays. Prospective applicants are encouraged to review the programme s Frequently Asked Questions page for additional guidance before submitting their application. Equal Opportunity Statement Yale University maintains a formal equal opportunity and nondiscrimination policy that applies to the Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship. Full details of this policy are publicly available on Yale s official website. Why This Fellowship Matters The clean energy transition is one of the defining global challenges of this era, and the countries of the Global South across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean are simultaneously among those most affected by climate change and most critical to shaping an equitable and effective global response. Yet professionals from these regions have historically had less access to the elite academic institutions, international policy networks, and high-level convenings where global climate strategy is often shaped. The Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship directly addresses this gap by bringing accomplished mid-career professionals from the Global South into direct, sustained engagement with Yale faculty, IEA experts, OECD representatives, and a global advisory board while also fully funding the travel costs associated with the programme s in-person components. The result is a uniquely positioned cohort of leaders equipped not only with deepened technical and policy knowledge, but with a global professional network and an international platform from which to advance climate action in their home countries and regions. Learn More Conclusion The Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship 2027 offers an exceptional and rare opportunity for accomplished mid-career professionals from Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean to deepen their expertise in clean energy and climate change policy while joining a prestigious global network anchored by Yale University, the International Energy Agency, and leading institutions across the climate and energy space. With a thoughtfully structured five-month programme spanning an in-person orientation at Yale, months of remote expert-led learning, and a culminating closing week in Paris, the fellowship offers far more than academic enrichment it offers a genuine platform for career-defining leadership development and international influence. With only sixteen fellows selected per year and admission described as highly competitive, prospective applicants should take the application process seriously and begin preparing their materials including a strong personal statement, a compelling video statement, a concise CV, and a thoughtful letter of recommendation well ahead of the firm deadline of Thursday, 30 July 2026 at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. For mid-career professionals from the Global South who are passionate about climate leadership and eager to expand their global network and impact, the Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship represents a truly transformative opportunity. Apply early, as no extensions will be granted, and take the next step toward shaping the future of the global clean energy transition. title: Apply for the 2026–2027 World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council: Global Leadership Opportunity for Young Ocean and Climate Advocates
summary: Young leaders who are passionate about ocean conservation, climate action, environmental advocacy, and community impact now have an exciting opportunity to join the 2026–2027 World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council. Applications are officially open for young people from around the world who are already making a difference in their communities and are eager to strengthen their leadership skills, expand their global networks, and contribute to international efforts aimed at protecting our blue planet. The World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council brings together a diverse group of 20–25 young leaders from different countries and backgrounds who are actively involved in conservation efforts. Since its establishment in 2016, the Council has played a significant role in advancing youth engagement and leadership within the global environmental movement. About the World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council The World Ocean Day Youth Advisory Council is a global network of young environmental leaders committed to ocean protection, climate action, and sustainable development. Council members collaborate throughout the year to share ideas, strengthen conservation initiatives, develop leadership skills, and inspire collective action for a healthier planet. The Council supports the broader mission of World Ocean Day, which seeks to unite individuals, organizations, businesses, governments, and communities worldwide in taking meaningful action for the ocean. Given that the ocean covers approximately 71% of the Earth s surface and plays a critical role in regulating climate systems, the Council focuses on empowering young people to become influential voices in environmental stewardship. Over the years, the Youth Advisory Council has grown into a vibrant global network. The Youth Advisory Council Alumni Network currently includes 173 members representing 75 countries, demonstrating the program’s international reach and impact. Why This Opportunity Matters Young people are increasingly at the forefront of environmental advocacy and climate action. The Youth Advisory Council provides participants with a unique platform to: Collaborate with like-minded youth leaders from across the globe. Develop practical leadership and advocacy skills. Influence global conversations around ocean and climate protection. Expand professional and conservation networks. Gain visibility for their local environmental initiatives. Access future opportunities through a worldwide network of organizations and conservation professionals. Through this experience, participants can amplify their impact both locally and internationally. What Council Members Will Do Members of the Youth Advisory Council are expected to continue their existing conservation work while contributing to broader global initiatives. Key responsibilities include: 1. Deepen Community Impact Council members will continue the conservation, advocacy, and environmental initiatives they are already leading in their communities while exploring ways to increase their effectiveness and reach. 2. Participate in Conservation Events Members are encouraged to engage in ocean, climate, and environmental events throughout the year at local, national, regional, and international levels. 3. Serve as World Ocean Day Ambassadors Council members act as ambassadors for World Ocean Day by promoting awareness and encouraging individuals and organizations to take action for ocean protection. 4. Collaborate with Global Peers Participants work closely with fellow Council members and alumni on projects such as: Organizing events Developing educational resources Supporting conservation campaigns Creating community engagement initiatives Promoting youth-led environmental action 5. Provide Strategic Guidance Members contribute ideas and perspectives that help shape the future direction of World Ocean Day and related conservation campaigns. 6. Participate in Public Awareness Campaigns Council members may: Share environmental content through social media. Contribute blog posts highlighting community projects. Participate in social media takeovers. Engage in awareness and outreach campaigns. Program Commitment Applicants should be prepared to actively participate throughout the one-year term. Commitment requirements include: One-year term lasting through June 2027. Attendance at a minimum of five virtual video conference meetings. Completion of three to four advisory surveys during the term. Regular communication through email and WhatsApp at least once or twice each month. Participation in the Youth Leadership Training Program. Engagement in regional hub development activities. Optional participation in collaborative projects with other Council members. Youth Leadership Training Program A major benefit of the Council is access to a comprehensive Youth Leadership Training Program. The training includes: Virtual leadership sessions. Weekly one-hour meetings. Additional 30-minute discussion sessions exclusively for Council members. Four-week training period scheduled for October/November 2026 (subject to change). The program is designed to strengthen participants’ abilities in: Campaign organization Advocacy Community mobilization Event planning Goal setting and implementation Public engagement Environmental leadership Benefits of Joining the Youth Advisory Council Successful applicants gain access to a wide range of personal, professional, and leadership development opportunities. Benefits include: Leadership Development Comprehensive onboarding. Professional leadership training. Practical advocacy experience. Global Recognition Council members receive opportunities to showcase their work through: Guest blog posts. Social media features. Newsletter spotlights. Media interviews. Speaking engagements. International Networking Participants can connect with: Current Council members. Alumni across 75 countries. Environmental organizations. Conservation professionals. Policymakers and advocates. Event and Campaign Experience Members receive hands-on opportunities to: Organize environmental events. Lead campaigns. Coordinate community initiatives. Mobilize public participation. Access to Future Opportunities The Ocean Project works with a global network of more than 2,000 organizations in nearly 200 countries. Council members may gain access to future opportunities including: Internships Professional positions Collaborative projects Conference participation Environmental leadership initiatives Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the following criteria: Be between 16 and 25 years old at the time of application. Be fluent in English. Have reliable internet access. Demonstrate previous conservation experience. Show commitment to environmental protection and climate action. Advocacy and organizing experience are considered an added advantage but are not mandatory. Ideal Candidates The program is seeking young people who: Are already engaged in conservation activities. Understand the connection between ocean health and climate stability. Value collaboration and collective action. Want to share ideas and experiences with a global audience. Are eager to build leadership and advocacy skills. Are committed to environmental restoration and sustainability. Application Process The application process follows several stages: Stage 1: Initial Application Applications opened on 25 June 2026 . Stage 3: Second-Round Notification Candidates selected for the next stage will be notified on 10 August 2026 . Since launching global coordination efforts in 2002, the organization has collaborated with youth leaders, community organizations, businesses, and conservation partners worldwide. Through partnerships spanning nearly 200 countries, The Ocean Project continues to strengthen public engagement, support environmental education, and encourage meaningful action to protect marine ecosystems and address climate challenges.
