title: Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship 2027: Fully Supported Pathway for Emerging Development Economics Researchers from Low and Lower-Middle-Income Countries
summary: The Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship 2027 is a prestigious opportunity designed to identify, support, and elevate talented aspiring researchers from low and lower-middle-income countries who are interested in pursuing academic careers in development economics. Offered by the Weiss Fund for Research in Development Economics, this fellowship aims to bridge the gap between undergraduate or master s studies and doctoral-level education by connecting promising candidates with leading economists and world-class universities. The fellowship seeks to address the underrepresentation of researchers from developing countries within highly competitive predoctoral programs. Through endorsement, mentorship opportunities, and institutional support, successful applicants gain access to pathways that can significantly strengthen their prospects of securing admission into top-tier Ph.D. programs in Economics. About the Weiss Fund for Research in Development Economics The Weiss Fund for Research in Development Economics supports innovative and impactful research that improves the lives of people living in developing countries. The fund is committed to fostering rigorous, evidence-based solutions to complex development challenges while nurturing the next generation of researchers in the field. Beyond funding research projects, the Weiss Fund actively works to: Attract talented individuals into development economics. Support creative and rigorous academic research. Build stronger connections between research, policy, and implementation. Expand opportunities for talented researchers from underrepresented regions. Promote equitable access to academic mentorship and research training. Through the Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship, the Weiss Fund continues this mission by helping talented candidates gain access to leading research environments and mentorship from renowned development economists. What Is the Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship? The fellowship is specifically designed for individuals interested in pursuing predoctoral research positions. Predoctoral roles serve as an important stepping stone between undergraduate education and doctoral studies, providing hands-on research experience, advanced quantitative training, and mentorship from experienced academics. Successful fellowship finalists may receive: Official endorsement from the Weiss Fund. Opportunities to be invited by leading faculty members to apply for pre-approved two-year predoctoral research positions. Increased visibility among top universities and development economists. Support throughout the placement process. Access to valuable academic and professional networks. Previous fellowship finalists have secured positions with Weiss Fund-affiliated faculty at globally recognized institutions including: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Northwestern University Stanford University University of California, Berkeley Yale University While placements vary each year, finalists may be invited to apply for opportunities at leading universities participating in the fellowship network. Why This Fellowship Matters Many talented students from developing countries face barriers when attempting to enter elite academic and research pathways. These barriers often include: Limited access to mentorship. Lack of exposure to internationally recognized economists. Fewer opportunities for research experience. Limited access to recommendation networks. Financial constraints associated with academic advancement. The Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship is specifically designed to reduce these barriers and create pathways for highly talented researchers who demonstrate strong potential for success in development economics. Benefits of the Fellowship Successful finalists benefit from several advantages throughout the application and placement process. 1. Endorsement for Highly Competitive Predoctoral Programs The Weiss Fund endorsement provides candidates with a valuable signal of academic potential and research capability. Participating universities take this endorsement into consideration during their selection process. 2. Opportunity to Work with Leading Economists Fellows who secure placement may work directly with globally recognized development economists on cutting-edge research projects. 3. Research and Technical Skill Development Participants may strengthen their: Quantitative analysis skills. Coding and programming abilities. Research methodology knowledge. Data analysis competencies. Academic writing skills. 4. Exposure to Real-World Research Predoctoral positions provide practical experience through: Research project management. Fieldwork exposure. Data collection and analysis. Policy-relevant research activities. Research publication support. 5. Mentorship for Doctoral Applications Participants receive guidance that can significantly improve future Ph.D. applications through: Academic mentorship. Graduate school preparation. Research career advice. Professional development opportunities. 6. Publication and Collaboration Opportunities Fellows may have opportunities to: Collaborate on academic publications. Contribute to high-impact research projects. Potentially co-author research papers. 7. Increased Academic Visibility Finalists and fellowship recipients may be featured on the Weiss Fund website, providing visibility to their academic interests, achievements, and research potential. Eligibility Requirements To be considered for the fellowship, applicants must satisfy the following requirements: Educational Requirements Applicants must possess: A Bachelor s degree or Master s degree from an institution located in a low-income or lower-middle-income country. Alternatively: Applicants who completed secondary education in a low-income or lower-middle-income country but obtained their university education elsewhere may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Academic Requirements Applicants should demonstrate: Strong mathematical abilities. Strong quantitative reasoning skills. Proficiency in written and spoken English. GRE Requirement Applicants are expected to have: A GRE Quantitative score above 160. Candidates who have not yet taken the GRE may still apply under the designated application track and may later be required to complete a similar assessment administered by the Weiss Fund. Preferred Qualifications Competitive candidates may possess one or more of the following qualifications. Academic Background Degrees in fields such as: Economics Mathematics Statistics Physics Engineering Computer Science Actuarial Science Related social science disciplines with strong quantitative foundations Research Experience Preferred applicants may have experience in: Academic research environments. Data analysis projects. Quantitative research. Development economics research. Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs). Technical Skills Experience with statistical and programming software is highly valued, including: Stata R Python Matlab Professional Competencies Strong candidates typically demonstrate: Interest in development economics research. Commitment to continuous learning. Ability to work independently. Strong teamwork skills. Excellent communication abilities. Effective time-management skills. Attention to detail. Ability to thrive in fast-paced environments. GRE Preferences for Advanced Selection Stages During later phases of the selection process, stronger consideration may be given to candidates with: GRE Quantitative score above 168 or 90th percentile. GRE Verbal score of 156 or above (70th percentile). The Weiss Fund will cover GRE examination fees for selected pre-finalists who have not yet completed the test. Fellowship Award Terms Successful applicants may be matched with host institutions following independent evaluation processes conducted by participating universities. Important conditions include: Host institutions will handle visa sponsorship. Host institutions will provide compensation and relevant employment benefits. The Weiss Fund will subsidize part of the hiring costs. Finalists may receive invitations to apply to one or more pre-approved predoctoral positions. Application Tracks Applicants may choose from two application pathways. Track 1: GRE Score Available Applicants who already possess GRE scores can: Apply by July 24, 2026. Be reviewed on a rolling basis. Potentially be considered for placement beginning Fall 2026. If GRE scores do not meet the required threshold, applicants may be asked to retake the examination, with costs covered by the Weiss Fund. Track 2: GRE Score Pending Applicants without GRE scores may: Submit applications by July 24, 2026. Receive additional preparation time. Complete the GRE after initial screening. Final decisions for this track are expected between December 2026 and January 2027. The Weiss Fund will cover GRE fees for eligible pre-finalists. Application Deadline Deadline: July 24, 2026 Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their complete applications before the deadline. Application Process The application process includes the following stages: Submit a complete application by July 24, 2026. Undergo initial review and screening. Receive invitation for further assessment if shortlisted. Complete GRE requirements if necessary. Participate in final selection and placement coordination. Potentially receive invitations to apply for pre-approved predoctoral positions. Applicants should note that placement and visa processing may take several months after selection. Required Documents Applicants must prepare the following: Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV). Academic transcripts. GRE quantitative score (if available). Recommendation letters are not required during the initial application stage but will be requested from candidates who advance further in the selection process. Final Thoughts The Kabir Banerjee Predoctoral Fellowship 2027 represents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring researchers from low and lower-middle-income countries to access world-class mentorship, advanced research training, and highly competitive predoctoral opportunities. Through endorsement from the Weiss Fund and potential placement with leading economists at top universities, successful applicants can significantly strengthen their academic profiles and prepare for future doctoral studies in Economics. For talented individuals seeking to build a career in development economics, this fellowship provides a valuable pathway toward academic excellence and global research impact. title: African Union Junior Program Officer (AfCFTA) Recruitment 2026 in Ghana | Earn Up to US$77,425 Per Year
summary: The African Union (AU) has officially opened applications for the Junior Program Officer (AfCFTA) position at the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat in Accra, Ghana. This exciting international career opportunity is ideal for young professionals seeking to contribute to Africa s economic integration while building a rewarding career within one of the continent s most respected intergovernmental organizations. The position offers competitive remuneration, career development opportunities, exposure to high-level regional programmes, and the chance to work directly on initiatives supporting Africa s largest free trade agreement. If you possess experience in monitoring and evaluation, programme coordination, economics, statistics, development studies, public finance, or related disciplines, this could be your opportunity to join the African Union and contribute to the successful implementation of Agenda 2063. About the African Union The African Union (AU) is Africa s premier continental organization dedicated to promoting unity, peace, sustainable development, economic integration, and prosperity among its member states. Through Agenda 2063, the AU seeks to create: An integrated Africa A prosperous Africa A peaceful Africa A citizen-driven Africa A globally influential Africa The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is one of the flagship projects under Agenda 2063 and represents one of the world s largest free trade areas. Position Overview Position: Junior Program Officer (AfCFTA) Requisition ID: 3020 Location: Accra, Ghana Department: Director Coordination Programmes Reports To: Program Officer Job Grade: P1 Contract Type: Fixed-Term The successful candidate will support programme coordination, implementation, monitoring, and resource mobilization activities that strengthen funding coordination and ensure effective implementation of AfCFTA programmes. Purpose of the Position The Junior Program Officer will assist in coordinating and monitoring resource mobilization initiatives that support programme implementation across the AfCFTA Secretariat. The role focuses on ensuring: Better coordination among programmes. Effective implementation of funding plans. Improved partnerships. Enhanced monitoring. Reduced duplication of efforts. Sustainable programme financing. Key Responsibilities The successful candidate will perform a wide range of responsibilities, including: Programme Coordination Monitor implementation of resource mobilization work plans. Track programme progress and prepare reports. Support implementation of funding strategies. Coordinate programme activities across departments. Resource Mobilization Review existing resource mobilization frameworks. Support continuous improvement of funding strategies. Assist departments in updating resource mobilization plans. Facilitate financing discussions with stakeholders. Monitoring and Evaluation Work closely with Monitoring and Evaluation teams. Ensure implementation follows established standards. Support performance tracking. Promote accountability throughout programme implementation. Coordination and Partnerships Promote information sharing across departments. Identify and reduce duplication of efforts. Strengthen collaboration among programme teams. Maintain productive working relationships with stakeholders. Capacity Building Support capacity development for AU Member States. Assist in organizing structured financing dialogues. Strengthen institutional knowledge on resource mobilization. Additional Duties The officer may also perform other responsibilities assigned by supervisors or the Director. Educational Requirements Applicants must possess a university degree in one of the following fields: Monitoring and Evaluation Economics Statistics Development Studies Demography Public Finance Or another related discipline Professional Experience Candidates must have: At least two (2) years of relevant professional experience. Experience in programme management, monitoring, evaluation, donor coordination, development finance, or public sector programmes will be advantageous. Required Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Excellent written communication skills. Strong verbal communication abilities. Sound planning and organizational skills. Ability to manage uncertainty. Cultural sensitivity. Ability to work across departments and countries. Strong teamwork skills. Good analytical abilities. Leadership Competencies Successful applicants should demonstrate: Strategic insight Developing others Change management Risk management Core Competencies The African Union values candidates who exhibit: Teamwork and collaboration Accountability Compliance with organizational rules Continuous learning Professional ethics Functional Competencies Candidates should possess: Strong influencing and communication skills. Technical job knowledge. Information sharing abilities. Results-oriented mindset. Continuous improvement focus. Contract Duration The appointment will initially be offered on a fixed-term contract of one or two years. The first six months will serve as a probation period. Following successful performance evaluation and subject to funding availability, the contract may be renewed up to two additional times. Salary and Benefits The African Union offers an attractive remuneration package. Annual salary includes: US$77,425.50 for internationally recruited staff. US$59,805.19 for locally recruited staff. These amounts are inclusive of applicable allowances. Language Requirements Applicants must be proficient in at least one of the African Union s official working languages: Arabic English French Kiswahili Portuguese Spanish Knowledge of an additional AU language is considered an added advantage. Equal Opportunity Employer The African Union is committed to equal employment opportunities. Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply. The AU also encourages applications from underrepresented member states to promote balanced continental representation. Required Application Documents Applicants should prepare: A fully completed online application. The mandatory African Union CV template. An African passport. Academic certificates and qualifications. Relevant professional certificates. Failure to use the mandatory AU CV template may affect the application. How to Apply Interested candidates should complete the online application through the African Union Careers Portal. Before applying: Download the official AU CV template. Complete the template accurately. Upload all required supporting documents. Submit the application before the deadline. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted no later than 7 July 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC . Late submissions will not be considered. Apply Here Why You Should Apply This opportunity provides professionals with the chance to: Work with Africa s leading continental organization. Contribute to implementation of the AfCFTA. Build international development experience. Earn a competitive salary. Develop expertise in programme coordination and resource mobilization. Collaborate with governments, development partners, and regional institutions. Advance a meaningful career supporting Africa s economic transformation. title: Nexa Climate and Health Innovation Funding 2026: Up to Transform Local Health Systems Across Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean
summary: Climate change is no longer only an environmental issue—it has become one of the greatest public health challenges of our time. Rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, poor air quality, and the rapid spread of mosquito-borne diseases are placing unprecedented pressure on healthcare systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. To help address these growing challenges, Nexa , a global climate and health innovation initiative, is investing in bold, locally led innovations that enable health systems to anticipate climate-related risks and respond before they become health emergencies. Led by Grand Challenges Canada and the Science for Africa Foundation , together with an international consortium of funding partners, Nexa is now accepting applications for its 2026 Climate and Health Innovation Funding Opportunity . Organizations and innovators from Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean are invited to submit innovative solutions that strengthen healthcare systems and protect vulnerable communities from climate-driven health threats. Application Deadline: July 22, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) / 6:00 p.m. UTC About Nexa Nexa is a global initiative dedicated to accelerating climate and health innovations that improve the resilience of health systems facing increasing climate-related challenges. Rather than applying one-size-fits-all approaches, Nexa prioritizes locally led innovations , recognizing that health workers, researchers, innovators, and humanitarian organizations working directly within affected communities understand their challenges better than anyone else. The initiative focuses on turning climate-risk information into practical health actions that reduce illness and save lives. Nexa is co-led by: Grand Challenges Canada Science for Africa Foundation Working alongside global partners including: Novo Nordisk Foundation Sanofi Foundation Fund for Innovation in Development Global Grand Challenges Network Botswana Innovation Fund NCST Malawi NCST Rwanda Institut Pasteur Dakar South African Medical Research Council Government of Canada Why Climate and Health Innovation Matters Climate change is creating new health emergencies across the world. Approximately 3.6 billion people currently live in regions that are highly vulnerable to climate change. The effects are becoming increasingly severe, including: Expansion of mosquito-borne diseases into new regions. Increased frequency of extreme heat events. Poor air quality affecting millions of people. Greater pressure on already overstretched health systems. Communities that experience the greatest risks include: Pregnant women Children Older adults People living with chronic illnesses Rural and underserved populations Communities with limited healthcare access Without stronger healthcare systems capable of anticipating these risks, millions of people remain vulnerable. Community-Led Innovation Drives Nexa Unlike many global funding initiatives, Nexa s priorities have been shaped directly by frontline professionals. In January 2025, Grand Challenges Canada, the Science for Africa Foundation, the Global Grand Challenges Network, and The Geneva Learning Foundation launched the largest global climate and health survey ever conducted. The survey gathered responses from: More than 6,400 health and humanitarian workers Across 107 low- and middle-income countries These insights helped identify the most urgent climate-health challenges and informed Nexa s investment priorities. Nexa s Areas of Focus Applicants should develop innovations that address one or more of the following priority areas. 1. Climate-Informed Early Warning and Monitoring Systems Nexa seeks innovations that help communities detect climate-related health risks before they escalate into emergencies. Examples include: Early warning systems Climate surveillance platforms Disease forecasting tools Integrated weather and health monitoring systems Risk prediction technologies Community alert systems Solutions should help communities prepare for: Mosquito-borne diseases Extreme heat Air pollution Other climate-driven health risks 2. Climate-Responsive Patient Care Delivery Healthcare providers need better tools to continue delivering quality care during climate emergencies. Nexa supports innovations that improve: Diagnosis Treatment Patient monitoring Continuity of healthcare services Health service delivery during climate stress Projects may focus on: Heat-related illnesses Air pollution-related diseases Malaria Dengue Other mosquito-borne infections What Kind of Innovations Does Nexa Support? Successful proposals may include innovations that: Combine weather data with health information. Improve disease prediction. Support healthcare decision-making. Enable rapid response before disease outbreaks occur. Improve patient care during climate events. Help healthcare systems remain operational during climate stress. Strengthen local healthcare capacity. Reduce climate-related illness and deaths. Nexa particularly encourages practical, scalable, and community-driven solutions. Why This Funding Opportunity Is Important Climate change affects countries differently. Local innovators understand local realities better than external organizations. Nexa therefore prioritizes: Local leadership Community ownership Evidence-based innovation Sustainable health solutions Scalable technologies Strong partnerships The initiative seeks solutions that can create lasting improvements while protecting the most vulnerable populations. Who Should Apply? This funding opportunity is ideal for: Health innovators Universities Research institutions Technology developers Public health organizations NGOs Healthcare providers Social enterprises Climate innovators Humanitarian organizations Applicants should have innovative ideas capable of strengthening healthcare delivery in climate-vulnerable settings. Benefits of the Nexa Climate and Health Innovation Funding Selected innovators will benefit from: Funding to advance innovative climate-health solutions. Opportunities to scale impactful innovations. Global visibility. Collaboration with leading international partners. Access to an international climate-health innovation network. Support for strengthening local healthcare systems. Contribution to improving health outcomes in climate-vulnerable communities. Important Deadline Applications must be submitted by July 22, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. ET (6:00 p.m. UTC). Late applications may not be considered. How to Apply Interested applicants should review the complete funding guidelines and application requirements before submitting their proposals. Applicants are encouraged to prepare early and ensure their projects clearly demonstrate how they will strengthen climate resilience within healthcare systems. Apply Here Final Thoughts Climate change is rapidly transforming global health challenges, demanding innovative and locally driven responses. Through Nexa, innovators across Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean have an opportunity to develop groundbreaking solutions that help healthcare systems anticipate climate risks, protect vulnerable communities, and improve health outcomes for millions of people. Organizations with bold ideas that combine climate science, healthcare, technology, and community engagement are strongly encouraged to apply before the application deadline. title: MFWA 2026 Fully Funded Training Workshop for Journalists in Anglophone West Africa: Apply to Strengthen Your Reporting on Africa–China Trade, Investment and Political Relations
summary: The Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) , in partnership with the Wits Centre for Journalism (WCJ) in South Africa, has officially opened applications for its 2026 Training Workshop on Critical Coverage of Africa–China Trade, Investment and Political Relations . This fully funded capacity-building programme is designed for journalists from selected Anglophone West African countries who are interested in strengthening their reporting on one of the most important global relationships shaping Africa s future. Scheduled to take place in Accra, Ghana , during the last quarter of 2026, the three-day workshop will bring together journalists from across the region to deepen their understanding of the complex political, economic, and social dimensions of Africa–China relations. The organisers aim to equip media professionals with the knowledge, analytical skills, and investigative techniques required to produce balanced, evidence-based, and impactful journalism that serves the public interest. Application Deadline: July 30, 2026 About the MFWA Training Workshop Africa s relationship with China has expanded significantly over the past two decades. China has become one of Africa s largest trading partners and investors, financing major infrastructure projects, supporting industrial development, and increasing cooperation in technology, mining, agriculture, energy, and manufacturing. However, this growing relationship also raises important questions surrounding: Trade and economic partnerships Infrastructure development Development financing Natural resource extraction Labour practices Technology transfer Environmental sustainability Governance and accountability International diplomacy Public policy As geopolitical dynamics continue to evolve, journalists play a critical role in helping citizens understand the opportunities, challenges, and implications of Africa–China cooperation. Reporting on these issues requires more than simply covering official announcements—it demands context, critical analysis, investigative skills, and an understanding of international affairs. Recognising this need, the Media Foundation for West Africa has partnered with the Wits Centre for Journalism to organise this specialised workshop titled Building Capacity to Cover a Complex Story – Africa and China Relations. The programme is funded by the University of the Witwatersrand and is intended to strengthen the reporting capacity of journalists across Anglophone West Africa. What Participants Will Learn The workshop combines subject-matter expertise with practical journalism skills. Participants will gain insights into: Understanding the evolving Africa–China relationship Reporting on international trade and investment Analysing development financing and infrastructure projects Investigating governance and accountability issues Covering natural resource extraction responsibly Reporting on labour, technology, and environmental concerns Applying investigative journalism techniques Producing balanced, accurate, and evidence-based stories Framing stories from African perspectives Understanding global geopolitical shifts and their implications for African countries The training seeks to improve both the depth and quality of reporting on international affairs while encouraging journalism that promotes transparency and informed public debate. Benefits of the Programme Successful applicants will receive comprehensive financial support throughout the programme. The organisers will cover: Return economy-class airfare Accommodation Meals Local transportation within Ghana This ensures participants can focus entirely on learning and networking without worrying about travel expenses. Additional Opportunities After the Training One of the most exciting aspects of this programme is that participation does not end after the workshop. Graduates will have the opportunity to apply for: Reporting grants to produce in-depth investigative stories on Africa–China relations. Funding support for publishing high-quality public-interest journalism. Professional mentorship and continued engagement with experts. Furthermore, three outstanding participants will be selected for a fully funded opportunity to attend the Africa Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC) , scheduled for 10–12 November 2026 in Kenya , where they will present and discuss their reporting projects. Who Can Apply? Applicants must meet all of the following requirements: Be based in one of the eligible Anglophone West African countries. Work in print, radio, television, or digital journalism. Report on one or more of the following beats: Politics Economy Business Trade Development Environment Extractive industries Infrastructure International affairs Be available during September–October 2026. Obtain a formal permission letter from their editor allowing participation. Be capable of producing an in-depth story after completing the workshop. Why Journalists Should Apply Today s journalists increasingly cover stories that extend beyond national borders. International trade agreements, foreign investments, infrastructure financing, and geopolitical developments directly affect local communities and national development. This workshop provides a unique opportunity to strengthen professional skills while learning from leading experts in journalism and international affairs. Participants will also build valuable regional networks with fellow journalists, exchange experiences, and gain practical tools for producing investigative stories that inform public debate and promote accountability. For journalists interested in politics, economics, business reporting, development journalism, or investigative reporting, this programme represents an important opportunity for career development and professional growth. How to Apply Interested journalists should complete the official online application form provided by the Media Foundation for West Africa. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Applicants are encouraged to prepare their applications carefully and ensure they meet every eligibility requirement before submitting. Application Deadline: July 30, 2026. title: Gustave Roussy Prize 2027: €200,000 International Cancer Research Award Now Accepting Applications Worldwide
summary: Researchers making groundbreaking contributions to the fight against cancer now have the opportunity to gain one of the world s most prestigious recognitions in oncology. The Gustave Roussy Prize 2027 has officially opened applications, inviting outstanding cancer researchers from across the globe to compete for an award valued at €200,000 . Established by the Fondation Gustave Roussy , with the support of Laboratoires Pierre Fabre as its founding sponsor, the prize recognizes researchers whose scientific discoveries have significantly transformed cancer diagnosis, treatment, prevention, or patient care. Since its launch in 2025, the award has rapidly become one of the most highly respected international distinctions in oncology research, celebrating scientific excellence and innovations that deliver measurable and lasting benefits for cancer patients worldwide. Application Deadline: August 26, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. CEST About the Gustave Roussy Prize Cancer remains one of the world s leading health challenges, affecting millions of people every year. Continuous scientific research has resulted in remarkable progress in early diagnosis, precision medicine, immunotherapy, targeted therapies, prevention strategies, and patient-centered care. The Gustave Roussy Prize was created to recognize researchers whose discoveries have contributed substantially to these advances. The award was launched in 2025 to commemorate two important milestones: The 150th anniversary of Professor Gustave Roussy s birth. The centenary of the Gustave Roussy Institute. Professor Gustave Roussy is widely recognized as a pioneer in cancer care. In 1921, he established one of the world s first medical consultations dedicated specifically to patients with tumors, laying the foundation for modern comprehensive oncology care. Today, Gustave Roussy is recognized as Europe s leading cancer center and continues to drive innovation through cutting-edge research, education, and patient care. Prize Value The Gustave Roussy Prize carries a total value of €200,000 , making it one of the largest international awards dedicated to cancer research. The funding is divided into two components: €100,000 awarded directly to the laureate for unrestricted personal use. €100,000 allocated to support an innovative oncology research project, enabling continued scientific discovery and future breakthroughs. Purpose of the Award The prize celebrates scientific breakthroughs that have created tangible improvements in cancer care and patient outcomes. Research achievements may relate to: Cancer diagnosis Cancer treatment Cancer prevention Clinical oncology Translational medicine Precision medicine Immunotherapy Biomarker discovery Screening technologies Therapeutic innovation Improved quality of patient care Better understanding of cancer biology The emphasis is not simply on academic achievement but on research that demonstrates measurable clinical impact and has improved the lives of patients. Who Can Apply? Applications are welcomed from researchers worldwide regardless of nationality or institutional affiliation. Eligible candidates include researchers working at: Universities Cancer research institutes Medical schools Hospitals Public research organizations Private research institutions International research centers Applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional scientific excellence and a research record that has significantly advanced oncology. Selection Process Applications will be evaluated by an independent international jury composed of leading experts in oncology and biomedical research. Selection will be based exclusively on: Scientific excellence Originality of discoveries Clinical impact Innovation Long-term contribution to oncology Demonstrated benefits for patients Importantly, evaluations are conducted without regard to discipline, institution, or nationality, ensuring a fair and merit-based selection process. Why This Prize Matters Receiving the Gustave Roussy Prize represents more than financial recognition. It places recipients among the world s leading oncology researchers and highlights discoveries that have changed the landscape of cancer care. The prize also encourages continued innovation by providing dedicated funding for future research projects, ensuring that today s breakthroughs continue generating tomorrow s solutions. With cancer affecting millions globally, supporting transformative research remains essential for improving survival rates, enhancing quality of life, and developing more effective treatments. This award reinforces the importance of scientific collaboration and recognizes researchers whose work creates lasting benefits for humanity. Previous Laureates The prize has already honored internationally renowned scientists. Previous recipients include: 2025: Professor Charles Swanton 2026: Professor Luis Diaz Jr. These researchers were recognized for discoveries that have significantly influenced modern oncology and patient treatment. Award Ceremony The selected laureate for the 2027 edition will receive the prize on February 4, 2027 , during World Cancer Day , highlighting the global importance of cancer research and international collaboration in combating the disease. How to Apply Researchers interested in the Gustave Roussy Prize 2027 should complete the official online application before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to present their most impactful scientific achievements, clearly demonstrate clinical relevance, and provide evidence showing how their discoveries have advanced cancer diagnosis, treatment, prevention, or patient care. Application Deadline: August 26, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. CEST. title: Aspen Institute Michael Cromartie Forum 2026 for Emerging Journalists in the USA: Apply for a Transformative Journalism Experience
summary: The Aspen Institute s Religion Society Program is now accepting applications for the Michael Cromartie Forum 2026 , an exclusive professional development opportunity designed for emerging journalists who want to deepen their understanding of the role religion plays in shaping politics, culture, public policy, and civic life. Taking place in Middleburg, Virginia, USA , from August 30 to September 1, 2026 , the Forum provides an intellectually engaging environment where early-career journalists can interact with experienced reporters, editors, scholars, and thought leaders through meaningful conversations rooted in the Aspen Institute s long-standing tradition of respectful dialogue and critical thinking. The Michael Cromartie Forum is more than a journalism conference—it is an immersive learning experience that equips participants with new perspectives, stronger reporting skills, and valuable professional networks that can influence their careers for years to come. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and are expected to close around July 1, 2026. Early applications are strongly encouraged. About the Michael Cromartie Forum In today s rapidly evolving media landscape, journalists are expected to cover increasingly complex issues that intersect with politics, religion, identity, ethics, democracy, and culture. Religion continues to influence elections, policymaking, international affairs, education, social movements, and community life, making religious literacy an essential skill for modern journalism. Recognizing this need, the Aspen Institute s Religion Society Program established the Michael Cromartie Forum to help emerging journalists better understand how faith and religion influence public life while strengthening their ability to report accurately, fairly, and thoughtfully on these issues. Named in honor of the late Michael Cromartie , a respected advocate for improving religion reporting in mainstream media, the Forum continues his legacy by creating space for journalists to engage with scholars and experienced practitioners in open, nonpartisan dialogue. The program emphasizes curiosity, intellectual humility, and rigorous discussion rather than debate or advocacy. What Participants Can Expect During the three-day Forum, participants will engage in a series of carefully curated discussions, presentations, and interactive sessions covering topics at the intersection of religion and public life. The program brings together: Experienced journalists from leading media organizations. Editors with expertise in religion, politics, and public affairs reporting. Distinguished scholars and researchers. Public intellectuals and subject-matter experts. Fellow emerging journalists from diverse backgrounds. Rather than focusing on breaking news, the Forum encourages participants to examine the deeper historical, cultural, philosophical, and ethical dimensions of current events. This format allows journalists to gain insights that strengthen their long-term reporting and storytelling abilities. Why You Should Apply Participating in the Michael Cromartie Forum offers numerous professional and personal benefits, including: Exposure to leading scholars and experienced journalists. A deeper understanding of religion s influence on politics, society, and culture. Opportunities to improve reporting on complex public issues. Networking with fellow journalists from different media organizations. Participation in thoughtful, nonpartisan discussions. Membership in a growing community of journalism professionals committed to intellectual excellence. Professional growth through meaningful dialogue and collaborative learning. The Forum provides participants with the time and space to think critically about journalism beyond the pressures of daily newsroom deadlines. Who Is the Forum Designed For? The program is primarily intended for emerging journalists between the ages of 22 and 30 , although the organizers clearly state that there are no strict age requirements . Applicants may include: Print journalists. Broadcast journalists. Digital media reporters. Multimedia journalists. Editors early in their careers. Independent journalists. Freelance reporters. Journalism graduates beginning their professional careers. The organizers welcome applicants who demonstrate intellectual curiosity, a commitment to high-quality journalism, and an interest in understanding the role religion plays in contemporary society. Venue and Dates The 2026 Michael Cromartie Forum will take place in: Location: Middleburg, Virginia, USA Dates: August 30 – September 1, 2026 The setting is intentionally designed to encourage focused learning, reflection, relationship-building, and open dialogue among participants. Why Religion Reporting Matters Religion remains one of the most influential forces shaping communities across the world. It affects public policy, elections, education, healthcare, international relations, social justice movements, humanitarian work, and cultural identity. Despite this influence, religion is often misunderstood or underreported in mainstream journalism. The Michael Cromartie Forum seeks to bridge this gap by helping journalists: Improve religious literacy. Better understand diverse faith traditions. Report accurately on religion-related issues. Explore how religious beliefs intersect with politics and public life. Produce more nuanced, balanced, and informed journalism. These skills are increasingly valuable in today s interconnected and multicultural world. Professional Networking Opportunities One of the Forum s greatest strengths is the opportunity to build lasting professional relationships. title: EU-LAC Women’s Political Leadership School 2026: Birregional Training for Women Leaders in Local Politics Across Latin America, the Caribbean, and the European Union
summary: The EU-LAC Foundation has officially launched the EU-LAC Birregional School of Local Political Leadership for Women 2026 , a high-impact leadership development programme designed to strengthen women’s political participation, advocacy skills, and leadership capacity at the local level across Latin America, the Caribbean, and the European Union . This initiative is a strategic space for training, exchange, and networking , bringing together women leaders from different political, community, and social backgrounds. The programme is built on a feminist, intersectional, and human rights-based approach , aiming to empower women to lead democratic, inclusive, and transformative change within their communities. The School combines virtual preparatory sessions with a face-to-face intensive training in Panama , ensuring both accessibility and meaningful intercultural exchange among participants. Objective of the EU-LAC Women’s Political Leadership School The main goal of the programme is to strengthen the capacity of women engaged in territorial and local leadership by providing: Advanced training in political leadership and governance Practical tools for communication, negotiation, and public management Opportunities for intergenerational mentoring Strong birregional networking between Europe, Latin America, and the Caribbean A platform for sharing lived experiences and community-based leadership strategies Through this initiative, the EU-LAC Foundation aims to reinforce women’s leadership in democratic governance and civic participation at the local level . Format of the Leadership School The programme follows a blended learning structure , combining digital and in-person components: Virtual Preparatory Phase Online training modules before the in-person session Introduction to leadership concepts, tools, and frameworks Networking and group discussions across regions In-Person Intensive Session Held in Panama (October 2026) High-level training workshops Interactive leadership sessions Cross-regional experience sharing Networking with women leaders from EU-LAC regions Follow-Up Activities Continued engagement through networks Participation in the EU-LAC WIN Network Knowledge sharing and leadership development continuation Profile of Applicants The programme is designed for two main categories of women leaders: Young Women Leaders Applicants should demonstrate: Membership in a network, organisation, programme, or institution Interest in territorial political leadership (formal or informal) Engagement in civic participation, feminist groups, or community initiatives Motivation to strengthen leadership skills and collaborate with women across regions Interest in EU-LAC relations, gender equality, or local development Willingness to join or engage with the EU-LAC WIN Network Senior Women Leaders Applicants should demonstrate: Strong and consolidated leadership experience in political or community spaces Proven impact in local governance, municipalities, councils, or civil society initiatives Membership in a recognised institution, network, or organisation Capacity to mentor and support younger women leaders Commitment to feminist and intersectional leadership principles Active contribution to community transformation and policy influence Required Application Documents All applications must be submitted in English or Spanish and include: Signed application form Proof of membership in a network, organisation, or institution Letter of endorsement or support from a relevant institution or organisation and personal development opportunities, including: High-level leadership training in political and civic engagement Strengthening negotiation, communication, and governance skills Participation in a title: Postdoctoral Research Fellowship (PDRF) Opportunities at the University of Johannesburg: Global Excellence and Societal Impact (GES 4.0) Initiative
summary: The University of Johannesburg (UJ) , through its Global Excellence and Stature (GES 4.0) Social Impact Initiative , is inviting applications from highly qualified and early-career researchers for its Postdoctoral Research Fellowship (PDRF) programme . This prestigious fellowship is designed to attract outstanding postdoctoral researchers who can contribute meaningfully to high-impact research, innovation, interdisciplinarity, and societal transformation. This fellowship is part of UJ’s long-term strategic vision (UJ Strategic Plan 2035), which positions the university as a globally competitive research institution addressing critical challenges facing society, the environment, governance systems, and technological transformation. The programme seeks exceptional scholars who demonstrate strong academic excellence, innovative thinking, and a commitment to solving real-world problems aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Overview of the Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Programme The PDRF at the University of Johannesburg is a full-time research fellowship that supports emerging scholars in conducting advanced research across priority thematic areas. Fellows will be embedded within recognized research entities, centres, institutes, SARChI Chairs, or strategic research programmes at UJ. This ensures that successful applicants are fully integrated into a vibrant academic environment that promotes collaboration, mentorship, and interdisciplinary research output. Priority Research Areas Applicants must align their research proposals with one or more of the following thematic areas: Sustainability, Climate Change, and Environmental Governance (ESG) Water, Energy, Food, and Environmental Security Public Health and Mental Health Systems Education and Child Development Migration, Social Justice, and Inequality Governance, Democracy, and Public Policy African Futures and Pan-African Thought Advanced Manufacturing and Industry 4.0 Smart Systems and Data Science Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Societal Impact Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation These areas reflect UJ’s commitment to addressing global and African developmental challenges through cutting-edge research. Fellowship Conditions and Benefits Successful applicants will receive a highly competitive research support package designed to enable impactful academic work. Key Benefits Include: Competitive tax-free stipend of R250,000 per year Initial appointment for 12 months , renewable based on performance and funding availability Access to world-class UJ research infrastructure Integration into national and international research networks Mentorship from senior academics and research leaders Opportunities for professional development and academic growth The fellowship does not include relocation or accommodation support. Expectations of Postdoctoral Fellows Fellows are expected to contribute actively to the academic and research environment at UJ. Responsibilities include: Participation in capacity-building and research activities Co-supervision of postgraduate students Development of research funding proposals Presentation of research findings at conferences, seminars, and webinars Publishing research in peer-reviewed journals, books, or scholarly platforms Active participation in collaborative research networks Contribution to additional research initiatives aligned with host entities This ensures fellows not only conduct research but also contribute to the broader academic ecosystem. Eligibility and Minimum Requirements Applicants must meet the following criteria: Academic Requirements Hold a PhD or equivalent doctoral qualification (NQF Level 10) PhD must have been obtained within the last five years Must not have held a previous postdoctoral fellowship at the host discipline (preferred condition) Research Competencies Strong scholarly and research performance record Excellent academic writing and communication skills Proven research output or publications Other Requirements Ability to work full-time for the duration of the fellowship Demonstrated interest in interdisciplinary research and societal impact Preference for candidates with international collaboration experience Application Requirements Applicants must submit a complete application package including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) Certified copies of academic qualifications Copy of doctoral thesis abstract Motivation letter outlining suitability for the fellowship Research proposal (3–5 pages) aligned to a host research area Two academic reference letters Evidence of publications or research outputs Application Process Applications must be submitted electronically to the designated application platform or contact person provided by the university. For enquiries: Contact: Mr Thabiso Masango Email: thabisom@uj.ac.za Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Value of the Fellowship The PDRF at UJ is not only a financial opportunity but also a career-defining academic experience. It provides: High-level research exposure in a globally recognized institution Access to interdisciplinary academic networks Opportunities to shape policy-relevant and impactful research Strong foundation for future academic or research leadership roles Application Deadline 15 July 2026 Conclusion The University of Johannesburg Postdoctoral Research Fellowship under the GES 4.0 Initiative represents one of the most competitive research opportunities in Africa. It is designed for emerging scholars who are ready to contribute to global knowledge production while addressing pressing societal challenges. Applicants with strong academic backgrounds, innovative research ideas, and interdisciplinary interests are strongly encouraged to apply. title: British Council TNE Grants with India 2026–27: £30,000 Funding for UK–India Higher Education Partnerships in Emerging Technologies
summary: The British Council has officially launched the highly anticipated TNE Grants with India 2026–27 under the Going Global Partnerships initiative, offering an exciting opportunity for UK and Indian higher education institutions to collaborate on innovative transnational education (TNE) programmes in cutting-edge disciplines. This international grant programme is designed to strengthen UK–India higher education collaboration by supporting the development and launch of new TNE courses and degree programmes in future-focused sectors that are shaping the global economy. With funding of up to £30,000 available per project, the initiative aims to encourage interdisciplinary academic innovation, academia-industry engagement, and workforce readiness in emerging technologies and scientific fields. What Are the TNE Grants with India 2026–27? The TNE Grants with India programme supports collaborative partnerships between UK universities, Indian higher education institutions, and industry partners to co-develop impactful educational programmes aligned with future industry demands. The grants are part of the British Council’s broader Going Global Partnerships programme, which promotes international collaboration in higher education, skills, and research. The initiative focuses specifically on developing innovative transnational education models that can enhance student mobility, academic excellence, employability, and cross-border institutional partnerships. Funding Details Selected partnerships will receive: Grant amount: £30,000 Project duration: 17 months Project start date: 30 September 2026 The funding is intended to support the planning, development, and launch of new TNE courses and academic programmes in strategic emerging areas. Priority Areas of Focus Applications are invited for projects connected to the following high-priority disciplines and innovation sectors: 1. AI and Machine Learning and Quantum Computing Projects focused on artificial intelligence, advanced machine learning systems, data science, quantum technologies, and computational innovation. 2. Genomics and Proteomics CRISPR-Based Therapies Programmes exploring genomics, biotechnology, genetic engineering, precision medicine, and CRISPR therapeutic applications. 3. Sustainable Energy and Climate Change Technology Courses addressing renewable energy, sustainability, green transition technologies, climate adaptation, and environmental resilience. 4. Synthetic Biology and Neurotechnology Innovative interdisciplinary programmes combining biology, neuroscience, engineering, and advanced medical technologies. 5. Circular Economy-Based Research Initiatives supporting sustainability, waste reduction, resource efficiency, recycling systems, and circular economic models. 6. Advanced Engineering, Robotics, and Space Technologies Programmes connected to robotics, aerospace innovation, automation, advanced manufacturing, and engineering technologies. 7. Semiconductor Technologies Projects focusing on semiconductor manufacturing, chip technologies, electronics innovation, and advanced computing infrastructure. 8. Critical Minerals, Geological and Earth Sciences Academic programmes supporting research and workforce development in geological sciences, mineral resources, and earth systems. Why This Opportunity Matters The TNE Grants with India 2026–27 represent a major step forward in strengthening educational and innovation ties between the UK and India. The programme aims to: Build sustainable UK–India higher education partnerships Support industry-relevant academic programmes Encourage interdisciplinary innovation Create opportunities for students in emerging sectors Enhance graduate employability Strengthen academia-industry collaboration Develop future-ready talent pipelines By encouraging collaboration between universities and industry, the grants aim to ensure that newly developed programmes remain relevant to rapidly evolving global workforce demands. Academia-Industry Collaboration Requirement One of the defining features of this grant programme is its strong emphasis on industry engagement. Applications must involve a three-way partnership consisting of: One or more UK higher education institutions One or more Indian higher education institutions Industry partners from either the UK or India Industry partners may include: Startups Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) Large corporations Commercial organizations operating legally within their jurisdictions This collaboration model is intended to ensure that TNE programmes are practical, industry-informed, and aligned with real-world technological and economic needs. Who Can Apply? UK Institutions Eligible UK applicants include: Higher education providers with degree-awarding powers Indian Institutions Eligible Indian institutions include: Government-funded higher education institutions Privately funded recognized higher education institutions Universities recognized by UGC, AICTE, or other competent Indian authorities Institutes of Eminence Institutes of National Importance Industry Partners Eligible industry collaborators include: Commercial organizations Micro enterprises Small and medium enterprises Large companies compliant with local laws Important Dates Applicants should carefully note the following deadlines: Clarification deadline: 28 July 2026 Application submission deadline: 5 August 2026 Submission time: 11:59 a.m. BST Project commencement: 30 September 2026 Late submissions may not be accepted. Final Thoughts The British Council TNE Grants with India 2026–27 provide a valuable platform for universities and industry leaders to shape the future of global higher education through innovation-driven collaboration. As emerging technologies continue to redefine industries worldwide, this initiative offers institutions a chance to create globally relevant academic programmes that address future workforce challenges while strengthening UK–India educational ties. Institutions interested in transnational education, interdisciplinary innovation, and international academic partnerships should strongly consider applying before the deadline. title: WIPO City of Innovation Awards 2026: Global Call for Cities Driving Innovation and Creativity
summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) has officially opened applications for the prestigious WIPO City of Innovation Awards 2026, a newly launched global initiative designed to recognize visionary cities committed to fostering innovation, creativity, and community-driven transformation. Cities across all 194 WIPO Member States are invited to submit bold pledges demonstrating how they will champion innovation and creativity over a 12-month period. Unlike traditional awards that only celebrate past achievements, the WIPO City of Innovation Awards focus on future-oriented commitments and transformative ideas capable of shaping sustainable and inclusive urban development. The deadline to apply is June 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (CEST). About the WIPO City of Innovation Awards The WIPO City of Innovation Awards were launched for the first time in 2026 by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), the United Nations agency responsible for promoting innovation and creativity through intellectual property systems worldwide. This award program seeks to identify and recognize cities that are actively building environments where creativity, innovation, entrepreneurship, technology, and citizen participation can thrive. The initiative acknowledges the important role city leaders play in shaping innovative urban ecosystems and empowering local communities to contribute to social, economic, and cultural progress. The award is open to: Cities of all sizes Municipal governments Urban innovation ecosystems Creative and technology-driven communities Innovation-focused city administrations WIPO encourages mayors, governors, local government authorities, innovators, startups, artists, and community organizations to collaborate in developing strong city pledges capable of inspiring long-term transformation. Why the WIPO City of Innovation Awards Matter Cities are increasingly becoming centers of technological advancement, entrepreneurship, sustainability, cultural development, and creative expression. Through this award, WIPO aims to spotlight municipalities that are taking bold steps toward: Encouraging innovation-driven economic growth Empowering local creators and entrepreneurs Building sustainable urban futures Enhancing citizen participation Creating inclusive innovation ecosystems Promoting intellectual property awareness Strengthening local creative industries The award also serves as an international platform for sharing best practices and inspiring municipalities around the world to invest in innovation-led urban development. What Winning Cities Receive Selected cities will receive a comprehensive international recognition package designed to maximize visibility and showcase their innovation commitments globally. 1. Official WIPO Trophy Winning cities will receive a specially crafted symbolic WIPO City of Innovation trophy recognizing their commitment to urban transformation and creative leadership. 2. Global Recognition and International Visibility Award-winning cities will gain: International exposure through WIPO platforms Recognition during the official award ceremony in Geneva Networking opportunities with global policymakers Connections with innovation leaders and the international intellectual property community 3. Sponsored International Participation Travel expenses for one official city representative will be fully covered, enabling participation in: The official award ceremony High-level international networking events Meetings with mayors and diplomatic representatives from around the world 4. Professional Media and Storytelling Support WIPO’s professional media team will collaborate with winning cities to: Document innovation initiatives Showcase progress on city pledges Produce professional visual and media content Feature successful projects on selected WIPO platforms This provides cities with valuable international promotional exposure. 5. Permanent City Recognition Winning cities will receive the exclusive right to display the official commemorative WIPO City of Innovation plaque within their municipality. WIPO will provide the design specifications while cities maintain full control over installation and placement. Eligibility Criteria The WIPO City of Innovation Awards are open to cities located within WIPO Member States. Key eligibility conditions include: Applications are open to cities across all 194 WIPO Member States A maximum of three cities per country may apply Cities of all population sizes are encouraged to participate Applications must include a 12-month innovation and creativity pledge Applications must be approved and signed by an authorized city representative Authorized signatories may include: Mayors Governors Heads of city administrations Other authorized municipal officials Required Innovation Pledge Applicants must submit a clear and ambitious pledge describing how their city will promote innovation and creativity over the next 12 months. The pledge should explain: The city’s innovation vision Planned initiatives and programs Expected community impact Strategies for citizen engagement Long-term sustainability plans How innovation and creativity will be nurtured locally WIPO will evaluate the clarity, feasibility, originality, and long-term impact potential of each pledge. Application Process for the WIPO City of Innovation Awards 2026 Cities interested in applying must follow a structured multi-step application process. Step 1: Complete the Online Application Form Applicants must complete the official online application form in one of the six United Nations languages: English Arabic Chinese French Russian Spanish Step 2: Obtain Official Authorization The application form must be signed by a duly authorized city representative. Step 3: Submit Through Official Diplomatic Channels A PDF copy of the completed application form must be submitted to WIPO through: The country’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations Office at Geneva, or The Ministry of Foreign Affairs if no Permanent Mission exists Important Deadline Application Deadline: June 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (CEST) Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit early to allow adequate processing time through diplomatic channels. WIPO City of Innovation Awards Timeline Applications Open April 1, 2026 Applications Close June 30, 2026 Announcement of Finalists September 21, 2026 An independent international jury panel will evaluate shortlisted applications based on the official selection criteria. Award Ceremony October 12, 2026 The winners will be announced during an official ceremony at WIPO headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, alongside the Sixth Meeting of the UN Forum of Mayors. Up to three cities may be selected each year. Understanding the WIPO City of Innovation Trophy The WIPO City of Innovation trophy symbolizes the transformative power of cities through the elements of fire and water. According to WIPO: Fire represents technological ingenuity and the spark of innovation Water symbolizes creativity’s ability to adapt, overcome barriers, and shape communities over time The natural stone base reflects the enduring strength and resilience of cities Together, these elements embody the fusion of innovation, creativity, transformation, and sustainable urban progress. Why Cities Should Apply Participating in the WIPO City of Innovation Awards offers cities a rare opportunity to: Gain global visibility Showcase innovation leadership Build international partnerships Attract investment and collaboration Strengthen local creative ecosystems Inspire civic participation Promote sustainable urban growth The award also provides long-term reputational benefits by positioning cities as international leaders in innovation and creativity. About WIPO The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations dedicated to building a balanced and effective global intellectual property ecosystem. WIPO works to: Promote innovation worldwide Support creativity and entrepreneurship Encourage sustainable development Strengthen intellectual property systems internationally Through initiatives like the WIPO City of Innovation Awards, the organization seeks to encourage local governments to become catalysts for creative and technological transformation. title: IWMF Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism 2026: Up to $5,000 Grant for Women and Nonbinary Journalists Worldwide
summary: The International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF) has officially opened applications for the prestigious Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism 2026, an important funding opportunity designed to support compelling, impactful, and deeply human-centered storytelling from women and nonbinary journalists around the world. This grant program honors the legacy of Kari Howard, an editor celebrated for championing stories that captured the emotional depth of everyday life while illuminating major social issues through powerful narrative journalism. The fund aims to empower journalists who are passionate about telling meaningful stories that connect audiences with real people, communities, and experiences. For journalists seeking financial support to pursue ambitious reporting projects, this opportunity provides funding of up to $5,000 to help bring important stories to life. About the Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism The Kari Howard Fund was established by Kari Howard’s family and friends in partnership with the International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF). The initiative reflects Kari Howard’s dedication to narrative journalism that combines investigative depth with emotional resonance. The grant supports print journalists and multimedia teams producing narrative-driven reporting projects published in English anywhere in the world. Projects funded through this program are expected to focus on immersive storytelling, meaningful reporting, and journalism that highlights critical issues through personal and compelling narratives. Grant Benefits Selected applicants will receive several important benefits, including: Grants averaging approximately $5,000 Financial support for reporting and production expenses International recognition through the IWMF network Opportunity to pursue impactful narrative journalism projects Support for both independent journalists and collaborative multimedia teams Increased visibility for underreported or deeply human-centered stories Who Can Apply? The opportunity is specifically designed for: Women journalists Nonbinary journalists Gender nonconforming journalists Applicants may apply as: Freelance journalists Staff journalists Print journalists leading multimedia reporting teams Eligibility Requirements To qualify for the Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism 2026, applicants must meet the following criteria: Professional Experience Applicants must have: At least three (3) years of professional journalism experience Journalism as their primary profession Please note that internships do not count toward the required professional experience. Journalism Focus Applicants must be: Print journalists Or print journalists leading a multi-format or multimedia team Any multimedia components must support and supplement the primary print journalism project. Language Requirement Applicants must: Apply in English Publish their reporting project in English Stories may be published digitally and do not necessarily need to appear in traditional newspapers or magazines. Editorial Support Applicants must either: Demonstrate proof of interest from an editor, or Show a strong publication history in prominent media outlets Eligible Reporting Projects The IWMF welcomes narrative journalism projects covering important issues from anywhere in the world. Projects may include: Social justice reporting Human rights stories Investigative narratives Community-centered storytelling Cultural reporting Gender-focused reporting Political or humanitarian issues Environmental storytelling Longform journalism projects The focus should be on strong storytelling that creates emotional connection while addressing important issues. Project Timeline Successful applicants must: Complete all reporting and publication activities within six months of receiving the grant award Applicants should therefore submit realistic timelines and achievable reporting plans in their proposals. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the IWMF Kari Howard Fund for Narrative Journalism 2026 is: July 12, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST Applicants are expected to receive decisions by early September 2026. Why This Opportunity Matters Narrative journalism remains one of the most powerful forms of storytelling in modern media. Through immersive reporting and emotionally engaging narratives, journalists can help audiences better understand complex issues affecting people worldwide. The Kari Howard Fund continues to preserve and promote this important journalistic tradition by supporting reporters dedicated to telling stories with empathy, depth, and authenticity. For women and nonbinary journalists looking to pursue meaningful reporting projects, this grant offers not only financial support but also recognition from one of the world’s leading organizations supporting women in media. Learn More Apply Interested applicants should prepare: A strong narrative journalism project proposal Evidence of professional journalism experience Proof of editorial interest or publication history A realistic reporting and publication timeline Any required supplementary application materials Applicants are encouraged to apply early to avoid last-minute technical issues.
