title: Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge 2026: Win an All-Expenses-Paid Trip to Oxford and Transform Your Climate Innovation into Global Impact
summary: Are you a high school student with a groundbreaking climate technology idea? Or are you a teacher passionate about inspiring the next generation of environmental innovators? The Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge 2026 presents an extraordinary opportunity for students and educators from around the world to showcase innovative, technology-driven solutions to one of humanity s greatest challenges—climate change. Organized by Saïd Business School, University of Oxford , this prestigious global competition invites high school student teams and teachers to develop practical, creative, and impactful solutions that address pressing climate issues. Participants will have the opportunity to compete on an international stage, gain recognition from one of the world s leading universities, and win incredible all-expenses-paid prizes, including a trip to Oxford. Best of all, participation is completely free . About the Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge 2026 Climate change continues to affect every country and community across the globe. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, biodiversity loss, food insecurity, water scarcity, and pollution are becoming increasingly urgent challenges that require innovative solutions. The Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge was created to empower young people and educators to use technology, creativity, and problem-solving skills to develop practical solutions that can create real environmental impact. The competition also provides an international platform where participants can present their ideas, collaborate with like-minded innovators, and engage with academics, practitioners, and global experts. In the previous edition, the competition attracted more than 1,600 entries from 75 countries , demonstrating its global reach and reputation. Why You Should Apply Participating in the Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge offers far more than the opportunity to win prizes. Participants will benefit from: Free entry with no application fee. Opportunity to compete on a global stage. International recognition from the University of Oxford. Opportunities to develop technology-driven climate solutions. Exposure to leading academics and climate experts. Networking with students, teachers, and innovators worldwide. Strengthened research, teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills. A certificate of participation for all approved submissions. The chance to present innovative ideas at Oxford. Competition Themes Participants are encouraged to develop solutions that use technology to address climate-related challenges. Possible focus areas include: Air pollution Extreme weather Food security Biodiversity conservation Water scarcity Other climate-related challenges affecting local, national, or global communities Projects should demonstrate how technology can be used to monitor, adapt to, or solve climate-related problems. Student Team Competition Student teams are invited to submit innovative climate technology ideas that demonstrate creativity, feasibility, and real-world impact. Team Requirements Entries must: Be submitted by teams of 3 to 5 students . Include students aged 15 to 18 years . Individual entries are not accepted . Teams may come from: The same school. Different schools. The same country. Different countries or regions. Student Submission Requirements Each student team must submit: A 10-page PowerPoint presentation , saved as a PDF (preferably under 10 MB). A video presentation of up to three minutes . A completed parental or guardian consent form for each participating student. The presentation should clearly explain: The problem being addressed. The inspiration behind the idea. Teacher Competition Teachers are invited to create lesson plans that inspire students to understand climate change and explore innovative technological solutions. Outstanding Prizes The Oxford Saïd Global Climate Tech Challenge offers exceptional rewards for both students and teachers. Student Grand Prize The winning student team will receive: A full scholarship to the Future Climate Tech Innovators Summer School 2027 in Oxford. An all-expenses-paid experience. An all-expenses-paid visit to Oxford. Finalist Awards All shortlisted student teams and teachers will receive: An all-expenses-paid trip to Oxford . The opportunity to present their ideas during the global finals. Travel and accommodation fully covered. Participation Certificates Every student and teacher whose submission is approved will receive an official Certificate of Participation from Saïd Business School, University of Oxford. Judging Criteria Student Teams Student entries will be evaluated based on: Problem identification. Research and analysis. Innovation and creativity. Feasibility and practicality. Scalability. Quality of presentation. Teamwork and collaboration. Ethical considerations. Sustainability and long-term impact. Overall professionalism and commitment. Teachers Teacher submissions will be assessed according to: Educational impact. Curriculum alignment. Innovation and creativity. Clarity and organization. Student engagement. Assessment methods. Technology integration. Ethical considerations. Practicality and replicability. Overall quality. Research Support Participants are encouraged to strengthen their submissions through high-quality research. The competition s media and knowledge partner, the Financial Times , provides: Climate Capital resources. Climate technology explainers. Trusted journalism. Expert climate analysis. Resources on emerging technologies such as direct air capture, grid-scale batteries, and heat pumps. title: Young Leaders Fellowship 2026 for Emerging Changemakers from the Global South: Fully Funded Leadership Development Opportunity
summary: Applications are now open for the Young Leaders Fellowship 2026, a prestigious one-year leadership development program designed to support young leaders from the Global South who are actively working to prevent violence against children in and through schools. Organized by the Coalition for Good Schools in partnership with Raising Voices, this fellowship seeks to strengthen the next generation of leaders who are committed to creating safer, more inclusive, and violence-free learning environments for children worldwide. The fellowship recognizes that violence in schools remains one of the most significant barriers to education, child development, and well-being. Across many countries, children continue to experience various forms of violence, including bullying, corporal punishment, sexual violence, and emotional abuse. Through this fellowship, participants will gain the leadership skills, confidence, networks, and exposure necessary to drive meaningful change within their communities and influence global conversations on child protection and school safety. About the Young Leaders Fellowship The Young Leaders Fellowship is a year-long program specifically designed for young individuals who are passionate about ending violence against children in educational settings. The fellowship brings together a cohort of 8–10 emerging leaders from across the Global South, creating a collaborative space where participants can learn from one another, share experiences, and strengthen their impact. Rather than focusing solely on technical knowledge, the fellowship emphasizes leadership transformation. Fellows are encouraged to reflect on their leadership journey, strengthen their confidence, and develop the skills required to become influential voices in the field of violence prevention and child protection. The program is built on the belief that effective leadership begins with personal growth. Participants will engage in meaningful discussions, peer learning opportunities, coaching sessions, and exposure to global experts who have dedicated their careers to advancing children’s rights and creating safe schools. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will receive a wide range of benefits aimed at supporting both their personal leadership development and the growth of their initiatives. Leadership Development Participants will engage in regular leadership-focused conversations that encourage self-reflection and personal growth. These sessions are designed to help fellows understand their strengths, navigate challenges, and become more effective leaders within their organizations and communities. Increased Global Visibility One of the fellowship’s major advantages is the opportunity to gain recognition as a global voice in the field of school-based violence prevention. Fellows will have opportunities to participate in policy discussions, expert seminars, conferences, and thought leadership activities that influence the future direction of the sector. Access to Expert Coaching Fellows will receive coaching and mentorship from experienced practitioners who have worked extensively in violence prevention, child protection, education reform, and leadership development. Participants will analyze their projects, identify areas for improvement, and develop strategies for long-term sustainability and impact. Continuous Learning Opportunities The fellowship provides ongoing educational programming that connects practical work with global evidence and research. Fellows will learn from academics, government leaders, civil society experts, and practitioners working in child protection and education. Training topics may include: Pitching and communication Compliance and governance Recruitment and personnel management Program design and implementation Monitoring and evaluation Leadership and organizational growth Field Exposure and Networking Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the global ecosystem working to prevent violence against children. Through networking events and guided discussions, fellows will build valuable relationships with practitioners, researchers, policymakers, and funders from around the world. In-Person Convening During the fellowship year, all fellows will participate in one in-person gathering. This convening will provide opportunities for deeper collaboration, networking, and collective learning among cohort members. Who Should Apply? The fellowship welcomes applications from young leaders who are already involved in efforts to prevent violence against children in schools or educational settings. Applicants may be: Founders of non-profit organizations Staff members of NGOs Community organizers Social entrepreneurs Education advocates Government-affiliated practitioners Leaders of school-based initiatives Importantly, initiatives do not need to be large or highly established. Early-stage ideas and emerging projects are also encouraged, provided applicants demonstrate commitment and clarity of purpose. Eligibility Criteria To qualify for the Young Leaders Fellowship, applicants must: Be between 18 and 35 years old at the time of application. Be based in and actively working in a Global South country. Be leading or significantly contributing to an initiative focused on preventing violence against children in and through schools. Be able to fully participate in English. Be willing to engage in virtual sessions conducted across different time zones. Be available to attend the fellowship’s in-person convening. Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on several key factors: Demonstrated Commitment Applicants should show sustained engagement with issues related to violence prevention, child protection, and safe learning environments. Leadership Potential The selection committee seeks individuals who demonstrate strong leadership qualities and a clear vision for creating change. Ability to Influence the Field Candidates should have the capacity or potential to contribute meaningfully to local, regional, and global conversations about preventing violence in schools. Openness to Learning Successful applicants will be curious, collaborative, and willing to learn from peers working in diverse cultural and geographic contexts. The fellowship will also prioritize equity in geography and gender representation when selecting the final cohort. About the Organizers The Young Leaders Fellowship is powered by Raising Voices and the Coalition for Good Schools. Raising Voices is a Uganda-based organization widely recognized for its groundbreaking work in violence prevention. It is particularly known for developing the Good School Toolkit and the SASA! methodology, both of which have influenced violence prevention initiatives across multiple countries. The Coalition for Good Schools is a growing global network of practitioners, researchers, advocates, and funders dedicated to ensuring that every child has access to a safe, inclusive, and violence-free educational environment. Together, these organizations bring decades of experience, evidence-based knowledge, and extensive global networks to support the next generation of leaders. How to Apply Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official fellowship application page provided by the Coalition for Good Schools. Aspiring leaders who are passionate about creating safer schools and protecting children from violence are strongly encouraged to apply before the deadline. title: Smithsonian Hirshhorn Museum Internship 2026 in Washington, DC | Paid Museum & Archives Opportunity for International Students
summary: The Smithsonian Institution’s Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden has officially opened applications for its highly sought-after Exhibition History Cataloging Internship 2026 in Washington, DC. The internship specifically focuses on exhibition history cataloging and database management using TMS (The Museum System), a professional museum collections database widely used across museums and cultural institutions. Database Documentation Participants will learn how museums organize and maintain historical records using professional cataloging software and archival standards. 3. title: The British Library Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme 2026–2027 | Fully Funded Postdoctoral Fellowship Opportunities in the UK
summary: Applications Open for Two Prestigious British Library Research Fellowships The British Library has officially launched applications for the highly anticipated Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme 2026–2027, offering two funded fellowship opportunities for postdoctoral early-career researchers who are passionate about cultural heritage, archives, artificial intelligence, digital discovery, and historical collections. With applications closing on 15 July 2026 , this fellowship programme provides researchers with a unique opportunity to work directly with one of the world’s most important research libraries while collaborating with expert curators, archivists, and specialist research teams. The 12-month fellowship programme is designed to bridge the gap between doctoral study and long-term professional research careers by equipping fellows with advanced practical, interdisciplinary, and future-focused skills within the cultural and heritage sector. The fellowship will officially begin from 1 September 2026 , with part-time arrangements potentially extending the fellowship duration. About the Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme The Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme was established through a generous donation from Joanna and Graham Barker to support postdoctoral researchers at a critical stage in their academic and professional journey. The initiative focuses on helping early-career researchers gain: Practical institutional experience Research leadership skills Project management exposure Interdisciplinary collaboration opportunities Cultural heritage sector expertise Professional mentoring and development Access to world-class archival collections The British Library aims to create a structured pathway for emerging researchers to thrive within the rapidly evolving knowledge economy and research landscape. This fellowship particularly addresses the significant funding gap faced by postdoctoral researchers across academia and the cultural sector. Fellowship Research Themes for 2026 Applicants are invited to co-design a research project with the British Library based on one of the following two specialist themes. 1. Colonial Legal Deposit and the British Library Newspaper Collection This fellowship is based within the: News Moving Image Department Sound Vision Teams Research Focus The fellowship explores the historical and contemporary implications of colonial legal deposit systems and their relationship with newspaper collections preserved by the British Library. Potential areas of exploration may include: Colonial-era newspaper acquisition systems Historical legal deposit practices Representation and preservation of colonial narratives Media archives and empire studies Accessibility of historical newspaper collections Decolonisation of archival practices Historical metadata and discoverability Newspaper preservation and interpretation Researchers interested in: Media history Colonial studies Digital archives Historical collections Cultural memory Information preservation may find this theme especially relevant. 2. Local Large Language Models for Personal Digital Archives This fellowship is based within: Contemporary British and Irish Archives and Manuscripts Research Focus The second fellowship investigates how Local Large Language Models (LLMs) can improve the discovery, accessibility, interpretation, and management of personal digital archives. The project aligns with the growing importance of artificial intelligence in archives and cultural heritage institutions. Possible research areas include: Ethical AI implementation in archives Local LLM development AI-powered archival discovery tools Digital preservation Metadata enhancement Privacy-aware AI systems Personal digital archive accessibility Human-centered archival technologies Machine learning for cultural heritage collections This opportunity is ideal for researchers working in: Artificial Intelligence Digital Humanities Archival Science Computational Humanities Library and Information Science Machine Learning Cultural Informatics Digital Preservation Fellowship Benefits and Opportunities Selected fellows will receive an extensive range of professional and research benefits throughout the programme. Key Fellowship Advantages 1. Fully Funded Research Opportunity Participants will undertake a funded 12-month fellowship embedded within the British Library. 2. Collaboration with Leading Experts Fellows will work closely with: Curators Archivists Research specialists Digital humanities professionals Cultural heritage experts 3. Access to World-Class Collections Researchers will gain privileged access to: British Library archival collections Newspaper repositories Manuscripts Digital archives Cultural heritage datasets 4. Professional Development The fellowship includes: Research training Project management experience Leadership development Interdisciplinary collaboration Institutional research exposure 5. Career Advancement The scheme is specifically designed to strengthen the long-term career prospects of postdoctoral researchers across academia and the GLAM sector. Why This Fellowship Matters The British Library highlights that postdoctoral researchers often face limited funding opportunities after completing their PhDs. Research studies show that career precarity disproportionately affects: Women researchers Researchers of colour Researchers with disabilities First-generation academics Researchers with caring responsibilities This fellowship directly addresses those challenges by creating inclusive and sustainable research pathways. Main Objectives of the Fellowship Scheme The programme aims to: Build upon the success of collaborative doctoral programmes Support the transition toward independent research careers Expand opportunities in the cultural and heritage sector Strengthen interdisciplinary research practices Enhance discoverability and interpretation of collections Promote equality, diversity, and inclusion in research Generate impactful institutional knowledge Improve public engagement with cultural collections Fellowship Duration Duration: 12 months Start Date: 1 September 2026 Flexible part-time arrangements may extend the duration Eligibility Criteria To apply for the British Library Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme, applicants must meet all of the following requirements: Mandatory Requirements Applicants must: Hold a doctorate in a relevant subject OR Possess equivalent professional experience and skills Applicants must also: Demonstrate commitment to working with the cultural and heritage sector Be based in the UK Be eligible to work in the UK for the full fellowship duration Self-identify as an early-career postdoctoral researcher according to AHRC guidance Important PhD Completion Requirement Applicants who have: Passed their viva with minor corrections before the deadline are eligible However: Applicants requiring major corrections that extend beyond the application deadline are not eligible. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Commitment The British Library strongly promotes inclusive talent development and equitable research opportunities across: Galleries Libraries Archives Museums (GLAM sector) The fellowship prioritises accessibility, diversity, and broad participation in cultural heritage research. Application Deadline Deadline: 15 July 2026 Interested applicants should prepare their proposals early and carefully review the research themes before applying. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is highly suitable for: Postdoctoral researchers Digital humanities scholars Archivists AI and machine learning researchers Library and information science professionals Cultural heritage practitioners Humanities researchers Computational humanities specialists Media historians Archive technologists Final Thoughts The Joanna and Graham Barker Fellowship Scheme 2026–2027 represents an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers seeking to combine academic excellence with real-world cultural heritage impact. title: Georgetown University Global Competitiveness Leadership Program 2027 (GCL 2027) | Scholarships Available for Emerging Leaders from Latin America & the Caribbean

title: IIE Scholar Rescue Fund (IIE-SRF) Fellowship 2026: Complete Application Guide for Threatened and Displaced Scholars Worldwide
summary: The IIE Scholar Rescue Fund (IIE-SRF) Fellowship 2026 offers a critical lifeline for scholars, researchers, and academics who are facing threats, persecution, conflict, violence, or other circumstances that prevent them from safely continuing their academic work in their home countries. Administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE), the Scholar Rescue Fund provides fellowship support to qualified scholars whose academic careers and personal safety are at risk. Through this prestigious fellowship, scholars can continue their research, teaching, publishing, and other academic activities at host institutions in safe locations around the world. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year, with fellowships awarded quarterly. Application Deadline For consideration at the September 2026 Selection Committee meeting, applications must be submitted no later than July 26, 2026 . Although the program accepts applications on a rolling basis, applicants are encouraged to submit complete applications as early as possible. What Is the IIE Scholar Rescue Fund Fellowship? The IIE Scholar Rescue Fund Fellowship is designed to support scholars who are unable to continue their academic work due to threats, violence, political instability, armed conflict, persecution, or other dangerous circumstances in their home countries. The fellowship enables qualified academics to: Continue their research activities. Pursue teaching opportunities. Publish scholarly work. Maintain academic productivity. Preserve academic freedom. Continue contributing to global knowledge and scholarship. Work safely at host institutions outside their home country. The program recognizes the essential role scholars play in advancing education, innovation, research, and intellectual development worldwide. Why the IIE-SRF Fellowship Matters Across many regions of the world, scholars face significant challenges that threaten both their professional careers and personal safety. These challenges may include: Armed conflict and war. Political persecution. Restrictions on academic freedom. Targeted threats against researchers and educators. Harassment based on academic work. Institutional collapse due to crises. Human rights violations affecting academics. Security risks that make scholarly work impossible. The IIE-SRF Fellowship helps preserve academic careers while ensuring that scholars can continue contributing valuable research and expertise to the global academic community. Fellowship Application Process Scholars can submit their applications directly to the IIE Scholar Rescue Fund by email. In situations where an applicant cannot personally submit the materials, a third party may submit the application on the scholar’s behalf. Required Application Materials Applicants must prepare and submit several important documents to support their fellowship application. 1. Completed Application Form Every applicant must complete and submit the official IIE-SRF application form. 2. Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume The CV or resume should be detailed and include comprehensive information about the applicant’s academic and professional background. The CV must include: Academic Degrees Provide details for all earned degrees, including: Degree-granting institution. Academic field or discipline. Date the degree was awarded. Current Academic Position Include: Institution location. Employment dates. Professional title. Primary responsibilities and duties. Previous Academic Positions List all previous academic appointments in chronological order, including: Institution name. Location. Employment dates. Professional title. Key responsibilities. Academic Publications Applicants should provide a detailed publication record, including: Journal articles. Books. Book chapters. Research reports. Exhibitions. Other scholarly outputs. Each publication should include: Full citation. Authors. Publication title. Publication date. Page numbers where applicable. Additional Academic Contributions Applicants should also include: Master s thesis supervision. Ph.D. supervision. Conference presentations. Research grants. Honors and awards. Professional affiliations. Other significant academic achievements. 3. Academic Statement Applicants must submit a thorough academic statement of at least one page. The statement should explain: Academic background. Professional experience. Research interests. Areas of specialization. Academic accomplishments. Teaching experience. Research activities. Publishing activities. Proposed fellowship activities. Applicants should clearly describe what they intend to accomplish during the fellowship period, including future research, teaching, publishing, or related scholarly activities. 4. Personal Statement A personal statement of at least one page is required. The statement should provide: Reasons for applying to IIE-SRF. Detailed explanation of threats faced. Description of risks and challenges. Circumstances preventing continued work in the home country. Need for fellowship support. Impact of current conditions on academic work and personal safety. Applicants are encouraged to provide clear, detailed, and factual information that helps reviewers understand their circumstances. Reference Letter Requirements IIE-SRF requires a minimum of three original reference letters. Additional letters may be requested when necessary. Letters from colleagues both within and outside the applicant’s home country are preferred. Academic and Professional Reference Letters Applicants should provide academic or professional references from colleagues who can evaluate: Research quality. Publications. Teaching effectiveness. Academic achievements. Professional contributions. Specialized expertise. These references should demonstrate the applicant’s scholarly qualifications and impact within their field. Personal Reference Letters Applicants should also submit personal references from individuals familiar with their situation. These references should explain: Threats faced by the applicant. Personal circumstances. Security concerns. Reasons the applicant requires protection and support. Important Reference Letter Guidelines Reference letters should: Be original and individualized. Reflect the referee’s direct knowledge of the applicant. Avoid identical wording. Avoid AI-generated content. Be prepared on official letterhead whenever possible. Be sent directly to IIE-SRF when feasible. Additional Supporting Documents Applicants must also provide: Copy of Highest Degree Submit a copy of the Ph.D. degree or the highest academic degree earned. Recent Research Publications Provide samples of the most recent scholarly publications. Host Institution Letter (Optional) Applicants who have already secured a host institution may submit a letter confirming the institution’s intention to host the fellowship if awarded. This document is optional and not required for application consideration. Minimum Documents Needed for Initial Review To begin evaluating an application, IIE-SRF must receive: Application Form. Current CV. Academic Statement. Personal Statement. The remaining supporting documents may be submitted later. Important Policy on Originality and AI-Generated Content IIE-SRF places significant importance on authenticity and originality. All application materials must: Be unique to the individual applicant. Reflect personal academic experiences. Reflect personal circumstances. Avoid copied content. Properly cite borrowed information. The program strongly discourages the use of artificial intelligence tools, including ChatGPT, for preparing application materials or answering program-related questions. According to IIE-SRF guidelines, suspected AI-generated language may negatively affect an application during the assessment process. Applicants should therefore ensure that all submitted materials genuinely reflect their own experiences, academic achievements, and personal circumstances. Special Guidance for Married Applicants Spouses who both qualify for the fellowship and intend to apply should submit their applications simultaneously. Applicants should note: Each spouse must submit a separate application. Each application must contain unique materials. Shared or duplicated application content is not permitted. Delayed submission by one spouse after the other has already received a fellowship award may affect consideration. How Applications Are Reviewed IIE-SRF conducts a comprehensive assessment of every application. Reviewers evaluate: Academic qualifications. Research achievements. Scholarly contributions. Publication record. Professional accomplishments. Nature of the threats faced. Urgency of the applicant’s situation. Potential fellowship impact. During the review process, IIE-SRF may: Contact references. Consult independent experts. Seek information about the applicant’s academic field. Request clarification from applicants. Verify details regarding reported threats and circumstances. The organization states that identifying information will not be shared without the applicant’s permission. Selection and Fellowship Awards Fellowships are awarded quarterly through a formal selection process. Because demand for support is extremely high, meeting eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee fellowship funding. Applicants are encouraged to submit complete, compelling, and well-documented applications that clearly demonstrate both scholarly excellence and urgent need. Click here for more and to apply Final Thoughts The IIE Scholar Rescue Fund Fellowship 2026 represents a unique opportunity for threatened scholars to continue their academic careers in safety while preserving their contributions to global research, teaching, and intellectual advancement. Scholars facing serious risks in their home countries are encouraged to prepare strong, original applications and submit them before the July 26, 2026 deadline for consideration in the September 2026 review cycle. title: OITS 2026 Policy Fellowship Applications Open: A Unique Opportunity for UK Civil Servants to Collaborate with Leading Academics and Shape Evidence-Based Policy

title: Horizon Europe Cluster 3 Civil Security for Society 2026: European Commission Opens Major Research Funding Opportunities with Deadline of 5 November 2026
summary: The European Commission, through the European Research Executive Agency (REA), has launched a major funding opportunity under Horizon Europe Cluster 3: Civil Security for Society. This initiative aims to strengthen Europe s capacity to address growing security challenges through cutting-edge research, innovation, and collaboration among researchers, institutions, public authorities, and industry stakeholders. With proposals due by 5 November 2026 , this funding programme offers organizations the opportunity to secure support for projects that contribute to crime prevention, counter-terrorism efforts, cybersecurity, disaster resilience, border management, and critical infrastructure protection. As global security threats continue to evolve, the Horizon Europe Cluster 3 programme seeks innovative solutions that enhance the safety, resilience, and security of societies across Europe and beyond. About Horizon Europe Cluster 3: Civil Security for Society Horizon Europe is the European Union s flagship research and innovation framework programme. Within this framework, Cluster 3 focuses specifically on Civil Security for Society. The programme responds to a broad range of contemporary security challenges, including: Cybercrime and cybersecurity threats Terrorism and organized crime Border security challenges Natural disasters Human-made disasters Protection of critical infrastructure Privacy and trust in digital systems Crisis management and emergency response Through strategic investments in research and innovation, the European Commission aims to support solutions that help build safer, more resilient, and more secure societies. title: Fully Funded Matsumae International Foundation Research Fellowship 2027 in Japan: Six-Month Research Opportunity for Global Scholars
summary: Researchers seeking international collaboration, advanced research facilities, and meaningful academic exchange now have an exceptional opportunity to conduct fully funded research in Japan through the Matsumae International Foundation (MIF) Research Fellowship Program 2027. The prestigious fellowship supports outstanding non-Japanese researchers by providing financial support, research opportunities, and access to world-class Japanese universities and research institutions. Successful fellows will spend six months in Japan conducting research while building international partnerships and contributing to scientific advancement. The fellowship is designed to promote mutual understanding, academic cooperation, and long-term relationships between Japan and researchers from around the world. Applications for the 2027 fellowship cycle are currently open. About the Matsumae International Foundation Research Fellowship The Matsumae International Foundation (MIF) was established in 1979 by Dr. Shigeyoshi Matsumae, the founder of Tokai University. The foundation was created with a vision of promoting global peace and international friendship through academic exchange and research collaboration. For more than four decades, the fellowship has welcomed talented researchers from around the world to Japan, providing opportunities to undertake advanced research projects while fostering cultural understanding and international cooperation. The program enables researchers to work closely with Japanese academics and institutions, helping participants expand their expertise and strengthen their professional networks. Fellowship Duration Selected fellows will conduct research in Japan for: Six months Research activities may be undertaken during the fellowship period scheduled between June 2027 and March 2028. Fellowship Benefits The Matsumae International Foundation Research Fellowship is fully funded and offers a comprehensive support package. Benefits include: Monthly Allowance Fellows receive: JPY 220,000 per month This allowance is intended to cover living expenses and support research activities during the fellowship period. Arrival Grant Successful applicants receive: JPY 120,000 arrival allowance This funding assists fellows with initial settlement costs upon arrival in Japan. Round-Trip Airfare The fellowship covers: Economy-class airfare between the fellow s home country and Japan Insurance Coverage Participants receive: Overseas travel and medical insurance during their fellowship stay Study Tour Fellows may also participate in: Organized cultural and academic study tours in Japan These activities provide opportunities to learn more about Japanese society, culture, and research environments. Research Fields The fellowship welcomes research proposals from a broad range of academic disciplines. Priority is often given to research in: Natural Sciences Engineering Medicine Agriculture The program particularly values research that can contribute to solving important challenges facing society and support development in the fellow s home country. title: Bracken Prize for Young Authors 2026: Win £15,000 for Your Unpublished Business Book Proposal

The competition is designed to encourage fresh thinking and bold ideas that address today s rapidly changing business landscape. title: GEF Small Grants Programme CSO Challenge Program 2026: Receive Up to $300,000 to Scale High-Impact Environmental Solutions
summary: Civil society organizations around the world are playing a critical role in addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation, pollution, and other environmental challenges. Yet many of these organizations struggle to secure the resources needed to expand successful initiatives and increase their impact. To address this gap, the GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) CSO Challenge Program has launched a new funding opportunity designed to identify, reward, and support innovative environmental solutions led by civil society organizations. Supported by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and led by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the program provides grants of up to USD $300,000 to help qualified organizations scale proven environmental solutions, replicate successful models, and expand their impact. In addition to funding, selected organizations will benefit from technical assistance, capacity-building opportunities, peer learning, strategic partnerships, and international visibility. For the current call, applications are open for organizations operating in the Eastern Europe, Caucasus, and Central Asia (EECCA) region. About the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program The GEF Small Grants Programme has a long history of supporting community-led environmental action across the globe. Building on the success of previous initiatives, the CSO Challenge Program was created to provide larger grants and more comprehensive support to organizations that have already demonstrated success and are ready to grow. The program recognizes that civil society organizations and local communities are often at the forefront of environmental conservation and sustainable development. Their innovations, local knowledge, and grassroots approaches are essential for addressing some of the world s most pressing environmental challenges. The CSO Challenge Program aims to amplify these efforts by helping organizations scale their solutions, reach new communities, and create lasting environmental impact. Funding Amount Selected organizations can receive: Grants of up to USD $300,000 Funding for projects lasting up to 24 months Tailored technical support Capacity-building assistance Networking opportunities Peer-to-peer learning opportunities Partnership development support Increased international recognition and visibility Unlike traditional GEF Small Grants Programme funding, this initiative prioritizes larger grants that can significantly accelerate growth, replication, and scaling of successful environmental solutions. Program Objectives The CSO Challenge Program seeks to achieve several important goals: 1. Recognize Innovative Environmental Solutions The program identifies and rewards organizations that have developed effective and innovative approaches to environmental conservation and sustainability. 2. Strengthen Organizational Capacity Selected organizations receive support to enhance their ability to design, manage, and expand impactful environmental programs. 3. Scale Successful Models The program helps organizations replicate proven approaches in new regions, communities, and contexts. 4. Encourage Knowledge Sharing Participants are encouraged to exchange experiences, lessons learned, and best practices with other organizations and stakeholders. 5. Promote Inclusion The program supports initiatives that actively engage: Women Youth Indigenous Peoples Local communities Marginalized populations What Types of Projects Are Funded? Funding is available for initiatives that focus on scaling and expanding successful environmental solutions. Supported activities include: Replicating Proven Models Organizations can replicate successful environmental approaches in new communities, regions, or countries. Adapting Existing Solutions Projects may adapt effective models to suit different local conditions and environmental contexts. Testing Scaling Strategies Organizations can explore innovative approaches to expanding the reach and impact of promising environmental initiatives. Strategic Priority Areas Applicants must work within one of the program’s five strategic priority areas. 1. Community-Based Management of Threatened Ecosystems and Species Projects that support local communities in protecting biodiversity, restoring ecosystems, and conserving threatened species. 2. Sustainable Agriculture, Fisheries, and Food Security Initiatives that promote sustainable food systems while protecting natural resources and strengthening livelihoods. 3. Low-Carbon Energy Access Projects that improve access to renewable and low-carbon energy solutions while delivering environmental and social benefits. 4. Chemicals and Waste Management Programs that reduce pollution, improve waste management systems, and protect environmental and human health. 5. Sustainable Urban Solutions Innovative approaches that improve environmental sustainability, climate resilience, and resource efficiency in urban areas. Who Can Apply? Eligible applicants must meet all of the following requirements: Civil Society Organization Status Applicants must: Be a legally registered Civil Society Organization (CSO) Possess legal status in their country Maintain a bank account in the organization s name Geographic Eligibility The applicant organization and the initiative to be replicated or scaled must be located in an eligible GEF Recipient Country. Eligible regions include: Africa 54 eligible countries Latin America and the Caribbean 33 eligible countries Eastern Europe, Caucasus and Central Asia (EECCA) 21 eligible countries Asia-Pacific 41 eligible countries Why This Grant Matters Many environmental organizations develop highly effective local solutions but lack the resources needed to expand their reach. The CSO Challenge Program addresses this challenge by investing in organizations that have already demonstrated success and are ready for growth. Through funding, mentoring, partnerships, and technical support, the program helps organizations move from local success stories to scalable models capable of generating regional and global impact. Application Process The CSO Challenge Program uses a two-stage selection process. Stage 1: Concept Note Submission Applicants must submit a Concept Note outlining their proposed project and scaling strategy. Stage 2: Full Proposal Submission Organizations shortlisted during the first stage will be invited to prepare and submit a comprehensive Full Proposal. A diverse selection committee comprising representatives from: The GEF Secretariat Civil society organizations Indigenous Peoples organizations Youth organizations Women s organizations IUCN will evaluate submissions and select finalists and winners. Languages Accepted Applications may be submitted in: English French Spanish Application Timeline Step 1: Concept Note Stage 05 June 2026 Call for proposals opens 20 June 2026 Deadline for questions 20 July 2026 Deadline to submit Concept Notes Step 2: Full Proposal Stage 19 August 2026 Finalists notified and invited to submit Full Proposals 18 September 2026 Deadline for Full Proposal submission Step 3: Final Selection 18 October 2026 Winners and finalists notified Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on: Alignment with SGP 2.0 priority areas Impact potential Alignment with national Multilateral Environmental Agreement (MEA) commitments Scalability Inclusivity Organizational capacity and sustainability Benefits Beyond Funding In addition to financial support, successful applicants will gain access to: Expert technical assistance Organizational capacity strengthening International exposure Peer learning opportunities Strategic partnerships Networking with governments, donors, and private sector actors Knowledge-sharing platforms Organizations Behind the Program Global Environment Facility (GEF) The GEF is one of the world s leading environmental funding institutions. Over more than three decades, it has provided over $26 billion in financing and mobilized an additional $148 billion to support environmental projects globally. International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) IUCN is the world s largest and oldest global environmental network, working with governments, civil society organizations, and experts in over 160 countries to address environmental and development challenges. RTI International RTI International is a globally recognized independent scientific research institute that supports evidence-based solutions across environmental, social, and technical disciplines. Organizations with proven environmental impact and ambitions to scale their solutions now have a unique opportunity to secure up to $300,000 in funding and join a global network of environmental change-makers working to build a more sustainable future. title: 2026 EU Gender Equality Champions Award: Win Up to €100,000 and Gain European Recognition for Advancing Equality in Research and Innovation
summary: The European Commission has officially opened applications for the prestigious 2026 EU Gender Equality Champions Award, a major initiative designed to recognize and celebrate institutions that are making significant progress in advancing gender equality across research, innovation, leadership, and higher education. With a total prize fund of €400,000 available, the award highlights organizations that are embedding gender equality into their institutional culture, governance structures, research environments, and innovation ecosystems. The initiative forms part of the European Union’s broader commitment to creating a more inclusive, diverse, and competitive European Research Area. A significant development for the 2026 edition is the expansion of eligibility criteria. For the first time, research and innovation organizations from EU candidate countries can participate alongside institutions from EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Organizations interested in applying must submit their applications by 29 September 2026 through the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. About the 2026 EU Gender Equality Champions Award Established in 2022 by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Research and Innovation, the EU Gender Equality Champions Award recognizes institutions that have successfully implemented transformative gender equality measures within their organizations. The award aims to encourage structural and sustainable change by highlighting successful institutional practices that promote equal opportunities, diversity, inclusion, and fairness within research and innovation environments. By rewarding excellence and innovation in gender equality, the European Commission seeks to inspire organizations across Europe and beyond to adopt ambitious Gender Equality Plans (GEPs) and implement meaningful reforms that improve workplace culture, leadership representation, and research excellence. Why Gender Equality Matters in Research and Innovation Gender equality is increasingly recognized as a critical factor in strengthening research quality, innovation outcomes, and institutional performance. Research environments that embrace diversity benefit from: Broader perspectives and ideas Improved decision-making processes Enhanced research quality Greater innovation potential Increased institutional competitiveness More inclusive leadership structures Better opportunities for underrepresented groups The European Commission considers gender equality not only a social objective but also a strategic advantage that contributes to Europe’s long-term competitiveness and scientific excellence. Prize Value and Benefits Successful applicants will receive substantial recognition and financial support through the award program. Benefits include: 1. Financial Awards Winning institutions can receive prizes worth up to €100,000. The total prize fund for the 2026 edition amounts to €400,000. 2. International Recognition Award recipients gain visibility across Europe’s research and innovation community, positioning themselves as leaders in gender equality and institutional transformation. 3. Enhanced Institutional Reputation Recognition from the European Commission can strengthen an institution’s profile among: Researchers Students Policymakers Funding agencies International partners Industry collaborators 4. Showcase of Best Practices Winning organizations serve as examples of successful gender equality implementation, helping inspire similar initiatives across Europe and beyond. 5. Networking Opportunities Award recipients gain opportunities to connect with influential stakeholders in European research, innovation, and higher education. Award Categories Applicants may apply to only one category. 1. Sustainable Gender Equality Champions This category recognizes organizations that have demonstrated a strong and long-term commitment to gender equality through sustained implementation of Gender Equality Plans. Eligible organizations should show: Significant structural achievements Long-term institutional impact Demonstrated progress over multiple years Sustainable gender equality outcomes Number of Winners: One winner Prize: €100,000 2. Newcomer Gender Equality Champions This category celebrates institutions that have recently completed their first Gender Equality Plan and achieved significant progress in implementation. Organizations should demonstrate: Successful launch of their first GEP Strong early-stage results Effective implementation strategies Clear institutional commitment Number of Winners: Two winners Prize: €100,000 per winner 3. Inclusive Gender Equality Champions This category recognizes organizations that go beyond gender equality by addressing multiple dimensions of inclusion and diversity. Applicants should demonstrate efforts that combine gender equality with at least two additional social categories, including: Racial or ethnic origin Disability Sexual orientation Social origin Other dimensions of diversity and inclusion Number of Winners: One winner Prize: €100,000 Important Eligibility Rules Organizations planning to apply should carefully review all eligibility requirements before submitting an application. Key rules include: Applicants may apply to only one category. Previous award winners are not eligible to participate again. Organizations must operate within research and innovation sectors. Institutions must satisfy category-specific criteria. Applications must comply with the official Rules of Contest. What Is a Gender Equality Plan (GEP)? A Gender Equality Plan (GEP) is a strategic framework that outlines measures and objectives aimed at improving gender equality within an organization. Typical components include: Gender-balanced leadership and governance Equal career progression opportunities Inclusive recruitment processes Work-life balance measures Prevention of gender-based discrimination Gender-sensitive research and teaching practices Monitoring and evaluation systems Under Horizon Europe, many public bodies, research organizations, and higher education institutions are required to maintain active Gender Equality Plans to qualify for certain research funding opportunities. Application Process Organizations must submit their applications electronically through the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. Application Steps Review the official Rules of Contest. Identify the most suitable award category. Gather evidence of gender equality achievements. Prepare all required supporting documentation. Complete the online application form. Submit the application before the deadline. Application Deadline Deadline: 29 September 2026 Late submissions will not be considered, so applicants are encouraged to begin preparations well in advance. Selection Process After the submission deadline, applications will be assessed by an independent jury composed of international experts. The evaluation will focus on: Impact Innovation Sustainability Institutional commitment Quality of implementation Inclusiveness Successful organizations will be selected based on their demonstrated achievements and long-term contributions to gender equality. Announcement of Winners The winners of the 2026 EU Gender Equality Champions Award will be officially announced during a dedicated award ceremony in Brussels in 2027. The ceremony will celebrate institutions that are driving meaningful cultural and structural change across Europe’s research and innovation landscape. Why Organizations Should Apply The 2026 EU Gender Equality Champions Award represents more than a financial prize. It provides an opportunity for institutions to gain European recognition for their commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion. Organizations that have invested in building equitable workplaces, inclusive leadership structures, and transformative Gender Equality Plans can use this platform to showcase their achievements, inspire others, and contribute to a stronger and more inclusive European research ecosystem. With expanded eligibility now including EU candidate countries, the 2026 edition offers a unique opportunity for a wider range of institutions to join Europe’s growing movement toward gender equality and institutional excellence. title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University 2027: Fully Funded Master’s Scholarships for African Leaders in Public Health, Public Policy, Nutrition, and Sustainable Agriculture
summary: Applications Opening Soon for One of Canada s Most Prestigious Fully Funded Graduate Scholarship Programs for African Students The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University is now preparing to launch its 2027 application cycle, offering a transformative opportunity for talented young African leaders to pursue fully funded master s studies at one of Canada s most prestigious universities. Hosted by McGill University in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, this highly competitive scholarship program is designed to support outstanding African students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, leadership potential, commitment to community service, and a strong desire to contribute to the social and economic development of Africa. The scholarship is far more than a financial award. It is a comprehensive leadership and educational initiative that empowers scholars to become agents of change capable of transforming sectors such as public health, nutrition, public policy, food systems, environmental sustainability, and agriculture across the African continent. Each year, the program awards approximately 35 fully funded scholarships across 13 eligible graduate programs, covering all major educational and living expenses while providing leadership development opportunities and access to one of the world s leading academic communities. About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative that seeks to develop the next generation of ethical and transformative leaders. At McGill University, the program specifically focuses on preparing African scholars to address critical development challenges in: Sustainable agriculture Food security Public health Nutrition Environmental management Water resources Biotechnology Public policy The program recognizes that Africa s future depends heavily on investing in talented young people who can drive innovation, influence policy, strengthen institutions, and improve the well-being of communities across the continent. By combining academic excellence with leadership training, community engagement, and global networking opportunities, the scholarship creates pathways for scholars to make lasting contributions both during and after their studies. What Makes the McGill Mastercard Foundation Scholarship Unique? Unlike many traditional scholarships that focus only on tuition support, the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program offers a holistic support system designed to remove financial barriers and help scholars succeed academically, professionally, and personally. The scholarship places strong emphasis on: Leadership development Community impact Social responsibility Academic excellence Sustainable development Long-term contribution to Africa Successful scholars become part of a global network of Mastercard Foundation Scholars and alumni working to create positive change in their communities and countries. Scholarship Benefits The Mastercard Foundation Scholarship at McGill University is fully comprehensive and covers virtually all expenses associated with graduate studies in Canada. Benefits include: Full Tuition Coverage The scholarship covers the complete international student tuition fees required to pursue an eligible master s degree at McGill University. On-Campus Housing Scholars receive accommodation support through on-campus housing arrangements, helping ensure a smooth transition into university life. Monthly Living Stipend Recipients receive financial support to cover living expenses throughout their studies. Academic Resources and Learning Support The program provides access to academic tools, learning materials, and support services designed to maximize academic success. Pre-Arrival and Immigration Support Scholars receive guidance and support throughout: Immigration procedures Study permit preparation Travel planning Arrival and settlement processes Leadership Development Opportunities Participants gain access to: Leadership training Mentorship opportunities Professional development activities Networking events Community engagement initiatives Access to a Global Scholars Network Students become members of an international community of Mastercard Foundation Scholars, opening doors to lifelong collaborations and opportunities. Number of Scholarships Available McGill University offers: 35 Scholarships Annually These scholarships are distributed across 13 eligible graduate programs. Competition is expected to be intense due to the program s prestige and comprehensive funding package. Eligible Academic Programs The scholarship supports selected master s programs that align with Africa s development priorities. Non-Thesis Programs Eligible non-thesis programs include: Sustainable Agriculture Animal Science: Sustainable Agriculture Environmental and Water Resources Engineering Bioresource Engineering – Environmental Engineering Bioresource Engineering – Integrated Water Resource Management Food Systems and Biotechnology Biotechnology Food Science Food Safety Integrated Food Bioprocessing Health and Public Health Human Nutrition (Project) Biostatistics Public Health Public Policy Public Policy Thesis-Based Programs Eligible thesis programs include: Animal Science Bioresource Engineering Important Note for Thesis Applicants Applicants interested in thesis-based programs must not contact professors or supervisors directly. Instead: Apply through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Wait for scholarship screening results. If selected for a fee waiver, McGill will provide instructions regarding supervisor matching. Who Can Apply? The scholarship targets exceptional African students who demonstrate both academic excellence and a commitment to creating positive social impact. Applicants must: Academic Requirements Hold a bachelor s degree or recognized equivalent. Meet McGill University s graduate admission requirements. Have a degree closely related to the chosen graduate program. Demonstrate strong academic performance. Applicants with First Class Honors or equivalent qualifications are considered especially competitive. Citizenship Requirements Applicants must: Be citizens of an African country. Currently reside in Africa. Age Requirement Applicants must be: 35 years old or younger at the time of application. Leadership and Service Candidates should demonstrate: Community involvement Leadership experience Volunteerism Civic engagement Service initiatives Financial Need Applicants must clearly demonstrate that financial barriers have limited or prevented access to educational opportunities. Commitment to Africa Strong candidates will show: A desire to contribute to their communities. Commitment to Africa s development. Plans to create positive impact after graduation. Priority Groups The program strongly encourages applications from: Women Women applicants are given priority consideration. Persons with Disabilities Applicants living with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Displaced Populations Priority is given to: Refugees Asylum seekers Internally displaced persons (IDPs) Returnees Ineligible Applicants The following individuals are not eligible: Applicants who have already completed a master s degree. Applicants currently enrolled in a master s degree. Permanent residents of Canada. Permanent residents of the United States. Permanent residents of the United Kingdom. Permanent residents of EU countries. Dual citizens with these residency privileges. Eligible Countries The scholarship is open to citizens and residents of every country in Africa, including: Ghana Nigeria Kenya Uganda Rwanda Ethiopia South Africa Tanzania Zambia Zimbabwe Senegal Morocco Algeria Egypt And all other African Union member states. Learn more about the Eligibility HERE Mandatory Information Sessions One of the most important requirements of the application process is attendance at an official information session. Is Attendance Mandatory? Yes. Only eligible applicants who attend an information session will receive access to the application form. Failure to attend an information session means you cannot apply. Information Session Schedule North Africa West Africa June 23, 2026 June 25, 2026 East Africa Southern Africa June 30, 2026 July 2, 2026 Central Africa July 7, 2026 July 9, 2026 Open Session for All Regions July 15, 2026 Applicants should register for the session corresponding to their region. Technology Barriers Applicants unable to attend because of internet or technology challenges may submit a technological barrier disclosure form. Learn more about the Info Sessions HERE Selection Criteria Applications are evaluated based on: Academic Merit Applicants must be academically competitive for admission to McGill University. Leadership Potential The committee seeks transformative leaders capable of driving meaningful change. Community Service Applicants should demonstrate active engagement in community development initiatives. Development Impact Strong consideration is given to candidates whose studies can positively impact their home countries. Overcoming Barriers Applicants who have overcome: Financial barriers Social barriers Personal challenges Health-related challenges may receive additional consideration. Learn more about the Selection Criteria HERE Detailed Application Timeline Information Sessions June 23 – July 15, 2026 Scholarship Applications Open August 3, 2026 (9:00 AM EST) Scholarship Application Deadline August 21, 2026 (4:00 PM EST) No late applications will be accepted. McGill Admission Stage September – November 2026 Selected candidates receive instructions to apply to McGill University. University Application Deadline December 1, 2026 Only applicants who receive fee waivers can proceed. Admission Decisions February – March 2027 Scholarship Selection Mid-February – Early March 2027 Scholarship Results Late March – Early April 2027 Understanding the Selection Process The scholarship process involves several stages. Stage 1: Information Session Applicants attend a mandatory session. Stage 2: Scholarship Application Applicants complete the Mastercard Foundation application. Stage 3: Pre-Screening Applications undergo eligibility assessment. Stage 4: Fee Waiver Invitation Successful applicants receive fee waiver instructions. Stage 5: McGill Admission Application Candidates submit university applications. Stage 6: Admission Decision McGill evaluates academic eligibility. Stage 7: Scholarship Selection Final scholarship recipients are selected. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What Is the Purpose of This Scholarship? The scholarship aims to support talented African leaders pursuing master s studies in fields critical to Africa s development, including public health, nutrition, public policy, and sustainable agriculture. What Does the Scholarship Cover? The scholarship covers: Full tuition Housing Monthly stipend Immigration support Academic resources Leadership development opportunities How Many Scholarships Are Available? McGill awards approximately 35 scholarships each year. Is the Scholarship Available for Undergraduate Students? No. The scholarship is exclusively for master s-level studies. Is Attendance at an Information Session Mandatory? Yes. Only attendees receive access to the application form. Can I Apply If I Don t Meet McGill Admission Requirements? No. Applicants must first meet graduate admission requirements. What Happens During Pre-Screening? McGill evaluates: Age eligibility Citizenship Residency Academic readiness Leadership profile Motivation Master s degree history How Long Does Pre-Screening Take? Applicants can expect results within 4–6 weeks. What Happens If I Pass Pre-Screening? Successful candidates receive: Application fee waivers Instructions for applying to McGill What Is Conditional Admission? Conditional admission means admission is dependent on receiving the scholarship. What Happens If I Am Admitted But Not Awarded the Scholarship? Conditional admission will be withdrawn. Applicants may reapply during future cycles. Can I Appeal Scholarship Decisions? No. All decisions are final. Visit HERE for more FAQs about the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University 2027. Conclusion The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University remains one of the most prestigious fully funded master s scholarship opportunities available to African students. With comprehensive financial support, world-class education, leadership development opportunities, and access to a powerful global network, the program provides exceptional young African leaders with the tools needed to transform communities and drive sustainable development across the continent. For ambitious students passionate about public health, nutrition, public policy, biotechnology, food systems, environmental sustainability, and agriculture, this scholarship represents a life-changing opportunity to study at one of Canada s leading universities while preparing to become a catalyst for positive change in Africa. title: European Youth Energy Forum (EYEF) 2026 in Nice, France: Applications Open for Students, Young Professionals, and Researchers Driving the Energy Transition
summary: The European Youth Energy Forum (EYEF) 2026 is now accepting applications for its highly anticipated fifth edition, offering an exceptional opportunity for students, young professionals, researchers, and emerging leaders to engage directly in shaping the future of Europe s energy transition. Scheduled to take place from 26–29 October 2026 in Nice, France, the forum will bring together some of the brightest young minds from across Europe and the Mediterranean region to exchange ideas, collaborate on solutions, strengthen professional networks, and contribute to discussions that will influence the future of sustainable energy systems. Organized by the European Youth Energy Network (EYEN), EYEF has become one of Europe s leading youth platforms dedicated to empowering the next generation of energy professionals and ensuring that youth perspectives are represented in the global energy dialogue. Applications are open from 11 May to 21 June 2026, and selected participants will embark on a multi-month journey that combines virtual learning, collaboration, and networking activities before culminating in the in-person forum in Nice. About the European Youth Energy Forum (EYEF) The European Youth Energy Forum is more than a conference. It is a youth-driven platform designed to connect ambitious young people who are passionate about energy, climate action, sustainability, innovation, and policy development. Since its inception, EYEF has provided a unique space where participants can: Discuss pressing energy challenges Explore innovative solutions Learn from industry experts Collaborate across disciplines Build international partnerships Develop leadership skills Contribute to Europe s energy transition agenda The forum recognizes that young people are not simply future stakeholders in the energy sector—they are already playing critical roles in shaping sustainable energy systems, influencing climate action policies, and advancing innovation across industries. EYEF 2026 Theme: From Skills to Impact The 2026 edition of the forum is built around the theme: From Skills to Impact: Empowering Young Professionals to Implement the Energy Transition This theme reflects a growing recognition that achieving energy transition goals requires more than technical knowledge alone. It requires: Leadership Collaboration Innovation Practical implementation skills Cross-sector partnerships Youth engagement The forum seeks to equip participants with the tools, networks, and experiences needed to translate knowledge into real-world impact. Why EYEF 2026 Matters Europe is undergoing one of the most significant energy transformations in history. Countries across the continent are investing heavily in: Renewable energy Green hydrogen Energy efficiency Smart grids Sustainable mobility Climate resilience Decarbonization strategies At the same time, governments, industries, and institutions increasingly recognize the importance of involving young people in decision-making processes. EYEF serves as a bridge between youth talent and the institutions driving Europe s energy future. The forum provides participants with opportunities to: Engage with industry experts Learn from policymakers Connect with researchers Collaborate with peers Develop innovative solutions A Unique International Experience One of the defining features of EYEF is its international and interdisciplinary nature. The forum welcomes participants from diverse academic and professional backgrounds, creating a rich environment for knowledge sharing and collaboration. Participants typically represent fields such as: Renewable energy Engineering Environmental sciences Climate policy Sustainable development Economics Energy law Innovation and entrepreneurship Research and academia This diversity allows participants to explore energy challenges from multiple perspectives and develop more comprehensive solutions. Building on Collaboration with IRENA The European Youth Energy Forum continues its collaboration with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Youth Forum. This partnership strengthens connections between regional and global youth energy initiatives and provides participants with greater exposure to international energy discussions. The collaboration contributes to: Global knowledge exchange International networking opportunities Exposure to renewable energy developments Youth participation in global energy governance What Selected Participants Can Expect Participants selected for EYEF 2026 will participate in a comprehensive programme that extends beyond the in-person event. Online Learning Journey Before arriving in Nice, participants will engage in an online programme running from July to October 2026.
