title: U.S. Department of State Launches Up to $60 Million Funding Opportunity to Strengthen Uganda’s Health System Through the Health Foreign Assistance MOU Implementation Plan
summary: The U.S. Department of State, through its Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), has announced a major funding opportunity under the Advancing Global Health Annual Program Statement (APS) aimed at supporting the implementation of the Health Foreign Assistance Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the United States Government and the Government of Uganda . With up to $60 million in available funding and up to 15 anticipated awards , this initiative seeks to accelerate Uganda’s transition toward a sustainable, accountable, and government-led health system capable of maintaining and expanding gains in public health outcomes. Organizations with the expertise, capacity, and commitment to strengthening health systems are invited to submit Statements of Interest (SOIs) for projects that align with the priorities outlined in the Uganda MOU Implementation Plan. Funding Overview Funding Opportunity Details Funding Opportunity Title: Advancing Global Health Funding Opportunity Number: DFOP0017890 Addendum Title: Health Foreign Assistance Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Implementation in Uganda Administering Agency: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD) Total Funding Available: Up to $60,000,000 Number of Awards: Up to 15 Project Duration: Up to 5 years Application Process: Two-step process First Step: Submission of a Statement of Interest (SOI) Important Deadlines Deadline for Questions: June 17, 2026 Statement of Interest (SOI) Deadline: July 31, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT (GMT-4) Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all program guidance and amendment documents before submitting questions or applications. Why This Funding Opportunity Matters Uganda is currently implementing a transformative five-year health transition framework covering the period from April 2026 through December 2030 . The framework is designed to: Strengthen national health systems Improve disease prevention and epidemic control Enhance healthcare service delivery Increase accountability and transparency Expand government ownership of health programs Ensure long-term sustainability of health investments The initiative supports Uganda’s efforts to maintain progress in: HIV prevention and treatment Tuberculosis control Malaria prevention and response Maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) Immunization services Outbreak preparedness and response Health security systems A key feature of the MOU is the gradual transition from donor-driven implementation models toward government-led and performance-based programming , enabling Uganda to take greater ownership of its healthcare future. Key Areas of Investment The Department of State is seeking innovative and capable partners to support two major implementation tracks. Track 1: Sustainable Faith- and Community-Based Health Systems Faith-based and community-based health facilities play a critical role in Uganda’s healthcare landscape. These institutions contribute significantly to: HIV treatment services Tuberculosis case detection Malaria treatment Child immunization programs Maternal healthcare Outbreak detection and response However, many remain dependent on externally funded projects. This funding opportunity aims to help these institutions become financially sustainable and operationally resilient. Objective 1: Establish and Scale Sustainable Community-Based Health Financing Mechanisms Organizations may propose initiatives that create sustainable financing models capable of reducing dependence on donor funding. Potential activities include: Community Health Insurance Development Establishing new community health insurance schemes Strengthening governance and oversight systems Developing digital enrollment platforms Implementing claims management systems Building actuarial capacity Improving financial management systems Income Generation and Revenue Diversification Organizations are encouraged to: Link community health insurance schemes with income-generating initiatives Strengthen financial resilience among participating communities Reduce premium payment defaults Improve long-term sustainability Equitable Access Projects should also: Conduct willingness-to-pay studies Introduce sustainable user fee structures Establish transparent waiver systems for vulnerable populations Objective 2: Sustain Integrated Service Delivery in Faith- and Community-Based Facilities Recipients will help ensure uninterrupted delivery of critical health services during the transition period. Priority service areas include: HIV treatment and prevention Tuberculosis services Malaria programs Maternal and child health Immunization Global health security interventions Expected activities include: Integrated Care Models One-stop healthcare services Reduction of fragmented service delivery Alignment with Ministry of Health integration strategies Strengthening Health Facility Systems Support may include: Electronic medical records Laboratory networks Diagnostic systems Commodity management Human resource management systems Workforce Development Organizations may support: Clinical mentorship programs Continuous quality improvement initiatives Performance monitoring systems Skills enhancement and professional development Objective 3: Build Faith- and Community-Based Organization Capacity Applicants may focus on strengthening institutional capacity across health facility networks. Potential interventions include: Organizational Capacity Building Governance strengthening Financial management systems Strategic planning Institutional development Revenue Diversification Projects may support: Dedicated health budgets Financial sustainability plans Leveraging affiliated financial institutions Community mobilization initiatives Transition Planning Organizations will be expected to develop plans that gradually shift operational costs toward domestic funding sources. Track 2: Enabling Systems for Accountable, Government-Led Programming This track focuses on strengthening the systems required to support Uganda’s transition to performance-based and government-led health programming. Objective 4: Strengthen and Scale Digital Health Systems Applicants may support the deployment, integration, and transfer of national digital health systems to government ownership. Systems include: Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) eAfya ClinicMaster Laboratory Information Systems ALIS LabExpert DHIS2-based surveillance systems National Data Warehouse eCHIS iHRIS National supply chain management systems Projects should ensure: Full interoperability Government ownership Sustainable operations Transition of staffing and recurrent costs Objective 5: Expand Sustainable Power Solutions for Health Facilities Organizations may support the installation and maintenance of sustainable energy solutions for up to 700 health facilities by 2029 . Potential interventions include: Solar power systems Energy-efficient infrastructure Backup power solutions User training programs Maintenance systems All technology solutions should be supported by lifecycle cost analysis and coordinated with relevant government authorities. Objective 6: Institutionalize Supply Chain Accountability and GS-1 Traceability The Department seeks support for modernizing Uganda’s health supply chain. Activities may include: GS-1 Implementation Product identification systems Serial number tracking End-to-end medicine traceability Digital Integration Linking traceability systems with LMIS platforms Automated alerts and monitoring Improved data reconciliation Annual Supply Chain Audits Recipients may conduct audits covering: Procurement and contract management Warehousing and inventory management Distribution and transportation Data quality and information systems Objective 7: District-Level Risk Assessments and Performance Verification Applicants may support: Government Readiness Assessments Financial management evaluations Funds-flow analyses IFMIS readiness assessments Internal controls verification Risk Mitigation Planning Organizations will help local authorities: Identify risks Develop mitigation measures Strengthen governance systems Independent Verification Recipients may conduct: Quarterly reviews Semi-annual reviews Annual verification exercises Performance-based payment verification Objective 8: Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) Quality Assurance Projects may focus on malaria prevention through quality assurance support for Indoor Residual Spraying programs across 35 districts. Key responsibilities may include: Spray planning support Household coverage verification Environmental compliance monitoring Safety assurance Efficacy testing and verification The goal is to verify: At least 85% household spray coverage 100% spray efficacy in sampled households after 30 days Guiding Principles for Applicants All proposed projects should align with the Department of State’s guiding principles, including: Sustainability and Country Ownership Projects should: Strengthen Ugandan institutions Promote domestic financing Reduce long-term dependence on external support Protection of Essential Services Programs must safeguard: HIV services Tuberculosis services Malaria interventions Maternal and child health programs Immunization programs Data-Driven Accountability Projects should: Generate quality data Improve decision-making Strengthen accountability systems Integrated Service Delivery Applicants should prioritize: Coordination Efficiency Reduced duplication People-centered approaches Local Partnerships Organizations should collaborate with: Government institutions Local NGOs Community-based organizations Faith-based organizations Private sector partners Evidence-Based Programming Activities must be informed by: Local evidence National priorities Context-specific realities Application Process The funding opportunity uses a two-stage application process . Step 1: Submit a Statement of Interest (SOI) Organizations must submit a concise SOI outlining: Proposed objectives Project approach Expected outcomes Organizational capacity Step 2: Invitation for Full Proposal Selected applicants may be invited to submit a full proposal for further consideration. Interested organizations may submit SOIs addressing one or multiple objectives. Apply Here Final Thoughts This significant investment represents one of the most ambitious efforts to strengthen Uganda’s health systems while advancing long-term country ownership and sustainability. Organizations with expertise in health systems strengthening, digital health, supply chain management, health financing, governance, community health, and public health service delivery have a unique opportunity to contribute to Uganda’s transition toward a resilient, accountable, and government-led health system. With up to $60 million in funding available , successful applicants will play a critical role in supporting healthcare transformation, improving service delivery, strengthening epidemic preparedness, and ensuring that health gains are sustained for generations to come. title: ACET Youth Policy Lab 2026: Fully Virtual Pan-African Policy Innovation Challenge for Young Leaders Driving Africa’s Future
summary: The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) has officially opened applications for the ACET Youth Policy Lab (AYPL) 2026, a unique continent-wide policy innovation challenge designed to place young Africans at the center of policymaking, innovation, and economic transformation. Under the theme, From Coordination to Commercialization: Youth, Innovation Growth, the 2026 edition invites ambitious young Africans to step into the role of policymakers and tackle some of Africa s most pressing development challenges through evidence-based policy design, collaboration, mentorship, and leadership development. The ACET Youth Policy Lab is much more than a competition. It is an immersive learning experience that combines the excitement of a hackathon with the rigor of real-world policy development, equipping participants with practical skills in governance, innovation, leadership, and policy analysis. For young Africans who aspire to influence public policy, drive innovation, and contribute to sustainable development across the continent, this opportunity offers a powerful platform to learn, collaborate, and create impact. What is the ACET Youth Policy Lab? The ACET Youth Policy Lab is a simulation-based policy innovation platform that empowers young Africans to engage directly with policymaking processes. Participants are placed within a fictional institution known as the National Youth Transformation Authority (NYTA), where they assume the role of decision-makers responsible for developing solutions to real-world development challenges facing African countries. The program is specifically designed to: Strengthen youth participation in policymaking Develop policy analysis and problem-solving skills Promote innovation-driven development solutions Enhance leadership capabilities Foster collaboration among young Africans Increase youth representation in governance spaces Unlike traditional competitions, participants are challenged to think critically about policy trade-offs, institutional constraints, and implementation realities. Theme for 2026: From Coordination to Commercialization – Youth, Innovation Growth The 2026 Youth Policy Lab focuses on one of Africa’s most important development priorities: transforming innovative ideas into sustainable economic growth opportunities. Participants will explore how effective policy coordination, innovation ecosystems, and commercialization strategies can create jobs, strengthen industries, and accelerate Africa’s economic transformation. The theme encourages young leaders to design practical solutions that support inclusive growth while addressing systemic barriers that often limit innovation and entrepreneurship across the continent. Policy Challenges Participants Will Address Through the simulation, participants will work on policy challenges connected to: 1. Youth Employment and Skills Development Participants will explore policies that can: Reduce youth unemployment Improve workforce readiness Strengthen technical and vocational education Enhance employability and entrepreneurship opportunities 2. Innovation and Commercialization Teams will examine strategies for: Supporting innovators and startups Commercializing research and innovation Building stronger innovation ecosystems Scaling locally developed solutions 3. Digital Transformation Participants will develop ideas related to: Digital inclusion Emerging technologies Digital entrepreneurship Technology-driven public services 4. Governance and Institutional Reform The program challenges participants to consider: Effective governance structures Public sector reforms Accountability systems Institutional efficiency 5. Financing and Donor Coordination Teams will analyze ways to: Mobilize development financing Improve donor coordination Strengthen resource allocation Increase investment effectiveness Experience Real-World Policymaking One of the most exciting aspects of the ACET Youth Policy Lab is its realism. Participants will not simply generate ideas; they will navigate the same challenges policymakers face every day, including: Limited national budgets IMF restrictions Political pressures Competing stakeholder interests Resource constraints Implementation challenges This approach ensures participants gain practical experience in balancing ambition with reality. Why You Should Apply The ACET Youth Policy Lab offers a wide range of professional and leadership benefits. Build Practical Policy Skills Participants gain hands-on experience in: Policy analysis Research Strategic thinking Public problem-solving Evidence-based policymaking Receive Expert Mentorship Selected participants will receive guidance from leading African experts and practitioners. Mentors will help teams refine ideas, strengthen proposals, and improve policy recommendations. Collaborate Across Africa Participants will work with talented young leaders from different countries and backgrounds. This cross-cultural collaboration strengthens teamwork and exposes participants to diverse perspectives. Develop Leadership Skills The program helps participants enhance: Communication skills Decision-making abilities Negotiation techniques Leadership capacity Create a Policy Proposal Each team will develop a comprehensive three-page policy proposal that addresses a critical development challenge. Pitch Your Ideas Participants will present their solutions during a live virtual pitch event before experts and judges. Gain Access to Future Opportunities The program offers pathways to: Internship opportunities Ambassador roles Professional mentorship Regional visibility Recognition across ACET platforms Additional Benefits for Winning Participants Winning participants will receive: Cash vouchers Internship opportunities Mentorship support Certificates of participation and achievement Regional recognition through ACET networks and platforms These rewards are designed to support participants continued growth and leadership development. How the ACET Youth Policy Lab Works The program follows a structured journey that combines learning, collaboration, coaching, and competition. Step 1: Application Stage Young Africans submit their applications and demonstrate their interest in policy innovation and leadership. Step 2: Team Formation Selected applicants are grouped into six teams, each consisting of five participants. Step 3: Mentorship and Coaching Teams participate in mentorship sessions and receive guidance from experts. Step 4: Policy Development Participants collaborate to design evidence-based policy solutions and prepare their proposals. Step 5: Virtual Pitch Event Teams present their recommendations during the final virtual pitch competition. Step 6: Winners Announcement Top-performing teams are recognized and rewarded. Step 7: YES Ambassador Program Participants may have opportunities to join a regional youth network through the YES Ambassador Program. Eligibility Criteria To apply, candidates must meet the following requirements: Age Requirement Applicants must be between 18 and 35 years old. Citizenship Requirement Applicants must be citizens of African countries. Language Requirement Applicants must be fluent in either: English French Commitment Requirement Applicants must be able to dedicate approximately 4–6 hours weekly throughout the program. Important Dates Applications Open 15 June 2026 Application Deadline 7 July 2026 Team Shortlisting 8 July – 31 July 2026 Team Interviews 1 August – 31 August 2026 Participant Onboarding 1 September – 18 September 2026 Coaching and Mentorship Period 21 September – 16 October 2026 Grand Finale and Virtual Pitch Event 4 November 2026 Winners Announcement Following the final pitch event. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the Online Application Form through the official ACET Youth Policy Lab portal . For inquiries: youthpolicylab@acetforafrica.org Applicants are encouraged to apply early and carefully review all program information before submitting their applications. Why This Opportunity Matters for Africa s Future Africa has the world s youngest population, making youth participation in policymaking essential for sustainable development. The ACET Youth Policy Lab recognizes that young people are not merely beneficiaries of policy decisions; they are innovators, entrepreneurs, problem-solvers, and future leaders capable of driving transformative change. By equipping young Africans with practical policymaking experience, leadership training, and access to expert mentorship, the program contributes to building a stronger generation of leaders who can shape inclusive and prosperous futures across the continent. Visit HERE to learn more about ACET Youth Policy Lab 2026. Conclusion The ACET Youth Policy Lab 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity for ambitious young Africans to gain hands-on experience in policymaking, innovation, leadership, and economic transformation. Through collaboration, mentorship, policy simulation, and competitive pitching, participants will develop the skills needed to influence real-world change and contribute meaningfully to Africa s development agenda. For young leaders passionate about governance, innovation, entrepreneurship, public policy, and sustainable development, this program offers a unique platform to learn from experts, connect with peers across Africa, and transform ideas into impactful policy solutions. Interested candidates should submit their applications before the 7 July 2026 deadline and take the next step toward becoming part of Africa s next generation of changemakers. title: WHO Youth Council 2026–2028: Global Call for Youth Organizations to Shape International Health Policy
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has officially launched a global call for expressions of interest for the third term of the WHO Youth Council (2026–2028). This exciting opportunity invites youth-led and youth-focused organizations from around the world to play a direct role in influencing global health discussions, policies, and strategies. As one of WHO s flagship youth engagement platforms, the WHO Youth Council provides an avenue for young people and youth organizations to contribute meaningfully to international health governance. Through advocacy, collaboration, innovation, and policy engagement, selected organizations will help strengthen youth participation in shaping healthier and more resilient communities worldwide. Organizations interested in becoming part of this influential network are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline and carefully review all eligibility requirements. About the WHO Youth Council The WHO Youth Council was established to strengthen youth engagement within the World Health Organization by creating a structured platform through which young people can contribute to health-related decision-making processes. The Council serves multiple purposes, including: Amplifying youth voices in global health discussions Providing insights from young people on emerging health challenges Supporting WHO s health promotion and advocacy initiatives Encouraging innovative youth-led solutions to public health issues Strengthening collaboration between youth organizations and international health stakeholders Promoting youth participation in health systems and policy development The Council reflects WHO s commitment to ensuring that young people are not merely beneficiaries of health policies but active contributors to the design and implementation of solutions that affect their lives and communities. Why the WHO Youth Council Matters Young people represent a significant proportion of the global population and are increasingly recognized as critical stakeholders in addressing public health challenges. Through the WHO Youth Council, participating organizations can: Influence Global Health Policies Council members have opportunities to provide perspectives and recommendations that inform WHO strategies and initiatives. Elevate Youth Priorities Organizations can ensure that issues affecting young people are represented in international health conversations. Strengthen Global Networks Members gain access to a diverse network of youth organizations, health advocates, experts, and policymakers from around the world. Promote Youth Leadership The Council provides a platform for organizations to demonstrate leadership and advocate for meaningful youth participation in health governance. Contribute Innovative Solutions Organizations can share innovative approaches and experiences that support stronger and more inclusive health systems. Who Is WHO Looking For? WHO is seeking a diverse and representative group of organizations from across the globe. Eligible organizations include: 1. Youth-Led Organizations Organizations where young people hold leadership positions and drive decision-making processes. 2. Youth-Focused Organizations Organizations that primarily work to support, empower, or advocate for young people. 3. Youth Chapters of Larger Organizations Youth branches or youth wings operating within larger national or international organizations. WHO has also indicated its interest in selecting a balanced mix of organizations from both: Health-related sectors Non-health sectors This multidisciplinary approach ensures diverse perspectives and strengthens the Council s ability to address complex public health challenges. Eligibility Requirements To qualify for membership, organizations must satisfy all requirements outlined in the revised WHO Youth Council Terms of Reference. Key eligibility expectations include: Active engagement at the international level Demonstrated commitment to youth engagement and participation Alignment with WHO values and objectives Capacity to contribute meaningfully to Council activities Compliance with WHO membership requirements Applicants are strongly encouraged to thoroughly review the Terms of Reference before submitting their application. WHO Civil Society Commission Requirement An important requirement for participation in the WHO Youth Council is membership in the WHO Civil Society Commission. WHO has announced that all Youth Council members will also be expected to participate in the WHO Civil Society Commission. Organizations that are not already members must: Submit an application to join the WHO Civil Society Commission. Complete this step before submitting their WHO Youth Council expression of interest. WHO has clarified that applications to the Youth Council can still be considered while the organization s Civil Society Commission application is under review. This requirement aims to strengthen collaboration between youth organizations and broader civil society stakeholders engaged in global health initiatives. Application Process Organizations wishing to apply must complete all required application components. Step 1: Complete the WHO Youth Council Application Form Applicants must fill out the official online application form and provide all requested information. Step 2: Submit the Tobacco-Arms Disclosure Form In addition to the application form, organizations must complete and submit the Tobacco-Arms Disclosure Form. Step 3: Ensure Compliance with Eligibility Requirements Applications will be evaluated based on: Compliance with eligibility criteria Organizational experience and track record Motivation for joining the Council Proposed plans and contributions Diversity and representation considerations Organizations should provide clear and compelling information demonstrating how they can contribute to the Council s mission and objectives. APPLY HERE Selection Criteria WHO will assess applications using several factors, including: Organizational Relevance The organization s work and activities should align with youth engagement and meaningful participation. Experience Applicants should demonstrate relevant experience in advocacy, leadership, public health, youth development, community engagement, or related areas. Motivation Organizations should clearly explain why they wish to join the Council and how they plan to contribute. Diversity WHO seeks broad geographic, thematic, and organizational representation to ensure that multiple perspectives are reflected within the Council. Important Dates Application Deadline 30 June 2026 at 23:59 CEST Organizations are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical challenges. First In-Person Meeting October 2026 Selected organizations will participate in the Council s first in-person meeting, marking the beginning of the 2026–2028 term. Documents Applicants Must Review Before applying, organizations should carefully read and complete the following documents: WHO Youth Council Terms of Reference Tobacco-Arms Disclosure Form Reviewing these materials is essential for understanding the Council s responsibilities, expectations, and operational framework. Benefits of Joining the WHO Youth Council Participation in the WHO Youth Council offers several valuable advantages: Opportunity to engage directly with WHO Influence international health policy discussions Amplify youth voices at the global level Collaborate with youth organizations worldwide Strengthen advocacy and leadership capacity Expand international partnerships and networks Contribute to global public health initiatives Participate in high-level dialogues and consultations Increase organizational visibility within the global health ecosystem Support meaningful youth participation in health systems strengthening How to Prepare a Strong Application Organizations seeking selection should consider the following strategies: Demonstrate Impact Highlight measurable achievements and successful initiatives led by your organization. Showcase Youth Leadership Clearly explain how young people participate in leadership and decision-making processes. Emphasize Global Engagement Illustrate international partnerships, collaborations, or activities that demonstrate global reach. Present Clear Goals Explain how your organization intends to contribute to the Council s work during the 2026–2028 term. Align with WHO Priorities Demonstrate a commitment to health equity, inclusion, youth participation, and sustainable development. Interested organizations are required to complete the online WHO Youth Council Application Form . Click HERE to learn more about the WHO Youth Council 2026–2028. Conclusion The WHO Youth Council 2026–2028 presents an exceptional opportunity for youth-led and youth-focused organizations to engage directly with one of the world s most influential health institutions. Through this platform, organizations can help shape health policies, advocate for youth priorities, contribute innovative ideas, and strengthen youth participation in global health governance. Organizations from around the world that are passionate about advancing youth engagement and improving public health outcomes should take advantage of this opportunity and submit their applications before the 30 June 2026 deadline. Participation in the WHO Youth Council offers not only global visibility and networking opportunities but also a meaningful chance to influence the future of international health policy and practice. Discover more global Fellowship , Health and Leadership Development opportunities on OFY. title: PhD Scholarship Opportunity: Future Rural Africa Project (Subproject B03 “Violent Futures”) in Tanzania & Kenya – Fully Funded Ethnographic Research Position
summary: The Future Rural Africa Project is inviting applications for a highly competitive PhD scholarship under its Subproject B03 titled “Violent Futures.” This research-focused doctoral opportunity is designed for scholars interested in understanding how emerging carbon credit initiatives influence social relations, conflict dynamics, and future-making processes in rural African contexts, particularly in Tanzania and Kenya . This is a long-term, field-intensive academic opportunity ideal for candidates with strong interests in anthropology, political ecology, development studies, and conflict research. The project places special emphasis on ethnographic fieldwork , meaning selected candidates will engage in deep, immersive research within communities affected by carbon credit and climate-related development initiatives. About the Research Project: “Violent Futures” The Subproject B03 “Violent Futures” investigates the complex relationship between future-oriented carbon credit schemes and their real-world impacts on social structures, land use, and conflict formation in East Africa. Key Research Focus Areas The PhD candidate will contribute to understanding: Carbon Credit Projects and Social Transformation How carbon credit and climate mitigation initiatives reshape rural economies The role of global climate markets in local governance systems Conflict and Social Relations Emerging tensions between communities, institutions, and investors Land access disputes linked to environmental and conservation policies Ethnographic Fieldwork in Tanzania and Kenya Long-term immersion in rural communities Qualitative data collection including interviews, participant observation, and field notes Future-Making and Environmental Governance How communities imagine and negotiate their futures under climate interventions Power relations between local actors and international climate finance structures Scholarship Details This PhD scholarship offers a structured research environment with financial support for the full duration of the program. Key Facts Duration: 41 months Monthly stipend: €1,475 Start date: Ideally 1 August 2026 Application deadline: 21 June 2026 What the Opportunity Offers This PhD position provides a unique combination of academic training, field experience, and financial support. Key benefits include: Long-term funded doctoral research Access to a major interdisciplinary research project Opportunity to conduct fieldwork in Tanzania and Kenya Engagement with global debates on climate justice and carbon markets Development of advanced ethnographic and qualitative research skills Collaboration with international researchers and institutions Application Deadline All applications must be submitted by: 21 June 2026 Late submissions will not be considered, so applicants are encouraged to prepare their documents early. Ideal Candidate Profile This opportunity is best suited for candidates who demonstrate: Strong academic background in social sciences or related disciplines Interest in anthropology, political ecology, environmental studies, or development studies Experience or strong willingness to conduct ethnographic fieldwork Analytical interest in climate change, governance, and conflict studies Ability to work independently in field environments in East Africa Strong writing and research skills at postgraduate level Application Link Click here for more and to apply For more global scholarship opportunities, Click here The post PhD Scholarship Opportunity: Future Rural Africa Project (Subproject B03 “Violent Futures”) in Tanzania Kenya – Fully Funded Ethnographic Research Position appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Boston College Connell School of Nursing Ph.D. Program 2027: Fully Funded Nursing Doctorate in the USA for Future Nurse Scientists, Educators, Researchers, and Policy Leaders
summary: The Boston College Connell School of Nursing (CSON) is inviting applications for its prestigious Ph.D. Program in Nursing, a fully funded doctoral program designed to prepare the next generation of nurse scientists, educators, researchers, and healthcare policy leaders. Located at Boston College in Massachusetts, United States, the program combines advanced scientific inquiry, nursing theory, and rigorous research training to equip scholars with the knowledge and expertise needed to transform healthcare systems and improve patient outcomes globally. One of the most attractive features of the program is its comprehensive financial support package. The Connell School of Nursing fully funds tuition, fees, and health insurance for all full-time Ph.D. students during their first three years of study, making it one of the most competitive nursing doctoral opportunities available. With a strong emphasis on research excellence, leadership development, and interdisciplinary collaboration, graduates emerge prepared to influence healthcare policy, conduct groundbreaking nursing research, educate future healthcare professionals, and lead innovation across healthcare institutions worldwide. About the Boston College Connell School of Nursing Ph.D. Program The Connell School of Nursing Ph.D. Program integrates science, theory, and research methodologies to prepare highly skilled nurse scientists capable of addressing complex healthcare challenges. The program attracts students from diverse academic, clinical, and professional backgrounds who share a commitment to advancing nursing science and improving healthcare delivery. Students work closely with distinguished faculty members whose expertise spans numerous healthcare and nursing disciplines. Throughout their doctoral journey, candidates receive mentorship, research guidance, and professional development opportunities designed to support successful academic and professional careers. Program Highlights Fully Funded Doctoral Education Every full-time Ph.D. student receives: Full tuition coverage Mandatory fees coverage Health insurance coverage Financial support for the first three years of study This funding package significantly reduces financial barriers and allows students to focus fully on their academic and research pursuits. Duration of Study Students generally complete the Ph.D. program within four years. Program Start Date The program begins each Fall semester. Academic Structure Most students complete: 20 courses 46 total academic credits The curriculum is designed to progressively develop research expertise, analytical thinking, and advanced nursing scholarship. Curriculum Overview The doctoral curriculum combines foundational nursing science with advanced research methods and statistical analysis. First-Year Core Courses Fall Semester Evidence Appraisal and Synthesis Philosophical Inquiry for Knowledge Development in Nursing Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis Survey of Research Methods in Social and Behavioral Science Spring Semester Strategies for Knowledge Development Advanced Qualitative Research Methods Regression Analysis for Social and Behavioral Science These courses establish a strong foundation in research design, statistical analysis, evidence-based practice, and theoretical development. Research Opportunities A major strength of the Connell School Ph.D. Program is its extensive focus on research. Students actively participate in scholarly activities and contribute to studies addressing critical healthcare challenges such as: Public health and health systems Chronic disease management Mental health Healthcare quality and safety Nursing ethics Genomic healthcare disparities Substance use and chronic pain management Doctoral candidates regularly present their findings at national and international conferences and publish in respected academic journals. Many students also receive prestigious honors and recognition, including induction into the American Academy of Nursing and selection as Jonas Center for Nursing Excellence Scholars. Distinguished Faculty Mentorship Students benefit from mentorship by internationally recognized nursing scholars and researchers. title: Lululemon Community Wellbeing Grant 2027: Comprehensive Guide for Global Non‑Profits Advancing Movement & Wellbeing
summary: Overview of the Lululemon Community Wellbeing Grant 2027 The Community Wellbeing Grant , powered by lululemon Gives , is a global annual grant program designed to support community‑led charitable organizations that advance physical, mental, and social wellbeing through movement. Since 2016, lululemon has invested in community resilience by funding organizations that create inclusive access to wellbeing practices. In 2025, lululemon achieved its five‑year goal of investing $75 million USD , impacting over 10 million people worldwide. The company is now committing an additional $100 million to reach 20 million more people by 2030 . The 2027 Community Wellbeing Grant continues this mission by offering financial support, optional wellbeing resources, and a collaborative community for organizations working to remove barriers to wellbeing. Grant Amount and Funding Structure Organizations may apply for up to $50,000 USD , with the following conditions: The requested amount must not exceed 40% of the organization’s most recently completed fiscal year operating budget. Grants are administered through lululemon’s Donor‑Advised Fund at Charities Aid Foundation America (CAFA) . Organizations operating in China Mainland will receive funding directly from lululemon China . The grant is a one‑year program with optional wellbeing support offerings throughout the cycle. Lululemon’s Definition of Wellbeing Lululemon defines wellbeing as a lifetime practice of three interconnected elements: Physical Wellbeing – Feeling empowered to give the body what it needs for health and quality of life. Mental Wellbeing – Feeling emotionally prepared and able to handle the future. Social Wellbeing – Feeling connected, supported, and part of a larger community. Organizations must advance wellbeing through movement programming to qualify. Eligibility Criteria Organizations must meet all of the following: Be a registered non‑profit or charity , or be fiscally sponsored by one. Advance wellbeing by creating equitable access to movement programming . Be community‑led and serve communities experiencing barriers to wellbeing. Operate in one or more of the following countries: Australia, Canada, China Mainland, France, Germany, Hong Kong SAR, India, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Macau SAR, Malaysia, Mexico, Korea, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, UK, USA, Vietnam. Have an annual budget under $3 million USD (priority consideration). Organizations NOT Eligible Lululemon does not fund: Individuals, religious groups, or third‑party fundraisers Political, legislative, or military‑related initiatives Hospitals, clinics, or health services accepting direct payment Schools, PTAs, libraries, museums, or academic institutions Government entities, private foundations, or registered businesses Organizations funded by lululemon for three consecutive years Organizations with budgets over $10 million USD Organizations with fewer than three board members Organizations operating programming for less than one year Grant Funds Cannot Be Used For One‑time events, retreats, workshops, or sponsorships Regranting or scholarships Lobbying or incentives for government officials Benefits to lululemon or its employees Real estate, endowments, or interest‑bearing accounts Equipment or capital assets totaling $5,000 USD or more Timeline Deadlines Registration Period June 1 – July 24, 2026 (5:00 PM PT) Organizations must complete a registration form to verify eligibility. Eligibility notifications are typically sent within 72 hours . Registration after July 24 disqualifies organizations from applying. Selection Period October 19, 2026 Applicants receive selection notifications. Awards are conditional pending CAFA validation. Documentation CAFA Eligibility Application October 19 – November 13, 2026 Selected organizations must sign a Relationship Agreement. CAFA will request documentation and conduct due diligence. title: Fulbright Scholarship Australia 2026: Fully Funded Opportunity to Study, Research, and Build Global Networks in the United States
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious Fulbright Scholarship Australia 2026 , one of the most respected international scholarship programs in the world. The scholarship provides Australian students, researchers, professionals, and scholars with the opportunity to undertake study, research, teaching, or professional development in the United States while building long-term academic, professional, and cultural connections. Established to strengthen mutual understanding between Australia and the United States, the Fulbright Program has transformed the careers of thousands of scholars by providing access to leading universities, world-class research institutions, and influential professional networks. Whether you are pursuing postgraduate studies, conducting advanced research, developing innovative solutions to global challenges, or expanding your professional expertise, the Fulbright Scholarship offers substantial financial support and a life-changing international experience. About the Fulbright Scholarship Program The Fulbright Program was established in Australia in 1949 through a binational treaty between the Australian and United States Governments, inspired by the vision of U.S. Senator J. William Fulbright. Today, the program is administered by the Australian-American Fulbright Commission and remains one of the world s most prestigious international exchange initiatives. The mission of the Fulbright Program is to promote: Educational exchange Research collaboration Cultural understanding Academic excellence Professional development Long-term partnerships between Australia and the United States Over the decades, Fulbright alumni have gone on to become leaders in government, academia, science, business, technology, healthcare, arts, and international affairs. Why the Fulbright Scholarship Is So Prestigious The Fulbright Scholarship is far more than a funding opportunity. It is a globally recognized program that provides scholars with: Access to leading U.S. universities International research collaborations Professional networking opportunities Leadership development Cultural exchange experiences Global recognition and credibility Lifelong membership in the Fulbright alumni network The program emphasizes not only academic achievement but also the ability of scholars to act as ambassadors who strengthen relationships between nations. Scholarship Benefits Fulbright Scholarships provide extensive financial and professional support. Benefits vary depending on the specific award category and level of study, but generally include: Monthly Living Stipend Recipients receive a monthly stipend based on the cost of living in the city where their host institution is located. This support helps cover: Accommodation Meals Transportation Daily living expenses Tuition Support Depending on the scholarship category, recipients may receive: Partial tuition support for one academic year, or Full tuition support under selected awards such as the Fulbright Future Award Round-Trip International Airfare The scholarship covers: ✈️ Economy-class return airfare from the scholar s home city in Australia to the host institution in the United States. Establishment Allowance Recipients receive financial assistance to help settle into their new academic environment upon arrival. Dependent Allowance Where applicable, additional support may be available for eligible dependents accompanying the scholar. title: Lisle International Global Seed Grants 2026: Funding Opportunity for Intercultural Exchange and Global Citizenship Projects Worldwide
summary: Organizations working to promote intercultural understanding, global citizenship, international collaboration, and meaningful cross-cultural experiences now have an exciting opportunity to secure funding through the Lisle International Global Seed Grants 2026 . Lisle International has officially announced the opening of its Global Seed Grant application process, providing support for innovative projects that align with its mission of building world citizens through intercultural engagement and international understanding. The Global Seed Grant program is designed to help organizations launch, strengthen, and expand initiatives that foster meaningful connections across cultures, communities, and countries. Through a structured two-phase application process, selected organizations can access funding and personalized mentorship to help transform promising ideas into impactful projects. Organizations interested in applying should prepare early, as the Request to Apply (RTA) submission window may close before the official deadline if a high volume of applications is received. About Lisle International Lisle International is dedicated to supporting a global community of changemakers by promoting intercultural experiences, international collaboration, and global citizenship. Through its grant programs and international network, the organization helps individuals and institutions develop projects that bridge cultures, encourage understanding, and contribute to positive global engagement. Its flagship Global Seed Grant program provides financial support and mentoring to organizations working to create transformative intercultural initiatives around the world. What Are the Global Seed Grants? The Global Seed Grants are competitive funding opportunities designed to support projects that align with Lisle International’s mission and values. These grants aim to: Promote intercultural understanding Foster international collaboration Encourage global citizenship Support innovative educational initiatives Build connections across diverse communities Strengthen cross-cultural learning experiences Empower organizations working for positive social impact The program is particularly interested in supporting projects that demonstrate creativity, sustainability, and meaningful engagement among participants from different cultural backgrounds. How the Grant Process Works The Global Seed Grant program uses a two-phase application process . This approach allows Lisle International to identify promising projects before inviting selected applicants to submit comprehensive proposals. Phase One: Request to Apply (RTA) The first step involves submitting a Request to Apply (RTA) through Lisle International’s online grant portal. During this stage, applicants provide information about: Their organization Project concept Expected impact Alignment with Lisle International s mission Project goals and objectives The RTA serves as an initial screening process. Lisle reviews all submissions and identifies projects that demonstrate strong potential and alignment with the organization s values. Only applicants whose RTAs are approved will move forward to the second phase. Why the RTA Matters The Request to Apply is not merely an expression of interest. It serves as a critical evaluation stage where reviewers assess: Project relevance Feasibility Innovation Potential impact Organizational capacity Alignment with grant priorities Organizations should therefore invest time in preparing a strong and thoughtful RTA submission. Phase Two: Full Proposal Submission Organizations that successfully pass the RTA stage will receive an invitation to submit a full proposal. This stage allows applicants to provide more detailed information about: Project design Implementation strategy Expected outcomes Budget Monitoring and evaluation plans Sustainability measures The full proposal provides reviewers with a comprehensive understanding of the project s objectives and potential impact. Dedicated Grant Mentor Support One of the most valuable features of the Lisle International Global Seed Grant program is the mentorship component. Applicants invited to submit a full proposal are assigned a Lisle Grant Mentor . What Does a Grant Mentor Do? The mentor helps applicants: Navigate the application process Refine project concepts Strengthen proposal quality Align projects with Lisle s mission and values Clarify application requirements Address questions and concerns The mentor serves as a dedicated point of contact throughout the proposal development process. This personalized support helps organizations present stronger and more competitive grant applications. Funding Focus While Lisle International emphasizes intercultural engagement and global citizenship, applicants should carefully review the eligibility criteria to ensure that their proposed projects align with the organization s mission. Projects may involve: International education Cross-cultural exchange Global citizenship development Youth engagement Community partnerships International collaboration Cultural understanding initiatives Educational exchanges Leadership development Social impact projects with intercultural components Organizations are encouraged to explore Lisle s eligibility requirements before beginning their applications. Important Application Dates Request to Apply (RTA) Opens 📅 5 June 2026 Request to Apply (RTA) Deadline 📅 30 June 2026 However, applicants should note that: The RTA portal may close earlier than the advertised deadline if a high volume of submissions is received. For this reason, organizations are strongly encouraged to submit as early as possible. Notification of RTA Results 📅 Before the end of July 2026 Selected applicants will receive invitations to proceed to the full proposal stage. Full Proposal Deadline 📅 1 September 2026 Only organizations invited after the RTA review process may submit full proposals. Grant Recipient Announcement 📅 30 November 2026 Successful Global Seed Grant recipients will be selected during the annual Lisle Meeting and officially announced by the end of November. Project Implementation Period Funded projects are expected to be implemented during the following calendar year. Project Timeline 📅 1 January – 31 December (Project Year) Organizations should plan their activities within this implementation period. Application Deadline Timing Both the Request to Apply and the Full Proposal (for invited applicants) must be submitted no later than: 🕛 11:59 PM U.S. Eastern Time Applicants should carefully account for time zone differences when planning their submissions. Why Organizations Should Apply The Lisle International Global Seed Grant offers several significant advantages beyond funding. Financial Support Selected organizations receive seed funding to launch or strengthen impactful projects. Professional Mentorship Applicants gain access to experienced grant mentors who provide valuable guidance throughout the process. Global Network Access Organizations become connected to a broader community of changemakers and intercultural practitioners. Increased Visibility Successful projects benefit from association with a respected international organization dedicated to global citizenship. Capacity Building The structured application and mentoring process helps organizations improve project planning and grant-writing skills. Tips for a Strong Application Organizations interested in applying should: 1. Demonstrate Clear Alignment Show how the project directly supports intercultural understanding and global citizenship. 2. Focus on Impact Clearly explain the difference the project will make and who will benefit. 3. Be Specific Provide concrete objectives, activities, and outcomes rather than broad ideas. 4. Highlight Sustainability Explain how project benefits will continue after the grant period. 5. Submit Early Because the RTA portal may close before the official deadline, early submission is highly recommended. How to Apply All applications must be submitted through Lisle International s official grant portal known as Submit . Applications sent through any other method will not be considered. Organizations should carefully review the eligibility requirements and preview application materials before beginning the submission process. Contact Information For questions regarding the grant program: 📧 office@lisleinternational.org 📍 Lisle International 539 W. Commerce St #1782 Dallas, TX 75208 United States Apply Here Final Thoughts The Lisle International Global Seed Grants 2026 present an outstanding opportunity for organizations dedicated to fostering intercultural understanding, international collaboration, and global citizenship. With a supportive mentorship model, a transparent application process, and a commitment to empowering changemakers worldwide, the program offers more than funding—it provides a pathway for organizations to expand their impact and contribute to a more connected and understanding world. Organizations with innovative projects are encouraged to prepare early and submit their Request to Apply before the application window closes. title: Johns Hopkins SAIS Public Service Fellows & Scholars Scholarships 2026–2027: Study in Washington DC with Up to 100% Tuition Funding for Future Global Leaders
summary: Are you passionate about public service, international development, diplomacy, human rights, climate action, national security, social justice, refugee issues, or global policy? Do you aspire to build a meaningful career that contributes to solving some of the world s most pressing challenges? The Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) is offering an exceptional opportunity for future and current public service leaders through its prestigious Public Service Fellows Scholarship Program and Public Service Scholars Scholarship Program. These highly competitive scholarships support outstanding students pursuing graduate studies in international relations and public policy at one of the world s leading institutions for global affairs. The programs provide substantial tuition support, leadership development opportunities, exclusive networking events, and direct engagement with public service practitioners and policymakers. Whether you are an early-career professional seeking a fully funded master s degree or a mid-career professional looking to strengthen your policy expertise, these scholarships can help accelerate your impact and career growth. About Johns Hopkins SAIS The Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) is part of Johns Hopkins University, America s first research university, established in 1876. Located in Washington, DC, SAIS is globally recognized for excellence in: International Relations Public Policy Diplomacy International Economics Security Studies Development Studies Global Governance Its strategic location in the United States capital provides students with direct access to policymakers, diplomats, international organizations, think tanks, and development institutions. What Are the Public Service Fellows and Scholars Programs? The Public Service Fellows and Scholars Programs were created to support talented individuals dedicated to serving society through careers in public policy, government, nonprofit leadership, international development, diplomacy, and social impact. The programs aim to: Promote leadership in public service. Support talented students from diverse backgrounds. Encourage innovative approaches to policy challenges. Foster engagement with public service practitioners. Build a community of future changemakers. Johns Hopkins SAIS specifically seeks applicants who are: Culturally aware. Adaptable. Strategic thinkers. Effective problem-solvers. Committed to public service. The programs welcome individuals interested in fields such as: Human Rights Diplomacy National Security International Development Climate Change Refugee Issues Gender Diversity Social Justice Public Policy Public Service Fellows Scholarship Program Overview The Public Service Fellows Scholarship Program is designed for highly talented graduate students pursuing the Master of Arts in International Relations (MAIR) at the Johns Hopkins SAIS Washington, DC campus. The program supports individuals who aspire to build careers dedicated to public service and global leadership. Public Service Fellows Scholarship Benefits Selected Fellows receive: 1. Full Tuition Scholarship Recipients receive: 100% tuition coverage during the first year. Renewal for the second year upon meeting academic requirements. Funding for up to four semesters. 2. Exclusive Professional Programming Participants gain access to: Leadership lectures. Policy seminars. Public service workshops. Special networking events. 3. Access to Influential Leaders Fellows engage directly with: Policy experts. Public sector leaders. Alumni. Government officials. International practitioners. 4. Career Development Support The Office of Global Careers provides: Career coaching. Public service career guidance. Professional networking opportunities. Internship and employment support. 5. Community and Volunteer Engagement Participants join social and volunteer activities designed to build: Leadership skills. Teamwork. Civic engagement. Professional relationships. Public Service Fellows Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be citizens of any country. Gain admission to the Master of Arts in International Relations (MAIR) program in Washington, DC. Demonstrate leadership potential. Show academic excellence. Demonstrate commitment to public service through professional experience or academic work. Special consideration is given to applicants who demonstrate financial need. Public Service Fellows Program Requirements Recipients must: Remain full-time MAIR students. Maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.4 or higher. Participate in at least one admissions recruitment activity each semester. Complete semester and final program surveys. Submit the Office of Global Careers Employment Outcomes Survey before graduation. Public Service Fellows Application Process Applicants must: Apply for admission to the MAIR program. Indicate interest in institutional financial aid. Indicate interest in a Public Service Award. Submit: Financial Aid Application. Scholarship Essay. U.S. citizens and permanent residents must complete the FAFSA using school code E00474. Public Service Scholars Scholarship Program Overview The Public Service Scholars Scholarship Program is intended for experienced mid-career professionals pursuing the Master of International Public Policy (MIPP). Applicants should have prior experience in public service and intend to continue serving communities and institutions after graduation. The scholarship is available only to Fall applicants. Public Service Scholars Benefits Selected Scholars receive: 1. Significant Tuition Support Recipients receive: Up to 50% tuition scholarship. 2. Exclusive Leadership Programming Participants gain access to: Public policy seminars. Leadership workshops. Professional networking events. Public service discussions. 3. Career Advancement Opportunities Participants receive: Guidance from the Office of Global Careers. Access to influential networks. Mentorship opportunities. Career development support. 4. Community Building Activities Scholars participate in: Volunteer initiatives. Networking events. Cohort activities. Public Service Scholars Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be citizens of any country. Be admitted to the MIPP program at the Washington, DC campus. Be enrolled full-time or part-time (minimum of two courses per semester). Demonstrate leadership and professional achievement. Show commitment to public service. Special consideration is also given to applicants with demonstrated financial need. Public Service Scholars Requirements Recipients must: Begin studies during the Fall semester. Maintain a GPA of 3.4 or higher. Participate in recruitment activities or mentor Public Service Fellows. Complete required surveys. Submit employment outcome reports before graduation. Why You Should Apply This scholarship program offers far more than tuition support. Participants gain: Access to one of the world s leading international affairs schools. Study opportunities in Washington, DC. Connections with global leaders and policymakers. Leadership development experiences. Career acceleration opportunities. Public service-focused mentorship. Exposure to real-world policy challenges. Graduates are positioned for impactful careers in: Government International Organizations NGOs Public Policy Institutions Human Rights Organizations Development Agencies Think Tanks Diplomatic Services Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion Johns Hopkins SAIS strongly values diversity and welcomes applicants from: Different socioeconomic backgrounds. First-generation students. Historically underrepresented groups. Diverse cultures and nationalities. All genders and identities. The institution believes diverse experiences strengthen public service leadership and policymaking. Information Sessions Prospective applicants are encouraged to attend Public Service Information Sessions hosted by admissions representatives and current students. These sessions provide insights into: Academic programs. Student life. Scholarship opportunities. Career pathways. Financial aid options. Visit HERE to learn more about the Johns Hopkins SAIS Public Service Fellows Scholars Scholarships 2026–2027. Conclusion The Johns Hopkins SAIS Public Service Fellows and Public Service Scholars Scholarships represent a remarkable opportunity for individuals committed to creating meaningful change through public service. With tuition support of up to 100%, access to world-class education in Washington, DC, exclusive leadership programming, career development support, and a global network of policymakers and practitioners, these programs are designed to empower the next generation of leaders tackling today s most complex global challenges. title: Fully Funded PhD Position in Human Geography at the University of Zurich, Switzerland (2026): Join a Groundbreaking SNSF Research Project on Educational Inequality, Racism, and Classism
summary: Are you passionate about social justice, educational equality, youth studies, and qualitative research? The Department of Geography at the University of Zurich (UZH) is inviting applications for a fully funded PhD Position in Human Geography as part of an innovative Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) research project examining institutional racism and classism within highly selective secondary schools in Switzerland. This exceptional doctoral opportunity offers aspiring researchers the chance to contribute to cutting-edge research, pursue a doctoral degree within a structured graduate program, engage with young people and educational institutions, and develop an academic career in one of Europe s leading universities. The position is offered at 80% employment and is scheduled to begin on 1 October 2026 or by mutual agreement. About the University of Zurich The University of Zurich (UZH) is the largest university in Switzerland, with approximately 30,000 students and over 10,000 employees. Renowned for its excellence in research, innovation, and teaching, UZH provides an intellectually stimulating environment where doctoral researchers can thrive. Located in Zurich, one of the world s most livable cities, UZH offers outstanding academic resources, international collaboration opportunities, and a vibrant multicultural atmosphere. About the Research Project The successful candidate will join the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project titled: Institutional Conditions for Racially and/or Socio-Economically Minoritized Students at Highly Selective Secondary Schools in Switzerland. The project is led by Dr. Sara Landolt , Principal Investigator and researcher at the Department of Geography. Research Context Educational systems across many Western societies continue to reproduce social inequalities. In Switzerland, racially and socio-economically minoritized students remain significantly underrepresented in academically selective state-funded secondary schools known as Gymnasia. Existing international research suggests that students from marginalized backgrounds often experience institutional discrimination, including: Racism Classism Social exclusion Structural inequalities Barriers to educational advancement Despite growing awareness of these issues, there remains limited research exploring how institutional racism and classism operate within highly selective educational environments. Main Aim of the Project The project seeks to deepen understanding of: Institutional racism in education Institutional classism The intersection of race and socio-economic inequalities Strategies for preventing discrimination Practices that promote inclusive educational environments The research adopts a post-structuralist processual perspective inspired by the work of Ahmed (2012). Research Objectives The study pursues several important objectives: 1. Investigating the Reproduction of Inequality The project seeks to uncover the underlying mechanisms that reproduce: Racism Classism Intersecting forms of discrimination Resistance to discriminatory practices within Gymnasia in German-speaking Switzerland. 2. Identifying Effective Practices Researchers will explore successful initiatives already implemented within schools to address and reduce: Racism Socio-economic exclusion Educational inequalities 3. Understanding Student Experiences The project aims to understand: How institutional discrimination affects students How students respond to and navigate discriminatory environments Strategies students use to cope with and challenge inequalities 4. Supporting Educational Change Findings will be shared with school leaders to help create educational environments that are free from racism and classism. Responsibilities of the PhD Researcher The selected doctoral researcher will play a central role in the project and will work closely with Dr. Sara Landolt. Key responsibilities include: Research Activities Designing and implementing project activities. Conducting original fieldwork. Carrying out qualitative interviews. Working with school leaders and students. Collecting and managing research data. Fieldwork The researcher will conduct qualitative interviews with: Headteachers of Gymnasia. Racially minoritized students. Socio-economically minoritized students. The fieldwork will primarily take place in German-speaking Switzerland. Data Analysis Responsibilities include: Qualitative data coding and analysis. Participatory data analysis workshops. Interpretation of research findings. Development of evidence-based recommendations. Doctoral Dissertation The successful candidate will complete a paper-based doctoral dissertation based on the project findings. Academic Contributions The researcher will: Participate in project workshops. Attend international conferences. Contribute to scholarly publications. Produce practice-oriented outputs. Engage with stakeholders and educational institutions. Teaching Responsibilities The position also includes contributions to: Human Geography teaching. Geography Teacher Training Unit (GTT) activities. Departmental service responsibilities. Graduate School Participation The doctoral candidate will participate in the: Zurich Graduate School in Geography Earth System Science which provides structured doctoral training and professional development opportunities. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is ideal for individuals who are passionate about: Educational equality Social justice Human geography Youth studies Qualitative research Racism and classism studies Institutional change Participatory methodologies Applicants should have a strong commitment to critical and socially relevant research. Required Qualifications Applicants must possess: A completed Master s degree or be close to completion. Academic training in a relevant discipline. Experience in qualitative research methods. Excellent communication skills. Strong teamwork abilities. Interest in field-based research. Motivation to engage with issues of inequality and justice. Relevant Academic Backgrounds Include: Geography Sociology Educational Studies Youth Studies Social Anthropology Social Work Related disciplines Additional Advantage Experience with participatory research methods will be considered a strong asset. Language Requirements Applicants must be fluent in: German English Both written and spoken proficiency are required. Benefits of the Position The University of Zurich offers an outstanding package of academic and professional benefits. Academic Benefits Fully funded doctoral position. SNSF-funded research environment. Structured doctoral training. Regular academic mentoring. Career development support. International conference participation. Publication opportunities. Employment Benefits Salary according to Swiss National Science Foundation scales. Dedicated office workspace. Technical equipment and research support. Access to university resources. Work-Life Balance Flexible working arrangements. Part-time employment model. Family-friendly policies. Childcare support options. Professional Development Continuing education courses. Language training opportunities. Skills development programs. Health and Wellbeing Access to sports facilities through ASVZ. Seasonal flu vaccinations. Wellbeing and relaxation facilities. Discounts and Additional Perks Car-sharing programs. Vehicle rental discounts. Technology discounts. Mobile phone subscription offers. Hotel reservation discounts. International Support The university provides dedicated support for international staff relocating to Switzerland. Living in Zurich Zurich consistently ranks among the best cities in the world for quality of life. Residents benefit from: Safe and clean urban environments. Excellent public transportation. Rich cultural life. International communities. Access to lakes and mountains. Outdoor recreation opportunities. World-class educational institutions. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit all materials as a single PDF file in English. Required documents include: Motivation Letter. Curriculum Vitae (CV). Contact details of two referees. Academic transcripts. Writing sample (such as an MSc thesis). Essay (400–500 words). Essay Topic Applicants should explain: Their interest in researching racism and/or classism in education and their conceptual approach; OR Their interest in conducting research with young people and the methodological challenges involved. Applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their application through the University of Zurich recruitment portal.
