title: Inclusive AI Innovations in Africa 2026: Apply for Up to USD Equivalent of KES 5 Million to Scale Disability Inclusion Solutions Across Africa
summary: The Hub for Artificial Intelligence and Disability Inclusion (HAIDI) Innovation Track has officially launched its Call for Applications for the Inclusive AI Innovations in Africa Programme 2026, offering catalytic funding and long-term support to innovators developing responsible AI solutions that improve the lives of persons with disabilities across Africa. Announced during the Global Data Festival 2026, this initiative is designed to identify and support high-potential post-MVP ventures that are already building practical AI-driven solutions capable of creating measurable social impact across the continent. Selected ventures will receive an intensive 18-month support package that combines funding, technical guidance, community-based user testing, and access to strategic partnerships to help scale inclusive technologies responsibly and sustainably. Applications close on 17 July 2026. About the HAIDI Innovation Track The Hub for Artificial Intelligence and Disability Inclusion (HAIDI) Innovation Track is focused on advancing disability inclusion through the ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Across Africa, millions of persons with disabilities continue to experience barriers when accessing education, employment, healthcare, caregiving support, digital services, and critical information systems. Many existing technologies are not designed with accessibility or inclusion in mind, limiting opportunities and participation. Through this programme, HAIDI aims to support innovators who are creating AI-powered solutions that address these challenges while ensuring that disability communities are actively involved in the design, testing, and improvement of these technologies. The programme prioritizes innovations that are not only technologically strong but also socially impactful, user-centered, and scalable across diverse African contexts. What Selected Ventures Will Receive The programme provides far more than just financial support. Selected applicants will gain access to a comprehensive ecosystem designed to help them refine and scale their innovations effectively. 1. Grants of Up to KES 5,000,000 Selected ventures will receive catalytic grants of up to KES 5 million (or USD equivalent) to support the development, testing, and scaling of their AI solutions. The funding can help ventures: Improve product development Expand accessibility features Strengthen technical infrastructure Conduct pilot implementations Scale operations across new communities Enhance research and validation efforts 2. Hands-On Technical and Product Support Participants will receive direct technical guidance and product support throughout the 18-month programme. This includes: Product refinement support Technical mentorship AI development guidance Responsible AI implementation support Scaling and operational advice Product usability improvement strategies The programme aims to help ventures strengthen both the technical quality and real-world effectiveness of their solutions. 3. User Testing With Disability Communities Across Africa One of the most important elements of the programme is direct engagement with disability communities. Selected innovators will have opportunities to: Test their products with real users Gather feedback from persons with disabilities Improve accessibility and usability Validate impact in real-world settings Ensure products are culturally and contextually relevant This user-centered approach helps ensure that AI solutions are developed responsibly and inclusively rather than in isolation. 4. Access to Partnerships and Future Funding Opportunities Participants will also gain exposure to a broader ecosystem of partners, experts, and funding networks. Benefits include: Strategic partnerships Networking opportunities Visibility within the AI and innovation ecosystem Connections with funders and investors Opportunities for future collaborations Access to expert communities and advisors This support can help ventures continue growing beyond the duration of the programme. Focus Areas for Innovation The HAIDI Innovation Track is looking for AI-driven solutions that address challenges affecting persons with disabilities across Africa. Key areas of interest include: Education Employment Mental health Caregiving Assistive technology Accessibility tools Inclusive communication systems Disability-focused digital services Community empowerment solutions Innovations from related sectors that contribute to disability inclusion are also encouraged to apply. Who Can Apply? The programme welcomes applications from a wide range of innovators and organizations working on inclusive AI technologies. Eligible applicants include: AI startups and SMEs Individual innovators Researchers Research institutions Universities Multi-stakeholder consortia Post-MVP ventures with existing AI solutions Applicants should already have a functional solution or product that demonstrates strong potential for scaling and impact. Why This Opportunity Matters Artificial intelligence has the potential to significantly improve accessibility, independence, and inclusion for persons with disabilities. However, many AI systems globally are still developed without sufficient representation or accessibility considerations. The HAIDI Innovation Track aims to change that by supporting African innovators who are building inclusive technologies with disability communities at the center of the process. This initiative represents a major opportunity for innovators who want to: Build socially impactful AI solutions Scale accessibility-focused technologies Collaborate with disability communities Gain funding and technical support Expand across African markets Strengthen responsible AI practices By investing in inclusive innovation, the programme seeks to help create a more accessible and equitable digital future across Africa. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Inclusive AI Innovations in Africa Programme 2026 is: 17 July 2026 Interested applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications before the deadline. About the Organizations Behind the Initiative The AI for Development (AI4D) initiative supports responsible AI research and innovation across Africa. The initiative is funded by: FCDO IDRC Sida Community Jameel The programme is supported by the Global Center on AI Governance (GCG). Final Thoughts The Inclusive AI Innovations in Africa Programme 2026 is one of the most important opportunities currently available for innovators working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, accessibility, and social impact in Africa. With substantial grant funding, long-term technical support, community-based testing, and strategic partnerships, the programme provides a powerful platform for scaling inclusive AI solutions that can improve the lives of persons with disabilities across the continent. Innovators building impactful and responsible AI technologies are strongly encouraged to apply before the 17 July 2026 deadline . How to Apply Interested applicants can apply through the official application portal HERE . Click HERE for more information about the Inclusive AI Innovations in Africa 2026. title: Council of Europe Traineeship Programme 2026–2027 in France and Europe: Paid International Internship for Students and Graduates in Human Rights, Democracy, Law, Policy, Communications, IT, HR, and More
summary: Applications are now open for the Council of Europe Traineeship Programme 2026–2027, a prestigious international traineeship opportunity designed for students and recent graduates who want to contribute to the promotion of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law across Europe. The Council of Europe is offering approximately 80 traineeship positions for the October 2026–March 2027 session, providing participants with a unique opportunity to gain practical experience within one of Europe’s most influential international organizations. Trainees will work alongside experts, policymakers, legal professionals, researchers, and administrative specialists while contributing to meaningful projects that support the Council of Europe’s mission. The programme offers hands-on professional experience, mentoring, networking opportunities, and financial support, making it one of the most attractive international traineeship opportunities available for young professionals interested in public policy, international affairs, law, governance, communications, human rights, technology, and organizational support services. About the Council of Europe The Council of Europe is Europe’s leading organization dedicated to promoting: Human rights Democracy Rule of law Founded in 1949, the organization works with its member states to strengthen democratic institutions, protect human rights, promote social cohesion, and uphold legal standards across Europe. The Council of Europe is responsible for many landmark initiatives and institutions, including the European Convention on Human Rights and the European Court of Human Rights. Through its traineeship programme, the organization seeks to engage talented young people who are passionate about contributing to these values while developing their professional skills in an international environment. Why Apply for the Council of Europe Traineeship Programme? The Council of Europe Traineeship Programme is more than just an internship. It is a professional development experience that allows participants to become actively involved in the daily work of an international organization while learning directly from experienced professionals. Participants gain exposure to: International policy-making Human rights protection Democratic governance International cooperation Public administration Legal affairs Communications Technology and innovation Human resources Organizational management The programme is designed to help trainees build the skills, knowledge, and professional network needed for future careers in international organizations, government institutions, NGOs, academia, and the private sector. Number of Traineeship Opportunities For the 2026–2027 session, approximately: 80 traineeship positions will be available across various Departments and Institutions of the Council of Europe. Traineeship Duration The main traineeship session will run: 1 October 2026 – 31 March 2027 Duration: 6 Months Parliamentary Assembly Traineeships Some traineeships at the Parliamentary Assembly will follow a different schedule: 1 September 2026 – 28 February 2027 Traineeship Locations Although most traineeships are based in Strasbourg, France, opportunities are also available in several European cities. Potential duty stations include: Strasbourg, France Brussels, Belgium Budapest, Hungary Geneva, Switzerland Graz, Austria Lisbon, Portugal Luxembourg The Hague, Netherlands Applicants should carefully review individual traineeship descriptions to identify available locations. What Will Trainees Do? As a Council of Europe trainee, participants become active members of their host teams and contribute to ongoing projects and organizational activities. Depending on the department selected, trainees may: Research and Policy Analysis Conduct research on European affairs and public policy issues Analyze legal and political developments Support policy initiatives and programmes Collect and synthesize information for reports Drafting and Documentation Contribute to studies and reports Draft briefing notes Assist with publications and official documents Prepare background materials for meetings Meeting and Event Support Help organize international conferences Coordinate committee meetings Support expert consultations Facilitate stakeholder engagement Communications and Outreach Develop communication materials Create digital content Support social media initiatives Assist with awareness campaigns Organizational Support Functions Trainees may also work in support departments including: Human Resources Information Technology Security Services Catering Services Administration Legal Advice Political Affairs Mentorship and Professional Development One of the strongest features of the programme is its mentoring component. Every trainee receives support from an experienced mentor who helps them: Navigate their responsibilities Develop professional skills Understand organizational processes Expand their professional network Maximize learning opportunities This mentorship ensures trainees gain valuable guidance throughout their placement. Benefits of the Council of Europe Traineeship Selected trainees receive a range of benefits. Financial Support Trainees in Strasbourg receive approximately: EUR 1,320 gross per month Health Insurance Participants are provided with: Health insurance coverage Leave Entitlement Trainees receive: 2.5 days of leave per month worked Flexible Work Arrangements Where feasible, trainees may work remotely for: Up to 50% of each two-week period Professional Benefits Participants gain: International work experience Access to European experts and policymakers Mentorship support Networking opportunities Exposure to multicultural working environments Professional skill development Eligibility Criteria To apply for the Council of Europe Traineeship Programme, applicants must satisfy all eligibility requirements before the application deadline. Educational Requirements Applicants must: Have completed at least three years of university studies Hold a Bachelor s degree or equivalent first-cycle degree under the Bologna Process Framework Special Note: For traineeships at the European Court of Human Rights, applicants must have completed: The first year of a Master s degree Language Requirements Candidates must possess: Very good knowledge of English or French These are the Council of Europe’s official working languages. Age Requirement Applicants must be: At least 18 years old Citizenship Requirement Candidates must be citizens of a Council of Europe member state. Previous Participation Restriction Applicants must not have previously: Completed a Council of Europe traineeship Participated in a Council of Europe study visit Worked for the Council of Europe in any capacity Family Relationship Restriction Applicants cannot be: Parent Child Stepchild Grandchild of a serving Council of Europe staff member. Skills and Competencies Sought The Council of Europe values candidates who demonstrate: Learning and Development Curiosity Adaptability Commitment to growth Continuous learning Teamwork and Cooperation Collaboration skills Communication abilities Respect for diversity Ability to work in multicultural teams Application Process Applicants can indicate: First-choice team Second-choice team during the application process. Application Timeline Applications Open: 4 June 2026 Application Deadline: 17 June 2026 Deadline Time: 23:59:59 CET/CEST APPLY HERE You may find out more information on how to fill in and submit an application on the Frequently asked questions page . Selection Process The process generally includes: Online application submission Eligibility screening Review by selected teams Online interview (if shortlisted) Final selection decision Notification of results Signature of traineeship agreement Start of traineeship Applicants are typically informed of the outcome approximately two months before the traineeship begins. For any questions, please contact traineeship@coe.int Equal Opportunity and Inclusion The Council of Europe is committed to diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunity. Applications are welcomed regardless of: Gender Sexual orientation Ethnic origin Social origin Disability Religion Belief The organization also provides reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities or specific needs throughout the recruitment process and traineeship period. title: WFF Academic Engagement 2026 Applications Open: Connect Your Research to Global Food Policy and Agrifood Systems Transformation

title: William P. Fuller Fellowship in Peacebuilding 2026: Fully Funded Leadership Opportunity for Emerging Peacebuilders Across Asia and the Pacific
summary: Applications are now open for the 2026 William P. title: United Nations Regional Course in International Law for Asia-Pacific 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand (Fully Funded Fellowship Available)

title: EERC 2026 Cohort 4 Fellowship for Mid–Senior Level Nigerian Researchers
summary: The Environmental and Economic Resource Centre (EERC) has officially opened applications for its 2026 Cohort 4 Fellowship , a prestigious opportunity designed for mid to senior‑level researchers across Nigerian universities and research institutions. The application deadline is June 30, 2026 . Working with a broad network of local and international partners, EERC focuses on generating evidence‑based solutions that strengthen: Inclusive agriculture Sustainable livelihoods Natural resource conservation Environmental management EERC’s work spans four major programs: Agriculture and Environmental Management (AEM) Natural Resource Conservation (NRC) Livelihood and Economic Development (LED) Human Resource and Capacity Building (HRCB) These programs cover a wide range of research areas, including climate‑smart agriculture, climate change, food systems, health and nutrition, migration, renewable energy, carbon markets, land use change, rural livelihoods, and gender and social inclusion. EERC partners include: University College London World Disaster Centre Stockholm Environment Institute Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research Personal Benefits Include: Monthly allowance (in addition to salary from home institution) Free accommodation at the EERC Guest House, equipped with: 24‑hour power supply Internet access Gym and sports facilities Training and travel opportunities Joint publications with leading researchers in agriculture, climate change, and land‑use systems Opportunities to strengthen research networks between EERC and home institutions Eligibility Criteria Applicants must meet the following requirements: Hold a PhD in one of the eligible fields Demonstrate strong research leadership experience Have experience supervising early‑career scientists Maintain an active affiliation with a Nigerian research institution or university Show proficiency in statistical/econometric tools such as SAS, R, and STATA Demonstrate the ability to write proposals covering at least two of the eligible fields Researchers from Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria (ARCN) institutions are strongly encouraged to apply Required Application Documents Applicants must submit the following: Two reference letters on institutional letterhead: One from the Head of Department One from the Head/Representative of the institution Motivation letter Concept note (max 5 pages) including: Background Objective Methodology Analytical approach Budget summary Timeline Expected results References (as appendix) Support letters from department and institutional heads Curriculum Vitae (CV) with evidence of lead‑author publications in high‑impact journals Academic qualifications Institutional ID card Applications missing any of these documents will not be reviewed. title: UNOPS Senior Mediation Adviser Jobs 2026: Multiple Home-Based International Positions for Global Peacebuilding Experts
summary: UNOPS Opens Applications for Senior Mediation Advisers: Multiple International Opportunities Available The United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) has announced applications for multiple Senior Mediation Adviser positions, offering experienced peacebuilding and conflict-resolution professionals an opportunity to contribute to some of the world s most complex mediation, dialogue, and peace processes. These highly specialized international positions are home-based and designed for experts capable of supporting mediation efforts, constitutional processes, ceasefire negotiations, power-sharing arrangements, gender inclusion initiatives, and climate-related conflict resolution across various regions of the world. Working under the Development and Special Initiatives Portfolio based in New York, successful candidates will become part of a global network of senior advisers supporting United Nations mediation efforts aimed at advancing peace, stability, and sustainable development. About UNOPS The United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) serves as the operational arm of the United Nations, supporting partners in implementing peacebuilding, humanitarian, and development projects worldwide. UNOPS operates in some of the most challenging environments globally and works closely with governments, UN entities, regional organizations, and development partners to promote sustainable peace and development outcomes. With personnel located across numerous countries, UNOPS provides technical expertise, operational support, and project implementation services to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). About the Senior Mediation Adviser Role The Senior Mediation Adviser position is designed for highly experienced professionals who can provide technical expertise and strategic guidance to mediation teams, conflict parties, governments, regional organizations, and other stakeholders involved in peace processes. Selected experts may work in one or more specialized thematic areas depending on their expertise and deployment requirements. Areas of Specialization Applicants may be selected for one or more of the following areas: Design and Conduct of Mediation, Facilitation and Dialogue Processes Security Arrangements and Ceasefire Mechanisms Constitution-Making and Constitutional Reform Power-Sharing and Governance Arrangements Gender and Inclusion Climate Change and Natural Resources Management in Conflict Contexts Key Responsibilities When Deployed to Peace Processes Senior Mediation Advisers may be called upon to: Provide technical advice and expertise to mediation teams. Support negotiation frameworks and dialogue processes. Facilitate peace negotiations and stakeholder consultations. Contribute to drafting peace agreements and political settlements. Advise conflict parties and key stakeholders. Support national and local dialogue initiatives. Design and manage implementation frameworks for peace agreements. Promote meaningful participation of women, youth, civil society, and marginalized groups. Conduct training and capacity-building workshops. Produce reports, briefings, and analytical documents. Ensure gender-responsive approaches throughout mediation efforts. When Not Deployed Advisers continue contributing remotely by: Providing virtual technical support to mediation teams. Conducting research and policy analysis. Producing thematic briefing papers. Developing operational guidance notes. Delivering training programmes for UN personnel. Supporting lessons-learned reviews and best-practice documentation. Strengthening global mediation knowledge networks. Specialized Areas of Expertise 1. Mediation, Facilitation and Dialogue Experts in this area help design and manage inclusive dialogue and peace processes while supporting negotiations among conflict parties. 2. Security Arrangements Professionals with expertise in: Ceasefires Cessation of hostilities Security sector reform Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) play a critical role in supporting peace implementation efforts. 3. Constitutional Issues Advisers support: Constitution-making processes Constitutional reforms National dialogue initiatives Transitional institutional arrangements They also contribute to ensuring inclusive constitutional frameworks that protect rights and promote democratic governance. 4. Power-Sharing Arrangements Specialists provide expertise on: Federalism Decentralization Regional autonomy Political power-sharing structures which are often central components of peace agreements. 5. Gender and Inclusion This specialization focuses on: Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agendas Inclusive peace processes Gender-responsive mediation Participation of marginalized groups in decision-making processes. 6. Climate Change and Natural Resources Experts help address conflicts linked to: Water resources Land use Minerals Oil and gas Environmental degradation Climate-related security risks while supporting sustainable resource governance and conflict prevention initiatives. Required Experience and Qualifications Applicants should possess: Professional Experience Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience. Demonstrated experience in peacebuilding, mediation, facilitation, conflict resolution, or related fields. Strong field experience in conflict or post-conflict environments. Experience advising senior mediators, special envoys, governments, or conflict parties. Experience in training and capacity building. Experience engaging with civil society organizations and community stakeholders. Key Competencies Successful candidates should demonstrate: Advanced analytical skills Excellent communication abilities Strong negotiation expertise Strategic thinking Leadership capabilities Cultural sensitivity Commitment to diversity and inclusion Ability to work under pressure Adaptability in rapidly changing environments Strong report writing and policy drafting skills. Additional Requirements Applicants should also possess: Strong understanding of United Nations structures, mandates, and operations. Familiarity with international peacebuilding frameworks. Knowledge of humanitarian and human rights principles. Understanding of UN Security Council Resolution 1325 on Women, Peace and Security. Ability to travel internationally on short notice, often within 72 hours. Ability to undertake field missions lasting between two and five weeks or longer when required. Contract Details Successful candidates will receive: International Individual Contractor Agreement (ICA) Contract Level: IICA-4 / ICS-12 Home-based duty station Ongoing open-ended contract arrangement subject to organizational requirements, funding availability, and satisfactory performance. Professionals selected for this roster will contribute to some of the most significant peacebuilding efforts globally while working alongside United Nations entities, governments, regional organizations, civil society actors, and local communities. title: Independent Expert Group for the ARISE Program (CIF): Global Call for Climate Finance and Resilience Experts
summary: The Climate Investment Funds (CIF) , established in 2008, is one of the world’s leading multilateral climate finance initiatives supporting developing countries in their transition toward low-emission, climate-resilient development. Through its collaboration with multilateral development banks (MDBs) and partner governments, CIF has pioneered large-scale concessional financing aimed at driving systemic change in energy, infrastructure, agriculture, water, and social resilience systems. Building on 17 years of implementation experience under the Pilot Program for Climate Resilience (PPCR) , CIF has launched a transformative initiative known as the Accelerating Resilience Investments and Innovations for Sustainable Economies (ARISE) program. ARISE is designed to help developing countries convert national resilience priorities into structured, investable, and scalable climate solutions. To support the technical integrity, fairness, and strategic direction of this program, CIF is now recruiting an Independent Expert Group (IEG) composed of globally recognized professionals in climate change, finance, and development economics. A critical milestone in this initiative is the submission of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) by participating countries, with a deadline set for June 8th, 2026 . About the ARISE Program The ARISE program is a forward-looking climate resilience financing framework that focuses on turning climate adaptation needs into actionable investment pipelines. It prioritizes critical systems that are most vulnerable to climate risks, including: Food systems and agricultural resilience Water security and resource management Climate-resilient infrastructure development Sustainable and low-carbon energy systems The program seeks to ensure that climate finance is not only accessible but also strategically deployed to generate long-term resilience outcomes and unlock private sector participation. Role of the Independent Expert Group (IEG) The Independent Expert Group (IEG) will consist of six internationally selected experts with deep technical and strategic experience in climate adaptation, development finance, and economic systems transformation. The group will include balanced representation from both contributing and recipient countries, ensuring fairness, inclusivity, and technical rigor in decision-making. From among the six members, two co-chairs will be appointed. Key Responsibilities The Independent Expert Group will undertake the following core functions: 1. Evaluation of Country Submissions Review Expressions of Interest (EoIs) submitted by eligible countries Assess proposals against established CIF and ARISE evaluation criteria Ensure alignment with resilience investment priorities 2. Technical Research and Review Analyze annexed project and policy documents Conduct supplementary desk research using the Integrated Results Framework (IRF) Validate technical feasibility and investment readiness 3. Stakeholder Consultation Conduct structured interviews with country representatives Engage with multilateral development banks (MDBs) Confirm compliance with MDB partnership standards and coordination frameworks 4. Reporting and Recommendations Produce a ranked list of countries based on evaluation outcomes Submit formal recommendations to the Strategic Climate Fund (SCF) Trust Fund Committee (TFC) Provide methodological notes detailing evaluation approaches Document limitations, challenges, and gaps identified during assessment Include a full list of consulted stakeholders for transparency and accountability Selection Criteria for Applicants Applicants interested in serving on the Independent Expert Group must meet the following requirements: Academic Qualifications A Master’s degree or PhD in fields relevant to climate change, development economics, environmental science, finance, or related disciplines Professional Experience Minimum of 12 years of relevant professional experience Proven work in climate resilience, development finance, or related sectors Experience in developing country contexts is highly preferred Additional Preferred Qualifications Prior experience working with multilateral institutions, international organizations, or global development agencies is an advantage but not mandatory Timeline and Availability Selected experts must be available for engagement between June and October 2026 . Primary workload duration: approximately 6 to 8 weeks Work will include review cycles, consultations, and report drafting phases Flexibility and responsiveness during peak evaluation periods will be essential Application Process and Requirements Applicants are required to submit their applications directly via email: CIF Secretariat Email: CIFSecretariat@cif.org Application Requirements: Full name and contact information Detailed area of expertise Updated curriculum vitae (CV/resume) Disclosure of any conflicts of interest (including current or past employment with CIF partner MDBs or related institutions) Important Deadline: Application submission deadline: June 19, 2026 Submissions through any channel other than the official email will not be considered Compensation Selected experts will be remunerated in accordance with World Bank consultant procurement rules and regulations , ensuring standardized and competitive international compensation structures for technical experts. title: OHCHR Global Youth Network for Human Rights 2026: Join the United Nations’ Worldwide Youth Community Advancing Human Rights
summary: Young people around the world who are passionate about human rights now have an exciting opportunity to become part of a global movement through the Global Youth Network for Human Rights (GYNfHR), an initiative coordinated by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). The Global Youth Network for Human Rights is designed to connect young people from every region of the world who are committed to promoting, protecting, and advancing human rights. Whether participants are experienced human rights advocates or simply interested in learning more about human rights issues, the Network offers an inclusive and accessible platform for engagement, dialogue, collaboration, and action. Importantly, the Network is open to all young people regardless of their educational background, previous experience, organizational affiliation, or level of knowledge about human rights. The initiative aims to ensure that youth voices from all walks of life are heard and represented in conversations shaping the future of human rights globally. About the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is the principal United Nations entity responsible for promoting and protecting human rights worldwide. OHCHR works to: Promote universal human rights. Monitor and report on human rights issues globally. Support governments in implementing human rights obligations. Strengthen accountability mechanisms. title: King’s College London Fully Funded 3-Year PhD Studentship 2026 in Psychology: Receive £23,805 Annual Stipend Plus £3,000 Research Funding to Conduct Groundbreaking Research in the UK
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious Fully Funded 3-Year PhD Studentship in the Department of Psychology at King’s College London for the 2026/27 academic year . This exceptional doctoral opportunity offers aspiring researchers the chance to pursue a fully funded PhD at one of the world s leading universities while receiving a generous annual stipend, full tuition fee support, dedicated research funding, and valuable teaching experience. Hosted within the renowned Department of Psychology at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology Neuroscience (IoPPN), the studentship provides an outstanding platform for talented graduates interested in advancing psychological science through innovative and impactful research. Successful candidates will join one of four cutting-edge research projects spanning food psychology, autism and gastrointestinal health, decision-making under risk, and intergenerational development. Application Deadline: 21 June 2026 (23:59 GMT) Why Study at King’s College London? King s College London is consistently ranked among the world s leading universities and is internationally recognized for excellence in research, teaching, and innovation. The university s Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology Neuroscience is one of the largest and most influential centers for mental health and psychological research globally. Students benefit from: World-class supervision Access to leading researchers Cutting-edge research facilities International academic networks Interdisciplinary collaborations Excellent career development opportunities This studentship offers a unique opportunity to conduct high-impact research while developing advanced academic and professional skills. Overview of the Fully Funded Psychology PhD Studentship The Department of Psychology is seeking one outstanding PhD candidate to undertake research in one of four pre-defined doctoral projects. The studentship will begin on: Start Date: 1 October 2026 The successful applicant will be enrolled in a full-time PhD program lasting three years. Financial Benefits This fully funded doctoral scholarship provides substantial financial support throughout the duration of the PhD. Annual Stipend The selected student will receive: Annual stipend equivalent to the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI/RCUK) doctoral stipend rate. Current stipend value: £23,805 per year , including London weighting. Stipend subject to annual updates. Full Tuition Fee Coverage The studentship covers: Full tuition fees for Home students. PhD registration costs for the entire three-year duration. Research and Travel Funding In addition to the stipend, students will receive: Up to £3,000 annually for: Research activities Conference attendance Fieldwork expenses Academic travel Project-related costs Over three years, this could amount to: Up to £9,000 in additional research support Available PhD Research Projects Applicants must apply for one of the following projects. Project 1 (FC01): Food and the Self Supervisor Contact: Dr Francesca Cotier This innovative project investigates the relationship between food, eating behaviors, and personal identity. Research Areas The project will: Examine how food identity has been conceptualized across psychological literature. Investigate how food choices contribute to self-concept and identity formation. Explore lived experiences related to food and identity. Research Methods Students will: Conduct systematic reviews. Carry out qualitative interviews. Develop psychological assessment tools. Validate new measures of food identity. Potential Impact Findings could contribute to: Better understanding of eating behavior. Improved public health interventions. More culturally sensitive nutrition and health programs. Project 2 (JF02): Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) in Autistic Adults Supervisor Contact: Dr James Findon This project focuses on gastrointestinal symptoms among autistic adults using a disorders of gut-brain interaction framework. Research Activities The project will involve: Reviewing existing scientific evidence. Analyzing secondary datasets. Comparing autistic and non-autistic adults. Examining healthcare utilization patterns. Key Variables Research will explore: Anxiety Interoception Sensory processing Neurodevelopmental mechanisms Expected Outcomes The study aims to: Improve understanding of gastrointestinal conditions in autism. Inform clinical practice. Support better healthcare interventions. Project 3 (CH03): Described and Experienced Risk in Decision-Making Supervisor Contact: Dr Claire Heard This project examines how individuals make decisions when information about risk is both explicitly provided and learned through experience. Research Questions The study investigates: How people combine described and experienced information. How risk perceptions evolve. Which factors influence decision quality. Research Approach Using experimental methods, the project will assess: Timing of information Sequencing effects Information completeness Behavioral responses Real-World Applications Results could inform: Consumer behavior research Marketing strategies Financial decision-making Online review systems Public communication campaigns Project 4 (SY04): Intergenerational Play Supervisor Contact: Dr Sumeyra Yalcintas This project explores the differences between parent-child and grandparent-child interactions and their effects on development and wellbeing. Research Components The project includes: Video-recorded play sessions Behavioral coding analysis Questionnaires Interviews with families Areas of Investigation Researchers will examine: Interaction patterns Child developmental outcomes Family relationships Grandparent wellbeing Importance of the Research The findings may provide valuable insights into: Child development Family psychology Healthy ageing Intergenerational relationships Teaching and Professional Development Opportunities An important component of the studentship involves serving as a Graduate Teaching Assistant (GTA). Responsibilities may include: Leading seminars Supporting practical classes Marking coursework Providing feedback to undergraduate students Supporting the BSc Psychology programme These teaching duties provide valuable academic experience for students considering careers in: Higher education Research Academic leadership Eligibility Criteria Applicants must meet the following minimum academic requirements: Standard Entry Route Bachelor s degree with 2:1 Honours classification (or overseas equivalent). Alternative Entry Route Applicants with: Bachelor s degree with 2:2 Honours Plus a Master s degree with Merit may also be considered. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit: Academic Transcripts Official academic transcripts must accompany the application where applicable. Qualification Documents Copies of degree certificates and qualifications. Curriculum Vitae (CV) Including: Educational background Employment history Research experience Publications (if any) Personal Statement Applicants must explain: Why they are interested in the project. Their academic interests. Their research experience. Their motivation for pursuing a PhD. The personal statement must clearly identify the selected project code (e.g., FC01, JF02, CH03, or SY04). Teaching Experience Information Applicants should include any: Teaching experience Tutoring experience Academic mentoring activities Academic Reference One academic reference is required. References must: Be submitted from an institutional email address. Meet the specified submission timeline. Important Application Instructions Applicants should: Apply through the King s College London admissions portal. Select: Department of Psychology Research MPhil/PhD (Full-Time); or Department of Psychology Research MPhil/PhD (Part-Time). Tick Box 5 in the Funding Section. Include the project reference code. Skip the Research Proposal section because the projects have already been predefined. Applicants are encouraged to contact supervisors for additional information before submitting their applications. title: Call for Applications: Professor Tord Kjellström Indicator Development Award for Monitoring Mental Health Impacts of Climate Change (Up to £100,000 Funding)
summary: The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change has officially announced a competitive and highly significant call for applications for the Professor Tord Kjellström Indicator Development Award for Mental Health and Climate Change . This initiative is designed to support the development of a scientifically rigorous indicator that will track and monitor the mental health impacts of climate change-related hazards globally. This award is established in honour of Professor Tord Envold Kjellström (1948–2025), a globally respected environmental and occupational health scientist whose pioneering research significantly advanced understanding of climate-related health risks, including occupational heat exposure and environmental change impacts. The selected expert or expert team will collaborate closely with the Lancet Countdown team to design an indicator that meets strict scientific criteria and contributes to global climate-health monitoring systems. Objective of the Award The primary goal of this opportunity is to develop a robust and validated indicator capable of measuring how climate change influences mental health outcomes. This indicator will become part of the Lancet Countdown’s annual monitoring framework, contributing to global policy and scientific understanding. The work will focus on: Developing a scientifically valid mental health–climate change indicator Ensuring methodological rigor aligned with Lancet Countdown indicator standards Collaborating with global experts in climate health monitoring Supporting integration into annual global reporting systems Advancing evidence-based climate and mental health policy Funding Details This award provides substantial research support for the selected applicant(s): Funding amount: Up to £100,000 per award Funding duration: 6 to 18 months Number of awards: One Co-applicants: Eligible Funding structure: One-off award Host requirements: Must be eligible to receive funding from Wellcome Key Dates and Timeline Applicants must carefully note the official timeline: Applications open: 1 June 2026 at 08:00 BST Application deadline: 12 July 2026 at 17:00 BST Duration of project: 6–18 months following award allocation Late submissions will not be considered. Application Process Interested applicants are expected to: Review the full Guidance for Applicants provided by Lancet Countdown Download and complete the official application pack Submit applications via the designated Qualtrics submission platform once applications open Participate in or review the information webinar for further clarification on requirements Applicants are encouraged to ensure that their proposals align closely with the Lancet Countdown’s scientific framework and indicator methodology. For further inquiries, applicants may contact: Email: info@lancetcountdown.org Expected Outputs Successful applicants will be responsible for producing: A validated mental health and climate change indicator Scientific documentation supporting methodology and implementation Collaboration outputs with Lancet Countdown research teams Contribution to global annual climate-health reporting Importance of This Award Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major driver of mental health challenges, including anxiety, trauma, displacement stress, and disaster-related psychological impacts. title: AI Hub for Sustainable Development Cyber4Africa Programme 2026: Fully Supported Cybersecurity Capacity Building Opportunity for African AI Startups
summary: Applications Open for the AI Hub for Sustainable Development Cyber4Africa Programme African artificial intelligence startups now have a unique opportunity to strengthen their cybersecurity capabilities, improve operational resilience, and prepare for sustainable growth through the AI Hub for Sustainable Development Cyber4Africa Programme. These challenges include: Data protection vulnerabilities Cybersecurity threats Infrastructure security risks Regulatory compliance requirements Operational security weaknesses Trust and safety concerns within AI systems To address these issues, Cyber4Africa helps startups integrate cybersecurity principles throughout the AI development lifecycle. The programme promotes a “safety-by-design” approach that embeds security considerations into products, platforms, and services from the earliest stages of development. By participating in the programme, startups can strengthen their resilience while increasing investor confidence, customer trust, and readiness for expansion into new markets. Programme Objectives The Cyber4Africa Programme seeks to: Improve cybersecurity awareness among African AI startups. Strengthen digital resilience across emerging AI businesses. Enhance data protection and privacy practices. Support secure infrastructure development. Enable safer deployment of AI technologies. Foster sustainable growth within Africa’s AI ecosystem. title: J-PAL Global Senior Training Associate Position 2026: Apply for a Three-Year Research, Education, and Training Role at MIT
summary: The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab, widely known as J-PAL, is inviting applications for the Senior Training Associate position at J-PAL Global . This opportunity is based at the J-PAL Global office at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States . This is a strong opportunity for candidates with a background in economics, political science, education, international development, program evaluation, quantitative research, randomized evaluations, or related fields. The role is designed for individuals who are passionate about poverty alleviation, evidence-informed policymaking, rigorous impact evaluation, and global development research. The successful candidate will join J-PAL’s Research, Education, and Training team , supporting the design, planning, delivery, and evaluation of training programs for policymakers, practitioners, researchers, governments, NGOs, foundations, universities, and development organizations around the world. About J-PAL Global The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab is a global research center working to reduce poverty by ensuring that public policy is shaped by scientific evidence. J-PAL is anchored by a network of more than 1,100 leading researchers based at universities across the world. Headquartered at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology , J-PAL works across multiple global offices and has more than 500 staff members supporting research, policy engagement, education, training, and partnerships. J-PAL’s work focuses on using rigorous research, especially randomized evaluations, to understand what works in reducing poverty and improving lives. Through its partnerships with governments, non-governmental organizations, foundations, multilateral institutions, and universities, J-PAL helps turn evidence into policy action. Position Overview J-PAL Global is recruiting a Senior Training Associate to support its mission of promoting evidence-informed policy. The position will be based at the J-PAL Global office at MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The role is part of J-PAL’s Research, Education, and Training team , also known as the RET team. This team works in a fast-paced and collaborative environment to equip policymakers, researchers, practitioners, and staff with the knowledge and tools needed to conduct and use rigorous impact evaluations. The Senior Training Associate will contribute to J-PAL’s global training work by developing new teaching materials, supporting online and in-person courses, assisting with workshops, and strengthening learning resources on randomized evaluations and cost-effectiveness. The role also includes working with learners and partners from around the world, creating open-access resources for J-PAL’s online courses, and developing tailored training materials for partner organizations. Key Details of the Opportunity Position title: Senior Training Associate Organization: J-PAL Global Host institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology Location: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States Earliest start date: 1 July 2026 Length of commitment: Three years or more Application deadline: June 15 Application review: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis Work format: Hybrid, with at least two in-office days per week Visa sponsorship: Not available Why This Role Matters This position is ideal for someone who wants to contribute to global development through research, training, and evidence-based policy. Many governments and development organizations want to solve urgent problems related to poverty, education, health, labor markets, social protection, agriculture, governance, and economic opportunity. However, effective solutions require strong evidence. J-PAL’s training work helps policymakers, researchers, and development practitioners understand how to generate, interpret, and use evidence responsibly. As a Senior Training Associate, the selected candidate will help build the capacity of people and institutions working on real-world policy challenges. The role combines research communication, teaching, data analysis, training design, partnership support, and global development engagement. Main Responsibilities The Senior Training Associate will contribute to several areas of J-PAL’s training and education work. Responsibilities may include the following: 1. Developing Teaching Materials The selected candidate will research and design new teaching modules for J-PAL’s training programs. These materials may cover topics such as randomized evaluations, impact evaluation methods, cost-effectiveness analysis, data use, and evidence-informed decision-making. This may involve preparing: Presentations Case studies Training manuals Course exercises Learning guides Technical explanations Teaching resources for online and in-person learners 2. Supporting Online and In-Person Training The Senior Training Associate will serve as a teaching assistant for J-PAL’s online and in-person training offerings. This includes helping learners strengthen their ability to generate and use rigorous evidence. The role may involve supporting learners during courses, explaining technical concepts, assisting with assignments, answering questions, and helping participants understand randomized evaluation methods. 3. Planning and Delivering Workshops The position involves assisting with the planning, organization, and delivery of training courses and workshops for key partners around the world. These partners may include: Government agencies Non-governmental organizations Foundations Universities Multilateral aid agencies Research institutions Development practitioners The selected candidate may also have opportunities to travel domestically and internationally to support or participate in training courses. 4. Collaborating Across J-PAL Offices J-PAL operates through a global network of regional offices. The Senior Training Associate will coordinate and collaborate with training colleagues across these offices. This may include contributing to knowledge management, improving training processes, organizing shared resources, and helping ensure consistency and quality across J-PAL’s training materials. 5. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Data Analysis The role includes maintaining tracking, monitoring, and evaluation systems for J-PAL’s courses. The selected candidate will help analyze data to assess learning outcomes, participant engagement, and course effectiveness. This makes the role suitable for candidates who are comfortable with quantitative data analysis and interested in improving educational and training programs through evidence. 6. Supporting Partner Relationships The Senior Training Associate will also support the development of relationships with key partners in governments, NGOs, foundations, universities, multilateral aid agencies, and other institutions around the world. This aspect of the role requires strong communication skills, cultural awareness, professionalism, and an interest in working across different institutional and global contexts. Required Qualifications Applicants should meet the following educational, technical, and professional requirements. Educational Background A bachelor’s degree is required in one of the following fields: Economics Political science Education International development A related field A master’s degree is preferred , but not strictly required. Applicants must have training in and a strong technical understanding of: Econometrics Randomized evaluations Quantitative research methods Impact evaluation methods Experience Requirements J-PAL prefers candidates with around four years of relevant work experience . This experience may include work gained as a student. Relevant experience may include: Program evaluation Quantitative data analysis Economics research Development research Education or training work Impact evaluation Policy research Research assistance Data management Related analytical roles Applicants with fewer than four years of experience are also welcome to apply. Exceptional candidates with less than four years of experience may be considered for an Associate-level position . Skills and Competencies Required Strong Interest in Poverty Alleviation Candidates should have a strong interest in poverty alleviation policy and research. This interest may be demonstrated through coursework, research, study abroad, work abroad, development experience, or professional exposure to policy and social impact work. Quantitative Skills Applicants must have knowledge of: Data management Data analysis Econometrics Quantitative research methods These skills are important because the role involves working with training materials related to randomized evaluations, evidence generation, and policy-relevant research. Software Skills Applicants must have a good command of at least one of the following: Stata R Python Candidates should also be comfortable using Google Workspace tools, including: Google Docs Google Sheets Google Slides Google Forms Additional skills that are considered a plus include: LaTeX GitHub Other coding languages Thoughtful use of AI tools to streamline workflows Cultural Competencies J-PAL is looking for applicants who are comfortable working in a diverse and multicultural environment. The role involves collaboration with colleagues, learners, partners, policymakers, and institutions from different parts of the world. Applicants should demonstrate sensitivity and adaptability across: Culture Gender Religion Race Nationality Age Professional background J-PAL encourages diversity, equity, and inclusion in its work and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. The organization especially encourages people who are underrepresented in economics to apply. Location and Work Arrangement This position is based in Cambridge, Massachusetts , at J-PAL Global’s office at MIT. The role follows a hybrid work arrangement. Staff are currently expected to work in the office at least two days per week , specifically Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Remote work is allowed on the remaining three days. However, hybrid work policies may change annually. The position is not eligible for full-time remote work. Visa Sponsorship Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Candidates must already be authorized to work in the United States for a minimum of three years. This is an important requirement, and applicants should confirm their work authorization before applying. Compensation and Benefits J-PAL states that pay range and pay grade information for this role is available through the relevant MIT compensation information page. As a member of the MIT community, the successful candidate will receive a competitive compensation package for the non-profit international development field. Benefits may include: Comprehensive health insurance 401(k) match Pension-based retirement plan Tuition assistance Commuter benefits MIT community discounts Generous vacation policy Additional MIT benefits J-PAL staff members may also be eligible to take proctored exams in the Data, Economics, and Design of Policy MicroMasters courses at no cost. These course certificates can count toward the DEDP MicroMasters credential. Application Process Interested candidates must apply through the MIT human resources system . Applicants should search for MIT Job ID: 25712 and complete the application on the MIT portal. The application requires candidates to upload a single PDF document into the “Resume” field. This single PDF should include: Cover letter The cover letter should explain why the applicant is interested in the position at J-PAL Global and why they are qualified for the role. Resume or CV The resume or CV should clearly show relevant education, work experience, technical skills, research experience, and training-related experience. Transcripts for all previous university-level coursework Unofficial transcripts are accepted. Applicants should only apply to the J-PAL Global Senior Training Associate position, MIT Job ID 25712 . Selection Process All applicants will be asked to complete a short data task as part of the screening process. Shortlisted applicants will then be asked to complete a short technical screening interview via Zoom. Candidates who advance further will be invited to additional Zoom interviews. Because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, interested candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible before the June 15 deadline. Why You Should Apply This opportunity is suitable for candidates who want to combine research, education, training, and global development impact. It is especially relevant for people who enjoy translating technical research concepts into practical learning materials for policymakers, practitioners, and researchers. You should consider applying if you: Are passionate about poverty reduction and evidence-based policy Have a background in economics, education, political science, international development, or related fields Understand econometrics, randomized evaluations, or quantitative research methods Enjoy developing teaching materials and training resources Have experience in data analysis or program evaluation Want to work with global partners in government, NGOs, foundations, universities, and multilateral agencies Are comfortable working in a multicultural environment Are authorized to work in the United States for at least three years Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the J-PAL Global Senior Training Associate position is June 15 . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so applicants should submit their materials as early as possible. How to Apply To apply, candidates should visit the MIT human resources system, search for MIT Job ID 25712 , and submit the required application materials. title: Oxford University Accelerator Fellowship Programme 2026: Funding and Support for High-Impact Ethical AI Projects
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious Accelerator Fellowship Programme at the Institute for Ethics in AI, University of Oxford. Designed to advance responsible and ethical artificial intelligence, this pioneering fellowship supports individuals and teams working on impactful projects that can influence policy, industry, public understanding, and the future direction of AI. The programme is seeking 3–4 fellows for its current cohort and offers a unique opportunity to collaborate with one of the world s leading centres for AI ethics research. About the Accelerator Fellowship Programme The Accelerator Fellowship Programme is a flagship initiative of the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI. The programme was created in response to the growing ethical challenges posed by the rapid advancement and adoption of artificial intelligence technologies across society. Unlike traditional research fellowships that focus primarily on academic outputs, this programme emphasizes real-world impact. It seeks to support projects that can shape the development of AI in ethical and socially beneficial directions while extending the influence of research already taking place within the Institute. The fellowship is grounded in: Philosophical inquiry Academic independence Interdisciplinary collaboration Practical impact Responsible innovation Through this approach, Oxford aims to bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI ethics research and meaningful implementation in society. Fellowship Objectives The Accelerator Fellowship Programme supports work that: Creates significant impact beyond academia Promotes the responsible and ethical development of AI Aligns with one or more research priorities of the Institute for Ethics in AI Amplifies and extends the impact of existing research at the Institute The programme encourages fellows to transform research insights into practical initiatives capable of influencing decision-making, industry practices, public understanding, and governance frameworks. Types of Projects Supported Oxford s Accelerator Fellowship Programme welcomes a diverse range of initiatives focused on ethical AI. Potential areas of impact include, but are not limited to: 1. AI Policy and Governance Innovation Projects that contribute to: AI regulation Governance frameworks Public policy development Ethical standards and accountability systems International cooperation on AI governance 2. Professional Development and Capacity Building Initiatives designed to: Train AI professionals in ethical practices Create educational opportunities Develop responsible AI leadership Build ethics competencies across sectors 3. Commercial and Technical Innovation Projects that support: Responsible AI products Ethical AI tools and systems Industry best practices Commercial solutions that prioritize fairness, transparency, and accountability 4. Strategic Networks and Partnerships Efforts focused on: Building alliances across sectors Connecting academia, industry, and government Facilitating interdisciplinary collaboration Creating sustainable AI ethics ecosystems 5. Public Engagement and Awareness Projects aimed at: Improving public understanding of AI Encouraging informed discussions about AI ethics Increasing public participation in AI-related decision-making Transforming public discourse around emerging technologies What Makes a Strong Application? The Institute has clearly stated that it is looking for projects that are already on a well-defined path toward impact. Applicants should note that this fellowship is not intended for: Early-stage concepts Idea-stage proposals Proof-of-concept projects Blue-sky research without implementation plans Instead, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate: Existing Project Development Projects should already be underway, with evidence of meaningful progress. Established Partnerships Applicants should have: Existing collaborators Strategic partners already engaged Clearly identified stakeholders who will support implementation Defined Delivery Roadmap Applications should include: Concrete milestones Realistic timelines Deliverables Implementation strategies Impact Measurement Framework Applicants must explain: How impact will be achieved How outcomes will be measured What indicators will be used to evaluate success Why This Fellowship Matters Artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping economies, governments, healthcare systems, education, security, and everyday life. As AI capabilities continue to expand, ethical considerations have become more important than ever. Questions around fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, safety, and societal impact require practical solutions that go beyond academic discussion. The Accelerator Fellowship Programme seeks to bridge this gap by supporting leaders who can transform ethical AI research into actionable solutions that benefit society. Fellowship Benefits Although detailed funding information is provided within the fellowship s expanded sections, participants can generally expect: Affiliation with the University of Oxford s Institute for Ethics in AI Access to world-class expertise and networks Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration Support in accelerating project impact Increased visibility for ethical AI initiatives Engagement with leading researchers, policymakers, and industry practitioners Number of Fellowships Available The Institute for Ethics in AI is seeking to recruit: 3–4 Accelerator Fellows for the current cohort. Application Process Interested applicants should: Review the official eligibility criteria carefully. Ensure their project aligns with at least one Institute research priority. Demonstrate existing project development and partnerships. Prepare a clear impact strategy and implementation roadmap. Submit their application through the official Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI channels. Apply Here Important Contact Information For fellowship-related enquiries: Email: aiethicsafp@philosophy.ox.ac.uk For general enquiries: Email: aiethicscomms@philosophy.ox.ac.uk Final Thoughts The Oxford Accelerator Fellowship Programme represents a unique opportunity for researchers, innovators, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and practitioners working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and ethics. By supporting projects that are already positioned for impact, the programme aims to accelerate real-world solutions that promote responsible AI development, strengthen governance frameworks, build strategic collaborations, and improve public understanding of AI. For individuals and teams committed to ensuring that artificial intelligence develops in ways that are ethical, inclusive, and socially beneficial, this fellowship offers access to one of the world s most influential platforms for AI ethics leadership. title: Scholars Incubator Program 2026: Global Research Fellowship for Emerging Scholars in MENA Studies by Social Sciences Lab MENA
summary: The Scholars Incubator Program offered by the Social Sciences Lab MENA (SSL MENA) is a prestigious international research development initiative designed to support, mentor, and empower emerging scholars in the fields of social sciences and MENA-focused research. This program is not just a short-term training course—it is a structured academic incubation ecosystem that provides junior researchers, graduate students, and early-career scholars with the institutional support, mentorship, and research environment needed to advance their academic careers on a global scale. Based in Europe and focused on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, SSL MENA is an independent, non-governmental, and non-partisan research institution that fosters interdisciplinary collaboration and academic excellence. The Scholars Incubator Program is one of its flagship initiatives, designed to bridge the gap between early academic potential and global research opportunities. About Social Sciences Lab MENA (SSL MENA) The Social Sciences Lab MENA is a European-based independent research institution dedicated to building a global scholarly community focused on MENA studies. The Lab brings together researchers from different academic disciplines, ideologies, and regions to encourage collaboration, knowledge exchange, and high-quality research output. Its core mission includes: Developing interdisciplinary research networks focused on the MENA region Supporting emerging scholars in academic publishing and funding applications Providing institutional affiliation to researchers worldwide Facilitating field research and research support services Connecting scholars across senior and junior academic levels Promoting independent research and intellectual freedom Unlike traditional institutions, SSL MENA does not impose a fixed research agenda. Instead, it empowers scholars to pursue their own research interests with institutional guidance and support. What is the Scholars Incubator Program? The Scholars Incubator Program is a structured academic development fellowship designed to help emerging researchers strengthen their academic identity, research capabilities, and publication potential. It provides participants with: Academic mentorship and supervision Research collaboration opportunities Institutional affiliation with a European research institute Publishing and funding application support Access to academic networks and research communities The program is designed to be both intellectually rigorous and professionally supportive, ensuring scholars develop practical research skills while advancing their academic careers. Program Vision and Philosophy The Scholars Incubator Program is built on the belief that researchers should have intellectual freedom, structured support, and collaborative opportunities. Key principles include: 1. Researcher-Centered Approach Participants are encouraged to develop independent research ideas rather than follow a fixed institutional agenda. 2. Inclusive Academic Environment The program welcomes scholars from diverse backgrounds, ideologies, and academic traditions, provided they adhere to research ethics and academic standards. 3. Interdisciplinary Collaboration Scholars from different disciplines work together to enrich research perspectives and outcomes. 4. Long-Term Academic Growth The program is designed not just for short-term training but for long-term academic career development. Key Benefits of the Scholars Incubator Program Participants in the program gain access to a wide range of academic, professional, and institutional benefits. 1. Research Affiliation One-year affiliation with the Social Sciences Lab MENA Possible extension through continued engagement with the Lab Community Recognition of academic participation and training 2. Mentorship and Academic Supervision Personalized mentorship from experienced scholars Guidance on research design and methodology Support in developing academic career pathways 3. Publishing and Academic Writing Support Participants receive: Guidance on academic publishing processes Editing and proofreading support Assistance in preparing journal submissions Feedback on research manuscripts 4. Funding and Career Development Support The program provides structured guidance for: Applying to research grants and fellowships European funding schemes such as: ERC (European Research Council) Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Erasmus+ programs Research position applications across academic institutions 5. Access to Research Resources Scholars benefit from: Access to research data and institutional resources Participation in collaborative research projects Fieldwork and methodological support Integration into thematic research groups 6. Networking and Academic Community Participants join a global scholarly network that includes: Junior and senior researchers Principal investigators Guest scholars and experts Interdisciplinary academic communities This network enables long-term academic collaboration and professional development. 7. Certification and Institutional Recognition Participants receive: Affiliation certificate from SSL MENA Recognition of training participation Support letters when required for academic applications Program Structure and Learning Experience The Scholars Incubator Program is structured to provide a balanced academic and practical experience. Core Activities Include: 1. Mentorship Sessions 30 minutes monthly (individual sessions) Focused academic guidance and progress review 2. Monthly Group Sessions 1-hour collaborative academic discussions Peer learning and research exchange 3. Workshops and Opportunities Sessions 1-hour monthly training sessions Focus on research tools, publishing, and funding applications 4. Focus Zone Sessions 2-hour intensive group research discussions Project development and methodological support 5. Research Groups (Bonus Component) Participation based on availability of senior scholars and principal investigators Collaborative interdisciplinary research projects Research Environment and Academic Philosophy SSL MENA emphasizes flexibility and intellectual independence while maintaining academic rigor. Key features include: No fixed daily schedule for activities Flexible online participation model Weekend-focused sessions to accommodate global participants Clear deadlines for specific tasks Strong emphasis on peer collaboration and academic excellence Post-Program Opportunities and Long-Term Support One of the strongest aspects of the program is its continued support after completion. Participants gain access to the Lab Community , which provides: Continued research collaboration opportunities Access to funding calls and grant databases Integration into research projects and teams Ongoing mentorship and academic support Opportunities to publish and present research Career development across global academic networks This ensures that scholars continue to grow beyond the formal program duration.
