title: FAO Global Youth Contest 2026: Win a Fully Funded Trip to Rome for the World Food Forum
summary: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), through the FAO elearning Academy and the World Food Forum (WFF), has launched the Global Youth Contest: From Learning to Impact 2026 , a prestigious international competition designed to showcase how young people are transforming knowledge into meaningful action. The contest offers an exciting opportunity for young learners and professionals worldwide to share how courses completed through the FAO elearning Academy have contributed to their personal growth, academic development, professional advancement, and community impact. Three outstanding winners will be selected to receive a fully funded trip to Rome, Italy , where they will participate in the World Food Forum 2026 , one of the world s leading platforms for youth engagement in sustainable agrifood systems. Applications are open until 31 July 2026 (23:59 CEST) . About the FAO Global Youth Contest 2026 The Global Youth Contest seeks to celebrate inspiring stories of learning and impact from young people who have benefited from the FAO elearning Academy. The initiative aims to demonstrate how digital learning can empower individuals to acquire valuable knowledge, develop practical skills, and create positive change within their communities and professional environments. Participants are invited to submit a compelling written story explaining: How the FAO elearning Academy has influenced their educational or professional journey. The skills and knowledge gained through FAO courses. How they have applied their learning in real-world situations. The impact their learning has generated within their community, workplace, organization, or field of study. Applicants must support their stories with verified course completion records and certified digital badges earned through the FAO elearning Academy. Why You Should Apply The FAO Global Youth Contest offers much more than recognition. 1. Win a Fully Funded Trip to Rome Three winners will receive: Round-trip international travel Accommodation Participation costs Access to the World Food Forum 2026 The World Food Forum will take place in Rome, Italy, from 12–15 October 2026 . 2. Gain International Visibility Selected winners will be featured through: Video interviews FAO elearning Academy website FAO Education Hub YouTube Channel FAO social media platforms This exposure can significantly strengthen participants professional profiles and networks. 3. Share Your Story Globally The contest provides a platform for young people to inspire others through their experiences and achievements. 4. Join a Global Community of Changemakers Participants become part of a worldwide movement focused on: Sustainable agriculture Food security Climate resilience Rural development Sustainable agrifood systems 5. Showcase Your Impact The contest recognizes individuals who have successfully translated learning into action and tangible outcomes. Objectives of the Contest The FAO Global Youth Contest aims to: Highlight Stories of Impact Showcase how FAO learning opportunities are creating meaningful change globally. Promote Learning-to-Action Approaches Demonstrate practical applications of knowledge acquired through FAO courses. Encourage Peer Learning Enable young people to learn from one another’s experiences and innovations. Amplify Youth Voices Increase global awareness of youth-led solutions in agriculture and food systems. Support Sustainable Development Recognize young leaders contributing to more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient agrifood systems. Who Can Apply? To be eligible, applicants must: Age Requirement Be between 18 and 35 years old . Registration Requirement Be a registered learner of the FAO elearning Academy. Learning Requirement Applicants must demonstrate that FAO elearning Academy courses have contributed to: Knowledge acquisition Skills development Academic growth Professional advancement Community impact Digital Badge Requirement Applicants must: Complete FAO elearning Academy courses. Obtain certified digital badges. Travel Requirement Selected winners must possess: A passport valid until at least April 2027 . Eligible Countries The contest is open globally. Applicants can come from: Africa Asia Europe North America South America Oceania Caribbean nations Small Island Developing States FAO specifically encourages participation from: Underrepresented groups Vulnerable communities Marginalized populations Contest Prize Three winners will receive: Fully Funded Participation at the World Food Forum 2026 The prize includes: International airfare Accommodation Participation costs Attendance at the World Food Forum in Rome Global Recognition Winners will be featured in: Professional video interviews FAO elearning Academy homepage FAO Education Hub Official FAO communication channels Evaluation Criteria Applications will be reviewed based on: 1. Availability for the Award Process Applicants must be able to participate in: Interviews Travel requirements World Food Forum activities 2. Number of Digital Badges Earned A stronger portfolio of completed courses and badges may strengthen an application. 3. Quality of the Impact Story Reviewers will assess: Clarity Authenticity Demonstrated impact Practical application of learning 4. Course Completion Verification Applicants must have verifiable completion records for FAO Academy courses. 5. Inclusion Considerations Additional consideration may be given to applicants from: Vulnerable groups Marginalized communities Underrepresented populations How to Apply Step 1: Create an FAO elearning Academy Account If you are not already registered, create an account on the FAO elearning Academy platform. Step 2: Complete Courses Enroll in courses relevant to your interests and career goals. Step 3: Earn Digital Badges Successfully complete courses and collect certified digital badges. Step 4: Prepare Your Impact Story Write a compelling story (maximum 4,000 characters) describing: Your learning journey Skills acquired Career or academic development Community impact Real-world application of knowledge Step 5: Complete the Application Form Submit: Your personal information FAO Academy account email List of earned badges Impact story Step 6: Submit Before the Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 31 July 2026 (23:59 CEST) Apply Here Important Rules Applicants should note that: Only one application is permitted per participant. Applications must be submitted in English. AI-generated responses are strictly prohibited. False information may lead to disqualification. Applicants must own the rights to submitted content. Winners must participate in promotional activities and interviews. Why This Opportunity Matters The FAO Global Youth Contest 2026 offers a rare opportunity for young people to gain international recognition while demonstrating how education can drive meaningful impact. Whether you are a student, researcher, entrepreneur, agricultural professional, development practitioner, or community leader, this contest provides a global platform to showcase your achievements and connect with fellow changemakers working toward more sustainable agrifood systems. Young people who have actively engaged with the FAO elearning Academy and transformed knowledge into action should strongly consider applying for this prestigious opportunity. title: University of Gothenburg Doctoral Position in Peace and Development Research 2026: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity in Sweden on Host-State Responses to Transnational Repression
summary: The University of Gothenburg, one of Scandinavia s leading research-intensive universities, has announced an exceptional doctoral opportunity for aspiring researchers interested in peace, development, migration, human rights, governance, and security studies. The institution is inviting applications for a fully funded Doctoral Student Position in Peace and Development Research with a specialized focus on Host-State Responses to Transnational Repression (TNR). This prestigious PhD opportunity is hosted by the School of Global Studies at the University of Gothenburg and forms part of an international research project examining transnational repression and the responses of host states across the Nordic-Baltic region. The successful candidate will join a vibrant international research environment and contribute to cutting-edge scholarship on one of the most important emerging issues in global politics, migration, democracy, and human rights. Deadline: 14 August 2026 Interested candidates must submit their complete application no later than 14 August 2026 . About the University of Gothenburg The University of Gothenburg is one of Sweden s largest and most respected higher education institutions. With approximately 58,000 students and over 6,800 employees, the university provides a dynamic environment for learning, innovation, and research. Known for addressing major societal challenges through interdisciplinary knowledge and international collaboration, the university attracts talented researchers and students from around the world. Its commitment to academic excellence, diversity, inclusion, and global engagement makes it an attractive destination for doctoral candidates seeking world-class research training. About Peace and Development Research at the University of Gothenburg Peace and Development Research at the University of Gothenburg is internationally recognized as a leading interdisciplinary research environment. The department includes approximately 50 researchers who employ diverse theoretical and methodological approaches to investigate critical global challenges. Research themes include: Peace and conflict Security studies Human rights Gender and development Migration and diaspora studies Global governance Regional governance Political economy Resistance and social movements International relations Democracy and authoritarianism The doctoral candidate will become part of this thriving academic community and contribute to internationally relevant research. Understanding the Research Focus: Host-State Responses to Transnational Repression The advertised doctoral project focuses on Transnational Repression (TNR), a growing phenomenon attracting significant international attention. Transnational repression refers to actions undertaken by authoritarian governments to intimidate, silence, punish, monitor, or undermine dissidents, activists, journalists, and political opponents living outside their home countries. The doctoral research will be conducted within a larger international project examining: How transnational repression occurs across borders How democratic host states respond to these threats Legal frameworks addressing transnational repression Public policy responses Institutional awareness and preparedness Protection mechanisms for vulnerable diaspora communities Possible Research Areas Applicants are encouraged to develop innovative research proposals connected to host-state responses to transnational repression. Potential areas of investigation include: 1. Awareness Among Government Institutions Research may examine awareness levels among: Law enforcement agencies Immigration authorities Border control institutions Cybersecurity agencies National security organizations 2. Government Outreach to Vulnerable Diasporas Candidates may investigate: State engagement with migrant communities Protection initiatives Trust-building measures Community resilience strategies 3. Collaboration Between Government and Civil Society Research could focus on: Partnerships between public institutions and NGOs Advocacy networks Human rights organizations Community support structures 4. Reporting Mechanisms for TNR Incidents Potential topics include: Incident reporting procedures Victim support systems Accessibility of reporting channels Institutional responsiveness 5. Investigation and Prosecution of Perpetrators Candidates may explore: Criminal justice responses Legal frameworks Judicial processes International cooperation mechanisms 6. Other Relevant Topics The university encourages applicants to propose innovative research ideas related to transnational repression and democratic governance. Comparative Nordic-Baltic Research Framework The doctoral project will adopt a comparative approach focusing on two or three Nordic-Baltic countries. Possible case countries include: Sweden Norway Estonia Applicants are encouraged to justify their case selection and explain how comparative analysis can contribute to advancing academic understanding of transnational repression. Structure of the Doctoral Programme The doctoral programme spans four years of full-time study and leads to the award of a Doctoral Degree (PhD). Programme Components Coursework The first year includes structured doctoral-level coursework designed to strengthen theoretical, methodological, and analytical competencies. Research Activities Three years are primarily devoted to: Data collection Fieldwork Comparative analysis Academic writing Conference participation Publication development Dissertation The programme culminates in the production of an original doctoral dissertation that makes a significant scholarly contribution to Peace and Development Research. Employment and Funding Upon admission, the successful candidate will be employed by the University of Gothenburg as a doctoral student. Benefits include: Fully funded doctoral position Monthly salary according to University of Gothenburg regulations Access to university resources and facilities Participation in international research networks Academic supervision by leading scholars Professional development opportunities Possibility of teaching experience The university applies local doctoral salary agreements and provides employment benefits associated with Swedish higher education institutions. Teaching and Departmental Responsibilities Doctoral students may undertake departmental duties corresponding to up to 20% of full-time employment. These responsibilities may include: Teaching undergraduate courses Assisting in graduate-level instruction Research support activities Administrative responsibilities Such duties extend the total study period accordingly. Required Qualifications Applicants must satisfy both general and specific doctoral admission requirements. title: IGAD In-Country Training and Mentorship for Women and Youth MSMEs on Gender-Sensitive Digital Trade 2026: Fully Sponsored Regional Capacity Building Programme for Entrepreneurs in East Africa
summary: Applications are now open for the IGAD In-Country Training and Mentorship for Women and Youth MSMEs on Gender-Sensitive Digital Trade 2026, a regional initiative under the Horn of Africa Digital Market Integration (HDMI) Project – Phase I. Organized by the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), this important programme seeks to strengthen the capacity of women and youth-led micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across the IGAD region through specialized training and mentorship on digital trade, e-commerce, digital financial services, and cross-border market opportunities. The programme will run from July to December 2026 across multiple IGAD Member States and is specifically designed to empower entrepreneurs with practical digital trade skills that will help them access regional and global markets, leverage technology for business growth, and benefit from opportunities created through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). As Africa continues to accelerate digital transformation and regional economic integration, women and youth entrepreneurs remain central to building inclusive economic growth. However, gender inequalities, limited access to technology, digital literacy gaps, and restricted financial inclusion continue to affect the participation of women and youth in digital trade ecosystems. Through this initiative, IGAD aims to close these gaps by equipping MSMEs with the tools, knowledge, and mentorship required to compete successfully in today’s digital economy. The training programme will use the Gender Action Learning System (GALS) methodology, a participatory and inclusive approach designed to strengthen gender-sensitive economic empowerment and business development. title: UNITAR–FAO Trade, Food Security and Nutrition (TFSN) Course 2026: Free Online Training Opportunity for Policymakers, Researchers, and Agricultural Trade Professionals in Africa
summary: The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), in partnership with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), is offering a fully funded online training programme titled Trade, Food Security and Nutrition (TFSN) . This highly specialized course is designed to strengthen the capacity of policymakers, government officials, researchers, and agricultural trade professionals across Eastern and Southern Africa. Scheduled to run from 13 July 2026 to 14 August 2026 , this five-week e-learning programme provides participants with a unique opportunity to deepen their understanding of the complex relationship between agricultural trade, food security, nutrition, and sustainable development. The course is offered completely free of charge and is delivered online, making it accessible to professionals across multiple African countries without the need for travel. Successful participants will receive a certificate of completion from UNITAR and FAO. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early as places are limited and participation is subject to a competitive selection process. Why This Course Matters Food security remains one of the most pressing development challenges facing Africa. At the same time, trade is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for promoting economic growth, agricultural transformation, and poverty reduction. The relationship between trade and food security has become a major focus of global development discussions, particularly as countries work toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including the goal of ending hunger by 2030. Through the 2014 Malabo Declaration, African governments committed to increasing intra-African agricultural trade and leveraging regional and international markets to stimulate agricultural development. However, expanding trade alone does not automatically improve food security. Policymakers must carefully design trade policies that enhance agricultural productivity while ensuring access to nutritious food and supporting vulnerable populations. This course addresses these critical issues by helping participants understand how trade policies can support food security, nutrition, and sustainable development. About the Trade, Food Security and Nutrition Course The Trade, Food Security and Nutrition (TFSN) Course aims to strengthen institutional and individual capacity across Eastern and Southern Africa. Participants will learn how to: Analyze the relationship between trade and food security Understand the effects of agricultural trade on nutrition outcomes Evaluate trade policy measures Formulate evidence-based trade policies Negotiate trade agreements effectively Assess food security implications of trade liberalization Understand international trade governance frameworks Promote policy coherence between trade and nutrition objectives The course combines theoretical foundations with practical regional experiences and case studies relevant to Africa s agricultural and economic realities. Learning Objectives By the end of the programme, participants will be able to: 1. Assess Trade and Food Security Challenges Participants will gain the ability to: Identify opportunities created by trade liberalization Evaluate risks associated with increased market openness Analyze food security outcomes resulting from trade policies 2. Understand Trade Policy Measures Learners will explore: Different types of trade interventions Agricultural support policies Trade facilitation mechanisms Policy design considerations Implementation challenges 3. Examine Global Trade Governance Participants will study: The World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on Agriculture Global trade governance systems Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) International food security frameworks 4. Evaluate Trade and Nutrition Linkages The course will help participants understand: How trade influences food prices The impact of trade on dietary diversity Nutrient availability and food imports Policy coherence between nutrition and trade agendas Course Structure and Curriculum The programme is divided into four comprehensive units. Unit 1: Introduction to Trade and Food Security Lesson 1.1: Definitions and Linkages Between Trade and Food Security Topics include: Trade fundamentals Food security concepts Economic linkages Agricultural market dynamics Lesson 1.2: Impacts of Trade on Food Security Participants will examine: Positive and negative impacts of trade Household food access Agricultural productivity Market integration Unit 2: Trade Policy Supportive of Food Security Lesson 2.1: Trade Policy Measures and Agricultural Development Areas covered include: Tariffs Trade restrictions Agricultural support measures Market interventions Lesson 2.2: Design and Implementation of Trade Policy Measures Participants will learn: Policy formulation approaches Implementation frameworks Monitoring and evaluation mechanisms Unit 3: Governance of Trade and Food Security Lesson 3.1: Introduction to the Multilateral Trading System Topics include: WTO fundamentals Global trade agreements International trade governance Lesson 3.2: Policy Space for Food Security in the Multilateral Trading System Participants will explore: National policy flexibility Trade obligations Food security safeguards Lesson 3.3: Towards Improved Governance for Trade and Food Security Focus areas include: Institutional coordination Governance reforms Regional cooperation Unit 4: Trade and Nutrition – Policy Coherence for Healthy Diets Lesson 4.1: Trade and Nutrition Linkages Participants will study: Food systems Nutrition outcomes International food trade Lesson 4.2: Trade in Food and Nutrients Topics include: Food diversity Nutrient availability Food affordability Market access Lesson 4.3: Strengthening Policy Coherence for Trade and Nutrition Participants will learn strategies for: Integrating nutrition objectives into trade policies Supporting healthier diets Aligning national development priorities Course Delivery Method The programme is delivered entirely online through UNITAR s e-learning platform. Duration Five weeks 13 July 2026 – 14 August 2026 Language English only Learning Format Participants will engage in: Self-paced learning Reading assignments Interactive discussions Case study exercises Assessment quizzes Expert-led webinars The course is facilitated by international experts with extensive practical experience in agricultural trade, food security, and development policy. Benefits of Participating Participants will gain numerous professional and technical benefits, including: Professional Development Enhanced trade policy expertise Improved understanding of food security issues Practical knowledge of agricultural trade governance Increased capacity for policy formulation Networking Opportunities Interaction with professionals across Africa Access to international experts Exposure to regional perspectives and experiences Career Advancement Strengthened policy analysis skills Greater capacity to influence trade and food security decisions Enhanced professional credentials Certification Participants who successfully complete all assignments and assessments will receive an official Certificate of Completion from UNITAR and FAO. Selection Process Because the course is offered free of charge, spaces are limited. Selection will be conducted by FAO based on: Relevance of applicant s professional role Geographic representation Gender balance considerations Potential impact of acquired knowledge Priority will be given to professionals who influence agricultural trade policies and food security programmes at regional, national, or sector levels. Applicants selected for participation may also be required to obtain approval from their direct supervisors before receiving final confirmation. Application Deadline Deadline: 15 June 2026 Why You Should Apply Trade and food security are increasingly interconnected issues shaping the future of agriculture, economic development, and nutrition across Africa. This UNITAR–FAO programme offers a rare opportunity to learn directly from leading international experts while gaining practical skills that can immediately be applied within government institutions, research organizations, development agencies, and the private sector. With no participation fee, expert-led instruction, flexible online learning, and an internationally recognized certificate, the Trade, Food Security and Nutrition Course is an outstanding professional development opportunity for anyone working at the intersection of agriculture, trade, food systems, and public policy. The programme offers an exceptional opportunity for women in Nigeria to gain hands-on exposure to one of the world s fastest-growing sectors while contributing to the global transition toward clean and sustainable energy. title: WUSC DREEM Deputy Project Director Job 2026: Lead a Pan-African Initiative Empowering One Million Refugee and Displaced Youth Across Africa
summary: The World University Service of Canada (WUSC) is seeking an exceptional bilingual development professional to join its flagship DREEM initiative as Deputy Project Director (DPD). This senior leadership opportunity offers experienced professionals the chance to contribute to one of Africa’s most ambitious refugee and displaced youth empowerment programs. The position supports the implementation of the second phase of the DREEM initiative (2026–2031), a transformative Pan-African programme that aims to significantly improve education and employment opportunities for refugee, displaced, and host community youth, particularly young women. The successful candidate will play a central role in shaping strategy, managing technical teams, coordinating partnerships, and driving implementation across multiple African countries. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interested candidates are strongly encouraged to apply early. About WUSC World University Service of Canada (WUSC) is a leading Canadian international development organization dedicated to creating positive educational and economic opportunities for young people around the world. WUSC’s vision is a world where every young person thrives and feels a sense of belonging. Through innovative partnerships and locally driven solutions, the organization works to ensure that young people can realize their aspirations and build meaningful futures. Headquartered in Ottawa, Canada, WUSC operates across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, Latin America, and the Middle East. The organization is recognized globally for delivering sustainable development programs that create measurable and lasting impact. WUSC offers a dynamic multicultural working environment that brings together professionals from diverse backgrounds who share a commitment to social justice, inclusion, and youth empowerment. About the DREEM Initiative In January 2026, WUSC launched Phase II of the DREEM programme, which will run until 2031. The initiative focuses on supporting refugee, displaced, and host community youth (RDP youth) across Africa by helping them access dignified employment opportunities and quality education. Building on the achievements of its first phase, DREEM Phase II seeks to expand its reach into new geographic areas while strengthening local systems that support refugee and displaced populations. Vision and Goals of DREEM Phase II The programme has set highly ambitious targets for the next five years, including: Indirectly enabling one million refugee, displaced, and host community youth to secure dignified employment opportunities. Supporting 35,000 young people to access education opportunities. Strengthening the inclusion of refugee and displaced youth in economic systems. Enhancing access to higher education and technical education pathways. Building sustainable local capacity through Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs). The programme places a strong emphasis on supporting young women and promoting gender-responsive development approaches. The Strategic Role of Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs) A defining feature of DREEM Phase II is its commitment to localization and refugee leadership. The initiative recognizes Refugee-Led Organizations as critical actors in creating sustainable and community-driven solutions. The programme will support RLOs through three key mechanisms: 1. RLO Opportunity Fund Providing direct financial access and support to Refugee-Led Organizations. 2. Capacity Strengthening Equipping RLOs with technical expertise and organizational development support. 3. Integrated Participation Embedding RLOs throughout programme implementation and decision-making processes. This strategy aims to create sustainable local ownership and long-term impact. Position Overview: Deputy Project Director The Deputy Project Director serves as the second-in-command of the DREEM programme and works closely with the Project Director to ensure successful programme implementation and achievement of results. The DPD will support strategic planning, operational oversight, staff management, partnership coordination, and technical leadership at the Pan-African level. The role is ideal for a visionary leader who combines technical expertise with strong people management and partnership-building skills. Preferred Duty Stations WUSC offers flexibility regarding the candidate s duty station. Preference will be given to candidates based in: Nairobi, Kenya Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire Accra, Ghana Kigali, Rwanda Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Lagos, Nigeria The successful candidate must already possess legal work authorization in the country where they intend to be based. No relocation allowance will be provided. Key Technical Areas of Responsibility The Deputy Project Director will oversee three major technical pillars of the programme. 1. Refugee-Led Organization Engagement Supporting localization efforts and strengthening refugee-led institutions. 2. Technical Assistance Mechanism Providing technical support to partners across the DREEM ecosystem. 3. Higher Education Inclusion Expanding access to higher education opportunities for refugee and displaced youth. The DPD will directly supervise Senior Technical Managers responsible for these pillars as well as the Training and Curriculum Development Specialist. Core Responsibilities The successful candidate will be responsible for a wide range of leadership, technical, and operational functions. Strategic Programme Leadership Responsibilities include: Ensuring project activities achieve annual workplan commitments. Supporting adaptive management and programme quality assurance. Driving implementation of programme objectives across Africa. Staff Leadership and Capacity Building The Deputy Project Director will: Mentor and coach programme staff. Strengthen competencies in project management and partnership development. Build staff capacity around refugee inclusion approaches. Training and Technical Support Responsibilities include: Developing training materials and capacity-building tools. Designing coaching and mentoring interventions. Supporting organizational learning initiatives. Partnership Development and Stakeholder Engagement The role involves: Building relationships with implementing partners. Coordinating with consultants and subcontractors. Managing strategic donor relationships. Collaborating with government stakeholders and institutions. Donor Coordination The Deputy Project Director will work closely with: Mastercard Foundation WUSC headquarters in Canada African country teams Youth Advisory Board Youth Technical Committee The DPD may also represent the programme when required. Programme Planning and Management Additional responsibilities include: Budget development Annual work planning Project reporting Monitoring implementation performance Ensuring compliance with donor requirements Qualifications and Experience Required WUSC is seeking a highly qualified professional with extensive experience in international development and refugee inclusion. Education Candidates must possess: A Master s Degree in: International Development Education Public Policy Social Sciences Or a related discipline Additional project management certifications such as PMP or PRINCE2 are considered strong assets. Language Requirements Fluency in both English and French is mandatory. This bilingual requirement reflects the programme s Pan-African scope and the need to work effectively across Anglophone and Francophone countries. Sector Expertise Candidates should demonstrate substantial experience in one or more of the following sectors: Forced displacement Refugee inclusion Inclusive market systems Higher education International development Specialized Technical Expertise Applicants should possess expertise in at least one of the following areas: Localization and organizational strengthening Refugee-Led Organization development Refugee inclusion in higher education Technical assistance design and delivery Leadership and Project Management Experience The ideal candidate will demonstrate: Extensive project management experience Budget management expertise Work planning experience Team leadership and coaching abilities Cross-cultural management skills Why This Opportunity Stands Out This position offers a unique opportunity to shape one of Africa s largest refugee and displaced youth inclusion programmes. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to: Influence policy and programming across multiple African countries. Contribute to improving opportunities for one million young people. Work with leading international development partners. Lead innovative approaches to refugee inclusion. Strengthen Refugee-Led Organizations across Africa. Drive systemic change in education and employment ecosystems. Additional Considerations Candidates should be aware that: The position may require periodic travel across Africa. Flexible working hours may occasionally be required. Criminal background verification may be conducted where appropriate. WUSC maintains a strict commitment to safeguarding, accountability, respect, and professional integrity. Application Information Applications are reviewed continuously on a rolling basis. Because the recruitment process may close once a suitable candidate has been identified, interested professionals are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible. This is a rare opportunity for experienced bilingual development leaders to contribute to transformative change for refugee and displaced youth across Africa while working with one of the continent s most innovative and impactful international development initiatives. title: Uganda Refugee Support, Empowerment and Transformation (ReSET) Project 2026: Up to £20 Million Available for NGOs Supporting Refugees and Host Communities in Uganda
summary: Organizations working to improve the lives of refugees and host communities in Uganda now have an important opportunity to secure significant funding through the Uganda Refugee Support, Empowerment and Transformation (ReSET) Project. The British High Commission in Kampala, through the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO), has officially launched a call for proposals seeking experienced partners to help address humanitarian needs while building long-term resilience and self-reliance among refugee populations and host communities. With a total funding envelope of up to £20 million over a period of two and a half years, this initiative represents one of the most significant refugee-focused development funding opportunities currently available in Uganda. The programme is designed to support vulnerable refugee populations, strengthen host communities, and contribute to Uganda’s globally recognized refugee policy framework. Organizations interested in participating must submit their concept notes by 16 June 2026 at 11:59 PM East Africa Time (EAT). About the Uganda ReSET Programme The Uganda Refugee Support, Empowerment and Transformation (ReSET) Programme is a bilateral partnership between the United Kingdom and the Government of Uganda. The initiative seeks to support Uganda’s transition from a predominantly humanitarian refugee response model toward a more sustainable approach centered on resilience, empowerment, and self-reliance. Uganda is internationally recognized for its progressive refugee policies, which provide refugees with rights and opportunities that are often unavailable in many other refugee-hosting countries. However, increasing refugee numbers and growing resource constraints have created significant challenges that require innovative and sustainable solutions. To address these challenges, the ReSET Programme focuses on helping refugees become more self-reliant while ensuring that urgent humanitarian needs continue to be met. The programme s business case was approved in March 2026, and activities funded through this call for proposals will run from August 2026 through March 2029. Funding Overview Key details of the funding opportunity include: Funding Organization: Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) through the British High Commission Kampala Programme Name: Refugee Support, Empowerment and Transformation (ReSET) Total Available Funding: Up to £20 million Implementation Period: August 2026 – March 2029 Duration: Approximately 2.5 years Geographic Focus: Uganda Eligible Applicants: NGOs registered under the Uganda NGO Bureau Deadline: 16 June 2026 at 11:59 PM EAT Objectives of the ReSET Programme The ReSET Programme aims to create lasting positive change by supporting both immediate humanitarian assistance and long-term development outcomes. The initiative is built around two major pillars that organizations may choose to address individually or jointly. Pillar 1: Meeting Core Humanitarian Needs The first pillar focuses on ensuring that the most vulnerable refugees and affected host communities receive critical humanitarian support. This includes: Food Security Support Organizations may propose interventions that: Improve access to food for vulnerable populations Reduce food insecurity among refugee households Support nutrition-sensitive programming Address emergency food needs among newly arrived refugees Protection Services Projects may focus on: Child protection Gender-based violence prevention and response Legal protection services Community-based protection mechanisms Protection of vulnerable groups Multisectoral Humanitarian Assistance Applicants are encouraged to design integrated responses that combine multiple services to effectively address urgent humanitarian needs. Special attention should be given to: Newly arrived refugees Vulnerable women and girls Persons with disabilities Youth Host communities affected by humanitarian shocks Pillar 2: Building Self-Reliance and Resilience The second pillar focuses on helping refugees and host communities move beyond dependence on humanitarian assistance. The objective is to enable economically vulnerable households to build sustainable livelihoods and increase resilience against future shocks. Areas of intervention may include: Economic Empowerment Projects could support: Income generation Entrepreneurship Vocational training Financial inclusion Skills development Livelihood Strengthening Potential interventions include: Agricultural development Market access initiatives Value chain development Business incubation Employment creation Resilience Building Organizations may propose activities aimed at: Improving household resilience Strengthening community coping mechanisms Enhancing disaster preparedness Reducing vulnerability to economic and environmental shocks Cross-Cutting Themes and Priorities The British High Commission and FCDO emphasize that all projects should align with several important cross-cutting priorities. Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Applicants should demonstrate how their interventions will: Promote gender equality Empower women and girls Increase opportunities for marginalized groups Ensure inclusive participation Climate Resilience Projects should integrate climate-smart approaches and support communities in adapting to environmental challenges. Social Cohesion Successful proposals should strengthen positive relationships between refugees and host communities. Localization Organizations are encouraged to incorporate local leadership and community-driven solutions into project design and implementation. Alignment with Government Priorities Proposals should demonstrate alignment with: Government of Uganda policies National refugee frameworks International Financial Institution (IFI) priorities Existing development strategies Who Can Apply? The ReSET call for proposals is open to organizations that meet the following requirements: Eligible Organizations International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) National Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs) Registration Requirement All applicants must possess valid registration under the Uganda NGO Bureau. Consortium Applications Encouraged The British High Commission welcomes applications from: Individual organizations Partnerships Consortia Consortium approaches may provide opportunities to combine expertise across multiple sectors and improve the overall impact of proposed interventions. How to Apply Organizations must submit an Expression of Interest through a concept note. Concept Note Requirements Applicants are required to submit: A concept note not exceeding seven pages A clear implementation strategy Expected outcomes and impacts Alignment with ReSET objectives Budget considerations Organizational capacity information Applicants May Propose Activities Under: Pillar 1 only – Core Humanitarian Needs Pillar 2 only – Self-Reliance and Resilience Both Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 Organizations should clearly indicate which pillar(s) their proposal addresses. Why This Funding Opportunity Matters Uganda hosts one of the largest refugee populations in Africa and continues to demonstrate leadership through its inclusive refugee policies. However, increasing humanitarian demands require innovative approaches that not only address immediate needs but also create sustainable pathways toward independence and resilience. Through the ReSET Programme, the UK Government aims to: Improve humanitarian outcomes Strengthen economic opportunities Enhance social cohesion Promote gender equality Build climate resilience Support long-term development solutions The programme represents a major investment in creating durable solutions for refugees and host communities while strengthening Uganda’s refugee response system. Key Benefits of the ReSET Funding Opportunity Organizations selected under this initiative may benefit from: Access to a funding pool worth up to £20 million Long-term implementation period of approximately 2.5 years Opportunity to influence refugee policy and development outcomes Support for both humanitarian and development programming Increased visibility through partnership with the UK Government Potential for large-scale impact among refugee and host populations Opportunities for collaboration through consortium approaches Important Deadline Organizations must submit their concept notes no later than: 16 June 2026 at 11:59 PM East Africa Time (EAT) Late submissions may not be considered. Contact Information For questions and clarifications regarding the ReSET call for proposals, applicants may contact: bhckampala.submissions@fcdo.gov.uk Interested organizations are encouraged to begin preparing their concept notes immediately to ensure sufficient time for proposal development and submission before the deadline. title: How GiveWell Is Searching for the Best Ways to Help in 2026: A $500 Million Strategy to Save Lives Through Global Health, Nutrition, Water, Vaccination, and Poverty Reduction
summary: As global development challenges continue to affect millions of people worldwide, identifying the most cost-effective ways to save and improve lives remains one of the most important tasks in philanthropy. In 2026, GiveWell has unveiled an ambitious strategy aimed at directing at least $500 million toward the highest-impact opportunities in global health and development. The organization s research efforts are centered on two major goals: Expanding its research capacity to identify more highly effective programs capable of absorbing significant funding. Granting at least $500 million to interventions that can generate measurable improvements in health, survival, and well-being. To achieve these goals, GiveWell has doubled the size of its research team in recent years. The organization now employs approximately 60 researchers distributed across 11 specialized research units covering critical sectors such as malaria prevention, nutrition, vaccination, water quality, livelihoods, health systems strengthening, and emerging global health opportunities. This article explores GiveWell s comprehensive roadmap for 2026 and the strategies it plans to use to identify and fund life-saving interventions around the world. GiveWell s Research Expansion Strategy GiveWell s growing research infrastructure reflects its commitment to evidence-based philanthropy. Rather than focusing solely on proven interventions, the organization is increasingly investing in identifying new opportunities with the potential for large-scale impact. Its research structure now includes specialized teams dedicated to: Malaria Nutrition Vaccination Water Quality Livelihoods and Poverty Reduction New Global Health Areas Cross-Cutting Research Research Operations Commons (Research Review and Quality Assurance) Each team contributes to a broader mission of ensuring that donor funding reaches programs capable of generating the greatest possible benefit per dollar spent. Malaria: GiveWell s Largest Research Area Malaria remains one of the deadliest infectious diseases globally, causing approximately 600,000 deaths annually. Young children in Africa bear the greatest burden, accounting for roughly 70% of malaria-related deaths. Recognizing the scale of this challenge, GiveWell s malaria research division has become its largest research area, consisting of 15 specialists working across three major subteams. Antimalarial Medicines This team focuses on medicines used to prevent and treat malaria infections. Key Priorities for 2026 1. Optimizing Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC) The team will continue supporting the highly successful SMC programs implemented by organizations such as Malaria Consortium while concentrating on a limited number of high-value research questions. 2. Expanding SMC Coverage Researchers will explore opportunities to increase malaria prevention coverage while evaluating alternative implementing partners. 3. Developing New Prevention Approaches Potential interventions include: Perennial malaria chemoprevention Post-malaria discharge prevention Preventive treatment for school-aged children Improved SMC delivery strategies 4. Improving Access to Treatment Following changes in global health funding, GiveWell has identified gaps in malaria treatment services and plans to continue funding interventions that improve access to diagnosis and treatment. Malaria Vector Control This team focuses on preventing malaria transmission by targeting mosquito populations. Major Research Priorities Expanding Insecticide-Treated Net Distribution Researchers are identifying regions with significant net shortages, particularly in high-burden countries where reductions in aid may have widened coverage gaps. Exploring New Mosquito-Control Technologies Potential future investments include: Routine mosquito net distribution systems Spatial repellents Insecticide-treated baby wraps Innovative vector-control technologies Strengthening Partner Capacity The team will assess and improve collaborations with key implementing organizations to maximize efficiency and impact. Malaria Cross-Cutting Research This group challenges existing assumptions and explores entirely new malaria solutions. Areas of Focus Funding innovative malaria pilot projects Supporting diagnostic market improvements Investigating malaria rebound effects Improving cost-effectiveness modeling Publishing reports that invite external expert review The goal is to continuously refine GiveWell s malaria funding strategy and uncover opportunities that traditional grantmaking channels may overlook. Nutrition: Fighting Hidden Hunger and Malnutrition Nutrition remains one of the most cost-effective areas for improving health outcomes in low- and middle-income countries. The Nutrition Team focuses on interventions targeting: Vitamin A deficiency Iron deficiency anemia Acute malnutrition Micronutrient deficiencies Vitamin A Supplementation Expansion GiveWell continues to support vitamin A supplementation programs where deficiency and child mortality rates remain high. In 2026, researchers will: Explore new geographic areas for expansion Conduct surveys and trials Improve estimates of intervention impact Addressing Anemia in Africa Anemia affects millions of children and women across Africa. The team is currently studying: Iron supplementation strategies Food fortification programs Multiple micronutrient supplementation The interaction between iron interventions and malaria infections Findings from this research may unlock major new funding opportunities across the continent. Reducing the Cost of Malnutrition Treatment Although acute malnutrition treatment can save lives, many programs currently fall below GiveWell s cost-effectiveness threshold. To address this challenge, GiveWell plans to: Consult implementers and donors Identify cost-saving innovations Fund pilot projects Test new treatment models Exploring Additional Health Opportunities Researchers are also investigating broader nutrition-related opportunities, including: Cardiovascular disease prevention Emerging public health interventions Future grantmaking pipelines Vaccination: Reaching the Last Mile Vaccines are among the most effective public health tools ever developed. Despite strong global funding, millions of children still miss essential vaccinations due to geographic and logistical barriers. Expanding Vaccination Outreach Programs GiveWell has already funded outreach initiatives in multiple countries. In 2026, the organization plans to: Launch additional vaccination programs Reach remote communities Conduct independent coverage surveys Evaluate program effectiveness Caregiver Incentive Programs Building on successful experiences with New Incentives, GiveWell is exploring programs that provide small financial incentives to encourage caregivers to vaccinate children. The organization aims to: Recruit new implementing partners Test innovative operational models Expand successful approaches Supporting Malaria Vaccine Rollout Researchers will evaluate opportunities to support: Malaria vaccine deployment Supply chain improvements Vaccine delivery innovations Research and development initiatives Water Quality: Tackling a Global Health Crisis More than one billion people still lack access to safe drinking water. Contaminated water contributes to hundreds of thousands of deaths annually through diseases such as: Diarrhea Cholera Dysentery Typhoid Exploring Alternative Water Treatment Technologies GiveWell is expanding beyond traditional chlorination programs. Technologies under consideration include: Ultraviolet purification systems Water filtration technologies Water kiosks Direct clean-water delivery systems Partnering with Development Banks A promising strategy involves integrating water treatment solutions into large-scale infrastructure projects financed by multilateral development institutions. If successful, this approach could unlock substantial future funding opportunities. Investing in Water Innovation Researchers are supporting: Improved contamination testing systems Low-cost chlorine sensors Market-shaping initiatives Innovation prizes These efforts aim to improve both effectiveness and scalability. Livelihoods: Reducing Extreme Poverty GiveWell has recently increased its focus on interventions that improve economic well-being. The organization is testing whether livelihoods programs deserve a larger share of future philanthropic funding. Cash Transfers Researchers are studying how cash transfers affect: Household consumption Housing quality Local economies Prices and wages The findings may help optimize future poverty-reduction programs. Ultra-Poor Graduation Programs These interventions combine: Productive assets Training Temporary financial support Savings mechanisms Evidence suggests they can create sustainable pathways out of extreme poverty. GiveWell is evaluating newer, potentially more cost-effective versions of these programs. Microfinance Innovation The team is exploring modern microfinance approaches that may produce stronger outcomes than earlier models. Research priorities include: Productive asset financing New targeting mechanisms Improved delivery models New Areas: Expanding Beyond Traditional Funding Priorities GiveWell is actively exploring health interventions that have received relatively little funding in the past. Potential focus areas include: Tuberculosis Medical oxygen Drug quality improvement Artificial intelligence for global health Hypertension HIV treatment Family planning Health systems strengthening The organization plans to increase grantmaking in these areas by approximately 20% compared with 2025. Leveraging AI and Advanced Research Methods One of GiveWell s most innovative priorities for 2026 is integrating artificial intelligence into its research workflow. Applications include: Literature reviews Evidence synthesis Research support Operational efficiency improvements The organization is also systematically evaluating AI performance to determine how future advances may improve philanthropic decision-making. Strengthening Research Quality and Operations As GiveWell scales its grantmaking, maintaining research quality remains essential. Supporting teams will focus on: Hiring and training researchers Evaluating past grants Monitoring and evaluation Knowledge management Process optimization Partner coordination These efforts are designed to ensure that larger funding volumes continue to produce meaningful impact. Conclusion GiveWell s 2026 strategy represents one of the most ambitious evidence-based philanthropy efforts currently underway. By combining rigorous research, innovative grantmaking approaches, emerging technologies, and a commitment to learning, the organization aims to direct at least $500 million toward interventions that can save lives and improve well-being on a massive scale. From malaria prevention and nutrition programs to safe drinking water, vaccination outreach, poverty reduction, and emerging health innovations, GiveWell s expanding research agenda demonstrates how data-driven philanthropy can identify opportunities capable of generating extraordinary social returns. As global funding uncertainties continue to challenge health and development programs worldwide, GiveWell s commitment to finding and supporting the most cost-effective interventions may play a critical role in improving millions of lives in 2026 and beyond. title: Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program 2027 at Stanford University: Fully Funded Graduate Scholarship for Global Leaders Across All Disciplines
summary: Applications are now open for the Knight-Hennessy Scholars (KHS) Program 2027 at Stanford University in the United States. Recognized as one of the world’s most prestigious fully funded graduate scholarship and leadership development programmes, Knight-Hennessy Scholars supports outstanding students from around the world who are preparing to pursue graduate studies at Stanford University while developing as ethical, visionary, and globally minded leaders. The Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program is designed to build a multidisciplinary, multicultural community of future leaders committed to solving the world’s most complex challenges. Every year, up to 100 scholars are selected from across the globe to receive funding for graduate studies at Stanford University while participating in leadership development programmes, mentorship opportunities, experiential learning, and global networking activities. Unlike many traditional scholarships that focus primarily on academic performance, Knight-Hennessy Scholars evaluates applicants holistically. The programme seeks individuals who demonstrate independence of thought, purposeful leadership, and a civic mindset. The application process is therefore designed not only to assess academic excellence, but also to understand who applicants are, how they think, how they lead, and how they aspire to create positive impact in the world. The 2027 application cycle introduces detailed guidance for applicants regarding application preparation, leadership reflection, essays, recommendation letters, AI usage, interviews, and the invitation-only Finalist Experience. About the Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program Knight-Hennessy Scholars is Stanford University’s flagship graduate scholarship programme. The initiative brings together graduate students from all seven Stanford schools into a collaborative and interdisciplinary leadership community. The programme was founded to prepare a new generation of global leaders capable of addressing pressing challenges in: Public policy Science and technology Medicine and healthcare Business and entrepreneurship Education Law and governance Climate action Social innovation International development Artificial intelligence Sustainability Human rights Economic development Knight-Hennessy Scholars emphasizes leadership, service, innovation, ethical decision-making, and collaboration across cultures and disciplines. The programme provides: Full funding for graduate study Leadership training Professional development Global networking opportunities Community engagement Multidisciplinary collaboration Experiential learning Access to Stanford’s world-class ecosystem Why the Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program Stands Out The Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program is unique because it combines: Fully funded graduate education Leadership development Multidisciplinary learning Global community building Civic engagement Personal growth and reflection The programme recognizes that solving modern global problems requires leaders who can: Think critically Collaborate across disciplines Understand diverse perspectives Lead ethically Adapt to ambiguity Inspire positive change Every scholar joins a diverse cohort representing different: Countries Cultures Academic fields Professional backgrounds Lived experiences Leadership journeys The programme explicitly states that there is no “typical” Knight-Hennessy Scholar. Learn More Fully Funded Scholarship Benefits Knight-Hennessy Scholars receive extensive financial support to pursue graduate studies at Stanford University. The scholarship generally covers: Full tuition Living stipend Academic expenses Travel costs Leadership programme participation Professional development opportunities The programme also supports scholars through: Leadership training workshops Mentorship programmes Global networking Community-building events Cultural activities Interdisciplinary collaboration opportunities In addition, finalists invited to the Finalist Experience receive covered travel expenses, including: Airfare Accommodation at Stanford Meals during the programme Local programme expenses Learn More Graduate Programmes Covered Knight-Hennessy Scholars supports students pursuing eligible full-time graduate degrees at Stanford University, including: MA MBA MS MFA MPP JD MD DMA PhD Other eligible graduate programmes Applicants must separately apply to both: Knight-Hennessy Scholars An eligible Stanford graduate degree programme The admissions processes are separate but concurrent. Knight-Hennessy Scholars Selection Criteria The programme evaluates applicants based on three core criteria. 1. Independence of Thought Knight-Hennessy Scholars seeks visionary thinkers who are: Curious Analytical Open-minded Reflective Creative Eager to learn from diverse perspectives Strong applicants demonstrate: Intellectual curiosity Clear thinking Problem-solving ability Comfort with ambiguity Innovative thinking Desire for continuous learning The programme values applicants who challenge assumptions and generate meaningful ideas to solve real-world problems. 2. Civic Mindset Knight-Hennessy Scholars values individuals who are: Collaborative Empathetic Humble Trustworthy Community-oriented Strong applicants often demonstrate: Service to others Commitment to social good Respect for diverse viewpoints Integrity Accountability Desire to improve society The programme strongly emphasizes community engagement and service-oriented leadership. Requirement 1: Admission to Stanford Applicants must: Apply to and gain admission into a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme Enroll in the Stanford programme concurrently with Knight-Hennessy Scholars Eligible applicants include: New graduate applicants Applicants with deferred Stanford admission First-year Stanford PhD students Stanford students applying for a new eligible graduate degree Requirement 2: Undergraduate Degree Timeline Applicants must have earned their bachelor’s degree: In January 2020 or later for the 2027 cohort Military applicants receive an extended eligibility window to January 2018. Learn More No Restrictions Based on Background The programme has: No age restrictions No nationality restrictions No quotas by country No quotas by discipline No quotas by academic field Applicants from all regions and academic disciplines are encouraged to apply. Online Application Form Applicants must complete an online form that includes: Personal information Academic history Activities and achievements Employment background Awards and honors Leadership experiences The programme encourages applicants to provide detailed context rather than simplifying their experiences. 2. One-Page Resume Applicants must submit a one-page resume highlighting: Academic achievements Leadership experiences Professional activities Extracurricular involvement Key accomplishments The programme requests: Reverse chronological order No photographs No hyperlinks Legible formatting One US Letter-sized page only 3. Transcripts and Test Scores Applicants must upload: Undergraduate transcripts Graduate transcripts (if applicable) Degree conferral information If required by the Stanford graduate programme, applicants must also submit: GRE GMAT LSAT MCAT TOEFL IELTS PTE (MBA only) There is no minimum GPA or standardized test score requirement for Knight-Hennessy Scholars itself. 4. Strong recommenders should: Know the applicant closely Provide specific examples Address the three selection criteria Demonstrate the applicant’s leadership and character The programme emphasizes that the content of the letter matters more than the recommender’s status or title. 5. Short Answers and Essay Applicants must complete several written responses. Short Answer Questions Applicants answer questions related to: Academic and professional goals Courage and resilience Working with diverse perspectives Moments of failure “Improbable facts” about themselves The programme explains that improbable facts should reveal surprising or unexpected aspects of the applicant’s identity rather than simply listing achievements. title: Chatham House Molchanov Sustainability Internship 2026–2027 in London, UK: Paid Six-Month Opportunity for Future Leaders in International Affairs and Sustainability
summary: Applications are now open for the highly competitive Molchanov Sustainability Internship 2026–2027 at Chatham House, one of the world s most respected policy institutes. This six-month paid internship offers aspiring professionals the opportunity to gain practical experience, build professional networks, and deepen their understanding of international affairs, sustainability, public policy, and global challenges. Hosted by Chatham House, also known as the Royal Institute of International Affairs, this internship provides participants with direct exposure to the operations of a globally recognized think tank dedicated to building a sustainably secure, prosperous, and just world. The programme is specifically designed to help early-career professionals gain hands-on experience while developing the skills, confidence, and networks required for successful careers in policy, research, international development, sustainability, and related fields. About Chatham House Chatham House is an independent policy institute based in London with a global reputation for excellence in research, analysis, and policy engagement. For over a century, the organization has brought together policymakers, researchers, academics, business leaders, diplomats, and civil society representatives to discuss and address the world s most pressing issues. Its work focuses on: International affairs Global governance Climate and sustainability Security and defense Economic development Democracy and governance International cooperation Regional and geopolitical issues The institution is widely known for the Chatham House Rule, a principle designed to encourage open and honest discussion during policy dialogues and international forums. About the Molchanov Sustainability Internship The Molchanov Sustainability Internship is designed to provide practical exposure to policy research, programme development, events management, communications, stakeholder engagement, and organizational operations within a leading international affairs institution. Interns become part of a supportive learning environment where they work closely with experienced professionals, researchers, and policy experts while contributing to ongoing projects and initiatives. The programme emphasizes professional development, mentorship, networking, and experiential learning. Internship Teams Available Successful candidates will be placed within one of the following teams: Africa Programme This team focuses on political, economic, governance, and development issues across the African continent. Environment and Society Centre Interns support research and policy discussions relating to sustainability, climate change, environmental governance, and social transformation. Europe Programme / Russia and Eurasia Programme This joint internship explores political, economic, and security developments across Europe, Russia, and Eurasia. Events Team Participants gain experience in planning, organizing, and delivering high-level policy events, conferences, workshops, and discussions. Middle East and North Africa Programme This programme examines developments affecting countries across the Middle East and North Africa region. UK in the World Programme / US and North America Programme Interns support research and engagement related to transatlantic relations, international policy, and global affairs. What Interns Will Gain The internship provides a rich learning experience through direct participation in Chatham House activities. Participants will: Work on Real Projects Interns will contribute directly to: Research initiatives Events development Programme administration Stakeholder engagement Policy analysis Communications activities Develop Research Skills Responsibilities may include: Conducting background research Preparing briefing materials Supporting policy analysis Drafting summaries and reports Reviewing publications Improve Communication Skills Interns gain experience in: Writing policy-related content Drafting newsletters Producing social media content Editing publications Preparing event communications Build Event Management Experience Participants may support: High-level conferences Policy roundtables Workshops Expert discussions Public events Expand Professional Networks Interns will have opportunities to interact with: Global policymakers Researchers Diplomats International affairs experts Industry leaders Sustainability practitioners Mentorship and Professional Development Every intern receives dedicated mentorship and guidance throughout the programme. Mentors support interns by: Providing career guidance Recommending learning opportunities Offering professional feedback Assisting with skills development Supporting personal growth goals Interns also participate in a cohort-based experience, allowing them to learn and grow alongside fellow participants. Benefits of the Internship Selected participants will receive access to numerous benefits, including: Professional Development Tailored learning and development programme Exposure to international policy work Practical project experience Mentorship from experts Networking Opportunities Meetings with policymakers Interactions with international researchers Networking events Connections with sustainability professionals Access to Resources Chatham House Library Online e-Library Research publications Expert events and discussions Membership Benefits Participants may receive complimentary Chatham House membership following a successful performance evaluation. Who Should Apply? The programme is ideal for individuals who: Are passionate about international affairs Have an interest in sustainability and public policy Want to work in research or think tanks Aspire to careers in diplomacy, development, government, or academia Enjoy learning and problem-solving Are proactive and motivated Have strong communication skills Person Specification Applicants should demonstrate: Interest in the work of Chatham House Excellent written communication skills Strong verbal communication abilities Curiosity and willingness to learn Ability to manage multiple tasks Teamwork and collaboration skills Professionalism and initiative Motivation for continuous personal development Internship Location The internship is based at Chatham House headquarters in: St James s Square, London, United Kingdom The organization operates a hybrid work model, with interns generally expected to work from the office approximately two days per week. International remote working is not supported. Internship Duration The internship is a: Six-month fixed-term contract Full-time position 35 hours per week Start Date: 8 September 2026 (or shortly thereafter) Salary Interns receive compensation at the London Living Wage. Current Rate: £13.85 per hour Eligibility Requirements To be eligible, applicants must: Be aged 18 years or older Be residing in the United Kingdom throughout the internship Hold a valid right to work in the UK Be available to start in September 2026 Be able to commit to the full six-month programme Important Application Guidance Chatham House specifically advises applicants not to use artificial intelligence tools to generate application responses. Applications are screened anonymously, and candidates are encouraged to avoid including identifying personal information in written responses. Application Deadline Deadline: 10 June 2026 at 23:59 BST Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, meaning early submission is strongly encouraged. Apply Here Why You Should Apply For individuals seeking a career in international affairs, sustainability, policy research, diplomacy, development, or global governance, the Molchanov Sustainability Internship offers a rare opportunity to gain practical experience at one of the world s leading think tanks. title: MASS African Design Centre Fellowship 2026–2027 in Rwanda: Fully Paid Opportunity for African Architects and Designers to Shape the Future of Africa’s Built Environment
summary: The African Design Centre (ADC) at MASS has officially opened applications for its 2026–2027 Fellowship Cohort, offering one of Africa’s most prestigious opportunities for emerging architects, designers, and built-environment professionals. The African Design Centre Fellowship is a 12-month paid residency program based in Kigali, Rwanda, designed to equip Africa’s next generation of design leaders with the skills, mentorship, resources, and practical experience needed to tackle some of the continent’s most pressing development challenges. The fellowship is specifically designed for young African professionals who are passionate about using architecture, urban planning, landscape design, engineering, and related disciplines to create lasting social, environmental, and economic impact across Africa. About the African Design Centre (ADC) The African Design Centre is an initiative of MASS that transforms insights from real-world projects into sustainable movements for change. The centre serves as a hub for innovation, research, and leadership development, with a strong commitment to preserving Africa’s cultural heritage while advancing contemporary design solutions. ADC believes that Africa’s architectural future should be shaped by: Indigenous knowledge systems Local narratives and histories Traditional craftsmanship Community-centered design approaches Environmentally responsible development Through its programs, ADC supports professionals who are committed to creating design solutions that are both innovative and deeply rooted in African contexts. Core Areas of Work at the African Design Centre The ADC operates through three major workstreams: 1. Research The centre investigates how poor design and inadequate infrastructure contribute to: Unequal development Limited healthcare access Climate vulnerability Educational barriers Economic inequality Through research, ADC seeks practical design interventions capable of generating transformational change. 2. Catalyst Projects ADC pilots innovative projects that demonstrate how thoughtful design can address critical challenges. Examples include: Maternal health facilities Innovation hubs Conservation infrastructure Educational campuses Community-centered public spaces These projects serve as scalable models for development across Africa. 3. Systems Change Through leadership development initiatives such as the ADC Fellowship, the centre is building a new generation of African design professionals capable of leading the continent’s urban transformation. About the ADC Fellowship The African Design Centre Fellowship is a year-long immersive residency hosted in Kigali, Rwanda. The program provides selected fellows with direct exposure to real-world projects, expert mentorship, collaborative learning opportunities, and practical design challenges. The fellowship seeks to empower participants to create culturally grounded and community-driven solutions that address Africa’s infrastructure needs while preserving its architectural heritage. These include work in areas such as: Maternal and newborn healthcare Economic development and social opportunity Climate-positive infrastructure Community-led innovation Design research Sustainable urban development Fellows are encouraged to contribute their own ideas, experiences, perspectives, and questions while collaborating with experts across multiple disciplines. Fellowship Responsibilities Conduct Design Research Fellows will: Explore indigenous knowledge systems Study vernacular architecture Investigate urban development patterns Analyze culturally rooted design practices Participate in Pilot Projects Participants will: Work on community-centered design initiatives Collaborate with stakeholders Contribute to real-world infrastructure solutions Support project development and implementation Disseminate Knowledge Fellows will be expected to: Publish reflective articles Share lessons learned Document research findings Contribute to broader discussions on African architecture and design Mentorship and Professional Support Selected fellows will receive guidance from: MASS program staff Professional design mentors Industry experts Leadership coaches The fellowship is structured to provide continuous support throughout the residency period. Fellowship Benefits Participants will receive numerous professional and personal benefits, including: A paid fellowship opportunity Full immersion in a leading African design institution Access to expert mentorship Hands-on project experience Professional development opportunities Exposure to cutting-edge design and research practices Opportunities to collaborate with leading practitioners Expanded regional and international professional networks Leadership development training Practical experience addressing Africa’s development challenges Eligibility Criteria To be eligible, applicants must: Be nationals of an African country Be 35 years old or younger Hold a degree in architecture, urban design, landscape architecture, engineering, or a related field Be able to relocate to Kigali, Rwanda, for the full duration of the fellowship Demonstrate a commitment to social justice and environmental responsibility Show interest in community-driven and culturally grounded design solutions Application Process The fellowship uses a three-stage selection process. Fellowship Timeline Residency Period October 2026 – September 2027 Selected fellows will live and work in Kigali, Rwanda throughout the fellowship. Why This Fellowship Matters Africa is experiencing one of the fastest rates of urbanization in the world. The continent’s future depends on visionary architects, planners, designers, and engineers who can create sustainable, culturally relevant, and community-centered solutions. The African Design Centre Fellowship is more than a professional development program—it is an investment in the next generation of leaders who will shape Africa’s cities, infrastructure, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, and public spaces for decades to come. For young African professionals passionate about design, innovation, social impact, and sustainable development, this fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity to learn, lead, and contribute to transformational change across the continent. title: Youth Side Program 2026 in Berlin, Germany: Fully Funded Global Health Advocacy Opportunity for Young Leaders at the World Health Summit
