title: Natural Catalysts 2026: Leadership Programme Advancing Racial Equity in the Environmental Sector Opens Applications
summary: The environmental sector continues to face significant challenges around racial representation and equitable leadership pathways. Despite increasing awareness about diversity and inclusion, leadership roles within environmental organisations still do not reflect the diversity of wider society. To help address this systemic challenge, Common Purpose and Makani Cambridge have launched Natural Catalysts, a transformative 12-month leadership programme designed to reshape how leadership is understood, accessed, practised, and sustained across the environmental sector. Applications are now open for the Natural Catalysts Programme 2026, an initiative specifically created to support Global Majority Leaders and Senior Leaders working together to create lasting systemic change. The programme aims to build more equitable, inclusive, and sustainable leadership pathways across environmental organisations in the UK. What Is the Natural Catalysts Programme? Natural Catalysts is a leadership development initiative focused on: Racial equity Leadership transformation Organisational change Systems thinking Inclusive environmental leadership The programme is delivered through a partnership between: Common Purpose Makani Cambridge It is supported by: Esmée Fairbairn Foundation Unlike many leadership initiatives that focus solely on individual career progression, Natural Catalysts adopts an ecosystem approach. This means the programme seeks to influence: Individuals Organisations Leadership structures Sector-wide systems Organisational culture Access to power and decision-making The programme was developed following a year-long research and co-design process involving: Global Majority Leaders Senior Leaders Environmental organisations Equity practitioners Community stakeholders Why the Natural Catalysts Programme Matters The environmental sector has historically struggled with racial representation in leadership positions. According to the programme organisers, the issue is not simply about talent shortages or recruitment pipelines. Instead, it is deeply connected to: How leadership is defined How opportunities are distributed Organisational power structures Informal access to networks Visibility and sponsorship Systemic inequities Natural Catalysts seeks to challenge and transform these structures. The programme recognises that meaningful and lasting change requires: Organisational commitment Shared accountability Cross-level collaboration Honest conversations about race and power Structural change beyond symbolic representation Programme Vision and Goals Natural Catalysts is designed to: Increase equitable leadership opportunities Support Global Majority Leaders Encourage institutional accountability Shift leadership culture in the environmental sector Build long-term systemic change The programme aims to move organisations: From representation to access and influence From mentoring to sponsorship and visibility From individual progression to collective transformation Who Can Apply? Natural Catalysts is open to organisations operating within the environmental sector. Organisations are invited to nominate a “duo” of participants who will complete the programme together. Required Participant Structure 1. Global Majority Leader The nominated Global Majority Leader must: Be in a paid role Have lived experience of racialisation in the UK Identify within communities racialised as Black, Asian, Brown, or Arab in the UK context Be operating at mid-management level or above Be navigating leadership pathways within the environmental sector 2. Senior Leader The Senior Leader must: Be in a paid senior role Hold significant decision-making power Influence organisational direction Be part of senior management or executive leadership Examples may include: CEOs Directors Senior Management Team members Executive leaders The organisers emphasise that leadership titles may vary across organisations. What matters most is: Influence Strategic authority Organisational decision-making power Important Participation Rule A Global Majority Leader cannot participate without senior leadership involvement. However: A Senior Leader may participate independently if their organisation does not currently employ a Global Majority Leader. This structure is intentional because the programme seeks to create organisational change rather than focusing only on individual leadership development. Additional Participation Opportunity for HR and DEI Professionals Organisations may also nominate professionals from: Human Resources (HR) Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Learning and Development (L D) These participants will join a dedicated: Community of Practice This additional track helps organisations embed learning into policies, systems, and workplace culture. What Participants Will Learn The programme explores critical themes around: Leadership Race Power Equity Organisational systems Community-centred change Participants will: Deepen understanding of power structures Explore leadership beyond hierarchy Learn across lived experiences and roles Build supportive professional communities Strengthen organisational influence Reflect on accountability and responsibility Develop sustainable leadership practices Programme Structure Natural Catalysts is a 12-month programme involving: 40 participants total 20 Global Majority Leaders 20 Senior Leaders The programme combines: In-person residential learning Online sessions Peer communities Collaborative reflection Leadership development Systems-change approaches Programme Components 1. Online Onboarding Session The programme begins with a: Two-hour online onboarding session Participants will: Build initial connections Understand programme expectations Explore themes of leadership and systemic change 2. Global Majority Leaders Track This specialised leadership track includes: In-Person Residential Three-day residential gathering Community-building activities Leadership reflection Collective learning experiences Community of Practice Ten one-hour sessions Peer support and collaborative learning Shared reflection and sense-making 3. Senior Leaders Track Senior leaders will engage in: Organisational leadership reflection Power and accountability discussions Influence and systems-change learning Cross-sector collaboration 4. Joint Learning Track Participants from different leadership levels will learn together through: Shared discussions Collaborative exercises Organisational change exploration Leadership practice reflection 5. HR, DEI, and Leadership Professionals Track This specialised track supports organisational professionals responsible for: Workplace culture Equity systems Inclusion practices Leadership development frameworks 6. Final In-Person Gathering The programme concludes with a: 24-hour residential gathering Participants will: Reflect on learning outcomes Share organisational insights Discuss change implementation Celebrate programme completion Time Commitment The programme requires meaningful participation and organisational engagement. Global Majority Leaders 4 in-person days 18 hours online Senior Leaders 20 hours online 1 in-person day Shadowing and visibility commitments HR/DEI Participants 4 hours online The organisers emphasise that this programme is intended to influence participants’ work directly rather than exist alongside it as a separate activity. Benefits of Participating Natural Catalysts offers extensive personal, professional, and organisational benefits. Leadership Development Participants strengthen: Strategic leadership skills Systems thinking Cross-boundary leadership Organisational influence Networking and Community Participants gain: Access to supportive peer networks Cross-sector relationships Collaborative learning communities Organisational Impact Organisations benefit from: More inclusive leadership practices Stronger equity frameworks Improved representation pathways Enhanced organisational reflection Exposure and Visibility Participants gain: Increased visibility Sponsorship opportunities Access to influential spaces and networks Sector-Wide Transformation The programme contributes to: More equitable environmental leadership Sustainable systems change Greater racial representation in leadership roles Cost and Financial Support Programme Fee £500 for organisations able to pay Bursaries Bursaries are available. The organisers state clearly that: Financial limitations should not prevent organisations from applying. Information Webinar An information webinar will be held for interested applicants. Webinar Details Date: 23 June 2026 Time: 12:00–13:00 BST Platform: Zoom The webinar will provide: Programme insights Application guidance Opportunity for questions and discussion About the Organising Partners Common Purpose Common Purpose is an international leadership development organisation founded in 1989. The organisation: Operates in over 100 cities worldwide Has over 130,000 alumni globally Focuses on cross-boundary leadership development Supports collaborative problem-solving across sectors Makani Cambridge Makani Cambridge CIC is a community-rooted organisation focused on: Racial equity Leadership Collective care Community-led systems change Since 2024, Makani has: Delivered more than 70 programmes and events Reached over 1,000 participants across the UK Their work centres: Lived experience Community-rooted learning Equity-focused systems change Deadline for Applications Midnight UK Time, Sunday 12 July 2026 How to Apply Interested organisations can learn more and apply through the official Common Purpose platform. Apply Here Final Thoughts The Natural Catalysts Programme represents a significant effort to address long-standing inequities in environmental leadership by moving beyond surface-level diversity initiatives toward meaningful structural change. Through collaboration between Global Majority Leaders, Senior Leaders, and organisational professionals, the programme seeks to transform how leadership is practised and sustained across the environmental sector. For organisations committed to racial equity, inclusive leadership, and systems transformation, Natural Catalysts offers a rare opportunity to engage deeply with the realities of power, representation, and organisational change while building lasting networks and practical leadership capacity. title: CQUniversity Australia RTP Stipend Scholarship 2026: Fully Funded Research Scholarship Worth $38,000 Per Year for Domestic and International Students
summary: CQUniversity Australia has officially opened applications for the highly competitive Research Training Program (RTP) Stipend Scholarship 2026, a prestigious fully funded research scholarship supported by the Australian Government. The RTP Stipend Scholarship is designed to support outstanding domestic and international students pursuing a Research Higher Degree (RHD) at CQUniversity Australia. The scholarship provides substantial financial assistance to help students cover their living expenses while conducting advanced research studies in Australia. With a scholarship value of AUD $38,000 per annum for up to three years, this opportunity offers talented researchers the chance to focus fully on their academic and research goals within one of Australia’s leading regional universities. The scholarship remains open throughout the year, and applicants are encouraged to begin discussions early with potential supervisors and research teams. About the CQUniversity RTP Stipend Scholarship The Research Training Program (RTP) Stipend Scholarship is funded by the Australian Government and administered through CQUniversity Australia. The scholarship supports students undertaking higher degree research programs by providing a living allowance stipend paid fortnightly through the university payroll system. In addition to the living stipend, domestic students who receive the RTP Stipend Scholarship will also automatically receive an RTP Fees Offset Scholarship, which fully covers tuition fees during the scholarship period. This scholarship is part of Australia’s broader initiative to strengthen research excellence, innovation, and academic development across universities. Benefits Include: Annual stipend of AUD $38,000 Financial support for living expenses Opportunity to study and conduct research in Australia Access to world-class research facilities and supervision Automatic RTP Fees Offset Scholarship for domestic students Tuition fee coverage for eligible domestic students Long-term research and academic career development opportunities Exposure to international research networks and collaborations Fortnightly scholarship payments through the university payroll system Opportunity to contribute to high-impact research projects Eligibility Criteria To qualify for the RTP Stipend Scholarship, applicants must satisfy the eligibility requirements outlined in the Commonwealth Scholarship Guidelines (Research) 2017. Eligible Candidates Applicants must be: Domestic students, or International students enrolled in an accredited Research Higher Degree course at CQUniversity Income Restrictions To remain eligible for the RTP Stipend: Applicants must not receive another source of income supporting general living costs if the income exceeds 75% of the RTP Stipend rate. Income unrelated to the research program is not considered in eligibility assessments. Tuition Scholarship Restriction Applicants are not eligible for an RTP Fees Offset Scholarship if they already receive another equivalent Commonwealth scholarship intended to offset research tuition fees. Selection Criteria The RTP Stipend Scholarship is highly competitive and awarded based on academic merit and research potential. CQUniversity uses a Scholarship Assessment Scale consisting of three major performance categories. Assessment Categories 1. Academic Achievement and Writing Skills (0–20 points) Applicants will be evaluated based on: Academic excellence Research writing quality Publications and academic outputs Overall academic achievements 2. Quality of Research Project and Alignment with University Priorities (0–15 points) Assessment focuses on: Research proposal quality Innovation and originality Alignment with CQUniversity research priority areas Potential research impact 3. Motivation, Research Experience, and Research Environment (0–15 points) Applicants must demonstrate: Strong research motivation Previous research experience Capacity to succeed in research training Supportive supervisory and research environment How to Apply Unlike many scholarship programs, there is no direct application process for the RTP Scholarship. Application Process Step 1: Discuss with a Supervisory Team Interested applicants must first discuss their research interests and scholarship intentions with a potential supervisory team at CQUniversity. Step 2: Recommendation by Supervisors Based on the recommendation of the supervisory team, prospective applicants may then be invited by the School of Graduate Research to submit a formal application. Step 3: Submit Supporting Documents Applicants invited to apply must provide all required supporting documentation. Required Supporting Documents Applications must include: Written submission Supporting academic documents Any additional documentation requested by CQUniversity Incomplete applications will not be considered. Scholarship Assessment Rounds Although applications remain open throughout the year, CQUniversity may conduct multiple scholarship assessment rounds annually depending on scholarship availability. Typical Assessment Round Deadlines Assessment rounds are generally scheduled around: End of April End of September However, the timing and number of rounds may vary from year to year. Following each assessment round: Applications are reviewed Successful applicants are selected Candidates are notified via email Important Dates Scholarship Opening Date 31 December 2025 Scholarship Closing Date 31 December 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin contacting potential supervisors early to improve their chances of consideration. Why You Should Apply The CQUniversity RTP Stipend Scholarship is an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers seeking fully funded postgraduate education in Australia. The scholarship not only removes financial barriers but also provides access to: Advanced research training Expert supervision International academic exposure Career development opportunities Global research collaborations Whether your goal is an academic career, research leadership, innovation, or industry impact, the RTP Scholarship can provide the resources and support necessary to achieve your ambitions. Official Scholarship Link For complete scholarship details and official information, visit the CQUniversity Australia scholarship page. There are no direct applications for RTP Scholarships. Please discuss your interest in an RHD Scholarship with your supervisory team. Prospective applicants will be invited by the School of Graduate Research to complete an application, based on the recommendation of the supervisory team. Depending on the availability of RTP stipend scholarships, CQUniversity may conduct more than one assessment round within the calendar year. These rounds are typically scheduled to close at the end of April and September; however, the timing and number of rounds cannot be guaranteed and may vary from year to year. Applications remain open throughout the year. Following the close of each assessment round, applications will be reviewed and applicants will be notified of the outcome via email. Applicants will be notified by email when the scholarships have been awarded. title: The World Around Young Climate Prize 2026: Global Mentorship, Fellowship & New York Summit Opportunity for Young Climate Leaders Under 25
summary: Applications are now officially open for the third cycle of The World Around’s Young Climate Prize 2026, a prestigious global mentorship, accelerator, and fellowship programme designed to support exceptional young climate innovators, activists, designers, and changemakers working on the front lines of the climate crisis. The programme identifies and accelerates self-initiated climate action projects led by young people aged 25 and under from anywhere in the world. Through mentorship, masterclasses, international networking, strategic support, and global exposure, the Young Climate Prize empowers the next generation of climate leaders to strengthen and scale their impact. The application deadline for the 2026 Young Climate Prize Cycle 03 is June 30, 2026 , at 11:59 PM EDT . The programme is free to enter and participation is completely free for selected applicants. About The World Around Young Climate Prize The Young Climate Prize is a global mentorship and award programme created by The World Around, an international nonprofit organization focused on design, architecture, climate action, and social innovation. The initiative aims to identify, support, and amplify young people already creating meaningful climate solutions within their communities. Every two years, 25 outstanding young changemakers under the age of 25 are selected through an international open call. These participants represent diverse regions, communities, and climate realities from around the globe. The programme combines: One-on-one mentorship Climate leadership development Design Academy masterclasses International networking Professional development Global visibility Fellowship opportunities Public presentation opportunities The programme culminates at The World Around Summit in New York City, where selected winners present their work to an international audience of designers, policymakers, educators, climate experts, and global leaders. What Makes the Young Climate Prize Unique? Unlike many climate competitions focused only on ideas or proposals, the Young Climate Prize specifically supports young people who are already leading live projects with measurable climate impact in their communities. The programme is particularly unique because it: Prioritizes real-world climate action Focuses on mentorship and long-term support Supports interdisciplinary climate solutions Uses design as a tool for climate innovation Builds a global youth climate network Continues support through a three-year fellowship programme The initiative recognizes that young people are not just future leaders—they are already leading climate action today. Who Can Apply? The Young Climate Prize is open globally to young people actively working on climate solutions. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be between 13 and 25 years old at the time of application Be the founder or co-founder of a live climate-related project Be actively leading the project at the time of application Demonstrate measurable or visible community impact Submit a climate-focused initiative addressing climate change mitigation or adaptation Team Applications Groups of up to three people may apply together. However: Every team member must meet all eligibility requirements Each participant must fall within the age range All members must actively contribute to the project Global Eligibility Applicants may come from: Any country Any continent Any community or region worldwide The programme welcomes participants from: Urban communities Indigenous communities Coastal regions Rural communities Climate-vulnerable areas Marginalized populations What Types of Projects Are Eligible? The programme accepts a wide variety of climate-related projects and creative practices. Eligible projects may include: Climate advocacy campaigns Environmental education initiatives Sustainable architecture projects Circular economy solutions Waste reduction systems Urban resilience initiatives Indigenous climate knowledge preservation Renewable energy innovations Community adaptation projects Climate storytelling Conservation efforts Food systems innovation Biodiversity protection Sustainable fashion projects Climate communication platforms Ecological design projects The programme places special emphasis on design as a driver of climate solutions. Programme Structure 1. One-on-One Mentorship Each selected participant is paired with an internationally recognized mentor whose expertise, network, and experience align with the participant’s work. Mentorship sessions help participants: Strengthen project strategy Improve communication Expand project visibility Access global networks Scale impact Refine storytelling Build professional confidence Young Climate Prize Design Academy Selected participants also join the Young Climate Prize Design Academy, a weekly learning and development programme featuring: Workshops Masterclasses Talks Strategy sessions Professional development training The academy focuses on: Climate leadership Communication Design thinking Public engagement Advocacy Storytelling Project scaling Systems thinking Global Experts Mentors The Design Academy masterclasses are led by members of The World Around’s global network of designers, educators, architects, curators, and climate thinkers. Notable mentors and contributors include: Paola Antonelli Bruce Mau Mariam Issoufou Douglas Cardinal Alice Rawsthorn Al Borde Carson Chan Dominique Petit-Frère Kotchakorn Voraakhom These globally respected experts provide insights across: Architecture Design Sustainability Climate communication Urbanism Ecology Landscape design Community development Final Awards International Recognition At the conclusion of the programme, an international jury selects: Young Climate Designer Remove featured image Young Climate Visionary Young Climate Voice The selected winners receive the opportunity to: Travel to New York City Present their work at The World Around Summit 2027 Gain international exposure Connect with global climate leaders Showcase their projects to influential audiences Three-Year Fellowship Opportunity One of the strongest aspects of the programme is that all cohort participants automatically transition into the Young Climate Prize Fellowship after completing the programme cycle. The fellowship provides: Three years of ongoing support Continued mentorship Access to resources Networking opportunities Professional growth support Project development opportunities Global collaborations This long-term structure distinguishes the programme from one-time competitions or awards. What Participants Gain Selected participants receive several benefits throughout the programme. Benefits Include: Personalized mentorship Access to world-renowned climate and design leaders Weekly Design Academy masterclasses Global networking opportunities Climate leadership development Storytelling and communication training Strategic guidance for project growth Exposure to international audiences Fellowship opportunities Potential travel to New York City Opportunity to present at The World Around Summit Connection to a global climate innovation community Submission Requirements Applicants must submit: A short introductory video about their project Written or visual materials showing evidence of impact Supporting documentation demonstrating project work Submissions may be completed in: English Spanish Application Deadline June 30, 2026 , at 11:59 PM EDT Applicants are encouraged to apply early to avoid technical issues and to ensure enough time to prepare strong submissions. How to Apply Applicants can apply through the official Young Climate Prize application platform. Apply to Young Climate Prize Cycle 03 here . The World Around also welcomes nominations here . Why Young Climate Leaders Should Apply Climate change is one of the defining global challenges of our time, and young people are already creating transformative solutions within their communities. The Young Climate Prize offers: Recognition Mentorship International exposure Long-term fellowship support Leadership development Professional growth Community building For young changemakers already taking action, this programme provides the tools, guidance, and network needed to expand their impact globally. Learn more about the Young Climate Prize 2026 HERE . Conclusion The World Around Young Climate Prize 2026 is more than just a competition—it is a long-term global accelerator and fellowship programme designed to empower young people shaping the future of climate action. By combining mentorship, education, storytelling, design, leadership, and global collaboration, the programme creates a powerful platform for youth-led climate innovation worldwide. Young climate leaders, designers, activists, and community innovators under 25 who are already creating meaningful environmental impact should strongly consider applying before the June 30, 2026 deadline. title: Darwin Initiative Round 32 Grants 2026 — Up to £5 Million Funding for Global Biodiversity, Climate & Poverty Reduction Projects
summary: The Darwin Initiative Round 32 funding call is now officially open, offering grant opportunities of up to £5 million to support innovative projects that protect and restore biodiversity while also addressing poverty reduction and sustainable economic development. Funded by the UK Government through the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) , the Darwin Initiative is one of the world’s longest-running and most impactful biodiversity funding programmes. Since its launch in 1993, it has invested over £289 million across 1,370+ projects in more than 150 countries . This funding round is designed to support high-impact conservation projects that not only protect ecosystems but also strengthen livelihoods, governance systems, and long-term sustainability in biodiversity-rich regions. About the Darwin Initiative The Darwin Initiative is part of the Biodiversity Challenge Funds , supporting countries and communities to develop practical, scalable solutions to biodiversity loss. It focuses on: Conservation and restoration of nature Poverty reduction through sustainable resource use Strengthening local and national environmental governance Supporting climate resilience and ecosystem-based adaptation Promoting sustainable economic growth through biodiversity protection Rather than short-term interventions, the programme prioritizes systemic, long-term impact across landscapes and communities. Funding Available (Round 32) Applicants can access funding depending on the scheme: Funding Levels: Up to £5 million per project Scheme Types: Darwin Initiative Extra Darwin Initiative Main Darwin Initiative Capability Capacity Each scheme has different eligibility rules, timelines, and application stages. Key Focus Areas for Round 32 This funding round introduces updated priorities to improve global impact and efficiency. 1. Biodiversity Hotspot Targeting Applications must focus on 13 priority biodiversity hotspots across 35 countries , ensuring: Higher impact concentration Stronger ecosystem protection outcomes Reduced fragmentation of funding efforts Better coordination among projects 2. Systems-Level Change Approach Projects are encouraged to move beyond direct interventions and instead strengthen: Environmental governance systems Institutional frameworks Market systems linked to conservation Long-term sustainability mechanisms This shift ensures that outcomes remain impactful even after project completion. 3. Reduced Application Burden To improve accessibility: Stage 1 applications (Extra Main) are now shorter concept notes Only high-potential projects progress to Stage 2 4. Funding Structure Changes Innovation scheme removed (now covered by GCBC – Global Centre on Biodiversity for Climate) More funding redirected to remaining schemes Stronger emphasis on quality and strategic alignment 5. Lead Applicant Limitation To encourage fairness and local leadership: Organisations may lead only one application per scheme Partners can still join multiple applications Programme Impact and Achievements Since 1993, the Darwin Initiative has achieved: £289 million invested globally 1,370+ conservation projects funded Millions of hectares of ecosystems protected Over 100,000 people supported in climate resilience Major biodiversity protection across forests, wetlands, and marine ecosystems Example Impact: In Indonesia, Darwin-funded projects have helped: Manage 1.3 million hectares of forests and fisheries sustainably Contribute to a 12.6 million-hectare UNESCO Biosphere Reserve Improve regional biodiversity governance and planning Webinar: Round 32 Funding Updates A dedicated webinar will provide insights into the latest updates and application changes. Webinar Details: Date: 28 May 2026 Time: 6:00 pm (Vietnam Time) / 12:00–1:00 pm UK time (GMT+1) Format: Online briefing session What You Will Learn: Key updates for Round 32 Changes in application structure and priorities New geographic focus areas Guidance on eligibility and funding schemes Opportunity for Q A Application Deadlines (Round 32) Darwin Initiative Main Stage 1: 20 July 2026 Stage 2 (invite only): 30 November 2026 Darwin Initiative Extra Stage 1: 1 July 2026 Stage 2 (invite only): 2 November 2026 Capability Capacity Single Stage Deadline: 31 August 2026 How to Apply Click here for more and to apply Applicants are strongly advised to: Read full guidance documents carefully Select the correct scheme (Extra, Main, or Capability Capacity) Align proposals with biodiversity hotspot priorities Focus on systems-level impact and sustainability Ensure strong local partnerships and implementation capacity Click here for more global grant opportunities. title: Change Collective 2026 — Fully Funded Intergenerational Climate Leadership Programme in Nature (UK)
summary: The Change Collective 2026 is a powerful intergenerational learning and reflection programme designed for people working in climate and environmental change , offering space to rethink purpose, direction, and collective action in a time of global uncertainty. This initiative is co-hosted with Jonathon Porritt , a leading voice in sustainability and environmental strategy, and brings together experienced practitioners, activists, policymakers, and young changemakers. At a time when young people are facing an economic crisis, accelerating climate impacts, political instability, and rising global uncertainty, this programme creates a rare opportunity to pause, reflect, and reimagine action with clarity and resilience. Importantly, 2 fully funded bursary places are available for 18–25 year olds , making this an exceptional opportunity for emerging climate leaders. About the Change Collective Programme The Change Collective is a nature-based leadership and reflection programme designed for individuals already engaged in climate and environmental work across sectors including: Activism and campaigning Policy and governance Business and corporate sustainability Community organising Environmental advocacy and education It is built around one central question: “What now, and what is mine to do?” This question guides all learning, reflection, and peer exchange throughout the programme. Core Purpose of the Programme The Change Collective is designed to help participants: Gain clarity in a complex and rapidly changing world Strengthen emotional and professional resilience Build meaningful peer-to-peer networks Reconnect with purpose and direction Develop collective intelligence for climate action Step back from urgency and reconnect with strategic thinking Programme Structure Overview The programme combines a 3-day residential retreat in nature with a 3-month online community of practice . 1. Three-Day Residential Retreat (In-Person) 📍 Location: Sheepdrove Organic Farm, Berkshire, United Kingdom 📅 Dates: Wednesday 1 July – Friday 3 July 2026 What Happens During the Residential: Participants engage in immersive reflection and facilitated dialogue in a natural environment designed to support clarity and transformation. Key elements include: Deep reflective sessions on personal and collective roles Structured conversations on climate systems and change Guided nature immersion experiences Group dialogue and peer learning Emotional and strategic reflection on climate work Time away from institutional pressure and urgency The residential is structured around three core lenses: Me — Personal Reflection What in me needs to evolve for this moment? What habits or patterns no longer serve? What needs to end for new clarity to emerge? You — Relational Awareness How do I relate to others under pressure? Where is trust strong or weak? How do I navigate fear, fatigue, and tension? Us — Collective Systems What systems do I operate within? What are their limits and strengths? How can collective agency be strengthened? 2. Three-Month Community of Practice (Online) After the residential, participants continue in an extended learning journey through structured online engagement. Key Components: Three group online workshops: 24 July 2026 11 September 2026 25 September 2026 Fortnightly peer coaching sessions (4 total) Monthly action learning groups (3 sessions) Structured reflection and accountability spaces Peer collaboration and feedback loops Focus of the Online Phase: Translating reflection into real-world action Strengthening peer support systems Developing collaborative climate initiatives Exploring strategic dilemmas together Maintaining long-term accountability and clarity What Participants Gain By the end of the programme, participants will leave with: Clearer understanding of their role in climate and environmental systems Improved emotional resilience in the face of uncertainty Stronger decision-making and strategic clarity Tools for relational and collective leadership Renewed energy and motivation for climate work A trusted peer network of climate practitioners Greater confidence in navigating complexity and change Why This Programme Matters The Change Collective responds directly to the reality that: Climate impacts are accelerating globally Political systems are increasingly unstable Institutions are under pressure and often failing Many climate professionals feel burnout and uncertainty Collective action requires deeper collaboration and reflection By combining nature immersion, reflective dialogue, and structured peer learning , the programme creates space for deeper thinking and more grounded action. Venue: Sheepdrove Organic Farm The residential takes place at Sheepdrove Organic Farm , a certified organic and environmentally restored landscape in the North Wessex Downs. The site includes: Chalk grasslands Ancient woodlands Wetlands and reedbeds Biodiversity-rich ecosystems Sustainable farming systems Accommodation options include: Single rooms Twin rooms Camping options The natural environment plays a central role in the programme by supporting: Reduced stress Improved clarity and focus Better emotional regulation Deeper systems thinking Facilitators and Leadership Team The programme is convened by experienced leaders in climate strategy, facilitation, and systems change: Jonathon Porritt — environmental campaigner and sustainability strategist Chloe Revill — facilitator and climate diplomacy expert Andy Raingold — leadership coach and transformation facilitator Together, they bring experience across: Climate policy and diplomacy Civil society and activism Government advisory work Organisational transformation Nature-based leadership development Why Nature Is Central Nature is not just a setting—it is a core methodology of the programme. Being in nature helps participants: Reduce cognitive overload Improve attention and clarity Step away from urgency-driven thinking Reconnect with long-term systems thinking Reflect on complexity with greater calm It supports more grounded decision-making in high-pressure environments. Key Dates Residential: 1–3 July 2026 Online Workshop 1: 24 July 2026 Online Workshop 2: 11 September 2026 Online Workshop 3: 25 September 2026 Application deadline: Rolling / bursary-based (via links provided) Click here for more and to apply. title: EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research 2026: Fully Online AI Research Mentorship Program for Aspiring Researchers Worldwide
summary: Aspiring AI researchers, programmers, students, and open science enthusiasts from around the world now have an exciting opportunity to gain hands-on research experience through the EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR) 2026 program. The Summer of Open AI Research is a five-week, fully online mentorship and research initiative sponsored by EleutherAI, one of the leading organisations in open-source artificial intelligence research. The programme is designed to help individuals with little or no prior research experience contribute to meaningful AI research projects under the mentorship of experienced researchers and experts in the field. Participants will collaborate on real-world open science projects in areas such as: AI interpretability AI safety Representation learning Mechanistic interpretability Scientific reasoning AI for science Information retrieval Autonomous systems Audio and generative modelling Successful participants will contribute directly to active research projects and may receive formal credit on resulting publications and research outputs. Applications for the Summer of Open AI Research 2026 are open until 8 June 2026. What Is the EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR)? The Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR) is an online AI research programme focused on: Open science Collaborative AI development Research mentorship Skill development Community-driven innovation The initiative connects aspiring researchers with experienced mentors to work collaboratively on open-source AI research projects over five weeks. The programme seeks to lower barriers to AI research participation by welcoming: Students Self-taught learners Programmers Independent researchers Individuals outside traditional academic systems SOAR creates opportunities for participants to gain: Structured mentorship Practical research experience Collaboration opportunities Publication experience Exposure to cutting-edge AI topics About EleutherAI EleutherAI is a prominent open-source AI research organisation known for advancing collaborative and transparent artificial intelligence research. The organisation focuses on: Open-source AI models Language modelling AI interpretability Alignment research Mechanistic interpretability Safety research Community-driven AI innovation Unlike proprietary AI ecosystems, EleutherAI promotes open and collaborative research accessible to the global AI community. The “Open AI” in the programme title refers to open and collaborative artificial intelligence research, not the company behind ChatGPT. Programme Overview The Summer of Open AI Research is fully online and hosted through the EleutherAI Discord community platform. Programme Duration 5 weeks Programme Format Fully remote Online collaboration Mentorship-based learning Research-focused teamwork Participants will work closely with mentors and research groups on selected projects while developing practical AI research skills. Who Should Apply? EleutherAI encourages applications from individuals interested in contributing to open-source AI research. Ideal applicants include: Experienced programmers interested in AI research BS, MS, and PhD students Computer science students Mathematics students Physics students Self-taught AI researchers Independent learners seeking mentorship Open science contributors Importantly, applicants do not need prior research experience to apply. The programme explicitly encourages individuals outside traditional academic environments to participate. Eligibility Requirements According to EleutherAI: Anyone can apply Applicants will be evaluated based on their ability to contribute Research experience is not mandatory Applicants are expected to demonstrate: Technical curiosity Programming ability Commitment to collaborative work Interest in AI research Research Areas and Project Tracks Participants can apply to projects across multiple AI research domains. Interpretability and Reasoning Projects Research topics include: Detecting reasoning errors in open-weight models Evaluating interpretability methods Semantic compression in foundation models Hierarchy analysis in sparse autoencoders Activation verbalizer experiments Tracing subliminal learning during pretraining AI Safety Projects Participants may work on: Subliminal prompting mechanisms Alignment and interpretability Behavioural shift prediction Deceptive compliance in AI agents AI Applications Projects Project areas include: AI for astronomy Information retrieval systems Autonomous drone simulations Singing voice synthesis models These projects provide practical exposure to modern AI research methodologies and tools. Example Research Project One highlighted project is: Detecting Right-Answer, Wrong-Reason Behavior in Open-Weight Reasoning Models This project examines whether AI models can arrive at correct answers using flawed reasoning processes. Participants will: Create reasoning problem datasets Analyse model behaviour Compare reasoning outputs Study sparse autoencoder features Evaluate internal evidence for genuine reasoning Skills Required for Participation While research experience is not required, participants are expected to have some technical foundation. Preferred skills include: Python programming Basic machine learning knowledge Familiarity with PyTorch Familiarity with Hugging Face tools Data analysis experience Git and GitHub workflows Ability to read technical materials carefully Strong experimental thinking and analytical curiosity are especially valuable. Mentorship and Collaboration Participants will work under the mentorship of experienced researchers from institutions and organisations such as: MIT CSAIL Stanford University EleutherAI Constellation Institute Algoverse The mentorship model is one of the programme’s strongest features, offering participants direct guidance while working on practical AI research problems. Participant Benefits The SOAR programme offers multiple academic and professional benefits. Research Experience Participants gain: Hands-on AI research exposure Real-world project experience Collaborative research training Mentorship Selected participants receive: Guidance from experienced researchers Structured learning support Exposure to advanced AI topics Publication and Recognition Participants may: Receive project credit Contribute to publishable research Build academic and technical portfolios Networking Opportunities Participants can connect with: AI researchers Students Open-source developers Technical communities worldwide Open Science Contribution Participants contribute directly to: Open-source AI development Collaborative scientific research Publicly accessible AI innovation Programme Timeline Important Dates 15 May 2026 Project proposal deadline 18 May 2026 Participant applications open 8 June 2026 Participant application deadline 5 July 2026 Application decisions released Rolling decisions may arrive earlier. 6 July 2026 Project preparation begins 13 July 2026 Main programme begins 1 August 2026 Short research talks and progress presentations 16 August 2026 Final talks and programme conclusion Time Commitment The required time commitment depends on the selected project. Each project listing provides estimated weekly hours. For example: Some projects may require approximately 6 hours per week Participants should review project requirements carefully before applying. Why This Programme Matters AI research opportunities are often limited to individuals within elite academic institutions or established research labs. The Summer of Open AI Research programme seeks to make AI research more accessible by: Supporting independent learners Encouraging open collaboration Expanding research access globally Promoting mentorship-based learning Strengthening open science ecosystems For many participants, SOAR may become: Their first AI research experience A pathway into advanced research careers An opportunity to build professional networks A stepping stone toward publication and graduate research How to Apply Interested applicants can apply online before the deadline. Apply here Final Thoughts The EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research 2026 programme presents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring researchers, programmers, students, and independent learners to gain practical AI research experience within a collaborative and mentorship-driven environment. With projects spanning interpretability, AI safety, representation learning, and advanced AI applications, participants will engage directly with cutting-edge research while contributing to the broader open science movement. For individuals interested in entering the world of artificial intelligence research, the SOAR programme offers both valuable technical development and meaningful community engagement in one of the most dynamic fields in technology today. title: International Geneva Peace Fellowship Programme 2026.
summary: The International Geneva Peace Fellowship Programme 2026 is a highly competitive, residential leadership initiative designed to develop the next generation of global experts in peacebuilding, humanitarian diplomacy, mediation, and inclusive international cooperation . This Fellowship is jointly implemented by the Interpeace and the Geneva Graduate Institute , with support from the Foundation for the Adaptation of International Geneva (FAGI). Based in Geneva, Switzerland, the programme places selected Fellows directly inside one of the world’s most influential diplomatic ecosystems— International Geneva —where global policies, humanitarian responses, and peace processes are shaped. Only 10 Fellows worldwide will be selected for the 2026 cohort, making this one of the most selective peace and diplomacy fellowships globally. About the International Geneva Peace Fellowship Programme The Fellowship is a 9-month full-time residential programme (September 2026 – June 2027) designed to combine: Real institutional work in global organizations Residential learning and collaboration Applied peacebuilding research Professional mentorship Leadership development It is not a theoretical academic programme. Instead, it is a hands-on professional immersion in global peace and humanitarian systems. Core Purpose of the Programme The Fellowship is built to respond to urgent global challenges such as: Fragmentation of global conflicts Weakening multilateral cooperation systems Limited entry points into peace and diplomacy careers Growing demand for innovative peace leadership Key Objectives: Train emerging global peace leaders Strengthen humanitarian diplomacy capacity Build cross-regional leadership networks Support innovation in peacebuilding practices Reinforce Geneva as a global peace hub Bridge research, policy, and field operations Programme Structure (Three Core Pillars) 1. Residential Programme in Geneva Fellows live together in Domaine Barton (Lake Geneva) while participating in intensive professional development. Key Activities: Living in a fully immersive residential environment Participation in peace and diplomacy projects Study visits across International Geneva institutions Collaborative research and policy work Peer-to-peer leadership development This environment is designed to build strong global collaboration and leadership capacity . 2. Institutional Collaboration Placements Each Fellow is placed in a leading international organization in Geneva for hands-on experience. What Fellows Do: Work on real-time peace and humanitarian projects Support institutional programmes and policy work Engage in diplomatic and research activities Receive mentorship from senior professionals Build long-term career networks Key Partner Institutions: Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue Kofi Annan Foundation Centre for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC) World Council of Churches This ensures direct exposure to real-world humanitarian diplomacy and peace operations . 3. Co-Creation, Research Leadership Development This pillar focuses on innovation, research, and strategic leadership building. Key Components: Intensive 1-week training programme at the start Advanced learning in peace and humanitarian diplomacy Development of applied research projects Participation in policy innovation work Continuous mentorship and peer exchange Independent strategic project development Fellows are encouraged to develop innovative peacebuilding solutions that can influence global policy and practice. Thematic Focus Areas (2026 Cohort) Each Fellow is selected under one of six thematic tracks aligned with global peace challenges. 1. New Frontiers of Peacemaking Focuses on modern conflict environments and innovation in mediation. Includes: Addressing neglected conflicts Building inclusive peace processes Climate-related conflict risks Digital and technological conflict dynamics Gender-inclusive mediation approaches 2. Health and Peace Explores the intersection between health systems and peacebuilding. Includes: Health systems in conflict zones Climate and environmental health risks Integrated peace-health frameworks Strengthening global health governance 3. Ecumenical Peacebuilding and Faith-Based Diplomacy Focuses on religious and interfaith contributions to peace. Includes: Faith-based mediation efforts Interreligious dialogue and reconciliation Role of churches and faith leaders in diplomacy Community-level peacebuilding initiatives 4. Youth Leadership, Participation Peacebuilding Focuses on empowering young people in peace processes. Includes: Youth leadership development Civic engagement in conflict prevention Peace education and advocacy Youth participation in policy processes 5. Protection of Civilians Modern Conflict Dynamics Focuses on civilian safety in evolving conflicts. Includes: Civilian protection strategies Urban warfare and explosive weapons AI and drone warfare risks Forced displacement and humanitarian access Protection of vulnerable populations 6. Women, Peace Security (WPS) and Inclusive Peacebuilding Focuses on gender equality in peace processes. Includes: Women’s participation in peace negotiations Gender-responsive peacebuilding policies Local women-led peace initiatives Structural barriers to inclusion Eligibility Criteria Applicants must fall into one of the following categories: 1. Recent Graduates Master’s degree holders OR PhD candidates (advanced stage) Graduated within the last 12 months 2. Junior Professionals 1–4 years of experience 3. Mid-Career Professionals 5–10 years of experience Required Qualifications Applicants must demonstrate: Strong leadership potential in peace or humanitarian work Background in international relations, law, development, or social sciences OR relevant field or policy experience Excellent English or French communication skills Ability to work in multicultural environments Adaptability to international field and institutional settings Full availability for a 9-month residency in Geneva Important Note: This is NOT a PhD or academic research fellowship. It is a practice-based leadership programme combining policy, fieldwork, and applied research . Application Requirements Applicants must submit: 1. CV Maximum 2 pages 2. Cover Letter (max 500 words / 1 page) Must include: Preferred thematic area Relevant leadership experience Motivation for joining the Fellowship A strategic idea or initiative to be developed during the programme Application Deadline 7 June 2026 — 11:59 pm CET Click here for more and to apply For more global fellowship opportunities, Click here The post International Geneva Peace Fellowship Programme 2026. appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: NATO Internship Programme 2027 in Rome, Italy: Fully Funded International Internship Opportunity for Students and Recent Graduates from NATO Member Countries
summary: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization has officially opened applications for the NATO Internship Programme 2027 at the prestigious NATO Defense College . This highly competitive international internship programme offers students and recent graduates from NATO member countries the opportunity to gain hands-on experience within one of the world’s most influential international security and defense alliances. The internship programme will take place in Rome, Italy, with intake periods scheduled for February 2027 and August 2027. This opportunity is ideal for ambitious young professionals seeking international exposure in areas related to international relations, security studies, diplomacy, defense policy, political affairs, strategic studies, and multinational cooperation. Applications close on 22 June 2026 . About NATO North Atlantic Treaty Organization is one of the world’s most important political and military alliances, bringing together member countries committed to collective defense, international peace, security cooperation, and democratic values. Founded in 1949, NATO works to: Maintain international peace and security Promote democratic values Encourage political consultation among member states Address emerging security threats Strengthen global defense cooperation Support crisis management and conflict prevention NATO plays a critical role in international diplomacy, strategic defense planning, cybersecurity, military cooperation, and geopolitical stability. The alliance also invests heavily in research, education, leadership development, and international policy dialogue through institutions such as the NATO Defense College. About the NATO Defense College (NDC) NATO Defense College is NATO’s premier academic institution dedicated to higher-level strategic education and research. Located in Rome, Italy, the college provides advanced education and training to military officers, diplomats, policymakers, and civilian officials from NATO member states and partner countries. The institution focuses on: International security studies Strategic leadership Defense policy Political-military affairs Geopolitical analysis Crisis management International cooperation Interns selected for the programme will gain exposure to a dynamic international working environment and contribute to ongoing institutional activities within the college. NATO Internship Programme 2027 Overview Internship Details Category Details Organization NATO Institution NATO Defense College Location Rome, Italy Intake Periods February 2027 August 2027 Programme Type Internship Application Deadline 22 June 2026 Why the NATO Internship Programme is Important The NATO Internship Programme provides young professionals with a rare opportunity to understand the inner workings of international organizations focused on diplomacy, defense, policy development, and security cooperation. Interns will have the opportunity to: Gain professional experience in an international institution Learn from experts in defense and strategic affairs Develop cross-cultural communication skills Build international professional networks Enhance knowledge of global security issues Strengthen policy research and analytical skills Understand multinational cooperation frameworks The programme also serves as a valuable stepping stone for careers in: International relations Diplomacy Public policy Security studies Defense analysis International organizations Government service Research institutions Political affairs Eligibility Requirements for the NATO Internship Programme 2027 Applicants must meet several strict eligibility conditions before applying. 1. Age Requirement Applicants must: Be at least 21 years old Be under 30 years old on the application closing date This requirement ensures the programme remains focused on students and early-career professionals. 2. Nationality Requirement Applicants must be: Citizens of a NATO member country Only nationals from NATO member states are eligible to apply for this internship opportunity. 3. Educational Requirement Applicants must satisfy one of the following educational conditions: Have completed at least two years of university study and currently be enrolled in a third year OR Have obtained their highest university degree no more than one year prior to application The programme is therefore suitable for both current university students and recent graduates. 4. Language Requirement Applicants must demonstrate: Proficiency in at least one of NATO’s official languages: English French Additionally: Working knowledge of the second official language is considered an advantage. Knowledge of other languages may also strengthen an application for certain positions. Strong communication skills in multilingual environments are highly valued within NATO institutions. What Interns Can Expect Selected interns will work in a highly multicultural and intellectually stimulating environment. Participants may gain exposure to: Strategic policy discussions Research activities International cooperation projects Administrative and organizational tasks Security and defense studies Academic conferences and seminars Policy drafting and analytical work Interns will also have opportunities to interact with experts, diplomats, military officials, researchers, and policymakers from across NATO member countries. Benefits of the NATO Internship Programme Although the vacancy notice focuses mainly on eligibility and recruitment information, participating in the NATO Internship Programme offers several significant professional advantages. Key Benefits Include: International work experience Exposure to NATO operations and structures Networking with global professionals Career development opportunities Experience working in a multinational environment Enhanced understanding of international security and diplomacy Strong addition to academic and professional CVs Access to a globally respected institution The internship experience can significantly strengthen applications for future opportunities in government, diplomacy, international development, research, and security-related careers. Equal Opportunity and Diversity Commitment North Atlantic Treaty Organization emphasizes equal opportunity and non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process. According to the official notice, NATO does not discriminate based on: Gender Race Ethnic origin Religion Nationality Disability Sexual orientation Age The organization encourages applications from qualified individuals across all eligible backgrounds. Application Process Qualified candidates must apply through NATO’s official e-recruitment system. Applicants are encouraged to: Carefully review all eligibility requirements Prepare supporting documents in advance Submit applications before the deadline Regularly monitor the NATO Defense College website for updates Application Deadline Deadline: 22 June 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early due to the highly competitive nature of the programme. How to Apply Interested applicants can learn more and submit applications through the official NATO platforms Apply here Why Students and Graduates Should Apply The NATO Internship Programme is an outstanding opportunity for young people seeking international exposure in policy, diplomacy, security, and strategic affairs. For students and graduates interested in global governance, international cooperation, and multinational institutions, this internship offers: Real-world policy exposure International networking opportunities Career-building experience Academic enrichment Practical understanding of international organizations Interns will develop valuable professional and intercultural skills while contributing to one of the world’s leading international alliances. title: UN Women Call for Proposals 2026: Up to USD 200,000 Grant for Civil Society Organizations Fighting Online Violence Against Women and Girls in the Western Balkans
summary: UN Women has officially launched a major regional Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) under the EU-funded programme focused on gender equality and ending violence against women in the Western Balkans. This important funding opportunity seeks qualified civil society organizations to design and implement a large-scale behavioural change and awareness-raising campaign addressing online and technology-facilitated violence against women and girls across the Western Balkans region. The initiative falls under the regional programme: “EU4 Gender Equality – Women’s Economic Empowerment and Ending Violence Against Women in the Western Balkans” The selected organization will receive funding ranging between USD 180,000 and USD 200,000 to carry out strategic communication, advocacy, awareness, and behavioural change initiatives aimed at combating violence against women and girls, particularly in digital spaces. Applications must be submitted by 12 June 2026 at 12:00 CET . About UN Women UN Women is the United Nations entity dedicated to advancing gender equality and empowering women worldwide. The organization works globally to: End violence against women and girls Promote women’s economic empowerment Advance women’s leadership and participation Strengthen gender-responsive governance Support feminist movements and civil society Promote equal rights and opportunities UN Women collaborates with governments, civil society organizations, development partners, regional institutions, and grassroots groups to address structural inequalities and create inclusive societies. About the EU4 Gender Equality Regional Programme The programme “EU4 Gender Equality – Women’s Economic Empowerment and Ending Violence Against Women in the Western Balkans” is funded by the European Union and implemented in partnership with UN Women. The programme focuses on addressing critical gender equality challenges in the Western Balkans region, including: Violence against women and girls Online harassment and abuse Economic inequalities Social norms and harmful stereotypes Gender discrimination Limited access to services and support systems The programme seeks to strengthen regional cooperation, public awareness, and institutional responses to gender-based violence. Purpose of the Call for Proposals UN Women is seeking a qualified Civil Society Organization (CSO) to serve as a Responsible Party responsible for implementing a regional behavioural change communication initiative. The selected organization will develop and execute a comprehensive awareness campaign targeting violence against women and girls, with a specific focus on: Online violence Technology-facilitated abuse Digital harassment Cyber violence Gender-based violence in digital spaces The initiative aims to improve awareness, shift harmful attitudes, increase knowledge of rights, and strengthen access to available support services across the Western Balkans. Key Objectives of the Programme The selected CSO will help achieve several major objectives. 1. Raise Awareness on Violence Against Women and Girls The programme seeks to increase public understanding of the various forms of violence women and girls experience both offline and online. This includes awareness around: Cyber harassment Digital stalking Online hate speech Non-consensual image sharing Gender-based online abuse Technology-enabled intimidation 2. Promote Behavioural Change A major focus of the programme is changing harmful attitudes, stereotypes, and behaviours that contribute to violence against women and girls. The campaign is expected to encourage: Respectful online behaviour Gender equality Positive social norms Digital safety Accountability Community engagement 3. Increase Knowledge of Rights and Support Services The campaign should also help women and girls better understand: Their legal rights Available support systems Protection mechanisms Reporting channels Access to services and assistance This is particularly important for vulnerable populations affected by online violence and discrimination. 4. Support Regional Advocacy Efforts In addition to campaign implementation, the selected CSO will contribute to the creative communication concepts for the: Regional Forum on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls Specifically, the organization will support communication strategies for the: 2026 edition 2027 edition This provides an opportunity for the selected organization to contribute to high-level regional advocacy and policy conversations. Funding Amount The budget range for the proposal is: USD 180,000 – USD 200,000 Important notes: Proposals exceeding the maximum amount will not be considered. Applicants should ensure budgets align with programme expectations and deliverables. This significant funding opportunity can support large-scale regional communication and advocacy activities. Who Should Apply? UN Women is specifically inviting: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Organizations with experience in gender equality, women’s rights, digital safety, communications, behavioural change campaigns, advocacy, and regional programme implementation are particularly well positioned for this opportunity. Expected Areas of Expertise The selected organization is expected to demonstrate strong expertise in areas such as: Gender equality programming Ending violence against women Behavioural change communication Public awareness campaigns Advocacy and outreach Digital communication Regional programme implementation Human rights Online safety and cyber violence Community engagement Experience working in the Western Balkans region may provide an added advantage. Geographic Focus The programme specifically targets the: Western Balkans Campaign activities and outreach efforts are expected to address populations across the region. Information Session for Applicants UN Women will organize an online information session to help interested organizations understand the proposal requirements and application process. Information Session Details Event Details Format Zoom Date 1 June 2026 Time 12:00 CET Applicants can register in advance through the official registration platform provided by UN Women. After registration, participants will receive confirmation details and instructions for joining the session. Important Administrative Requirements Selected organizations must: Accept all legal terms outlined in the Partner Agreement Register and undergo verification on the UN Partner Portal (UNPP) The UNPP is an online collaboration platform used by UN agencies to manage partnerships with civil society organizations. Organizations should prepare early for registration and verification processes if not already registered. Proposal Submission Deadline Deadline: 12 June 2026 at 12:00 CET UN Women emphasizes that proposals must be received before the official deadline. Late submissions may not be considered. Contact Information For additional inquiries, interested organizations may contact: Contact Person: Natalija Ostojic Email: ecaro.cfp@unwomen.org Why This Opportunity Matters Technology-facilitated violence against women and girls is becoming one of the fastest-growing forms of gender-based violence globally. This UN Women initiative recognizes the urgent need for: Public education Digital safety awareness Behavioural transformation Survivor-centered support Regional cooperation Advocacy and prevention strategies The programme presents a major opportunity for civil society organizations to shape regional conversations and strengthen protections for women and girls in digital spaces. How to Apply Interested organizations should carefully review all proposal documents and annexes provided by UN Women before preparing submissions. title: UNCCD COP17 Youth Delegation 2026 in Mongolia: Open Call for Young Leaders and Climate Changemakers Worldwide
summary: Young leaders, environmental advocates, youth organisations, and aspiring changemakers from around the world now have an exciting opportunity to participate in one of the most important global environmental conferences focused on land restoration, drought resilience, and sustainable development. The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) has officially launched the Open Delegation Call for Youth Participation at COP17 and the UNCCD Youth Forum 2026, which will take place in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, from 17 to 28 August 2026. Held under the theme “Restoring Land, Restoring Hope,” UNCCD COP17 is expected to bring together governments, civil society, youth leaders, environmental experts, and global stakeholders to address the growing challenges of: Land degradation Desertification Climate resilience Food insecurity Sustainable livelihoods Environmental sustainability The conference comes at a time when more than three billion people worldwide are affected by land degradation and declining ecosystems, making this summit a critical platform for global action and youth participation. The UNCCD Youth Forum 2026, which will take place on 18 and 19 August 2026, aims to strengthen the meaningful engagement of young people in environmental policy discussions and implementation efforts while promoting youth-led eco-entrepreneurship and agribusiness innovation. This open delegation call offers eligible young people and youth organisations the opportunity to participate in COP17 activities and potentially receive partial financial support should funding become available. About UNCCD COP17 2026 The seventeenth session of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification is one of the world’s leading international gatherings focused on combating land degradation and strengthening drought resilience. Event Details Event: UNCCD COP17 Location: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia Dates: 17–28 August 2026 Theme: “Restoring Land, Restoring Hope” The summit will serve as a major international platform where governments, policymakers, scientists, civil society organisations, and youth representatives collaborate on solutions for sustainable land management and environmental restoration. The conference seeks to accelerate global action toward: Land restoration targets Drought resilience Climate adaptation Sustainable agriculture Ecosystem protection Food security solutions UNCCD Youth Forum 2026 Building on the success of previous Youth Forums organised during COP13, COP14, COP15, and COP16, the fifth UNCCD Youth Forum will take place alongside COP17. Youth Forum Dates 18–19 August 2026 The Youth Forum aims to: Empower young people in global environmental governance Increase youth participation in UNCCD implementation Strengthen youth advocacy Promote youth-led environmental innovation Support eco- and agripreneurship initiatives The forum will also provide space for young leaders to: Share experiences Build international partnerships Discuss environmental challenges Advocate for supportive policies Collaborate on sustainable development initiatives Who Can Apply? The open call is open to two major categories of applicants: 1. UNCCD Youth Accredited Organisations Youth organisations accredited under the UNCCD framework may nominate representatives to participate in COP17 and the Youth Forum. 2. Individual Young Applicants Young people may also nominate themselves independently for participation in: UNCCD COP17 UNCCD Youth Forum 2026 This provides opportunities for youth leaders, climate advocates, environmental innovators, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, and grassroots organisers to engage directly in international environmental discussions. Eligibility Criteria Applicants and nominees must meet the following requirements: Age Requirement Applicants must be: Between 18 and 35 years old Eligible Regions Applicants must come from one of the following regions: Africa Asia-Pacific Latin America and the Caribbean Central and Eastern Europe Western Europe and Others Registration Requirement Applicants must: Already be registered for UNCCD COP17 OR Be willing to complete registration upon confirmation of participation Who Is This Open Call Intended For? The call specifically targets: Young People Already Planning to Attend COP17 Individuals who have already secured participation arrangements for COP17 in Mongolia are encouraged to apply. Young People Seeking Financial Support Applicants who require partial financial assistance to attend the Youth Forum and COP17 are also encouraged to submit applications. However, organisers have clarified that: Funding has not yet been confirmed Financial support is not guaranteed Applicants are strongly encouraged to seek independent funding where possible The information collected through the application process will help identify potential delegates should sponsorship opportunities become available. Possible Financial Support If funding becomes available, selected participants may receive partial participation support. Potential Support Includes: Shared accommodation Travel assistance Daily Subsistence Allowance (DSA) Participation support during COP17 Support for attending the UNCCD Youth Forum The support would cover activities taking place between: 17–28 August 2026 including: Youth Forum sessions COP17 events Networking opportunities Side events and policy discussions Important Funding Notice Applicants should note carefully that: Submission of the form does not guarantee sponsorship Financial assistance depends entirely on funding availability Delegates are encouraged to independently secure financial support whenever possible This means applicants should proactively explore: Institutional sponsorships Grants Youth participation funds NGO support Government travel support University funding opportunities Why This Opportunity Matters Participation in UNCCD COP17 and the Youth Forum can provide young people with: Global exposure International networking opportunities Policy engagement experience Leadership development Environmental advocacy skills Collaboration opportunities with global stakeholders Participants will gain firsthand experience engaging in: International climate discussions Sustainable development policymaking Environmental governance Youth-led advocacy Global sustainability initiatives This experience can significantly strengthen careers and initiatives related to: Climate action Environmental sustainability Agriculture Youth development International policy Sustainable innovation Why Youth Participation Is Important Young people are increasingly at the forefront of: Climate advocacy Land restoration campaigns Sustainable agriculture innovation Environmental entrepreneurship Community resilience initiatives The UNCCD Youth Forum recognises that youth voices are essential for building: Sustainable futures Inclusive environmental policies Resilient communities Innovative climate solutions The forum therefore creates opportunities for young people to directly influence conversations around: Environmental justice Land restoration Climate resilience Sustainable livelihoods Application Deadline Deadline: 14 June 2026 Time: 23:59 CEST Applicants are encouraged to apply before the deadline to ensure consideration. How to Apply Interested applicants can apply through the official application form. Learn more and apply here: UNCCD COP17 Youth Delegation Application Form Event Location Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia Mongolia will host the global gathering, bringing together environmental leaders, policymakers, civil society organisations, and youth representatives from around the world. The location reflects growing international attention toward: Sustainable land management Climate resilience Ecosystem restoration Environmental cooperation Final Thoughts The Open Delegation Call for Youth Participation at UNCCD COP17 and the Youth Forum 2026 represents a major opportunity for young environmental leaders and changemakers to engage directly in international sustainability discussions. Although funding has not yet been confirmed, the opportunity offers participants a chance to: Join a global environmental movement Participate in international policymaking discussions Build meaningful networks Strengthen advocacy skills Contribute to solutions for land restoration and climate resilience For young people passionate about sustainability, climate justice, environmental governance, and youth leadership, UNCCD COP17 in Mongolia could become a transformative international experience.
