title: Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab Pilot 2026: Fully Supported Program for Young Agrifood Innovators in Australia and the Pacific
summary: Applications are now open for the Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab Pilot 2026, a transformative initiative designed to empower young innovators passionate about creating sustainable, resilient, and inclusive food systems across Australia and the Pacific region. Led by the World Food Forum (WFF) Australia Youth Chapter and WFF Fiji Chapter in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (UN FAO) and regional partners, this two-month pilot program will support youth-driven solutions addressing some of the most pressing challenges facing modern agrifood systems. The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab will run virtually from 1 July to 31 August 2026 and is open to individuals and teams aged 18–35 who are based in Australia or the Pacific. Application Deadline: 14 June 2026 (11:59 PM) About the Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab is part of the global Youth Food Lab network, joining similar initiatives already active in Europe, Africa, North America, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Nepal. The initiative aims to help young innovators develop impactful organisations and projects that improve sustainability, resilience, food security, nutrition, climate adaptation, and public health outcomes within agrifood systems. Participants do not need to have a fully developed startup or organization before applying. The program is designed for people who may only have a problem they want to solve or an early-stage idea they want to explore further. The initiative welcomes a broad range of project models, including: Startups Social enterprises Non-profit organizations Cooperatives Charities Community-led initiatives Early-stage impact ventures Program Duration and Structure The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab Pilot 2026 will run over two months: Start Date: 1 July 2026 End Date: 31 August 2026 The program is entirely virtual, allowing participants from different parts of Australia and the Pacific region to collaborate and participate online. Weekly Commitment Participants are expected to commit to: Two hours per week for online masterclasses One hour every fortnight for mentorship sessions This structure makes the program accessible for students, working professionals, entrepreneurs, and community leaders balancing other commitments. What Participants Will Gain The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab is designed to provide practical support, mentorship, and international exposure for emerging agrifood innovators. 1. Develop Your Own Food Systems Project Participants will work on a project that addresses a challenge within their local or regional food system. Possible focus areas include: Sustainable agriculture Climate-resilient farming Nutrition and public health Food waste reduction Sustainable fisheries Food distribution and supply chains Community food access Indigenous food systems Agritech innovation Circular food economies Youth engagement in agriculture Applicants may enter the program with: A problem they want to solve A rough idea An early-stage project A developing organization The program emphasizes potential, creativity, and commitment rather than polished business plans. 2. Expert-Led Masterclasses Participants will gain access to practical masterclasses led by experts in food systems, innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainability. Key learning areas include: Systems thinking Partnership development Impact measurement Fundraising and financing Building sustainable organizations Community engagement Leadership development Social innovation Project implementation strategies These sessions are designed to equip participants with actionable skills they can apply directly to their projects. 3. Personalised Mentorship Each participant or team will be paired with a mentor aligned with their area of interest and project focus. Mentorship benefits include: Practical guidance Strategic advice Industry insights Networking opportunities Accountability and support Feedback on project development Participants will attend structured mentorship calls every fortnight throughout the program. 4. Showcase Event At the end of the pilot program, participants will present their project ideas and progress during a showcase event. The showcase is designed to: Increase visibility for participants Connect innovators with supporters and stakeholders Open pathways to future funding and collaboration opportunities Build momentum for ongoing project development 5. Access to a Global Network Participants will become part of the international Youth Food Lab network, connecting them with innovators and changemakers across multiple regions worldwide. This community provides: International collaboration opportunities Peer learning Networking Shared innovation Cross-regional partnerships Exposure to global food systems conversations Mission of the Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab The mission of the Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab is to equip young innovators with the mentorship, skills, and opportunities needed to create impactful agrifood solutions aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The initiative seeks to improve: Food security Nutrition outcomes Sustainability Climate resilience Public health Community wellbeing Agricultural innovation Who Can Apply? The program is open to individuals and teams who meet the following criteria: Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be between 18 and 35 years old Be based in Australia or the Pacific region Have an interest in sustainable and resilient food systems Be motivated to create positive impact within agrifood systems Be interested in building a new organization, initiative, startup, or project Be available to participate from 1 July to 31 August 2026 Ideal Applicants Include The program welcomes applications from: University students Researchers Entrepreneurs Farmers Fishers Educators Community organizers Sustainability advocates Public health innovators Food systems practitioners Climate action leaders Social innovators Both individuals and teams are encouraged to apply. Why This Opportunity Matters Food systems globally are facing increasing pressure from climate change, food insecurity, environmental degradation, rising costs, and public health challenges. Young people across Australia and the Pacific are uniquely positioned to develop innovative, community-driven solutions that strengthen sustainability and resilience. The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab creates an important platform for youth to: Build practical solutions Access mentorship and training Collaborate internationally Launch impactful initiatives Develop leadership skills Contribute to the future of food systems in their communities Application Deadline Applications for the Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab Pilot 2026 close on: 14 June 2026 at 11:59 PM Shortlisted applicants will be invited for interviews before final selections are made. Final Thoughts The Australia-Pacific Youth Food Lab Pilot 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for young innovators to transform ideas into meaningful action within sustainable food systems. Whether you are a student exploring solutions to food insecurity, a farmer developing climate-resilient practices, or an entrepreneur building a sustainable agrifood initiative, this program provides the mentorship, knowledge, and global network needed to strengthen your impact. Young leaders across Australia and the Pacific who are passionate about creating resilient and sustainable food systems are strongly encouraged to apply before the deadline. title: Fully Funded UCC School of Law PhD Scholarship 2026 in Ireland | €25,000 Annual Stipend for International and EU Students
summary: Applications are now officially open for the highly prestigious School of Law PhD Scholarship 2026 at University College Cork (UCC) in Ireland. This fully funded doctoral scholarship offers outstanding students the opportunity to pursue advanced legal research at one of Ireland’s leading universities while receiving comprehensive financial support. The scholarship is open to both EU and non-EU applicants and provides: Full tuition fee coverage An annual stipend of EUR 25,000 Funding support for up to four years This opportunity is designed for ambitious scholars who are passionate about legal research, academic excellence, and contributing meaningful knowledge to the field of law. With access to internationally recognised supervisors, a vibrant doctoral research community, and tailored academic support systems, the UCC School of Law PhD Scholarship represents an exceptional pathway for aspiring legal researchers and academics. About University College Cork (UCC) University College Cork (UCC) is one of Ireland’s leading higher education institutions, internationally recognised for academic excellence, research innovation, and student development. The School of Law at UCC is known for: High-quality legal research Internationally respected faculty Strong doctoral training Interdisciplinary legal scholarship Supportive academic environment The university offers doctoral researchers access to: Expert supervision Research training Academic resources Networking opportunities Professional development activities Students joining the programme become part of a thriving research community committed to advancing legal scholarship and public impact. Overview of the UCC School of Law PhD Scholarship 2026 The School of Law PhD Scholarship is offered to candidates commencing PhD studies in Autumn 2026. The scholarship supports students pursuing doctoral research in any field of law and aims to attract highly talented researchers with strong academic backgrounds and research potential. This fully funded scholarship allows recipients to focus on high-level research without the burden of tuition costs or financial constraints. Scholarship Benefits The UCC School of Law PhD Scholarship 2026 provides substantial financial and academic support to successful candidates. 1. Full Tuition Fee Coverage The scholarship fully covers tuition fees for: EU applicants Non-EU applicants This makes the programme accessible to international students from around the world. 2. Annual Stipend of EUR 25,000 Recipients will receive: EUR 25,000 per year Funding support for a maximum of four years The stipend is intended to help cover living expenses and allow students to focus on their research activities. 3. Access to Internationally Recognised Supervisors PhD scholars at UCC benefit from supervision by experts who are internationally recognised in their respective legal fields. This provides students with: High-level academic mentorship Research guidance Professional development support Opportunities for scholarly collaboration 4. Vibrant Doctoral Research Community Students become part of a dynamic and supportive doctoral environment with access to: Research seminars Workshops Academic conferences Collaborative research opportunities Tailored doctoral support systems 5. Potential Teaching and Tutoring Opportunities The university notes that separately remunerated opportunities in: Lecturing Tutoring may also become available during the PhD programme. These experiences can help doctoral students build teaching portfolios and strengthen future academic career prospects. Research Areas One of the major strengths of this scholarship is its flexibility regarding research topics. The scholarship is open to candidates in: Any field of law Applicants are encouraged to: Develop a strong research proposal Identify potential supervisors Contact supervisors before applying This early engagement can help applicants strengthen their applications and align research interests with faculty expertise. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must carefully review the scholarship requirements before applying. Minimum Academic Requirements Candidates must have: A First-Class honours degree or a high 2.1 honours undergraduate degree in law (or equivalent) In addition, applicants should also possess: A Master’s degree in law or a related field OR Extensive and relevant professional experience demonstrating capacity for independent research and academic writing Ideal Candidates for the Scholarship The scholarship is best suited for applicants who: Have strong academic records Demonstrate research potential Possess analytical and writing skills Are passionate about legal scholarship Intend to contribute to legal research and policy development Applicants with interdisciplinary legal interests may also find this opportunity highly valuable. title: Media Foundation for West Africa Investigative Journalism Mentorship Programme for Women 2026 in Ghana
summary: Investigative journalism remains one of the most powerful tools for promoting accountability, exposing corruption, combating disinformation, and strengthening democratic governance. However, women continue to be underrepresented in investigative and accountability journalism across many African countries, including Ghana. To bridge this gap and empower the next generation of female investigative journalists, the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA), with support from the European Union through International Media Support, has announced the 2026 Investigative Journalism Mentorship Programme for Women in Ghana. This fully funded 12-month hybrid mentorship programme is designed to equip young Ghanaian women with practical investigative journalism skills, newsroom exposure, professional mentorship, and editorial support to become strong voices in accountability journalism. The initiative forms part of the African Media Integrity and Resilience Programme being implemented by the MFWA. About the Investigative Journalism Mentorship Programme The programme is targeted at female journalism graduates, early-career journalists, and young professionals who are passionate about governance reporting, investigative journalism, ethical media practice, and countering disinformation. Selected participants will undergo a structured mentorship experience that combines residential training, virtual coaching, and newsroom attachment opportunities. The programme aims to nurture women journalists who can contribute meaningfully to public accountability, transparency, and democratic development in Ghana. Structure of the Programme The mentorship programme will run from July 2026 to June 2027 and will follow a hybrid format. 1. Two Months Residential Training Participants will begin with an intensive two-month in-person residential training programme. Accommodation will be fully provided at a designated training location. During this phase, fellows will receive hands-on training in: Investigative journalism techniques Governance and policy reporting Leadership development Mobile journalism Fact-checking and verification Multimedia storytelling Digital content production Women’s safety in journalism Ethical and accountability reporting 2. Ten Months Virtual Mentorship Following the residential component, participants will continue with ten months of virtual mentorship and professional coaching. This stage will connect fellows with experienced female editors, investigative journalists, and governance experts who will guide participants throughout the programme. The mentorship phase is designed to help fellows: Strengthen investigative reporting skills Develop editorial judgment Build professional confidence Improve storytelling techniques Navigate challenges in journalism careers Expand professional networks 3. Six-Month Newsroom Attachment Within the mentorship period, participants will also complete a six-month newsroom attachment with The Fourth Estate, the investigative journalism project of the MFWA. This practical newsroom experience will expose fellows to real investigative reporting projects and editorial processes. Benefits of the Programme Successful applicants will enjoy several professional and financial benefits throughout the mentorship programme. Key Benefits Include: Intensive investigative journalism training Professional mentorship from experienced female editors Coaching from governance experts Financial support for investigative story production Editorial support for published stories Opportunity to produce at least five investigative stories Six-month newsroom attachment with The Fourth Estate Monthly stipend Certificate of honour upon successful completion Expanded professional journalism network Enhanced digital and multimedia storytelling skills Who Can Apply? The programme is open to: Female Ghanaian journalism graduates Early-career journalists Young professionals passionate about accountability journalism Applicants must also be willing to fully participate in the programme from July 2026 to June 2027. The organisers particularly encourage applications from candidates residing in: Greater Accra Region Eastern Region Central Region Ashanti Region Bono East Region Savannah Region Northern Region Upper West Region Required Application Documents Interested applicants must submit the following documents: A motivation letter (maximum 300 words) explaining why they should be considered for the programme Links to two published works: News articles for journalists Blog posts for other professionals Letter of consent from employer (required for staff journalists) Updated CV with two referees How to Apply Applicants should send all required documents via email to: applications@mfwa.org Email Subject Line: “Application for Female IJ Mentorship” Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all requirements before submission to ensure their applications are complete. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Media Foundation for West Africa Investigative Journalism Mentorship Programme for Women is: May 27, 2026 Late applications may not be considered, so interested candidates are encouraged to apply early. Why This Programme Matters The underrepresentation of women in investigative journalism continues to limit diversity in newsrooms and public discourse. Programmes such as this mentorship initiative are critical in creating opportunities for women to build successful careers in investigative reporting and governance journalism. By equipping young women with investigative skills, mentorship, and newsroom experience, the programme contributes to stronger media accountability systems and more inclusive journalism in Ghana. This opportunity is particularly valuable for aspiring investigative journalists seeking practical exposure, professional guidance, and long-term career development in media and governance reporting. For enquiries, applicants may contact Josephine Badu-Nyarko via: Phone: 0547043404 Email: josephine@mfwa.org For more information about this opportunity, visit here . title: Social Fiction Design Competition 2026: Win USD 10,000 by Imagining a Better World for Young People in 2050
summary: Young writers, dreamers, storytellers, and changemakers from around the world are invited to participate in the Social Fiction Design Competition 2026, a global creative writing competition that challenges participants to imagine a better, fairer, and more sustainable world for young people in the year 2050. Organized by Yunus Center and powered through YY Ventures , this international initiative encourages people everywhere to use the power of imagination and storytelling to envision solutions to today’s social and environmental challenges. The competition is open globally with no age restrictions and no geographical limitations, making it one of the most inclusive international creative writing opportunities currently available. Participants stand a chance to win a grand prize of USD 10,000 while contributing to conversations about the future of humanity, sustainability, innovation, and social transformation. What is the Social Fiction Design Competition? The Social Fiction Design Competition is an international writing competition focused on “Social Fiction” — a form of imaginative storytelling similar to science fiction, but centered on social innovation and human progress rather than futuristic technology alone. The competition invites participants to imagine: What the world could look like in 2050 How young people may live in the future How societies can overcome inequality and injustice What sustainable communities might become How governments, businesses, and communities can work together for positive change The goal is to inspire new ways of thinking about social innovation and encourage people to imagine the world they truly want to build. According to Nobel Peace Laureate Muhammad Yunus : “If we do not imagine, it will not be done. If we imagine, someday it will happen.” This powerful idea forms the foundation of the competition. What is Social Fiction? Social Fiction is a storytelling approach that imagines a future society shaped by positive social transformation. Unlike traditional science fiction, which often focuses heavily on futuristic machines or scientific advancement, Social Fiction focuses on: Human-centered innovation Social justice Sustainability Equality Community transformation Ethical development Inclusive economies Environmental healing The concept encourages writers to creatively explore solutions to real-world problems and imagine societies where communities thrive. The organizers believe that imagination can inspire real-world innovation and policy change. Competition Theme: The Life of a Young Person in 2050 Participants are asked to imagine and describe: “How do you wish to see the life of a young person in the year 2050?” Writers are encouraged to take readers on a journey into a future world that is free from the social and environmental injustices affecting communities today. The competition emphasizes optimism, innovation, and bold thinking. Applicants should imagine a future where systems, institutions, and communities have evolved to create better opportunities and improved quality of life for younger generations. Writing Requirements Participants must submit an original Social Fiction piece between: Minimum: 1,000 words Maximum: 5,000 words The writing should creatively explore a fictional world in 2050 while addressing one or more major social or environmental issues. Suggested Focus Areas Participants may choose to focus on one or several of the following areas: Climate Change Agriculture Technology and Innovation Micro-credit Transport Literature Music Waste Management Circular Economy Tourism WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) Employment Sports Health and Well-being Community Development Sustainability Social Equity The organizers encourage participants to think broadly and creatively about how these sectors could evolve positively by 2050. What Should Your Story Include? The competition encourages writers to explain how different stakeholders contribute to building a better future. Stories may include the role of: Governments Educational institutions Corporate organizations Local businesses Community leaders Entrepreneurs Youth movements Civil society organizations Participants should demonstrate how collaboration and innovation help shape a more just and sustainable society. Why This Competition Matters The Social Fiction Design Competition is not just a writing contest. It is a platform for global imagination and social innovation. At a time when the world faces challenges such as: Climate change Rising inequality Unemployment Environmental degradation Mental health concerns Economic instability Social exclusion The competition seeks bold visions of hope and possibility. It encourages people to move beyond criticism and begin imagining actionable futures worth building. Prize Opportunity: Win USD 10,000 One of the major attractions of the competition is the opportunity to win: USD 10,000 The prize recognizes outstanding creativity, originality, optimism, and social imagination. Beyond financial rewards, participants gain international exposure and become part of a global conversation on innovation and sustainable futures. Who Can Participate? One of the strongest features of the Social Fiction Design Competition is its accessibility. There are: No age restrictions No geographical limitations This means anyone from anywhere in the world can participate. Students, writers, professionals, activists, researchers, entrepreneurs, and aspiring storytellers are all encouraged to apply. Can You Apply More Than Once? According to the competition FAQ: Multiple applications are not permitted. Applicants are encouraged to focus on submitting one strong and well-developed Social Fiction piece. Is There an Application Fee? The competition states that there is: No application fee Participation is completely free. Can Teams Apply? The FAQ section indicates that applicants should review the application guidelines regarding team participation. Participants are encouraged to verify current submission rules through the official competition platform. Previous Winners and Finalists The competition has already attracted talented participants from different countries around the world. Previous Winner Amit Kumar Mishra – Nepal Previous Finalists Neha Sabu – India Wan Faizal Mohd – Malaysia Anne Julienne Barcelona – United States Tyfur Rahman – Bangladesh The diversity of past finalists demonstrates the truly international nature of the competition. Why You Should Apply Participating in the Social Fiction Design Competition can help writers and changemakers: Showcase creativity globally Build visibility as a thought leader Contribute to social innovation conversations Inspire real-world solutions Develop storytelling and writing skills Gain recognition for visionary ideas Connect imagination with impact For young innovators, students, activists, and creative thinkers, this is a unique opportunity to influence future thinking through storytelling. How to Apply Applicants are required to: Write an original Social Fiction piece Ensure the submission falls within 1,000–5,000 words Complete the online application form Submit the story through the official competition platform For inquiries: Email: info@yy.ventures WhatsApp: +880 1648-397420 Apply Here For more information on this competition visit here Discover more opportunities on OFY here The post Social Fiction Design Competition 2026: Win USD 10,000 by Imagining a Better World for Young People in 2050 appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: BASE Fellows Fall 2026: Fully Remote AI Safety Fellowship Empowering Black Researchers and Leaders Worldwide
summary: The BASE Fellows Fall 2026 programme is now accepting applications from Black researchers, professionals, students, and practitioners interested in advancing their expertise in AI Safety, AI Governance, and AI Security. Designed as a fully remote and part-time fellowship, the programme offers a unique opportunity for members of the Black diaspora to gain hands-on research experience, expert mentorship, and foundational training in some of the world’s most important and rapidly evolving fields in artificial intelligence. Organised by Black in AI Safety and Ethics, the fellowship seeks to increase Black representation and leadership within the global AI ecosystem while ensuring that future AI systems are safe, equitable, accountable, and human-centered. Applications for the BASE Fellows Fall 2026 programme close on 16 June 2026 at 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AOE). The initiative is specifically designed to support and develop Black talent in critical AI-related fields that are shaping the future of technology and society. The programme focuses on three major areas: AI Safety AI Governance AI Security Through structured mentorship, collaborative learning, and practical research projects, fellows gain the knowledge and experience necessary to contribute meaningfully to the AI safety ecosystem and emerging governance discussions worldwide. The fellowship aims to ensure that the Black diaspora remains actively involved in shaping the development and regulation of advanced AI systems rather than being excluded from these transformative conversations. Mission of Black in AI Safety and Ethics (BASE) Black in AI Safety and Ethics was established to create a connected and informed Black community within the fields of AI safety, governance, and security. The organisation’s mission includes: Increasing Black representation in AI leadership Supporting Black researchers and practitioners Promoting ethical and equitable AI systems Building a global network of Black AI experts Preventing the marginalisation of Black communities in the age of artificial intelligence Ensuring fairness, accountability, and collective well-being in future AI systems As artificial intelligence increasingly influences economies, governance, communication, employment, and public life, BASE seeks to guarantee that Black voices remain influential in shaping AI policy and technological development. Foundational Training in AI Safety Ecosystems The fellowship equips fellows with critical foundational knowledge about the rapidly evolving AI landscape. Networking and Community Building Participants join a growing international network of Black researchers, professionals, and AI leaders. Leadership Development The programme helps participants strengthen their leadership capacity in technical, interdisciplinary, and policy-focused AI spaces. Fellows are encouraged to become future leaders capable of influencing the direction of AI development and governance globally. Duration 13 weeks Programme Period September 2026 to December 2026 Format Fully remote Part-time participation Participants are expected to communicate their weekly availability and explain how they intend to balance the fellowship with existing commitments. BASE Fellowship Selection Process The fellowship selection process occurs in multiple stages to ensure that applicants are matched appropriately with mentors and research tracks. Phase 1: Initial Application Review Applicants first submit a comprehensive application including: Resume/CV Educational background Work experience Research interests Motivation statement Professional achievements Track selection Research and leadership experiences Phase 2: Pre-Screening Assessment Applicants who pass the initial review will receive: A coding test for technical tracks, or A work test for non-technical tracks This stage evaluates the candidate’s readiness for the selected fellowship pathway. Phase 4: Final Offers Final fellowship offers are issued directly by the BASE team after mentor selection is completed. The BASE Fellowship is ideal for: Black researchers in AI-related fields Policy professionals interested in AI governance Students exploring AI safety research AI practitioners and technologists Interdisciplinary researchers Professionals seeking leadership opportunities in ethical AI The fellowship welcomes applicants from technical, policy, and interdisciplinary backgrounds. Why the BASE Fellowship Matters Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming every sector of society, from healthcare and education to governance, security, and employment. However, conversations around AI safety and governance often lack sufficient representation from Black communities globally. The BASE Fellowship seeks to address this gap by creating pathways for Black professionals and researchers to participate actively in shaping the future of AI systems. By supporting Black leadership in AI governance and safety, the programme contributes to building more equitable and inclusive technological futures. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the BASE Fellows Fall 2026 programme is: 16 June 2026 at 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AOE) Interested applicants are encouraged to apply early and prepare all required documents before submission. With expert mentorship, hands-on research opportunities, and a growing global community, the fellowship helps participants position themselves at the forefront of AI safety, governance, and security discussions worldwide. As AI technologies continue to influence humanity’s future, initiatives like the BASE Fellowship are essential for ensuring inclusive leadership and diverse representation within the global AI ecosystem. title: JournalismAI Skills Lab 2026: Free 14-Week Virtual AI Programme for Journalists, Editors, and Media Professionals Worldwide

title: Free Online Course on Promoting Youth Employment 2026 | Get Certified by ITCILO
summary: Youth unemployment remains one of the biggest global development challenges today. Across many countries, young people continue to face barriers in accessing decent work opportunities, transitioning from education into employment, and securing quality jobs that provide sustainable livelihoods. To help address these challenges, the International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITCILO) has launched a new free self-paced online course titled “Promoting Youth Employment: Challenges, Policies and Emerging Opportunities.” This course provides participants with practical knowledge, policy insights, and emerging labour market trends that can help shape inclusive and sustainable youth employment strategies worldwide. The program is completely free of charge and comes with an official digital certificate of completion upon successfully finishing the course modules and assessment. About the Promoting Youth Employment Course The “Promoting Youth Employment: Challenges, Policies and Emerging Opportunities” course is designed to introduce learners to the International Labour Organization’s (ILO) approach to youth employment. The course combines: Labour market analysis Youth employment policy strategies Practical development approaches Emerging economic opportunities Inclusion and gender equality frameworks Decent work principles Participants will gain valuable insights into how governments, organizations, and development practitioners can better support young people in securing meaningful and sustainable employment opportunities. The course also explores how major global trends such as digitalization, climate change, demographic shifts, and economic transformation are shaping the future of work for young people around the world. Why Youth Employment Matters Youth employment is central to achieving inclusive economic growth and sustainable development. Many young people globally face challenges such as: High unemployment rates Informal employment Limited access to quality jobs Skills mismatches Poor transition from school to work Gender inequality in employment Limited economic opportunities These challenges are becoming even more complex due to: Rapid technological changes Climate-related disruptions Population growth Economic uncertainty Changing labour market demands This course helps participants understand these realities while identifying practical policy solutions that can create better employment pathways for young people. What You Will Learn By the end of the course, participants will be able to: 1. Understand Global Youth Employment Challenges Learners will explore the major factors affecting youth employment globally, including unemployment trends, labour market inequalities, and barriers to decent work. 2. Learn Key Labour Market Concepts The course introduces important labour market concepts used by the International Labour Organization (ILO), helping participants understand employment systems more effectively. 3. Identify Effective Youth Employment Policies Participants will learn practical policy approaches that can support young people in accessing sustainable and decent employment opportunities. 4. Explore Emerging Employment Sectors The course highlights employment opportunities in fast-growing sectors such as: Digital economy Green economy Care economy Creative economy These sectors are increasingly shaping the future global labour market. 5. Understand Inclusion and Gender Equality Special attention is given to: Gender equality Social inclusion Decent work standards Equitable labour market participation Participants will learn why inclusive employment strategies are essential for sustainable development. Course Modules The course is divided into three structured modules designed to progressively build understanding and practical knowledge. Module 1 – Understanding the Youth Employment Challenge This module examines the current realities of youth unemployment and labour market transitions worldwide. Module 2 – Promoting Youth Employment: Policies and Solutions Participants explore evidence-based policy approaches and practical solutions that support youth employment. Module 3 – Promoting Youth Employment in Emerging Sectors This section focuses on future-oriented employment opportunities in sectors driving economic transformation and sustainability. Each module includes: Conceptual explanations Real-world examples Interactive exercises Knowledge assessments Reflection activities Course Duration and Learning Format The course is fully self-guided, allowing participants to study at their own pace from anywhere in the world. Duration Approximately 4–5 hours total learning time Learning Format 100% online Self-paced Flexible learning schedule This makes it ideal for: Working professionals Government officials Researchers Students Development practitioners Languages Available The course is accessible in multiple languages, making it available to a broad international audience. Available languages include: English French Spanish Portuguese Certification Participants who successfully complete the modules and pass the short assessment test will receive an official ITCILO digital certificate of completion. This certificate can help participants: Strengthen their professional profile Demonstrate expertise in youth employment policy Enhance career opportunities Showcase commitment to sustainable development and labour market inclusion Who Should Take This Course? This course is particularly valuable for: Government policymakers Employment officers Youth program coordinators NGO professionals Development practitioners Labour market researchers Academics Trainers and educators International organization staff Students interested in labour and development issues Anyone interested in understanding the future of youth employment and sustainable labour market solutions can benefit from this course. Benefits of Joining the Course Participants can gain several important benefits, including: Free access to expert knowledge Flexible self-paced learning Internationally recognized certificate Practical labour market insights Understanding of emerging job sectors Knowledge of youth employment policy frameworks Enhanced professional development Improved understanding of inclusion and gender equality in employment How to Enroll Click here for more and to apply Since the course is self-paced, participants can start learning immediately after registration. Final Thoughts As the future of work continues to evolve rapidly, understanding youth employment challenges and opportunities has become increasingly important for governments, organizations, and development professionals worldwide. The “Promoting Youth Employment: Challenges, Policies and Emerging Opportunities” course offers a valuable opportunity to gain practical skills and insights from the International Labour Organization’s approach to decent work, inclusion, and sustainable labour market development. With free enrollment, multilingual access, flexible learning, and certification included, this course is an excellent opportunity for professionals and learners who want to contribute to creating better employment opportunities for young people globally. title: RestorLife Awards 2026: Win Up to $25,000 in Funding and Global Recognition for Environmental Restoration

Organizations dedicated to ecological restoration, biodiversity protection, sustainable livelihoods, and environmental conservation now have a limited opportunity to apply before the official deadline of May 31, 2026. The RestorLife Awards celebrate the inspiring work of communities, restoration champions, NGOs, and businesses that are actively safeguarding ecosystems and creating sustainable futures. The initiative aims to amplify local success stories while providing financial support and international exposure to organizations leading environmental transformation worldwide. The awards are backed by leading environmental and sustainability stakeholders, including Ma Earth and the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). The initiative recognizes the importance of community-led environmental action and corporate responsibility in tackling global environmental challenges. The awards focus on supporting initiatives that: Restore degraded ecosystems Protect biodiversity Improve sustainable livelihoods Support local communities Promote environmental sustainability Encourage responsible business practices Strengthen climate resilience Drive nature-positive action The 2026 edition of the awards aims to spotlight impactful environmental initiatives from around the world while encouraging more organizations to scale their restoration efforts. NGO Award The NGO Award is targeted at registered non-profit organizations actively involved in environmental restoration and community-based conservation efforts. title: Social Fiction Design Competition 2026: Win USD 10,000 by Imagining a Better World for Young People in 2050
summary: Young writers, dreamers, storytellers, and changemakers from around the world are invited to participate in the Social Fiction Design Competition 2026, a global creative writing competition that challenges participants to imagine a better, fairer, and more sustainable world for young people in the year 2050. Organized by Yunus Center and powered through YY Ventures , this international initiative encourages people everywhere to use the power of imagination and storytelling to envision solutions to today’s social and environmental challenges. The competition is open globally with no age restrictions and no geographical limitations, making it one of the most inclusive international creative writing opportunities currently available. Participants stand a chance to win a grand prize of USD 10,000 while contributing to conversations about the future of humanity, sustainability, innovation, and social transformation. What is the Social Fiction Design Competition? The Social Fiction Design Competition is an international writing competition focused on “Social Fiction” — a form of imaginative storytelling similar to science fiction, but centered on social innovation and human progress rather than futuristic technology alone. The competition invites participants to imagine: What the world could look like in 2050 How young people may live in the future How societies can overcome inequality and injustice What sustainable communities might become How governments, businesses, and communities can work together for positive change The goal is to inspire new ways of thinking about social innovation and encourage people to imagine the world they truly want to build. According to Nobel Peace Laureate Muhammad Yunus : “If we do not imagine, it will not be done. If we imagine, someday it will happen.” This powerful idea forms the foundation of the competition. What is Social Fiction? Social Fiction is a storytelling approach that imagines a future society shaped by positive social transformation. Unlike traditional science fiction, which often focuses heavily on futuristic machines or scientific advancement, Social Fiction focuses on: Human-centered innovation Social justice Sustainability Equality Community transformation Ethical development Inclusive economies Environmental healing The concept encourages writers to creatively explore solutions to real-world problems and imagine societies where communities thrive. The organizers believe that imagination can inspire real-world innovation and policy change. Competition Theme: The Life of a Young Person in 2050 Participants are asked to imagine and describe: “How do you wish to see the life of a young person in the year 2050?” Writers are encouraged to take readers on a journey into a future world that is free from the social and environmental injustices affecting communities today. The competition emphasizes optimism, innovation, and bold thinking. Applicants should imagine a future where systems, institutions, and communities have evolved to create better opportunities and improved quality of life for younger generations. Writing Requirements Participants must submit an original Social Fiction piece between: Minimum: 1,000 words Maximum: 5,000 words The writing should creatively explore a fictional world in 2050 while addressing one or more major social or environmental issues. Suggested Focus Areas Participants may choose to focus on one or several of the following areas: Climate Change Agriculture Technology and Innovation Micro-credit Transport Literature Music Waste Management Circular Economy Tourism WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) Employment Sports Health and Well-being Community Development Sustainability Social Equity The organizers encourage participants to think broadly and creatively about how these sectors could evolve positively by 2050. What Should Your Story Include? The competition encourages writers to explain how different stakeholders contribute to building a better future. Stories may include the role of: Governments Educational institutions Corporate organizations Local businesses Community leaders Entrepreneurs Youth movements Civil society organizations Participants should demonstrate how collaboration and innovation help shape a more just and sustainable society. Why This Competition Matters The Social Fiction Design Competition is not just a writing contest. It is a platform for global imagination and social innovation. At a time when the world faces challenges such as: Climate change Rising inequality Unemployment Environmental degradation Mental health concerns Economic instability Social exclusion The competition seeks bold visions of hope and possibility. It encourages people to move beyond criticism and begin imagining actionable futures worth building. Prize Opportunity: Win USD 10,000 One of the major attractions of the competition is the opportunity to win: USD 10,000 The prize recognizes outstanding creativity, originality, optimism, and social imagination. Beyond financial rewards, participants gain international exposure and become part of a global conversation on innovation and sustainable futures. Who Can Participate? One of the strongest features of the Social Fiction Design Competition is its accessibility. There are: No age restrictions No geographical limitations This means anyone from anywhere in the world can participate. Students, writers, professionals, activists, researchers, entrepreneurs, and aspiring storytellers are all encouraged to apply. Can You Apply More Than Once? According to the competition FAQ: Multiple applications are not permitted. Applicants are encouraged to focus on submitting one strong and well-developed Social Fiction piece. Is There an Application Fee? The competition states that there is: No application fee Participation is completely free. Can Teams Apply? The FAQ section indicates that applicants should review the application guidelines regarding team participation. Participants are encouraged to verify current submission rules through the official competition platform. Previous Winners and Finalists The competition has already attracted talented participants from different countries around the world. Previous Winner Amit Kumar Mishra – Nepal Previous Finalists Neha Sabu – India Wan Faizal Mohd – Malaysia Anne Julienne Barcelona – United States Tyfur Rahman – Bangladesh The diversity of past finalists demonstrates the truly international nature of the competition. Why You Should Apply Participating in the Social Fiction Design Competition can help writers and changemakers: Showcase creativity globally Build visibility as a thought leader Contribute to social innovation conversations Inspire real-world solutions Develop storytelling and writing skills Gain recognition for visionary ideas Connect imagination with impact For young innovators, students, activists, and creative thinkers, this is a unique opportunity to influence future thinking through storytelling. How to Apply Applicants are required to: Write an original Social Fiction piece Ensure the submission falls within 1,000–5,000 words Complete the online application form Submit the story through the official competition platform For inquiries: Email: info@yy.ventures WhatsApp: +880 1648-397420 Apply Here For more information on this competition visit here Discover more opportunities on OFY here The post Social Fiction Design Competition 2026: Win USD 10,000 by Imagining a Better World for Young People in 2050 appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Global AgriInno Challenge 2026: Fully Funded International Opportunity for Agrifood Innovators Solving Climate and Food Challenges in Small Island Developing States
summary: The Global AgriInno Challenge (GAC) 2026 is now officially open for applications, offering an exceptional international platform for startups, agripreneurs, researchers, and innovation teams developing transformative agrifood solutions for Small Island Developing States (SIDS). Co-organized by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations , Zhejiang University , and Pinduoduo , the Global AgriInno Challenge has become one of the world’s leading youth-focused agrifood innovation competitions. The initiative connects emerging innovators with investors, policymakers, researchers, global experts, and technical partners to accelerate impactful solutions for sustainable food systems. The 2026 edition specifically focuses on Small Island Developing States (SIDS), which face increasing threats from climate change, food insecurity, biodiversity loss, geographic isolation, and limited innovation ecosystems. Despite these vulnerabilities, many SIDS remain underserved in global investment and technology opportunities, making this challenge particularly significant. Applications are open globally until 20 June 2026 (24:00 CEST) . What is the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026? The Global AgriInno Challenge is an international innovation competition designed to identify, support, and scale technology-driven agrifood solutions that can strengthen resilience and sustainability in vulnerable island regions. The challenge seeks innovations capable of transforming food systems while addressing pressing environmental, economic, and social issues affecting island communities worldwide. GAC 2026 emphasizes both “blue” and “green” agrifood systems, encouraging solutions related to: Agriculture Fisheries Aquaculture Climate resilience Sustainable food production Nutrition Biodiversity conservation Rural livelihoods Youth employment Digital agriculture The competition creates opportunities for innovators to gain international visibility, receive mentorship and coaching, network with industry leaders, and pitch their solutions on a global stage. Why the Focus on Small Island Developing States (SIDS)? Small Island Developing States are among the regions most vulnerable to: Rising sea levels Extreme weather events Climate-related disasters Dependence on imported food Limited agricultural land Fragile ecosystems Economic vulnerability Youth unemployment Weak innovation infrastructure At the same time, SIDS possess enormous potential for sustainable innovation, climate-smart agriculture, fisheries transformation, renewable systems, and community-based development. The Global AgriInno Challenge aims to support practical innovations that respond directly to the realities of island life and create long-term resilience for local communities. Challenge Themes for Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 Applicants must develop or scale solutions aligned with at least one of the four key pillars critical to SIDS resilience. 1. Better Production This pillar focuses on strengthening food production systems despite environmental and geographic limitations. Innovations may address: Limited arable land Climate pressures on agriculture Fisheries sustainability Food-import dependency Fragmented supply chains Precision agriculture Smart farming technologies Sustainable aquaculture Digital farming systems Solutions that improve productivity while promoting sustainability are highly encouraged. 2. Better Nutrition This theme focuses on improving access to affordable, healthy, and nutritious diets. Applicants may propose innovations that tackle: Malnutrition Obesity Diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) Food affordability challenges Nutrition education Food quality Local food systems The challenge encourages scalable approaches that can improve public health outcomes in island communities. 3. Better Environment Environmental protection is a major priority for SIDS due to their highly vulnerable ecosystems. Relevant innovation areas include: Coral reef protection Coastal ecosystem restoration Biodiversity conservation Climate adaptation Sustainable resource management Forest conservation Ocean sustainability Climate-smart technologies Solutions should demonstrate measurable environmental impact and long-term sustainability. 4. Better Life This pillar focuses on improving livelihoods and inclusive economic development. Applications may address: Rural development Youth unemployment Gender inclusion Digital inclusion Economic empowerment Entrepreneurship Job creation Community resilience The challenge seeks innovations capable of improving quality of life and expanding opportunities for underserved populations. Who Can Apply for the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026? Applications are open to agripreneurs and innovation teams from around the world. To qualify, applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements: Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be registered as a company or legal entity. Have less than USD 1,000,000 in annual turnover. Have operated for less than 5 years. Possess a technology-based solution or business model at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7–9. Provide evidence that the innovation is beyond the MVP (Minimum Viable Product) stage. Have at least one team leader under the age of 35. Commit to active participation throughout the entire programme. Have a solution directly addressing agrifood challenges in SIDS or already piloted in island environments. Important Notes Teams from outside SIDS are fully eligible to apply. Preference will be given to teams originating from or led by individuals from SIDS. Teams with female agripreneurs are strongly encouraged to apply. Only one application per applicant will be accepted. The final submission will be considered the official application. Programme Activities and International Exposure Selected teams will participate in several international activities designed to strengthen their innovations and visibility. Innovation for Good Workshops Finalists will receive coaching, mentorship, and capacity-building support through specialized workshops focused on innovation scaling, pitching, and agrifood entrepreneurship. Global Final Pitch Event in Hangzhou, China Finalists will travel to Hangzhou, China in August 2026 to present their solutions before international experts, investors, policymakers, and stakeholders. This stage offers substantial global exposure and networking opportunities. FAO Science and Innovation Forum Showcase in Rome, Italy Outstanding teams may also be showcased during the FAO Science and Innovation Forum in Rome in October 2026, further increasing international recognition and partnership opportunities. Key Benefits for Finalists and Winners Participants selected for the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 can expect numerous benefits, including: Global visibility and recognition International networking opportunities Access to investors and technical experts Mentorship and coaching support Participation in global innovation workshops Exposure to policymakers and development partners Opportunities for collaboration and partnerships Inclusion in long-term alumni activities Potential international showcase opportunities The challenge provides a strong platform for scaling innovative agrifood solutions globally. Working Languages The official working languages for GAC 2026 are: English Chinese However: All proposals must be submitted in English. All presentations must also be conducted in English. Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 Timeline Key Dates Date Activity 19 May – 20 June 2026 Open Call for Applications 18 June – 30 June 2026 Preliminary Round Selection 2 July 2026 Announcement of Top 13 Finalists July 2026 Remote Preparation and Coaching August 2026 Innovation for Good Workshops and Global Final Pitch Event in Hangzhou 12 – 16 October 2026 FAO Science and Innovation Forum Showcase in Rome 2027 onwards Alumni Network Activities Why Agrifood Startups Should Apply The Global AgriInno Challenge is more than a competition. It is a strategic opportunity for young innovators to gain access to: International markets Global investors Policy stakeholders Technical mentorship International recognition High-level innovation ecosystems For startups working in climate-smart agriculture, food systems, aquaculture, fisheries, rural livelihoods, nutrition, environmental sustainability, and digital agriculture, this challenge offers a unique platform to scale impact globally. Innovators already working in African island contexts, Caribbean nations, Pacific islands, and other vulnerable coastal environments may find this opportunity especially relevant. Data Protection and Privacy According to the organizers, FAO processes all personal and non-personal data in line with its internal Data Protection Policy and procedures. The organization emphasizes: Fair data processing Transparency Security Integrity Responsible handling of information Applicants are encouraged to review the official privacy policies before submitting applications. title: NASA Creator Proposals 2026: Opportunity for Filmmakers, Storytellers, Songwriters, Poets and Documentarians to Partner with NASA
summary: NASA has opened an exciting opportunity for creative professionals who want to help tell the stories behind some of the agency’s most ambitious missions and innovations. As NASA continues to push the boundaries of space exploration, aviation research, nuclear propulsion, and lunar missions, the agency is inviting creators to submit proposals for potential partnerships that will help bring these mission stories to wider audiences. This opportunity is designed for filmmakers, documentarians, songwriters, storytellers, poets, and other creative professionals who can develop powerful content around NASA’s work. Through this call, NASA is looking for partners who can communicate the agency’s missions in compelling, accessible, educational, and inspiring ways. NASA published the Announcement for Proposals on May 21 and is inviting eligible creators to submit their proposals by Tuesday, June 30 . About the NASA Creator Proposals Opportunity The NASA Creator Proposals opportunity is part of the agency’s wider effort to share the human stories, technical achievements, scientific goals, and future possibilities connected to its missions. NASA is currently working on major programs that could shape the future of space exploration and aviation. These include the Artemis Moon missions, the development of future lunar infrastructure, nuclear propulsion technologies, missions connected to Mars exploration, and advanced aeronautics research. Through this opportunity, NASA wants creative partners who can help translate these complex missions into stories that the public can understand, appreciate, and engage with. In this initial round, NASA is seeking up to 10 partners through unfunded Space Act Agreements . These partnerships will allow selected creators to work with NASA in sharing stories, insights, and educational content related to selected agency missions and programs. What NASA Is Looking For NASA is looking for creators who can present strong storytelling ideas connected to the agency’s missions and innovation areas. Eligible creative professionals may include: Filmmakers Documentarians Songwriters Storytellers Poets Creative producers Multimedia creators Other content creators with strong storytelling proposals The agency is especially interested in proposals that can help communicate the stories behind NASA’s missions, not just the technical details. This means applicants should think about how their creative work can explain the significance, challenges, human effort, innovation, and future impact of NASA’s work. NASA Mission Areas Covered by This Opportunity NASA has identified several areas of focus for this opportunity. Applicants can submit proposals connected to one or more of these mission areas. 1. Artemis Program and Future Moon Missions One of the major focus areas is NASA’s Artemis program. The Artemis program is NASA’s effort to return humans to the Moon and prepare for future deep space exploration. Through Artemis, NASA aims to establish a long-term human presence on and around the Moon while developing the knowledge, technologies, and systems needed for future missions to Mars. The opportunity mentions several Artemis-related areas, including: The Artemis program as a whole The recently added Artemis III mission in 2027 The Artemis IV lunar landing in 2028 NASA’s plans to develop a Moon Base Broader stories connected to lunar exploration and future human presence on the Moon Creators interested in space exploration, human achievement, science communication, lunar missions, and the future of humanity beyond Earth may find this area especially suitable. 2. Nuclear Propulsion and Mars Exploration NASA is also inviting proposals connected to its advancement of nuclear propulsion. Nuclear propulsion is an important area of future space exploration because it could support faster and more efficient travel beyond Earth orbit. This technology could play a key role in future missions to Mars and other deep space destinations. The announcement specifically mentions NASA’s nuclear propulsion work, including: The Space Reactor-1 Freedom mission to Mars in 2028 The Skyfall payload Broader innovation in nuclear propulsion for future space missions This focus area may be ideal for creators interested in futuristic technology, engineering, Mars exploration, science storytelling, and the next generation of space travel. 3. NASA Aeronautics and Aviation Innovation NASA’s work is not limited to space exploration. The agency is also involved in cutting-edge aviation research and aeronautics innovation. Through flight tests and other aviation-focused efforts, NASA continues to contribute to the future of air travel, aircraft performance, flight safety, sustainability, and advanced aviation technology. Creators may submit proposals focused on NASA’s aviation work, including: Flight tests Aeronautics research Advanced aircraft concepts Innovation in aviation technology Stories behind NASA’s work in improving air travel and flight systems This area may appeal to creators interested in aviation, engineering, technology, climate-conscious transport innovation, and the future of flight. Nature of the Partnership Selected creators will enter into unfunded Space Act Agreements with NASA. This means the opportunity is a partnership arrangement rather than a traditional funded grant. NASA is not offering direct funding under this opportunity. Instead, selected partners may receive collaboration opportunities that could include access to NASA expertise, facilities, personnel, mission insights, or other support depending on the approved proposal and NASA’s needs. Applicants should clearly explain what kind of support they need from NASA to carry out their project. Possible needs may include: Access to NASA facilities Access to NASA personnel Interviews with mission teams Technical background information Mission-related insights Coordination support Visual, educational, or archival resources where available Other specific support required to complete the proposed creative work Applicants should also clearly explain their own funding and distribution plans. What Proposals Should Include NASA has stated that proposals should include clear details about the applicant’s area of focus, funding arrangements, distribution approach, and specific needs from the agency. A strong proposal should likely explain: The mission area of interest Applicants should state whether they want to focus on Artemis, Moon missions, nuclear propulsion, Mars-related innovation, aeronautics, or another NASA mission area. The creative concept Applicants should describe the story they want to tell and why it matters. The format of the project This may include a film, documentary, song, poetry project, storytelling series, digital media project, educational content, or another creative format. The intended audience Applicants should explain who the project is designed for, such as students, general audiences, science enthusiasts, educators, families, young people, or global audiences. Funding arrangements Since this is an unfunded partnership, applicants should explain how the project will be financed or supported. Distribution arrangements Applicants should explain how the final creative work will reach audiences. This may include film festivals, streaming platforms, social media, schools, museums, public events, media outlets, or digital platforms. Specific support needed from NASA Applicants should be clear about any access, interviews, facilities, personnel, or mission information they need from NASA. Production timeline A clear timeline can help NASA understand whether the project is realistic and achievable. Experience and capacity Applicants should show that they have the skills, creative experience, or team capacity needed to deliver the proposed project. Who Can Apply? This opportunity is primarily focused on U.S. creators . However, NASA has indicated that it will consider proposals that include a minority of international participants . This means international creators may be included as part of a proposal, but the opportunity is mainly intended for U.S.-based creators or U.S.-led creative teams. Applicants should review the full requirements carefully before submitting. Why This Opportunity Matters NASA’s missions are some of the most important scientific and technological efforts in the world. However, these missions are not only about rockets, aircraft, spacecraft, engineering systems, or scientific instruments. They are also about people, imagination, discovery, risk, innovation, and the future of humanity. Creative professionals play an important role in helping the public connect emotionally and intellectually with science and exploration. Through storytelling, film, music, poetry, documentary work, and multimedia content, creators can help audiences understand: Why NASA’s missions matter How space exploration benefits humanity What challenges scientists and engineers are solving How aviation and space technology affect everyday life What the future of the Moon, Mars, and deep space exploration may look like How young people can be inspired to pursue science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics This opportunity gives creators a chance to help shape how the public experiences and understands NASA’s next chapter. Deadline for Applications The deadline to submit proposals is Tuesday, June 30 . Interested applicants are encouraged to review the full requirements and prepare a detailed proposal before the deadline. Application Link Full requirements and application details are available here: https://go.nasa.gov/CreatorProposals Contact Information For further information, applicants may contact: Camille Gallo NASA Headquarters, Washington Phone: 202-358-1600 Email: camille.m.gallo@nasa.gov Cheryl Warner NASA Headquarters, Washington Phone: 202-358-1600 Email: cheryl.m.warner@nasa.gov Final Thoughts The NASA Creator Proposals 2026 opportunity is a unique chance for creative professionals to partner with one of the world’s leading space and aeronautics agencies. Whether through film, documentary, music, poetry, storytelling, or multimedia production, selected creators will have the opportunity to help communicate the stories behind NASA’s missions and innovations. For creators passionate about space exploration, science communication, aviation, the Moon, Mars, and the future of humanity, this opportunity offers a powerful platform to contribute to public understanding and inspiration. Applicants should prepare strong, clear, and realistic proposals that explain their creative vision, distribution plan, funding arrangements, and the support they would need from NASA. Deadline: Tuesday, June 30 APPLY HERE. For more information about this opportunity click here. Discover more proposal writing opportunities on OFY here. title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Quantitative Political Science at the University of Oxford (Voter ID Project)
summary: The University of Oxford invites applications for the prestigious role of Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Quantitative Political Science , contributing to the ESRC‑funded Voter ID Project led by Principal Investigator Prof Petra Schleiter . This full‑time, fixed‑term position offers an exceptional opportunity to join one of the world’s most respected political science research environments and contribute to cutting‑edge work on electoral behaviour, voter identification policies, and democratic participation in the United Kingdom. This role is based within the Department of Politics and International Relations (DPIR) , one of the largest and most influential political science departments globally. The successful candidate will work closely with a distinguished research team, including co‑investigators Prof Margit Tavits and Prof Jonathan Homola , and will engage deeply with experimental survey design, advanced quantitative analysis, and policy‑relevant research dissemination. Application Deadline: 12 noon (UK time) on Friday, 26 June 2026 About the Voter ID Project The ESRC‑funded Voter ID Project investigates the effects of introducing mandatory photo identification in the UK—a country without national ID cards. The research integrates multiple data sources and methodologies to understand how voter ID requirements shape political behaviour, attitudes, and participation. The project includes three major components: Original surveys with embedded experiments Designed to measure behavioural and attitudinal responses to voter ID requirements. Historical data from Northern Ireland Examining the introduction of voter ID in the early 2000s. Data from the English voter ID trials (2018–2019) Providing comparative insights into turnout, postal voting, and demographic impacts. A new and significant strand of the project focuses on young voters , including those aged 16–17 , to understand how voter ID policies influence the youngest cohort of current and future voters. Key Responsibilities The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will play a central role across all strands of the project. Responsibilities include: 1. Experimental Research Design and Survey Management Contributing to the design of experimental research. Coding and testing survey instruments. Monitoring data collection and quotas in collaboration with survey firms. Conducting data quality checks. 2. Methodological Development Adapting existing methodologies and developing new ones tailored to the project’s data. Advising team members on methodological and procedural matters. 3. Data Analysis Analysing original survey data. Working with historical voter ID data from Northern Ireland. Examining turnout, postal voting, and related electoral datasets. 4. Dissemination and Policy Engagement Presenting findings at conferences. Contributing to world‑class publications. Preparing policy briefs. Supporting engagement with policymakers, including: The Electoral Commission The Department for Housing, Levelling Up and Communities House of Commons Committee Clerks 5. Project Administration Assisting with grant applications. Organising workshops and conferences. Managing personal research activities and workload. 6. Required Training Upon Appointment New staff must complete training in: Information Security and Data Protection Implicit Bias Bullying and Harassment Equality and Diversity Harassment in Higher Education Selection Criteria Essential Qualifications and Experience Applicants must demonstrate: A completed or near‑completed doctorate in political science or a related field. Experience with survey experiments, survey design, and survey data analysis. Expertise in advanced quantitative methods and research design. Proficiency in R . Strong understanding of UK electoral politics. Ability to publish in leading political science journals. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion. Evidence of good citizenship and willingness to contribute to administrative tasks. Ability to critically evaluate recent trends in the field. Desirable Attributes Experience collaborating on research articles for publication. About the University of Oxford The University of Oxford is a global leader in research and education, known for its commitment to innovation, academic excellence, and societal impact. Oxford fosters a diverse, inclusive, and supportive environment where scholars thrive and contribute to global knowledge. The University is: A top institution for research excellence. A leader in entrepreneurship, producing 15–20 spin‑out companies annually. Home to world‑class cultural, academic, and professional resources. About the Social Sciences Division Oxford’s Social Sciences Division is a powerhouse of interdisciplinary research, supporting scholars through: Research development guidance Funding opportunities Project design and management support Career development resources About the Department of Politics and International Relations (DPIR) DPIR is one of the world’s most respected political science departments, ranked #1 in the UK by The Guardian (2024). With around 90 academic staff, the department hosts major research projects, postdoctoral researchers, and a vibrant academic community. The department is committed to: Equality, diversity, and inclusion Applying for the Athena Swan Bronze Award Supporting staff wellbeing Providing a collaborative and dynamic research environment Benefits of Working at Oxford Oxford offers an exceptional benefits package, including: 38 days of paid holiday Generous pension schemes Travel discounts Professional development opportunities Free entry to University museums and gardens Discounted access to sports facilities Childcare support and family‑friendly policies Staff networks for BME, LGBT+, disabled staff, and researchers Support for relocation and visa applications How to Apply Applications must be submitted through Oxford’s online recruitment portal. Applicants must upload: A CV A supporting statement addressing each selection criterion Details of two referees All documents must be submitted as PDFs.
