title: University of Florence PhD Programmes 2026/2027 in Italy: Fully Funded Doctoral Opportunities with Scholarships, International Support, and Research Funding
summary: The University of Florence has officially opened applications for its prestigious XLII Cycle PhD Programmes for the 2026/2027 academic year. Hosted in one of Italy’s most renowned academic institutions, these doctoral programmes provide exceptional opportunities for students and researchers from around the world to pursue advanced research across multiple disciplines while benefiting from scholarships, international mobility support, and access to a vibrant academic environment. The call for applications includes several doctoral programmes headquartered at the University of Florence, with positions available both with and without scholarships. The programmes are scheduled to begin on November 1, 2026, and applications must be submitted before the official deadline of June 11, 2026. For international students, especially those interested in pursuing doctoral studies in Europe, this is an outstanding opportunity to study in Italy while engaging in world-class research and academic collaboration. About the University of Florence PhD Programmes The University of Florence is one of Italy’s oldest and most respected universities, known for its strong research culture, international collaborations, and commitment to academic excellence. The XLII Cycle PhD Programmes are designed to: Develop advanced research skills Promote scientific innovation Encourage international academic cooperation Prepare researchers for academic and professional careers Foster multidisciplinary and multicultural research environments These doctoral programmes are governed by the Italian Ministry of University and Research (MUR) and are subject to accreditation procedures in accordance with Ministerial Decree no. 226/2021. Duration of the PhD Programmes The duration of the doctoral programmes is: 3 years full-time Planned start date: November 1, 2026 Students admitted to the programmes are expected to undertake continuous research and academic activities throughout the doctoral cycle. Fields and Research Areas The call covers multiple PhD programmes hosted by the University of Florence. The specific research areas, available scholarships, reserved positions, and admission procedures are outlined in Annex 2 of the official call. Depending on the programme selected, candidates may engage in research areas such as: Engineering Sciences Humanities Social sciences Technology Health sciences Environmental studies Artificial intelligence Cybersecurity Space research International studies Economics Arts and culture Some scholarships are linked to specific research topics and funded by external organizations or public institutions. Number of Available Positions and Scholarships The University of Florence offers: Multiple doctoral positions Scholarship-funded positions Positions without scholarships Reserved positions for specific categories Additional positions that may become available later The number of available positions may increase if additional scholarship funding becomes available before enrolment. Some scholarships are funded by: Public institutions Private organizations Italian Space Agency (ASI) National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) International research entities Scholarship Benefits The PhD scholarships offered by the University of Florence provide substantial financial support to selected candidates. Annual Scholarship Amount The annual scholarship amount is: €16,243 per year (before social security charges) The scholarship is paid monthly in arrears. Additional Financial Benefits In addition to the annual scholarship, PhD students may receive several other financial advantages. 1. Research Abroad Funding Increase Students conducting research activities abroad can receive: A 50% increase in scholarship funding This support is available for: Up to 12 months abroad Up to 18 months for co-supervised international doctoral programmes 2. Research Budget Each doctoral student receives: A research budget equal to at least 10% of the scholarship amount This funding supports: Research activities Academic travel Conference participation Research materials Specialized training 3. One-Off Financial Support for International Students To encourage international participation, the University of Florence, supported by the Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, offers: One-off financial support of up to €5,000 This support targets international doctoral students meeting specific criteria. Who Can Receive the €5,000 International Support? The one-off grant is intended for candidates who: Reside in a non-EU country Hold a foreign qualification for PhD access Are under 35 years old Importantly: No separate application is required Beneficiaries are selected automatically The grant may be combined with scholarships If funds remain available, the support may also extend to: EU residents studying abroad Candidates with degrees obtained outside Tuscany Eligibility Criteria The University of Florence welcomes applicants from all nationalities without age or citizenship restrictions for the main PhD competition. Eligible applicants include candidates holding: A Master’s degree under Ministerial Decree 270/2004 A Master’s degree under Ministerial Decree 509/1999 A pre-509/1999 Italian degree lasting at least four years A second-level AFAM academic degree An equivalent foreign academic qualification Applicants Completing Degrees Later Students who will complete their degrees before the programme start date may also apply. However: They must submit proof of graduation within 10 days after obtaining the qualification Failure to submit documentation leads to exclusion Admission Process Admission to the doctoral programmes involves a competitive selection procedure. Depending on the programme, the selection may include: Evaluation of academic qualifications Assessment of research proposals Written examinations Oral interviews Preliminary screening Language proficiency assessments Interview Options For programmes allowing online interviews: Candidates may participate by videoconference This option must be selected during application The interview may also assess: English proficiency Other foreign language skills Italian language knowledge for foreign applicants Application Process Applications must be submitted exclusively through the online platform. Official application portal: University of Florence PhD Application Portal Required Documents Applicants must upload: For Italian Degrees Identity document Self-declaration of academic records Thesis title and grades For Foreign Degrees Bachelor’s and Master’s degree copies Academic transcripts Grading scale Thesis title and graduation score Certified translations into English or Italian Additional documents may be required depending on the doctoral programme. Application Fee Applicants must pay: €30 non-refundable application fee A separate fee is required for each doctoral programme application. Important Application Deadline Deadline: June 11, 2026 at 12:00 noon (Italian time) The university strongly advises applicants to submit applications well in advance because the online system automatically closes at the deadline. Important Dates Application Opening May 12, 2026 Ranking Publication By July 31, 2026 Enrolment Deadline for Successful Candidates August 25, 2026 Programme Start Date November 1, 2026 International Student Information International students from non-EU countries must: Register through the Universitaly portal Apply for an Italian study visa Provide translated and legalized academic documents Accepted documentation may include: Declaration of Value CIMEA Statements of Comparability and Verification Diploma Supplement for EU degrees Attendance Requirements PhD students must: Attend full-time Conduct continuous research activities Participate in academic training Complete international mobility requirements Earn complementary skills credits Intellectual Property and Research Publications The University of Florence protects: Intellectual property rights Industrial property rights Research publication rights Doctoral students may also be required to sign confidentiality agreements regarding research and institutional information. Why You Should Apply The University of Florence PhD Programmes provide a remarkable opportunity to: Study in Italy Conduct advanced international research Receive generous financial support Join a multicultural academic environment Build international research networks Access European academic opportunities Advance careers in academia, research, and innovation For students seeking a prestigious European doctoral experience, this programme offers excellent academic, professional, and financial advantages. Official Call and Information Applicants can access the official programme details through the University of Florence website: University of Florence Official PhD Call Page Apply here Learn More For more information about this opportunity, Click here More global Scholarship opportunities for youth, visit the OFY website: Click here The post University of Florence PhD Programmes 2026/2027 in Italy: Fully Funded Doctoral Opportunities with Scholarships, International Support, and Research Funding appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Estonia in UN Internship Fall 2026 in New York: Monthly Allowance Opportunity for EU Students Interested in Diplomacy and International Affairs
summary: The Permanent Mission of Estonia to the United Nations has officially announced its Internship Fall 2026 opportunity in New York, offering students and young professionals an exceptional chance to gain practical diplomatic experience at the heart of global policymaking. This prestigious internship program allows selected candidates to work directly with Estonian diplomats at the United Nations headquarters while contributing to important international discussions on climate policy, human rights, peace and security, humanitarian affairs, development, and institutional reforms. For students passionate about international relations, diplomacy, global governance, public policy, law, development cooperation, or multilateral negotiations, this internship provides valuable exposure to the daily operations of a Permanent Mission to the United Nations. The internship is based in New York City, operates full-time at 40 hours per week, and includes a monthly allowance to support interns during their placement. Why the Estonia in UN Internship 2026 Is a Unique Opportunity Interning at the Permanent Mission of Estonia to the United Nations offers participants direct exposure to international diplomacy and multilateral cooperation. Interns become part of a professional diplomatic environment where they support Estonia’s engagement with the UN system and contribute to discussions on major global issues affecting countries worldwide. This internship is particularly valuable for students aiming to build careers in: International relations Diplomacy Public policy Human rights advocacy Peace and security International development International law Climate governance Humanitarian affairs Global governance institutions Interns will work alongside experienced diplomats and policy experts while developing research, analytical, negotiation-monitoring, and communication skills that are highly valued in international careers. About the Permanent Mission of Estonia to the United Nations The Permanent Mission of Estonia to the UN represents Estonia’s interests within the United Nations system. The Mission actively participates in UN negotiations, policy discussions, international cooperation initiatives, and multilateral decision-making processes. Located in New York City, the Mission engages in global discussions on: Peace and international security Human rights Sustainable development Climate change Humanitarian response Legal affairs UN reforms and administration The internship program allows participants to observe and contribute to these high-level international processes firsthand. Internship Responsibilities Selected interns will support the Mission’s delegates and diplomatic staff in several important areas. Interns will actively participate in the Mission’s daily work and gain real-world diplomatic experience. Responsibilities include: 1. Supporting UN Meetings and Negotiations Interns will assist Mission delegates in preparing for and following important UN meetings, negotiations, and policy discussions. Tasks may include: Preparing meeting briefs Attending UN sessions Taking notes during negotiations Summarizing key developments Assisting with follow-up documentation 2. Monitoring UN Proceedings Interns will monitor discussions and developments within the UN system related to Estonia’s foreign policy priorities and areas of interest. This may involve: Tracking resolutions Following committee discussions Reporting policy developments Monitoring voting outcomes Identifying emerging diplomatic issues 3. Conducting Policy Research Research is a major component of the internship. Interns will help diplomats by preparing background analyses and policy documents. Research assignments may include: Comparative policy analysis International legal research Human rights monitoring Climate and development policy reviews Geopolitical analysis 4. Drafting Briefing Notes and Reports Interns will contribute to the drafting of: Briefing notes Policy memos Analytical reports Meeting summaries Diplomatic background papers This helps interns strengthen their professional writing and policy communication skills. 5. Working Across Specialized Policy Areas Interns may contribute to one or several policy portfolios depending on their academic background, interests, and skills. Available Policy Areas Applicants are encouraged to indicate their preferred policy area(s) in their motivation letter. The available areas include: Climate Policy Work on issues related to environmental governance, climate negotiations, sustainability, and global climate commitments. Development Policy Support initiatives focused on sustainable development, international cooperation, poverty reduction, and global development agendas. Human Rights Contribute to discussions and monitoring related to international human rights mechanisms and protections. Humanitarian Affairs Engage with global humanitarian response issues, emergency assistance, and crisis coordination. Legal Affairs Assist with legal analysis related to international law, treaties, UN resolutions, and diplomatic procedures. Peace Security Follow discussions concerning conflict prevention, peacekeeping, international security, and geopolitical developments. UN Administration Reforms Support work linked to institutional reform, governance modernization, and efficiency within the UN system. Eligibility Criteria To qualify for the Estonia in UN Internship Fall 2026, applicants must meet several important requirements. Candidates should: Be enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree program at a higher education institution Demonstrate strong analytical and research skills Show commitment to multilateral cooperation and international diplomacy Possess creativity and problem-solving abilities Have an open-minded, curious, and positive attitude Be fluent in English Have knowledge of another UN official language (considered an advantage) Be eligible for and able to maintain security clearance by Estonian authorities Important Language Advantage Although English fluency is mandatory, applicants who speak additional UN official languages may have an advantage during the selection process. Additional languages may include: French Spanish Arabic Chinese Russian Internship Duration and Work Schedule The internship generally lasts between 3 and 4 months. Key details include: Start period: September 2026 and throughout the year Workload: 40 hours per week Format: On-site in New York City Number of positions: Multiple openings available The exact internship dates will be agreed upon during the selection process. Financial Information The internship is technically unpaid; however, selected interns receive a monthly allowance. Applicants should note that interns remain responsible for: Accommodation costs Daily living expenses Travel costs Health and personal insurance The Permanent Mission of Estonia will assist selected candidates with the U.S. visa application process. Benefits of the Estonia UN Internship Participating in this internship offers numerous professional and academic benefits. Key Benefits Include: Direct exposure to international diplomacy Hands-on experience within the United Nations system Opportunity to work with experienced diplomats Practical policy research experience Networking opportunities in global affairs Development of analytical and communication skills Exposure to high-level international negotiations Experience living and working in New York City Monthly financial allowance Enhanced career prospects in international organizations How to Apply Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, meaning interested candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible. Applicants must send: A detailed CV A motivation letter The motivation letter should clearly indicate: Preferred policy area(s) Availability period Relevant academic or professional interests Applications should be submitted via email to: mission.newyork@mfa.ee Application Deadline There is no fixed deadline mentioned for this opportunity because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Early application is strongly recommended. Official Opportunity Link For more details about the internship opportunity, applicants can visit the official Estonia in UN page: Estonia in UN Internship Fall 2026 Official Page Final Thoughts The Estonia in UN Internship Fall 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for EU students seeking real-world diplomatic experience inside one of the world’s most influential international institutions. From policy analysis and multilateral negotiations to global governance and peacebuilding, interns will gain meaningful exposure to the inner workings of international diplomacy. For ambitious students interested in shaping global policy and pursuing careers within the United Nations, international organizations, foreign ministries, NGOs, or development institutions, this internship can serve as a strong foundation for future success. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Send your CV and motivation letter, including your preferred policy area(s) and availability to: mission.newyork@mfa.ee Learn More For more information about this opportunity, Click here More global Internship opportunities for youth, visit the OFY website: Click here The post Estonia in UN Internship Fall 2026 in New York: Monthly Allowance Opportunity for EU Students Interested in Diplomacy and International Affairs appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: UNDP Youth4Climate Mentorship Programme 2026: Global Call for Climate Experts, Entrepreneurs, Investors, and Professionals to Mentor Youth-Led Climate Innovators
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), through the Youth4Climate initiative, has officially launched a global call for mentors for the Youth4Climate Mentorship Programme 2026. This international opportunity is inviting experienced professionals from across the world to support youth-led climate innovators through mentorship, technical guidance, masterclasses, ecosystem connections, and scale-up support. The mentorship programme is designed to connect young climate leaders with experienced professionals who can provide practical expertise, strategic insights, and real-world guidance to help youth-led climate projects grow sustainably and achieve long-term impact. Selected mentors will participate in a six-month engagement running from June 2026 to December 2026 and will become part of a global ecosystem focused on accelerating youth-driven climate action, innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development. Professionals with expertise in climate finance, entrepreneurship, clean energy, sustainability, digital innovation, fundraising, impact measurement, communications, and business development are strongly encouraged to apply before the application deadline of May 18, 2026 at 23:59 CEST. The programme provides young climate innovators with: Funding opportunities Mentorship Learning resources Visibility Networking opportunities Ecosystem support Capacity development The initiative aims to empower young people who are building innovative climate solutions capable of addressing some of the world’s most urgent environmental and sustainability challenges. Between 2023 and 2025, Youth4Climate supported numerous youth-led projects focused on: Renewable energy Climate-smart agriculture Circular economy solutions Waste management Sustainable food systems Digital climate innovation Nature-based solutions The programme recognizes that funding alone is not enough to ensure long-term impact. As a result, the mentorship programme was developed to ensure awardees gain access to experienced professionals, strategic guidance, technical support, and networks that can help them scale their initiatives effectively. The programme focuses on helping youth-led projects strengthen: Project implementation Operational systems Strategic planning Investment readiness Business development Sustainability pathways Growth and scale-up potential Mentors will support young innovators working across several climate and sustainability sectors and thematic areas. Mandatory Commitment Selected mentors are expected to: Commit a minimum of 2 hours per month Schedule mentorship sessions flexibly based on availability Provide tailored support and practical guidance Help mentees navigate implementation and growth challenges The mentorship arrangement is intentionally flexible to accommodate professionals from different industries and time zones. Masterclasses Mentors may lead group learning sessions covering topics such as: Climate innovation Entrepreneurship Communications Operational readiness Business growth Fundraising Sustainability strategies These sessions are designed to help awardees gain practical knowledge and industry insights. 2. Theory in Practice Talks Experienced professionals will share: Real-world experiences Lessons learned Growth journeys Scaling strategies Practical industry insights The goal is to expose youth innovators to practical examples from successful climate and development practitioners. 3. Investor Showcases and Scaling Pathways Mentors may also support advanced projects by helping them: Improve business models Strengthen investor pitches Increase investment readiness Develop scaling strategies Build strategic partnerships This component is particularly valuable for youth-led startups and scalable climate enterprises. Why Professionals Should Join the Youth4Climate Mentorship Programme The programme offers mentors the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to global climate action while expanding their professional networks and visibility. Key Benefits of Becoming a Mentor 1. Support Real Climate Solutions Mentors will directly contribute to projects addressing: Climate resilience Renewable energy Food security Sustainable agriculture Circular economy innovation Community sustainability 2. Join a Global Network Participants will connect with: Climate experts UNDP stakeholders Entrepreneurs Investors Researchers Innovation leaders Sustainability practitioners 3. Gain Visibility and Recognition Mentors will gain visibility through participation in a globally recognized UNDP-backed initiative supporting youth innovation and climate action. 4. Contribute to Youth Empowerment The programme allows professionals to directly support the next generation of climate leaders and changemakers. 5. Flexible Engagement Structure The mentorship structure is designed to accommodate busy professionals with: Flexible scheduling Limited monthly time requirements Multiple engagement pathways Who Can Apply? UNDP is seeking experienced professionals from diverse sectors and industries. Eligible Professionals Include: Climate experts Entrepreneurs Corporate leaders Investors Academics Researchers Development professionals Sustainability practitioners Technical experts Innovation specialists Required Experience Applicants must have: At least 5 years of relevant work experience Expertise in one or more relevant climate or development fields Prior mentorship experience is welcomed but not mandatory. title: Wellcome Accelerator Awards 2026: Funding Opportunity for Early and Mid-Career Researchers of Black, Bangladeshi, and Pakistani Heritage in the United Kingdom
summary: The Wellcome Accelerator Awards is a targeted funding initiative designed to support early-career and mid-career researchers in the United Kingdom who identify as being from Black, Bangladeshi, or Pakistani heritage backgrounds. The scheme is delivered by Wellcome and aims to address underrepresentation in research funding while strengthening career progression within academia and health-related research fields. This award provides flexible financial and professional development support to help researchers advance to the next stage of their academic or research careers. It allows recipients to engage in research and research-adjacent activities such as training, secondments, networking, and pilot research projects. Overview of the Wellcome Accelerator Awards The Accelerator Awards are structured to provide both financial support and career development opportunities for researchers working within the UK research ecosystem. The scheme runs annually until 2028 and is highly competitive, focusing on career progression and research impact. Key Funding Details Funding body: Wellcome Funding duration: Up to 2 years Funding amount: Up to £200,000 for project expenses plus salary (if required) Application deadline: 25 August 2026 at 15:00 BST Webinar date: 2 June 2026 at 14:00 BST Application platform: Wellcome Funding Platform Award frequency: Annual (until 2028) Co-applicants: Not permitted Purpose of the Award The Wellcome Accelerator Awards are designed to: Address inequalities in research funding access Support career progression for underrepresented researchers Strengthen academic and research leadership pathways Enable researchers to build competitive profiles for future funding opportunities Support both research and career development activities By the end of the award period, researchers are expected to be better positioned for promotions, major research grants, and leadership roles in academia or research institutions. Eligibility Criteria To apply for the Wellcome Accelerator Awards, applicants must meet strict eligibility requirements. 1. Heritage Requirement Applicants must self-identify as being from one of the following backgrounds: Black heritage (including mixed Black heritage such as Black African, Black Caribbean, or other Black backgrounds) Bangladeshi heritage (including mixed Bangladeshi heritage) Pakistani heritage (including mixed Pakistani heritage) 2. Location Requirement Applicants must: Be currently working in or ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom Hold a position at a UK-based administering organisation 3. Academic and Research Training Requirement Applicants must have completed a substantive period of research training, such as: A PhD or equivalent higher research degree OR completion of a PhD viva by the deadline (if still studying) OR at least four years of equivalent research experience (for non-PhD pathways) Additionally, applicants must have: An undergraduate degree or PhD awarded by a UK institution 4. Employment and Career Stage Conditions Applicants must: Be early-career or mid-career researchers Have been appointed to a permanent or long-term role within the last 3 years (with some exceptions for career breaks, part-time work, or clinical roles) Not hold another active Wellcome award as a lead applicant 5. Time Commitment Requirements At least 80% of research time must be dedicated to the grant Salary-supported applicants should limit non-research duties to: Maximum 20% (general roles) Up to 40% for clinical specialists Scope of Activities Funded The award is highly flexible and supports both research and career-building activities. Eligible Research Activities Pilot studies and proof-of-concept research Scoping studies and preliminary data collection Writing research papers or grant applications Collaborative research projects Eligible Research-Adjacent Activities Advanced skills training and professional development courses Research secondments (UK or international) Networking activities and academic conferences Industry or NGO placements (e.g., pharmaceutical companies or research organizations) Collaborative research meetings Funding Coverage The award may cover a wide range of costs, including: Salary support (if requested) Research materials and consumables Travel and fieldwork expenses Equipment and access charges Training and career development costs Open access publication fees Clinical research costs (where applicable) Overheads and institutional support costs Relocation and overseas allowances Public engagement and patient involvement activities Application Process Step 1: Preparation Applicants must prepare: Career goals and long-term vision Detailed project plan Skills development plan Budget justification Step 2: Submission Applications must be submitted via the Wellcome Funding Platform and approved by the host institution. title: Multilingual AI for Health Challenge 2026: Build AI Systems for African Languages and Win Up to $5,000 USD
summary: Access to reliable healthcare information remains one of the biggest challenges across many African communities, particularly in underserved and low-resource settings where language barriers limit access to accurate medical guidance. To address this gap, the Multilingual Health Question Answering in Low-Resource African Languages Challenge has officially launched on Zindi, inviting AI innovators, developers, researchers, machine learning engineers, and language technology enthusiasts to build multilingual AI systems capable of answering health-related questions in African languages. The challenge is organized in collaboration with the Hub for Artificial Intelligence in Maternal, Sexual and Reproductive Health (HASH) and focuses specifically on maternal, sexual, and reproductive health information in African communities. Participants will work on creating AI models that can understand and generate accurate, fluent, and culturally appropriate responses in languages such as Akan, Kiswahili, Luganda, and Amharic. The competition offers a total prize pool of $5,000 USD and is fully online, making it accessible to participants from across the globe. Why This Challenge Matters Despite the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and natural language processing technologies, most large language models are still heavily trained on English and other high-resource languages. As a result, millions of African language speakers remain underserved by AI-powered healthcare systems. This challenge seeks to change that reality by encouraging the development of multilingual health assistants capable of supporting African communities in their native languages. Such systems could eventually power: Rural health worker assistants Community healthcare support systems Maternal health education tools Adolescent sexual health platforms HIV and STI awareness systems Clinic support applications Patient education chatbots By enabling people to ask sensitive health questions privately and receive responses in their own language, these AI systems could significantly improve healthcare accessibility, awareness, and informed decision-making across Africa. About the Organizers The challenge is spearheaded by the Hub for Artificial Intelligence in Maternal , Sexual and Reproductive Health ( HASH ), a multidisciplinary consortium bringing together experts in healthcare, public health, artificial intelligence, data science, and social sciences. The consortium includes: Infectious Disease Institute (IDI) Makerere University Makerere Centre for Artificial Intelligence (MAK-AI) Sunbird AI HASH focuses on advancing AI-driven healthcare solutions across Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in areas such as: Maternal health HIV care Sexually transmitted infections Adolescent sexual and reproductive health Their goal is to promote locally grounded AI innovations tailored specifically to African realities and healthcare systems. Challenge Objective Participants are required to build a multilingual AI model capable of: Understanding health-related questions posed in low-resource African languages Generating accurate and contextually appropriate answers Responding fluently in the same language as the question The challenge dataset consists of curated health question-and-answer pairs focused on maternal, sexual, and reproductive health. Competitors are encouraged to use open-source tools, publicly available pretrained models, and freely accessible datasets where applicable. Supported Skills and Technologies This challenge is especially suitable for individuals interested in: Large Language Models (LLMs) Natural Language Processing (NLP) Machine Translation Multilingual AI Low-resource language modeling Deep learning Healthcare AI systems Participants will gain hands-on experience building socially impactful AI technologies for African communities. Prize Pool The challenge offers the following prizes: 1st Prize — $2,500 USD 2nd Prize — $1,500 USD 3rd Prize — $1,000 USD Additionally, participants can earn: 5,000 Zindi points Recognition within the African AI ecosystem Opportunities for collaboration and visibility in AI for healthcare Evaluation Metrics Submissions will be evaluated using a multi-metric scoring system combining lexical overlap, structural similarity, and semantic judgment. ROUGE-1 F1 (37%) Measures overlap of individual words between prediction and reference answers. ROUGE-L F1 (37%) Measures sentence structure similarity using the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS). LLM-as-a-Judge (26%) Uses a language model to evaluate: Factual accuracy Completeness Language appropriateness Overall response quality Top-performing solutions will also undergo additional evaluation using AfroLM BertScore F1, which measures semantic similarity using embeddings from AfroLM : a multilingual transformer pretrained on 23 African languages. Important Rules and Requirements Participants should note the following: Maximum team size: 4 people Fully online participation Open-source tools only No paid services or proprietary tools allowed Automated machine learning tools are prohibited Maximum of 5 submissions per day Maximum of 50 submissions overall Top 10 teams must submit reproducible code and reports Final winners must publicly share their code and models The challenge also enforces strict anti-cheating policies, including penalties and disqualification for multiple accounts, unauthorized collaboration, or unreproducible submissions. Webinar Information Participants are encouraged to register for the official webinar scheduled for: Date: 20 May 2026 Time: 6:00 PM – 7:00 PM GMT+2 The webinar will likely provide guidance on: Dataset structure Evaluation methods Submission process Baseline models Best practices for multilingual healthcare AI systems Deadline Application Deadline: 21 July 2026 Why You Should Participate This challenge is more than a competition. It is an opportunity to contribute to the future of inclusive healthcare technology in Africa. By participating, you can: Build real-world AI solutions with social impact Strengthen your NLP and LLM expertise Gain exposure within the African AI ecosystem Collaborate with innovators across the continent Contribute to healthcare accessibility in underserved communities Compete for international recognition and cash prizes For students, researchers, startups, healthcare innovators, and machine learning engineers passionate about African language technologies, this challenge represents a rare opportunity to combine technical innovation with meaningful impact. Deadline 21st July ,2026. APPLY HERE For more information on this opportunity, click here. For more global opportunities, click here. title: Research Associate in African Democracy and Political Parties at University of Strathclyde (Fully Funded Postdoctoral Opportunity in the UK)
summary: The Department of Government and Public Policy at the prestigious University of Strathclyde is inviting applications for the position of Research Associate under the groundbreaking European Research Council-funded project titled Political Parties in Africa and Democracy (PPADEM). This exciting postdoctoral opportunity is designed for emerging scholars who are passionate about African politics, democratic governance, political institutions, elections, comparative politics, and large-scale empirical research. The role offers successful candidates the chance to join an internationally recognized team of scholars working on one of the largest studies of political parties ever conducted globally. The position is fixed-term for 24 months and provides an excellent platform for early-career academics to build a strong international research profile while contributing to high-impact scholarship on democracy and political parties in Africa. Salary and Employment Details Successful applicants will receive: Salary ranging between £37,694 – £46,049 Full-time employment (35 hours per week) A fixed-term contract lasting 24 months Opportunities for international collaboration and publication Exposure to leading researchers and institutions in African politics and democracy studies Application Deadline 29 May 2026 About the PPADEM Project The Political Parties in Africa and Democracy (PPADEM) project is a major international research collaboration involving: University of Strathclyde Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology University of Bristol University of Reading The project seeks to understand the major drivers behind democratic decline and democratic progress across Africa by conducting the most comprehensive empirical study of political parties ever undertaken. Researchers involved in the project aim to answer critical questions such as: What role do political parties play in democratisation processes in Africa? Under what conditions do political parties strengthen or weaken democracy? How can political parties across Africa be supported to defend and expand democratic governance? Academic Publishing and Conferences Successful applicants will: Present findings at local and international conferences Participate in workshops and scholarly meetings Contribute to co-authored and sole-authored publications Work toward publication in leading peer-reviewed journals 5. Research Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement The Research Associate will: Assist in organizing seminars and project meetings Participate in skills-sharing activities Engage stakeholders and support dissemination of findings Work closely with an international team of senior and early-career scholars Essential Qualifications Applicants must possess: A PhD in Political Science or a closely related social science discipline Strong skills in survey design Strong skills in survey data analysis Expertise in comparative politics The PhD must be completed no later than the date on which the appointment decision is made. Established by the United Nations General Assembly in July 2010, the organization works globally to eliminate discrimination against women and girls while advancing women’s rights, participation, and leadership across all sectors. UN Women’s Strategic Plan 2026–2029 focuses on addressing systemic inequalities through integrated approaches centered around: Women’s leadership and decision-making Women’s economic empowerment Ending violence against women and girls Women, peace, security, and humanitarian action The organization operates through regional offices, country offices, and partnerships with governments, civil society organizations, youth groups, and the private sector. title: Launch to Work: Africa (L2W) 2026 Employability Programme for Young African Graduates
summary: Applications are now open for the Launch to Work: Africa (L2W) 2026 programme, a fully funded employability initiative designed to support young African graduates as they transition from education into the professional world. Developed through a partnership between SOS Children s Villages Worldwide and Industry Immersion Africa , the Launch to Work: Africa programme seeks to bridge the gap between academic achievement and employment opportunities by equipping graduates with workplace skills, professional development support, and internship placements. Unlike many employability initiatives that focus primarily on STEM graduates, L2W is intentionally inclusive and open to graduates from all academic disciplines. The programme recognizes that talent exists across every field of study and aims to create pathways into meaningful employment for young Africans from diverse educational backgrounds. About Launch to Work: Africa (L2W) Launch to Work: Africa was created to address one of the most significant challenges facing graduates across the continent: transitioning successfully from university to employment. While many graduates possess academic qualifications, they often lack access to professional guidance, industry exposure, and practical workplace experience that employers increasingly expect. L2W is designed to help participants build confidence, career clarity, employability skills, and professional readiness through a structured development journey. The programme focuses on preparing graduates not only to secure opportunities but also to succeed in today’s rapidly evolving workplace. What Makes the Programme Different? Many graduate programmes focus heavily on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) disciplines. However, Launch to Work: Africa takes a broader and more inclusive approach. The programme welcomes graduates from all educational backgrounds, recognizing that employability and innovation are not limited to a single academic field. Whether applicants studied: Arts and humanities Social sciences Business Education Technology Communications Health sciences Engineering Or any other accredited discipline they are encouraged to apply if they are motivated to build their careers. Programme Structure The Launch to Work: Africa programme is organized into three key stages designed to support participants throughout their employability journey. 1. Align The Align phase helps participants develop clarity around their professional identity, career goals, strengths, and personal brand. Participants will learn how to: Understand their career interests Position themselves professionally Present their skills effectively to employers Build confidence in workplace environments This stage focuses on helping graduates define who they are professionally and how they can communicate their value in competitive job markets. 2. Launch The Launch stage focuses on practical innovation and workplace readiness skills needed in modern professional environments. Participants will gain exposure to: Innovation and problem-solving Workplace communication Professional collaboration Career readiness training Industry expectations Practical employability skills The programme is designed to prepare graduates for real-world professional challenges rather than only academic success. 3. Employ The final Employ stage provides participants with supported internship placement opportunities. Rather than ending with training alone, the programme helps graduates gain direct workplace exposure through internship experiences that can strengthen their resumes and improve long-term employability. This practical component is one of the programme’s major strengths, offering participants an opportunity to apply their learning in professional settings. Programme Benefits Participants selected for Launch to Work: Africa will benefit from: Fully Funded Participation The programme is completely free for selected participants, removing financial barriers to career development opportunities. Professional Identity Development Graduates receive support in understanding and communicating their professional strengths and career goals. Workplace Readiness Skills Participants gain practical innovation and employability skills relevant to today’s job market. Internship Placement Support The programme includes a supported internship placement component to provide real-world professional experience. Career Confidence and Exposure Participants build confidence, workplace knowledge, and professional networks that can support long-term career growth. Who Should Apply? The programme is ideal for: Recent graduates Young African professionals Individuals seeking their first professional opportunity Graduates struggling to transition into employment Young people looking to strengthen their workplace readiness Applicants from all academic backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Why This Programme Matters Youth unemployment and underemployment remain major challenges across Africa, even among university graduates. Many graduates complete their studies with strong academic credentials but face difficulties entering the workforce due to limited professional exposure, lack of practical experience, or insufficient employability support. Launch to Work: Africa seeks to address these gaps by helping graduates: Build career confidence Gain workplace skills Improve employability Access internship opportunities Transition successfully into professional careers The programme’s inclusive approach also challenges traditional assumptions that career development initiatives should focus only on STEM fields. Application Deadline Applications for the Launch to Work: Africa (L2W) 2026 programme are open until: 3 July 2026 Interested applicants are encouraged to apply early. title: Max Planck Institute Opens Research Positions in Education Inequality and Teacher Politics Under the TICA Project
summary: The Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods and the interdisciplinary research group “Teachers, Inequality and Collective Action” (TICA) are inviting applications for multiple academic research positions beginning in Autumn 2026. Led by Dr. Hania Sobhy , the TICA research group examines teachers as central actors in the transformation and restructuring of public education systems worldwide. The project focuses on how educators respond to social inequality, political change, privatization, digitalization, and evolving professional demands within schooling systems. The initiative is part of the wider EduTrack network — a six-year interdisciplinary research collaboration exploring the future of education across multiple Max Planck institutes. The newly announced openings provide exceptional opportunities for researchers interested in education policy, inequality, political sociology, teacher mobilization, and comparative education research. Available Positions The TICA research group is currently recruiting for the following academic positions: Researcher Position Application Deadline: 6 June 2026 Expected Start Date: Autumn 2026 Postdoctoral Researcher Position Application Deadline: 31 May 2026 Expected Start Date: Autumn 2026 Doctoral Researcher Position Application Deadline: 31 May 2026 Expected Start Date: Autumn 2026 These positions are designed for scholars seeking to contribute to cutting-edge interdisciplinary research on public education systems, inequality, and collective action. About the TICA Research Group The “Teachers, Inequality and Collective Action” (TICA) project investigates how teachers navigate major transformations currently affecting public education systems around the world. The group studies how educators’ social positions, political beliefs, professional experiences, and institutional contexts shape their views on inequality and influence their actions within education systems. The project addresses major global concerns related to: Underfunding of public education Privatization of schooling Digital transformation in education Political polarization Challenges to liberal democratic values Educational stagnation and inequality While education crises in parts of the Global South have long been recognized, the project also examines growing concerns over educational decline and stagnation in parts of the Global North. Research Focus Areas The TICA project combines political sociology, education research, and social inequality studies to explore several major themes. Teachers and Social Inequality One key area of research investigates how teachers perceive inequalities shaped by: Social class Gender Migration background Language Intersectional inequalities The project explores how teachers explain these inequalities and what forms of intervention they consider effective. Collective Action and Teacher Organization Another major focus area examines teachers’ engagement in collective representation and organization, including: Trade unions Professional associations Alternative organizing structures Collective advocacy efforts Researchers will explore how professional experiences and political beliefs influence teachers’ participation in collective action. Educational System Transformation The project also studies how teachers perceive broader structural changes affecting education systems globally, including privatization, austerity, and technological change. The research investigates how these perceptions vary across: Professional profiles Social backgrounds Generational cohorts Political ideologies Methodology and Research Approach TICA employs an interdisciplinary and mixed-methods research framework combining: Institutional mapping Survey data analysis Qualitative research methods Comparative education research Political and sociological analysis This approach enables researchers to examine both structural trends and lived educational experiences across diverse contexts. Regional Focus: Middle East and North Africa (MENA) The empirical work of the TICA project is anchored in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. The region offers important comparative insights into how public education systems are being reshaped under conditions of political transition, economic pressure, privatization, and social transformation. The research group also seeks to foster broader international dialogue on teacher politics, inequality, and collective action beyond the MENA region through workshops, collaborations, and academic exchanges. About the EduTrack Network TICA is part of the EduTrack initiative — a six-year interdisciplinary research network funded by the Max Planck Society . EduTrack explores the future of education through collaborative research involving multiple Max Planck institutes, including: Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research Max Planck Institute for the History of Science Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Sciences The network is coordinated by Population Europe . Why These Positions Matter The restructuring of public education systems is one of the defining global challenges of the modern era. Teachers increasingly operate under conditions shaped by economic inequality, political tension, technological disruption, and changing social expectations. The TICA project offers scholars an opportunity to contribute to globally relevant research examining how educators understand and respond to these transformations. Researchers joining the project will become part of a major international academic network while contributing to interdisciplinary debates on education, inequality, governance, and social change. Application Deadlines Researcher Position Deadline: 6 June 2026 Postdoctoral Researcher Position Deadline: 31 May 2026 Doctoral Researcher Position Deadline: 31 May 2026 Applicants are encouraged to prepare materials early due to the competitive nature of Max Planck research opportunities. title: Young Women in Mind 2026–2028 Grant Programme: Up to £500,000 for Mental Health Services Supporting Young Women in the UK
summary: The Young Women in Mind 2026–2028 funding programme is now open for applications, offering significant grant funding to charities delivering therapeutic mental health support for girls and young women across the United Kingdom. The programme recognizes that many young women struggle to access timely mental health care that reflects their lived experiences and responds effectively to their needs. Through this collaborative funding initiative, the participating trusts aim to support charities that already provide therapeutic mental health services and help them: Expand existing services Strengthen operational capacity Adapt programmes to meet growing demand Improve accessibility and inclusivity Deliver timely interventions before mental health challenges become more severe The programme places strong emphasis on community-based support and trusted environments where young women already seek help. Programme Focus Areas The Young Women in Mind initiative specifically supports charities providing gender-specific therapeutic mental health services for girls and young women aged 14–25. title: 2026–2027 NABJ-Apple News Fellowship: Paid Journalism Fellowship at Apple News for Emerging Digital Journalists
summary: The 2026–2027 NABJ-Apple News Fellowship is now open for applications, offering an extraordinary opportunity for recent graduates and early-career journalists to gain hands-on experience at one of the world’s leading digital news platforms. Through a partnership between Apple News and the National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ), this fellowship is designed to help emerging journalists build practical newsroom expertise while working at the intersection of journalism, media innovation, and technology. The fellowship provides participants with direct exposure to Apple News editorial operations, collaboration with major publisher partners, mentorship from experienced newsroom professionals, and competitive compensation throughout the program period. This unique journalism fellowship is ideal for aspiring digital journalists seeking newsroom experience in breaking news coverage, editorial curation, audience engagement, newsletters, and audio storytelling. About the NABJ-Apple News Fellowship Apple News reaches millions of readers worldwide by delivering trusted journalism from globally recognized news organizations. Through this fellowship, Apple and NABJ aim to create pathways for emerging journalism talent to gain experience in digital media production and editorial decision-making at a world-class newsroom. The selected fellow will join the Apple News editorial team and participate in a structured learning experience that introduces them to the platform’s major editorial divisions. Fellows will work alongside Apple editors and publishing partners while contributing directly to editorial projects and news coverage strategies. The fellowship combines professional newsroom training, mentorship, editorial collaboration, and practical experience in modern digital journalism. Fellowship Structure and Training Experience The NABJ-Apple News Fellowship is carefully structured to provide broad editorial exposure before allowing fellows to specialize in a key area of interest. Editorial Rotations During the first three months, the fellow will rotate through multiple editorial teams within Apple News. These rotations are intended to help participants understand the platform’s editorial ecosystem and develop a versatile journalism skill set. Editorial areas may include: Breaking news coverage Audio journalism Newsletter production Editorial curation Audience engagement News planning and coordination These rotations allow fellows to explore multiple newsroom functions while working with experienced editorial professionals. Specialization Phase After completing the initial rotations, the fellow and Apple News leadership will jointly determine a specialized editorial focus area for the remaining six months of the program. This second phase allows fellows to deepen their expertise and contribute more strategically to Apple News operations. Fellowship Responsibilities Participants in the NABJ-Apple News Fellowship will play an active role within the newsroom and contribute directly to editorial workflows. Key responsibilities include: Editorial Curation Fellows will curate high-quality news content while maintaining strong editorial standards related to accuracy, relevance, and context. Writing and Display Copy The selected candidate will write engaging display copy that encourages audience engagement with stories highlighted by Apple News and publisher partners. News Event Coverage Planning Fellows will help develop editorial plans for major global and national news events, contributing to newsroom coordination and coverage strategies. Collaboration with Publisher Partners The fellowship includes direct communication and collaboration with editors from Apple News publisher partners, helping fellows build industry relationships and editorial coordination skills. Standards and Quality Assurance Participants will work with the News Standards team to ensure all editorial content meets Apple News curation standards and editorial policies. Metrics and Strategic Growth Fellows will learn how editorial performance metrics influence newsroom decisions and audience engagement strategies. Internal Communication and Presentations Participants will communicate their work internally and present project findings and editorial insights to the broader Apple News organization. Fellowship Benefits and Compensation The 2026–2027 NABJ-Apple News Fellowship offers substantial professional and financial benefits. Competitive Pay Compensation: $45 per hour Work schedule: Up to 40 hours per week This makes the fellowship one of the more competitive paid journalism fellowships available to recent graduates and early-career reporters. Mentorship and Career Development The selected fellow will receive: Weekly one-on-one meetings with their manager Dedicated mentorship support Continuous editorial feedback Professional development opportunities Hands-On Experience at Apple News Fellows gain direct experience inside one of the most influential digital news ecosystems in the world. title: Independent Expert Group for the ARISE Program (CIF): Global Call for Climate Finance and Resilience Experts
summary: The Climate Investment Funds (CIF) , established in 2008, is one of the world’s leading multilateral climate finance initiatives supporting developing countries in their transition toward low-emission, climate-resilient development. Through its collaboration with multilateral development banks (MDBs) and partner governments, CIF has pioneered large-scale concessional financing aimed at driving systemic change in energy, infrastructure, agriculture, water, and social resilience systems. Building on 17 years of implementation experience under the Pilot Program for Climate Resilience (PPCR) , CIF has launched a transformative initiative known as the Accelerating Resilience Investments and Innovations for Sustainable Economies (ARISE) program. ARISE is designed to help developing countries convert national resilience priorities into structured, investable, and scalable climate solutions. To support the technical integrity, fairness, and strategic direction of this program, CIF is now recruiting an Independent Expert Group (IEG) composed of globally recognized professionals in climate change, finance, and development economics. A critical milestone in this initiative is the submission of Expressions of Interest (EoIs) by participating countries, with a deadline set for June 8th, 2026 . About the ARISE Program The ARISE program is a forward-looking climate resilience financing framework that focuses on turning climate adaptation needs into actionable investment pipelines. It prioritizes critical systems that are most vulnerable to climate risks, including: Food systems and agricultural resilience Water security and resource management Climate-resilient infrastructure development Sustainable and low-carbon energy systems The program seeks to ensure that climate finance is not only accessible but also strategically deployed to generate long-term resilience outcomes and unlock private sector participation. Role of the Independent Expert Group (IEG) The Independent Expert Group (IEG) will consist of six internationally selected experts with deep technical and strategic experience in climate adaptation, development finance, and economic systems transformation. The group will include balanced representation from both contributing and recipient countries, ensuring fairness, inclusivity, and technical rigor in decision-making. From among the six members, two co-chairs will be appointed. Key Responsibilities The Independent Expert Group will undertake the following core functions: 1. Evaluation of Country Submissions Review Expressions of Interest (EoIs) submitted by eligible countries Assess proposals against established CIF and ARISE evaluation criteria Ensure alignment with resilience investment priorities 2. Technical Research and Review Analyze annexed project and policy documents Conduct supplementary desk research using the Integrated Results Framework (IRF) Validate technical feasibility and investment readiness 3. Stakeholder Consultation Conduct structured interviews with country representatives Engage with multilateral development banks (MDBs) Confirm compliance with MDB partnership standards and coordination frameworks 4. Reporting and Recommendations Produce a ranked list of countries based on evaluation outcomes Submit formal recommendations to the Strategic Climate Fund (SCF) Trust Fund Committee (TFC) Provide methodological notes detailing evaluation approaches Document limitations, challenges, and gaps identified during assessment Include a full list of consulted stakeholders for transparency and accountability Selection Criteria for Applicants Applicants interested in serving on the Independent Expert Group must meet the following requirements: Academic Qualifications A Master’s degree or PhD in fields relevant to climate change, development economics, environmental science, finance, or related disciplines Professional Experience Minimum of 12 years of relevant professional experience Proven work in climate resilience, development finance, or related sectors Experience in developing country contexts is highly preferred Additional Preferred Qualifications Prior experience working with multilateral institutions, international organizations, or global development agencies is an advantage but not mandatory Timeline and Availability Selected experts must be available for engagement between June and October 2026 . Primary workload duration: approximately 6 to 8 weeks Work will include review cycles, consultations, and report drafting phases Flexibility and responsiveness during peak evaluation periods will be essential Application Process and Requirements Applicants are required to submit their applications directly via email: CIF Secretariat Email: CIFSecretariat@cif.org Application Requirements: Full name and contact information Detailed area of expertise Updated curriculum vitae (CV/resume) Disclosure of any conflicts of interest (including current or past employment with CIF partner MDBs or related institutions) Important Deadline: Application submission deadline: May 21st, 2026 Submissions through any channel other than the official email will not be considered Compensation Selected experts will be remunerated in accordance with World Bank consultant procurement rules and regulations , ensuring standardized and competitive international compensation structures for technical experts. title: NASA Service Member Fellowships 2026: Fully Immersive Opportunities for Transitioning U.S. Military Personnel Through SkillBridge & Operation Warfighter
summary: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is offering an extraordinary opportunity for transitioning U.S. military personnel through its Service Member Fellowships Program. Conducted in partnership with the Department of Defense (DoD) SkillBridge Program and the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Operation Warfighter (OWF) Program, these fellowships allow active-duty service members to gain meaningful, mission-driven experience at one of the world’s most respected space and research agencies. Whether your background is in engineering, cybersecurity, public affairs, human resources, science, technology, administration, or program management, NASA’s fellowship pathways are designed to help military personnel successfully transition into civilian careers while contributing to real NASA missions. The fellowship opportunities are available across multiple NASA centers nationwide, including remote and hybrid roles. Applicants selected for the program may work alongside NASA professionals in areas connected to: Human spaceflight Scientific research Technology development Communications and outreach Program management Cybersecurity and IT Engineering and innovation Administrative operations Public affairs and strategic communications This program is not only a career-transition opportunity but also a chance to become part of the NASA ecosystem and contribute to projects that shape the future of exploration and innovation. About the NASA Service Member Fellowships Program NASA’s Service Member Fellowships Program provides active-duty military personnel nearing separation from service the opportunity to work directly with NASA during their final months of military duty. The agency currently participates in two major military transition programs: SkillBridge Fellowship Program Operation Warfighter (OWF) Fellowship Program Through these pathways, selected participants can work with NASA for up to 180 days before completing military service. NASA does not advertise individual vacancies ahead of time. Instead, applicants submit their profiles into a centralized candidate pool. NASA centers then review applications and match candidates with opportunities based on mission needs and candidate qualifications. Current Fellowship Opportunities at NASA NASA has announced several exciting openings and pathways across the agency. Johnson Space Center (JSC) Opportunities at NASA’s Johnson Space Center include: Engineering Roles These positions require: A master’s degree Relevant professional or technical experience Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities Engineering fellows may support: Spaceflight systems Research and development Aerospace technologies Mission operations Technical innovation initiatives Public Affairs Roles Public affairs fellows may contribute to: NASA communications campaigns Outreach programs Media engagement Digital storytelling Strategic messaging and content creation These positions are ideal for individuals with communication, journalism, media production, branding, or outreach experience. NASA Headquarters (Remote Opportunities) NASA Headquarters is also recruiting fellows for remote program management support roles. Responsibilities may include: Supporting implementation of the NASA Service Member Fellowships Program Coordinating agency-wide initiatives Assisting with operational management Supporting strategic planning and reporting Engaging with stakeholders across NASA centers Remote opportunities provide flexibility while allowing fellows to contribute to important NASA-wide operations. Why This Fellowship Matters Transitioning from military to civilian life can be challenging, particularly when trying to align military experience with civilian careers. NASA’s fellowship program helps bridge that gap by giving service members practical, high-impact experience inside a federal agency environment. Participants gain: Hands-on NASA work experience Exposure to federal workplace culture Professional networking opportunities Career development support Resume enhancement as a “NASA Fellow” Access to mission-driven projects Mentorship from NASA professionals Although participation does not guarantee future employment with NASA, the experience significantly strengthens candidates for future federal and private-sector careers. Fields and Career Areas Available NASA offers fellowships across a broad range of disciplines. Possible fellowship areas include: Engineering, Science Technology Aerospace Engineering Mechanical Engineering Systems Engineering Physical Sciences Research Development Information Technology Cybersecurity Cybersecurity Operations Network Administration IT Infrastructure Software Support Information Systems Communications Public Affairs Media Relations Public Communication Content Development Branding Outreach Strategic Communications Business Administration Human Resources Administration Program Management Financial Management Procurement Contracts Budgeting Accounting Additional Fields Safety Occupational Health Social Sciences Mathematics Statistics Operational Analysis Fellowship Duration Selected fellows may participate during their final: Minimum: 90 days Maximum: 180 days The fellowship occurs while participants remain on active duty status. Locations and Work Environment NASA fellowship opportunities are available: Across multiple NASA centers in the United States In hybrid work environments Through fully remote positions in some cases NASA facilities support various mission areas, so applicants are encouraged to research which centers align best with their professional interests. Eligibility Requirements SkillBridge Fellowship Eligibility Applicants must: Be within the final 180 days of active-duty military service Be available for at least 90 days Complete the Transition Assistance Program (TAP) Obtain command approval Follow all service-specific SkillBridge regulations Understand that participation may be terminated due to mission requirements Operation Warfighter (OWF) Eligibility Applicants must: Be actively enrolled in the DHA Operation Warfighter Program Be assigned to a Regional OWF Coordinator Obtain medical and command approvals Follow the DHA Comprehensive Recovery Plan Acknowledge that participation may be terminated by medical providers or military command when necessary Important Application Information NASA independently manages participation in both SkillBridge and OWF fellowships. SkillBridge Application Process Step 1: Obtain Military Approval Applicants should: Review their branch’s SkillBridge policies Coordinate with their base education center Ensure eligibility for participation Step 2: Research NASA Facilities Applicants are encouraged to: Explore NASA centers Identify career-aligned mission areas Understand available work environments Step 3: Submit Application Applicants must submit information through the official NASA Service Member Fellowship application platform. Important note: NASA does not publicly post fellowship vacancies beforehand. Applications remain in a candidate pool until sponsoring centers identify suitable candidates. Operation Warfighter Application Process Step 1: Connect with Regional Coordinator Applicants should: Contact their assigned OWF Coordinator Confirm eligibility and program alignment Step 2: Submit Application Candidates must apply through NASA’s Veterans Application platform. As with SkillBridge, NASA centers review applications internally and contact selected candidates directly. NASA’s Policy on Artificial Intelligence in Applications NASA explicitly prohibits the use of artificial intelligence tools to draft fellowship application narratives. Applicants must: Write all responses independently Submit original materials Avoid AI-assisted writing tools NASA may verify submissions, and failure to comply can result in disqualification. Veterans Careers at NASA NASA continues to support veterans and military spouses through: Career development opportunities Flexible workplace arrangements Veteran-focused hiring pathways Federal hiring preferences Veterans separated under honorable conditions may qualify for additional hiring authorities and employment advantages within the federal system. Fellowship Benefits Participants may benefit from: Direct NASA work experience Exposure to high-impact national projects Professional mentorship Career transition support Enhanced federal employment readiness Networking with NASA teams Resume credibility as a NASA Fellow Participation in mission-driven work environments Deadline NASA has not announced a fixed application deadline. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and maintained within a candidate pool for review by NASA centers. Interested applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible before entering their final 180 days of active-duty service. Final Thoughts NASA’s Service Member Fellowships Program is one of the most unique military transition opportunities currently available in the United States. It combines professional development, national service, technical innovation, and real-world experience within a globally respected organization. For transitioning service members interested in engineering, public affairs, technology, administration, or scientific exploration, this fellowship offers a rare opportunity to work directly with NASA while preparing for the next phase of civilian life. Applicants who meet the eligibility requirements should begin preparing early, coordinate with their military leadership, and submit strong, original applications aligned with NASA’s mission and values. How to Apply Interested applicants can apply through the official application portal HERE . Click HERE for more information about the NASA Service Member Fellowships Program. Explore more global fellowship opportunities on OFY here .
