title: IOC Launches 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme for Olympic Studies Researchers Worldwide
summary: The International Olympic Committee (IOC), through its renowned Olympic Studies Centre (OSC), has officially launched the 2027 edition of the PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme. The initiative is designed to support scholars conducting research related to the Olympic Movement, Olympism, the Olympic Games, athletes, sports history, and the wider social and cultural impact of the Olympics across the world. The programme continues the IOC’s long-standing commitment to advancing academic research and encouraging global scholarly engagement in Olympic studies. Since its establishment in 1999, the grant programme has supported more than 148 researchers from different countries, helping them pursue innovative academic projects while also providing opportunities to access the IOC’s unique collections and historical archives in Lausanne, Switzerland. For researchers interested in sports history, sociology, international relations, culture, politics, media, education, and other areas linked to Olympism and the Olympic Games, this programme presents a major opportunity to receive institutional recognition and financial support for their academic work. About the IOC Olympic Studies Centre Research Grant Programme The IOC Olympic Studies Centre serves as the world’s leading hub for Olympic knowledge and research resources. The centre was created to preserve, develop, and share information related to the Olympic Movement and its influence on society. Through the PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme, the IOC aims to: Encourage high-quality academic research on Olympism and the Olympic Movement Promote interdisciplinary studies related to sports and society Support young and emerging scholars globally Increase global understanding of Olympic values and their societal impact Facilitate access to the IOC’s historical archives and collections The grant programme is open to scholars whose research explores different dimensions of the Olympic Games and Olympic culture. Topics may include: Olympic history and heritage Athlete development and representation Sports governance and policy Olympic education and values Gender and diversity in sports Media and communication in the Olympic Movement Social, political, and economic impact of the Olympics Olympic legacy and sustainability International relations through sports diplomacy Cultural influence of the Olympic Games The programme particularly values research conducted from humanities and social sciences perspectives. Access to Unique Olympic Research Resources One of the major advantages of this programme is access to the IOC Olympic Studies Centre’s world-class research resources. Selected researchers may have the opportunity to visit Lausanne, Switzerland, where they can consult the IOC’s extensive collections, including primary sources and historical archives related to the Olympic Movement. Researchers will also gain access to the Olympic World Library (OWL), a specialized library catalogue dedicated entirely to Olympic knowledge. The library contains more than 42,000 official and academic publications, making it one of the largest Olympic-related academic collections in the world. The IOC believes that giving scholars access to these resources helps improve the quality and originality of academic research while preserving Olympic heritage for future generations. Who Can Apply for the 2027 Research Grant Programme? The programme is specifically targeted at postgraduate researchers and early career academics involved in Olympic-related studies. Eligible applicants include: 1. PhD Students Applicants must currently be enrolled in a PhD degree programme within the humanities or social sciences. Their research must include Olympism, the Olympic Movement, or the Olympic Games as at least one of the main areas of focus. 2. Early Career Academics Academic staff members and postdoctoral fellows are also eligible if they completed their doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024. In some academic fields, a master’s degree may also qualify as the highest equivalent degree. This broad eligibility framework allows emerging scholars from different disciplines and countries to participate. Application Process and Deadline Interested applicants are required to prepare and submit their application forms directly to the IOC Olympic Studies Centre . According to the official announcement, all applications and related correspondence must be submitted before: Deadline: Tuesday, 22 September 2026 Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the official programme rules, guidelines, and application form available on the IOC Olympic Studies Centre website before submitting their applications. The IOC has also announced that two online information sessions will be organized for researchers intending to apply. These sessions are expected to provide guidance on eligibility, application requirements, research expectations, and the overall selection process. Grant Selection Committee Applications will be reviewed by a Grant Programme Selection Committee composed of internationally recognized academic experts involved in Olympic studies, alongside representatives from the IOC Olympic Studies Centre. The committee evaluates applications based on: Academic quality Originality of the research topic Relevance to Olympic studies Methodological strength Potential contribution to the field This rigorous review process ensures that the programme supports impactful and high-quality academic work. Additional Olympic Research Opportunities Beyond the PhD and Early Career Academics Grant Programme, the IOC also offers the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme. This separate programme targets established researchers, including: University professors Lecturers Senior research fellows Applicants for the advanced programme must hold academic or research appointments and have completed their doctorate. The IOC has confirmed that applications for the 2027–2029 edition of the Advanced Olympic Research Grant Programme will open in October 2026. Why This Opportunity Matters The IOC research grant programme has become one of the most respected opportunities for scholars studying sports and society. It not only provides funding support but also offers researchers global academic visibility and access to exclusive Olympic resources. For young academics seeking to establish themselves in sports studies, sociology, history, or cultural research, this programme could significantly strengthen their academic profile and international research networks. Researchers interested in applying are encouraged to begin preparing their proposals early and participate in the upcoming online information sessions to better understand the application process. For more information, applicants can visit the IOC Olympic Studies Centre website or contact the centre directly via email at studies.centre@olympic.org . Current PhD students Early career academics Academic staff members Postdoctoral fellows Researchers in humanities and social sciences Academic Qualifications Must be enrolled in a PhD programme OR Must have completed a doctorate or equivalent highest degree in or after 2024 Research must focus on Olympism, the Olympic Movement, or the Olympic Games Eligible Countries/Regions Open to applicants from all countries worldwide Discover more global grant opportunities on OFY here The post IOC Launches 2027 PhD Students and Early Career Academics Research Grant Programme for Olympic Studies Researchers Worldwide appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: Accelerate Africa Startup Programme: Empowering African Founders to Build Global Businesses
summary: African startups continue to transform industries, create jobs, and solve some of the continent’s biggest challenges through innovation and technology. However, many early-stage founders struggle with mentorship, funding access, strategic guidance, and global market expansion. To bridge this gap, Accelerate Africa has emerged as one of the continent’s most promising startup accelerator platforms focused on helping visionary African entrepreneurs build scalable and globally competitive businesses. Accelerate Africa is a startup accelerator programme designed specifically for ambitious founders across Africa who are building innovative solutions capable of addressing major social, economic, and technological challenges. The programme provides founders with hands-on mentorship, strategic support, access to investors, and practical guidance from experienced operators who have built and scaled successful African startups. According to the official platform, Accelerate Africa’s mission is to accelerate Africa’s bold and visionary founders in the earliest stages of building global businesses that solve Africa’s biggest challenges. What is Accelerate Africa? Accelerate Africa is an intensive accelerator programme created to support early-stage African startups through mentorship, workshops, advisory services, and networking opportunities. Unlike many traditional startup accelerators, Accelerate Africa focuses heavily on personalized founder support rather than a one-size-fits-all programme structure. The accelerator selects a limited number of founders who receive direct coaching and guidance from experienced entrepreneurs, operators, investors, and advisors with deep experience across African startup ecosystems. The programme was founded with the vision of helping African entrepreneurs create world-class businesses capable of competing globally while solving pressing continental problems. Accelerate Africa has already supported startups and founders linked to some of Africa’s most successful companies, including: Andela Flutterwave Moove Daystar Power DukaConnect Many of these businesses have grown into globally recognized companies, raised millions of dollars in funding, or been acquired by international corporations. Key Benefits of the Accelerate Africa Programme The programme offers several valuable benefits to startup founders who are looking to scale their businesses and attract investors. 1. One-on-One Coaching and Mentorship Selected founders receive personalized coaching from experienced startup operators, investors, and advisors who understand the realities of building businesses in Africa. This mentorship helps founders improve critical business areas such as: Business strategy Leadership Product development Market positioning Customer acquisition Scaling operations Investor readiness 2. Access to Investor Networks Accelerate Africa connects startups with local and international investors through demo days and investor showcases. Founders gain exposure to venture capital firms, angel investors, ecosystem builders, and strategic partners who may provide funding opportunities after the programme. According to programme information, startups may become eligible for optional post-programme investment opportunities ranging from $250,000 to $500,000 through Future Africa and partner networks after due diligence and approval processes. 3. Workshops Across Core Startup Areas The accelerator programme includes practical workshops and office hours covering: Storytelling and brand positioning Team building and leadership Product-market fit Go-to-market strategies Revenue growth Fundraising preparation Legal support Financial management These sessions are designed to help founders avoid common startup mistakes while improving their chances of long-term success. 4. Networking and Founder Community Participants also gain access to a strong community of ambitious African founders facing similar entrepreneurial challenges. The programme encourages peer learning, collaboration, and long-term networking opportunities across multiple African countries. 5. No Immediate Equity Requirement One of the unique features of Accelerate Africa is that the programme does not immediately take equity from startups upon admission. This founder-friendly structure allows entrepreneurs to access support and mentorship without giving away ownership early in the process. Programme Structure and Timeline Accelerate Africa typically runs cohort-based accelerator programmes involving a small group of selected startups. The programme generally includes: Virtual mentorship sessions In-person welcome week activities Workshops and advisory clinics Demo day preparation Investor pitch events Some programme editions run for approximately 8 to 12 weeks depending on the cohort structure. The accelerator prioritizes quality over quantity by selecting only a small number of founders for each cohort. Why Accelerate Africa Matters for African Startups Africa’s startup ecosystem continues to grow rapidly, but many founders still struggle with access to funding, mentorship, and growth support during the early stages of business development. Accelerate Africa aims to close this gap by helping entrepreneurs: Build scalable businesses Improve operational systems Reach international markets Raise venture capital funding Develop sustainable business models Create jobs and economic impact The programme’s focus on practical founder support and African market realities makes it especially valuable for entrepreneurs operating in emerging and underserved markets. Accelerate Africa has also positioned itself as a platform committed to supporting diversity and inclusion across the startup ecosystem, including women founders and entrepreneurs from different African countries and backgrounds. Accelerate Africa Portfolio and Impact According to official programme statistics, Accelerate Africa and its broader ecosystem have supported: 162 companies 170 founders More than $2.92 billion in funds raised Over 1,900 applications received These numbers reflect the growing influence of the accelerator within Africa’s startup and venture capital ecosystem. How to Apply Interested founders can apply directly through the official Accelerate Africa platform. Applicants are encouraged to prepare: A strong startup pitch Clear problem-solution explanation Business traction evidence Team information Growth strategy Market opportunity analysis Due to the highly competitive nature of the programme, founders are advised to apply early and ensure their applications clearly demonstrate scalability, innovation, and impact potential. For more details and applications, founders can visit: Accelerate Africa Official Website Opportunity Category Accelerator Programme / Grant Support Opportunity Eligible People and Regions Who Can Apply? Early-stage startup founders African entrepreneurs Tech-enabled startups Innovative business founders Startup co-founding teams Qualifications Must be building a scalable startup Must solve a meaningful African challenge Must demonstrate growth potential Startups should show innovation and market opportunity Some cohorts may prioritize startups with traction or MVPs Eligible Countries/Regions Open to founders across Africa African startups from multiple countries are encouraged to apply Discover more global accelerate programs on OFY here The post Accelerate Africa Startup Programme: Empowering African Founders to Build Global Businesses appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: CIFAR Horizon Networks 2026: International Research Funding Opportunity for Early- and Mid-Career Researchers
summary: Applications are now open for the CIFAR Horizon Networks 2026, an exciting international research funding opportunity designed to support early- and mid-career researchers in building interdisciplinary and global research collaborations. Organised by Canadian Institute for Advanced Research , the Horizon Networks initiative aims to foster innovative research communities that can shape emerging fields of inquiry and establish the next generation of global thought leaders. The programme provides selected research teams with collaborative funding, professional development opportunities, international networking, and logistical support over a three-year period. Through Horizon Networks, researchers from diverse disciplines and institutions can work together to address some of the world’s most pressing challenges in education, childhood development, identity, technology, and civic engagement. About CIFAR Canadian Institute for Advanced Research , widely known as CIFAR, is a globally recognised research organisation headquartered in Canada. CIFAR brings together leading researchers from around the world to collaborate across disciplines and generate transformative ideas capable of solving complex global challenges. Supported by the governments of Canada, Alberta, and Québec, alongside international foundations, corporations, and partner organisations, CIFAR has built a strong reputation for advancing groundbreaking research and supporting academic innovation on a global scale. The organisation is particularly known for fostering interdisciplinary collaboration and creating environments where researchers can develop bold and innovative ideas that may not emerge within traditional academic structures. What Are Horizon Networks? Horizon Networks are collaborative international research networks led by early- to mid-career researchers. These networks are designed to: Build emerging interdisciplinary research communities Explore new fields of inquiry Strengthen international academic collaboration Develop future research leaders Encourage innovative thinking across disciplines Each selected Horizon Network will operate over a three-year term and receive support from CIFAR to pursue collaborative research activities. What the Programme Offers Selected Horizon Networks receive extensive support and funding, including: Three-Year Research Network Support Networks operate over a three-year period with long-term collaborative engagement among members. In-Person Meetings Network members meet twice per year in person, with all logistics, financial arrangements, and administrative coordination managed by CIFAR. Collaborative Research Funding Each Horizon Network receives funding distributed across the team to support collaborative research activities and network initiatives. Flexible Fund Management While CIFAR distributes the funding, Horizon Network leads are responsible for allocating and managing the funds among team members. Professional Development All network members participate in annual professional development opportunities designed to strengthen leadership, collaboration, and research impact. International and Interdisciplinary Collaboration Researchers gain access to international academic networks and interdisciplinary partnerships that can significantly enhance research visibility and long-term career growth. Eligibility Requirements The Horizon Networks programme specifically targets emerging research leaders and interdisciplinary collaboration. Leadership Requirements Each network must be co-led by researchers who are alumni of CIFAR’s early-career leadership programmes. Team Composition Each Horizon Network may include: Up to eight additional early- to mid-career faculty members Researchers from diverse institutions and disciplines Individuals who may not have previously participated in CIFAR programmes Institutional Diversity Network co-leaders are encouraged to recruit members from a broad range of institutions to ensure diversity of perspectives and expertise. Current Horizon Networks Streams for 2026 Applicants must submit proposals under one of the following thematic streams. Stream 1: Belonging with Nature, Technology and People in Early Childhood Supported by the Bezos Family Foundation, this stream explores how children’s relationships with nature, technology, and social environments shape development and belonging during early childhood. Stream 2: Adolescence – Belonging, Identity and Civic Engagement in a Changing World Also supported by the Bezos Family Foundation, this stream focuses on adolescent identity formation, civic participation, and social belonging in rapidly evolving societal contexts. Stream 3: Education and Learning Variability Between Ages 2–12 This stream is supported by the Jacobs CIFAR Research Fellowship programme and must be co-led by current or former Jacobs CIFAR Research Fellows. The stream investigates learning variability and educational development among children aged 2 to 12. Why This Opportunity Matters The Horizon Networks programme stands out because it empowers researchers at relatively early stages of their careers to: Lead international research collaborations Shape emerging academic fields Develop leadership and management skills Build influential research communities Access international visibility and funding opportunities Rather than supporting individual projects alone, the programme invests in building sustainable research ecosystems that can continue generating impact beyond the funding period. Review and Selection Process Applications undergo a multi-stage review process. Eligibility Screening CIFAR staff first review all submissions to ensure eligibility requirements are met. Reciprocal Peer Review Applicants also participate in a reciprocal peer review process, where proposed Horizon Network leads review and evaluate other applications. Final Decision Final funding decisions are made by CIFAR together with funding partners where applicable. Applicants submitting proposals agree to: Review assigned proposals Participate in peer evaluation Engage in the collaborative assessment process Applications are scored using a rubric aligned with the official selection criteria. Key Dates for CIFAR Horizon Networks 2026 Applications Open 6 May 2026 Application Deadline 17 June 2026 at 12 PM ET Peer Review Deadline 15 July 2026 Decision Notifications Summer 2026 Applicants are encouraged to begin building interdisciplinary teams and developing strong collaborative proposals early. Ideal Applicant Profile This opportunity is particularly suitable for: Early- and mid-career faculty researchers Interdisciplinary scholars Researchers interested in collaborative international work Academics exploring emerging research questions Scholars focused on childhood, education, technology, identity, civic engagement, and human development Strong proposals will typically demonstrate: Innovative interdisciplinary thinking Clear collaborative structures Leadership potential Strong research vision Global relevance and societal impact Benefits of Participating in Horizon Networks Researchers selected for Horizon Networks gain access to: International research collaborations Leadership development opportunities Funding flexibility Academic visibility Long-term interdisciplinary partnerships Exposure to high-level global research communities The programme also creates valuable opportunities for future grants, publications, policy influence, and large-scale research initiatives. Final Thoughts The CIFAR Horizon Networks 2026 programme offers a unique platform for emerging academic leaders to build influential interdisciplinary research collaborations on a global scale. Through funding, mentorship, networking, and professional development, the programme helps researchers shape new fields of inquiry while addressing important societal challenges. For early- and mid-career researchers seeking to establish themselves as international thought leaders, Horizon Networks represents a highly valuable and prestigious opportunity. title: Fully Funded BIOFABRICATE PhD Studentship 2026 at Trinity College Dublin: Research Opportunity in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Sustainable Biomaterials
summary: Applications are now open for the fully funded BIOFABRICATE PhD Studentship 2026 at Trinity College Dublin , one of Europe’s most prestigious and internationally recognised universities. This exciting doctoral research opportunity is hosted within the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences at Trinity College Dublin and is funded by the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) in Ireland. The PhD studentship forms part of the larger BIOFABRICATE programme, a groundbreaking multi-institutional research initiative focused on developing sustainable bio-based materials and technologies from Irish forest biomass for applications across pharmaceuticals, construction, manufacturing, and packaging industries. This opportunity is ideal for candidates interested in pharmaceutical sciences, biomaterials, chemistry, sustainable manufacturing, and advanced pharmaceutical formulation research. About Trinity College Dublin Founded in 1592, Trinity College Dublin is Ireland’s leading university and one of the oldest and most respected institutions in Europe. Ranked 75th globally in the QS World University Rankings 2026, Trinity has built a strong international reputation for excellence in education, research, innovation, and global impact. The university is known for: World-class research facilities Strong international academic collaborations Leadership in sustainability and innovation Inclusive and diverse academic environment Commitment to equality, diversity, and work-life balance Trinity College Dublin also holds the Athena Swan Silver Award and is recognised as an EU Sustainable Gender Equality Champion. About the BIOFABRICATE Research Programme BIOFABRICATE stands for: Integrated Bio-based Innovations for Sustainable Manufacturing, Construction, and Pharmaceutical Applications from Irish Forest Biomass The programme is led by the University of Galway and involves collaboration with several Irish institutions, including: Trinity College Dublin Technological University Dublin Atlantic Technological University Dublin City University Teagasc Multiple industry partners The programme focuses on transforming Ireland’s growing forest biomass resources into advanced sustainable materials that can be applied across various industrial sectors. PhD Research Project Overview The selected PhD candidate will work under the supervision of Professor Anne Marie Healy in the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, with co-supervision from Dr. Ramesh Babu in the School of Chemistry. The project title is: “Evaluation of the Use of Microcrystalline Cellulose Generated from Irish Forestry Biomass in Pharmaceutical Solid Dosage Forms” The research will investigate the properties and pharmaceutical performance of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) produced from Irish forest biomass (IFB-MCC). The project aims to: Evaluate the physical and chemical properties of IFB-MCC Compare IFB-MCC with commercially available pharmaceutical excipients Assess suitability for tablet direct compression applications Explore sustainable alternatives for pharmaceutical manufacturing Support innovation in environmentally friendly pharmaceutical materials This interdisciplinary project combines pharmaceutical sciences, biomaterials research, chemistry, and sustainability. What the Studentship Offers The fully funded PhD studentship provides candidates with: Full doctoral research funding Opportunity to work within a major national research programme Access to advanced laboratories and research infrastructure Collaboration with leading researchers and institutions Exposure to interdisciplinary and industry-linked research Academic mentorship from internationally recognised supervisors Opportunity to contribute to sustainable pharmaceutical innovation The position also offers valuable research and professional development opportunities within a collaborative academic environment. Ideal Candidate Profile The programme is suitable for highly motivated applicants with backgrounds in: Pharmaceutical Sciences Pharmacy Chemistry Materials Science Biomedical Sciences Chemical Engineering Pharmaceutical Technology Related scientific disciplines Candidates with research experience in pharmaceutical formulations, biomaterials, analytical chemistry, or sustainable materials may have an advantage. Application Requirements Applicants are required to submit the following documents via email to Professor Anne Marie Healy: Required Documents Full Curriculum Vitae (CV) A short motivation statement (maximum one page) outlining: Interest in the project Understanding of the research topic Academic and research motivations A writing sample such as: Published paper Thesis excerpt Academic report Contact details of two referees, including email addresses Application Deadline The application deadline is: 25 May 2026 at 12 noon (Irish time) Shortlisted candidates will be invited for interviews in June 2026. Trinity College Dublin’s Commitment to Inclusion Trinity College Dublin strongly values equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from: International students Applicants with disabilities Individuals from non-traditional academic backgrounds Researchers displaced due to war or conflict Applicants with career breaks or caring responsibilities The university is committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive research environment where all scholars can thrive. Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out This fully funded PhD studentship is particularly attractive because it combines: High-impact sustainability research Pharmaceutical innovation Interdisciplinary collaboration Industry relevance International academic exposure Access to leading Irish research institutions The project also aligns with growing global priorities surrounding sustainable manufacturing and environmentally responsible pharmaceutical development. Career Opportunities After the PhD Graduates completing this research programme may pursue careers in: Pharmaceutical research and development Sustainable materials innovation Academia and scientific research Biotechnology industries Pharmaceutical manufacturing Regulatory and formulation sciences Biomaterials and green chemistry sectors The interdisciplinary nature of the project equips researchers with highly transferable technical and analytical skills. Final Thoughts The BIOFABRICATE PhD Studentship 2026 at Trinity College Dublin offers an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers passionate about pharmaceutical sciences, sustainability, and biomaterials innovation. With full funding, expert supervision, collaborative research networks, and the chance to contribute to sustainable pharmaceutical technologies, this doctoral programme represents an excellent pathway for candidates seeking impactful research careers. Interested applicants are encouraged to prepare strong application materials and apply before the deadline. title: Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship 2026 in the UK: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity for Mandela Rhodes Alumni
summary: The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship (SJMS) 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity for outstanding Mandela Rhodes Alumni who aspire to pursue doctoral studies in the United Kingdom. Created through a partnership between the Mandela Rhodes Foundation and the Leverhulme Trust , this prestigious scholarship is designed to support emerging African leaders in advancing their academic, professional, and leadership journeys through fully funded PhD studies. The scholarship is exclusively available to Mandela Rhodes Alumni and aims to amplify the long-term impact of the Mandela Rhodes network by empowering scholars with access to world-class research institutions, international academic networks, and advanced doctoral training opportunities in the UK. Initially known as the Leverhulme Mandela Rhodes Doctoral Scholarships, the programme was renamed in March 2020 in honour of Shaun Johnson, the founding Executive Director of the Mandela Rhodes Foundation, following his unexpected passing. The scholarship reflects Shaun Johnson’s vision of transformative leadership, education, and social impact across Africa. It seeks to empower Mandela Rhodes Alumni who demonstrate exceptional leadership potential and a commitment to contributing meaningfully to their communities and fields of expertise. The scholarship combines academic advancement with leadership development, ensuring that scholars are equipped not only with research skills but also with the networks and influence necessary to drive change across the African continent and beyond. Scholarship Benefits The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship offers comprehensive financial support for selected scholars pursuing PhD studies in the United Kingdom. Benefits include: Full funding for tuition fees A stipend to cover living expenses Opportunity to study at leading UK universities Access to globally recognised supervisors and research facilities Exposure to international academic and professional networks Integration into the Leverhulme and Mandela Rhodes alumni communities The programme is designed to remove financial barriers and allow scholars to focus fully on their doctoral research and leadership development. Purpose and Objectives of the Scholarship The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship aims to strengthen both vocational and leadership capacity among Mandela Rhodes Alumni. Supporting Vocational Capacity The programme seeks to: Enable scholars to deepen expertise in their chosen disciplines through doctoral study Provide access to world-class research environments and academic resources Connect scholars with leading supervisors and facilities that may not be available in their home countries Strengthening Leadership Capacity The scholarship also focuses on leadership development by: Supporting alumni who have clearly articulated the next phase of their leadership journey Encouraging scholars to use doctoral studies as a platform for long-term social and professional impact Expanding access to international academic and vocational influence networks through UK universities This unique combination of academic excellence and leadership development makes the SJMS one of the most impactful doctoral scholarship opportunities available to African scholars. Testimonial from a Previous Scholar According to Axolile Qina , a previous recipient of the scholarship: “The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship has been an incredible opportunity to further my career aspirations in the academy. [ ] The support from Leverhulme has been exceptional. Eligibility Requirements The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship is strictly open to Mandela Rhodes Alumni. Applicants must: Be alumni of the Mandela Rhodes Scholarship programme Intend to pursue doctoral studies in the United Kingdom Demonstrate strong academic and leadership potential Clearly articulate how the PhD aligns with their leadership and professional goals The programme is specifically designed for individuals who are committed to creating impact within their disciplines and communities. Application Process Applications for the Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship 2026 open on: 17 April 2026 The application deadline is: 17 May 2026 Applicants are encouraged to prepare their materials early due to the highly competitive nature of the programme. Unlike many traditional doctoral funding programmes, the Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship places equal importance on leadership development and academic excellence. Recipients become part of a dynamic network of scholars, researchers, and leaders committed to driving positive change across Africa and globally. The programme supports scholars not only financially but also through mentorship, networking, and community engagement opportunities. With only two scholarships awarded annually, recipients join a highly distinguished cohort of leaders and researchers. Why Pursue a PhD in the UK? The United Kingdom remains one of the world’s leading destinations for doctoral research due to: Globally recognised universities Advanced research infrastructure Diverse international academic communities Access to leading experts and supervisors Opportunities for international collaboration Strong research funding and innovation ecosystems Through the Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship, Mandela Rhodes Alumni can leverage these opportunities to further their academic and leadership ambitions. Final Thoughts The Shaun Johnson Memorial Scholarship 2026 offers Mandela Rhodes Alumni a transformative opportunity to pursue fully funded doctoral studies in the United Kingdom while strengthening their leadership impact and professional expertise. For scholars committed to academic excellence, social change, and leadership development, this programme provides a powerful platform to expand influence, deepen knowledge, and contribute meaningfully to Africa’s future. Interested candidates are strongly encouraged to begin preparations early and request the application forms before the deadline. title: Ferguson Scholarship 2026 at Aston University: Fully Funded Master’s Opportunity for Students from Africa and India
summary: The Ferguson Scholarship 2026 at Aston University offers an exceptional opportunity for talented students from Africa and India to pursue postgraduate education in the United Kingdom with significant financial support. Supported by the Allan and Nesta Ferguson Charitable Trust, this prestigious scholarship programme is designed to improve access to higher education for students who may not otherwise have the financial means to study abroad. For the 2026/27 academic year, Aston University will award three Ferguson Scholarships to outstanding international students enrolling in selected postgraduate taught programmes in the Health and Life Sciences field. Each successful applicant will receive full tuition fee coverage worth £22,500 in addition to a £6,000 contribution towards living expenses. This scholarship represents more than just financial support. It is an opportunity to study at one of the United Kingdom’s most innovative universities, gain world-class academic training, access cutting-edge research opportunities, and build an international network that can shape future careers in science, healthcare, biotechnology, psychology, and public health. About Aston University Aston University is one of the UK’s leading universities known for academic excellence, employability, social mobility, and impactful research. Located in the heart of Birmingham, the university hosts a diverse international student community representing more than 120 countries worldwide. The university has earned several recognitions, including: University of the Year for Student Success (Daily Mail University Guide 2025) Ranked among the top universities in the UK by The Guardian University Guide 2025 Recognised for strong graduate employability and social mobility outcomes A respected institution in health sciences, biotechnology, psychology, engineering, and innovation Students at Aston University benefit from modern facilities, supportive academics, practical learning approaches, and strong industry connections that help graduates transition successfully into global careers. What the Ferguson Scholarship Covers The Ferguson Scholarship 2026 provides substantial financial support to selected students. The scholarship package includes: Full tuition fee coverage valued at £22,500 Additional £6,000 contribution toward living expenses Opportunity to study in the UK at a highly ranked institution Access to advanced laboratories, research facilities, and academic resources Exposure to international academic and professional networks This funding support significantly reduces the financial burden associated with studying abroad and allows students to focus on academic and professional development. Eligible Master’s Programmes Applicants must apply for one of the eligible postgraduate taught programmes at Aston University to qualify for the Ferguson Scholarship. Eligible programmes include: MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences MSc Drug Delivery MSc Pharmacokinetics MSc Stem Cells Regenerative Medicine MSc Biotechnology MSc Psychology (Conversion Programme) MSc Neuroscience for Drug Discovery MSc Addiction and Mental Health MSc Bioinformatics and Genomic Medicine Master of Public Health (MPH) These programmes are designed to equip students with specialised knowledge and practical skills in rapidly growing sectors of health and life sciences. Ferguson Scholarship Eligibility Criteria To be considered for the Ferguson Scholarship 2026, applicants must meet the following requirements: Academic Requirements Applicants must hold at least a 2:1 degree or an equivalent qualification in a relevant field related to the programme they are applying for. Admission Offer Candidates must first obtain either a conditional or unconditional offer from Aston University for one of the eligible master’s programmes. Nationality Requirements The scholarship is open exclusively to: Students from African countries Students from India Funding Status Applicants must be self-funded students. Sponsored students are not eligible for this scholarship. Agency Restriction Candidates referred through agencies will not be considered. Applications submitted through educational agents are automatically removed from review. Financial Evidence Successful candidates must provide evidence to UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) demonstrating they can sufficiently contribute to their living costs while studying in the UK. How to Apply for the Ferguson Scholarship 2026 The application process involves two important stages. Step 1: Apply for an Eligible Course Applicants must first submit an application for one of the approved postgraduate programmes through Aston University’s official course application portal. Step 2: Complete the Scholarship Webform After submitting the course application, candidates must complete the Ferguson Scholarship application webform before the deadline. Applicants will need to provide their 9-digit Aston University application number beginning with “25”. title: UN Women International Consultant on Violence Against Women Survey in Albania 2026–2027 (Up to 50 Working Days)
summary: The United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) has officially announced applications for the position of International Consultant on Violence Against Women (VAW) Survey in Tirana, Albania. This high-level international consultancy presents an exceptional opportunity for experienced gender experts, statisticians, researchers, and violence prevention specialists to contribute to one of Europe’s most important national gender data initiatives. The application deadline is 18 May 2026. The consultancy will support Albania’s upcoming national Violence Against Women prevalence survey scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2027. The selected consultant will work closely with the Albanian National Institute of Statistics (INSTAT) and UN Women Albania to ensure the survey meets global methodological and ethical standards while aligning with European Union gender-based violence data requirements. About UN Women UN Women works globally to eliminate discrimination against women and girls, promote women’s empowerment, and achieve gender equality across all sectors of society. In Albania, UN Women is implementing its Strategic Note 2022–2026, focusing on ensuring women and girls fully enjoy their human rights and actively contribute to the country’s sustainable development and European Union integration process. This consultancy is part of broader initiatives funded by Sida and the European Union to strengthen gender equality systems, improve violence prevention mechanisms, and advance gender statistics in Albania. About the Violence Against Women Survey Albania was among the first countries to conduct a comprehensive national Violence Against Women prevalence survey in 2018 following the adoption of the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The next survey round for 2026–2027 will: Measure the prevalence of violence against women in Albania Produce internationally comparable gender-based violence data Support monitoring of SDG Indicator 5.2 Contribute to the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE) Gender Equality Index Support Albania’s EU accession reporting obligations Align with the EU Survey on Gender-Based Violence (EU-GBV) Follow WHO and UN statistical guidelines on violence against women surveys The survey will also incorporate updated legal frameworks following Albania’s January 2026 law on the Prevention and Protection from Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence. Technical and Methodological Leadership The consultant will: Guide overall survey implementation Ensure alignment with EU-GBV methodology Ensure compliance with Eurostat standards Support implementation according to WHO and UN ethical guidelines Provide methodological oversight across all survey stages 2. Survey Design and Methodology Responsibilities include: Reviewing sample strategies and survey design Supporting questionnaire adaptation and validation Reviewing fieldwork procedures and protocols Supporting development of respondent materials Reviewing enumerator manuals and survey tools 3. Data Processing and Analysis The consultant will support: Data cleaning and validation Weighting procedures Eurostat quality compliance Preparation of final datasets Development of tabulation plans Trend analysis comparing 2018 and 2026 data 7. title: Québec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students 2027–2028: Fully Funded Research Opportunities in Canada
summary: Canada continues to stand out as one of the world’s leading destinations for international education and advanced research. Among the most prestigious opportunities available to global scholars is the Québec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students 2027–2028, funded by Québec’s Ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur (MES) and administered by the Fonds québécois de la recherche sur la nature et les technologies (FQRNT). This highly competitive scholarship program is designed to attract outstanding international students and researchers to Québec universities by supporting cutting-edge research, academic collaboration, and professional development. The program provides substantial financial support for master’s studies, doctoral studies, postdoctoral fellowships, and short-term research projects. For ambitious international students looking to study in Canada with financial support, this scholarship presents a remarkable opportunity to advance academic and research careers at globally recognized institutions such as Université Laval and other Québec universities. What Is the Québec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students? The Québec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students is an initiative established by Québec’s Ministry of Higher Education to strengthen international research partnerships and encourage academic excellence in Québec universities. The scholarship program supports foreign students and researchers who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and strong research potential. The initiative aims to: Foster international collaboration in research and innovation Attract highly qualified foreign talent to Québec Support advanced academic training and scientific development Promote research excellence in Québec institutions Encourage global academic exchange and professional growth The scholarship is administered by the Fonds québécois de la recherche sur la nature et les technologies (FQRNT), one of Québec’s leading research funding organizations. Scholarship Categories and Funding Amounts The program offers four major scholarship categories, each tailored to different academic and professional levels. 1. VM – Master’s Research Scholarships The VM scholarship supports international students pursuing research-based master’s degrees in Québec universities. Funding Details Award Amount: CAD $20,000 per year Duration: Up to 2 years This category is ideal for students seeking financial support while conducting advanced research during their master’s studies. 2. V1 – Doctoral Research Scholarships The V1 scholarship is designed for international PhD candidates pursuing doctoral research in Québec. Funding Details Award Amount: CAD $25,000 per year Duration: Up to 4 years Doctoral candidates can use this funding to support tuition, research expenses, accommodation, and living costs throughout their studies. 3. V2 – Postdoctoral Fellowships The V2 category supports international researchers undertaking postdoctoral research projects in Québec. Funding Details Award Amount: CAD $35,000 Duration: Non-renewable This fellowship helps postdoctoral researchers collaborate with leading academics and research institutions in Canada. 4. V3 – Short-Term Research or Professional Development This category supports short-term academic or professional research stays. Funding Details Award Amount: CAD $3,000 per month Maximum Duration: 4 months The V3 scholarship is suitable for: Researchers Graduate students Professionals seeking specialized research exposure Individuals pursuing academic collaboration opportunities Why This Scholarship Is Important The Québec Merit Scholarship Program offers more than just financial support. Significant Financial Support Recipients receive generous funding that can substantially reduce the financial burden of studying and conducting research in Canada. 2. Applicants are encouraged to: Research potential supervisors early Contact faculty members professionally Present a strong research proposal Demonstrate alignment with the professor’s research interests The Preselection Process Explained The scholarship selection process begins with internal preselection at a Québec university. Only candidates who are preselected by a participating Québec university will be invited by FQRNT to participate in the final selection round. How the Process Works Applicant identifies a supervising professor Applicant prepares required documents Candidate submits application to the Québec university Internal university review and preselection occur Selected candidates advance to FQRNT’s final evaluation stage The internal selection results are expected to be announced in late September. Application Deadline Université Laval Preselection Deadline Applicants seeking preselection through Université Laval must submit their applications by: June 17, 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparations early, especially when contacting supervisors and preparing research proposals. Final Thoughts The Québec Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students 2027–2028 is an exceptional opportunity for international students and researchers who aspire to study and conduct research in Canada. With generous funding, access to prestigious universities, and opportunities for international collaboration, this scholarship can significantly shape the future of emerging researchers and academic professionals. Applicants should begin preparations early, secure academic supervision, and ensure all application materials meet institutional and FQRNT requirements before the deadline. For highly motivated students and researchers worldwide, this scholarship could be the gateway to world-class education and research excellence in Québec. title: Young Voices for Europe 2026: Fully Funded Opportunity to Shape the Future EU Youth Strategy in Lyon, France
summary: Young people across Europe now have a rare opportunity to directly influence the future of youth policies in the European Union through the “Young Voices for Europe” Youth Policy Dialogue with Commissioner Glenn Micallef. This exciting opportunity is designed for young people who are passionate about creating meaningful change in society, improving youth participation, and ensuring that the voices of young Europeans are heard at the highest policy-making levels. title: Re-D Fund 2026: Microgrants for Civil Society Organizations Advancing Digital Democracy in East and Southeast Asia
summary: The Tifa Foundation has launched the Re-D Fund, a major regional funding initiative designed to strengthen digital democracy, civic participation, human rights advocacy, and organizational resilience across East and Southeast Asia. The Re-D Fund, which stands for “Reimagining Futures for Digital Democracy,” provides financial and non-financial support to civil society groups using digital technologies to address shrinking civic space and growing barriers to democratic participation in the digital era. The initiative seeks to empower marginalized and underrepresented groups by providing microgrants and ecosystem support for projects that strengthen civic freedoms, inclusive governance, advocacy, and democratic innovation. The programme is expected to support at least 100 local collaborators across the region, with a strong emphasis on women, youth, grassroots organizations, Indigenous Peoples, and gender minorities. Main Objectives of the Re-D Fund The programme seeks to ensure that local civil society groups in East and Southeast Asia gain equitable access to: Financial resources Capacity-building opportunities Support ecosystems Advocacy platforms Digital democracy tools The ultimate goal is to enable organizations to develop and implement strategies that strengthen democratic participation and civic resilience amid digital-era challenges. Who the Re-D Fund Supports The Re-D Fund prioritizes support for marginalized and underrepresented groups, including: Women-led organizations Youth groups Informal and grassroots movements Indigenous Peoples Gender minorities Community-based advocacy groups Civil society networks At least 50% of supported subgrantees are expected to come from marginalized communities. Advancing Reforms for Civic Freedoms This thematic area supports: Legal reforms Civic freedoms advocacy Democratic governance innovation Policy development Human rights protections Eligible activities include: Legal research Policy research Advocacy campaigns Human rights monitoring Transparency initiatives Policy dialogue forums Democratic innovation activities 2. Enhancing Civic Participation of Marginalized Groups This focus area supports initiatives that: Increase participation of excluded communities Strengthen digital inclusion Promote equitable civic engagement Amplify marginalized voices 3. Strengthening Civic Influence Projects under this category may include: Public engagement strategies Advocacy campaigns Community mobilization Civic technology solutions Coalition-building efforts 4. Fostering Holistic Resilience The programme supports organizational resilience through: Digital security Operational sustainability Community resilience models Crisis preparedness Organizational strengthening 5. Expanding Civil Society Resources This thematic track focuses on: Capacity building Resource-sharing systems Infrastructure development Digital ecosystem support Long-term sustainability Grant Structure The Re-D Fund will support: Two cohorts of subgrantees Approximately 50 subgrantees per cohort Cohort I Project implementation period: March 1 – May 31, 2026 Status: Open Cohort II Project implementation period: July 22 – October 23, 2026 Status: Open Application Deadline Applications for Cohort II must be submitted before: June 5, 2026 Applicants are encouraged to apply early and carefully review all eligibility and thematic requirements. Single Applications Applicants may receive up to: USD 5,000 Joint Applications (2+ Organizations) Collaborative applications may receive up to: USD 10,000 The joint application category encourages partnerships, coalition-building, and collaborative democratic innovation efforts. Why the Re-D Fund Matters Civil society organizations across East and Southeast Asia increasingly face: Political restrictions Funding barriers Digital surveillance Shrinking civic space Exclusion from decision-making processes The Re-D Fund addresses these challenges by supporting grassroots organizations that often struggle to access traditional funding systems. The initiative recognizes that marginalized communities are frequently the most affected by democratic decline and digital inequality, yet remain among the least funded. Key Benefits of the Re-D Fund Selected organizations benefit from: Direct financial support Increased visibility Ecosystem networking opportunities Support for digital democracy initiatives Access to collaborative regional partnerships Flexible support for innovative civic solutions What Makes This Fund Unique? The Re-D Fund stands out because it: Prioritizes marginalized communities Supports grassroots and informal groups Focuses on digital democracy Encourages collaborative applications Combines financial and non-financial support Emphasizes feminist, inclusive, and rights-based approaches About Tifa Foundation The Tifa Foundation is an Indonesian organization that promotes: Openness Diversity Equality Justice Democratic participation The organization works through: Strategic multi-stakeholder collaboration Local and international partnerships Constructive engagement approaches Resource provision and direct implementation Tifa Foundation plays a critical role in advancing civic participation and democratic resilience across the region. The position is based at the Medway Campus in the United Kingdom and provides a unique opportunity for researchers passionate about gender studies, food systems, participatory research, social justice, and sustainable development. Within the university, the Natural Resources Institute (NRI) serves as a specialist research institute focused on: Food systems Sustainable agriculture Livelihoods and institutions Social justice Climate resilience International development NRI collaborates extensively with partners across the Global South and supports evidence-driven initiatives that influence both policy and practice globally. title: Restless Development Uganda Consultancy Opportunity 2026: Remote Financial Capacity Building Consultancy for Youth-Led Organizations Funded by the AU-EU Youth Voices Lab
summary: Restless Development is inviting qualified consultants and consultancy teams to apply for an important remote consultancy opportunity focused on strengthening the financial management systems and institutional capacity of youth-led organizations in Uganda. The consultancy forms part of the AU-EU Youth Voices Lab – Power of the Collective (AU-EU YVL-PoC), a major four-year initiative co-funded by the European Union to support youth participation, governance, and inclusive development across Africa and Europe. This opportunity is ideal for experienced finance, accounting, compliance, and NGO management professionals with strong expertise in capacity building, financial systems strengthening, and organizational development for grassroots and youth-led organizations. The consultancy will run for three months and offers a total budget of UGX 16,000,000 / €4,000 , inclusive of taxes and professional fees. Applications close on Thursday, May 21, 2026, at 5:00 PM (E.A.T) . About Restless Development Restless Development Official Website is a globally recognized youth-led development agency committed to supporting young people to create a just, equitable, and sustainable world. Since 1985, the organization has worked with thousands of young people globally to: Promote youth leadership Strengthen civic engagement Advance climate justice Improve livelihoods and education Promote sexual and reproductive health rights Encourage inclusive governance Restless Development believes that young people are powerful agents of change and should be at the forefront of addressing local and global challenges. The organization operates across multiple countries and works closely with youth-led organizations, governments, civil society actors, and development partners. About the AU-EU Youth Voices Lab – Power of the Collective The AU-EU Youth Voices Lab – Power of the Collective (AU-EU YVL-PoC) is a four-year programme designed to build more inclusive societies in Africa and Europe by ensuring that youth voices are integrated into governance and policy-making processes. The programme focuses on: Youth participation in governance Civic engagement Leadership development Advocacy skills Institutional responsiveness to youth concerns The initiative is implemented through a consortium of respected international organizations, including: Oxfam Restless Development Search for Common Ground Youthmakers Hub Makesense Africa The programme equips young people with the tools and skills needed to advocate for their priorities at: Local levels National levels Regional levels Continental platforms It also works with institutions and policymakers to strengthen youth inclusion in governance systems. Background of the Consultancy As part of the programme implementation, 15 youth-led organizations were selected through a competitive funding process by the Youth Advisory Board and Restless Development. Following selection: Due diligence assessments were conducted Organizational capacity gaps were identified Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) were jointly developed with grantees The assessments identified several institutional and financial management challenges requiring external technical support. Some of the key identified needs include: Weak internal control systems Limited financial management tools Gaps in procurement systems Inadequate human resource policies Weak compliance structures Organizational governance challenges This consultancy therefore seeks to provide technical assistance and tailored capacity-building support to selected grantees. Objective of the Consultancy The consultant will help strengthen the institutional and financial management capacity of prioritized youth-led organizations funded under the programme. The main goal is to ensure that grantees: Improve financial accountability Strengthen compliance systems Develop sustainable internal control mechanisms Enhance institutional resilience Meet donor financial reporting requirements Key Responsibilities of the Consultant The selected consultant or consultancy team will undertake several important tasks. Review Existing Organizational Systems The consultant will review: Due diligence reports Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) Organizational structures Financial policies Administrative systems Human resource procedures Procurement systems This assessment will help determine the specific support required by each organization. Deliver Tailored Capacity Building Training The consultant will: Develop a training schedule Conduct customized training sessions Strengthen accountability mechanisms Build sustainable financial management systems The training should support the development of: Democratic organizations Legitimate governance structures Sustainable institutional systems Transparent financial processes Support Development of Internal Policies The consultant will work directly with grantees to co-create and strengthen: Financial policies Procurement policies Human resource policies Internal control systems Risk management frameworks This support aims to improve organizational governance and operational efficiency. Educational Qualifications Candidates should have: An advanced degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field CPA or ACCA certification is preferred Professional Experience Applicants must demonstrate: At least 5–7 years of relevant professional experience Experience managing EU-funded projects Experience working with international NGOs Proven expertise in financial management and compliance Previous experience conducting organizational capacity-building assignments Required Skills and Expertise The ideal consultant should have: Strong knowledge of internal controls and risk management Experience supporting grassroots organizations Change management expertise Familiarity with youth-led programming Experience working with NGOs and civil society organizations in Africa Strong facilitation and training skills Safeguarding Commitment Restless Development places strong emphasis on safeguarding and the protection of: Children Young people Vulnerable adults The organization expects all consultants, staff, volunteers, and partners to comply fully with safeguarding standards and policies to ensure communities are protected from harm. By supporting financial systems and governance structures, the selected consultant will help youth organizations: Become more resilient Improve donor compliance Strengthen transparency Scale their impact Sustain long-term development initiatives The consultancy also offers valuable experience working within an international consortium funded by the European Union. title: EU AMAL Project Grants 2026: Up to €40,000 Funding for Palestinian CSOs Advancing Gender & Disability-Inclusive Advocacy
summary: The European Union-funded AMAL – Amplifying Mobilization and Local Leadership Project has officially launched its 2026 Call for Proposals, offering critical funding and technical support for Palestinian civil society organizations working to strengthen gender equality, disability rights, inclusive governance, and equitable recovery efforts across Palestine. Implemented by Oxfam Novib in partnership with the Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) and the Atfaluna Society for Deaf Children (ASDC), the AMAL Project is a 36-month initiative running from January 2025 to December 2027. The program aims to empower local civil society organizations (CSOs), marginalized communities, women, youth, and persons with disabilities (PWDs) to actively shape inclusive governance and sustainable development processes in Palestine. This grant opportunity is particularly important for organizations seeking to influence humanitarian response, recovery, reconstruction, policy development, and community-led advocacy initiatives in the Gaza Strip, East Jerusalem, and the West Bank. About the EU AMAL Project The AMAL Project focuses on strengthening the leadership and operational capacity of Palestinian CSOs and marginalized communities by supporting inclusive services, advocacy initiatives, and recovery mechanisms. According to the guidelines, the project specifically targets women, youth, children, and persons with disabilities. The project’s broader objectives include: Enhancing empowerment and well-being among vulnerable populations through improved access to inclusive services. Supporting local CSOs and marginalized groups to influence key stakeholders and promote equitable recovery and reconstruction policies. Strengthening disability-inclusive and gender-responsive advocacy at community and policy levels. The initiative is designed to amplify local leadership and ensure that recovery and reconstruction processes meaningfully include marginalized voices, especially women and persons with disabilities. Funding Details The total funding available under this call amounts to €120,000 and will be distributed among 3–4 organizations. Individual grants will range between €30,000 and €40,000. Key Funding Information Total available funding: €120,000 Number of grants: 3–4 Grant size: €30,000–€40,000 Project duration: Up to 12 months Implementation period: August 2026 – July 2027 Geographic focus: Gaza Strip West Bank East Jerusalem Selected organizations will also participate in capacity-building activities, learning exchanges, and advocacy initiatives organized by Oxfam and project partners throughout the AMAL project cycle until December 2027. What Types of Organizations Can Apply? The call is open to Palestinian organizations with demonstrated experience in gender equality, disability rights, advocacy, and inclusive development. Eligible organizations include: Civil society organizations (CSOs) Women’s rights organizations (WROs) Community-based organizations (CBOs) Registered CSO networks Non-profit entities legally operating in Palestine Organizations must demonstrate: Experience in gender and disability advocacy Policy development expertise Stakeholder engagement capacity Strong partnerships and networks Financial and operational management systems Eligibility Criteria To qualify, applicants must meet several mandatory requirements. Organizational Requirements Applicants must: Be legally registered and recognized by relevant ministries Operate as a not-for-profit entity Have active bank accounts Have no unresolved tax issues Maintain accounting and financial management systems Employ at least one accountant Demonstrate expertise in gender and disability inclusion advocacy Required documentation includes: Registration certificates Tax clearance certificates Audit reports for the past two years Bank account certificates Organizational policies (if available), including safeguarding and anti-fraud policies Priority Areas and Approaches Priority will be given to organizations and projects that adopt: Rights-Based and Inclusive Approaches Projects should ensure meaningful participation of women and persons with disabilities while incorporating intersectionality and inclusive governance practices. Evidence-Based Advocacy Organizations are encouraged to design interventions backed by data, research, and policy analysis to strengthen disability rights and gender inclusion in humanitarian recovery systems. Participatory Community Engagement Projects should actively involve: Youth-led organizations Community-based organizations Persons with disabilities Women-led groups throughout planning and implementation processes. Localization and Community Leadership The AMAL Project strongly prioritizes locally led solutions and community ownership. Eligible Activities Applicants are encouraged to design innovative and context-specific activities aligned with the project objectives. Examples include: Community-Based Inclusion Initiatives Programs demonstrating practical gender and disability inclusion in humanitarian recovery efforts. Income-Generating Projects Economic empowerment initiatives targeting women and youth with disabilities. Capacity-Building Programs Training for local organizations and women-led groups on disability-inclusive approaches and advocacy methods. Creative Advocacy Campaigns Activities such as: Digital storytelling Social media advocacy Cultural campaigns Public awareness initiatives promoting the inclusion of women and persons with disabilities in reconstruction processes. Policy Dialogues and Strategic Meetings Engagement sessions with government institutions, humanitarian actors, and local stakeholders to strengthen inclusive policymaking. Participation in Conferences and Advocacy Events Projects may include participation in regional or national advocacy initiatives related to gender rights, disability inclusion, and equitable recovery. Ineligible Activities and Costs Certain activities and costs are not eligible for funding. Ineligible Activities Individual scholarships Standalone training scholarships Ineligible Costs Examples include: Debt servicing Currency exchange losses Land or building purchases Unconditional cash transfers Salaries of national administration staff Credits to third parties Performance-based bonuses Evaluation Criteria Applications will be reviewed by a five-member Grant Selection Committee. Projects will be assessed based on: Project Selection Criteria Relevance Feasibility Sustainability Cost-effectiveness Community involvement and accountability Applicant Selection Criteria Organizational mandate Demonstrated expertise Experience in target areas Coordination and partnerships Project management capacity Financial management systems Ethical standards and safeguarding policies Applications are scored on a scale from 1 to 5, ranging from “Insufficient” to “Excellent.” Why This Opportunity Matters The AMAL Grant Scheme arrives at a critical moment for Palestinian civil society. By supporting locally led advocacy, inclusive governance, and disability rights initiatives, the program empowers organizations to shape recovery and reconstruction systems that genuinely reflect community needs. Beyond financial support, the program offers opportunities for: Long-term advocacy engagement Policy influence Capacity strengthening Regional networking Community leadership development Organizations working in gender equality, disability rights, humanitarian response, and inclusive governance should strongly consider applying. Submission Email OPT.Subgrants@oxfam.org Subject Line Format Organization Name / EU AMAL Project Required Annexes Applicants must submit: Application Form – Narrative Application Form – Budget Eligibility Checklist Applications can be submitted in English or Arabic. All signed documents must be provided in both PDF and editable formats. title: Shapoorji Pallonji Scholarship 2026 at SOAS University of London: Fully Funded Master’s Opportunity in Zoroastrian Studies
summary: The SOAS University of London has officially opened applications for the prestigious Shapoorji Pallonji Scholarship 2026, a fully funded opportunity designed for exceptional students interested in pursuing advanced studies connected to Zoroastrianism and related interdisciplinary fields. This scholarship offers full tuition coverage along with a maintenance stipend for one year, making it one of the most valuable master’s funding opportunities currently available for students passionate about Iranian, Middle Eastern, South Asian, religious, political, and cultural studies. Funded through the generous Shapoorji Pallonji endowment for scholarships in Zoroastrian Studies at SOAS, the award seeks to support academically outstanding students from around the world who are eager to explore Zoroastrianism through diverse academic lenses including history, anthropology, linguistics, religion, and cultural studies. The application deadline for the scholarship is 29 May 2026 . About the Scholarship The Shapoorji Pallonji Scholarship is hosted by the SOAS Shapoorji Pallonji Institute of Zoroastrian Studies at SOAS University of London . The scholarship is available for students beginning full-time taught master’s programmes during the 2026/27 academic year. Selected scholars will receive: Full tuition fee coverage A maintenance stipend for living expenses Access to world-class academic resources at SOAS The opportunity to specialize in Zoroastrian Studies within a globally respected institution Exposure to interdisciplinary approaches to religion, politics, history, language, and society The scholarship aims to encourage innovative academic engagement with Zoroastrianism and related fields while supporting future researchers, scholars, and professionals in the humanities and social sciences. Eligible Master’s Programmes Applicants can choose from the following eligible one-year full-time master’s programmes: MA Iranian Studies MA Religion, Politics and Society MA South Asian Area Studies MA Middle Eastern Studies Students awarded the scholarship will also be required to complete: A compulsory 60-credit dissertation in Zoroastrianism The 30-credit module: “Zoroastrianism, Historical and Contemporary Perspectives” Additionally, students may choose to study an extra language module such as Avestan language studies. Scholarship Benefits The Shapoorji Pallonji Scholarship offers substantial academic and financial support, including: 1. Full Tuition Coverage The scholarship fully covers tuition fees for the selected master’s programme. 2. Maintenance Stipend Recipients also receive financial support toward living costs during their studies in London. 3. Academic Development Students gain access to internationally respected faculty, specialized research opportunities, and interdisciplinary learning environments. 4. Research Opportunities The programme supports students interested in: Historical studies Religious studies Anthropology Linguistics Cultural studies Middle Eastern and South Asian studies 5. Global Recognition Studying at SOAS offers international academic exposure and networking opportunities within global research communities. Who Can Apply? The scholarship is open to both: Home students Overseas/international students Applicants from any country may apply provided they meet the academic and admission requirements. Academic Requirements To qualify, applicants should: Hold or expect to receive a first-class honours degree from a UK university or an international equivalent Demonstrate strong academic excellence through transcripts and references Have applied for an eligible master’s programme at SOAS Meet English language requirements if applicable Applicants with a 2:1 degree classification may still apply, although preference is generally given to candidates with first-class academic performance. Important Admission Conditions Applicants should note the following carefully: You do not need to receive an admission offer before submitting your scholarship application. However, you must obtain an unconditional admission offer before the scholarship selection panel meets. English language conditions must also be fulfilled before final consideration. Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply for admission as early as possible because programme assessments may take: Up to 4 weeks under normal circumstances Up to 6 weeks during busy periods Late or incomplete scholarship applications will not be considered. Scholarship Deadline Scholarship Application Deadline: 29 May 2026 (12 noon UK local time) Applicants are advised to complete both: Their programme application Their scholarship application well before the deadline to avoid delays. How to Apply Step 1: Apply for an Eligible Master’s Programme Candidates must first submit an application for one of the eligible master’s programmes at SOAS. Step 2: Apply for the Scholarship After applying for admission, applicants can access the scholarship application through the SOAS admissions portal using their login credentials. Applicants who cannot see the scholarship option in the portal should verify that they meet all eligibility requirements. Candidate Assessment Process Applications will be reviewed based on: Academic excellence Personal statement quality Proposed area of study References and transcripts Overall suitability for Zoroastrian Studies research The scholarship selection panel will carefully assess each candidate’s academic potential and alignment with the objectives of the programme. Notification of Results The scholarship selection process is expected to conclude around the end of May 2026 or shortly afterward. Successful candidates will be contacted first. Unsuccessful applicants will be notified once all awards have been allocated. Why This Scholarship Matters The Shapoorji Pallonji Scholarship represents a major opportunity for students interested in exploring religion, culture, history, politics, and society through an interdisciplinary and globally relevant perspective. With rising international tuition costs, fully funded opportunities like this are highly competitive and valuable. The programme also allows students to engage deeply with Zoroastrian traditions and their influence across regions such as Iran, South Asia, and the Middle East. For students seeking careers in academia, policy, cultural studies, international relations, religious studies, or heritage research, this scholarship can serve as a transformative academic pathway.
