title: Microsoft Student Ambassadors Program 2026: Learn AI Skills, Leadership, and Real-World Experience
summary: The Microsoft Student Ambassadors Program 2026 is opening a new chapter by offering students from all disciplines the opportunity to build AI skills, leadership experience, and real-world project portfolios—without a competitive application process. This reimagined program removes traditional barriers and creates a more inclusive pathway for students worldwide to engage with emerging technologies and innovation. About the Program For over two decades, the Microsoft Student Ambassadors program has supported student developers in gaining technical and leadership skills. In 2026, the program has been redesigned to reflect the changing nature of work and technology, especially the growing importance of artificial intelligence across all fields. The updated program is no longer limited to students with coding or technical backgrounds. Instead, it welcomes learners from diverse academic disciplines, recognizing that the future of AI will be shaped by people with varied perspectives, skills, and experiences. What makes this program particularly unique is its open-access model. There is no formal application or interview process. Students simply sign up, complete onboarding steps, and begin participating in activities aligned with their interests. Participants engage in hands-on learning experiences, including building projects, creating educational content, hosting events, and contributing to a global student community. As they progress, they unlock additional benefits, leadership opportunities, and deeper engagement with Microsoft teams. Why This Opportunity Matters The shift toward open access and interdisciplinary participation represents a significant change in how global tech programs operate. Traditionally, opportunities in technology have been highly competitive and often limited to specific academic paths. Microsoft’s approach challenges this model by prioritizing accessibility, inclusivity, and practical learning. In a world where AI is rapidly transforming industries, students need more than theoretical knowledge. They need opportunities to experiment, collaborate, and apply their skills in real-world contexts. This program provides exactly that. By removing barriers such as applications and interviews, the program ensures that motivated students—regardless of background—can begin building relevant skills immediately. It also reflects a broader trend in education and employment, where demonstrated skills and experience are becoming just as important as formal qualifications. What Participants Will Gain Participants in the Microsoft Student Ambassadors program gain access to a wide range of tools, experiences, and professional development opportunities. One of the most valuable aspects is hands-on experience with industry-leading technologies. Students receive access to tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Visual Studio Enterprise, and monthly Azure credits, enabling them to experiment with AI and cloud-based solutions. Beyond technical tools, the program emphasizes leadership and community engagement. Students can organize events, mentor peers, and contribute to educational initiatives that help others build skills. These experiences are critical for developing communication, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities. As participants progress, they unlock opportunities to engage directly with Microsoft teams through short-term, immersive experiences. These engagements provide insight into how real-world products are developed, offering exposure to industry practices and decision-making processes. Importantly, the program helps students build a strong professional profile. By completing projects, contributing to the community, and demonstrating impact, participants can create a portfolio that strengthens their CV and LinkedIn presence. Who Can Apply The program is open to students from all academic disciplines enrolled in higher education institutions worldwide. There is no requirement for prior technical experience, making it accessible to beginners as well as more advanced learners. Students who are curious about AI, motivated to learn through practical experience, and interested in contributing to their communities are especially encouraged to join. Eligible Areas The Microsoft Student Ambassadors program is available globally, although some regional restrictions may apply depending on local availability and institutional participation. Application Process and Deadline The application process is designed to be simple and accessible. Students can join by visiting the official Microsoft Student Ambassadors platform and selecting “Get Started.” After completing a short sign-up process, participants can immediately begin engaging with program activities. There is no fixed deadline, as the program operates on a rolling basis. Students can join at any time and progress through milestones at their own pace. title: CaribOx Visiting Fellowship & Travel Grants 2027: Funded Research Collaboration with the University of Oxford
summary: The CaribOx Visiting Fellowship Travel Grants 2027 offer fully funded opportunities for Caribbean-based researchers to collaborate with the University of Oxford while advancing their academic work. Designed for scholars across disciplines, this initiative provides funding, institutional access, and international research exposure through both long-term fellowships and short-term research visits. About the Program The Caribbean Oxford Initiative (CaribOx), led by TORCH , is a collaborative programme that connects researchers from Caribbean institutions with academic partners at Oxford. It aims to strengthen global research partnerships while amplifying Caribbean scholarship across disciplines. For 2027, the programme offers two main pathways: the Visiting Fellowship Scheme and Travel Grants. The Visiting Fellowship provides a 12-month engagement, combining ten months of virtual collaboration with a two-month in-person residency at Oxford during Trinity Term (April to June 2027). Fellows receive full financial support, including return flights, accommodation, a daily stipend, and access to Oxford’s academic resources. The Travel Grants, on the other hand, support shorter research stays of two to four weeks at Oxford. These grants are ideal for researchers seeking targeted collaboration, archival work, or participation in academic activities during the same term period. Both pathways are designed to foster meaningful academic exchange while removing financial barriers to international collaboration. Why This Opportunity Matters Access to global research networks remains uneven, particularly for scholars based in underrepresented regions. The CaribOx programme directly addresses this gap by investing in Caribbean researchers and enabling them to engage with one of the world’s leading academic institutions. By facilitating collaboration with Oxford-based scholars, the programme helps bridge geographic and institutional divides. It also ensures that Caribbean perspectives contribute to global academic conversations, strengthening diversity in research and knowledge production. Additionally, the initiative emphasizes inclusion by encouraging applications from researchers from minoritized backgrounds and those with non-traditional academic paths. What Participants Will Gain Participants benefit from more than just funding—they gain long-term academic value and global exposure. Fellows and grant recipients will have the opportunity to develop strong international research collaborations, which can lead to joint publications, future funding opportunities, and sustained academic partnerships. Access to Oxford’s libraries, resources, and academic community provides a significant boost to research quality and output. The in-person residency allows participants to immerse themselves in a world-class academic environment, attend seminars, and engage directly with leading experts in their field. At the same time, the structured virtual engagement ensures continuity and long-term collaboration beyond the physical visit. Financially, the programme removes key barriers by covering travel, accommodation, and living expenses, enabling researchers to focus entirely on their work. Who Can Apply The programme is open to researchers across all academic disciplines who are based at Caribbean research institutions. For the Visiting Fellowship, applicants must hold a PhD (or equivalent), be employed by a Caribbean academic institution, and have an existing or potential collaboration with an Oxford-based researcher. For the Travel Grants, eligibility is broader, covering doctoral students through to mid-career researchers, including those without a doctorate in certain cases. Applicants must demonstrate a clear research plan and show how participation will contribute to their academic development. Eligible Areas Applicants must be legal residents of Caribbean countries, including the Windward and Leeward Islands. They must also be affiliated with an academic institution within the region. All participants are required to comply with UK visa regulations, including a commitment to return to their home country after completing the programme. Application Process and Deadline Applications for both the Visiting Fellowship and Travel Grants must be submitted via email. For the Visiting Fellowship, applicants must secure a statement of support from an Oxford-based collaborator, submit a completed application form, provide a CV, and include a letter of support from their home institution. For the Travel Grants, applicants are required to submit an application form and CV outlining their research objectives and planned activities. The deadline for both opportunities is 15 September 2026 at 17:00 BST . Late or incomplete applications will not be considered, so early preparation is strongly advised. title: UNICEF Young Pasifika Wayfinders 2026: Join a Regional Youth Advisory Group and Shape Pacific Future
summary: The UNICEF Young Pasifika Wayfinders 2026 programme offers adolescent boys across the Pacific a unique opportunity to engage in youth advocacy, influence regional initiatives, and contribute to programmes that impact children and communities. Designed for young leaders aged 15–19, this initiative provides a platform to amplify youth voices while building skills in leadership, communication, and social impact. About the Program The Young Pasifika Wayfinders (YPW) is a regional advisory group launched by UNICEF in 2025 to ensure that adolescent boys are actively involved in shaping programmes, campaigns, and advocacy efforts across the Pacific. The initiative focuses on meaningful youth participation by engaging boys directly in conversations and actions around issues that affect their lives. Members work alongside UNICEF and other youth organisations to co-create solutions, challenge harmful stereotypes, and promote positive, inclusive models of masculinity. The programme covers a wide range of topics relevant to young people in the Pacific, including mental health, gender equality, bullying prevention, online safety, education, and healthy relationships. It also addresses emerging challenges such as climate change, rising health concerns, and social inequalities. The next phase of the programme will run from July 2026 to December 2027, and UNICEF is currently expanding its membership to include new participants from across the region. Why This Opportunity Matters Youth voices—especially those of boys and young men—are often underrepresented in discussions around social change and development. This programme directly addresses that gap by creating a structured platform for adolescent boys to participate in decision-making processes that affect their communities. By engaging youth in advocacy and programme design, UNICEF is strengthening community-led solutions and ensuring that interventions are relevant, inclusive, and effective. The initiative also contributes to broader efforts to redefine masculinity in the Pacific, promoting values such as respect, equality, and emotional wellbeing. For participants, this is more than a volunteer role—it is an opportunity to contribute to real change while developing a strong sense of purpose and leadership. What Participants Will Gain Participants in the Young Pasifika Wayfinders programme will gain valuable personal and professional development opportunities. Members receive training and mentorship from regional experts in youth advocacy, public speaking, and leadership. They also participate in workshops covering key topics such as mental health, digital safety, gender equality, and social impact. In addition to skill-building, participants will have opportunities to engage in regional and national events, collaborate with other youth networks, and contribute to campaigns and initiatives that reach a wide audience. All programme-related costs are covered by UNICEF, including travel, accommodation, meals, and visas for in-person workshops. This ensures that participants can fully engage in the experience regardless of their financial situation. Through their involvement, members will also strengthen their confidence, expand their networks, and gain hands-on experience in advocacy and community engagement. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to adolescent boys aged 15 to 19 years. Applicants must be from one of the following UNICEF Pacific Island countries: Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu, or Vanuatu. Young people living with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply, and UNICEF provides full support to ensure accessibility and inclusion throughout the programme. Eligible Areas The programme is specifically designed for youth from Pacific Island countries supported by UNICEF. Participation includes both online engagement and in-person regional activities within the Pacific. Application Process and Deadline Interested applicants are encouraged to review the programme details and eligibility criteria before completing the application form. Shortlisted candidates under the age of 18 will be required to provide parental or guardian consent. Selected participants must also commit to the full duration of the programme, which runs for approximately 18 months. The application period is open from 15 April to 30 April 2026. Late applications will not be considered. Learn more and apply on the official UNICEF Pacific Islands website . title: European Commission Internal Security Fund CEEP 2026: Up to €1.5M Grants for Civil Society Projects Combating Online Extremism
summary: The EU Internal Security Fund (ISF) CEEP Grant 2026 offers up to €1.5 million in funding for civil society-led projects aimed at preventing online radicalisation and strengthening community resilience across Europe. Designed for organisations working at the intersection of youth engagement, digital safety, and social cohesion, this opportunity supports collaborative, high-impact initiatives across multiple EU countries. About the Program The Community Engagement and Empowerment Programme (CEEP), funded under the Internal Security Fund (ISF), is a European Commission initiative focused on preventing and countering radicalisation that can lead to violent extremism and terrorism. Building on previous EU efforts such as the Civil Society Empowerment Programme (CSEP) and the Radicalisation Awareness Network (RAN), this call supports projects that address the growing risks associated with online radicalisation—particularly among youth and vulnerable communities. The program encourages evidence-based, participatory approaches that combine both online and offline interventions. Projects are expected to actively involve communities in their design and implementation, ensuring that solutions are grounded in real-world needs and experiences. With a total budget of €5 million, the call will fund several large-scale projects that demonstrate strong collaboration, innovation, and long-term impact. Why This Opportunity Matters Online spaces are increasingly being used to spread extremist ideologies, often targeting young people through sophisticated and emotionally engaging content. Addressing this challenge requires more than top-down interventions—it demands community-driven, inclusive, and sustainable solutions. This funding opportunity recognizes the critical role that civil society organisations play in prevention efforts. By supporting cross-border collaboration, the program enables organisations to share knowledge, scale effective practices, and respond more strategically to evolving threats. It also reflects a broader shift in EU policy toward prevention, resilience-building, and youth empowerment as central pillars in combating radicalisation. What Participants Will Gain This grant provides both financial and strategic benefits for participating organisations. Selected projects will receive substantial funding—ranging from €1 million to €1.5 million per project—with up to 90% of eligible costs covered. This allows organisations to implement ambitious, multi-year initiatives without bearing the full financial burden. Beyond funding, participants will gain the opportunity to: Build strong international partnerships across at least three EU Member States Engage directly with youth, educators, and community leaders in co-created initiatives Develop and scale innovative approaches to digital resilience and prevention Strengthen organisational capacity in research, monitoring, and evaluation Increase visibility and credibility through EU-supported programming Projects will also benefit from structured frameworks for impact measurement, ensuring that outcomes are not only achieved but clearly demonstrated. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to consortia of organisations rather than individual applicants. To be eligible, applications must include at least three organisations from three different EU Member States. Importantly, at least two of these must be civil society organisations. Eligible participants may include non-profits, NGOs, research institutions, and other relevant entities working in areas such as youth engagement, education, digital safety, or community development. Denmark is not eligible to participate in this call. Eligible Areas Projects must be implemented within EU Member States and may also involve relevant priority third countries, depending on the scope and partnerships. The program supports initiatives aligned with the following priority areas: Digital resilience and critical thinking online Strengthening community trust and social cohesion Addressing multiple forms of extremism, including jihadist and far-right narratives Youth empowerment and peer-led prevention strategies Inclusive, co-created approaches involving affected communities Application Process and Deadline Applications must be submitted through the EU Funding Tenders Portal using a structured online system. The submission process involves registering all participating organisations, preparing a detailed project proposal (including technical description, budget, and supporting documents), and uploading all required materials before the deadline. Proposals are evaluated based on three main criteria: Relevance (30 points) – alignment with program objectives and EU priorities Quality (50 points) – methodology, feasibility, and consortium strength Impact (20 points) – expected outcomes, sustainability, and scalability To be considered for funding, proposals must score at least 21 out of 30 in relevance and a minimum of 70 out of 100 overall. The final deadline to apply is 27 May 2026 at 17:00 CET . Late submissions will not be accepted. See all the requirements and apply on the official European Commission website . title: NASA FINESST 2025 Research Grants for Graduate Students in Earth and Space Science
summary: The NASA FINESST 2025 funding opportunity provides Master’s and PhD students in Earth and space science with direct support to lead their own independent research projects. As part of NASA’s Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) program, FINESST is designed to empower the next generation of researchers to develop innovative scientific ideas that advance understanding of Earth systems, space environments, and planetary science. This opportunity is specifically targeted at graduate students, offering them the chance to secure funding, gain research experience, and contribute to NASA’s long-term scientific missions. About the Program FINESST (Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology) is a competitive graduate student research program funded by NASA. It supports students pursuing Master’s and PhD degrees who are conducting research aligned with NASA’s Science Mission Directorate priorities. Unlike large institutional grants, FINESST is designed to directly fund students as principal investigators of their own research proposals. This makes it a unique opportunity in the academic landscape, allowing students to take ownership of scientific projects while receiving financial support and mentorship through their academic institutions. The program is part of NASA’s broader commitment to strengthening early-career scientific talent and ensuring continued innovation in Earth and space sciences. Why This Opportunity Matters Graduate research often depends on limited funding and institutional resources. FINESST addresses this gap by giving students the independence and financial backing to pursue original scientific questions without relying entirely on faculty-led funding structures. This program plays a key role in shaping future leaders in Earth observation, climate science, astrophysics, and planetary exploration. By supporting student-led research, NASA ensures that emerging scientists can contribute fresh perspectives to some of the most important scientific challenges of our time, including climate change, environmental monitoring, and space exploration. For students, FINESST is more than a grant — it is an entry point into NASA’s research ecosystem and a foundation for long-term academic and professional growth. What Participants Will Gain Selected applicants receive funding to support their research activities over multiple years, including data collection, analysis, fieldwork, and computational modeling. Beyond funding, participants gain the opportunity to develop independent research leadership skills, strengthen their academic profiles, and build connections within NASA’s scientific community. The program also enhances competitiveness for future fellowships, postdoctoral positions, and research careers. Students benefit from working on high-impact scientific questions while contributing to research that supports NASA’s missions and global scientific understanding. Who Can Apply FINESST is open to students enrolled in Master’s or PhD programs at accredited institutions. Applicants must be graduate students at the time of submission and must submit proposals through their academic institution. Each proposal must be student-led, with faculty advisors providing guidance but not serving as principal investigators. International students enrolled at eligible U.S. institutions may also be able to participate, depending on institutional eligibility. Eligible Areas Proposals must align with NASA’s Science Mission Directorate, which includes: Earth Science (climate systems, environment, natural hazards) Heliophysics (Sun–Earth interactions and space weather) Planetary Science (solar system formation and exploration) Astrophysics (universe, galaxies, and cosmic phenomena) Biological and Physical Sciences (effects of space environments on systems) Research can include theoretical work, data analysis, modeling, laboratory studies, or observational science. Application Process and Deadline Applications must be submitted electronically through NASA’s NSPIRES system. Students are required to prepare a detailed research proposal outlining objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes, along with a supporting budget and institutional documentation. The submission deadline for FINESST 2025 is July 14, 2026 . Office hours will be held by NASA Earth Science teams on June 23 and June 24 (1–2 PM ET) for applicants seeking clarification. Proposals undergo peer review based on scientific merit, feasibility, and relevance to NASA’s mission priorities. Successful applicants are typically notified several months after submission. title: South Africa–Canada Seed Grant for Collaborative Research 2026 | Funding for International Research Partnerships
summary: The South Africa–Canada Seed Grant for Collaborative Research offers researchers a unique opportunity to secure funding while building impactful international partnerships between South Africa and Canada. Designed for PhD-level researchers, this program supports collaborative projects that address global challenges through interdisciplinary research and capacity development. About the Program Launched through a partnership between the National Research Foundation (NRF) of South Africa and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) of Canada, this initiative strengthens academic collaboration under the South Africa–Canada Universities Network (SACUN). The program aims to foster long-term research relationships by supporting joint projects between researchers affiliated with eligible institutions in both countries. Up to eight projects will be funded, with each focusing on shared global priorities. Funded projects will run for 24 to 36 months , beginning in late 2026, and will support a wide range of collaborative activities such as joint publications, workshops, conferences, and research exchanges. Why This Opportunity Matters International collaboration is increasingly essential for addressing complex global challenges such as climate change, inequality, and technological transformation. This grant provides a structured pathway for researchers to build meaningful cross-border partnerships while contributing to impactful, real-world solutions. Beyond funding, the program strengthens academic networks, promotes knowledge exchange, and supports inclusive research ecosystems. It also emphasizes capacity building, particularly for emerging researchers, making it a strategic opportunity for long-term academic growth. What Participants Will Gain Participants in this program benefit from both financial support and professional development opportunities that extend beyond a single project. Researchers will gain access to: Funding to support collaborative research activities and mobility Opportunities to build and expand international research networks Experience working on interdisciplinary and globally relevant topics Increased visibility through joint publications and research outputs Capacity-building opportunities for early-career researchers and students For South African teams, funding can reach up to ZAR 300,000 per year for three years , while Canadian researchers may receive up to CAD $100,000 over two years , with the possibility of a one-year extension. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to researchers who meet specific academic and institutional requirements in both countries. Eligible Areas Projects must align with one of the program’s priority themes, which reflect shared global and national interests: Just and Resilient Societies Environmental Sustainability Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation Sustainable Economic Growth Mathematics Education Interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches are strongly encouraged, particularly those that integrate social sciences and humanities perspectives. Application Process and Deadline Applications must be submitted through a joint process led by the South African Principal Investigator via the NRF online system. Required documents include: CVs of all project partners Detailed project description Comprehensive budget breakdown Letters of intent from all collaborators The application deadline is May 28, 2026 , with institutional submissions due shortly after. Selected projects are expected to begin in October 2026 . Given the competitive nature of the program and the limited number of funded projects, applicants are encouraged to develop strong, well-structured proposals that clearly demonstrate collaboration, impact, and feasibility. title: UNESCO Science Club Challenge 2026 (African Edition): Empowering Young Innovators Across Africa
summary: The UNESCO Science Club Challenge 2026 – African Edition is now open for applications, offering an exciting opportunity for science clubs across Africa to showcase their impact, innovation, and commitment to STEM education. What is the UK Youth Fund? The UK Youth Fund is a strategic funding initiative focused on empowering small organisations that deliver vital services to young people. This approach recognizes that grassroots organisations are best positioned to understand their own challenges and opportunities, enabling them to: Strengthen core operations Invest in innovation Improve long-term sustainability Expand their impact on young people The fund builds on a successful partnership between UK Youth and Pears Foundation, which has already delivered impactful programmes such as the COVID Relief Fund (£2.2 million) and the Cost-of-Living Fund (£7 million) . Increased Capability and Organisational Resilience Through capacity-building support, organisations can: Strengthen internal systems Improve leadership and governance Enhance service delivery for young people Funding Details Eligible organisations can apply for multi-year unrestricted funding of up to: 10% of their annual turnover This proportional funding model ensures: Fair distribution of resources Sustainability aligned with organisational size Long-term financial resilience Organisations are encouraged to use the funding in ways that maximize impact, whether through: Operational strengthening Programme development Innovation initiatives Who Can Apply? title: Metropolis Mentoring Program 2026: Migration Mentorship Opportunity for Emerging Leaders

Each mentoring pair will be carefully matched based on professional experience, thematic interests, and development goals. The pilot cohort will include six mentoring pairs, with structured engagement supported by session templates, conversation frameworks, and curated resources to ensure consistency and impact throughout the program. Why This Opportunity Matters Migration systems worldwide are increasingly complex, requiring leaders who can respond to displacement, diversity, and integration challenges with evidence-based and inclusive approaches. However, many emerging professionals lack access to experienced mentors who can guide them through sector-specific challenges and career pathways. This program addresses that gap by creating structured mentorship relationships that support reflective practice, knowledge transfer, and leadership development. By connecting professionals across government, academia, community organisations, and international institutions, the initiative strengthens collaboration and improves the overall capacity of the migration and settlement sector. It also contributes to building more equitable leadership pathways by supporting diverse voices, including those with lived experience of migration and displacement, Indigenous perspectives, and diaspora leadership. What Participants Will Gain Participants in the Metropolis Mentoring Program 2026 will benefit from structured, meaningful professional development designed to support long-term career growth and sector impact. Mentees will gain personalised guidance tailored to their career goals, helping them navigate professional challenges, strengthen leadership skills, and build confidence in their chosen field. They will also develop clearer career direction through regular reflective conversations and practical advice from experienced mentors. Mentors will have the opportunity to contribute to leadership development in the migration sector while sharing expertise, expanding their professional networks, and engaging in reflective practice that strengthens their own leadership approach. Both mentors and mentees will benefit from structured sessions supported by conversation frameworks and tools designed to ensure productive engagement. The program also encourages networking within the wider Metropolis community, offering additional opportunities for professional exchange and collaboration. Who Can Apply The program is open to professionals working in migration, settlement, multicultural affairs, and related sectors. This includes individuals working in academic and research institutions, government agencies, non-governmental organisations, civil society, private sector organisations, and international bodies. Mentees are typically early-career professionals seeking guidance to advance their work and leadership development. Mentors are experienced practitioners committed to supporting the growth of emerging leaders through structured knowledge-sharing and professional mentorship. Eligible Areas Participants may work across a range of thematic areas, including women in leadership and migration policy, lived experience of displacement or migration, Indigenous and decolonial perspectives, and diaspora and community leadership. These themes ensure the program reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key challenges in global migration systems. Application Process and Deadline Applications for the Metropolis Mentoring Program Pilot are open through an Expression of Interest process. title: AI for Reproductive Health in Sub-Saharan Africa Innovation Challenge 2026
summary: The AI for Reproductive Health Innovation Challenge 2026 offers an opportunity for multidisciplinary teams across Sub-Saharan Africa to develop AI-powered solutions addressing critical maternal and reproductive health challenges while gaining technical experience, mentorship, and funding support. Across Sub-Saharan Africa, reproductive health outcomes continue to be shaped by persistent systemic and behavioral challenges. Issues such as delayed care-seeking, limited access to accurate information, high contraceptive discontinuation, and gaps in post-pregnancy loss care highlight the urgent need for innovative solutions. This innovation challenge is designed for young professionals, researchers, and technologists who want to apply their skills to real-world health problems and contribute to improving health systems through technology. About the Program The AI for Reproductive Health Innovation Challenge is a regional initiative organized by the Infectious Diseases Institute (IDI) and the African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC), with support from international partners including AI4D, IDRC, and FCDO. The program brings together multidisciplinary teams to co-design, prototype, and test AI-enabled solutions using real-world datasets. Over the course of a four-week virtual innovation sprint, participants will engage in structured activities including a needs assessment, expert-led capacity-building sessions, regular mentorship check-ins, and final project presentations. Participants are required to select one of two thematic tracks. The first track focuses on improving access to comprehensive early pregnancy loss care, addressing gaps in service delivery, referral systems, and timely treatment. The second track centers on empowering informed contraceptive decision-making by developing intelligent tools that help individuals choose suitable methods based on their health profiles and personal circumstances. Why This Opportunity Matters Reproductive health challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa remain a significant public health concern, with preventable maternal deaths and limited access to essential services still prevalent in many regions. At the same time, advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science offer new possibilities to address these issues at scale. This innovation challenge creates a platform where technical expertise and health knowledge intersect. By bringing together professionals from diverse backgrounds, the program encourages the development of context-specific, culturally relevant, and scalable solutions. It also supports capacity building among African innovators, helping to strengthen local expertise and reduce reliance on external solutions. What Participants Will Gain Participants in the innovation challenge will benefit from a combination of practical experience, technical development, and professional exposure. Teams will gain hands-on experience working with real-world datasets and applying AI tools to solve complex health problems. The program provides access to mentorship from experts in data science, healthcare, and digital innovation, helping participants refine their ideas and improve the quality of their solutions. Capacity-building webinars and technical sessions will strengthen participants’ analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in applying AI to health contexts. In addition to skill development, participants will have the opportunity to build meaningful collaborations across disciplines, expanding their professional networks. title: Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge 2026: A Comprehensive Opportunity for High School and University Students Worldwide
summary: The Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge 2026 is an exciting international academic competition designed to prepare the next generation of scientists, innovators, and critical thinkers for a rapidly advancing quantum future. Open to both high school and university students worldwide, this prestigious challenge provides a unique platform to test knowledge, develop analytical skills, and engage deeply with one of the most transformative fields in modern science: quantum mechanics. As quantum technologies continue to reshape industries ;from computing and cryptography to healthcare and materials science ;opportunities like this challenge serve as vital stepping stones for young minds aiming to make meaningful contributions in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Overview of the Competition Structure The Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge 2026 is structured into three rigorous and intellectually stimulating rounds: the Qualification Round, Semi-Final Round, and Final Exam. Each phase is carefully designed to progressively deepen participants’ understanding of quantum mechanics while testing both theoretical knowledge and practical problem-solving abilities. Qualification Round (Ongoing) The Qualification Round is currently open and accessible to all eligible students across the globe. Participants are required to solve five quantum mechanics problems independently from home. These problems are a mix of conceptual questions and calculation-based challenges, covering fundamental topics in quantum physics. Each problem carries 5 points, and participants must achieve a minimum score ;12, 14, or 17 points depending on their age group ;to advance to the Semi-Final Round. This flexible scoring system ensures fairness across varying educational levels. Importantly, all participants receive official participation certificates, recognizing their effort and engagement. Additionally, those who submit digitally typed solutions may receive special notes, highlighting the quality and clarity of their work. Semi-Final Round (July 2026) Students who successfully qualify proceed to the Semi-Final Round, which introduces a more advanced level of academic rigor. Participants will engage with real research papers in quantum physics, allowing them to experience how theoretical concepts are applied in actual scientific studies. This stage consists of a supervised 60-minute examination. All necessary materials will be provided via email and participant accounts on Friday, 24 July 2026. A registration fee of 12 EUR applies for this round; however, financial aid is available to support students from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, ensuring inclusivity and accessibility. Final Exam (25 August 2026) The Final Round represents the pinnacle of the competition. Scheduled for Tuesday, 25 August 2026, this globally coordinated exam challenges participants with approximately 30 questions in various formats, including multiple-choice and free-response problems. Participants are expected to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of quantum mechanics, drawing from both foundational principles and insights gained in earlier rounds. Why Participate in the Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge? Participation in this challenge offers far-reaching benefits beyond the competition itself. Academic Growth and Knowledge Expansion Students will explore key quantum concepts such as wave mechanics, quantum tunneling, and spin dynamics. Exposure to real scientific literature in the Semi-Final Round further prepares participants for advanced academic and research pursuits. Development of Critical Thinking and Creativity The competition features original problems crafted by domain experts, encouraging participants to think innovatively and approach challenges from multiple perspectives. This nurtures creativity and sharpens analytical reasoning—skills that are essential in any scientific career. Global Community and Networking Participants become part of a vibrant global network of like-minded students who share a passion for quantum science. This sense of community fosters collaboration, inspiration, and long-term academic connections. Recognition, Awards, and Prizes The competition boasts a total prize pool exceeding $1,500 USD. Awards include International Gold (top 5%), Silver (top 15%), and Bronze (top 30%) medals for each age group. Additional recognitions include National Awards for top performers in each country, as well as special Ambassador, Teacher, and School Awards. All participants, regardless of performance, receive official certificates acknowledging their participation and achievement. Additional Opportunities for Engagement The Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge extends beyond student participation by offering roles for teachers and student leaders. Teachers can register to supervise students, access teaching materials, monitor progress, and qualify for Teacher Awards. Schools can also partner with the program to facilitate group participation. Student leaders have the opportunity to become ambassadors, promoting the competition within their schools or regions. Ambassadors receive official certification, recognition on global platforms, and priority consideration for financial aid. The Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge 2026 is more than a competition; it is a transformative academic journey that equips students with the knowledge, skills, and global exposure needed to thrive in the future of science and technology. With its inclusive structure, valuable rewards, and emphasis on real-world application, it stands as a premier opportunity for any student interested in exploring the fascinating world of quantum mechanics. Students are encouraged to take advantage of this opportunity and submit their solutions before the deadline to begin their journey into the quantum future. summary: The YIM Macro Research Fellowship 2026–2027 presents a unique and intellectually rigorous opportunity for students and recent graduates who are passionate about influencing policy, advancing mental health systems, and exploring the intersection of technology and social impact. title: Grocers’ Charity Grant 2026: Funding Opportunity for UK Charities Supporting Communities, Health, and Social Impact

summary: The second Call for Proposals under the Migration and Mobility Dialogue (MMD) Grant Facility has officially been launched on April 7, 2026 , offering a strategic funding opportunity for organizations working at the intersection of migration, policy, research, and international cooperation . Overview of the MMD Grant Facility The MMD Grant Facility is designed to support short-term, high-impact projects that contribute to: Strengthening migration and mobility dialogues Enhancing policy coherence and cooperation Generating research and knowledge outputs Addressing emerging migration-related challenges This second call builds on the success of previous initiatives and continues to promote cross-regional collaboration between Africa and Europe . Funding Details The total indicative budget allocated for this call is: EUR 600,000 Individual grants will range between: EUR 100,000 and EUR 150,000 Importantly, the program allows: Up to 100% funding of eligible project costs , where properly justified This makes the grant particularly accessible to non-profit organizations and research institutions with limited co-financing capacity. Scope of Eligible Projects Projects submitted under this call must align with the overarching goals of the MMD framework. Specifically, eligible actions should: 1. Support Migration Dialogues Contribute to the operationalization of key migration frameworks, including: Rabat Process Khartoum Process C2CMMD 2. Generate Knowledge and Policy Input Projects should produce: Research outputs Policy recommendations Data-driven insights 3. Align with Strategic Priorities Actions must align with one or more domains of the: Joint Valletta Action Plan Or address transversal themes such as: Climate-induced migration Migration and gender Migration and health Geographic Scope and Implementation Projects must: Be implemented in up to three countries Include at least one African Union Member State Optionally include activities within the EU, particularly when targeting diaspora communities Project Duration Maximum duration: 6 months All projects must be completed by: March 1, 2027 Who Can Apply? The call is open to a wide range of non-profit and non-state actors , including: Civil society organizations (CSOs) Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) Diaspora organizations Social enterprises Universities and research centers Lead Applicant Requirements To be eligible, lead applicants must: Be established for at least 2 years Be registered in an African Union (AU) or European Union (EU) Member State Partnership Requirements Applications may include one co-applicant EU-based lead applicants must include an AU-based co-applicant , unless they are diaspora organizations AU-based applicants are not required to include co-applicants Affiliated entities may also be included Important Restriction Organizations that received funding under the first MMD Call for Proposals (as lead or co-applicant) are not eligible for this round. Application Process All applications must be submitted via the official platform managed by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development . Submission platform: ICMPD Electronic Application Platform Each organization may participate in only one application (as lead, co-applicant, or affiliated entity) Deadline Application Deadline: May 1, 2026 at 17:00 (Vienna time) Late submissions will not be considered. Additional Information Information Session An online information session will be held on: April 16, 2026 at 10:00 (Vienna time) The registration link will be available on the application platform. Questions and Clarifications Questions can be submitted via the platform until: April 23, 2026 Annual Retrospective Applicants are encouraged to review the 2025 Annual Retrospective , which highlights key achievements and impact of previously funded projects. title: Becoming a Force of Nature 2026: Global Online Programme Empowering Young Change-Makers in Climate and Social Justice
summary: In a rapidly changing world shaped by climate challenges and social inequalities, young people are increasingly stepping forward as catalysts for transformation. The Force of Nature Becoming a Force of Nature (BaFoN) Programme is a powerful global initiative designed to equip aspiring change makers with the clarity, skills, and confidence needed to turn their passion into meaningful action. This immersive online programme provides a structured yet deeply reflective journey, helping participants bridge the gap between their vision for a better world and the practical steps required to achieve it. If you are a young individual eager to create impact in climate or social justice spaces, this programme offers the tools and community you need to begin. What is the Becoming a Force of Nature Programme? Becoming a Force of Nature (BaFoN) is a three-part online programme tailored for individuals aged 16 to 35. It is delivered four times annually and focuses on guiding participants through a transformational process; from understanding their emotions and motivations to developing actionable solutions for real-world challenges. The programme runs over three weeks, with one session per week. Each session lasts between 90 and 120 minutes, making it flexible and accessible for students, young professionals, and emerging leaders worldwide. Participants are expected to dedicate approximately 2.5 hours per week, which includes live sessions and any reflective or follow-up activities. For those unable to attend live sessions, recordings are made available, ensuring inclusivity and convenience. Programme Structure and Learning Journey The BaFoN programme is thoughtfully divided into three interconnected workshops, each addressing a critical stage in the journey of becoming an effective changemaker. 1. Anxiety to Agency This session explores the emotional and psychological dimensions of climate change and social issues. Participants learn to: Understand the relationship between mental health and global challenges Identify and acknowledge complex emotions such as anxiety, fear, or frustration Build resilience strategies both individually and collectively Apply practical tools to manage emotions and transform them into motivation for action This stage is particularly important in helping participants move from feeling overwhelmed to feeling empowered. 2. Discovery (Agency to Efficacy) In this phase, participants begin to uncover their unique identity as changemakers. The session focuses on: Identifying personal strengths, passions, and talents Clarifying individual values and purpose (“your why”) Understanding what drives fulfillment and effectiveness in social impact work Building a personal framework to guide decision-making and action This stage ensures that participants are not only motivated but also aligned with their authentic selves. 3. Catalyst (Efficacy to Action) The final session is action-oriented and equips participants with the tools to implement their ideas. Participants will: Define and analyze a specific problem they want to address Map out the problem with a focus on affected communities Develop a clear and actionable plan Identify next steps to turn ideas into tangible impact By the end of this stage, participants leave with a concrete roadmap for creating change. Programme Schedule The upcoming May 2026 cohort will take place on: 12th May 2026 19th May 2026 26th May 2026 Each session is conducted online, making it accessible to participants from all parts of the world. Application Process and Deadline To join the Becoming a Force of Nature programme, applicants are required to complete an online application form. Application Deadline: 7th May 2026 at 12:00 PM BST Due to the competitive nature of the programme and its global reach, early application is strongly encouraged. Why You Should Apply The Becoming a Force of Nature programme is not just another online course; it is a transformational experience. Participants gain: A deeper understanding of their role in addressing global challenges Practical tools for managing climate anxiety and building resilience Clarity on personal purpose and direction Skills to design and implement impactful projects Access to a global network of like-minded young changemakers In a time when the world needs bold, thoughtful, and action-driven leaders, this programme provides a strong foundation for anyone ready to step into that role. The Becoming a Force of Nature programme stands out as a unique opportunity for young people to not only learn but also evolve. By combining emotional intelligence, self-discovery, and practical action planning, it ensures that participants are fully equipped to lead change in their communities and beyond. If you are passionate about climate action, social justice, or community impact, this programme could be your next big step toward making a difference. title: Horizon Scanning for Emerging Technologies 2035: UK Government Survey for Early-Career Academics
summary: As the global technological landscape evolves at an unprecedented pace, governments are increasingly relying on forward-looking research and expert insights to anticipate future disruptions. The Horizon Scanning for Emerging Technologies Survey , led by the UK Government Office for Science (GO-Science) , represents a unique opportunity for early-career academics based in the United Kingdom to directly contribute to shaping national policy and long-term strategic thinking. This initiative is part of a broader effort to identify emerging technologies, potential risks, and transformative opportunities that could define the world by the year 2035 . What is Horizon Scanning and Why Does It Matter? Horizon scanning is a strategic process used by governments and organizations to: Detect early signals of change Identify emerging technologies and trends Assess future risks and opportunities Support evidence-based policymaking Through this survey, the UK Government aims to gather expert-driven insights from academics who are actively engaged in cutting-edge research and innovation. About the Survey The survey is conducted by the Emerging Technology Team within GO-Science , a body dedicated to analyzing technological developments and informing policy decisions at the highest levels of government. Participants are invited to: Assess up to three emerging technologies within their field Share perspectives on potentially disruptive or unexpected innovations Reflect on how these technologies could evolve and impact society by 2035 All questions are optional , allowing participants flexibility in how they contribute. Why Participate? This survey offers a valuable opportunity to: Influence UK government policy and strategic planning Contribute to national and global conversations on technology Share your expertise on future innovations and disruptions Participate in a confidential and anonymous research initiative Your insights will play a critical role in shaping how governments prepare for technological change. Participation Details Participation in the survey is entirely voluntary . Respondents can: Choose which questions to answer Exit the survey at any time before submission Submit responses only when comfortable By completing and submitting the survey, participants confirm their consent to take part under the outlined conditions. Data Privacy and Anonymity A key feature of this initiative is its strong emphasis on privacy and ethical data handling : The survey is designed not to collect personal data Responses are fully anonymous Participants are advised not to include identifiable information Any accidental personal data will be removed before analysis This ensures that all contributions remain secure and confidential. How Your Responses Will Be Used The collected data will be analyzed in aggregate to: Identify key technological trends and themes Support government briefings and internal analysis Inform policy development and strategic decisions Importantly: Individual responses will not be attributed Any external publications will present high-level, non-identifiable insights Deadline No specific deadline has been publicly stated. Participants are encouraged to complete the survey as soon as possible to ensure their insights are included in the analysis. title: R2I Fellowship 2026 at Wale University: Bridging Africa’s Research Gap Through Innovation and Real-World Impact
summary: Africa stands at a critical crossroads where innovation, research, and real-world application must converge to unlock the continent’s full potential. At the forefront of this transformation is Wale University , through its dynamic initiative— Wale Lab Innovation —which is redefining how research translates into tangible impact. The R2I Fellowship 2026 (Research to Impact Fellowship) is now open, offering a unique opportunity for aspiring researchers and innovators across Africa to transform their ideas into real-world solutions. The Vision Behind Wale Lab Innovation Launched on February 2nd, 2025 , Wale Lab operates as a key arm of Wale University with a bold mission: to reverse Africa’s research deficit and empower a new generation of innovators capable of driving sustainable development. Unlike traditional academic frameworks, Wale Lab focuses on applied research , ensuring that ideas do not remain confined to theory but are developed into actionable, impactful solutions. Understanding the Research Gap in Africa Despite its vast human capital and intellectual potential, Africa faces significant structural challenges in research and innovation: 1. Population vs Research Output Gap Africa represents 18% of the global population , yet contributes less than 1% of global research output . This imbalance highlights systemic barriers in funding, infrastructure, and access to knowledge platforms. 2. Collaboration Access Gap Over 70% of African researchers lack access to global collaboration opportunities , limiting exposure, partnerships, and knowledge exchange essential for innovation. 3. Research Implementation Gap Nearly 90% of research ideas never reach real-world implementation , meaning valuable insights and solutions fail to create societal impact. How Wale Lab is Changing the Narrative Wale Lab is actively addressing these challenges by: Connecting African researchers with global opportunities and networks Providing expert mentorship from experienced professionals Supporting the transition from research to implementation Encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration across 22+ research areas Through this model, Wale Lab ensures that innovation is not only created but also scaled and applied . The R2I Fellowship: From Research to Impact The R2I Fellowship (Research to Impact) is a flagship program under Wale Lab designed to equip participants with the tools, guidance, and resources needed to turn research ideas into actionable solutions. What Makes This Fellowship Unique? The program stands out due to its strong emphasis on: Real-world application of research Mentorship-driven development Global collaboration opportunities Hands-on experience in innovation ecosystems Participants are not only trained but also supported in producing outputs that have measurable societal and economic impact. Program Reach and Impact Since its inception, Wale Lab has demonstrated remarkable growth and engagement: 2,500+ applications received for its inaugural cohort Participation from 9+ countries , showcasing strong regional diversity Support from 46+ expert mentors Development of 36+ research manuscripts ready for implementation This momentum reflects the urgent need and strong demand for platforms that bridge the gap between research and impact in Africa . Who Should Apply? The R2I Fellowship is ideal for: Students and recent graduates Early-career researchers Innovators and problem-solvers Individuals passionate about Africa’s development through research and innovation Applicants should have a clear interest in transforming ideas into practical solutions that address real-world challenges. Benefits of the R2I Fellowship Participants in the fellowship will gain: Access to expert mentorship and guidance Opportunities for global collaboration Support in developing research into implementable solutions Exposure to innovation-driven ecosystems The ability to contribute to Africa’s socio-economic transformation How to Apply Interested candidates are encouraged to apply through the official Wale Lab platform. Access the application portal Review program details Submit your application Deadline Application Deadline: May 3, 2026 Applicants are strongly advised to apply early to maximize their chances of selection. title: Democracy Camp 2026 Germany: A Transformative Youth Program on Democracy, Sustainability, and European Participation
summary: The Democracy Camp 2026 in Germany is a five-day international youth exchange program designed to empower young people to actively engage with democracy, sustainability, intersectionality, and European cooperation. Taking place in Vallendar, Germany, this immersive experience brings together 60 young participants from across Europe to explore how democratic systems function at different levels and how youth can meaningfully influence political and social change. This program is not just a learning experience it is a collaborative space where participants co-create ideas, develop civic engagement skills, and contribute to a tangible output: the Youth Participation Handbook, a policy-oriented publication aimed at improving youth inclusion in democratic processes across Europe. Overview of Democracy Camp 2026 Democracy Camp 2026 is structured as an intercultural training and dialogue platform that connects young people aged 16 to 26 from multiple European countries. The camp focuses on bridging the gap between youth and decision-making institutions while strengthening understanding of democracy in practice. Participants will engage in interactive workshops, group discussions, field visits, and collaborative projects. The program is built around real-world challenges such as climate change, social inequality, inclusion, and democratic participation at local, national, and European levels. The event will take place from 17 June to 21 June 2026 in Haus der Familie, Vallendar, Germany, with a digital preparatory session held in May 2026. Core Themes and Learning Objectives The Democracy Camp 2026 is built around two central guiding questions: What participation tools are available for young people today? How can these tools be used to promote sustainability, inclusion, and democratic engagement? Through these questions, participants will explore key thematic areas: Democracy and Political Participation Participants will gain a deeper understanding of democratic systems, from local governance to European Union structures and global institutions such as the United Nations. The camp emphasizes practical participation tools, including advocacy, civic campaigns, and youth-led initiatives. Sustainability and Climate Action The program highlights the relationship between democracy and sustainability, encouraging participants to examine how political decisions affect environmental outcomes and how youth can influence climate policy. Intersectionality and Inclusion A major focus is placed on social justice, equality, and inclusion. Participants will explore how intersecting identities influence access to political participation and how inclusive democracies can be strengthened. Youth Empowerment and Leadership The camp develops leadership, communication, and project management skills, enabling participants to design and implement impactful civic initiatives in their home countries. Program Structure and Activities The Democracy Camp 2026 is carefully structured into three phases: 1. Digital Kick-Off Session (26 May 2026) Participants will meet online before the camp begins to share ideas, set expectations, and connect with facilitators and fellow participants. This session introduces key themes and allows participants to shape the agenda. 2. In-Person Camp in Vallendar (17–21 June 2026) The main camp includes intensive workshops, intercultural exchange activities, and collaborative sessions. Participants will explore democratic practices across Europe, analyze case studies, and develop practical participation tools. A key highlight includes a study visit to Bonn, where participants will engage with the United Nations Campus and meet local civic initiatives working on democratic participation and sustainability. Evenings will be dedicated to reflection, networking, and intercultural exchange activities, culminating in a final celebration event. 3. Post-Camp Publication and Impact Phase After the camp, participants will co-author the Youth Participation Handbook 2026. This publication will include recommendations, tools, and insights designed to improve youth participation across Europe. The handbook will be shared with policymakers, including members of the European Parliament, to influence future youth engagement strategies. Costs and Financial Support One of the most attractive aspects of Democracy Camp 2026 is its full financial coverage: Participation is completely free of charge Travel reimbursement up to 250 EUR is provided Accommodation and meals are fully covered Vegetarian and vegan meals are provided throughout the program Participants are encouraged to use environmentally friendly travel options such as trains, buses, or carpooling, which are prioritized in the selection process. Accommodation and Facilities The camp will be hosted at Haus der Familie in Vallendar, Germany. The venue offers a comfortable and interactive environment with facilities such as sports fields, recreational spaces, and group activity areas. These facilities are designed to support both structured learning and informal intercultural exchange. Who Can Apply Applicants must meet the following requirements: Age between 16 and 26 years Ability to communicate in English for the duration of the program Willingness to engage in intercultural dialogue and teamwork Interest in democracy, sustainability, and civic participation Applications from young people with fewer opportunities are strongly encouraged and prioritized to ensure diversity and inclusion. Minors are welcome but must provide parental consent and be accompanied according to program safety guidelines. Application Deadline The application deadline for Democracy Camp 2026 is 16 March 2026. Why You Should Apply Democracy Camp 2026 offers a rare opportunity to: Connect with young leaders from across Europe Develop real-world civic engagement skills Understand European and global democratic systems Contribute to a policy-relevant publication Build a network of changemakers Gain hands-on experience in international collaboration This program is ideal for young people who are passionate about democracy, climate action, social justice, and international cooperation. Final Thoughts Democracy Camp 2026 is more than a youth exchange it is a platform for shaping the future of democratic participation in Europe. By bringing together diverse voices and ideas, the program empowers young people to become active contributors to policy discussions and social transformation. title: New American Speakers Program 2026 (Cohort 10): Fully Funded Storytelling & Public Speaking Training for Refugees in the U.S.
summary: The Refugee Storytellers Collective is now accepting applications for the New American Speakers Program (NASP) – Cohort 10 , a highly impactful initiative designed to empower refugees and immigrants in the United States to reclaim their narratives, amplify their voices, and become influential storytellers and advocates . About the CATCH Project The CATCH project aims to produce the first comprehensive environmental history of the Catholic Church from the 1960s to the present day. This period marks a significant transformation in the Church’s engagement with social and ecological issues—from the reforms of Vatican II to the global environmental advocacy seen during the papacy of Pope Francis. Key Research Focus The evolution of environmental awareness within the Catholic Church The Church’s role in international environmental governance and UN debates Regional case studies across: Europe Africa Asia The Americas The project is explicitly non-confessional, meaning participation does not require religious affiliation or belief. The Radical Environmental Humanities Hub (REH2) A major component of the project is the creation of the Radical Environmental Humanities Hub (REH2), which seeks to bridge the gap between Environmental Humanities and Political Ecology. Objectives of REH2 Foster interdisciplinary research Promote global South and non-Anglophone perspectives Support education, research, and public engagement Address pressing socio-ecological challenges The hub aims to become a leading research center in Southern Europe and the Mediterranean region. title: Paid Youth Technical Experts Opportunity 2026 ($1,000 Stipend) – African Youth Charter @20 | Apply by April 30
summary: Looking for a paid youth governance, policy, or research opportunity in Africa ? The African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) , in partnership with YouLead Africa and Restless Development , is now accepting applications for 20 Youth Technical Experts to support the African Youth Charter @20 appraisal . Key Details (Read This First) Stipend: $1,000 USD Deadline: 30 April 2026 (12:00 SAST) Duration: 3–4 months (May–August 2026) Commitment: ~8 hours/week Eligibility: African youth Location: Remote + country-level engagement Apply via: tender@aprm-au.org TERMS OF REFERENCE YOUTH TECHNICAL EXPERTS Call for Applications APRM/DP/YTE/IC/04/2026: CALL FOR TWENTY (20) YOUTH TECHNICAL EXPERTS TO APPRAISE THE AFRICAN YOUTH CHARTER @20 The Technical proposal must be submitted via email to tender@aprm-au.org on or before 30 April 2026 at 12.00 (SAST). Proposals shall be opened on the 30 of April 2026 at 12.00 (SAST) . A collaborative initiative of the African Peer Review Mechanism Continental Secretariat, YouLead Africa, and Restless Development 1. Programme Background In 2026, the African Youth Charter (AYC) marks its 20 th anniversary, a defining continental milestone that reaffirms Africa’s commitment to the socioeconomic inclusion of youth, democratic participation, and sustainable development. This anniversary presents a critical opportunity to reflect on progress achieved, assess implementation gaps, and redouble efforts to ensure meaningful youth empowerment across the continent. As Africa navigates profound transformation in governance, peace, development, and justice, young people, who constitute more than 75% of the continent’s population, are the leaders of tomorrow and also active actors shaping Africa today. Against this backdrop, the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) Continental Secretariat, YouLead Africa and Restless Development have launched the initiative: “Technical Experts on Youth Governance and Development: Consultations and Policy Briefs on the African Youth Charter @20” . As part of this initiative, young Africans are invited to serve as Youth Technical Experts to assess and document how African Union Member States, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), National Youth Councils, Civil Society Organisations, Development Partners, Private Sector and governance frameworks are implementing the AYC and related continental and regional commitments. The appraisal’s findings will directly inform a consolidated continental policy brief to be launched during Africa Youth Day commemorations and will contribute to the APRM Africa Governance Report (AGR) 2027, focusing on Youth in Governance: From Promise to Prosperity . 2. Aim of the Youth Technical Experts Youth Technical Experts will lead participatory, evidence-based assessments of how African Union frameworks, including the AYC, Agenda 2063, the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance (ACDEG), and the Africa Governance Architecture (AGA) Youth Engagement Strategy, are being implemented across the continent. Through a structured appraisal process, Youth Technical Experts will assess institutional responsiveness to youth needs and generate actionable, youth-informed recommendations and best practices to strengthen discourse on continental and regional governance. 3. Objectives of the Youth Technical Experts’ assessments Synthesise youth consultation outcomes from the APRM, YouLead Africa, and the Restless Development Youth Platform processes, capturing emerging perspectives on the implementation of the AYC and related AU frameworks. Analyse governance and participation trends, assessing how AU frameworks, including Agenda 2063, ACDEG, and the AGA Youth Engagement Strategy, have advanced youth inclusion. Identify implementation gaps and document barriers to youth participation at national, regional, and continental levels. Contribute to the consolidated continental policy brief with forward-looking recommendations to strengthen the implementation of the AYC and related AU frameworks. Amplify youth perspectives in continental policy dialogue and contribute to the drafting of the AGR 2027. Alongside the APRM Youth Unit, YouLead Africa, and Restless Development, coordinate consultation processes and ensure outputs align with the AYC @20 commemorations. 4. Thematic Areas of Focus Youth Technical Experts will assess implementation across the following thematic areas: Youth, Governance and Democratic Transformation: Youth political representation, elections, constitutional reforms, and digital civic engagement. Peace, Security and Youth Agency: Youth inclusion within the AGA – African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA), peacebuilding, and resilience in conflict contexts. Economic Justice, Development and Employment: Youth unemployment, African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and entrepreneurship, innovation, digital finance, and gig economy. Pan-Africanism, Identity and Youth Mobilisation: Diaspora engagement with the AU, cultural activism, and Afrocentric education. Policy and Institutional Responsiveness: Evaluation of the AU 1 Million Next Level Initiative, youth-led monitoring of Agenda 2063 and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the role of AU organs, RECs, and Member States. 5. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be between 18 and 35 years of age at the time of application. Be a national of an African Union Member State. Be active in civil society, youth networks, youth-led organisations, academic institutions, or community-based organisations. title: House of Lords Social Mobility Work Experience Programme 2026 (UK) – Apply Now
summary: Are you a Year 12 student in the UK looking to gain real-world experience inside Parliament? Applications are now open for the House of Lords Social Mobility Work Experience Programme 2026 — a unique opportunity to explore careers in public service, policy, and governance. Delivered by the House of Lords , this one-week immersive programme gives students a behind-the-scenes look at how Parliament operates and how laws are shaped in the UK. Key Details at a Glance Host: House of Lords Programme Type: Work Experience (Social Mobility Programme) Location: London, United Kingdom Duration: 1 Week Eligibility: Year 12 students (UK) Application Deadline: 22 April 2026 Programme Overview The House of Lords Social Mobility Work Experience Programme offers selected students the chance to: Experience Parliament beyond what you see in the news Learn how the House of Lords functions in practice Engage directly with professionals across departments Participate in real workplace activities and projects This is an ideal opportunity for students interested in politics, governance, communications, or public service careers . The House of Lords is running a social mobility work experience programme for Year 12 students. The House of Lords Social Mobility Work Experience Programme will offer students the opportunity to go beyond the headlines and experience Parliament from the inside. Over one exciting week, participants will explore how the House of Lords operates. The programme includes: Working alongside professionals in key departments Taking part in hands-on tasks and real workplace activities Shadowing staff and seeing how different roles come together behind the scenes Joining interactive workshops designed to build your skills and confidence. What you ll gain: A clear understanding of careers in Parliament Practical workplace experience you can talk about in applications Confidence, connections and inspiration. Whether you’re curious about politics, interested in public service or just want to try something new, this programme could be for you. Offices involved Property and Office Services This team is responsible for front of house services, houskeeping, heritage cleaning and accommodation as well as managing contracts for the parliamentary estate and supporting work on ceremonial events and maintenance projects. Black Rod s department The team plays a leading role in all ceremonial events such as the State Opening of Parliament and state visits, as well as supporting the day to day running of the House of Lords and controlling access to the chamber. Clerk of the Parliament s Office The office supports the Clerk of the Parliaments to carry out their duties as head of the Administration, plus other key officeholders such as the Senior Deputy Speaker, Convenor of the Crossbench Peers, Clerk Assistant and Chief Operating Officer. The office also includes teams responsible for governance, internal audit, interparliamentary relations, and Restoration and Renewal of the Palace of Westminster. Committees The Commitee Office provides support for Lords select committees; small groups of members investigating areas of public policy. The team provides committees with the policy, procedural, logistical, administrative and legal support they need to carry out their work. Communications Communications is responsible for explaining the role and work of the House of Lords to the public, increasing awareness and improving understanding of the the value it adds. The team includes press and media, digital communications, engagement, public enquiries and internal communications. title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026– Open for Applications
summary: The 2026 Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships are now open, offering €399.05 million in funding to support researchers worldwide. They support researchers in gaining new skills , expanding networks, and advancing careers through international, interdisciplinary, and inter-sectoral mobility . Fellows work with leading institutions worldwide and benefit from strong research collaboration and mentorship. Types of Fellowships 1. European Postdoctoral Fellowships Open to researchers of any nationality Hosted in EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries Duration: Up to 24 months 2. Global Postdoctoral Fellowships Open to EU nationals or long-term residents Research conducted in a third country (12–24 months) Includes a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe Additional Opportunity: Non-Academic Placement Fellows can request an additional 6-month placement in a non-academic organisation (e.g., industry, NGOs, public sector) in Europe, helping bridge research and real-world application. Researchers applying to Global Fellowships will need to seek the commitment of an organisation based in a third country , as they will carry out their research there for a period of between 12 and 24 months. The call is open to researchers wishing to reintegrate in Europe, to those displaced by conflict, as well as to researchers with high potential who are seeking to restart their careers.
