title: Fully Funded PhD on Youth & AI at KU Leuven (IAmAI Project) – Apply by May 31, 2026
summary: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming education, identity development, and how young people interact with the world. Yet, many AI systems are still designed without actively involving the very individuals they impact the most—youth. A groundbreaking fully funded PhD opportunity at KU Leuven aims to change that narrative by placing young people at the center of AI development through the innovative IAmAI Project: Youth in the Loop of AI Developments . About the PhD Opportunity This four-year doctoral position is hosted at the Centre for Methodology of Educational Sciences (CMPO), within the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences. The research is led by Melissa De Smet , an expert in qualitative and mixed-methods research. The project focuses on developing participatory methodologies that bridge the gap between how AI systems are built and how young people actually learn, grow, and experience the world. Why This PhD Stands Out This is not a conventional PhD. It is designed for researchers who want to: Explore how AI can be co-created with young people Develop innovative qualitative and participatory research methods Influence ethical AI design and policy recommendations Work within a multidisciplinary, international research environment By focusing on co-creation, this project ensures that AI systems better reflect the real, dynamic experiences of youth rather than relying solely on static datasets. Research Focus The IAmAI project tackles a critical issue in AI development—the mismatch between generalized data models and individual lived experiences. Your research will: Investigate interactions between youth and AI systems Develop and test participatory research methodologies Reimagine personalization in AI tools such as learning platforms and generative AI chatbots Translate findings into actionable policy and methodological recommendations Key Responsibilities During the PhD, you will: Conduct high-quality qualitative research Publish in internationally recognized academic journals Present findings at global conferences Support teaching in psychology and educational sciences programs What You Will Gain This position offers a highly supportive academic environment with opportunities to grow professionally and personally: Full funding for four years Access to international conferences, workshops, and training Collaboration with leading interdisciplinary researchers Additional benefits such as transport reimbursement, insurance, and eco-vouchers A dynamic, multicultural research setting in Leuven, Belgium Ideal Candidate Profile Applicants should have: A Master’s degree in educational sciences, psychology, or a related field Strong interest in qualitative research methods Passion for youth engagement and participatory approaches Interest in AI and ethical research practices Excellent communication skills Fluency in Dutch and English Experience in academic writing and familiarity with qualitative data collection and analysis are strong advantages. Location and Start Date Location: Leuven, Belgium Start Date: October 2026 (flexible upon agreement) Application Process Applicants are required to submit: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Motivation letter Academic transcripts Optional writing sample (thesis or research paper) Applications must be submitted via the official KU Leuven online platform. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for this PhD position is May 31, 2026 (23:59 CET) . Final Thoughts This PhD offers a rare opportunity to contribute to the ethical and inclusive future of AI by directly involving young people in its development. If you are passionate about research, education, and technology—and want to make a meaningful impact—this program provides the perfect platform. title: Internet Society Foundation Research Grant Program 2026: Up to $500,000 in Funding for Global Internet Research
summary: The Internet Society Foundation has officially opened applications for its highly anticipated Research Grant Program 2026 , offering funding between $200,000 and $500,000 to support innovative research projects that explore the evolving role of the Internet in society. This prestigious global program is designed to empower researchers and institutions to generate practical, open-access knowledge that can shape policies, improve digital ecosystems, and create a more inclusive, secure, and sustainable Internet for everyone. 💡 About the Research Grant Program The Research Grant Program supports forward-thinking research aligned with the Internet Society Foundation’s 2030 strategic vision —a world where everyone has access to affordable, reliable, and secure Internet connectivity. Over the past five years, the program has: Funded 70+ research projects Invested over $22 million globally Influenced policy decisions, industry practices, and technological innovation The program places strong emphasis on collaboration, diversity, and real-world impact , particularly encouraging researchers from the Global South and underrepresented communities. 🎯 Key Focus Areas Applicants must align their proposals with at least one of the following themes: 1. Inclusive Internet Research addressing barriers such as affordability, gender inequality, geography, and digital literacy that limit Internet access and participation. 2. Greening the Internet Projects exploring the environmental impact of Internet infrastructure, energy consumption, and climate resilience. 3. Measuring Meaningful Connectivity Studies focused on redefining connectivity beyond access—examining how Internet use enables real participation in economic, social, and civic life. 4. A Trustworthy Internet Research on Internet security, reliability, accountability, and emerging risks that affect trust in digital systems. 💰 Funding Details Up to $200,000 for independent researchers Up to $500,000 for organizations and institutions Funding supports applied, open research that addresses real-world challenges and is accessible to the global scientific community. ✅ Eligibility Criteria Independent researchers must hold a postgraduate degree (Master’s or PhD) and demonstrate prior research output Public research institutions must be non-profit (or equivalent) and aligned with the Foundation’s mission Projects must comply with ethical standards and local regulations Strong encouragement for applicants from underrepresented and Global Majority communities 🧠 Selection Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on: Alignment with thematic focus areas Innovation and originality Practical impact and policy relevance Collaboration and interdisciplinary approach Intersectional research design 📅 Important Deadline Application Opens: April 7, 2026 Application Deadline: May 22, 2026 (21:00 UTC) Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. 📝 How to Apply Applicants must submit their proposals through the Foundation’s online grant management system (Fluxx). Key steps include: Register on the platform at least 24 hours before the deadline Prepare and submit a complete application in English, French, or Spanish Ensure compliance with all eligibility and documentation requirements APPLY HERE. For more information about this apportunity, click here . Discover more grantopportunities, click here . 📢 Why You Should Apply This program is more than just funding—it’s an opportunity to: Influence global Internet policy and governance Contribute to cutting-edge research and innovation Collaborate with a diverse, international research community Create real-world impact in digital inclusion and sustainability 🔗 Useful Links Apply via the official platform (Fluxx) Attend info sessions (April 20 21, 2026) Contact: foundation@isocfoundation.org 📌 Final Thoughts If you are passionate about shaping the future of the Internet and addressing global digital challenges, the Internet Society Foundation Research Grant Program 2026 offers a powerful platform to turn your ideas into impactful solutions. title: Fully Funded German Bundestag IPS Africa Scholarship 2027 in Berlin (Stipend + Travel Covered)
summary: The German Bundestag is offering an incredible opportunity for politically and socially engaged young graduates from sub-Saharan Africa to participate in the prestigious International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS Africa) Programme 2027 in Berlin, Germany. This fully funded programme is designed to equip emerging leaders with firsthand knowledge of parliamentary democracy, governance, and political decision-making processes within one of Europe’s most influential legislative institutions. About the IPS Africa Programme Launched in 2020 under the patronage of the President of the German Bundestag, the IPS Africa Programme aims to empower young African leaders who are passionate about shaping the democratic future of their countries. Each year, up to 24 participants are selected from eligible African countries to take part in a four-week intensive programme in Berlin . Programme Duration Start Date: 4 January 2027 End Date: 2 February 2027 What to Expect Participants will gain practical and theoretical insights into Germany’s parliamentary system through: A one-week placement in the office of a Member of the German Bundestag Exposure to legislative processes and political decision-making Workshops on: Parliamentary democracy Anti-corruption strategies Intercultural communication Project management Discussions on: Pluralism and diversity Minority protection Historical memory and political responsibility The programme also supports fellows in developing projects that promote democracy and civic engagement in their home countries. Financial Benefits The IPS Africa Programme is fully funded and includes: Monthly stipend of €700 Free accommodation in Berlin Round-trip travel expenses Health, accident, and liability insurance coverage Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be citizens of one of the participating countries Be under 30 years old by January 1, 2027 Hold a university degree Have at least B2-level proficiency in German Demonstrate strong interest in political and social issues Show active engagement in civic or political activities Required Application Documents Applicants must submit: Proof of German language proficiency (B2 or higher) Motivation letter (in German, max. 2 pages, signed) Copy of passport or national ID University degree certificate (English or German) Letter of recommendation (German or English) Important: All application materials must be submitted in German. Application Process Applications must be submitted through the official IPS digital platform. Email submissions are no longer accepted. APPLY HERE. For more information about this apportunity, click here . Discover more short courses opportunities, click here . Selection Process Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview at a German diplomatic mission. Final selection is based on: Professional qualifications Social and political engagement Language proficiency Intercultural competence Application Deadline Application Period: 1 April – 15 May 2026 Late applications will not be considered. Important Note Applicants from Namibia and South Africa may also apply for the five-month IPS Global Programme. While it is possible to apply for both, only one programme can be attended. title: Apply for the CLA Foundation Scholarship 2026 and Receive $15,000 for Your Studies
summary: The CLA Foundation Opportunity Scholarship 2026 offers students across the United States the chance to receive $15,000 in funding to support their undergraduate or graduate studies in business, finance, technology, and other emerging professional fields. Open to high school seniors, current college students, and graduate students, this scholarship aims to support future leaders shaping the evolving landscape of professional services. Administered by Scholarship America, the program identifies high-potential students who demonstrate academic achievement, leadership, and a clear commitment to their chosen career path. With applications open until May 19, 2026 , this opportunity provides financial support while helping students advance toward careers in high-demand sectors. About the Program The CLA Foundation Opportunity Scholarship Program is designed to invest in students pursuing careers in both traditional and emerging professional service industries. These include fields such as accounting, finance, and business, as well as rapidly growing areas like artificial intelligence, data science, cybersecurity, and regulatory technology. The scholarship is funded by the CLA Foundation and administered by Scholarship America, one of the largest scholarship management organizations in the United States. Through this collaboration, the program ensures a rigorous and fair selection process, identifying students who demonstrate both academic excellence and future leadership potential. Recipients are awarded a one-time scholarship of $15,000, which can be used to support tuition and other educational expenses at accredited two-year or four-year colleges, universities, or graduate schools. Why This Opportunity Matters The professional services sector is undergoing rapid transformation due to advancements in technology and shifting global demands. Fields such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, and digital transformation are reshaping how businesses operate, creating new opportunities for skilled professionals. This scholarship supports students entering these evolving fields by reducing financial barriers and enabling them to focus on their education and career development. By investing in both traditional and emerging disciplines, the program helps prepare a new generation of professionals equipped to lead innovation and drive economic growth. In addition, the scholarship recognizes the importance of leadership, community involvement, and resilience. By selecting students who demonstrate these qualities, the program contributes to building a workforce that is not only skilled but also socially responsible and community-oriented. What Participants Will Gain The CLA Foundation Opportunity Scholarship provides both financial and professional advantages. Recipients receive $15,000 in funding, which can significantly reduce the cost of higher education and ease financial stress. Beyond financial support, the scholarship enhances students’ academic and professional profiles. Being selected as a recipient signals strong leadership potential and academic achievement, which can open doors to future opportunities. Participants may also gain access to internship opportunities with CLA-affiliated offices, providing valuable hands-on experience in professional services. Additionally, the recognition associated with the scholarship can strengthen future applications for jobs, graduate programs, and other competitive opportunities. Who Can Apply The scholarship is open to students in the United States who meet the following criteria: Applicants must be high school seniors, graduates, or current undergraduate or graduate students planning to enroll full-time in an accredited institution for the upcoming academic year. Eligible fields of study include accounting, business, finance, and a wide range of emerging disciplines such as computer science, data analytics, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and related areas. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. Candidates should also demonstrate leadership, participation in school or community activities, work experience, and clear educational and career goals. Financial need is considered as part of the selection process. Application Process and Deadline To apply, candidates must complete the online application through the official Scholarship America platform. The application requires submission of a complete academic transcript, a personal statement outlining educational and career goals, and one recommendation form. Applicants must ensure all materials are submitted electronically before the deadline. Incomplete applications will not be considered. The deadline to apply is May 19, 2026, at 3:00 PM CT . Applicants will be notified of the results in July, and scholarship funds will be distributed in early August. This scholarship provides a valuable opportunity for students to invest in their education, build their professional future, and contribute to the evolving world of professional services. title: Apply to Join the AWARD Reviewer Pool and Shape Africa’s Future Leaders in Agrifood Systems
summary: The AWARD Reviewer Pool offers experienced professionals the opportunity to contribute to the selection of Africa’s next generation of leaders in agrifood systems while gaining insight into emerging innovations in climate resilience and gender equality. Applications are open until 30 April 2026 for experts interested in supporting high-impact fellowship programs across the continent. African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD) is inviting qualified professionals to join its reviewer pool for flagship fellowship initiatives. This opportunity is designed for individuals with strong expertise in agriculture, policy, climate change, and leadership development who are committed to advancing inclusive and sustainable development across Africa. About the Program The AWARD Reviewer Pool plays a critical role in maintaining the quality and integrity of fellowship selection processes. Reviewers are responsible for evaluating applications submitted by candidates across AWARD’s programs, which aim to build leadership capacity and strengthen agrifood systems throughout Africa. Rather than being a full-time role, this opportunity is a flexible, short-term engagement that allows professionals to contribute alongside their existing responsibilities. Selected reviewers will assess a small number of applications using structured evaluation criteria and provide objective, constructive feedback to support fair decision-making. The reviewer role also includes participation in virtual briefing sessions and adherence to clear guidelines on confidentiality, ethics, and conflict of interest. Through this process, AWARD ensures that its fellowship cohorts are composed of high-potential individuals capable of driving meaningful change. Why This Opportunity Matters Africa faces complex challenges related to climate change, food security, and sustainable agriculture. Addressing these challenges requires strong leadership, innovation, and inclusive approaches that prioritize gender equality and community resilience. By joining the AWARD Reviewer Pool, professionals play a direct role in identifying and supporting individuals who are working to transform agrifood systems across the continent. This contribution helps ensure that fellowship programs select candidates with the potential to drive impactful solutions in research, policy, and practice. Additionally, the reviewer pool strengthens the credibility and transparency of selection processes. By involving diverse experts with regional and thematic knowledge, AWARD enhances the quality of its programs and promotes equity in access to opportunities. What Participants Will Gain Serving as a reviewer offers both professional and intellectual benefits. Participants gain exposure to innovative ideas, research proposals, and emerging leaders working in agrifood systems and climate adaptation. Reviewers also deepen their analytical and evaluation skills by engaging with structured assessment frameworks and providing detailed feedback. This experience can strengthen their expertise in selection processes, grant evaluation, and program design. In addition, reviewers become part of a broader community of professionals committed to advancing sustainable development in Africa. This engagement can lead to new collaborations, knowledge exchange, and long-term involvement in AWARD’s initiatives. A modest honorarium is provided in recognition of the time and expertise contributed by reviewers. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to professionals with strong experience in areas such as agricultural research, agrifood systems, climate change, policy, gender, and leadership development. Applicants should hold a Master’s degree, PhD, or equivalent experience, along with demonstrated expertise in research, academia, policy, or program leadership. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills are essential, as well as the ability to provide objective and high-quality assessments. Experience reviewing proposals, fellowships, or grants is considered an advantage, as is proficiency in English and/or French. Application Process and Deadline Interested candidates must submit their application through the official Reviewer Expression of Interest form available online. Applications submitted through other means will not be considered. The deadline to apply is 30 April 2026 . Selected reviewers will be contacted with further details regarding assignments, timelines, and onboarding processes. This is a valuable opportunity for experienced professionals to contribute their expertise to high-impact programs while supporting the development of future leaders working to address some of Africa’s most pressing challenges. To learn more and apply, visit the official African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD) website. title: Join DC Action’s Board of Directors: Lead Change for Youth in Washington, DC
summary: The DC Action Young Adult Board Member opportunity offers young leaders aged 18–30 the chance to gain governance experience while shaping policies that impact children and youth across Washington, DC. This unique leadership role is designed for individuals who are passionate about advocacy, equity, and community impact, and who want to contribute their voice to decision-making processes that influence real change. DC Action is currently seeking applications from motivated young adults ready to step into leadership roles and support its mission of ensuring that all children and youth in the District of Columbia grow up safe, resilient, and empowered. About the Program DC Action is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving outcomes for children and youth through research, advocacy, and collaboration. Formed through the merger of DC Action for Children and the DC Alliance of Youth Advocates, the organization works to unify efforts across sectors and ensure a more coordinated approach to supporting young people. As a Young Adult Board Member, selected candidates will serve on the organization’s Board of Directors and contribute to governance, oversight, and strategic decision-making. Board members play an important role in guiding the organization’s direction, ensuring accountability, and strengthening its advocacy efforts. This position is designed not only to support the organization but also to provide young leaders with hands-on experience in nonprofit governance and policy engagement. Why This Opportunity Matters Young people are often the most affected by policies related to education, housing, health, and economic opportunity, yet they are frequently underrepresented in decision-making spaces. This opportunity addresses that gap by placing young leaders directly at the table where key decisions are made. By joining the DC Action Board, young adults can bring their lived experiences and perspectives into discussions that shape programs and policies. This contributes to more inclusive, equitable, and effective solutions for communities. In addition, the organization’s commitment to racial equity and its focus on addressing systemic barriers ensures that board members are engaging in work that has long-term impact on social justice and community wellbeing. What Participants Will Gain Serving as a Young Adult Board Member offers both personal and professional development opportunities. Participants will gain valuable leadership experience by contributing to governance and strategic planning processes. They will also build skills in advocacy, event planning, and fundraising—key competencies for careers in nonprofit leadership, public policy, and community development. Board members will have the opportunity to expand their professional networks, collaborate with experienced leaders, and gain insight into how organizations operate at a strategic level. In addition, selected participants will receive a modest quarterly stipend, providing financial support while they contribute their time and expertise. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to young adults aged 18 to 30 who are passionate about improving outcomes for children and youth in Washington, DC. Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in advocacy, leadership, and community engagement. While prior board experience is not required, candidates should be committed to contributing actively to the organization’s mission and participating in governance activities. DC Action encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds and perspectives, particularly those from communities that are directly impacted by systemic inequities. Application Process and Deadline To apply, candidates must submit a resume and a cover letter outlining their interest, experience, and motivation for joining the board. Review the official requirements and responsibilities on the DC Action website . The deadline to apply is 15 May 2026 . Applicants are encouraged to submit thoughtful and well-prepared applications that clearly demonstrate their commitment to youth advocacy and leadership. This role provides a meaningful pathway for young leaders to influence policy, build skills, and contribute to a stronger future for children and youth in Washington, DC. title: Fully Funded Green RISE Africa Fellowship 2026: Empowering Climate Entrepreneurs Across Africa
summary: Looking to take your climate-focused enterprise to the next level? The Acumen Academy is now accepting applications for the Green RISE Africa Fellowship 2026. This fully funded leadership program supports entrepreneurs across East and West Africa who are building solutions at the intersection of climate action and poverty reduction. Designed for emerging leaders driving inclusive green growth, the fellowship offers a unique opportunity to strengthen your leadership, scale your enterprise, and join a global community of changemakers. Applications open on 11 May 2026 , with the program starting in July 2026. About the Opportunity The Green RISE Africa Fellowship (Resilient Impact through Sustainable Entrepreneurship) is a six-month hybrid leadership program that equips entrepreneurs with the tools, frameworks, and networks needed to grow sustainable, climate-aligned businesses. Unlike traditional business programs, this fellowship focuses on moral leadership —helping participants develop the values, mindset, and decision-making skills required to create long-term, inclusive impact. Fellows remain in their current roles while engaging in virtual learning, in-person immersives, and peer collaboration. The program is designed to support entrepreneurs who are not only building businesses, but also creating dignified work opportunities , particularly for women and youth in underserved communities. East vs West Africa Fellowship The fellowship is delivered through two regional tracks, each tailored to specific contexts while maintaining a shared mission of building an inclusive green economy. West Africa Fellowship This track focuses on entrepreneurs working to expand green job opportunities for young rural women and youth across West Africa. It emphasizes building enterprises rooted in dignity, equity, and sustainable growth. Participants engage in immersive learning experiences, including in-person sessions in Nigeria , while connecting with a diverse network of peers tackling similar challenges across the region. East Africa Fellowship The East Africa track is open to entrepreneurs in countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Burundi, South Sudan, and Somalia. It focuses on strengthening climate-aligned business models , improving resilience, and scaling impact across communities. Fellows participate in in-person immersives in Kenya and benefit from access to regional and global expertise. Why This Opportunity Matters Africa is at the forefront of both climate vulnerability and climate innovation. Entrepreneurs across the continent are developing solutions in renewable energy, agriculture, waste management, and more—but often face barriers in scaling their impact. The Green RISE Africa Fellowship addresses this gap by combining leadership development with practical enterprise support . It helps participants navigate complex challenges, engage stakeholders effectively, and build systems that prioritize both environmental sustainability and social inclusion. By fostering a strong community of leaders, the program also creates opportunities for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and long-term partnerships that extend far beyond the fellowship itself. What You’ll Gain Participants benefit from a comprehensive and fully funded experience, including: A structured 6-month leadership development program Access to Acumen’s global alumni network, The Foundry (2,000+ members) Training in key areas such as adaptive leadership, storytelling, and inclusive business strategies Participation in virtual sessions and in-person immersives Personalized mentorship and peer learning opportunities Continued engagement in a climate-focused community of practice after the program In addition, fellows may gain access to future funding and growth opportunities to further scale their enterprises. Program Structure The fellowship is designed to be flexible, requiring approximately 10 hours per month . It includes: A 3-day virtual orientation A 2-day virtual workshop Two 5-day in-person immersives Monthly cohort sessions and learning labs Self-paced assignments and one-on-one support This structure allows participants to immediately apply what they learn to their own enterprises. Eligibility This opportunity is ideal for individuals who: Are building or leading a green enterprise Focus on creating inclusive economic opportunities Are committed to addressing climate change and poverty Demonstrate leadership potential and a strong vision for impact Are based in eligible East or West African countries Application Process and Timeline To apply, candidates must: Review the Applicant Toolkit Submit an online application (opens 11 May 2026) Participate in a Selection Conference (4–6 June 2026) if shortlisted Begin the fellowship in July 2026 If you are ready to grow your enterprise and contribute to Africa’s green future, visit the official website to apply: See the West Africa Fellowship See the East Africa Fellowship Explore More Opportunities for Youth Want to discover more fellowships, scholarships, internships, and global programs like this one? title: UN Junior Professional Officer (JPO) in Programme Management 2026 – Fully Funded International Career Opportunity in New York
summary: If you are a young professional seeking a high-impact global career with the United Nations, the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) in Programme Management offers one of the most prestigious entry points into international development. Sponsored by the Government of the Netherlands and coordinated through the Nedworc Foundation , this opportunity places talented individuals at the heart of global policy and development coordination. What is the JPO Programme and Why It Matters The Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme is a globally recognized career pathway into the United Nations system. It is specifically designed to recruit and train young professionals who demonstrate strong academic backgrounds and a passion for global development. Participants gain: Hands-on experience within UN agencies Exposure to high-level policy processes Access to global professional networks Structured training and career development opportunities The programme plays a critical role in supporting the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, enabling professionals to contribute directly to global change. Detailed Job Description and Responsibilities As a JPO in Programme Management, you will work within the Office of the Assistant Secretary-General for Development Coordination. This role is deeply embedded in the strategic operations of the United Nations. Core Responsibilities Include: Coordinating contributions to high-level UN leadership briefings Drafting reports, background documents, and policy papers Supporting programme development, implementation, and evaluation Conducting research and analysis on global development issues Assisting in policy development and strategic planning Organizing meetings, conferences, and consultations Monitoring programme progress and recommending improvements You will also collaborate with multiple UN entities, including regional teams and partner organizations, ensuring integrated development coordination across the system. Eligibility Criteria – Who Can Apply This opportunity is highly competitive and has strict eligibility requirements. Age Requirement Must be 32 years or younger by 31 December of the application year Eligible Countries Applicants must be citizens of one of the following countries: Africa: Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia, Uganda, Senegal, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Mozambique, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Chad, Benin, Ivory Coast Asia Middle East: India, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Yemen, Bangladesh, Vietnam Others: Colombia, Ukraine, Palestinian Territory This means candidates from Africa and other developing regions are strongly encouraged to apply, making it a highly inclusive opportunity. Educational Qualifications To qualify, candidates must meet the following academic requirements: A Master’s degree in: Public Administration International Relations Business Management Or a closely related field Alternative Pathway: A Bachelor’s degree + minimum 4 years of relevant experience may be accepted Additionally, part of your academic studies must have taken place in an eligible country. Professional Experience Requirements While this is an entry-level professional role, candidates are expected to demonstrate: Strong analytical and research skills Experience in programme/project management Ability to draft reports and policy documents Knowledge of international development frameworks Relevant work or internship experience in international organizations, NGOs, or government institutions is highly advantageous. Training, Benefits, and Career Growth The JPO Programme is not just a job—it is a structured career development platform. Key Benefits Include: Participation in the UN JPO Orientation Programme in Turin (Italy) Annual $4,000 training and travel allowance Access to UN internal learning and development programmes Direct mentorship and supervision by senior UN officials Opportunity to transition into long-term UN careers By the end of the programme, participants gain: Advanced knowledge of UN systems and operations Experience in global policy coordination Strong professional networks within the UN system Who Should Apply (Target Audience) This opportunity is ideal for: Young professionals passionate about global development Graduates in international relations, public policy, or related fields Individuals seeking careers in the United Nations or multilateral organizations Candidates from developing countries looking for global exposure Why This Opportunity Stands Out Unlike many international roles, this JPO position: Is fully integrated into the UN system Offers direct exposure to senior leadership processes Provides structured training and mentorship Targets talent from developing countries, including Africa It is one of the few global career opportunities that combines policy influence, international exposure, and long-term career prospects. How to Apply Interested applicants must submit their applications through the official UN application portal. Before applying: Carefully review the eligibility criteria Prepare academic and professional documents Read the full job description and FAQ on the Nedworc Foundation website Important: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted, and late applications will not be considered. Apply here Deadline 26th April 2026 The UN JPO in Programme Management 2026 is a transformative opportunity for young professionals aiming to build a meaningful international career. With its strong focus on leadership development, policy engagement, and global impact, this programme serves as a gateway into the United Nations system. title: Fully Funded EU Traineeship for Young Graduates in Nigeria 2026
summary: If you are a young graduate looking to build a career in international relations, diplomacy, public policy, or global affairs, the Funded Traineeship for Young Graduates at the EU Delegation to the Federal Republic of Nigeria and ECOWAS 2026 is one of the most prestigious opportunities currently open. title: Frank Jennings Fellowship April 2026: Fully Funded Human Rights Fellowship in Ireland and Geneva for Global Graduates
summary: If you are passionate about human rights advocacy, international law, and global justice, the Frank Jennings Fellowship April 2026 offers one of the most prestigious early-career opportunities in the world. What is the Frank Jennings Fellowship? The Frank Jennings Fellowship is a highly competitive international fellowship designed to train and mentor the next generation of human rights professionals. It was established to honor Frank Jennings, a key figure in advancing human rights activism. The program provides a unique combination of NGO and UN-level experience, allowing fellows to work both with an international organization and within the United Nations system. Participants gain deep exposure to: Protection of human rights defenders International advocacy systems UN human rights mechanisms Policy drafting and global reporting processes Fellowship Structure (Detailed Breakdown) The fellowship is divided into three intensive phases, each designed to build expertise progressively: Phase 1: Dublin, Ireland – Training with Front Line Defenders (3–3.5 Months) During this phase, fellows receive foundational training and practical exposure to human rights protection work. Key responsibilities include: Supporting protection coordinators Drafting urgent appeals for at-risk defenders Managing databases and case documentation Conducting research on global human rights issues Phase 2: Geneva, Switzerland – Internship with OHCHR (6 Months) This is the core international experience where fellows work directly within the UN system. Key responsibilities include: Monitoring global human rights violations Drafting communications to governments Contributing to Human Rights Council reports Supporting UN Special Rapporteur mandates Phase 3: Return to Dublin (3 Months) Fellows return to apply their newly acquired UN experience in a practical NGO environment. Activities include: Supporting ongoing human rights cases Contributing to advocacy projects Strengthening field-based protection mechanisms Financial Benefits The fellowship is fully funded with a monthly stipend, making it accessible to candidates worldwide. Dublin: Approximately €1,651/month Geneva: Approximately €1,700/month This financial support helps cover living expenses during the program. Eligibility Criteria This fellowship is specifically designed for early-career professionals and recent graduates with a strong commitment to human rights. Who Can Apply? Recent university graduates (within one year of graduation) Final-year students eligible to graduate before the fellowship begins Individuals with demonstrated interest in human rights work Academic Professional Requirements Applicants must have: Knowledge of international human rights law and the UN system Strong research, writing, and analytical skills Administrative and organizational skills Ability to work in multicultural environments Language Requirements Fluency in English (mandatory) Fluency in Spanish (preferred) or French (often required) Additional Requirements Legal authorization to work in Ireland Strong communication and teamwork abilities Previous experience in human rights organizations (advantageous but not always mandatory Eligible Countries and Regions The fellowship is open to applicants globally, meaning candidates from: Africa Europe Asia North America South America Oceania can apply, provided they meet the eligibility criteria. title: Youth Innovating Democracy 2026 in Strasbourg, France: Fully Funded Council of Europe Youth Event on Shaping the Future of Democracy
summary: The Youth Innovating Democracy 2026 event, organized by the Council of Europe in partnership with the European Youth Forum, is a prestigious, fully funded international youth event designed to empower young leaders to actively contribute to the future of democracy in Europe and beyond. Why This Event Matters Across Europe and globally, democracy faces increasing challenges, including: Democratic backsliding Disinformation and misinformation Declining trust in institutions Youth underrepresentation in politics The New Democratic Pact for Europe aims to address these issues by strengthening democratic foundations, amplifying citizen participation, and innovating governance systems. The Youth Event plays a critical role in this process by ensuring that young people are at the center of these conversations and solutions. Key Themes of the Event The event is structured around three major thematic areas that address pressing challenges in democracy. 1. Juvenate Politics: Innovating the System This theme focuses on increasing youth participation in political systems. Key discussions include: Youth representation in decision-making Electoral reforms (e.g., youth quotas, voting age) Civic education and political engagement Inclusion of young people in governance 2. Live Equality: The Promise of Democracy This theme addresses social and economic inequalities affecting young people. Key focus areas: Access to social rights Economic justice and inclusion Impact of crises on youth (economic, political, health) Addressing marginalization and exclusion 3. Empower Communities: Building Participation Ecosystems This theme explores how to create enabling environments for youth participation. Topics include: Role of youth organizations and civil society Participatory democracy models Community engagement and grassroots initiatives Protection of democratic freedoms Objectives of the Programme The event aims to: Engage youth in shaping the New Democratic Pact for Europe Highlight innovative practices in youth participation Foster dialogue between youth and policymakers Promote democratic values and human rights Build a network of young leaders Programme Structure The three-day programme includes: Plenary sessions with political leaders Interactive workshops and discussions Creative and participatory activities Networking opportunities Development of policy proposals and outputs Participants will contribute directly to recommendations and creative outputs that will inform the New Democratic Pact. title: Call for Grant Proposals: Strengthening CSO Capacities in the Maldives
summary: The Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) in the Maldives has announced a Capacity Development Grant for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) , community-based organizations (CBOs), and research institutions. With a grant of up to US$75,000 and applications open until 18 April 2026 , this initiative aims to strengthen the technical skills, proposal development, and monitoring and evaluation (M E) capacities of local organizations. By equipping Maldivian CSOs with the tools to design high-quality proposals and manage projects effectively, this grant promotes sustainable development, community wellbeing, and environmental stewardship. Objectives of the Grant The Capacity Development Grant is part of the eighth operational phase of the SGP (OP8), which builds on over 30 years of empowering local civil society. The grant focuses on three key areas: Grant Proposal Writing and Technical Skills Selected organizations will conduct workshops and training sessions to improve the ability of CSOs and CBOs to write compelling and fundable grant proposals. These sessions will include guidance on donor expectations, structuring proposals, common pitfalls, and practical exercises. One dedicated workshop will focus on helping existing SGP grantees with interim and final report submissions, strengthening their compliance with funding requirements. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Knowledge Management Organizations will support grantees in monitoring and documenting project outcomes, using simplified M E tools, ensuring data quality, and developing reporting frameworks. This component aims to enhance grantees’ ability to track progress, analyze results, and disseminate lessons learned effectively, allowing successful projects to be scaled and replicated. Advocacy and Communication The grant also includes conducting a two-year advocacy campaign to raise awareness of the work and successes of Maldivian CSOs. This involves producing communication materials such as social media content, infographics, short videos, and reports, as well as organizing webinars, virtual networks, and roundtable meetings with stakeholders. Through these activities, CSOs can amplify their impact, influence policy, and foster multi-stakeholder collaboration. Why This Opportunity Is Important Local civil society organizations are vital actors in addressing social, environmental, and economic challenges in the Maldives. However, many face limitations in accessing funding, managing projects, and effectively communicating their results. By enhancing capacity in proposal writing, M E, and advocacy, this grant equips CSOs with the skills necessary to secure resources, manage projects efficiently, and generate meaningful impact in their communities. Moreover, the grant encourages the sharing of knowledge and best practices, promoting innovation and replication of successful projects. By linking CSOs, CBOs, local councils, line ministries, and development partners, the initiative strengthens networks and fosters collaboration. This ultimately leads to more sustainable community-driven development initiatives, improved environmental resilience, and empowerment of marginalized groups, including women, youth, and persons with disabilities. Who Can Apply This opportunity is open to: National and local CSOs and NGOs Community-based organizations (CBOs) Research bodies with relevant experience Eligible organizations must demonstrate experience in capacity building, proposal development, M E support, and advocacy campaigns. The team should include members with social sciences or management backgrounds, expertise in communications, and hands-on experience with community development projects. How to Apply Interested organizations should submit: A detailed proposal outlining methodology and approach for all three components (workshops, M E support, advocacy). A budget and work plan covering a period of 24–36 months (2026–2028). CVs of proposed team members with clearly defined roles. A letter of application describing relevant experience and capacity. All documents must be submitted as attachments; externally hosted or editable links will not be accepted. Applications will be evaluated solely on materials received by the deadline. Apply by: 18 April 2026 | 23:00 HRS (MVT) For more information and submission details, visit the official call for proposals . title: Fully Funded UN Youth Scholarship in Geneva: Chemicals and Waste Study Programme 2026
summary: The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), in collaboration with the Chemicals and Waste Youth Platform (CWYP), is offering a fully funded scholarship for young people to participate in the United Nations Chemicals and Waste Study Programme in Geneva, Switzerland. By equipping young leaders with knowledge, networks, and direct experience in policymaking, the programme helps build the next generation of professionals who can contribute to global solutions. title: 2026 Cook Center Summer Research Fellowships for Duke University Students
summary: The Samuel DuBois Cook Center on Social Equity at Duke University is now accepting applications for its 2026 Summer Research Fellowships. These fellowships are open to both graduate and undergraduate students and are designed to provide hands-on experience in cutting-edge research focused on social inequality. Participants gain the opportunity to deepen their scholarship, expand their professional networks, and actively contribute to the Cook Center’s mission of advancing social equity. The Cook Center conducts interdisciplinary research aimed at understanding the structures and systems that drive inequality in society. Its research pillars include educational and economic opportunity, health equity, carceral justice, and public policy engagement. The Center emphasizes a data-driven approach and methodological innovation, providing students with exposure to advanced research techniques and analytical tools. Fellows are integrated into dynamic research teams where they collaborate with faculty, postdoctoral researchers, graduate and undergraduate students, and other research professionals. Graduate fellows may mentor undergraduate students while simultaneously receiving guidance from senior scholars, ensuring a layered mentorship environment. This collaborative structure promotes leadership development, teamwork, and a comprehensive understanding of research practice in social equity. Why This Opportunity Matters Inequality remains a pressing challenge worldwide. The Cook Center Summer Research Fellowships provide students with the opportunity to investigate the causes and consequences of inequality and to develop evidence-based solutions. Through participation in this program, students gain valuable insight into how research informs policy, social programs, and public debate. The program emphasizes mentorship, collaborative research, and professional development, equipping students with the skills needed to succeed in academia, policy, and advocacy. Fellows gain practical experience, broaden their networks, and enhance their understanding of interdisciplinary approaches to social equity research. These experiences are crucial for students pursuing careers in research, public policy, education, and other fields focused on social justice. By fostering a diverse community of scholars, the Cook Center ensures that participants are prepared to contribute meaningfully to efforts aimed at reducing inequality and promoting social equity both nationally and globally. What You’ll Gain The Cook Center Summer Research Fellowships offer a wide range of professional, academic, and personal benefits: Stipend: Graduate fellows receive $10,625.01 for the summer term, while undergraduate fellows receive $2,500 per term, with the possibility of earning $5,000 if participating in both terms. Mentorship: Individualized guidance from faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and senior scholars provides valuable career support. Research Experience: Fellows gain practical skills by contributing to ongoing research projects, including data collection, literature review, analysis, and research dissemination. Skill Development: Build expertise in research methods, statistical analysis, interdisciplinary collaboration, project management, and communication. Networking: Engage with peers, mentors, and professionals across multiple disciplines, creating opportunities for future collaboration. Professional Exposure: Fellows share research outcomes through the Cook Center website and may gain visibility in academic and professional communities. Graduate fellows will also have the opportunity to mentor undergraduate fellows, fostering leadership and teaching skills, while undergraduates gain exposure to advanced research practices and interdisciplinary approaches to studying inequality. Eligibility Graduate Fellows: Must be current Duke University PhD students in good standing, enrolled for the Fall 2026 semester. Must coordinate with their department to ensure summer funding arrangements are compatible. Undergraduate Fellows: Must be current Duke University student enrolled for Fall 2026. Must be eligible to work in the United States. All Fellows: Must have a strong interest in social equity research and commit to active participation in fellowship activities. Must be able to attend biweekly team meetings and contribute to research projects for the duration of the fellowship. Application Process and Deadline Applicants interested in the 2026 Cook Center Summer Research Fellowships must download the appropriate application form for graduate or undergraduate students from the Cook Center website. All required materials, including completed application forms, curriculum vitae, statements of research interests, and letters of recommendation, should be compiled into a single PDF. Applicants will then submit their completed application according to the instructions provided on the official website. Deadlines: Priority consideration: March 31, 2026 Rolling applications: April 30, 2026, depending on availability To learn more and submit your application, visit the official Cook Center website . title: MSc in Olympic Studies 2026–2027: Advance Your Career in Olympic Education
summary: The University of Peloponnese, in partnership with the International Olympic Academy (IOA), invites applications for the Master’s Degree Programme in “Olympic Studies, Olympic Education, Organization and Management of Olympic Events” (MSc) for the academic year 2026–2027. This internationally recognized programme is supported by Olympic Solidarity, an initiative of the International Olympic Committee (IOC), which offers scholarships for selected candidates. The programme is designed for graduates and professionals who want to deepen their knowledge of the Olympic Movement, gain expertise in Olympic philosophy, education, and sport management, and contribute to the global development of sport and Olympic education. Classes are conducted in Ancient Olympia and Sparta, Greece, providing students with a unique immersive experience at the historical heart of Olympism. Through a combination of on-site lectures, practical workshops, and a master’s thesis completed remotely, the MSc offers an interdisciplinary approach, integrating education, sport, culture, and management. Students also benefit from the opportunity to join a global network of professionals and organizations involved in the Olympic Movement. What You’ll Gain Participants in the MSc will gain multiple benefits that advance their academic and professional careers: Specialized Knowledge: Acquire advanced understanding of Olympic philosophy, pedagogy, and the historical and modern Olympic Games. Practical Experience: Learn the organization and management of Olympic events and major sports competitions. Professional Development: Gain skills in sports marketing, sponsorship, strategic planning, and financial management of sports organizations. Global Networking: Connect with Olympic committees, international federations, and professionals engaged in sports education, culture, and event management. Scholarship Opportunities: Tuition and full-boarding scholarships are available through National Olympic Committees for eligible candidates. By combining theory and practical application, this programme prepares graduates to contribute to Olympic education programs, lead sport organizations, and participate actively in the international Olympic Movement. Eligibility Candidates must meet the following criteria: Hold a bachelor’s degree from a recognized Greek or foreign higher education institution. Preference is given to officials of National Olympic Academies, National Olympic Committees, the International Olympic Committee, international and national federations, and researchers in Olympic studies or sport management. Graduates from related fields such as education, sport, management, humanities, journalism, economics, pedagogy, or physical education are also eligible. Candidates must demonstrate professional experience, participation in sport events, Olympic education activities, or related research. Proficiency in English is required, with certificates for other languages considered an asset. Applicants must provide supporting documentation, including transcripts, CV, recommendation letters, identification, proof of participation in relevant activities, and any certifications relevant to their experience. Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed online. Programme Structure The MSc programme runs for three semesters : First Semester (18 Sept – 21 Nov 2026): On-site lectures in Ancient Olympia and Sparta, covering the history and philosophy of sport, modern Olympic Games, Olympic pedagogy, ethics, and research methods. Second Semester (3 Apr – 6 Jun 2027): On-site lectures in Greece, with modules on Olympic pedagogy, organization of games and major sports events, sports marketing, and optional modules such as integrity in sport, financial management, and sport policies. Third Semester (Sept 2027 – Feb 2028): Completion and submission of the master’s thesis, conducted remotely. All lectures are taught in English, and students are required to attend lectures, submit assignments, and complete examinations to progress successfully. Costs and Scholarships Tuition fees for the programme are 5,000 € for the three semesters, payable in three installments. Full-boarding at the IOA premises is approximately 3,500 € , with final costs confirmed individually. Scholarships are available through National Olympic Committees via IOC Olympic Solidarity. Applicants are encouraged to declare interest in scholarships in their application form and contact their National Olympic Committees for further guidance. Application Process and Deadline To apply, candidates must submit the following certified documents both via email and in hard copy to the programme secretariat by 30 April 2026 : Completed application form Bachelor’s degree certificate and transcript, including thesis title and grade CV detailing studies, professional experience, research, and extracurricular activities Language proficiency certificates Passport or ID copy Recommendation letters from professors or relevant sport organizations Supporting documents for professional experience, participation in sports, or Olympic activities 👉 To learn more and apply, visit the official MSc in Olympic Studies programme page . title: World Literacy Foundation Youth Ambassador Program 2026: Empowering Young Leaders for Global Literacy
summary: About the Opportunity The World Literacy Foundation (WLF) Youth Ambassador Program 2026 is a global initiative designed to empower young people to become active leaders in the fight against illiteracy. Through this program, participants aged 16 to 25 will join a worldwide community of changemakers, connect with peers across more than 60 countries, and develop skills to advocate for literacy at local and global levels. WLF is an international non-profit organization dedicated to reducing illiteracy and promoting equitable access to education. Its Youth Ambassador Program is grounded in the principle of youth empowerment, believing that young people’s creativity, vision, and energy are key to achieving meaningful impact. Over a three-month period from June to September 2026, 1000 young leaders will participate in online modules, collaborative projects, and advocacy initiatives designed to give them the tools to make a measurable difference in their communities. The program is entirely online, allowing participants from around the world to join without geographic constraints. Training focuses on leadership, advocacy, fundraising, social media communication, and project implementation. Ambassadors will gain hands-on experience designing campaigns, engaging with communities, and amplifying literacy initiatives. Participants who fundraise for WLF will receive a formal letter of completion, while all participants will receive a certificate recognizing their efforts upon completion of the program. Why This Opportunity Matters Literacy is a foundational skill for education, empowerment, and equitable development. Around the world, millions of children face barriers to learning due to poverty, conflict, or lack of resources. The Youth Ambassador Program enables young people to address these systemic challenges by raising awareness, mobilizing resources, and implementing advocacy campaigns. By participating, ambassadors gain a unique perspective on global literacy issues and learn how to create change that is both local and international. The program not only amplifies youth voices but also cultivates the next generation of global leaders committed to equitable education. In addition, ambassadors contribute to innovative solutions to combat illiteracy, ensuring that knowledge and learning opportunities reach underserved populations. What You’ll Gain The Youth Ambassador Program provides participants with multiple benefits that extend beyond the immediate three-month program: Skill Development: Ambassadors will build leadership, advocacy, communication, public relations, and fundraising skills applicable in both educational and professional contexts. Global Network: Participants join a diverse cohort of 1000 young leaders, fostering international collaboration and shared learning. Real-World Impact: By leading literacy campaigns and fundraising initiatives, ambassadors contribute directly to increasing access to education for vulnerable children globally. Recognition and Visibility: Ambassadors will have opportunities to have their voices amplified through WLF’s website, social media channels, and mainstream media features. Practical Experience in Advocacy: Through youth-led campaigns and creative projects, participants gain first-hand experience in social impact initiatives and community mobilization. This combination of benefits ensures that participants are not only contributing to literacy efforts but are also growing as capable, confident global leaders. Eligibility To participate in the Youth Ambassador Program 2026, applicants must meet the following criteria: Be 16 to 25 years old at the time of the program. Demonstrate a strong interest in literacy, education, human rights, or social impact . Be motivated to join a global community of young changemakers . Have access to a computer or smartphone and a reliable internet connection for online activities. Be active on social media and willing to use their voice to advocate for literacy. Commit to approximately 30 hours over three months to complete ambassador tasks. Be willing to support fundraising initiatives for WLF to expand global literacy programs. This program is inclusive, welcoming applicants from all countries and backgrounds who are passionate about literacy and social change. Application Process and Deadline Applicants begin by visiting the official World Literacy Foundation Ambassador Program page and selecting “Apply Now.” The website provides step-by-step instructions for completing the application form and submitting all required information. Applicants should carefully review the Terms and Conditions before applying, as the program is recurring annually and requires active commitment to the tasks outlined. The program will run from June to September 2026 , and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Early submission is encouraged to secure a spot in the global cohort. To learn more and apply, visit the official World Literacy Foundation website . title: Fully Funded PhD Scholarships at UQ: Co-Develop Solutions to Climate-Driven Loss and Damage in the Pacific
summary: The University of Queensland (UQ) is offering four fully funded PhD scholarships as part of the ARC Industry Laureate Fellowship , focused on co-developing solutions to climate-driven loss and damage in the Pacific. This is a unique opportunity to work closely with communities, governments, and regional partners to address the social, cultural, and justice dimensions of climate change. These scholarships are ideal for candidates passionate about applied research and committed to creating meaningful change for Pacific Island communities. Why Apply? PhD candidates will engage in research that directly impacts communities in the Cook Islands, Fiji, and Vanuatu , offering a rare combination of academic, field, and policy experience. Key benefits include: Fully funded scholarship covering tuition fees, living stipend (AU$37,500 per annum, tax-free), and Overseas Student Health Cover Access to world-class facilities and a dynamic, interdisciplinary research environment at the School of the Environment Funded fieldwork and collaboration with NGOs, regional organizations, and government agencies Mentorship from leading experts, including Professor Karen McNamara , Principal Supervisor Research Focus PhD projects will be co-designed with your advisory team to align with the Fellowship’s objectives: Develop and adapt methods for assessing climate-driven loss and damage Document lived experiences and community-led responses Implement and evaluate locally grounded interventions Inform policy and practice through multi-scalar insights and best-practice guidelines Projects are flexible and tailored to your research interests, disciplinary background, and the needs of partner communities. Who Should Apply Ideal candidates will have academic achievement in: Geography Environmental science Indigenous studies Development studies or related fields Experience or interest in climate adaptation, participatory research, or policy engagement is highly desirable. Scholars from Pacific Island nations, particularly Cook Islands, Fiji, and Vanuatu , are encouraged to apply. How to Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) Submitting an EOI is the first step toward securing your PhD scholarship. Here’s what you need to know: Step 1: Prepare Your EOI Include the following details: Proposed supervisor Scholarship details Previous academic qualifications Referee contacts (minimum two) English language proficiency information Step 2: Upload Required Documents Academic curriculum vitae (CV) Academic transcripts and degree certificates English language documents (if applicable) Formatting Guidelines: PDF format only File name: LASTNAME_firstname_document-name.pdf Include both original and official English translations if documents are in another language Step 3: Academic CV Your CV should focus on academic and research achievements, including: Personal details (name, contact, nationality, languages, ORCID ID) Education and academic awards Employment history and research experience Research outputs, publications, and grants Optional: a 200-word contextual statement on achievements relative to opportunities Do not include photographs, hobbies, or unrelated personal details. Step 4: Referee Details Provide at least two referees who can speak to your academic or research abilities. UQ will contact referees directly; do not submit pre-written letters. After Submitting Your EOI Your nominated supervisor will review your EOI (response typically within two weeks). If the supervisor is interested, an informal interview may be arranged to discuss your research fit. If supported, you will be invited to submit a final application , including: Passport copy Additional documents (proof of citizenship, name change, previous research studies) UQ-approved agent submission for some international applicants If your EOI is not supported, you may choose another supervisor and submit a new EOI. Deadline All EOIs must be submitted by 15 April, 2026 . Early submission is strongly recommended. title: EU Call for Proposals in Ethiopia 2026: Funding for Civil Society and Global Gateway Action
summary: A Major EU Funding Opportunity for Civil Society Organisations in Ethiopia The Delegation of the European Union to Ethiopia has opened a significant new funding opportunity for civil society organisations through the call titled “Supporting CSO role in sustainable and inclusive development and in Global Gateway Investments.” This initiative is designed to strengthen Ethiopian civil society organisations as independent, resilient, and accountable actors that can contribute to inclusive governance, equitable socio-economic development, and the implementation of Global Gateway investments in the country. This call is part of the CSOs Thematic Programme 2021–2027 and builds on earlier EU support to civil society in Ethiopia. The programme reflects the EU’s broader commitment to democratic participation, rights-based development, and stronger civic engagement, while also linking civil society action to priority investment sectors under the Global Gateway strategy. What This EU Call for Proposals Supports The overall objective of the call is to strengthen Ethiopian civil society organisations so they can play a stronger role in inclusive governance and sustainable development, while also contributing to Global Gateway investments. The call is divided into two separate lots , and applicants may apply under one lot only . For either lot, proposals are expected to use an integrated approach and address at least three priority areas under the selected lot rather than presenting isolated activities. This means applicants need to design proposals that are coherent, strategic, and clearly linked to measurable results. The guidelines also stress the importance of strong intervention logic, relevant indicators, monitoring plans, and meaningful partnerships between consortium members. Funding Available: Budget, Lots, and Grant Size The total indicative budget available under this call is EUR 5,829,000 . The funding is split equally across the two lots, with EUR 2,914,500 allocated to Lot 1 and EUR 2,914,500 allocated to Lot 2. The guidelines note that the Lot 2 allocation is tied to the EU budget for 2027 and is therefore subject to the prior availability of those funds. For both lots, the grant size is fixed at EUR 2,914,500 , meaning this is a high-value funding opportunity aimed at large-scale actions. The EU contribution must represent 95% of the total eligible costs of the action , with the remaining balance financed from other sources unless the applicant can justify full financing as essential for implementation. Lot 1: Strengthening Civil Society Capacity and Civic Space Lot 1 focuses on strengthening civil society’s role, capacity, and enabling environment in Ethiopia. Its specific objective is to improve the capacity, sustainability, and influence of local and grassroots CSOs so they can engage more effectively in policy-making, advocacy, dialogue with authorities, monitoring, and accountability processes at both local and national levels. Under this lot, priority areas include improving CSOs’ ability to influence public policy, support evidence-based advocacy, promote transparency and accountability, and build stronger partnerships and coalitions. It also supports inclusive social and economic development initiatives, stronger community engagement, and better internal governance, sustainability, fundraising, and organisational effectiveness. Another major focus is the protection of civic space and the promotion of an enabling legal and policy environment for civil society. The call also places strong emphasis on Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) under Lot 1. Applicants are expected to establish and manage at least one open and competitive support mechanism for local and grassroots CSOs, including capacity building, mentoring, and tailored technical support. At least EUR 1,860,000 must be reserved for FSTP to local and grassroots CSOs, and at least EUR 291,000 must be allocated to strengthening the capacities of those recipients. Lot 2: Civil Society Engagement in Global Gateway Priority Sectors Lot 2 is aimed at strengthening civil society engagement in Global Gateway priority sectors in Ethiopia. Its objective is to enhance the role and capacity of CSOs to contribute to transparent, inclusive, and sustainable policy-making, reform processes, and investment processes in four sectors: clean energy transition, sustainable agri-food value chains, health systems strengthening, and human-centric digital transformation . Priority areas under Lot 2 include improving governance and regulatory frameworks, increasing transparency and accountability in investment processes, empowering communities to participate in decision-making, and supporting inclusive skills development and economic opportunities linked to investment sectors. The call encourages actions that strengthen public oversight, promote environmental and social safeguards, support grievance mechanisms, and expand the role of communities and local CSOs across the investment cycle. Actions under Lot 2 must be implemented in at least three specific locations in Ethiopia where Global Gateway projects are already being implemented , and applicants must clearly explain how their chosen areas connect to relevant Global Gateway investments. Who Is Eligible to Apply? This opportunity is intended for non-profit legal entities such as civil society organisations, including NGOs, networks, and associations. To qualify, the lead applicant must be a legal person, be non-profit-making, and be directly responsible for the preparation and management of the action. Eligible lead applicants must be effectively established in an EU Member State, Ethiopia, or another country eligible under Article 28 of the NDICI-Global Europe regulation . A key requirement is that the lead applicant must apply together with at least two co-applicants established and registered in Ethiopia . In addition, the consortium must demonstrate experience managing at least one EU grant above EUR 1.5 million in the past three years , at least three years of practical experience working with local CSOs and building their capacity , and a proven track record in managing Financial Support to Third Parties schemes. For lead applicants not established in Ethiopia, the rules are stricter. They must demonstrate prior knowledge of Ethiopia’s civil society landscape, show that they have implemented at least two projects with local CSOs , and prove that local CSOs have been involved in the conception, governance, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the proposed action. Project Duration, Locations, and Design Requirements For both lots, the initial planned duration of an action must be at least 36 months and no more than 48 months . For Lot 1, actions must take place in at least three locations from the following exclusive list: Somali, Harari, Sidama, Gambella, South West Ethiopia, and Dire Dawa City Administration . Beyond location and duration, the guidelines require all proposals to demonstrate strong internal coherence between needs, objectives, expected results, activities, and indicators. Applicants are strongly encouraged to define one clear specific objective, include a solid monitoring plan, and describe genuine, balanced partnerships among consortium members. The call also includes mandatory cross-cutting priorities. All proposals must integrate meaningful youth engagement , a human rights-based approach , gender equality and women’s empowerment , and conflict sensitivity throughout the design and implementation of the action. How to Apply Through PROSPECT and PADOR This is a restricted call for proposals , which means the first stage requires the submission of a concept note only . Applicants whose concept notes are pre-selected will later be invited to submit a full application. Applications must be submitted online via PROSPECT , and organisations must register in PADOR . In addition, lead applicants and co-applicants must register in the European Commission’s Participant Register . The guidelines strongly recommend completing these registration steps well in advance rather than waiting until the final days before submission. Applicants must submit their concept notes in English , follow the official application format carefully, and ensure that the concept note contains all relevant information because no extra annexes are evaluated at that first stage. The full application stage, for those invited, will require more detailed documentation, including the budget, logical framework, and supporting eligibility documents. APPLY HERE. For more information about this apportunity, click here . Discover more grant opportunities, click here . Deadline and Key Dates The deadline for submission of concept notes is 13 May 2026 at 15:30 Brussels time . This is the most important immediate deadline for interested applicants. There will also be an information session on 17 April 2026 in hybrid format. Organisations interested in attending must send an email by 8 April 2026 with the requested participant details. According to the indicative timetable, applicants can expect the following milestones: information to pre-selected applicants and invitations to submit full applications: 25 June 2026 deadline for full applications: 11 August 2026 at 15:30 Brussels time notification of contracting authority decision: 20 October 2026 indicative contract signature: 20 November 2026 Final Tips Before You Apply For organisations considering this opportunity, early preparation will be essential. Because the call requires consortium formation, registration on multiple EU platforms, and a strong concept note aligned with one of the two lots, applicants should begin preparing as soon as possible. It is especially important to select the correct lot from the beginning, build a proposal with a strong and coherent intervention logic, and make sure the consortium’s experience clearly matches the requirements set out in the guidelines. For organisations applying under Lot 1, the design of the FSTP component will be particularly important. For Lot 2, applicants must be precise in linking their action to actual Global Gateway project locations in Ethiopia. For civil society organisations with the right structure, partnerships, and implementation capacity, this call represents a major opportunity to secure substantial EU support for long-term impact in Ethiopia. title: UNODC Junior Professional Officer (JPO) in Crime Research – Work on Global Security from Dakar
summary: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime is offering an exceptional opportunity for young professionals to launch an impactful international career. Through the United Nations Junior Professional Officer Programme , aspiring researchers can contribute to cutting-edge work addressing organized crime, terrorism, and drug-related challenges in West and Central Africa. 📌 About the Opportunity This Junior Professional Officer (JPO) position is based in Dakar, Senegal, within UNODC’s Regional Office for West and Central Africa.
