By combining training, mentorship, and networking opportunities, the initiative provides the tools and resources needed to help entrepreneurs grow their enterprises and strengthen their market presence. By investing in youth-led businesses, programmes like this accelerator contribute to: Job creation and economic inclusion Strengthening local value chains Promoting innovation and sustainable industries Supporting long-term economic resilience Young entrepreneurs often possess the creativity, energy, and vision needed to transform traditional industries. title: Help Shape Canada’s Health Research Future: Apply to Join a CIHR Institute Advisory Board
summary: The Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) is inviting applications for the 2026 Institute Advisory Board (IAB) Membership Cycle , offering professionals, researchers, and community leaders an opportunity to influence the future of health research in Canada. These advisory boards play a critical role in guiding CIHR’s Institutes by providing expert advice, strategic perspectives, and community insight to strengthen Canada’s health research ecosystem. Serving as an IAB member allows individuals to contribute to national health research priorities, collaborate with experts across disciplines, and ensure research initiatives reflect the needs of diverse communities. Application Deadline: April 25, 2026 What Are CIHR Institute Advisory Boards? Each of CIHR’s 13 Institutes has its own Institute Advisory Board composed of 8–14 volunteer members from Canada and abroad. These members provide advice to the Institute’s Scientific Director on a wide range of activities, including: Research priorities and strategic planning Knowledge mobilization strategies Community engagement initiatives Cross-Institute collaborations Health policy and innovation The boards represent a broad spectrum of expertise across the health research ecosystem, including academia, government, healthcare institutions, industry, and community organizations. The Role of an Institute Advisory Board Member IAB members serve in an independent advisory capacity , providing insights and recommendations that strengthen the direction and impact of health research initiatives. Key Responsibilities Members contribute by: Advising on Institute initiatives and strategic research priorities Encouraging interdisciplinary health research collaborations Strengthening partnerships with stakeholders and communities Supporting knowledge translation and research impact Considering ethical, policy, diversity, and inclusion factors in research initiatives Members also help ensure research priorities address emerging health challenges and the needs of diverse Canadian populations. Leadership and Governance Each Institute Advisory Board operates with a leadership structure that includes either: A Chair and Vice-Chair , or Two Co-Chairs These leaders guide discussions, develop meeting agendas with the Scientific Director, and ensure that advice represents the collective views of the board. Appointments are made by CIHR’s Governing Council based on expertise, experience, and representation needs. Membership Term and Time Commitment Selected members are invited to serve for: Initial term: Up to 3 years Possible renewal: Up to an additional 3 years Maximum service: 6 years Board meetings occur at least twice per year , either virtually or in person. While membership is voluntary , CIHR reimburses travel and meeting-related expenses at standard Government of Canada rates. Areas of Expertise Sought for 2026 For the 2026 cycle, CIHR Institutes are seeking applicants with expertise in areas such as: Artificial intelligence and data science in health research Indigenous health research and systems Health policy development and implementation Clinical research and trials Precision medicine and oncology Mental health and substance use policy Nutrition and metabolic diseases Population health and public health policy Digital health and learning health systems Gerontechnology and aging research Many Institutes are also seeking representation from individuals with lived experience, government professionals, patient partners, and international experts. Why Join a CIHR Institute Advisory Board? Serving on an IAB offers a unique opportunity to influence national health research priorities while working alongside leaders from multiple sectors. Impact Canada’s Health Research Agenda Your insights can help shape policies and research strategies that improve health outcomes across the country. Expand Your Professional Network Collaborate with researchers, policymakers, clinicians, and community leaders from Canada and around the world. Represent Diverse Voices CIHR is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion. Advisory board members help ensure health research reflects the needs of all Canadians. Commitment to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion CIHR actively encourages applications from individuals who bring diverse perspectives to the advisory boards. This includes candidates who identify as Indigenous, Francophone, gender diverse, living with disabilities, or members of racialized and marginalized communities. Representation across regions, sectors, and lived experiences is considered an essential part of building inclusive health research leadership. How the Selection Process Works Applications are reviewed during the annual membership cycle. Scientific Directors evaluate candidates based on: Expertise and professional experience Gaps in board representation Diversity and regional representation Current vacancies on each Institute’s board Selected candidates help fill expertise or representation needs within specific Institutes. Applications remain active in the IAB candidate pool for three years , allowing applicants to be considered for future openings. title: Civic Science Fellow 2026 at the Institute for Advanced Study (IAS) – $86,667 Salary for an 18-Month Fellowship in Princeton, USA

title: Apply for the Key Habitats Program 2026 — Funding & Support for Conservation and Community Initiatives in the Caribbean
summary: Conservationists, community leaders, NGOs, and environmental project teams in the Caribbean now have a valuable opportunity to apply for the Key Habitats Program 2026 , a funding initiative designed to support projects that conserve critical ecosystems and promote sustainable, community‑driven solutions. Led by the Dutch Caribbean Nature Alliance (DCNA) , the program provides financial support, technical guidance, and collaborative networks to help protect and restore biodiversity, strengthen local conservation capacity, and integrate community needs with environmental stewardship. ( dcnanature.org ) The Key Habitats Program targets initiatives that address priority conservation challenges, empowering local stakeholders to lead environmental action while contributing to long‑term ecosystem resilience across the Dutch Caribbean. About DCNA and the Key Habitats Program The Dutch Caribbean Nature Alliance is a regional partnership of nature conservation organizations across the Dutch Caribbean islands, including Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Sint Eustatius, and Sint Maarten. DCNA works to protect biodiversity, strengthen institutional capacity, and ensure sustainable use of natural resources. The Key Habitats Program serves as a strategic funding mechanism that facilitates impactful, community‑linked conservation projects. The initiative prioritizes efforts that are guided by scientific evidence and develop lasting environmental and social benefits. By providing targeted funding and tailored support, the program helps emerging and established conservation efforts realize measurable outcomes. Why This Opportunity Matters The Caribbean region is home to some of the world’s most unique and vulnerable ecosystems, including coral reefs, mangroves, and tropical forests. These habitats are crucial not only for biodiversity but also for the livelihoods, food security, and cultural heritage of communities. However, pressures such as climate change, habitat degradation, invasive species, and unsustainable use of resources threaten these ecosystems and the services they provide. The Key Habitats Program supports locally led efforts that address these challenges by strengthening institutional capacity, elevating community voices in conservation, and providing tools and resources for impactful action. For conservation practitioners, community leaders, and environmental advocates, this program offers a platform to implement meaningful change that resonates across ecological and social systems. What the Program Offers The Key Habitats Program provides a combination of financial resources, technical support, and collaborative engagement designed to elevate conservation projects from concept to action. Financial Support Selected applicants receive project funding that can be used to implement conservation activities, build capacity, or support community‑driven solutions. Funding helps cover essential project costs such as: Fieldwork and data collection Community education or outreach materials Equipment and supplies Training and facilitation activities This financial support enables organizations and initiatives to execute conservation plans that might otherwise be limited by resource constraints. Technical and Organizational Support In addition to funding, the program offers technical guidance from conservation specialists and professionals. This may include support with: Project planning and design Monitoring and evaluation Data analysis and reporting Communications and stakeholder engagement By connecting teams with technical expertise, DCNA ensures that projects are both scientifically sound and culturally relevant to local communities. Networking and Collaboration The Key Habitats Program encourages collaboration across the region. Participants gain access to: Regional conservation networks Peer learning opportunities Knowledge exchange with practitioners and experts Support from partner organizations in the Dutch Caribbean These connections help strengthen long‑term capacity and foster partnerships that extend beyond the duration of individual projects. Who Should Apply The Key Habitats Program is open to a range of applicants working on conservation and sustainability initiatives within the Dutch Caribbean region. Eligible applicants include: Nonprofit organizations engaged in conservation or community development Community groups or cooperatives with environmental projects Research teams working on habitat protection, restoration, or biodiversity studies Youth‑led or community‑led initiatives with a focus on sustainability Projects may vary in scope, but successful applications typically demonstrate a clear conservation objective, measurable outcomes, and strong community engagement. Areas of Focus and Project Priorities The Key Habitats Program prioritizes projects that contribute to the conservation of critical ecosystems and support local community resilience. Priority areas include: Habitat protection and restoration Biodiversity monitoring and research Community engagement and environmental education Sustainable livelihood integration with conservation goals Projects that link environmental outcomes to community benefits — such as sustainable fishing practices, ecotourism, or food security solutions — are particularly encouraged. By emphasizing both ecological and social dimensions, the program seeks to create holistic approaches that benefit both nature and people. Application Process and Timeline Interested applicants should review the Key Habitats Program guidelines and submit their proposals through the official DCNA application process. Applications typically require: A clear project description Objectives and measurable outcomes Budget and resource plan Letters of support or partner endorsements While DCNA publishes specific timelines and deadlines for each funding round, applicants are encouraged to prepare materials well in advance to ensure completeness and competitive quality. Application Deadline: 13 April 2026 Applicants should consult the official DCNA Key Habitats Program page for more submission details . title: Applications Open for Claude Community Ambassadors Program 2026
summary: Deadline: Rolling Applications Anthropic has opened applications for the Claude Community Ambassadors Program , a global initiative designed to support individuals who want to build and lead local communities around Claude. The program invites community builders, technical users, and AI enthusiasts to host events, share knowledge, and contribute to shaping the future of AI tools. The initiative focuses on empowering individuals to create vibrant local ecosystems where builders, developers, and curious learners can come together to explore and experiment with Claude. By supporting grassroots community efforts, Anthropic aims to expand access to AI knowledge while fostering collaboration across regions. About the Claude Community Ambassadors Program The Claude Community Ambassadors Program is built around the idea that strong communities drive innovation. Ambassadors are expected to organise meetups, workshops, and hackathons in their cities, creating spaces where people can learn, build, and exchange ideas. Participants are not required to be professional developers. While applicants should have meaningful experience using Claude tools such as Claude Code or Claude Cowork, the program places greater emphasis on community involvement and the ability to bring people together. This makes the opportunity accessible to a wide range of individuals, including educators, organisers, and tech enthusiasts. What Ambassadors Receive Selected ambassadors gain access to a range of resources to support their community-building efforts. These include: Funding support for local events such as meetups and hackathons Ready-to-use content and promotional assistance Swag and materials to enhance community engagement Monthly API credits to run demos and prototype ideas In addition, ambassadors receive early access to pre-release features and can participate in Builders Council sessions, where they share feedback directly with Anthropic’s product teams. Global and Flexible Participation The program is open to applicants from anywhere in the world, reflecting Anthropic’s focus on geographic diversity. There is no requirement to be based in a specific location, and multiple ambassadors can operate within the same city. This flexibility allows communities to grow organically across regions and ensures that participation is not limited by geography. Roles and Responsibilities Ambassadors are expected to take an active role in growing their local communities. This includes hosting events, running live demonstrations, and encouraging collaboration among participants. They are also responsible for sharing insights from their communities with Anthropic, helping shape future product development. Participants will join a private Slack network where they can connect with other ambassadors globally, exchange ideas, and collaborate on initiatives. Compensation and Benefits While the program does not provide direct financial compensation, it offers substantial support in other forms. Ambassadors receive event sponsorship, API credits, networking opportunities, promotional support, and recognition within the global AI community. These benefits are designed to help participants build impactful communities and expand their professional networks. Application Process Applications are open on a rolling basis, allowing interested individuals to apply at any time. Selected candidates will go through an onboarding process that includes signing an ambassador agreement, joining the private Slack workspace, and planning their first event. There is no cost to join the program, and all resources are provided by Anthropic. Why This Matters As AI continues to shape industries and societies, community-led initiatives play an important role in ensuring that knowledge and access are widely distributed. The Claude Community Ambassadors Program supports individuals who want to take the lead in making AI tools more accessible, collaborative, and locally relevant. For those passionate about community building and emerging technologies, the program offers a unique opportunity to contribute to a global network while creating impact at the local level. title: Apply for STIAS Fellowships 2027 — Fully Funded Research Fellowships in South Africa

Who Should Apply The STIAS Fellowship Programme is open to both emerging and established scholars, scientists, and artists . title: Applications Open for Rooted and Rising: Youth Leaders Grant 2026
summary: Deadline: April 17, 2026 The Conrad Prebys Foundation has launched the Rooted and Rising: Youth Leaders Grant initiative, aimed at strengthening civic participation by investing in youth leadership programs across San Diego County. The initiative recognises that a healthy democracy depends on active engagement—yet many young people are still positioned as passive recipients rather than active contributors to change. This funding opportunity seeks to shift that narrative by supporting programs that equip young people with the skills, confidence, and platforms needed to engage meaningfully in civic life. About the Youth Leaders Grant 2026 The Rooted and Rising initiative is designed to support programs that combine leadership development with real-world civic engagement. By focusing on middle and high school-aged youth, the program aims to nurture a generation capable of shaping more inclusive and equitable communities. The foundation highlights that young people already bring creativity, resilience, and a strong desire to contribute. However, access to structured civic engagement opportunities remains uneven. Through this initiative, the foundation aims to bridge that gap and position youth as active partners in community problem-solving. In recent years, there has been growing recognition that early exposure to civic processes—such as dialogue, community organising, and collaborative decision-making—can significantly shape long-term democratic participation. Programs that engage youth at this stage not only build individual confidence but also strengthen collective capacity within communities, ensuring that future leaders are better equipped to address complex social challenges. Key Focus Areas Funded programs must integrate skill-building with practical experience. This includes: Leadership, collaboration, and problem-solving training Experiential learning tied to real community challenges such as climate resilience, arts and culture, health, and democratic participation Opportunities for youth to engage in storytelling, content creation, and visible leadership roles Strong mentorship networks connecting youth with civic leaders and career pathways A central requirement is that all programs culminate in an action project , where participants actively contribute to solving real community issues. Funding Details Grant Amount: Up to $150,000 per award Total Funding Pool: $2.5 million Number of Grants: Approximately 15–20 Grant Duration: July 2026 to December 2027 (18 months) Funding Type: Programmatic Eligibility Criteria Applicants must meet the following requirements: Be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, fiscally sponsored organisation, or Tribal entity Operate in and/or serve San Diego County Focus on middle and/or high school-aged youth Deliver programs centred on leadership development, civic engagement, and community problem-solving Be an existing program that is expanding or strengthening its impact Programs must also demonstrate ongoing engagement rather than one-time activities and show clear outcomes such as participant numbers, skill development, and types of civic engagement activities. Program Expectations Proposals should include measurable outcomes and clearly defined program goals. Applicants are encouraged to highlight: Youth participation and leadership growth Civic engagement activities such as volunteering, advisory councils, or peer-led initiatives Use of youth-generated content like videos or social media storytelling Inclusion of diverse perspectives and community-informed approaches Preference will be given to programs that involve youth as co-designers or decision-makers and demonstrate strong community impact through structured frameworks or learning models. Registration approval may take 2–3 days, so early preparation is recommended. Why This Matters By investing in youth leadership, the initiative aims to strengthen not just individual participants but the broader civic ecosystem of San Diego. The program envisions a future where young people see themselves as stakeholders in their communities—capable of driving meaningful, long-term change. Organisations working at the intersection of youth development and civic engagement are encouraged to apply and contribute to building a more participatory and resilient society. title: Paid Student Fellowship Opportunity with the Global Campaign for Education-US (GCE-US)
summary: Students and young professionals seeking practical experience in international development, education policy, advocacy, and nonprofit communications now have an exciting opportunity through the Paid Student Fellowship offered by the Global Campaign for Education-US (GCE-US). This fellowship provides students with hands-on experience working with a leading advocacy coalition that promotes universal access to quality and inclusive education worldwide. The fellowship is designed to support students who are passionate about social change, global education rights, and policy advocacy. It allows participants to contribute meaningfully to international education campaigns while developing professional skills in communications, policy engagement, research, and nonprofit management. The fellowship also offers financial compensation and flexible working hours suitable for students balancing academic commitments. Participants can gain valuable exposure to international education policy networks and build connections with organizations advocating for education as a fundamental human right. About the Global Campaign for Education-US (GCE-US) The Global Campaign for Education-US (GCE-US) is a coalition of organizations working together to ensure that all children and youth worldwide have access to quality, inclusive, and equitable education. The organization focuses on advocacy efforts aimed at mobilizing political will in the United States and globally to support education initiatives. The coalition collaborates with civil society organizations, policy leaders, educators, and international partners to promote education policies that support sustainable development and human rights. Education is recognized as a key driver of social, economic, and political progress, and GCE-US works to ensure it remains at the center of global development agendas. Through this fellowship program, students gain a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advocacy, policy development, communication, and coalition building. Overview of the Paid Student Fellowship The GCE-US Paid Student Fellowship provides students with the opportunity to participate in real-world advocacy efforts supporting global education initiatives. Fellowship Key Details Category: Fellowship / Internship Compensation: Approximately $16.10 per hour Work Schedule: 10–20 hours per week Location: 100% remote (telework) Preferred Locations: Washington, DC or New York City metro areas for occasional meetings Duration: Flexible; preference for fellows who can continue for at least one academic year Start Date: As soon as possible Academic Credit: May be available depending on the student’s university Application Method: Email submission of cover letter and resume The fellowship is structured to allow students to work remotely while contributing to meaningful global education advocacy campaigns. Responsibilities of the GCE-US Student Fellow Fellows play an active role in supporting the coalition’s advocacy work, communication strategies, and member engagement. The fellowship provides a dynamic learning environment where participants gain practical experience in nonprofit operations and international policy advocacy. Communications and Social Media Management One of the key responsibilities of fellows is supporting GCE-US communication strategies. Fellows will: Create and manage social media content across platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, and YouTube. Design graphics and visual materials highlighting global education statistics and advocacy campaigns. Monitor engagement and analyze social media campaign performance. This experience helps fellows develop valuable digital communications skills applicable to nonprofit organizations, advocacy groups, and international development agencies. Research and Policy Advocacy Another important component of the fellowship involves conducting research on global education issues. Fellows will: Research international education policies and global education trends. Prepare presentations and reports for coalition members. Support advocacy initiatives aimed at promoting education rights globally. This research contributes to the organization’s efforts to influence policy decisions and strengthen global education systems. Coalition Engagement and Partnership Development GCE-US works with a wide network of partner organizations. Fellows help maintain these relationships through: Communicating with member organizations Coordinating coalition meetings Engaging partners in collaborative advocacy campaigns Supporting outreach to new organizations This responsibility allows fellows to gain experience in stakeholder engagement and international collaboration. Event Coordination and Meeting Support Fellows assist in planning and coordinating meetings, events, and advocacy campaigns. Typical responsibilities may include: Preparing agendas for coalition meetings Contacting speakers and participants Scheduling and organizing meetings Taking meeting minutes and tracking follow-up actions Supporting fundraising and advocacy events These tasks help fellows develop organizational and event management skills. Content Creation and Publication Fellows also contribute to producing educational and advocacy materials. Tasks may include: Writing blog posts and articles Coordinating the organization’s monthly newsletter Updating website content Publishing press releases and partner highlights These responsibilities strengthen fellows’ writing, editing, and public communication abilities. Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements To ensure fellows can effectively contribute to the organization’s work, GCE-US has outlined several qualifications and expectations. Academic Requirements Applicants must be: Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program, or Recently graduated from a recognized university. Fields of study that align well with the fellowship include: International development Education policy Public policy Communications Political science Social sciences Nonprofit management Professional Skills and Competencies Successful applicants should demonstrate the following skills: Strong writing, editing, and communication skills Ability to organize and manage multiple tasks Experience or interest in advocacy and social impact initiatives Knowledge of social media management and digital communications Ability to work independently and collaboratively in remote environments Applicants should also possess a strong attention to detail and excellent organizational skills. Technical Skills Preferred technical skills include familiarity with: Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) Google Workspace tools Zoom and remote collaboration platforms Graphic design tools such as Canva Website management platforms like WordPress Data analytics tools such as Google Analytics Although not mandatory, experience with these tools strengthens an applicant’s profile. Language Requirements The primary working language for the fellowship is English. However, additional language skills are considered an advantage. Languages that may strengthen an application include: Arabic French Portuguese Spanish International Sign Language American Sign Language Multilingual candidates are particularly valuable in international advocacy organizations working across different regions. Who Can Apply for the GCE-US Fellowship? Eligible Categories of Applicants The opportunity is open to: Undergraduate students Graduate students Recent university graduates Students interested in international development and advocacy Candidates from marginalized and underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply. Geographic Eligibility Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States because the organization cannot sponsor work permits. Therefore, eligible applicants typically include: Students studying in the United States U.S. citizens or permanent residents International students with legal work authorization in the U.S. Benefits of the GCE-US Paid Student Fellowship Participating in this fellowship offers several professional and academic benefits. Professional Development Fellows gain real-world experience working with an international advocacy organization. This exposure helps participants understand how policy advocacy campaigns operate at national and global levels. Networking Opportunities The fellowship allows students to connect with: Education policy experts International development professionals Nonprofit leaders Advocacy organizations and coalition members These connections can open doors to future employment opportunities. Advocacy Experience Fellows gain firsthand experience contributing to campaigns aimed at promoting education as a human right. This experience can be valuable for careers in: International development Public policy Education reform Human rights advocacy Academic Integration Because the fellowship offers flexible hours and potential academic credit, it is particularly suitable for students who want to combine practical experience with academic studies. How to Apply for the GCE-US Paid Student Fellowship Applicants must submit their application via email. Required Application Documents Applicants should send the following materials in a single document: Cover letter Resume The subject line should include: “Fellowship Application.” Apply here Information to Include in the Cover Letter Applicants must also address several questions in their cover letter: Why they want to work in the role How they learned about the opportunity Their salary expectations Availability and preferred work schedule Academic program details Confirmation of legal authorization to work in the United States Applications should be sent to the email address listed on the official opportunity page. Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Future Global Leaders Education advocacy remains one of the most important global development priorities. Access to quality education improves economic opportunity, promotes gender equality, and supports sustainable development worldwide. The GCE-US fellowship allows students to participate directly in advocacy initiatives that influence international education policy and funding decisions. Through hands-on work with coalition members and policy advocates, fellows gain the experience necessary to become future leaders in education reform and global development. This fellowship also equips students with practical skills in communication, research, nonprofit management, and coalition building, all of which are highly valued in the international development sector. Application Deadline 22nd March 2026 Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted). The GCE-US Paid Student Fellowship is an excellent opportunity for students passionate about global education, advocacy, and nonprofit leadership. With paid compensation, flexible working hours, and the chance to contribute to international education campaigns, the fellowship provides a meaningful platform for students to build their careers while making a positive global impact. title: GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme 2026 in Germany: Fully Funded Global Public Health Fellowship for Professionals Working in Epidemic Intelligence and Outbreak Response
summary: JThe GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme 2026 is a prestigious international fellowship designed to strengthen global capacity in epidemic intelligence, outbreak response, and public health emergency preparedness. The program is jointly coordinated by the Robert Koch Institute (RKI), the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, and the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN). This six-month fellowship provides public health professionals with the opportunity to design and implement impactful projects that improve surveillance systems, strengthen outbreak response capabilities, and contribute to global health security. The program equips fellows with advanced skills in public health surveillance, emergency response, and epidemic intelligence while fostering collaboration with leading global health experts and institutions. The fellowship is designed for professionals working within GOARN partner institutions and technical networks worldwide. Participants gain hands-on experience through mentorship, research, and collaborative projects while contributing to the development of innovative strategies that enhance global preparedness for future health emergencies. Overview of the GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme The GOARN Berlin Fellowship is a six-month project-based training and research fellowship aimed at developing the next generation of global health leaders. Participants undertake a project related to epidemic intelligence, public health surveillance, outbreak control, or emergency preparedness. The fellowship focuses on strengthening the capacity of institutions around the world to detect and respond to emerging public health threats. By working closely with experts from leading global health organizations, fellows gain practical insights and advanced knowledge that can be applied in their home institutions and countries. Key objectives of the fellowship include: Enhancing expertise in epidemic intelligence and disease surveillance Strengthening global collaboration in outbreak response and public health preparedness Supporting innovative research and operational projects that improve early warning systems Developing leadership capacity among public health professionals Building stronger international networks of public health experts Through the fellowship, participants become part of a global network of professionals working together to improve health security worldwide. Fellowship Structure and Tracks Beginning with the 2026 cohort, the GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme offers two flexible participation tracks, allowing fellows to tailor their experience to their professional circumstances and goals. 1. Berlin Track Under the Berlin Track, fellows relocate to Berlin, Germany, where they are based at the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence and the Robert Koch Institute. During their stay, fellows collaborate with global experts and participate in intensive training sessions, workshops, and project development activities. This track offers a fully immersive experience within one of the world’s leading public health ecosystems. 2. Country Track The Country Track allows fellows to implement their projects while remaining in their home country or institution. Although fellows work primarily within their local context, they still participate in joint training programs and collaborative activities in Berlin and Geneva. This flexible approach enables professionals who cannot relocate for the full six months to benefit from the fellowship while contributing directly to capacity development in their home institutions. Both tracks provide fellows with equal opportunities to engage in mentorship, collaborative research, and global health networking. Fellowship Duration The GOARN Berlin Fellowship runs for six months, during which fellows focus on implementing their project while receiving expert mentorship and training. The program is structured around: Project development and implementation Mentorship and technical guidance Training workshops and seminars Collaborative activities with global health experts Cohort learning experiences Throughout the fellowship, participants engage with professionals from international public health agencies, research institutions, and government health authorities. Institutions Coordinating the Fellowship The GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme is a collaborative initiative coordinated by several leading global health organizations: Robert Koch Institute (RKI) The Robert Koch Institute is Germany’s national public health institute and plays a central role in disease surveillance, epidemiological research, and health protection. WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence This World Health Organization hub focuses on improving global surveillance systems by using data and analytics to detect and respond to emerging health threats. Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN) GOARN is a global network of institutions and experts coordinated by the World Health Organization that responds to public health emergencies and disease outbreaks worldwide. Together, these organizations provide fellows with access to cutting-edge research environments, advanced data tools, and global expertise in epidemic intelligence. Fields and Areas of Work Projects developed during the fellowship typically focus on areas such as: Epidemic intelligence Public health surveillance systems Outbreak detection and response Pandemic preparedness and response strategies Risk assessment and emergency management Early warning systems for infectious diseases Data-driven public health decision making These projects contribute directly to strengthening national and global capacities for disease surveillance and outbreak response. Benefits of the GOARN Berlin Fellowship Participants in the GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme receive numerous professional and academic benefits, including: Advanced Training Fellows participate in training programs designed to strengthen skills in epidemic intelligence, outbreak response, and data analysis. Mentorship from Global Experts Participants receive mentorship from leading experts at the Robert Koch Institute, WHO Hub, and GOARN. International Collaboration The fellowship connects participants with global networks of public health professionals and institutions. Practical Project Implementation Fellows work on real-world projects that strengthen surveillance systems and outbreak preparedness in their home institutions. Professional Networking Participants build long-term collaborations with international researchers, policymakers, and public health experts. Global Health Leadership Development The program prepares fellows to become leaders in epidemic intelligence and public health emergency response. Eligibility Criteria To apply for the GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme, candidates must meet several eligibility requirements. Institutional Eligibility Applicants must be working at a GOARN partner institution or technical network. Only professionals affiliated with these institutions are eligible to apply. Professional Background Candidates should be public health professionals with experience in areas such as: Epidemiology Disease surveillance Emergency preparedness and response Public health research Risk communication and outbreak management Project Proposal Applicants are typically required to submit a project proposal related to epidemic intelligence, surveillance, or outbreak response. Professional Commitment Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to improving public health systems and contributing to global health security. Eligible Countries and Regions The fellowship is open to applicants from institutions that are members of the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network. GOARN partner institutions are located across multiple regions, including: Africa Asia Europe The Americas The Middle East Oceania Because GOARN is a global network, professionals from many countries worldwide may be eligible to apply if their organization is part of the network. Who Should Apply The fellowship is ideal for professionals who: Work in national public health institutes Serve in ministries of health Conduct public health research Participate in outbreak response teams Work in international health organizations Contribute to epidemic surveillance systems The program is particularly beneficial for professionals seeking to strengthen their expertise in epidemic intelligence and contribute to the improvement of disease surveillance systems in their home countries. Impact of the Fellowship The GOARN Berlin Fellowship Programme has already supported public health professionals from multiple countries in developing innovative projects that strengthen surveillance systems and outbreak preparedness. Fellows from previous cohorts have worked on projects such as: Improving early warning systems for infectious disease outbreaks Strengthening national surveillance platforms Enhancing risk assessment frameworks for public health emergencies Developing new approaches to epidemic intelligence These initiatives contribute to building stronger, data-driven public health systems worldwide. How to Apply Applicants interested in the fellowship should follow these steps: Confirm that their institution is a GOARN partner organization. Contact their institution’s GOARN focal point for application guidance. Prepare a project proposal related to epidemic intelligence or outbreak response. Complete the official application process through the program’s designated application channels. Because the program accepts a limited number of fellows, applicants are encouraged to submit strong proposals that demonstrate innovation, feasibility, and potential impact on global health. title: Fully Funded A. G. Leventis African Biodiversity Fellowship at Oxford University for African Conservation Professionals

Strengthening Conservation Leadership The fellowship supports professionals from NGOs, government institutions, and private sector organizations who are involved in designing and implementing biodiversity conservation initiatives. Fellows will either conduct their research independently or collaborate with members of the Megatrends Afrika project team or other researchers affiliated with the host institutions. During the fellowship, participants will also be encouraged to engage with ongoing research activities, seminars, and events organized by the host institutes. These engagements provide an opportunity for fellows to exchange ideas with international scholars and policymakers working on Africa-related issues. A key outcome of the fellowship is the production of a Megatrends Policy Brief , which will be published as part of the project’s research outputs. Research Themes in the Megatrends Fellowship The fellowship invites research proposals addressing important structural transformations shaping Africa’s future. Applicants are encouraged to submit research proposals aligned with one of the following core themes: Peace and Security Research proposals under this theme may explore issues related to conflict prevention, regional security cooperation, peacebuilding strategies, and evolving security dynamics across the African continent. Future of Democracy This theme focuses on governance, democratic institutions, political reforms, and citizen participation in African countries. Researchers may examine political transitions, democratic resilience, and governance challenges affecting African states. Economic Prospects The fellowship supports research examining Africa’s economic transformation and development prospects. Topics may include economic diversification, regional trade integration, sustainable development strategies, and economic policy reforms. Africa’s Role in the Global Order This theme explores Africa’s growing influence in global governance and international relations. Researchers may investigate Africa’s partnerships with global powers, its role in multilateral institutions, and its evolving geopolitical significance. Science Diplomacy and International Cooperation This research area focuses on the role of scientific collaboration and international partnerships in addressing global challenges and advancing development in Africa. Emerging Topics of Interest In addition to the core research themes, the program is also interested in proposals exploring emerging trends affecting Africa. These include topics such as: • Artificial intelligence and new technologies in African countries • Africa’s energy transition and international cooperation • Critical raw materials and global supply chains • Digitalization and its influence on governance • Urbanization and its impact on political systems These emerging topics reflect the rapidly changing global landscape and its implications for Africa’s future development. Fellowship Benefits and Financial Support The Megatrends Afrika Fellowship provides financial and logistical support to ensure that fellows can focus on their research during their stay in Germany. Selected fellows will receive: • A monthly grant of €2,800 • An economy-class return flight between their home country and Germany • Additional financial support for public transport, mobile phone credit, and other living expenses • Assistance with visa applications , including an official support letter if required These benefits help ensure that fellows can fully dedicate their time to research and academic collaboration. Fellowship Location and Duration The fellowship will take place in fall 2026 and will last for three months . Selected fellows will be hosted at one of the partner institutions: • Berlin – German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) • Bonn – German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) • Kiel – Kiel Institute for the World Economy During their stay, fellows will reside in the city of their host institution and actively participate in academic and research activities. Application Process Applicants must submit their fellowship application by email as a single PDF document . The application package must include: • A one-page motivation letter • An academic CV including a list of publications • Two recent academic publications • Copies of relevant academic transcripts or diplomas • A project concept note (maximum 2,000 words) The concept note should clearly outline the research topic, its academic and policy relevance, methodological approach, and feasibility within the three-month fellowship period. Applications must be sent to the following email address: Megatrends-Afrika@swp-berlin.org Selection Process Applications will be evaluated by a selection committee consisting of researchers from the participating institutions. Selection decisions will be based on several key criteria, including: • Academic merit and research track record • Relevance of the research project to the Megatrends Afrika themes • Feasibility of completing the research within the fellowship period • Ability to communicate research findings clearly to both academic and policy audiences Shortlisted candidates will be invited to participate in an online interview . Deadline for Applications The deadline to apply for the Megatrends Afrika Fellowship 2026 is: 📅 March 25, 2026 (11:59 p.m. CET) Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Learn More About This Opportunity To learn more about the Prestigious Megatrends Afrika Fellowship 2026 for African Researchers , click here Please send your application by email to Megatrends-Afrika@swp-berlin.org . Conclusion The Megatrends Afrika Fellowship 2026 provides an excellent opportunity for African scholars to conduct impactful research while engaging with international policy debates on Africa’s future. By offering financial support, access to leading research institutions, and opportunities for academic collaboration, the fellowship helps strengthen policy-relevant research on Africa’s evolving role in global affairs. title: Empowering Data Visualization Course 2026 by the World Bank Group Data Academy
summary: The Prestigious Data Visualization Course 2026 by the World Bank Group Data Academy is an excellent opportunity for professionals, students, and data enthusiasts who want to improve their ability to communicate insights using data. In today’s digital and data-driven world, the ability to transform complex information into clear and compelling visuals is a highly valuable skill across many sectors. Offered by the World Bank Group Data Academy , this online course introduces the fundamentals of data visualization and teaches participants how to craft impactful stories using charts, maps, and infographics. The course focuses on practical techniques for selecting the most appropriate visualization methods and presenting information in ways that support better understanding and decision-making. Participants will learn how to transform complex datasets into visuals that are intuitive, informative, and persuasive. Enrollment is currently open, and course materials will become available on March 31, 2026 . Participants who complete the course will also receive a free certification , making it a valuable addition to professional portfolios. Data Visualization Skills for Effective Communication In an era where data plays a central role in decision-making, the ability to communicate insights clearly is essential. This data visualization course helps learners develop the skills required to convert raw information into visual formats that are easy to interpret and act upon. Organizations across industries rely on visual storytelling to explain complex trends, highlight important patterns, and support evidence-based decisions. Through this course, participants will learn how to simplify complicated data and present it in ways that improve comprehension and engagement. The course demonstrates how well-designed visualizations can help audiences quickly understand key insights that might otherwise remain hidden in spreadsheets or reports. What You Will Learn in the Data Visualization Course The course introduces a wide range of practical concepts and techniques that are essential for effective data visualization. Participants will gain an understanding of the following topics: Choosing the Right Visualization Selecting the correct visualization type is one of the most important steps in communicating data effectively. The course explains how to match different chart types with specific datasets and communication goals. Learners will explore how to use bar charts, line charts, scatter plots, and other visual tools to present data in meaningful ways. Understanding Chart Anatomy Participants will learn the fundamental components of charts and how to design them effectively. This includes understanding elements such as axes, labels, legends, color usage, and layout design. Proper chart design ensures that visualizations remain clear and accessible to audiences. Best Practices for Data Visualization The course emphasizes best practices that improve the readability and clarity of visual content. These practices include simplifying visual elements, avoiding unnecessary complexity, and focusing on the most important insights within a dataset. Turning Complex Data Into Clear Stories One of the key skills taught in this course is data storytelling . Participants will learn how to interpret trends and communicate them through compelling visual narratives. Data storytelling combines analytical thinking with visual communication, enabling professionals to present insights that support strategic decisions. Practical Data Visualization Exercises The course includes hands-on exercises that allow participants to apply the concepts they learn. Through these exercises, participants will practice transforming complex questions into clear visual answers. These activities help learners develop the confidence and technical skills needed to work with real-world data. Participants will also gain practical experience using common visualization tools and techniques. Creating Maps and Infographics in Excel Another important component of the course is learning how to create maps and infographics using Excel . Excel remains one of the most widely used tools for data analysis and reporting. The course teaches participants how to use Excel’s visualization capabilities to create effective visual content. Participants will learn how to: • Create visually engaging charts • Develop simple infographics • Design maps that display geographic data These skills can be applied in many fields, including research, public policy, business analytics, journalism, and development work. Why Data Visualization Skills Matter Strong data visualization skills are increasingly important in the modern workplace. Professionals in fields such as development, economics, public policy, business analytics, journalism, and research rely on visual communication to present insights and support decision-making. By mastering data visualization, individuals can improve their ability to communicate findings clearly and influence strategic decisions. This course provides a strong foundation for anyone looking to strengthen their analytical and communication skills. Free Certification Opportunity Participants who successfully complete the course will receive a free certificate of completion from the World Bank Group Data Academy. This certificate demonstrates proficiency in data visualization techniques and can strengthen professional profiles, resumes, and LinkedIn profiles. For students and early-career professionals, this certification can also help demonstrate valuable analytical and communication skills to potential employers. Course Availability Enrollment for the Data Visualization Course 2026 is currently open. Participants who register will gain access to course materials beginning on March 31, 2026 . Because the course is offered online, participants can learn at their own pace and access the training materials from anywhere in the world. Learn More About This Opportunity To learn more about the Powerful Data Visualization Course 2026 by the World Bank Group Data Academy , visit the official course page here APPLY HERE Conclusion The World Bank Group Data Academy Data Visualization Course provides a valuable opportunity for individuals who want to improve their ability to communicate insights using data. Through practical exercises, visualization techniques, and storytelling strategies, participants will gain the skills needed to transform complex datasets into clear and impactful visuals. By mastering data visualization, learners can enhance their analytical capabilities and strengthen their ability to present data-driven insights effectively.
